body.text: āryaśūraviracitā bodhisattvāvadānamālāparaparyāyā
body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Āryaśūra</s>, also known as the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānamālā</s>

children.text: Jātakamālā
children.translated_text: <s>Jātakamālā</s> (Garland of Birth Stories)

body.text: om namaḥ śrīsarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to all the glorious <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

children.text: śrīmanti sadguṇaparigrahamaṅgalāni kīrtyāspadānyanavagītamanoharāṇi /
children.translated_text: The glorious deeds of the Sage in former births — auspicious through their embrace of true virtues, foundations of fame, captivating to the mind with songs never before heard —

children.text: pūrvaprajanmasu muneścaritādbhu tāni bhaktyā svakāvyakusumāñjalinārcayiṣye // Jm_1.1 //
children.translated_text: I shall worship with devotion, with a handful of flowers of my own poetry. || Jm 1.1 ||

children.text: ślādhyairamībhirabhilakṣitacinhabhūtairādeśito bhavati yatsugatatvamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: By these praiseworthy [deeds], which serve as distinguishing marks and signs, the path to <s>Sugata</s>-hood (Buddhahood) is revealed;

children.text: syādeva rūkṣamanasāmapi ca prasādo dharmyāḥ kathāśca ramaṇīyataratvamīyuḥ // Jm_1.2 //
children.translated_text: even those of harsh minds may find serenity, and righteous stories may attain even greater beauty. || Jm 1.2 ||

children.text: lokārthamityabhisamīkṣya kariṣyate 'yaṃ śrutyārṣayuktyaviguṇena pathā prayatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Considering 'this is for the welfare of the world,' this effort is being undertaken along a path not lacking in scriptural tradition, sage-reasoning, and logic,

children.text: lokottamasya caritātiśayapradeśaiḥ svaṃ prātibhaṃ gamayituṃ śrutivallabhatvam // Jm_1.3 //
children.translated_text: to convey my own literary talent to the state of being beloved by the learned, through the extraordinary passages of the deeds of the Supreme One of the world. || Jm 1.3 ||

children.text: svārthodyatairapi parārthacarasya yasya naivānvagamyata guṇapratipattiśobhā /
children.translated_text: Even by those devoted to their own aims, the splendor of his appreciation of virtues could never be fully grasped — he who is devoted to the welfare of others;

children.text: sarvajña ityavitathākṣaradīptakīrti mūrdhnā name tamasamaṃ sahadharmasaṃgham // Jm_1.4 //
children.translated_text: to him, the Omniscient One, whose fame blazes with the truth of that epithet, I bow my head, together with the community of <s>Dharma</s>. || Jm 1.4 ||

body.text: 1 vyāghrījātakam
body.translated_text: 1. The <s>Vyāghrī-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Tigress)

body.text: sarvasattveṣvakāraṇaparamavatsalasvabhāvaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaḥ pūrvajanmasvapi sa bhagavāniti buddhe bhagavati paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ // tadyathānuśrūyate - ratnatrayagurubhiḥ pratipattiguṇābhirādhitagurubhirguṇapravicayagurubhirasmadgurubhiḥ parikīrtyamānamidaṃ bhagavataḥ pūrvajanmāvadānam /
body.translated_text: That the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), even in his former births, was by nature supremely tender toward all beings without cause, being the very self of all creatures — in this, the highest faith should be placed in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. As is traditionally heard — this tale of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s former birth is recounted by our teachers, who revere the Three Jewels, who have won veneration through the virtues of their practice, and who are weighty in their discernment of qualities:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavānbhūtaḥ pratijñātiśayasadṛśairdānapriyavacanārthacaryāprabhṛtibhiḥ prajñāparigrahaniravadyaiḥ kārūṇyanisyandairlokamanugṛhṇan svadharmābhiratyupanataśucivṛttinyuditodite mahati brāhmaṇakule janmaparigrahaṃ cakāra / sa kṛtasaṃskārakramo jātakarmādibhirabhivardhamānaḥ
body.translated_text: This <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is said, was [formerly] a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, through acts of generosity, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and the like — all impeccable through the embrace of wisdom — streaming forth from compassion, befitting his extraordinary vows, was benefiting the world. He took birth in a great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family of pure and lofty conduct, naturally devoted to its own <s>dharma</s>. Having undergone the prescribed rites of passage beginning with the birth ceremony, growing up,

body.text: prakṛtimedhāvitvātsānāthyaviśeṣājjñānakautūhalādakausīdyācca nacireṇaivāṣṭādaśasu vidyāsthāneṣu svakulakramāviruddhāsu ca sakalāsu kalāsvācāryakaṃ padamavāpa /
body.translated_text: due to his innate intelligence, the special distinction of being without a master, his eagerness for knowledge, and his diligence, he attained the rank of teacher in all eighteen branches of learning and in all the arts not inconsistent with his family tradition, in no long time.

children.text: sa brahmavad brahmavidāṃ babhūva rājeva rājñāṃ bahumānapātram /
children.translated_text: He became, among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, like <s>Brahmā</s> himself; among kings, an object of great honor, like a king;

children.text: sākṣātsahasrākṣa iva prajānāṃ jñānārthināmarthacaraḥ piteva // Jm_1.5 //
children.translated_text: among the people, like <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (<s>Indra</s>, the thousand-eyed) in person; and to those seeking knowledge, a benefactor, like a father. || Jm 1.5 ||

body.text: tasya bhāgyaguṇātiśayasamāvarjito mahāṃ llābhasatkārayaśoviśeṣaḥ prādurabhūt / dharmābhyāsabhāvitamatiḥ kṛtapravrajyāparicayastu bodhisattvo na tenābhireme /
body.translated_text: A great and exceptional distinction of gain, honor, and fame appeared for him, drawn by the excellence of his merit and virtues. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whose mind was refined through the practice of <s>Dharma</s> and who was familiar with the path of renunciation, took no delight in it.

children.text: sa pūrvacaryāpariśuddhabuddhiḥ kāmeṣu dṛṣṭvā bahudoṣajātam /
children.translated_text: He, whose understanding was purified by his former practices, seeing the great mass of faults in sensual pleasures,

children.text: gārhasthyamasvāsthyamivāvadhūya kaṃcidvanaprasthamalaṃcakāra // Jm_1.6 //
children.translated_text: shaking off the householder's life as if it were an illness, adorned a certain forest hermitage. || Jm 1.6 ||

children.text: sa tatra niḥsaṅgatayā tayā (ca) prajñāvadātena śamena caiva /
children.translated_text: There, through that very detachment, and through tranquility bright with wisdom,

children.text: pratyādideśeva kukāryasaṅgādviśliṣṭaśiṣṭopaśamaṃ nṛlokam // Jm_1.7 //
children.translated_text: he seemed to instruct the world of men — estranged from the calm composure of the virtuous — to turn away from association with evil deeds. || Jm 1.7 ||

children.text: maitrīmayeṇa praśamena tasya visyandinevānuparītacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their minds pervaded, as if overflowing, by his tranquility imbued with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),

children.text: parasparadrohanivṛttabhāvāstapasvivad vyālamṛgā viceruḥ // Jm_1.8 //
children.translated_text: the wild beasts moved about having abandoned the tendency for mutual hostility, as if they too were ascetics. || Jm 1.8 ||

children.text: ācāraśuddhyā nibhṛtendriyatvātsaṃtoṣayogātkaruṇāguṇācca /
children.translated_text: Through purity of conduct, through restraint of the senses, through the practice of contentment, and through the virtue of compassion,

children.text: asaṃstutasyāpi janasya loke so 'bhūt priyastasya yathaiva lokaḥ // Jm_1.9 //
children.translated_text: he became dear even to people who had never met him, just as the world was dear to him. || Jm 1.9 ||

children.text: alpecchabhāvātkuhanānabhijñastyaktaspṛho lābhayaśaḥsukheṣu /
children.translated_text: Through his nature of desiring little, ignorant of hypocrisy, having abandoned craving for gain, fame, and pleasure,

children.text: sa devatānāmapi mānasāni prasādabhaktipravaṇāni cakre // Jm_1.10 //
children.translated_text: he made even the minds of the gods incline toward serene devotion. || Jm 1.10 ||

body.text: śrutvātha taṃ pravrajitaṃ manuṣyā guṇaistadīyairavabaddhacittāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, hearing that he had renounced, people whose hearts were captivated by his virtues,

body.text: vihāya bandhūṃśca parigrahāṃśca tacchiṣyatāṃ siddhimivopajagmuḥ // Jm_1.11 //
body.translated_text: abandoning their kinsmen and possessions, came to his discipleship as if attaining perfection. || Jm 1.11 ||

children.text: śīle śucāvindriyabhāvanāyāṃ smṛtyapramoṣe praviviktatāyām /
children.translated_text: In moral conduct and purity, in the cultivation of the senses, in unfailing mindfulness, in the practice of solitude,

children.text: maitryādike caiva manaḥsamādhau yathābalaṃ so 'nuśaśāsa śiṣyān // Jm_1.12 //
children.translated_text: in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the other [<s>brahmavihāras</s>], and in mental concentration, he instructed his disciples according to their capacity. || Jm 1.12 ||

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahātmā pariniṣpannabhūyiṣṭhe pṛthūbhūte śiṣyagaṇe pratiṣṭhāpite 'sminkalyāṇe vartmanyavatārite naiṣkramyasatpathaṃ loke saṃvṛteṣvivāpāyadvāreṣu rājamārgīkṛteṣviva sugatimārgeṣu dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārārthaṃ tatkālaśiṣyeṇājitenānugamyamāno yogānukūlān parvatadarīnikuñjānanuvicacāra /
body.translated_text: Then, one day, that great-souled one — when the group of disciples had mostly completed [their training], had grown large, had been established on this auspicious path, had been led onto the right path of renunciation, when the gates to the lower realms had been, as it were, closed for the world, and the paths to happy destinies had been made, as it were, into royal highways — accompanied by his disciple <s>Ajita</s> at that time, wandered among mountain caves and forest groves suitable for meditation, for the purpose of the bliss of abiding in the <s>Dharma</s> in this very life.

children.text: athātra vyāghravanitāṃ dadarśa girigahvare /
children.translated_text: And there he saw a tigress in a mountain cavern,

children.text: prasūtikleśadoṣeṇa gatāṃ nispandamandatām // Jm_1.13 //
children.translated_text: who had gone to a state of motionless torpor due to the exhaustion of giving birth. || Jm 1.13 ||

children.text: parikṣāmekṣaṇayugāṃ kṣudhā chātatarodarīm /
children.translated_text: Her pair of eyes emaciated, her belly hollowed out by hunger,

children.text: āhāramiva paśyantīṃ bālānsvatanayānapi // Jm_1.14 //
children.translated_text: she was looking at her own cubs as if they were food. || Jm 1.14 ||

children.text: stanyatarṣādupasṛtānmātṛvisrambhanirvyathān /
children.translated_text: The cubs, approaching out of thirst for milk, unsuspecting due to trust in their mother,

children.text: rorūyitaravaiḥ krūrairbhartsayantīṃ parāniva // Jm_1.15 //
children.translated_text: she was driving away with cruel growls, as if they were strangers. || Jm 1.15 ||

children.text: bodhisattvastu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhīro 'pi karuṇāvaśāt /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon seeing her, though steadfast, through the power of compassion,

children.text: cakampe paraduḥkhena mahīkampādivādrirāṭ // Jm_1.16 //
children.translated_text: trembled at another's suffering, like a king of mountains at an earthquake. || Jm 1.16 ||

children.text: mahatsvapi svaduḥkheṣu vyaktadhairyāḥ kṛpātmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of compassionate nature, even when displaying firmness in their own great sufferings,

children.text: mṛdunāpyanyaduḥkhena kampante yattadadbhutam // Jm_1.17 //
children.translated_text: tremble even at the slightest suffering of others — and that is truly wonderful. || Jm 1.17 ||

body.text: atha sa bodhisattvaḥ sasaṃbhramāmreḍitapadaṃ svabhāvātiśayavyañjakaṃ karuṇābalasamāhitākṣaraṃ śiṣyamuvāca - vatsa vatsa
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with words repeated in agitation, indicative of his extraordinary nature, with syllables composed by the force of compassion, spoke to his disciple: 'Dear child, dear child,

children.text: paśya saṃsāranairguṇyaṃ mṛgyeṣā svasutānapi /
children.translated_text: behold the wretchedness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence): this beast, even toward her own cubs,

children.text: laṅghitasnehamaryādā bhoktumanvicchati kṣudhā // Jm_1.18 //
children.translated_text: transgressing the boundaries of maternal love, desires to devour them out of hunger. || Jm 1.18 ||

children.text: aho batātikaṣṭeyamātmasnehasya rodratā /
children.translated_text: Alas, how terrible is this ferocity born of self-love,

children.text: yena mātāpi tanayānāhārayitumicchati // Jm_1.19 //
children.translated_text: by which even a mother desires to make food of her children! || Jm 1.19 ||

children.text: ātmasnehamayaṃ śatruṃ ko vardhayitumahati /
children.translated_text: Who would be capable of nourishing this enemy made of self-love,

children.text: yena kuryāt padanyāsamīdṛśeṣvapi karmasu // Jm_1.20 //
children.translated_text: by which one would take steps even toward such deeds as these? || Jm 1.20 ||

body.text: tacchīghramanviṣyatāṃ tāvatkutaścidasyāḥ kṣudduḥkhapratīkāraheturyāvanna tanayānātmānaṃ copahanti / ahamapi caināṃ prayatiṣye sāhasādasmānnivārayitum / sa tathetyasmai pratiśrutya prakrāntastadāhārānveṣaṇaparo babhūva / atha bodhisattvastaṃ śiṣyaṃ savyapadeśamativāhya cintāmāpede -
body.translated_text: Therefore, quickly let something be sought from somewhere as a remedy for her suffering from hunger, before she destroys her cubs and herself. And I too shall endeavor to restrain her from this violence.' He, having promised 'So be it,' set out, devoted to searching for food for her. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having sent that disciple away with a pretext, entered into reflection:

children.text: saṃvidyamāne sakale śarīre kasmātparasmānmṛgayāmi māṃsam /
children.translated_text: 'When this whole body of mine is at hand, why should I seek flesh from another?

children.text: yādṛcchikī tasya hi lābhasaṃpat kāryātyayaḥ syācca tathā mamāyam // Jm_1.21 //
children.translated_text: For obtaining that from another would be a matter of chance, and meanwhile my purpose here would be defeated. || Jm 1.21 ||

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nirātmake bhedini sārahīne duḥkhe kṛtadhne satatāśucau ca /
children.translated_text: In this body — selfless, subject to disintegration, devoid of essence, full of suffering, ungrateful, and perpetually impure —

children.text: dehe parasmāyupayujyamāne na prītimānyo na vicakṣaṇaḥ saḥ // Jm_1.22 //
children.translated_text: one who takes pleasure when it is being used for the benefit of another, he is neither wise nor discerning. || Jm 1.22 ||

children.text: svasaukhyasaṅgena parasya duḥkhamupekṣyate śaktiparikṣayādvā /
children.translated_text: One ignores the suffering of others out of attachment to one's own comfort or due to exhaustion of one's power;

children.text: na cānyaduḥkhe sati me 'sti saukhyaṃ satyāṃ ca śaktau kimupekṣakaḥ syām // Jm_1.23 //
children.translated_text: but when another's suffering exists, there is no comfort for me, and since I have the power, how could I be indifferent? || Jm 1.23 ||

children.text: satyāṃ ca śaktau mama yadyupekṣā syādātatāyinyapi duḥkhamagne /
children.translated_text: And if, having the power, I were to be indifferent to one engulfed in suffering, as if attacked by a murderer,

children.text: kṛtveva pāpaṃ mama tena cittaṃ dahyeta kakṣaṃ mahatāgnineva // Jm_1.24 //
children.translated_text: my mind would burn as if I had committed a sin, like dry grass consumed by a great fire. || Jm 1.24 ||

children.text: tasmātkariṣyāmi śarīrakeṇa taṭaprapātodgatajīvitena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, with this body, whose life rises up like a cliff-edge ready to fall,

children.text: saṃrakṣaṇaṃ putravadhācca mṛgyā mṛgyāḥ sakāśācca tadātmajānām // Jm_1.25 //
children.translated_text: I shall protect the tigress from the slaughter of her cubs, and her cubs from the tigress.' || Jm 1.25 ||

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ -
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: sadarśanaṃ lokahitotsukānāmuttejanaṃ mandaparākramāṇām /
children.translated_text: '[This deed shall be] a demonstration for those eager for the welfare of the world, an encouragement for those of feeble effort,

children.text: saṃharṣaṇaṃ tyāgaviśāradānāmākarṣaṇaṃ sajjanamānasānām // Jm_1.26 //
children.translated_text: a delight for those skilled in generosity, an attraction for the minds of the virtuous; || Jm 1.26 ||

children.text: viṣādanaṃ māramahācamūnāṃ prasādanaṃ buddhaguṇapriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: a source of dejection for the great armies of <s>Māra</s>, a source of joy for those who love the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: vrīḍodayaṃsvārthaparāyaṇānāṃ mātsaryalobhopahatātmanāṃ ca // Jm_1.27 //
children.translated_text: an occasion for shame in those devoted solely to their own interests and in those whose minds are afflicted by jealousy and greed; || Jm 1.27 ||

children.text: śraddhāpanaṃ yānavarāśritānāṃ vismāpanaṃ tyāgakṛtasmayānām /
children.translated_text: an inspiration of faith for those who have taken refuge in the supreme vehicle, a source of wonder for those who take pride in their generosity,

children.text: viśodhanaṃ svargamahāpathasya tyāgapriyāṇāmanumodi nṝṇām // Jm_1.28 //
children.translated_text: a purification of the great highway to heaven, and a cause of rejoicing for people who delight in generosity. || Jm 1.28 ||

children.text: kadā nu gātrairapi nāma kuryāṃ hitaṃ pareṣāmiti yaśca me 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: That wish of mine — "When shall I be able to benefit others even with my limbs?" —

children.text: manorathastatsaphalīkriyāṃ ca saṃbodhimagryāmapi cāvidūre // Jm_1.29 //
children.translated_text: let that be fulfilled, and may supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment) also be near!' || Jm 1.29 ||

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: na spardhayā naiva yaśo 'bhilāṣānna svargalābhānna ca rājyahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not out of rivalry, not from desire for fame, not for the attainment of heaven, not for the sake of kingship,

children.text: nātyantike 'pyātmasukhe yathāyaṃ mamādaro 'nyatra parārthasiddheḥ // Jm_1.30 //
children.translated_text: not even for ultimate personal happiness — my devotion lies nowhere else than in the accomplishment of others' welfare. || Jm 1.30 ||

children.text: tathā mamānena samānakālaṃ lokasya duḥkhaṃ ca sukhodayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And may I always have the power, simultaneously with this [body of mine], to remove the suffering of the world and to bring about its happiness,

children.text: hartuṃ ca kartuṃ ca sadāstu śaktistamaḥ prakāśaṃ ca yathaiva bhānoḥ // Jm_1.31 //
children.translated_text: just as the sun [has the power] to dispel darkness and create light.' || Jm 1.31 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭe guṇe 'nusmṛtimāgato vā spaṣṭaḥ kathāyogamupāgato vā /
children.translated_text: 'Whether having come to recollection upon seeing virtue, or having clearly entered the occasion of a story,

children.text: sarvaprakāraṃ jagato hitāni kuryāmajasraṃ sukhasaṃhitāni // Jm_1.32 //
children.translated_text: may I always bring about the welfare of the world in every way, accompanied by happiness.' || Jm 1.32 ||

children.text: evaṃ sa niścitya parārthasiddhyai prāṇātyaye 'pyāpatitapramodaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, filled with joy at relinquishing his life for the benefit of others,

children.text: manāṃsi dhīrāṇyapi devatānāṃ vismāpayansvāṃ tanumutsasarja // Jm_1.33 //
children.translated_text: astonishing even the steadfast minds of the gods, he cast down his own body. || Jm 1.33 ||

body.text: atha sā vyāghrī tena bodhisattvasya śarīranipātaśabdena samutthāpitakautūhalāmarṣā viramya svatanayavaiśasodyamāttato nayane vicikṣepa / dṛṣṭai va ca bodhisattvaśarīramudgataprāṇaṃ sahasābhisṛtya bhakṣayitumupacakrame / atha sa tasya śiṣyo māṃsamanāsādyaiva pratinivṛttaḥ kutropādhyāya iti vilokayaṃstadbodhisattvaśarīramudgataprāṇaṃ tayā vyāghrayuvatyā bhakṣyamāṇaṃ dardaśa / sa
body.translated_text: Then that tigress, her curiosity and anger aroused by the sound of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body falling, desisting from her effort to devour her own cubs, cast her eyes in that direction. And having seen the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with its life departed, she rushed to it at once and began to devour it. Then that disciple of his, having failed to find any meat, returned, and looking about — 'Where is the teacher?' — he saw that body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, its life departed, being eaten by that young tigress. He,

body.text: tatkarmātiśayavismayātprativyūḍhaśokaduḥkhāvegastadguṇāśrayabahumānamivodgirannidamātmagataṃ bruvāṇaḥ śobheta /
body.translated_text: his grief and pain displaced by astonishment at the extraordinary nature of that deed, as though pouring forth his admiration founded upon the virtues of his teacher, speaking thus within himself, would have appeared radiant:

children.text: aho dayāsya vyasanāture jane svasaukhyanaiḥsaṅgyamaho mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, his compassion for people afflicted by misfortune! Oh, his indifference to personal happiness! Oh, the greatness of his soul!

children.text: aho prakarṣaṃ gamitā sthitiḥ satāmaho pareṣāṃ mṛditā yaśaḥśriyaḥ // Jm_1.34 //
children.translated_text: Oh, the standard of the virtuous has been raised to its highest! Oh, the glories of fame of others have been crushed!' || Jm 1.34 ||

children.text: aho parākrāntamapetasādhvasaṃ guṇāśrayaṃ prema paraṃ pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, the valor displayed — fearless, a repository of virtue — the supreme love demonstrated!

children.text: aho namaskāraviśeṣapātratāṃ prasahya nītāsya guṇātanustanuḥ // Jm_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Oh, this body of his, a mass of virtues, has forcibly attained the status of being a supreme object of homage!' || Jm 1.35 ||

children.text: nisargasaumyasya vasuṃdharādhṛteraho pareṣāṃ vyasaneṣvamarṣitā /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, his impatience at the misfortunes of others — he who was gentle by nature and steadfast as the earth!

children.text: aho madīyā gamitā prakāśatāṃ khaṭuṅkatā vikramasaṃpadānayā // Jm_1.36 //
children.translated_text: Oh, my own unworthiness has been brought to light by the splendor of his heroic deed!' || Jm 1.36 ||

children.text: anena nāthena sanāthatāṃ gataṃ na śocitavyaṃ khalu sāṃprataṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: 'By this protector, the world has become protected — truly, the world should not be grieved for now;

children.text: parājayāśaṅkitajātasaṃbhramo dhruvaṃ viniścāsaparo 'dya manmathaḥ // Jm_1.37 //
children.translated_text: surely <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), seized with alarm at the fear of defeat, is today intent upon fleeing.' || Jm 1.37 ||

body.text: sarvathā namo 'stvasmai mahābhāgāya sarvabhūtaśaraṇyāyātivipulakāruṇyāyāprameyasattvāya bhūtārthabodhisattvāya mahāsattvāyeti / atha sa tamarthaṃ sabrahmacāribhyo nivedayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: 'In every way, homage to this most fortunate one, the refuge of all beings, of supremely vast compassion, of immeasurable being, a true <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being!' And then he reported that matter to his fellow <s>brahmacārins</s> (spiritual companions).

children.text: tatkarmavismitamukhairatha tasya śiṣyairgandharvayakṣabhujagaistridaśādhipaiśca /
children.translated_text: Then, by his disciples, their faces filled with wonder at that deed, and by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and lords of the gods,

children.text: mālyāmbarābharaṇacandanacūrṇavarṣaiśchannā tadasthivasudhā vasudhā babhūva // Jm_1.38 //
children.translated_text: showers of garlands, garments, ornaments, and sandalwood powder were rained down, and that piece of earth where his bones lay became a [sacred] ground. || Jm 1.38 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ sarvasattveṣvakāraṇaparamavatsalasvabhāvaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaḥ pūrvajanmasvapi sa bhagavāniti buddhe bhagavati paraḥ prasādaḥ kāryaḥ / jātaprasādaiśca buddhe bhagavati parā prītirutpādayitavyā / evamāyatanagato naḥ prasāda ityevamapyunneyam / tathā satkṛtya dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / evaṃ duṣkaraśatasamudānītatvāt karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyamevaṃ svabhāvātiśayasya niṣpādikā parānugrahapravṛttihetuḥ karuṇeti /
body.translated_text: Thus, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> was by nature supremely tender toward all beings without cause, being the very self of all creatures, even in his former births — in this, the highest faith should be placed in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And by those in whom faith has arisen, the highest love should be generated toward the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. 'Our faith has indeed found its proper object' — this too should be inferred. Likewise, the <s>Dharma</s> should be heard with due reverence. Since [this <s>Dharma</s>] has been accomplished through hundreds of difficult deeds, even in describing compassion, this should be stated: 'Compassion, which is the cause of the inclination to benefit others, is the producer of such extraordinary nature.'

body.text: iti vyāghrījātakaṃ prathamam
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Vyāghrī-jātaka</s> (Story of the Tigress), the first.

body.text: 2. Śibijātakam
body.translated_text: 2. The <s>Śibi-jātaka</s> (The Story of <s>Śibi</s>)

body.text: duṣkaraśatasamudānīto 'yamasmadarthaṃ tena bhagavatā saddharma iti satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate-
body.translated_text: This holy <s>Dharma</s>, accomplished by the <s>Bhagavān</s> through hundreds of difficult deeds for our sake, should be heard with due reverence. As is traditionally heard —

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavānaparimitakālābhyāsātsātmībhūtopacitapuṇyakarmā kadācicchibīnāṃ rājā babhūva / sa bālyātprabhṛtyeva bṛddhopāsanaratirvinayānurakto 'nuraktaprakṛtiḥ prakṛtimedhāvitvādanekavidyādhigamavipulataramatirutsāhamaṃtraprabhāva[prabhutva]śaktidaivasaṃpannaḥ svā iva prajāḥ prajāḥ pālayati sma /
body.translated_text: This <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having accumulated meritorious deeds that had become second nature through practice over an immeasurable span of time, once became king of the <s>Śibis</s>. From childhood itself he delighted in attending upon elders, was devoted to discipline, had subjects who were devoted to him, and owing to his natural intelligence his understanding had grown vast through mastery of numerous sciences; endowed with energy, counsel, the power of authority, and divine fortune, he protected his subjects as if they were his own children.

children.text: tasmiṃstrivargānuguṇā guṇaughāḥ saṃharṣayogādiva saṃniviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: In him, hosts of virtues conducive to the triple aim of life had assembled as if from the joy of being united together,

children.text: samastarūpā vibabhurna cāsurvirodhasaṃkṣobhavipannaśobhāḥ // Jm_2.1 //
children.translated_text: And shone forth in their complete form, their splendor undimmed by the agitation of mutual conflict.

children.text: viḍambanevāvinayoddhatānāṃ durmedhasāmāpadivātikaṣṭā /
children.translated_text: As if to mock the ill-mannered and arrogant, as if an extreme misfortune upon the dull-witted,

children.text: alpātmanāṃ yā madireva lakṣmīrbabhūva sā tatra yathārthanāmā // Jm_2.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Royal Fortune), who is like an intoxicant for the small-souled, became in his case true to her name.

children.text: udārabhāvātkaruṇāguṇācca vittādhipatyācca sa rājavaryaḥ /
children.translated_text: That best of kings, through his noble nature, his quality of compassion, and his lordship over wealth,

children.text: reme 'rthināmīpsitasiddhiharṣādakliṣṭaśobhāni mukhāni paśyan // Jm_2.3 //
children.translated_text: Took delight in beholding the faces of supplicants — radiant with the joy of having their desires fulfilled — faces whose beauty was effortless.

body.text: atha sa rājā dānapriyatvātsamantato nagarasya sarvopakaraṇadhanadhānyasamṛddhā dānaśālāḥ kārayitvā svamāhātmyānurūpaṃ yathābhiprāyasaṃpāditaṃ sopacāraṃ manoharamanatikrāntakālasubhagaṃ dānavarṣaṃ kṛtayugamegha iva vavarṣa / annamannārthibhyaḥ, pānaṃ pānārthibhyaḥ, śayanāsanavasanabhojanagandhamātyarajatasuvarṇādikaṃ tattadarthibhyaḥ / atha tasya rājñaḥ pradānaudāryaśravaṇādvismitapramuditahṛdayā nānādigabhilakṣitadeśanivāsinaḥ puruṣāstaṃ deśamupajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that king, out of his love for giving, had gift-halls built on all sides of the city, abundantly furnished with every provision, wealth, and grain, and in a manner befitting his own greatness, he rained down a shower of gifts — bestowed exactly as wished, accompanied by courteous attentions, captivating, and graced with perfect timeliness — like a cloud of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age). Food to those seeking food, drink to those seeking drink, beds, seats, garments, meals, perfumes, jewels, silver, gold, and such to those seeking each of these respectively. Then, upon hearing of that king's magnificent liberality, men dwelling in lands situated in various directions, their hearts struck with wonder and delight, came to that country.

children.text: parītya kṛtsnaṃ manasā nṛlokamanyeṣvalabdhapraṇayāvakāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ranged over the entire world of men in their minds, and finding no opening for affection elsewhere,

children.text: tamarthinaḥ prītamukhāḥ samīyurmahāhradaṃ vanyagajā yathaiva // Jm_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Those supplicants approached him with joyful faces, just as wild elephants approach a great lake.

body.text: atha sa rājā samantataḥ samāpatato lābhāśāpramuditamanasaḥ pathikajananepathyapracchāditaśobhasya vanīpakajanasya
body.translated_text: Then that king, as traders — whose splendor was concealed beneath the travel-worn garb of wayfarers — came flocking from every direction, their minds elated with the hope of gain,

children.text: viproṣitasyeva suhṛjjanasya saṃdarśanātprītivijṛmbhitākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: His eyes widening with delight at the sight of them as if they were long-absent friends,

children.text: yācñāṃ priyākhyānamivābhyanandaddattvā ca tuṣṭayārthijanaṃ jigāya // Jm_2.5 //
children.translated_text: He welcomed their requests as if they were tidings from a beloved, and by giving, he conquered the hearts of the supplicants with his generosity.

children.text: dānodbhavaḥ kīrtimayaḥ sugandhastasyārthināṃ vāganilaprakīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fragrance born of his giving, composed of fame, scattered by the wind of supplicants' words,

children.text: madaṃ jahārānyanarādhipānāṃ gandhadvipasyeva paradvipānām // Jm_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Drove away the pride of other kings, just as the scent of a rutting elephant drives away rival elephants.

body.text: atha kadācitsa rājā dānaśālāḥ samanuvicaraṃstṛptatvādarthijanasya praviralaṃ yācakajanasaṃpātamabhisamīkṣya dānadharmasyānutsarpaṇānna tuṣṭimupajagāma /
body.translated_text: Then once, that king, while inspecting the gift-halls, noticed that the flow of petitioners had become sparse because the supplicants were satisfied, and he found no contentment, since the practice of generous giving was not advancing.

children.text: tarṣa vininye 'rthijanastametya na tvarthinaḥ prāpya sa dānaśauṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: The supplicants quenched their thirst upon reaching him, but he, intoxicated with giving, found no satisfaction upon encountering supplicants,

children.text: na hyasya dānavyavasāyamarthī yācñāpramāṇena śaśāka jetum // Jm_2.7 //
children.translated_text: For no petitioner could match his resolve for generosity merely by the measure of his request.

body.text: tasya buddhirabhavat - atisabhāgyāste satpuruṣaviśeṣā ye visrambhaniryantraṇapraṇayamarthibhiḥ svagātrāṇyapi yācyante / mama punaḥ pratyākhyānarūkṣākṣaravacanasaṃtarjita ivārthijano dhanamātrake 'pragalbhapraṇayaḥ saṃvṛtta iti /
body.translated_text: This thought arose in him: "How supremely fortunate are those extraordinary virtuous beings whom supplicants ask even for their own limbs, with affection that is trusting and unreserved! But in my case, the supplicant folk, as if intimidated by the harsh syllables of refusal, have become timid in their affection, asking only for mere wealth."

children.text: atha kṣitīśasya tamatyudāraṃ gātreṣvapi sveṣu nivṛttasaṅgam /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving that exceedingly noble thought of the king, whose attachment had ceased even toward his own limbs,

children.text: vijñāya dānāśrayiṇaṃ vitarkaṃ patipriyā strīva mahī cakampe // Jm_2.8 //
children.translated_text: A thought resting upon giving — the Earth trembled, like a wife devoted to her lord.

body.text: atha śakro devendraḥ kṣititalacalanādakampite vividharatnaprabhodbhāsini sumerau parvatarāje kimidamiti samutpatitavitarkastasya rājña imaṃ vitarkātiśayaṃ dharaṇītalacalananimittamavetya vismayāvarjitahṛdayaścintāmāpede /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, when <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains — resplendent with the radiance of various gems — was shaken by the trembling of the earth's surface, started up with the thought "What is this?" and upon learning that this extraordinary resolve of the king was the cause of the earth's trembling, he was seized with wonder in his heart and fell to thinking.

children.text: dānātiharṣoddhatamānasena vitarkitaṃ kiṃ svididaṃ nṛpeṇa /
children.translated_text: "What is this that has been conceived by the king, whose mind is elated with the excessive joy of giving,

children.text: ābadhya dānavyavasāyakakṣyāṃ svagātradānasthiraniścayena // Jm_2.9 //
children.translated_text: Who has girded on the belt of resolve for giving, with a firm determination to give away his own body?"

body.text: tanmīmāṃsiṣye tāvadenamiti / atha tasya rājñaḥ paṣaṃdi niṣaṇṇasyāmātyagaṇaparivṛtasya samucitāyāṃ kṛtāyāmarthijanasya kaḥ kimicchatītyāhvānāvaghoṣaṇāyāmuddhāṭyamāneṣu kośādhyakṣādhisthiteṣu
body.translated_text: "I shall therefore put him to the test." Then, as that king was seated in his audience hall, surrounded by his circle of ministers, and when the customary proclamation had been made inviting supplicants — "Who desires what?" — and when heaps of gems, gold, silver, and wealth, presided over by the superintendent of the treasury, were being opened up, and when

body.text: maṇikanakarajatadhananicayeṣu viśleṣyamāṇāsu puṭāsu vividhavasanaparipūrṇagarbhāsu samupāvartyamāneṣu vinītavividhavāhanaskandhapratiṣṭhitayugeṣu vicitreṣu yānaviśeṣeṣu pravṛttasaṃpāte 'rthijane śakro devānāmindro vṛddhamandhaṃ brāhmaṇarūpamabhinirmāya rājñaścakṣuḥpathe prādurabhavat / atha tasya rājñaḥ kārūṇyamaitrīparibhāvitayā dhīraprasannasaumyayā pratyudgata iva pariṣvakta iva ca dṛṣṭyā kenārtha ityupanimantryamāṇaḥ kṣitipānucarairnṛpatisamopamupetya jayāśīrvacanapuraḥsaraṃ rājānamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: bundles filled with garments of every kind were being unwrapped, and when various splendid vehicles, fitted with yokes mounted on well-trained draft animals of various kinds, were being brought forward, and when supplicants had begun to arrive, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, fashioned the form of an old blind <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and appeared within the king's sight. Then, as that king's gaze — suffused with compassion and loving-kindness, steady, serene, and gentle — came forth to meet and, as it were, to embrace him, and as he was being invited by the king's attendants with the words "What do you need?", the Brāhmaṇa approached the king and, preceded by words of benediction for victory, addressed him thus:

children.text: dūrādapaśyansthaviro 'bhyupetastvaccakṣuṣo 'rthī kṣitipapradhāna /
children.translated_text: "An old man who cannot see from afar has come to you, O foremost of kings, desiring your eye.

children.text: ekekṣaṇenāpi hi paṅkajākṣa gamyeta lokādhipa lokayātrā // Jm_2.10 //
children.translated_text: For even with a single eye, O lotus-eyed lord of the earth, one could manage the journey of life."

body.text: atha sa bodhisattvaḥ samamilaṣitamanorathaprasiddhyā paraṃ prītyutsavamanubhavan kisvididaṃ satyamevoktaṃ brāhmaṇena syāduta vikalpābhyāsānmayaivamavadhāritamiti jātavimarśaścakṣuryācñāpriyavacanaśravaṇatṛṣitamatistaṃ cakṣuryācanakamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, experiencing the supreme festival of joy at the fulfillment of his long-cherished desire, and wondering "Can this really be true, what the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has said, or have I determined it thus through habitual imagining?" — his mind now filled with deliberation and thirsting to hear the beloved words of a request for his eyes — spoke to that seeker of eyes:

children.text: kenānuśiṣṭastvamihābhyupeto māṃ yācituṃ brāhmaṇamukhya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Instructed by whom have you come here to ask me for an eye, O chief among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>?

children.text: sudustyajaṃ cakṣuriti pravādaḥ saṃbhāvanā kasya mayi vyatītā // Jm_2.11 //
children.translated_text: The saying goes that the eye is exceedingly hard to relinquish — whose esteem for me has gone so far?"

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaveṣadhārī śakro devendrastasya rājña āśayaṃ viditvovāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, wearing the guise of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having discerned the king's inner disposition, spoke:

children.text: śakrasya śakrapratimānuśiṣṭyā tvāṃ yācituṃ cakṣurihātago 'smi /
children.translated_text: "By the instruction of <s>Śakra</s>, comparable to <s>Śakra</s> himself, I have come here to ask you for an eye.

children.text: saṃbhāvanāṃ tasya mamaiva cāśāṃ cakṣuḥpradānātsaphalīkuruṣva // Jm_2.12 //
children.translated_text: Fulfill his esteem and my hope by the gift of an eye."

body.text: atha sa rājā śakrasaṃkīrtanānnunamasya brāhmaṇasya bhavitrī devatānubhāvādanena vidhinā cakṣuḥsaṃpaditi matvā pramodaviśadākṣaramenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, upon hearing the mention of <s>Śakra</s>, thinking "Surely this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will attain his eyes through the power of the deity by this very means," spoke to him in words bright with joy:

children.text: yenābhyupeto 'si manorathena tameṣa te brāhmaṇa pūrayāmi /
children.translated_text: "The desire with which you have come, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall now fulfill for you.

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇāya madekamakṣi dadāmi cakṣurdvayamapyahaṃ te // Jm_2.13 //
children.translated_text: Though you wish for only one of my eyes, I give you both eyes."

body.text: sa tvaṃ vibuddhanayanotpalaśobhitāsyaḥ saṃpaśyato vraja yathābhimataṃ janasya /
body.translated_text: "Go then, your face adorned with eyes like blossoming blue lotuses, as you please, before the gaze of the people,

body.text: syāt kiṃ nu so 'yamuta neti vicāradolālolasya so 'yamiti cotthitavismayasya // Jm_2.14 //
body.translated_text: Who will be tossed on the swing of doubt — 'Is it he or is it not?' — and then filled with risen wonder, 'It is indeed he!'"

body.text: atha tasya rājño 'mātyāścakṣuḥpradānāvasāyamavetya sasaṃbhramāvegaviṣādavyathitamanaso rājānamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the king's ministers, perceiving his resolve to give away his eyes, their minds agitated with alarm, dismay, and grief, addressed the king:

children.text: dānātiharṣādanayamasamīkṣyāhitodayam /
children.translated_text: "From excessive delight in giving, without examining the harmful consequences that will arise,

children.text: prasīda deva mā maivaṃ na cakṣurdātumarhasi // Jm_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O lord! Do not do this — you should not give away your eyes!"

children.text: ekasyārthe dvijasyāsya mā naḥ sarvānparākṛthāḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the sake of this one <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, do not cast us all aside!

children.text: alaṃ śokāgninā dagdhuṃ sukhaṃ saṃvardhitāḥ prajāḥ // Jm_2.16 //
children.translated_text: Do not burn with the fire of grief your subjects, who have been nurtured in happiness!"

children.text: dhanāni lakṣmīpratibodhanāni śrīmanti ratnāni payasvinīrgāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Give wealth that awakens <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), splendid jewels, milk-giving cows,

children.text: rathān vinītāṃśca yujaḥ prayaccha madorjitaśrīlalitān dvipānvā // Jm_2.17 //
children.translated_text: Chariots, well-trained teams of horses — or elephants, magnificent with the grace of their rutting splendor."

children.text: samuccarannūpuranisvanāni śaratpayodābhyadhikadyutīni /
children.translated_text: "Give mansions with tinkling anklet-sounds rising within, surpassing autumn clouds in brilliance,

children.text: gṛhāṇi sarvartusukhāni dehi mā dāḥ svacakṣurjagadekacakṣuḥ // Jm_2.18 //
children.translated_text: Affording comfort in every season — but do not give your own eye, O you who are the sole eye of the world!"

body.text: vimṛśyatāmapi ca tāvanmahārāja /
body.translated_text: "And let this be considered further, O great king:

children.text: anyadīyaṃ kathaṃ nāma cakṣuranyatra yojyate /
children.translated_text: How can an eye belonging to one person be fitted into another?

children.text: atha devaprabhāvo 'yaṃ tvaccakṣuḥ kimapekṣyate // Jm_2.19 //
children.translated_text: And if this is a divine miracle, why should your eye be required?"

body.text: api ca deva /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O lord:

children.text: cakṣuṣā kiṃ daridrasya parābhyudayasākṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: What use is an eye to a poor man, an eye that merely witnesses the prosperity of others?

children.text: dhanameva yato dehi deva mā sāhasaṃ kṛthāḥ // Jm_2.20 //
children.translated_text: Give wealth instead, O lord — do not act rashly!"

body.text: atha sa rājā tānamātyānsānunayamadhurākṣaramityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king spoke to those ministers in words gentle with affection:

children.text: adāne kurute buddhiṃ dāsyāmītyabhidhāya yaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who, having declared 'I shall give,' then turns his mind to not giving,

children.text: sa lobhapāśaṃ prabhraṣṭamātmani pratimuñcati // Jm_2.21 //
children.translated_text: Fastens upon himself the noose of greed that had slipped away."

children.text: dāsyāmīti pratijñāya yo 'nyathā kurute manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who, having promised 'I shall give,' then thinks otherwise —

children.text: kārpaṇyāniścitamateḥ kaḥ syātpāpatarastataḥ // Jm_2.22 //
children.translated_text: What could be more sinful than one whose resolution is shaken by miserliness?"

children.text: sthirīkṛtyārthināmāśāṃ dāsyāmīti pratijñayā /
children.translated_text: "Having confirmed the hopes of supplicants by the promise 'I shall give,'

children.text: visaṃvādanarūkṣasya vacaso nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ // Jm_2.23 //
children.translated_text: There is no atonement for words made harsh by breaking that promise."

body.text: yadapi ceṣṭaṃ devatānubhāvādeva cakṣurasya kiṃ na saṃbhavatītyatra śrūyatām -
body.translated_text: "And as for what you have argued — that through divine power alone the eye could come to him — hear me on this:

children.text: naikakāraṇasādhyatvaṃ kāryāṇāṃ nanu dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Is it not observed that effects require more than a single cause?

children.text: kāraṇāntarasāpekṣaḥ syāddevo 'pi vidhiryataḥ // Jm_2.24 //
children.translated_text: For even a divine ordinance may depend upon another contributing cause."

body.text: tanna me dānātiśayavyavasāye vidhnāya vyāyantumarhanti bhavanta iti / amātyā ūcuḥ - dhanadhānyaratnāni devo dātumarhati na svacakṣuriti vijñāpitamasmābhiḥ / tanna devaṃ vayamatīrthe pratārayāmaḥ / rājovāca -
body.translated_text: "Therefore you should not strive to obstruct my resolve for this supreme act of giving." The ministers said: "We have only submitted that the lord should give wealth, grain, and jewels, not his own eyes. We would not mislead the lord in an unworthy cause." The king replied:

children.text: yadeva yācyeta tadeva dadyānnānīpsitaṃ prīṇayatīha dattam /
children.translated_text: "One should give precisely what is asked for; a gift of something undesired does not please.

children.text: kimuhyamānasya jalena toyairdāsyāmyataḥ prārthitamarthamasmai // Jm_2.25 //
children.translated_text: What use is water to one drowning in a flood? Therefore I shall give this man what he has requested."

body.text: atha tasya rājño dṛḍhataravisrambhapraṇayaḥ snehāvegādanapekṣitopacāro 'mātyamukhyastaṃ rājānamityuvāca - mā tāvad bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Then the king's chief minister, whose affection had deepened into firmer trust, and who in the rush of emotion dispensed with formalities, addressed the king thus: "Do not, my lord!

children.text: yā nālpena tapaḥsamādhividhinā saṃprāpyate kenacid
children.translated_text: That sovereignty which no one easily attains even by the discipline of austerity and meditation,

children.text: yāmāsādya ca bhūribhirmakhaśataiḥ kīrti divaṃ cāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: And having attained which, one may win fame and heaven through hundreds of great sacrifices —

children.text: saṃprāptāmatipatya tāṃ nṛpatitāṃ śakrarddhivispardhinīṃ
children.translated_text: Passing beyond that kingship, rivaling the splendor of <s>Śakra</s> himself,

children.text: kiṃ dṛṣṭvā nayane praditsati bhavānko 'yaṃ kutastyo vidhiḥ // Jm_2.26 //
children.translated_text: What have you seen that you wish to give away your eyes? What manner of course is this, and whence does it come?"

children.text: labdhāvakāśastridaśeṣu yajñaiḥ kīrtyā samantādavabhāsamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You who have gained a place among the gods through sacrifices, who shine on all sides with fame,

children.text: narendracūḍādyutirañjitāṅghriḥ kiṃ lipsamāno nu dadāsi cakṣuḥ // Jm_2.27 //
children.translated_text: Whose feet are adorned with the lustre of the diadem of kings — desiring what, pray, do you give away your eyes?"

body.text: atha sa rājā tamamātyaṃ sānunayamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king spoke to that minister with gentle affection:

children.text: nāyaṃ yatnaḥ sārvabhaumatvamāptuṃ naiva svargaṃ nāpavargaṃ na kīrtim /
children.translated_text: "This effort is not to attain universal sovereignty, nor heaven, nor liberation, nor fame.

children.text: trātuṃ lokānityayaṃ tvādaro me yācñākleśo mā ca bhūdasya moghaḥ // Jm_2.28 //
children.translated_text: This solicitude of mine is to deliver all beings — and may this man's anguish of supplication not be in vain!"

body.text: atha sa rājā nīlotpaladalaśakalarucirakānti nayanamekaṃ vaidyaparidṛṣṭena vidhinā śanakairakṣatamutpāṭya parayā prītyā cakṣuryācanakāya prāyacchat / atha śakro devendrastādṛśamṛddhyabhisaṃskāraṃ cakre yathā dadarśa sa rājā saparijanastattasya cakṣuścakṣuḥsthāne pratiṣṭhitam / athonmiṣitaikacakṣuṣaṃ cakṣuryācanakamabhivīkṣya sa rājā parameṇa praharṣeṇa samāpūrṇahṛdayo dvitīyamapyasmai nayanaṃ prāyacchat /
body.translated_text: Then that king, gently and without injury, following the procedure prescribed by the physician, extracted one eye — lovely in hue as a petal of a blue lotus — and with supreme joy gave it to the seeker of eyes. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, wrought such a feat of divine transformation that the king and his retinue beheld that eye established in its proper place in the Brāhmaṇa's eye-socket. Then, beholding the seeker of eyes now possessing one open eye, the king, his heart brimming with the highest elation, gave him his second eye as well.

body.text: tataḥ sa rājā nayane pradāya vipadmapadmākaratulyavaktraḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that king, having given away both eyes, his face like a lotus-pool bereft of its lotuses,

body.text: paurairasādhāraṇatuṣṭirāsītsamagracakṣurdadṛśe dvijaiśca // Jm_2.29 //
body.translated_text: Was beheld with eyes full by the citizens and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, who felt an extraordinary, unshared tenderness toward him.

children.text: antaḥpure 'tha manujādhipateḥ pure ca śokāśrubhirvasumatī siṣice samantāt /
children.translated_text: In the inner palace and in the city, the earth was sprinkled on all sides with tears of grief.

children.text: śakrastu vismayamavāpa parāṃ ca tuṣṭiṃ saṃbodhaye nṛpamakampyamatiṃ samīkṣya // Jm_2.30 //
children.translated_text: But <s>Śakra</s> was filled with wonder and the highest satisfaction, seeing the king's unwavering resolve toward <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (perfect enlightenment).

body.text: atha śakrasya vismayāvarjitahṛdayasyaitadabhavat -
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the wonder-struck heart of <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: aho dhṛtiraho sattvamaho sattvahitaiṣitā /
children.translated_text: "Ah, what fortitude! Ah, what courage! Ah, what devotion to the welfare of beings!

children.text: pratyakṣamapi karmedaṃ karotīva vicāraṇām // Jm_2.31 //
children.translated_text: Even though this deed is before one's very eyes, it inspires disbelief."

body.text: tannāyamāścaryasattvaściramimaṃ parikleśamanubhavitumarhati / yataḥ prayatiṣye cakṣurasyopāyapradarśanādutpādayitum / atha tasya rājñaḥ kramātsaṃrūḍhanayanavraṇasyāvagītapratanūbhūtāntaḥpurapaurajānapadaśokasya pravivekakāmatvādudyānapuṣkariṇyāstīre kusumabharāvanatarucirataruvaranicite mṛdusurabhiśiśirasukhapavane madhukaragaṇopakūjite paryaṅkeṇa niṣaṇṇasya śakro devendraḥ purastātprādurabhavat / ka eṣa iti ca rājñā paryanuyukto 'vravīt -
body.translated_text: "Therefore this noble being does not deserve to endure this suffering for so long. Hence I shall endeavor to produce an eye for him by showing him the means." Then, as that king's eye-wound gradually healed, and the grief of his inner court, townspeople, and countryfolk had been lamented and diminished, desiring solitude, he was seated on a couch on the bank of a garden pond — a place adorned with excellent trees bending beautifully under the weight of blossoms, with a soft, fragrant, cool, and pleasant breeze, humming with swarms of bees — when <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, appeared before him. And when asked by the king, "Who is this?" he replied —

body.text: śakro 'hamasmi devendrastvatsamīpamupāgataḥ /
body.translated_text: "I am <s>Śakra</s>, lord of gods, come into your presence."

body.text: rājovāca / svāgatam / ājñāpyatāṃ kenārtha iti / sa upacārapuraḥsaramukto rājānaṃ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: The king said: "Welcome! Command what purpose [brings you]." Thus addressed with due courtesy, he again spoke to the king —

body.text: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva rājarṣe yadicchasi taducyatām // Jm_2.32 //
body.translated_text: "Choose a boon, O royal sage; whatever you desire, let it be spoken." || Jm 2.32 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā pradānasamucitatvādanabhyastayācñākārpaṇyamārgo vidhṛtya vismayaśauṭīryamenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, being accustomed to giving rather than asking, unacquainted with the humiliation of begging, suppressing his wonder and pride, said to him —

children.text: prabhūtaṃ me dhanaṃ śakra śaktimacca mahad balam /
children.translated_text: "My wealth is abundant, O <s>Śakra</s>, and my great power is mighty;

children.text: andhabhāvāttvidānīṃ me mṛtyurevābhirocate // Jm_2.33 //
children.translated_text: but because of my blindness, only death now pleases me." || Jm 2.33 ||

children.text: kṛtvāpi paryāptamanorathāni prītiprasādādhikalocanāni /
children.translated_text: "Having fulfilled desires to satisfaction, the faces of supplicants, with eyes radiant with joy and grace,

children.text: mukhāni paśyāmi na yācakānāṃ yattena mṛtyurdayito mamendra // Jm_2.34 //
children.translated_text: I no longer see — therefore, O <s>Indra</s>, death is dear to me." || Jm 2.34 ||

body.text: śakra uvāca - alamalamanena te vyavasāyena / satpuruṣā evedṛśānyanuprāpnuvanti / api ca pṛcchāmi tāvad bhavantam /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: "Enough, enough of this resolve of yours! Only virtuous persons attain such [states]. Moreover, I ask you this:

body.text: imāmavasthāṃ gamitasya yācakaiḥ kathaṃ nu te saṃprati teṣu mānasam /
body.translated_text: "Having been brought to this condition by supplicants, what now is your disposition toward them?

body.text: pracakṣva tattāvadalaṃ nigūhituṃ vrajeśca saṃpratyapanīya tāṃ yathā // Jm_2.35 //
body.translated_text: Declare that openly — enough of concealment — and proceed now, having set that aside." || Jm 2.35 ||

body.text: rājovāca - ko 'yamasmān vikatthayitumatrabhavato nirbandhaḥ? api ca devendra śrūyatām -
body.translated_text: The king said: "What is this insistence of your honor to make us boast? Moreover, O lord of gods, hear this:

children.text: tadaiva caitarhi ca yācakānāṃ vacāṃsi yācñāniyatākṣarāṇi /
children.translated_text: "Then as now, the words of supplicants, with syllables devoted to petition,

children.text: āśīrmayāṇīva mama priyāṇi yathā tathodetu mamaikamakṣi // Jm_2.36 //
children.translated_text: are dear to me as if they were blessings — so may one eye of mine be restored." || Jm 2.36 ||

body.text: atha tasya rājñaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānabalāt puṇyopacayaviśeṣācca vacanasamanantaramevendranīlaśakalākrāntamadhyamiva nīlotpaladalasadṛśamekaṃ cakṣuḥ prādurabhavat / prādurbhūṃte ca tasminnayanāścarye pramuditamanāḥ sa rājā punarapi śakramuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then, by the power of that king's truthful resolve and by the special accumulation of his merit, immediately upon his words, a single eye appeared — resembling a blue lotus petal, as if a fragment of sapphire had been set in its center. And when that wondrous eye appeared, the king, delighted in mind, again spoke to <s>Śakra</s> —

children.text: yaścāpi māṃ cakṣurayācataikaṃ tasmai mudā dve nayane pradāya /
children.translated_text: "Even to one who begged a single eye from me, I would joyfully give both eyes;

children.text: prītyutsavaikāgramatiryathāsaṃ dvitīyamapyakṣi tathā mamāstu // Jm_2.37 //
children.translated_text: so that I might have my mind wholly absorbed in the festival of joy — may my second eye also [be restored] thus." || Jm 2.37 ||

body.text: athābhivyāhārasamanantarameva tasya rājño vispardhamānamiva tena nayanena dvitīyaṃ cakṣuḥ prādurabhavat /
body.translated_text: Then, immediately upon that utterance, a second eye appeared for that king, as if vying with the first.

children.text: tataścakampe sadharādharā dharā vyatītya velāṃ prasasāra sāgaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thereupon the earth with its mountains trembled, the ocean surged beyond its bounds,

children.text: prasaktagambhīramanojñanisvanāḥ prasasvanurduṃndubhayo divaukasām // Jm_2.38 //
children.translated_text: and the drums of the celestials resounded with deep, pleasing tones. || Jm 2.38 ||

children.text: prasādaramyaṃ dadṛśe vapurdiśāṃ rarāja śuddhyā śaradīva bhāskaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The quarters displayed a beauty radiant with serenity; the sun shone with the purity of autumn;

children.text: paribhramaccandanacūrṇarañjitaṃ papāta citraṃ kusumaṃ nabhastalāt // Jm_2.39 //
children.translated_text: colorful flowers, scented with whirling sandalwood powder, fell from the vault of heaven. || Jm 2.39 ||

children.text: samāyayurvismayaphullalocanā divaukasastatra sahāpsarogaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The celestials arrived there with their eyes wide with wonder, accompanied by troops of <s>Apsaras</s>;

children.text: vavau manojñātmaguṇaḥ samīraṇo manassu harṣo jagatāṃ vyajṛmbhata // Jm_2.40 //
children.translated_text: a breeze blew, endowed with delightful qualities, and joy blossomed in the hearts of all beings. || Jm 2.40 ||

body.text: udīritā harṣaparītamānasairmaharddhibhirbhūṃtagaṇaiḥ savismayaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Uttered by the great powerful spirit-hosts whose minds were filled with delight and wonder,

body.text: nṛpasya karmātiśayastavāśrayāḥ samantataḥ śuśruvire giraḥ śubhāḥ // Jm_2.41 //
body.translated_text: praises extolling the extraordinary deeds of the king were heard from all sides. || Jm 2.41 ||

children.text: aho bataudāryamaho kṛpālutā viśuddhatā paśya yathāsya cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Oh, what generosity! Oh, what compassion! Behold the purity of his mind!

children.text: aho svasaukhyeṣu nirutsukā matirnamo 'stu te 'bhyudgatadhairyavikrama // Jm_2.42 //
children.translated_text: Oh, what indifference to his own pleasures! Homage to you, whose courage and valor are exalted!" || Jm 2.42 ||

children.text: sanāthatāṃ sādhu jagadgataṃ tvayā punarvibuddhekṣaṇapaṅkajaśriyā /
children.translated_text: "The world's affliction has been well relieved by you, whose lotus-beauty of reopened eyes [shines forth];

children.text: amogharūpā bata puṇyasañcayāścirasya dharmeṇa khalūrjitaṃ jitam // Jm_2.43 //
children.translated_text: unfailing indeed are the accumulations of merit — at last, righteousness has truly triumphed!" || Jm 2.43 ||

body.text: atha śakraḥ sādhu sādhvityenamabhisaṃrādhya punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, saying "Excellent, excellent!" and having gladdened him, spoke again —

children.text: na no na vidito rājaṃstava śuddhāśayāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your pure intention is not unknown to us, O king;

children.text: evaṃ nu pratidatte te mayeme nayane nṛpa // Jm_2.44 //
children.translated_text: thus, in return for your [generosity], these two eyes are given to you by me, O ruler." || Jm 2.44 ||

children.text: samantādyojanaśataṃ śailairapi tiraskṛtam /
children.translated_text: "For a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in every direction, even [things] concealed by mountains,

children.text: draṣṭumavyāhatā śaktirbhaviṣyatyanayośca te // Jm_2.45 //
children.translated_text: the power to see unobstructed shall be yours through these [eyes]." || Jm 2.45 ||

body.text: ityuktvā śakrastathaiva cāntardadhe / atha bodhisattvo vismayapūrṇamanobhirmandamandanimeṣapravikasitanayanairamātyairanuyātaḥ pauraiścābhivīkṣyamāṇo jayāśīrvacanapuraḥsaraiśca brāhmaṇairabhinandyamānaḥ puravaramucchritadhvajavicitrapatākaṃ pravitanyamānābhyudayaśobhamabhigamya parṣadi niṣaṇṇaḥ sabhājanārthamabhigatasyāmātyapramukhasya brāhmaṇavṛddhapaurajānapadasyaivamātmopanāyikaṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Śakra</s> vanished just so. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, accompanied by ministers whose minds were filled with wonder, who slowly blinked their blossoming eyes, and gazed upon by the townspeople, and congratulated with words of victory-blessings by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, entered the excellent city, adorned with raised banners and colorful flags, its rising splendor spreading forth. Seated in the assembly, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> as his own offering to the assembly that had gathered to pay homage, led by ministers, elders among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and townsfolk and countryfolk, thus —

children.text: ko nāma loke śithilādaraḥ syāt kartuṃ dhanenārthijanapriyāṇi /
children.translated_text: "Who in this world would be negligent in doing what is dear to supplicants with wealth,

children.text: divyaprabhāve nayane mameme pradānapuṇyopanate samīkṣya // Jm_2.46 //
children.translated_text: seeing that these eyes of mine, of divine power, have been obtained through the merit of giving?" || Jm 2.46 ||

children.text: anekaśailāntaritaṃ yojanānāṃ śatādapi /
children.translated_text: "Though separated by many mountains, even from a hundred <s>yojanas</s> away,

children.text: adūrasthitavispaṣṭaṃ dṛśyaṃ paśyāmi sarvataḥ // Jm_2.47 //
children.translated_text: I see all visible things clearly as if close at hand." || Jm 2.47 ||

children.text: parānukampāvinayābhijātāddānātparaḥ ko 'bhyudayābhyupāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What better means to prosperity is there than giving, born of compassion, humility, and noble birth?

children.text: yanmānuṣaṃ cakṣurihaiva dattvā prāptaṃ mayā 'mānuṣadivyacakṣuḥ // Jm_2.48 //
children.translated_text: For having given human eyes here in this world, I have obtained superhuman, divine sight." || Jm 2.48 ||

children.text: etadviditvā śibayaḥ pradānairbhogena cārthān saphalīkurudhvam /
children.translated_text: "Knowing this, O <s>Śibis</s>, make your wealth fruitful through gifts and through enjoyment;

children.text: loke parasminniha caiṣa panthāḥ kīrtipradhānasya sukhodayasya // Jm_2.49 //
children.translated_text: this is the path to happiness, distinguished by fame, in this world and the next." || Jm 2.49 ||

children.text: dhanasya niḥsāralaghoḥ sa sāro yaddīyate lokahitonmukhena /
children.translated_text: "The essence of insubstantial, trifling wealth is that which is given by one intent on the welfare of the world;

children.text: nidhānatāṃ yāti hi dīyamānamadīyamānaṃ nidhanaikaniṣṭham // Jm_2.50 //
children.translated_text: for when given, it becomes a treasure; when not given, its sole end is destruction." || Jm 2.50 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ duṣkaraśatasamudānīto 'yamasmadarthaṃ tena bhagavatā saddharma iti satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ / tathāgatamāhātmye pūrvavacca karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyam - ihaiva puṇyaphalapradarśane caivaṃ satkṛtyopacitāni puṇyānīhaiva puṣpamātramātmaprabhāvasya kīrtisaṃtatimanoharaṃ pradarśayantīti //
body.translated_text: "Thus, this true <s>Dharma</s>, achieved through hundreds of difficult deeds for our sake by that Blessed One, should be heard with reverence." And in describing the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and also in the description of compassion as before — in the demonstration of the fruits of merit right here — "thus, merits accumulated with reverence display right here a blossom-like token of their own power, a garland of fame, delightful to the mind."

body.text: iti śibijātakaṃ dvitīyam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second [story], the <s>Śibi Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 3. Kulmāṣapiṇḍījātakam
body.translated_text: 3. The <s>Kulmāṣapiṇḍī Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Barley-Cake)

body.text: cittaprasādodgataṃ pātrātiśayapratipāditaṃ ca nālpakaṃ nāma dānamasti vipākamahattvāt / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: A gift that arises from mental clarity and is enhanced by an excellent recipient is never small, because of the greatness of its fruition. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavānkośalādhipatirbabhūva / tasyotsāhamantraprabhū [tvaśaktisampatprabhṛtīnāṃ prakarṣiṇāmapi rājaguṇānāṃ vibhūtimatiśiśye daivasampadguṇaśobhā /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was the lord of <s>Kośala</s>. Among his excellent royal qualities — enterprise, counsel, power of authority, and abundance of strength — his splendor of divine fortune surpassed even [those other] distinctions.

children.text: guṇāstasyādhikaṃ rejurdaivasamapadvibhūṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: His virtues, adorned by the splendor of divine fortune, shone all the more,

children.text: kiraṇā iva candrasya śaradunmīlitaśriyaḥ // Jm_3.1 //
children.translated_text: like the rays of the moon whose beauty is unveiled in autumn. || Jm 3.1 ||

children.text: tatyāja dṛptānapi tasya śatrūn rakteva reme tadapāśriteṣu /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) abandoned even his proud enemies and delighted, as if enamored, in those who sought his protection;

children.text: ityāsa tasyānyanarādhipeṣu kopaprasādānuvidhāyinī śrīḥ // Jm_3.2 //
children.translated_text: thus did his <s>Śrī</s> conform to wrath and favor toward other kings. || Jm 3.2 ||

children.text: dharmātmakatvānna ca nāma tasya paropatāpāśivamāsa cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of his righteous nature, his mind never harbored anything inauspicious against others;

children.text: bhṛtyānurāgastu tathā jajṛmbhe dviṣatsu lakṣmīrna yathāsya reme // Jm_3.3 //
children.translated_text: and the devotion of his servants flourished so greatly that <s>Lakṣmī</s> did not delight as much among his enemies. || Jm 3.3 ||

body.text: so 'nantarātītāṃ svajātimanusasmāra / tadanusmaraṇācca samupajātasaṃvego viśeṣavattaraṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyaḥ sukhahetunidānaṃ dānamadācchīlasaṃvaramanavarataṃ pupoṣa poṣadhaniyamaṃ ca parvadivaseṣu samādade / abhīkṣṇaṃ ca rājā parṣadi svasmiṃścāntaḥpure puṇyaprabhāvodbhāvanāllokaṃ śreyasi niyoktukāmaḥ pratītahṛdayo gāthādvayamiti niyatārthaṃ babhāṣe -
body.translated_text: He recalled his immediately previous birth. And from that recollection, being stirred with heightened spiritual urgency, he nourished more especially the giving of comfort to ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and forest-dwellers, and moral discipline and restraint unceasingly, and he also observed the fasting vow on holy days. And frequently, in the assembly and in his own inner court, the king, wishing to establish the people in virtue by demonstrating the power of merit, spoke with a faithful heart these two verses of definite meaning —

children.text: na sugataparicaryā vidyate svalpikāpi pratanuphalavibhūtiryacchrutaṃ kevalaṃ prāk /
children.translated_text: "There is no service to the well-gone ones that is too small, nor any whose fruit and glory are meager — this was heard previously as mere report;

children.text: tadidamalavaṇāyāḥ śuṣkarūkṣārūṇāyāḥ phalavibhavamahattvaṃ paśya kulmāṣapiṇḍyāḥ // Jm_3.4 //
children.translated_text: but behold the greatness of the fruit and prosperity of a single barley-cake, unsalted, dry, and coarse!" || Jm 3.4 ||

children.text: rathaturagavicitraṃ mattanāgendranīlaṃ balamakṛśamidaṃ me medinī kevalā ca /
children.translated_text: "This army of mine, splendid with chariots and horses, dark as rutting lordly elephants, is not insignificant; and this entire earth [is mine];

children.text: bahu dhanamanuraktā śrīrudārāśca dārāḥ phalasamudayaśobhāṃ paśya kulmāṣapiṇḍyāḥ // Jm_3.5 //
children.translated_text: abundant wealth, devoted <s>Śrī</s>, and noble wives — behold the splendor of the fruition of a barley-cake!" || Jm 3.5 ||

body.text: tamamātyā brāhmaṇavṛddhāḥ pauramukhyāśca kautūhalādhūrṇitamanaso 'pi na prasahante sma paryanuyoktuṃ kimabhisamīkṣya mahārājo gāthādvayamidamabhīkṣṇaṃ bhāṣata iti / atha tasya rājño vāgnityatvādavyāhatatarapraṇayaprasarā devī samutpannakautūhalā saṃkathāprastāvāgataṃ parṣadi paryapṛcchadenam /
body.translated_text: His ministers, elder <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and leading citizens, though their minds were churning with curiosity, did not dare to ask him: "With what purpose does the great king repeatedly recite these two verses?" Then, because of the king's gentle manner, his queen, whose affection flowed unobstructed, having become curious, asked him on the occasion of a conversation in the assembly:

children.text: niyatamiti narendra bhāṣase hṛdayagatāṃ mudamudgiranniva /
children.translated_text: "Certainly, O lord of men, you speak as if pouring forth the joy within your heart;

children.text: bhavati mama kutūhalākulaṃ hṛdayamidaṃ kathitena tena te // Jm_3.6 //
children.translated_text: my heart becomes agitated with curiosity at those words of yours." || Jm 3.6 ||

children.text: tadarhati śrotumayaṃ jano yadi pracakṣva tatkiṃ nviti bhāṣase nṛpa /
children.translated_text: "If this assembly is worthy of hearing, then declare, O king, what it is that you say;

children.text: rahasyamevaṃ ca na kīrtyate kvacitprakāśamasmācca mayāpi pṛcchyate // Jm_3.7 //
children.translated_text: for such a thing is never proclaimed in secret, and therefore I too ask openly." || Jm 3.7 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā prītyabhisnigdhayā dṛṣṭyā samabhivīkṣya devīṃ smitapravikasitavadana uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, gazing at the queen with a look softened by affection, his face blossoming with a smile, said —

children.text: avibhāvya nimittārthaṃ śrutvodgāramimaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: "Without understanding the meaning of the occasion, having heard this outburst of mine,

children.text: na kevalaṃ tavaivātra kautūhalacalaṃ manaḥ // Jm_3.8 //
children.translated_text: it is not yours alone — the mind here is restless with curiosity." || Jm 3.8 ||

children.text: samantamapyetadamātyamaṇḍalaṃ kutūhalāghūrṇitalolamānasam /
children.translated_text: "This entire circle of ministers too has minds swaying with curiosity,

children.text: puraṃ ca sāntaḥpuramatra tena me niśamyatāṃ yena mayaivamucyate // Jm_3.9 //
children.translated_text: and the city together with the inner court — therefore, let the reason I speak thus be heard." || Jm 3.9 ||

children.text: suptaprabuddha iva jātimanusmarāmi yasyāmihaiva nagare bhṛtako 'hamāsam /
children.translated_text: "As if awakened from sleep, I recall a birth in which I was a hired servant in this very city,

children.text: śīlānvito 'pi dhanamātrasamucchritebhyaḥ karmābhirādhanasamarjitadīnavṛttiḥ // Jm_3.10 //
children.translated_text: endowed with virtue yet earning a humble livelihood through the labor of serving those elevated merely by wealth." || Jm 3.10 ||

children.text: so 'haṃ bhṛtiṃ paribhavaśramadainyaśālāṃ trāṇāśayātsvayamavṛttibhayādvivikṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "I, seeking to escape from the wages that were a hall of humiliation, toil, and wretchedness, out of fear of destitution and with hope for protection,

children.text: bhikṣārthinaśca caturaḥ śramaṇānapaśyaṃ vaśyendriyānanugatāniva bhikṣulakṣmyā // Jm_3.11 //
children.translated_text: saw four wandering ascetics, with senses subdued, as if accompanied by the radiance of mendicancy." || Jm 3.11 ||

children.text: tebhyaḥ prasādamṛdunā manasā praṇamya kulmāṣamātrakamadāṃ prayataḥ svagehe /
children.translated_text: "Bowing to them with a mind softened by faith, I reverently offered in my own home a mere morsel of barley-cake;

children.text: tasyāṅkarodaya ivaiṣa yadanyarājacūḍāprabhāścaraṇareṇuṣu me niṣaktāḥ // Jm_3.12 //
children.translated_text: the sprouting of that [seed] is this — that the radiance from the crest-jewels of other kings now clings to the dust of my feet." || Jm 3.12 ||

children.text: tadetadabhisandhāya mayaivaṃ devi kathyate /
children.translated_text: "Having this in mind, O queen, I speak thus;

children.text: puṇyena ca labhe tṛptimarhatāṃ darśanena ca // Jm_3.13 //
children.translated_text: and I find satisfaction in merit and in the sight of the worthy." || Jm 3.13 ||

body.text: atha sā devī praharṣavismayaviśālākṣī sabahumānamudīkṣamāṇā rājānamityuvāca / upapannarūpaḥ puṇyānāmayamevaṃvidho vipākābhyudayaviśeṣaḥ / puṇyaphalapratyakṣiṇaśca mahārājasya yadayaṃ puṇyeṣvādaraḥ / tadevameva pāpapravṛttivimukhaḥ piteva prajānāṃ samyakparipālanasumukhaḥ puṇyagaṇārjanābhimukhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that queen, her eyes wide with delight and wonder, gazing at the king with great respect, said: "This extraordinary distinction of the ripening of merit is befitting. And it is proper that the great king, who has witnessed the fruits of merit firsthand, should have such regard for meritorious deeds. Therefore, just so, turning away from the course of sin, like a father kindly disposed to the proper protection of his subjects, devoted to the acquisition of merit —

children.text: yaśaḥśriyā dānasamṛddhayā jvalanpratiṣṭhitājñaḥ pratirājamūrdhasu /
children.translated_text: blazing with the glory of fame enriched by giving, your command established upon the heads of rival kings,

children.text: samīraṇākuñcitasāgarāmvarāṃ ciraṃ mahīṃ dharmanayena pālaya // Jm_3.14 //
children.translated_text: long may you protect this earth, garlanded by wind-rippled oceans, through the way of <s>Dharma</s>." || Jm 3.14 ||

body.text: rājovāca - kiṃ hyetaddevi na syāt?
body.translated_text: The king said: "How could this not be so, O queen?

children.text: so 'haṃ tameva punarāśrayituṃ yatiṣye śreyaḥpathaṃ samabhilakṣitaramyacihnam /
children.translated_text: "I shall endeavor again to follow that very path of virtue, whose lovely marks are clearly discerned;

children.text: lokaḥ praditsati hi dānaphalaṃ niśamya dāsyāmyahaṃ kimiti nātmagataṃ niśamya // Jm_3.15 //
children.translated_text: for when the world, hearing of the fruit of giving, is ready to give — shall I not give, having witnessed [the fruit] in my own experience?" || Jm 3.15 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā devīṃ devīmiva śriyā jvalantīmabhisnigdhamavekṣya śrīsampattihetukutūhalahṛdayaḥ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, gazing tenderly at the queen, who blazed with beauty like a goddess, his heart filled with curiosity about the cause of prosperity and fortune, spoke again —

children.text: candralekheva tārāṇāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye virājase /
akṛthāḥ kiṃ nu kalyāṇi karmātimadhurodayam // Jm_3.16 //

body.text: devyuvāca - asti deva kiñcidahamapi pūrvajanmavṛttiṃ samanusmarāmīti / kathaya kathayedānīmiti ca sādaraṃ rājñā paryanuyuktovāca -

children.text: bālye 'nubhūtamiva tatsamanusmarāmi dāsī satī yadahamuddhṛtabhaktamekam /
kṣīṇāsravāya munaye vinayena dattvā supteva tatra samavāpamiha prabodham // Jm_3.17 //
etatsmarāmi kuśalaṃ naradeva yena tvannāthatāmupagatāsmi samaṃ pṛthivyā /
kṣīṇāsraveṣu na kṛtaṃ tanu nāma kiñcidityuktavānasi yathaiva munistathaiva // Jm_3.18 //

body.text: atha sa rājā puṇyaphalapradarśanātpuṇyeṣu samutpāditabahumānāmabhiprasannamanasaṃ parṣadaṃ vismayaikāgrāmavetya niyatamīdṛśaṃ kiñcitsamanuśaśāsa -

children.text: alpasyāpi śubhasya vistaramimaṃ dṛṣṭvā vipākaśriyaḥ
syātko nāma na dānaśīlavidhinā puṇyakriyātatparaḥ /
naiva draṣṭumapi kṣamaḥ sa puruṣaḥ paryāptavitto 'pi san
yaḥ kārpaṇyatamisrayāvṛtamatirnāpnoti dānairyaśaḥ // Jm_3.19 //
tyaktavyaṃ vivaśena yanna ca tathā kasmaicidarthāya yat
tannyāyena dhanaṃ tyajanyadi guṇaṃ kañcitsamudbhāvayet /
ko 'sau tatra bhajeta matsarapathaṃ jānanguṇānāṃ rasaṃ
prītyādyā vividhāśca kīrtyanusṛtā dānapratiṣṭhāguṇāḥ // Jm_3.20 //
dānaṃ nāma mahānidhānamanugaṃ caurādyasādhāraṇaṃ
dānaṃ matsaralobhadoṣarajasaḥ prakṣālanaṃ cetasaḥ /
saṃsārādhvapariśramāpanayanaṃ dānaṃ sukhaṃ vāhanaṃ
dānaṃ naikasukhopadhānasumukhaṃ sanmitramātyantikam // Jm_3.21 //
vibhavasamudayaṃ vā dīptamājñāguṇaṃ vā tridaśapuranivāsaṃ rūpaśobhāguṇaṃ vā /
yadabhilaṣati sarvaṃ tatsamāpnoti dānād iti parigaṇitārthaḥ ko na dānāni dadyāt // Jm_3.22 //
sārādānaṃ dānamāhurdhanānām aiśvaryāṇāṃ dānamāhurnidānam /
dānaṃ śrīmatsajjanatvāvadānaṃ bālyaprajñaiḥ pāṃsudānaṃ sudānam // Jm_3.23 //

body.text: atha sā parṣattasya rājñastadgrāhakaṃ vacanaṃ sabahumānamabhinandya pradānādipratipattyabhimukhī babhūva /

tadevaṃ cittaprasādodgataṃ pātrātiśayapratipāditaṃ ca nālpakaṃ nāma dānamasti vipākamahattvāditi prasannacittenānuttare puṇyakṣetra āryasaṃghe dānaṃ dadatā parā prītirutpādayitavyā / adūre mamāpyevaṃvidhā ato viśiṣṭatarāśca sampattaya iti /
iti kulmāṣapiṇḍījātakaṃ tṛtīyam /
4. Śreṣṭhijātakam
atyayamapyavigaṇayya ditsanti satpuruṣāḥ / kena nāma svasthena na dātavyaṃ syāt? tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavānbhāgyātiśayaguṇādutthānasampadā cādhigatavipuladhanasamṛddhiraviṣamavyavahāraśīlatvālloke bahumānaniketabhūta udārābhijanavānanekavidyākalāvikalpādhigamavimalataramatirguṇamāhātmyādrājñā samupahṛtasammānaḥ pradānaśīlatvāllokasādhāraṇavibhavaḥ śreṣṭhī babhūva /

children.text: arthibhiḥ prītahṛdayaiḥ kīrtyamānamitastataḥ /
tyāgaśauryonnataṃ nāma tasya vyāpa diśo daśa // Jm_4.1 //
dadyānna dadyāditi tatra nāsīdvicāradolācalamānaso 'rthī /
khyātāvadāne hi babhūva tasminvisrambhadhṛṣṭapraṇayo 'rthivargaḥ // Jm_4.2 //
nā 'sau jugopātmasukhārthamarthaṃ na spardhayā lobhaparābhavādvā /
sattvārthiduḥkhaṃ na śaśāka soḍhuṃ nāstīti vaktuṃ ca tato jugopa // Jm_4.3 //

body.text: atha kadācittasya mahāsattvasya bhojanakāle snātānuliptagātrasya kuśalodārasūdopakalpite samupasthitevarṇagandharasasparśādiguṇasamudite vicitre bhakṣyabhojyādividhau tatpuṇyasambhārābhivṛddhikāmo jñānāgninirdagdhasarvakleśendhanaḥ pratyekabuddhastadgṛhamabhijagāma bhikṣārthī / samupetya ca dvārakoṣṭhake vyatiṣṭhata /

children.text: aśaṅkitācañcaladhīrasaumyamavekṣamāṇo yugamātramurvyāḥ /
tatrāvatasthe praśamābhijātaḥ sa pātrasaṃsaktakarāgrapadmaḥ // Jm_4.4 //

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyānbodhisattvasya tāṃ dānasampadamamṛṣyamāṇastadvidhnārthamantarā ca taṃ bhadantamantarā ca dvāradehalīṃ pracalajvālākarālodaramanekapauruṣamatigambhīraṃ bhayānakadarśanaṃ sapratibhayanirghoṣaṃ narakamabhinirmame visphuradbhiranekairjanaśatairācitam / atha bodhisattvaḥ pratyekabuddhaṃ

bhikṣārthinamabhigatamālokya patnīmuvāca - bhadre svayamāryāya paryāptaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dehīti / sā tatheti pratiśrutya praṇītaṃ bhakṣyabhojyamādāya prasthitā / narakamālokya dvārakoṣṭhakasamīpe bhayaviṣādacañcalākṣī sahasā nyavartata / kimetaditi ca bhartrā paryanuyuktā samāpatitasādhvasāpihitakaṇṭhī tatkathañcittasmai kathayāmāsa / atha bodhisattvaḥ kathamayamāryo madgṛhādanavāptabhikṣa eva pratiyāsyatīti sasambhramaṃ tattasyāḥ kathitamanādṛtya svayameva ca praṇītaṃ bhakṣyabhojyamādāya tasya mahātmanaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ pratipādayitukāmo dvārakoṣṭhakasamīpamabhigatastamatibhīṣaṇamantarā narakaṃ dadarśa / tasya kiṃ svididamiti samutpannavitarkasya māraḥ pāpīyānbhavanabhitterviniḥsṛtya saṃdṛśyamānadivyādbhūtavapurantarikṣe sthitvā hitakāma iva nāmābravīt - gṛhapate mahārauravanāmāyaṃ mahānarakaḥ /

children.text: arthipraśaṃsāvacanapralubdhā ditsanti dānavyasanena ye 'rthān /
śaratsahasrāṇi bahūni teṣāmasminnivāso 'sulabhapravāsaḥ // Jm_4.5 //
arthastrivargasya viśeṣahetustasminhate kena hato na dharmaḥ /
dharmaṃ ca hatvārthanibarhaṇena kathaṃ nu na syānnarakapratiṣṭhaḥ // Jm_4.6 //
dānaprasaṅgena ca dharmamūlaṃ ghnatā tvayārthaṃ yadakāri pāpam /
tvāmattumabhyudgatametadasmājjvālāgrajihvaṃ narakāntakāsyam // Jm_4.7 //
tatsādhu dānādviniyaccha buddhimevaṃ hi sadyaḥpatanaṃ na te syāt /
viceṣṭamānaiḥ karuṇaṃ rudadbhirmā dātṛbhirgāḥ samatāmamībhiḥ // Jm_4.8 //
pratigrahītā tu jano 'bhyupaiti nivṛttadānāpanayaḥ suratvam /
tatsvargamārgāvaraṇādviramya dānodyamātsaṃyamamāśrayasva // Jm_4.9 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo nūnamasyaitaddurātmano mama dānavighnāya viceṣṭitamityavagamya sattvāvaṣṭambhadhīraṃ vinayamadhurāvicchedaṃ niyatamityavocadenam /

children.text: asmaddhitāvekṣaṇadakṣiṇena vidarśito 'yaṃ bhavatāryamārgaḥ /
yuktā viśeṣeṇa ca daivateṣu parānukampānipuṇā pravṛttiḥ // Jm_4.10 //
doṣodayātpūrvamanantaraṃ vā yuktaṃ tu tacchāntipathena gantum /
gate prayāsaṃ hyupacāradoṣairvyādhau cikitsāpraṇayo vighātaḥ // Jm_4.11 //
idaṃ ca dānavyasanaṃ madīyaṃ śaṅke cikitsāviṣayavyatītam /
tathā hyanādṛtya hitaiṣitāṃ te na me manaḥ saṅkacati pradānāt // Jm_4.12 //
dānādadharmaṃ ca yadūcivāṃstvamarthaṃ ca dharmasya viśeṣahetum /
tanmānuṣī neyamavaiti buddhirdānādṛte dharmapatho yathārthaḥ // Jm_4.13 //
nidhīyamānaḥ sa nu dharmahetuścauraiḥ prasahyātha vilupyamānaḥ /
oghodarāntarvinimagnamūrtirhutāśanasyāśanatāṃ gato vā // Jm_4.14 //
yaccāttha dātā narakaṃ prayāti pratigrahītā tu surendralokam /
vivardhitastena ca me tvayā 'yaṃ dānodyamaḥ saṃyamayiṣyatāpi // Jm_4.15 //
ananyathā cāstu vacastavedaṃ svargaṃ ca me yācanakā vrajantu /
dānaṃ hi me lokahitārthamiṣṭaṃ nedaṃ svasaukhyodayasādhanāya // Jm_4.16 //

body.text: atha sa māraḥ pāpīyānpunarapi bodhisattvaṃ hitaiṣīva dhīrahastenovāca -

children.text: hitoktimetāṃ mama cāpalaṃ vā samīkṣya yenecchasi tena gaccha /
sukhānvito vā bahumānapūrvaṃ smartāsi māṃ vipratisāravānvā // Jm_4.17 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - marṣa marṣayatu bhavān /

children.text: kāmaṃ patāmi narakaṃ sphuradugravahniṃ jvālāvalīḍhaśithilāvanatena mūrdhnā /
na tvarthināṃ praṇayadarśitasauhṛdānāṃ sammānakālamavamānanayā hariṣye // Jm_4.18 //

body.text: ityuktvā bodhisattvaḥ svabhāgyabalāvaṣṭambhājjānānaśca niratyayatāṃ dānasya nivāraṇaikarasamavadhūya svajanaparijanaṃ sādhvasānabhibhūtamatirabhivṛddhadānābhilāṣo narakamadhyena prāyāt /

children.text: puṇyānubhāvādatha tasya tasminnapaṅkajaṃ paṅkajamudbabhūva /
avajñayevāvajahāsa māraṃ yacchuklayā keśaradantapaṅkatyā // Jm_4.19 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ padmasaṃkrameṇa svapuṇyātiśayanirjātenābhigamya pratyekabuddhaṃ prasādasaṃharṣāpūrṇahṛdayaḥ piṇḍapātamasmai prāyacchat /

children.text: manaḥprasādapratibodhanārthaṃ tasyātha bhikṣurviyadutpapāta /
varṣañjvalaṃścaiva sa tatra reje savidyududdyotapayodalakṣmyā // Jm_4.20 //
avamṛditamanorathastu māro dyutiparimoṣamavāpya vaimanasyāt /
tamabhimukhamudīkṣituṃ na sehe saha narakeṇa tatastirobabhūva // Jm_4.21 //

body.text: tatkimidamupanītam? evamatyayamapyavigaṇayya ditsanti satpuruṣāḥ / kena nāma svasthena na dātavyaṃ syāt? na sattvavantaḥ śakyante bhayādapyagatiṃ gamayitumityevamapyunneyam /
iti śreṣṭhijātakaṃ caturtham /
5. Aviṣahyaśreṣṭhijātakam
