na vibhavakṣayāvekṣayā samṛddhyāśayā vā pradānavaidhuryamupayānti satpuruṣāḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavāṃstyāgaśīlakulavinayaśrutajñānāvismayādiguṇasamudito dhanadāyamāno vibhavasaṃpadā sarvātithitvādanuparatadānasatro lokahitārthapravṛtto dāyakaśreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhī babhūva mātsaryādidoṣāviṣahyo 'viṣahya iti prakāśanāmā /

children.text: iṣṭārthasaṃpattivimarśanāśāt prītiprabodhasya viśeṣahetuḥ /
yathārthināṃ darśanamāsa tasya tathārthināṃ darśanamāsa tasya // Jm_5.1 //
children.translated_text: Just as the sight of him was [gratifying] for those in need, so the sight of those in need was [gratifying] for him. || Jm 5.1 ||

children.text: dehīti yācñāniyatārthamukto nāstīti nāsau gadituṃ śaśāka /
children.translated_text: When addressed with words fixed upon the purpose 'Give!' — the word 'It is not' he was unable to utter,

children.text: hṛtāvakāśā hi babhūva citte tasyārthasaktiḥ kṛpayā mahatyā // Jm_5.2 //
children.translated_text: for in his heart, attachment to wealth had been displaced by great compassion. || Jm 5.2 ||

children.text: tasyārthibhirnirhriyamāṇasāre gṛhe babhūvābhyadhikapraharṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: In his household, from which the essence was being carried away by supplicants, there arose even greater joy,

children.text: viveda sa hyugraghanānanarthānakāraṇakṣipravirāgiṇo 'rthān // Jm_5.3 //
children.translated_text: for he perceived that riches — which provoke severe and manifold calamities and which cause dispassion swiftly and without reason — are dangerous. || Jm 5.3 ||

children.text: bhavanti lokasya hi bhūyasārthā lobhāśrayād durgatimārgasārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: For most riches of the world, being grounded in greed, are provisions for the path to misfortune;

children.text: parātmanorabhyudayāvahatvādarthāstadīyāstu babhuryathārthāḥ // Jm_5.4 //
children.translated_text: but his riches, because they brought prosperity to both others and himself, were truly deserving of the name 'riches.' || Jm 5.4 ||

body.text: atha tasya mahāsattvasya yathābhilaṣitairakliṣṭaiḥ śiṣṭopacāravibhūṣaṇairvipulairarthavisargairyācanakajanaṃ samantataḥ saṃtarpayataḥ pradānaudāryaśravaṇādvismayāvarjitamanāḥ śakro devendraḥ pradānasthiraniścayamasya jijñāsamānaḥ pratyahaṃ dhanadhānyaratnaparicchadajātaṃ tattadantardhāpayāmāsa / api nāmāyaṃ vibhavaparikṣayāśaṅkayāpi mātsaryāya pratāryeteti / pradānādhimuktasya tu punarmahāsattvasya
body.translated_text: Then, as that great being was satisfying the community of supplicants on all sides with generous distributions of wealth — untroubled, as desired, adorned with the courtesies of the virtuous and abundant — <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his mind captivated by wonder upon hearing of his munificent generosity, wishing to test the firmness of his resolve in giving, caused his stores of money, grain, jewels, and possessions to disappear day after day — thinking, 'Perhaps he might be induced to avarice through fear of the exhaustion of his wealth.' But that great being, whose inclination was toward giving,

children.text: yathā yathā tasya vineśurarthāḥ sūryābhisṛṣṭa iva toyaleśāḥ /
children.translated_text: the more his riches vanished, like droplets of water exposed to the sun,

children.text: tathā tathainān vipulaiḥ pradānairgṛhātpradīptādiva nirjahāra // Jm_5.5 //
children.translated_text: the more he drove them out with generous gifts, as if from a house on fire. || Jm 5.5 ||

body.text: atha śakro devendrastyāgaparāyaṇameva taṃ mahāsattvamavetya prakṣīyamāṇavibhavasāramapi vismitataramatistasyaikarātreṇa sarvaṃ vibhavasāramantardhāpayāmāsānyatra rajjukuṇḍalāddātrāccaikasmāt / atha bodhisattvaḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ yathocittaṃ prativibuddhaḥ paśyati sma dhanadhānyaparicchadaparijanavibhavaśūnyaṃ niṣkūjadīnaṃ svabhavanaṃ rākṣasairivodvāsitamanabhirāmadarśanīyaṃ, kimiti ca samutthitavitarkaḥ samanuvicaraṃstadrajjukuṇḍalakaṃ dātraṃ ca kevalamatra dadarśa / tasya cintā prādurabhavat - yadi tāvat kenacidyācitumanucitavacasā svavikramopārjitopajauvinā madgṛhe praṇaya evaṃ darśitaḥ sūpayuktā evamarthāḥ / atha tvidānīṃ madbhāgyadoṣāducchrayamasahamānena kenacidanupayuktā eva vidrutāstatkaṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, perceiving that this great being remained devoted solely to generosity even as the substance of his wealth was being depleted, all the more astonished, caused all the substance of his wealth to disappear in a single night, leaving only a rope, a sickle, and a single basket. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having awakened at dawn as was his custom, saw his dwelling empty of money, grain, possessions, and servants — desolate and silent, uninviting to behold, as if cleared out by demons. Wondering why, and reflecting as he investigated, he saw there only that rope, sickle, and basket. The thought arose in him: 'If some person, speaking unseemly words to beg, has displayed his boldness — wealth acquired by his own prowess — as friendship in my house, then those riches are well employed. But if, on the other hand, some envious one unable to bear my prosperity has scattered them unused, then alas!

children.text: calaṃ sauhṛdamarthānāṃ viditaṃ pūrvameva me /
children.translated_text: 'The friendship of riches is fickle — this was known to me even before;

children.text: arthināmeva pīḍā tu dahatyatra mano mama // Jm_5.6 //
children.translated_text: but it is the distress of the supplicants that burns my mind here.' || Jm 5.6 ||

children.text: pradānasatkārasukhocitāściraṃ viviktamarthairabhigamya madgṛham /
children.translated_text: 'Those supplicants of mine, long accustomed to the pleasure of generous hospitality, upon approaching my house now bereft of wealth and desolate,

children.text: kathaṃ bhaviṣyanti nu te mamārthinaḥ pipāsitāḥ śuṣkamivāgatā hradam // Jm_5.7 //
children.translated_text: how will they fare — like thirsty ones arriving at a dried-up lake?' || Jm 5.7 ||

body.text: atha sa bodhisattvaḥ svadhairyāvaṣṭambhādanāsvāditaviṣādadainyastasyāmapyavasthāyāmanabhyastayācñākramatvāt parān yācituṃ paricitānapi na prasehe / evaṃ duṣkaraṃ yācitumiti ca tasya bhūyasī yācanakeṣvanukampā babhūva / atha sa mahātmā yācanakajanasvāgatādikriyāvekṣayā svayameva tadrajjukuṇḍalakaṃ dātraṃ ca pratigṛhya pratyahaṃ tṛṇavikrayopalabdhayā vibhavamātrayārthijanapraṇayasammānanāṃ cakāra / atha śakro devendrastasyemāmaviṣāditāṃ parame 'pi dāridrye pradānābhimukhatāṃ cāvekṣya savismayabahumānaḥ saṃdṛśyamānadivyādbhutavapurantarikṣe sthitvā dānādvicchandayaṃstaṃ mahāsattvamuvāca - gṛhapate
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the firmness of his own resolve, having not tasted dejection or humiliation even in that condition, could not bring himself to beg from others — even those he knew — because he had never practiced the manner of begging. And the thought 'How difficult it is to beg!' gave rise in him to even greater compassion for the supplicants. Then that great soul, out of concern for the rites of welcoming the community of supplicants and such duties, personally took up that rope, sickle, and basket, and day by day, with the modest income obtained from selling grass, he maintained the tradition of honoring the affection of the supplicant community. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, observing his undaunted disposition toward giving even in the extremity of poverty, with a mixture of wonder and respect, standing in the sky with his divine and wondrous form made visible, attempting to dissuade that great being from giving, said: 'Householder,

children.text: suhṛnmanastāpakarīmavasthāmimāmupetastvamatipradānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You have arrived at this condition — which causes anguish to the hearts of friends — through excessive giving,

children.text: na dasyubhirnaiva jalānalābhyāṃ na rājabhiḥ saṃhriyamāṇavittaḥ // Jm_5.8 //
children.translated_text: not because your wealth was seized by robbers, nor by flood or fire, nor by kings.' || Jm 5.8 ||

children.text: tattvāṃ hitāvekṣitayā bravīmi niyaccha dāne vyasanānurāgam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore I tell you, out of regard for your welfare: restrain your passionate attachment to giving;

children.text: itthaṃgataḥ sannapi cenna dadyā yāyāḥ punaḥ pūrvasamṛddhiśobhām // Jm_5.9 //
children.translated_text: if, having reached this state, you would not give, you would regain the splendor of your former prosperity.' || Jm 5.9 ||

children.text: śaśvat kṛśenāpi parivyayeṇa kālena dṛṣṭvā kṣayamarjanānām /
children.translated_text: 'Even by gradual expenditure, in time, seeing the decay of acquisitions,

children.text: cayena valmīkasamucchrayāṃśca vṛddhyarthinaḥ saṃyama eva panthāḥ // Jm_5.10 //
children.translated_text: and by accumulation, growths like those of an anthill — for one who seeks increase, self-restraint alone is the path.' || Jm 5.10 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pradānābhyāsamāhātmyaṃ vidarśayañchakramuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating the greatness of the practice of giving, said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: anāryamāryeṇa sahasranetra suduṣkaraṃ suṣṭhvapi durgatena /
children.translated_text: 'Ignoble [it would be] for a noble one, O Thousand-eyed One, and extremely difficult even for one who has been well reduced to poverty —

children.text: mā caiva tadbhūnmama śakra vittaṃ yatprāptihetoḥ kṛpaṇāśayaḥ syām // Jm_5.11 //
children.translated_text: and may I never have that wealth, O <s>Śakra</s>, for the sake of obtaining which I would become base-minded! || Jm 5.11 ||

children.text: icchanti yācñāmaraṇena gantuṃ duḥkhasya yasya pratikāramārgam /
children.translated_text: 'Those who wish to approach through begging the path of remedy for their suffering — the death of which [remedy would leave them helpless] —

children.text: tenāturān kaḥ kulaputramānī nāstīti śuṣkāśaninābhihanyāt // Jm_5.12 //
children.translated_text: what person of noble family-pride would strike them, when afflicted, with the thunderbolt of "There is nothing"?' || Jm 5.12 ||

children.text: tanmadvidhaḥ kiṃ svidupādadīta ratnaṃ dhanaṃ vā divi vāpi rājyam /
children.translated_text: 'What jewel, or wealth, or even sovereignty in heaven would one such as I acquire,

children.text: yācñābhitāpena vivarṇitāni prasādayennārthimukhāni yena // Jm_5.13 //
children.translated_text: if by it he could not bring joy to the faces of supplicants, made pale by the torment of having to beg?' || Jm 5.13 ||

children.text: mātsaryadoṣopacayāya yaḥ syānna tyāgacittaṃ paribṛṃhayedvā /
children.translated_text: 'That wealth which would serve only to increase the fault of avarice, or which would not foster a generous disposition,

children.text: sa tyāgamevārhati madvidhebhyaḥ parigrahacchadmamayo vighātaḥ // Jm_5.14 //
children.translated_text: deserves to be given away by the likes of me — possession of it is but disguised destruction.' || Jm 5.14 ||

children.text: vidyullatānṛttacale dhane ca sādhāraṇe naikavighātahetau /
children.translated_text: 'When wealth is as fleeting as the dance of lightning, shared by all, and a cause of numerous dangers,

children.text: dāne nidāne ca sukhodayānāṃ mātsaryamāryaḥ ka ivāśrayeta // Jm_5.15 //
children.translated_text: and when giving is the source of happiness — what noble person would resort to avarice?' || Jm 5.15 ||

children.text: taddarśitā śakra mayi svateyaṃ hitābhidhānādanukampito 'smi /
children.translated_text: 'Your concern for me has been shown, O <s>Śakra</s>, and I am gratified by your kind words;

children.text: svabhyastaharṣaṃ tu manaḥ pradānaistadutpathe kena dhṛtiṃ labheta // Jm_5.16 //
children.translated_text: but my mind, accustomed to the joy of giving — by what means could it find steadiness on a wrong path?' || Jm 5.16 ||

children.text: na cātra manyoranuvṛttimārge cittaṃ bhavānarhati saṃniyoktum /
children.translated_text: 'And you should not direct my mind onto the path of following anger;

children.text: na hi svabhāvasya vipakṣadurgamāroḍhumalpena balena śakyam // Jm_5.17 //
children.translated_text: for the difficult fortress of one's [opposing] nature cannot be scaled with little strength.' || Jm 5.17 ||

body.text: śakra uvāca - gṛhapate paryāptavibhavasya paripūrṇakośakoṣṭhāgārasya samyakpravṛttavividhavipulakarmāntasya virūḍhāyaterloke vaśīkṛtaiśvaryasyāyaṃ kramo nemāṃ daśāmabhiprapannasya / paśya -
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Householder, this course of action befits one whose wealth is sufficient, whose treasuries and granaries are full, whose various and extensive enterprises are properly conducted, whose growing influence has gained mastery in the world — not one who has reached this condition. Consider:

children.text: svabuddhivispandasamāhitena vā yaśo 'nukūlena kulocitena vā /
children.translated_text: 'Either by the exertion of one's own intelligence, or by [deeds] favorable to fame and befitting one's family,

children.text: samṛddhimākṛṣya śubhena karmaṇā sapatnatejāṃsyabhibhūya bhānuvat // Jm_5.18 //
children.translated_text: having attracted prosperity through meritorious action, having outshone rivals' splendor like the sun, || Jm 5.18 ||

children.text: jane prasaṅgena vitasya sadgatiṃ prabodhya harṣaṃ sasuhṛtsu bandhuṣu /
children.translated_text: 'having established good conduct among the people through association, having awakened joy among friends and kinsmen,

children.text: avāptasaṃmānavidhirnṛpādapi śriyā pariṣvakta ivābhikāmayā // Jm_5.19 //
children.translated_text: having received marks of honor even from kings, embraced as it were by desirable prosperity — || Jm 5.19 ||

children.text: atha pradāne pravijṛmbhitakramaḥ sukheṣu vā naiti janasya vācyatām /
children.translated_text: 'then, one may expand the course of giving; otherwise, he incurs the censure of people,

children.text: ajātapakṣaḥ khamivārurukṣayā vighātabhākkevalayā tu ditsayā // Jm_5.20 //
children.translated_text: like one without wings wishing to ascend the sky, meeting only with failure through a mere desire to give.' || Jm 5.20 ||

children.text: yato dhanaṃ saṃyamanaibhṛtāśrayādupārjyatāṃ tāvadalaṃ praditsayā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let wealth be acquired first through self-restraint, from a modest foundation — enough of the desire to give!

children.text: anāryatāpyatra ca nāma kā bhavenna yatpradadyā vibhaveṣvabhāviṣu // Jm_5.21 //
children.translated_text: And what ignobility is there in not giving when resources do not exist?' || Jm 5.21 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - alamatinirbandhenātrabhavataḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough of this excessive insistence on your part!

children.text: ātmārthaḥ syādyasya garīyān parakāryāt tenāpi syāddeyamanādṛtya samṛddhim /
children.translated_text: 'Even one for whom self-interest is more important than the welfare of others should give, disregarding prosperity,

children.text: naiti prītiṃ tāṃ hi mahatyāpi vibhūtyā dānaistuṣṭiṃ lobhajayādyāmupabhuṅkte // Jm_5.22 //
children.translated_text: for he does not find that joy even in great wealth which, through the conquest of greed, one enjoys as contentment through giving. || Jm 5.22 ||

children.text: naiti svargaṃ kevalayā yacca samṛddhyā dānenaiva khyātimavāpnoti ca puṇyām /
children.translated_text: 'One does not attain heaven by mere prosperity; and it is only through giving that one wins celebrated merit;

children.text: mātsaryādīnnābhibhavatyeva ca doṣāṃstasyā hetordānamataḥ ko na bhajeta // Jm_5.23 //
children.translated_text: nor does [mere prosperity] overcome faults such as avarice — therefore, for its sake, who would not resort to giving?' || Jm 5.23 ||

children.text: trātuṃ lokānyastu jarāmṛtyuparītānapyātmānaṃ ditsati kāruṇyavaśena /
children.translated_text: 'He who, in order to rescue beings beset by old age and death, is willing to give even his own self through the power of compassion,

children.text: yo nāsvādaṃ vetti sukhānāṃ paraduḥkhaiḥ kastasyārthastvadgatayā syādapi lakṣmyā // Jm_5.24 //
children.translated_text: who knows no taste of happiness when there is suffering of others — what use would wealth obtained through your means be to him?' || Jm 5.24 ||

body.text: api ca devendra /
body.translated_text: 'Moreover, O Lord of the Gods:

children.text: saṃpattiriva vittānāmadhruvā sthitirāyuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The duration of life is as uncertain as the fortune of wealth;

children.text: iti yācanakaṃ labdhvā na samṛddhiravekṣyate // Jm_5.25 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having obtained a supplicant, prosperity is not to be considered.' || Jm 5.25 ||

children.text: eko rathaśca bhuvi yadvidadhāti vartma tenāparo vrajati dhṛṣṭataraṃ tathānyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When one chariot makes a track on the earth, another travels along it more boldly, and then yet another;

children.text: kalyāṇamādyamimamityavadhūya mārgaṃ nāsatpathapraṇayane ramate mano me // Jm_5.26 //
children.translated_text: rejecting this first auspicious path, my mind does not delight in the pursuit of a wrong course.' || Jm 5.26 ||

children.text: arthaśca vistaramupaiṣyati cetpunarme hartā manāṃsi niyamena sa yācakānām /
children.translated_text: 'And if my wealth should again grow to abundance, it will inevitably captivate the hearts of supplicants;

children.text: evaṃgate 'pi ca yathāvibhavaṃ pradāsye mā caiva dānaniyame pramadiṣma śakra // Jm_5.27 //
children.translated_text: and even in such a case, I shall give according to my means — may we never be negligent in the discipline of giving, O <s>Śakra</s>!' || Jm 5.27 ||

body.text: ityukte śakro devendraḥ samabhiprasāditamanāḥ sādhu sādhvityenamabhisaṃrādhya sabahumānasnigdhamavekṣamāṇa uvāca -
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his mind fully satisfied, commending him with 'Excellent, excellent!' and looking upon him with respectful affection, said:

children.text: yaśaḥsapatnairapi karmabhirjanaḥ samṛddhimanvicchati nīcadāruṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'People seek prosperity even through deeds that rival glory yet are vile and dangerous,

children.text: svasaukhyasaṅgādanavekṣitātyayaḥ pratāryamāṇaścapalena cetasā // Jm_5.28 //
children.translated_text: heedless of peril out of attachment to personal comfort, being led astray by a fickle mind. || Jm 5.28 ||

children.text: acintayitvā tu dhanakṣayaṃ tvayā svasaukhyahāniṃ mama ca pratāraṇām /
children.translated_text: 'But by you, without considering the loss of wealth, the diminishment of your own comfort, or my attempts to dissuade you,

children.text: parārthasaṃpādanadhīracetasā mahattvamudbhāvitamātmasaṃpadaḥ // Jm_5.29 //
children.translated_text: with a mind resolute in accomplishing the welfare of others, the greatness of your own character has been manifested.' || Jm 5.29 ||

children.text: aho bataudāryaviśeṣabhāsvataḥ pramṛṣṭamātsaryatamisratā hṛdaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, how wonderful! Your heart, radiant with the distinction of magnanimity, has wiped away the darkness of avarice;

children.text: pradānasaṃkocavirūpatāṃ gataṃ dhane pranaṣṭe 'pi na yattadāśayā // Jm_5.30 //
children.translated_text: even when wealth is lost, your disposition has not fallen into the deformity of restraining generosity.' || Jm 5.30 ||

children.text: na cātra citraṃ paraduḥkhaduḥkhinaḥ kṛpāvaśāllokahitaiṣiṇastava /
children.translated_text: 'And this is not surprising for you, who suffer at the suffering of others, who through the power of compassion desire the welfare of the world;

children.text: himāvadātaḥ śikharīva vāyunā na yatpradānādasi kampito mayā // Jm_5.31 //
children.translated_text: that you were not shaken by me from giving, like a snow-white mountain peak by the wind.' || Jm 5.31 ||

children.text: yaśaḥ samudbhāvayituṃ parīkṣayā dhanaṃ tavedaṃ tu nigūḍhavānaham /
children.translated_text: 'In order to bring out your glory through this test, I had concealed this wealth of yours;

children.text: maṇirhi śobhānugato 'pyato 'nyathā na saṃspṛśedratnayaśomahārghatām // Jm_5.32 //
children.translated_text: for a gem, though accompanied by beauty, would not otherwise touch the great value and fame of a jewel.' || Jm 5.32 ||

children.text: yataḥ pradānairabhivarṣa yācakān hradān mahāmegha ivābhipūrayan /
children.translated_text: 'Since you rain upon supplicants with gifts like a great cloud filling lakes,

children.text: dhanakṣayaṃ nāpsyasi matparigrahādidaṃ kṣamethāśca viceṣṭitaṃ mama // Jm_5.33 //
children.translated_text: you shall not experience the exhaustion of wealth under my protection — and may you forgive this action of mine!' || Jm 5.33 ||

body.text: ityenamabhisaṃrādhya śakrastaccāsya vibhavasāramupasaṃhṛtya kṣamayitvā ca tatraivāntardadhe /
body.translated_text: Having thus honored him, <s>Śakra</s> restored the substance of his wealth, asked his forgiveness, and vanished right there.

body.text: tadevaṃ na vibhavakṣayāvekṣayā samṛddhyāśayā vā pradānavaidhuryamupayānti satpuruṣā iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, virtuous persons do not abandon the eagerness for giving out of regard for the loss of wealth or out of desire for prosperity.

body.text: ity aviṣahyaśreṣṭhijātakaṃ pañcamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Aviṣahya-śreṣṭhi-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Unconquerable Merchant), the fifth.

body.text: 6. Śaśajātakam
body.translated_text: 6. The <s>Śaśa-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Hare)

body.text: tiryaggatānāmapi satāṃ mahātmanāṃ śaktyanurūpā dānapravṛttirdṛṣṭā / kena nāma manuṣyabhūtena na dātavyaṃ syāt? tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even among great beings of noble nature born in animal form, the inclination toward giving in accordance with one's ability has been observed. What human being, then, should not give? As is traditionally heard:

body.text: kasmiṃścidaraṇyāyatanapradeśe manojñavīruttṛṇatarugahananicite puṣpaphalavati vaiḍūryanīlaśucivāhinyā saritā vibhūṣitaparyante mṛduśādvalāstaraṇasukhasaṃsparśadarśanīyadharaṇītale tapasvijanavicarite bodhisattvaḥ śaśo babhūva /
body.translated_text: In a certain region of a forest hermitage — dense with beautiful creepers, grasses, and trees, bearing flowers and fruits, adorned at its borders by a river flowing pure as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), with ground pleasing to the sight and soft to the touch with carpets of tender grass, frequented by ascetics — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born as a hare.

children.text: sa sattvayogādvapuṣaśca saṃpadā balaprakarṣādvipulena caujasā /
children.translated_text: He, through his excellence of character, the beauty of his form, the superiority of his strength, and the vastness of his energy,

children.text: atarkitaḥ kṣudramṛgairaśaṅkitaścacāra tasminmṛgarājalīlayā // Jm_6.1 //
children.translated_text: unsuspected and unfeared by the small animals, moved about in that [forest] with the gait of a king of beasts. || Jm 6.1 ||

children.text: svacarmājinasaṃvītaḥ svatanūruhavalkalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Clad in his own skin as an antelope-hide, wearing his own body-hair as bark-cloth,

children.text: munivattatra śuśubhe tuṣṭacittastṛṇāṅkuraiḥ // Jm_6.2 //
children.translated_text: he shone there like a sage, his mind contented with sprouts of grass. || Jm 6.2 ||

children.text: tasya maitryavadātena manovākkāyakarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Through his actions of mind, speech, and body, purified by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),

children.text: āsurjṛmbhitadaurātmyāḥ prāyaḥ śiṣyamukhā mṛgāḥ // Jm_6.3 //
children.translated_text: the animals, whose wickedness had been stifled, were for the most part like disciples. || Jm 6.3 ||

body.text: tasya guṇātiśayasaṃbhṛtena snehagauraveṇa viśeṣavattaramavabaddhahṛdayāstu ye sahāyā babhūvurudraḥ śṛgālo vānaraśca, te parasparasaṃbandhanibaddhasnehā iva bāndhavā anyonyapraṇayasaṃmānanāvirūḍhasauhārdā iva ca suhṛdaḥ saṃmodamānāstatra viharanti sma / tiryaksvabhāvavimukhāśca prāṇiṣu dayānuvṛttyā laulyapraśamādvismṛtasteyapravṛttyā dharmāvirodhinyā ca yaśo 'nuvṛttyā paṭuvijñānatvādviniyamadhīrayā ca sajjaneṣṭayā ceṣṭayā devatānāmapi vismayanīyā babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: His companions who became most especially bound in heart through the affection and reverence engendered by the superabundance of his virtues were an otter, a jackal, and a monkey. They, their affection bound by mutual connection like kinsmen, their friendship grown through mutual love and respect like true friends, dwelt there in delight. And being averse to the nature of animals, through compassion toward beings, through the calming of greed resulting in the abandonment of thievish inclinations, through conduct conforming to <s>dharma</s> and pursuit of good repute, and through sharp discernment producing firmness in self-restraint and conduct pleasing to the virtuous — they became objects of wonder even to the gods.

children.text: sukhānulome guṇabādhini krame guṇānukūle ca sukhoparodhini /
children.translated_text: When the course of action is agreeable to pleasure but injurious to virtue, or favorable to virtue but obstructive of pleasure,

children.text: naro 'pi tāvadguṇapakṣasaṃśrayādvirājate kimvatha tiryagākṛtiḥ // Jm_6.4 //
children.translated_text: even a man shines by taking the side of virtue — how much more then one in animal form! // Jm_6.4 //

children.text: abhūtsa teṣāṃ tu śaśākṛtiḥ kṛtī parānukampāpratiṣadgururguruḥ /
children.translated_text: Among them, the one in the form of a hare was a being of great accomplishment, a weighty teacher whose gravity lay in his unwavering compassion for others,

children.text: svabhāvasaṃpacca guṇakramānugā yaśo yadeṣāṃ suralokamapyagāt // Jm_6.5 //
children.translated_text: and whose innate excellence followed the course of virtue — so that the fame of these companions reached even the world of the gods. // Jm_6.5 //

body.text: atha kadācit sa mahātmā sāyāhnasamaye dharmaśravaṇārthamabhigataiḥ sabahumānamupāsyamānastaiḥ sahāyaiḥ paripūrṇaprāyamaṃḍalamādityaviprakarṣādvyavadāyamānaśobhaṃ rūpyadarpaṇamiva tsaruvirahitamīṣatpārśvāpavṛttabimbaṃ śuklapakṣacaturdaśīcandramasamuditamabhisamīkṣya sahāyānuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then once, that great soul, at the time of evening, being reverently attended upon by those companions who had come for the purpose of hearing the <s>dharma</s>, beheld the moon of the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight rising — its disc nearly full, its beauty clarifying as the sun receded, like a silver mirror without a handle with its reflection slightly turned to one side — and addressed his companions:

children.text: asāvāpūrṇaśobhena maṇḍalena hasanniva /
children.translated_text: With its orb of nearly full splendor, as if smiling,

children.text: nivedayati sādhūnāṃ candramāḥ poṣadhotsavam // Jm_6.6 //
children.translated_text: the moon announces to the virtuous the festival of <s>poṣadha</s> (the observance day). // Jm_6.6 //

body.text: tadvyaktaṃ śvaḥ pañcadaśī / yato bhavadbhiḥ poṣadhaniyamamabhisaṃpādayadbhirnyāyopalabdhenāhāraviśeṣeṇa kālopanatamatithijanaṃ pratipūjya prāṇasaṃdhāraṇamanuṣṭheyam / paśyantu bhavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Clearly, tomorrow is the fifteenth. Therefore, while observing the <s>poṣadha</s> vow, you should honor any guest who may arrive at the appropriate time with food lawfully obtained, and thus sustain your lives. Consider, honored ones:

children.text: yatsaṃprayogā virahāvasānāḥ samucchrayāḥ pātavirūpaniṣṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Since all unions end in separation, all rises culminate in the deformity of falling,

children.text: vidyullatābhaṅgaralolamāyustenaiva kāryo dṛḍhamapramādaḥ // Jm_6.7 //
children.translated_text: and life is as fleeting as the flickering of a lightning vine — for that very reason one must be firmly vigilant. // Jm_6.7 //

children.text: dānena śīlābharaṇena tasmāt puṇyāni saṃvardhayituṃ yatadhvam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, through generosity and the ornament of moral conduct, strive to increase your merit,

children.text: vivartamānasya hi janmadurge lokasya puṇyāni parā pratiṣṭhā // Jm_6.8 //
children.translated_text: for merit is the supreme refuge of the world as it turns upon the perilous road of birth. // Jm_6.8 //

children.text: tārāgaṇānāmabhibhūya lakṣmīṃ vibhāti yatkāntiguṇena somaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is by the quality of his radiance that <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) shines, overpowering the beauty of the hosts of stars,

children.text: jyotīṃṣi cākramya sahasraraśmiryaddīpyate puṇyaguṇocchrayaḥ saḥ // Jm_6.9 //
children.translated_text: and it is by the eminence of merit that the thousand-rayed one (the Sun) blazes, surpassing all other luminaries. // Jm_6.9 //

children.text: dṛptasvabhāvāḥ sacivā nṛpāśca puṇyaprabhāvāt pṛthivīśvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: Proud-natured ministers and kings, through the power of the merit of sovereigns,

children.text: sadaśvavṛttyā hatasarvagarvāḥ prītā ivājñādhuramudvahanti // Jm_6.10 //
children.translated_text: with all their arrogance subdued like well-trained horses, gladly bear the yoke of obedience. // Jm_6.10 //

children.text: puṇyairvihīnānanuyātyalakṣmīrvispandamānānapi nītimārge /
children.translated_text: Misfortune pursues those devoid of merit, even when they exert themselves on the path of statecraft,

children.text: puṇyādhikaiḥ sā hyavabhartsyamānā paryetyamarṣādiva tadvipakṣān // Jm_6.11 //
children.translated_text: for she, being repelled by those rich in merit, turns as if in indignation upon their adversaries. // Jm_6.11 //

children.text: duḥkhapratiṣṭhādayaśo 'nubaddhādapuṇyamārgāduparamya tasmāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, desisting from the path of demerit, which is grounded in suffering and attended by infamy,

children.text: śrīmatsu saukhyodayasādhaneṣu puṇyaprasaṅgeṣu matiṃ kurudhvam // Jm_6.12 //
children.translated_text: set your minds upon meritorious endeavors, which are glorious and the means of producing happiness. // Jm_6.12 //

body.text: te tathetyasyānuśāsanāṃ pratigṛhyābhivādya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ svānsvānālayānabhijagmuḥ / aciragateṣu ca teṣu sahāyeṣu sa mahātmā cintāmāpede /
body.translated_text: They, having accepted his instruction with 'So be it,' saluted him, circumambulated him, and departed to their respective abodes. And when those companions had gone not long after, that great soul fell into reflection:

children.text: atitherabhyupetasya saṃmānaṃ yena tena vā /
children.translated_text: These others have the capacity to honor a guest who has arrived

children.text: vidhātuṃ śaktirastyeṣāmatra śocyo 'hameva tu // Jm_6.13 //
children.translated_text: by one means or another — but it is I alone who am to be pitied here. // Jm_6.13 //

children.text: asmaddantāgravicchinnāḥ paritiktāstṛṇāṅkarāḥ /
children.translated_text: The grass sprouts, bitten off at the tips by my teeth and rendered bitter,

children.text: śakyā nātithaye dātuṃ sarvathā dhigaśaktitām // Jm_6.14 //
children.translated_text: cannot possibly be given to a guest — alas, shame upon this powerlessness! // Jm_6.14 //

children.text: ityasāmarthyadīnena ko nvartho jīvitena me /
children.translated_text: Thus, wretched in my incapacity, what use is life to me,

children.text: ānandaḥ śokatāṃ yāyādyasyaivamatithirmama // Jm_6.15 //
children.translated_text: whose joy would turn to sorrow if a guest of mine were treated so? // Jm_6.15 //

body.text: tatkutredānīmidamatithiparicaryāvaiguṇye niḥsāraṃ śarīrakamutsṛjyamānaṃ kasyacidupayogāya syāditi vimṛśansa mahātmā smṛtiṃ pratilebhe / aye /
body.translated_text: Then, reflecting 'Where now, in this failure of hospitality, might this worthless little body being cast off be of use to someone?' — that great soul arrived at a recollection. Ah!

children.text: svādhīnasulabhametanniravadyaṃ vidyate mamaiva khalu /
children.translated_text: There is indeed something within my own power, easily available and blameless —

children.text: atithijanapratipūjanasamartharūpaṃ śarīradhanam // Jm_6.16 //
children.translated_text: the wealth of this body, which is capable of duly honoring a guest. // Jm_6.16 //

body.text: tatkimahaṃ viṣīdāmi?
body.translated_text: Then why do I despair?

children.text: samadhigatamidaṃ mayātitheyaṃ hṛdaya vimuñca yato viṣādadainyam /
children.translated_text: O heart, abandon this dejection and wretchedness, for I have found my means of hospitality;

children.text: samupanatamanena satkariṣyāmyahamatithipraṇayaṃ śarīrakeṇa // Jm_6.17 //
children.translated_text: with this very body I shall fulfill my devotion to the guest who has arrived. // Jm_6.17 //

body.text: iti viniścatya sa mahāsattvaḥ paramamiva lābhamadhigamya paramaprītamanāstatrāvatastheḥ /
body.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that great being, as though having obtained the greatest of gains, remained there with a mind of supreme delight.

children.text: vitarkātiśaye tasya hṛdaye pravijṛmbhite /
children.translated_text: When that extraordinary resolve blossomed forth in his heart,

children.text: āviścakre prasādaśca prabhāvaśca divaukasām // Jm_6.18 //
children.translated_text: the serene grace and the majestic power of the celestial beings became manifest. // Jm_6.18 //

children.text: tataḥ praharṣādiva sācalā calā mahī babhūvānibhṛtārṇavāṃśukā /
children.translated_text: Then, as if from joy, the earth with its mountains trembled, its ocean-garments unsteady,

children.text: vitastanuḥ khe suradundubhisvanā diśaḥ prasādābharaṇāścakāśire // Jm_6.19 //
children.translated_text: the sound of divine drums spread thin across the sky, and the quarters shone, adorned with serenity. // Jm_6.19 //

children.text: prasaktamandastanitāḥ prahāsinastaḍitpinaddhāśca ghanāḥ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: Clouds all around, with continuous gentle thunder, flashing with lightning as if laughing,

children.text: parasparāśleṣavikīrṇareṇubhiḥ prasaktamenaṃ kusumairavākiran // Jm_6.20 //
children.translated_text: showered flowers upon him ceaselessly, their pollen scattered by mutual embracing. // Jm_6.20 //

children.text: samudvahandhīragatiḥ samīraṇaḥ sugandhi nānādrumapuṣpajaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: The breeze, moving with a steady pace, bearing the fragrant pollen born of various tree-blossoms,

children.text: mudā praviddhairavibhaktabhaktibhistamarcayāmāsa kṛśāṃśukairiva // Jm_6.21 //
children.translated_text: seemed to worship him with fine garments, as it were, joyfully cast forth with undivided devotion. // Jm_6.21 //

body.text: tadupalabhya pramuditavismitamanobhirdevatābhiḥ samantataḥ parikīrtyamānaṃ tasya vitarkādbhūtaṃ śakro devendraḥ samāpūryamāṇavismayakautūhalena manasā tasya mahāsattvasya bhāvajijñāsayā dvitīye 'hani gaganatalamadhyamabhilaṅghamāne paṭutarakiraṇaprabhāve savitari prasphulitamarīcijālavasanāsu bhāsvarātapavisarāvaguṇṭhitāsvanālokanakṣamāsu dikṣu saṃkṣipyamāṇacchāyeṣvabhivṛddhacīrīvirāvonnāditeṣu vanāntareṣu vicchidyamānapakṣisaṃpāteṣu dharmaklamāpītotsāheṣvadhvageṣu śakro devānāmadhipatirbrāhmaṇarūpo bhūtvā mārgapranaṣṭa iva kṣuttarṣaśramaviṣādadīnakaṇṭhaḥ sasvaraṃ prarudannātidūre teṣāṃ vicukrośa /
body.translated_text: Perceiving that, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, whose wonder and curiosity were being filled to the brim — while the extraordinary resolve of that great being was being celebrated all around by gods whose minds were delighted and astonished — on the second day, when the sun was crossing the middle of the sky's expanse with increasingly sharp rays, when the directions were wrapped in blazing heat and unfit for gazing upon with their nets of rays fully opened, when shadows were contracting, when the forest interiors resounded with the heightened cries of <s>cīrīvī</s> birds, when the flights of other birds had ceased, when travelers were exhausted in their zeal by the weariness of the noon heat — <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, having assumed the form of a Brahmin, as though lost on the road, his voice wretched with hunger, thirst, fatigue, and despair, weeping aloud, cried out not far from them:

children.text: ekaṃ sārthātparibhraṣṭaṃ bhramantaṃ gahane vane /
children.translated_text: One who has strayed from the caravan, wandering in the dense forest,

children.text: kṣucchramaklāntadehaṃ māṃ trātumarhanti sādhavaḥ // Jm_6.22 //
children.translated_text: his body exhausted by hunger, toil, and fatigue — let the virtuous ones deign to rescue me! // Jm_6.22 //

children.text: mārgāmārgajñānaniścetanaṃ māṃ diksaṃmohātkvāpi gacchantamekam /
children.translated_text: I who am unable to discern road from non-road, wandering alone somewhere in the confusion of directions,

children.text: kāntāre 'smindharmatarṣaklamārtaṃ mā bhaiḥ śabdaiḥ ko nu māṃ hlādayeta // Jm_6.23 //
children.translated_text: afflicted by weariness and thirst for <s>dharma</s> in this wilderness — who would gladden me with a 'fear not'? // Jm_6.23 //

body.text: atha te mahāsattvāstasya tena karuṇenākranditaśabdena samākampitahṛdayāḥ sasaṃbhramā drutataragatayastaṃ deśamabhijagmuḥ / mārgapranaṣṭādhvagadīnadarśanaṃ cainamabhisamīkṣya samabhigamyopacārapuraḥsaraṃ samāśvāsayanta ūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those great beings, their hearts shaken by that piteous cry of lamentation, hastened with agitation and swift steps to that place. And beholding him with the wretched appearance of a traveler lost on the road, they approached him and consoled him with words preceded by courteous attentions, saying:

children.text: kāntāre vipranaṣṭo 'hamityalaṃ vibhrameṇa te /
children.translated_text: 'I am lost in the wilderness' — enough of this distress of yours!

children.text: svasya śiṣyagaṇasyeva samīpe vartase hi naḥ // Jm_6.24 //
children.translated_text: For you are in our presence, as if among your own circle of disciples. // Jm_6.24 //

children.text: tadadya tāvadasmākaṃ paricaryāparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, today at least, by accepting our service,

children.text: vidhāyānugrahaṃ saumya śco gantāsi yathepsitam // Jm_6.25 //
children.translated_text: bestow your grace upon us, O gentle one, and then you shall go wherever you wish. // Jm_6.25 //

body.text: athodrastasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvādanumatamupanimantraṇamavetya harṣasaṃbhramatvaritagatiḥ sapta rohitamatsyānsamupanīyāvocadenam -
body.translated_text: Then the otter, understanding from his silence that the invitation was accepted, with steps quickened by joyful excitement, brought seven <s>rohita</s> fish and addressed him:

children.text: mīnāribhirvismaraṇojjhitā vā trāsotplutā vā sthalamabhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether forgotten and abandoned by fishermen, or having leapt ashore in fright,

children.text: khedaprasuptā iva sapta matsyā labdhā mayaitānnivaseha bhuktvā // Jm_6.26 //
children.translated_text: these seven fish were found by me, lying as if asleep from exhaustion — eat them and stay here. // Jm_6.26 //

body.text: atha śṛgālo 'pyenaṃ yathopalabdhamannajātamupasaṃhṛtya praṇāmapuraḥsaraṃ sādaramityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the jackal too, having gathered whatever food he had obtained, spoke to him respectfully with a salutation, saying with care:

children.text: ekā ca godhā daghibhājanaṃ ca kenāpi saṃtyaktamihādhyagaccham /
children.translated_text: 'A monitor lizard and a pot of curds, abandoned here by someone, I have found;

children.text: tanme hitāvekṣitayopayujya vane 'stu te 'sminguṇavāsa vāsaḥ // Jm_6.27 //
children.translated_text: use these, offered with regard for your welfare, and let your dwelling in this forest be a dwelling among virtues.' // Jm_6.27 //

body.text: ityuktvā paramaprītamanāstadasmai samupajahāra /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, with a mind of supreme delight, he presented them to him.

body.text: atha vānaraḥ paripākaguṇādupajātamārdavāni manaḥśilācūrṇarañjitānīvātipiñjarāṇyatiraktabandhanamūlāni piṇḍīgatānyāmraphalānyādāya sāñjalipragrahamenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the monkey, carrying mangoes gathered in clusters — softened by the quality of ripeness, exceedingly golden as if dusted with <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) powder, with deeply reddened stems — addressed him with hands joined in reverence:

children.text: āmrāṇi pakvānyudakaṃ manojñaṃ chāyā ca satsaṃgamasaukhyaśītā /
children.translated_text: 'Ripe mangoes, delightful water, and shade cool with the pleasure of good company —

children.text: ityasti me brahmavidāṃ variṣṭha bhuktvaitadatraiva tavāstu vāsaḥ // Jm_6.28 //
children.translated_text: these are mine to offer, O best among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>; eat and let your stay be here.' // Jm_6.28 //

body.text: atha śaśaḥ samupasṛtyainamupacārakriyānantaraṃ sabahumānamudīkṣamāṇaḥ svena śarīreṇopanimantrayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the hare, having approached him and after performing courteous attentions, gazing at him with great reverence, invited him with his own body:

children.text: na santi mudgā na tilā na taṇḍulā vane vivṛddhasya śaśasya kecana /
children.translated_text: 'There are no beans, no sesame seeds, no rice grains — nothing at all for a hare raised in the forest;

children.text: śarīrametattvanalābhisaṃskṛtaṃ mamopayujyādya tapovane vasa // Jm_6.29 //
children.translated_text: this body of mine, consecrated by fire, use it and dwell today in this grove of austerities.' // Jm_6.29 //

children.text: yadasti yasyepsitasādhanaṃ dhanaṃ sa tanniyuṅkte 'rthisamāgamotsave /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever wealth one has that can accomplish what is desired, one devotes it at the festival of a supplicant's arrival;

children.text: na cāsti dehādadhikaṃ ca me dhanaṃ pratīccha sarvasvamidaṃ yato mama // Jm_6.30 //
children.translated_text: and I have no wealth greater than this body — accept therefore this, my all.' // Jm_6.30 //

body.text: śakra uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: anyasyāpi vadhaṃ tāvatkuryādasmadvidhaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: 'One such as I would not even kill another being —

children.text: iti darśitasauhārde kathā kaiva bhavadvidhe // Jm_6.31 //
children.translated_text: what need is there then to speak of one like you, who has shown such tender friendship?' // Jm_6.31 //

body.text:
śaśa uvāca - upapannarūpamidamāsannānukrośe brāhmaṇe / tadihaiva tāvadbhavānāstāmasmadanugrahāpekṣayā yāvatkutaścidātmānugrahopāyamāsādayāmīti /
atha śakro devānāmindrastasya bhāvamavetya taptatapanīyavarṇaṃ sphuratpratanujvālaṃ vikīryamāṇavisphuliṅgaprakaraṃ nirdhūmamaṅgārarāśimabhinirmame / atha śaśaḥ samantato 'nuvilokayaṃstamagniskandhaṃ dadarśa / dṛṣṭvā ca prītamanāḥ śakramuvāca - samadhigato 'yaṃ mayātmānugrahopāyaḥ / tadasmaccharīropayogātsaphalāmanugrahāśāṃ me kartuṃmarhasi / paśya mahābrāhmaṇa /
deyaṃ ca ditsāpravaṇaṃ ca cittaṃ bhavadvidhenātithinā ca yogaḥ /
body.translated_text: The hare said: 'This is a fitting response from a Brahmin in whom compassion is near at hand. Then please wait right here, with an expectation of favor from me, while I procure from somewhere the means of self-offering.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, perceiving his intention, created a heap of embers — the color of molten gold, with thin flickering flames, scattering showers of sparks, and smokeless. Then the hare, looking all around, beheld that mass of fire. And seeing it, with a delighted heart, he said to <s>Śakra</s>: 'I have found the means of self-offering. Therefore, deign to make my hope of grace fruitful by making use of this body of mine. Behold, O great Brahmin!

body.text: nāvāptumetaddhi sukhena śakyaṃ tatsyādamoghaṃ bhavadāśrayānme // Jm_6.32 //
body.translated_text: The gift is ready, my heart is inclined to giving, and the meeting is with a guest such as you — for this is not easily obtained; so may my reliance upon you not be in vain.' // Jm_6.32 //

body.text: ityanunīya sa mahātmā saṃmānanādarādatithipriyatayā cainamabhivādya,
body.translated_text: Having thus entreated him, that great soul, out of respect for honoring a guest and out of devotion to the pleasure of a guest, saluted him.

children.text: tataḥ sa taṃ vahnimabhijvalantaṃ nidhiṃ dhanārthī sahasaiva dṛṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that blazing fire suddenly, as a man seeking wealth sees a treasure,

children.text: pareṇa harṣeṇa samāruroha toyaṃ hasatpadmamivaikahaṃsaḥ // Jm_6.33 //
children.translated_text: he leapt upon it with supreme joy, like a solitary goose alighting upon a lake with smiling lotuses. // Jm_6.33 //

body.text: taddṛṣṭvā paramavismayāvarjitamatirdevānāmadhipatiḥ svameva vapurāsthāya divyakusumavarṣapuraḥsarībhirmanaḥśrutisukhābhirvāgbhirabhipūjya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ kamalapalāśalakṣmīsamṛddhābhyāṃ bhāsurāṅgalībhūṣaṇālaṃkṛtābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ svayameva cainaṃ parigṛhya tridaśebhyaḥ saṃdarśayāmāsa / paśyantvatrabhavantastridaśālayanivāsino devāḥ, samanumodantāṃ cedamativismayanīyaṃ karmāvadānamasya mahāsattvasya /
body.translated_text: Beholding that, the lord of the gods, his mind overcome with supreme wonder, assuming his own true form, and having honored that great being with celestial showers of flowers accompanied by words delightful to mind and ear, took him up with his own hands — adorned with brilliant finger-ornaments and resplendent as lotus petals — and displayed him to the <s>Tridaśa</s> gods, saying: 'Let the gods dwelling in the celestial abodes behold! And let them rejoice at this most wondrous deed and heroic act of this great being!

children.text: tyaktaṃ batānena yathā śarīraṃ niḥśaṅkamadyātithivatsalena /
children.translated_text: How fearlessly this body was abandoned today by one so devoted to his guest!

children.text: nirmālyamapyevamakampamānā nālaṃ parityaktumadhīrasattvāḥ // Jm_6.34 //
children.translated_text: Those of feeble spirit could not so unflinchingly cast off even a withered garland. // Jm_6.34 //

children.text: jātiḥ kveyaṃ tadvirodhi kva cedaṃ tyāgaudāryaṃ cetasaḥ pāṭavaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: What is this lowly birth, and what contrasting it is this magnificence of generosity and keenness of mind!

children.text: vispaṣṭo 'yaṃ puṇyamandādarāṇāṃ pratyādeśo devatānāṃ nṛṇāṃ ca // Jm_6.35 //
children.translated_text: This is a clear rebuke to gods and men who are indifferent to merit. // Jm_6.35 //

children.text: aho bata guṇābhyāsavāsitāsya yathā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Ah, how wonderful is the disposition of one whose mind is perfumed by the practice of virtues!

children.text: aho sadvṛttavātsalyaṃ kriyaudāryeṇa darśitam // Jm_6.36 //
children.translated_text: Ah, how his devotion to righteous conduct has been demonstrated by the nobility of his deed! // Jm_6.36 //

body.text: atha śakrastatkarmātiśayavikhyāpanārthaṃ lokahitāvekṣī śaśabimbalakṣaṇena vaijayantasya prāsādavarasya sudharmāyāśca devasabhāyāḥ kūṭāgārakarṇike candramaṇḍalaṃ cābhyalaṃcakāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, looking toward the welfare of the world, in order to proclaim the extraordinary nature of that deed, adorned the pinnacle-chamber of the supreme palace <s>Vaijayanta</s> and the divine assembly-hall <s>Sudharmā</s> with the mark of a hare-figure, and also [adorned] the orb of the moon.

children.text: sampūrṇe 'dyāpi tadidaṃ śaśabimbaṃ niśākare /
children.translated_text: Even today, this hare-figure upon the night-maker, now fully visible,

children.text: chāyāmayamivādarśe rājate divi rājate // Jm_6.37 //
children.translated_text: shines in the heavens like a shadow-image in a mirror. || Jm 6.37 ||

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti lokena kumudākarahāsanaḥ /
children.translated_text: From that time onward, the moon, who makes the <s>kumuda</s> lotuses and the hands [of all] laugh,

children.text: kṣaṇadātilakaścandraḥ śaśāṅka iti kīrtyate // Jm_6.38 //
children.translated_text: the forehead-ornament of the night, is celebrated by the world as '<s>Śaśāṅka</s>' (the hare-marked one). || Jm 6.38 ||

body.text: te 'pyudraśṛgālavānarāstataścyutvā devaloka upapannāḥ kalyāṇamitraṃ samāsādya //
body.translated_text: And those — the otter, the jackal, and the monkey — having departed from that [life], were reborn in the world of the gods, having encountered the good spiritual friend.

body.text:
tadevaṃ tiryaggatānāmapi mahāsattvānāṃ śaktyanurūpā dānapravṛttirdṛṣṭā /
kena nāma manuṣyabhūtena na dātavyaṃ syāt? tathā tiryaggatā api guṇavātsalyāt saṃpūjyante sadbhiriti guṇeṣvādaraḥ kārya ityevamapyunneyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, even among beings in animal births, the inclination toward giving, in proportion to their capacity, has been seen in great beings. What human being, then, should fail to give? Furthermore, this too should be inferred: that even those born as animals are honored by the virtuous on account of their devotion to good qualities, and therefore one should cultivate esteem for virtues.

body.text: iti śaśajātakaṃ ṣaṣṭham /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth [story], the <s>Śaśa Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Hare).

body.text: 7. Agastyajātakam
body.translated_text: 7. The <s>Agastya Jātaka</s>

body.text: tapovanasthānāmapyalaṃkārastyāgaśauryaṃ prāgeva gṛhasthānāmiti / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even for those dwelling in a hermitage, the ornament [of character] is generosity and courage — how much more so for householders! As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavāṃllokahitārthaṃ saṃsārādhvani vartamānaścāritraguṇaviśuddhyabhilakṣitaṃ kṣititalatilakabhūtamanyatamaṃ mahad brāhmaṇakulaṃ gaganatalamiva śaradamalaparipūrṇamaṇḍalaścandramāḥ samutpatannevābhyalaṃcakāra / sa yathākramaṃ śrutismṛtivihitānavāpya jātakarmādīn saṃskārānadhītya sāṅgānvedānkṛtsnaṃ ca kalpaṃ vyāpya vidyāyaśasā manuṣyalokaṃ guṇapriyairdātṛbhirabhyarthya pratigṛhyamāṇavibhavatvāt parāṃ dhanasamṛddhimabhijagāma /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, traversing the road of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the welfare of the world, graced a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family — one distinguished by purity of virtuous conduct, a tilaka-mark upon the surface of the earth — by being born into it, like the moon with its full and spotless autumnal orb rising into the vault of the sky. In due order, having undergone the sacraments beginning with the birth-ceremony as prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, having studied the <s>Vedas</s> with their auxiliary sciences and the entire body of ritual, having pervaded the world of men with the fame of his learning, and being entreated by virtue-loving donors who received [gifts from him], he attained supreme abundance of wealth on account of his being one whose riches were constantly replenished through acceptance.

children.text: sa bandhumitrāśritadīnavargānsaṃmānanīyānatithīngurūṃśca /
children.translated_text: The groups of kinsmen, friends, dependents, the destitute, those worthy of honor, guests, and teachers —

children.text: prahlādayāmāsa tathā samṛddhyā deśānmahāmedha ivābhivarṣan // Jm_7.1 //
children.translated_text: he delighted them all with his prosperity, like a great cloud raining down upon the lands. || Jm 7.1 ||

children.text: vidvattayā tasya yaśaḥ prakāśaṃ tattyāgaśauryādadhikaṃ cakāśe /
children.translated_text: Through his learning, his fame shone forth, and through his generosity and courage it blazed even more,

children.text: niśākarasyeva śaradviśuddhaṃ samagraśobhādhikakānti bimbam // Jm_7.2 //
children.translated_text: like the orb of the moon in autumn, pure, resplendent with complete beauty and surpassing radiance. || Jm 7.2 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā kukāryavyāsaṅgadoṣasaṃbādhaṃ pramādāspadabhūtaṃ dhanārjanarakṣaṇaprasaṅgavyākulamupaśamavirodhivyasanaśaraśatalakṣyabhūtamaparyantakarmāntānuṣṭhānaparigrahaśramamatṛptijanakaṃ kṛśāsvādaṃ gārhasthyamavetya taddoṣaviviktasukhāṃ ca dharmapratipattyanukūlāṃ mokṣadharmārambhādhiṣṭhānabhūtāṃ pravrajyāmanupaśyan mahatīmapi tāṃ dhanasamṛddhimaparikleśādhigatāṃ lokasaṃnatimanoharāṃ tṛṇavadapāsya tāpasapravrajyāvinayaniyamaparo babhūva / pravrajitamapi taṃ mahāsattvaṃ yaśaḥprakāśatvāt pūrvasaṃstavānusmaraṇāt saṃbhāvitaguṇatvāt praśamābhilakṣitatvācca śreyo 'rthī janastadguṇagaṇāvarjitamatistathaivābhijagāma / sa taṃ gṛhijanasaṃsargaṃ pravivekasukhapramāthinaṃ vyāsaṅgavikṣepāntarāyakaramabahumanyamānaḥ pravivekābhirāmatayā dakṣiṇasamudramadhyāvagāḍhamindranīlabhedābhinīlavarṇairanilabalākalitairūrmimālāvilāsairācchuritaparyantaṃ sitasikatāstīrṇabhūmibhāgaṃ puṣpaphalapallavālaṃkṛtaviṭapairnānātarubhirupaśobhitaṃ vimalasalilāśayapratīraṃ kārādvīpamadhyāsanādāśramapadaśriyā saṃyojayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, perceiving that household life was constricted by the fault of entanglement in bad deeds, a breeding-ground of negligence, disturbed by involvement in acquiring and guarding wealth, a target for hundreds of arrows of passions opposed to tranquility, exhausting through the burden of performing endless undertakings, and of meager savor that never produces satisfaction — and perceiving on the other hand that the homeless life was free from those faults, pleasant, conducive to the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, and the foundation for undertaking the path to liberation — he cast aside that great wealth, acquired without hardship and captivating to the minds of the world, as if it were grass, and became devoted to the discipline and observances of an ascetic's renunciation. Even after his renunciation, people seeking their welfare, their minds captivated by the aggregate of his virtues, continued to approach that great being just as before, because of the renown of his fame, the recollection of his former praise, the esteem for his qualities, and the marks of his tranquility. He, not esteeming that contact with the household community — which was destructive of the happiness of solitude and an obstacle causing the distraction of attachment — out of his delight in solitude, connected the island of <s>Kāra</s>, plunged deep into the southern ocean, with the beauty of a hermitage-site — an island whose periphery was playfully ruffled by garlands of waves, dark as the blue of sapphire fragments, agitated by the force of the wind, whose terrain was strewn with white sand, adorned with various trees decorated with flowers, fruits, and young shoots, and situated on the shore of a lake of pure water.

children.text: sutanustapasā tatra sa reje tapasātanuḥ /
children.translated_text: There, emaciated by austerity, that slender one shone,

children.text: navacandra iva vyomni kāntatvenākṛśaḥ kṛśaḥ // Jm_7.3 //
children.translated_text: like a new crescent moon in the sky — attractive despite his thinness, thin yet not diminished. || Jm 7.3 ||

children.text: praśamanibhṛtaceṣṭitendriyo vrataniyamaikaraso vane vasan /
children.translated_text: Dwelling in the forest, his senses restrained with tranquil movement, absorbed solely in the essence of vows and observances,

children.text: muniriti tanubuddhiśaktibhirmṛgavihagairapi so 'nvagamyata // Jm_7.4 //
children.translated_text: he was recognized as a sage even by the deer and birds, with their slender powers of understanding. || Jm 7.4 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā pradānocitatvāttapovane 'pi nivasan kālopanatamatithijanaṃ yathāsaṃnihitena mūlaphalena śucinā salilena hṛdyābhiśca svāgatāśīrvādapeśalābhistapasvijanayogyābhirvāgbhiḥ saṃpūjayati sma / atithijanopayuktaśeṣeṇa ca yātrāmātrārthamabhyavahṛtena tena vanyenāhāreṇa vartayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, being by nature disposed to giving, even while dwelling in the hermitage, honored the guest-folk who arrived at the proper time with whatever roots and fruits were at hand, with pure water, and with heartfelt words of welcome and blessing, sweet and appropriate for an ascetic community. And he sustained himself with whatever remained after the guests had partaken — that forest food consumed only in the measure needed for bare sustenance.

body.text: tasya tapaḥprakarṣāt pravisṛtena yaśasā samāvarjitahṛdayaḥ śakro devendraḥ sthairyajijñāsayā tasya mahāsattvasya tasminnaraṇyāyatane tāpasajanopabhogayogyaṃ mūlaphalamanupūrveṇa sarvamantardhāpayāmāsa / bodhisattvo 'pi dhyānaprasṛtamānasatayā saṃtoṣaparicayādanadhimūrcchitatvādāhāre svaśarīre cānabhiṣvaṅgānna tamantardhānahetuṃ manasi cakāra / sa taruṇāni taruparṇānyadhiśrāya tairāhāraprayojanamabhiniṣpādyātṛṣyamāṇa āhāraviśeṣānutsukaḥ svasthamatistathaiva vijahāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his heart won over by the fame that had spread abroad from the intensity of his austerities, wishing to test the steadfastness of that great being, gradually caused all the roots and fruits fit for the use of ascetic folk in that forest hermitage to disappear. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, his mind absorbed in meditation, did not take note of the cause of that disappearance, because of his familiarity with contentment, because he did not cling excessively to food, and because of his detachment from his own body. Resorting to the tender leaves of trees, he accomplished the purpose of sustenance with those, and without craving, without eagerness for special food, with a tranquil mind, he continued to live just as before.

children.text: na kvacid durlabhā vṛttiḥ saṃtoṣaniyatātmanām /
children.translated_text: For those whose selves are governed by contentment, livelihood is never hard to find anywhere;

children.text: kutra nāma na vidyante tṛṇaparṇajalāśayāḥ // Jm_7.5 //
children.translated_text: where indeed are grass, leaves, and bodies of water not to be found? || Jm 7.5 ||

body.text: vismitataramanāstu śakro devendrastasya tenāvasthānena sthirataraguṇasaṃbhāvanastatparīkṣānimittaṃ tasminnaraṇyavanapradeśe nidāghakālānilavatsamagraṃ vīruttṛṇatarugaṇaṃ parṇasamṛddhyā viyojayāmāsa / atha bodhisattvaḥ pratyārdratarāṇi śīrṇaparṇāni samāhṛtya tairudakasvinnairanutkaṇṭhitamatirvartamāno dhyānasukhaprīṇitamanāstatrāmṛtatṛpta iva vijahāra /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his mind struck with even greater wonder at his perseverance in that condition, and his esteem for the firmness of his qualities even more confirmed, as a further test caused the entire host of shrubs, grasses, and trees in that forest region to be stripped of their foliage, as if by the hot-season wind. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gathering up the still somewhat moist fallen leaves, sustaining himself with those moistened in water, his mind untroubled, his heart nourished by the joy of meditation, continued to live there as if sated with nectar.

children.text: avismayaḥ śrutavatāṃ samṛddhānāmamatsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Absence of wonder in the learned, absence of envy in the prosperous,

children.text: saṃtoṣaśca vanasthānāṃ guṇaśobhāvidhiḥ paraḥ // Jm_7.6 //
children.translated_text: and contentment in forest-dwellers — these are the supreme rule of the splendor of virtues. || Jm 7.6 ||

body.text: atha śakrastena tasyādbhutarūpeṇa saṃtoṣasthairyeṇa samabhivṛddhavismayaḥ sāmarṣa iva tasya mahāsattvasya vratakāle hutāgnihotrasya parisamāptajapyasyātithijanadidṛkṣayā vyavalokayato brāhmaṇarūpamāsthāyātithiriva nāma bhūtvā purastātprādurabhūt / sa prītamanāḥ samabhigamya cainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsareṇāhārakālanivedanenopanimantrayāmāsa / tūṣṇīṃbhāvāttu tasyābhimatamupanimantraṇamavetya sa mahātmā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his wonder growing ever greater at the wondrous nature of that steadfast contentment of his, and somewhat vexed as it were, appeared before that great being — who, at the time of his religious observance, having offered his <s>agnihotra</s> oblation and completed his recitation, was looking about with desire to see if any guest had come — assuming the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and becoming, as it were, a guest. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his mind delighted, approached him and invited him with an announcement of the mealtime, preceded by pleasant words of welcome and greeting. And from his silence, understanding that the invitation was accepted, that great soul,

children.text: ditsāpraharṣavikasannayanāsyaśobhaḥ snigdhairmanaḥśrutisukhairabhinandya vākyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: his eyes and face radiant with the joy of the desire to give, with words affectionate, pleasing to the mind and ear, greeting him warmly,

children.text: kṛcchropalabdhamapi tacchrapaṇaṃ samastaṃ tasmai dadau svayamabhūcca mudeva tṛptaḥ // Jm_7.7 //
children.translated_text: gave to him all the cooked food, though obtained with difficulty, and himself became, as it were, satisfied by joy alone. || Jm 7.7 ||

body.text: sa tathaiva praviśya dhyānāgāraṃ tenaiva prītiprāmodyena tamahorātramatināmayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: He then entered his meditation-chamber and, with that very joy and gladness, passed that day and night in supreme well-being.

body.text: atha śakrastasya dvitīye tṛtīye caturthe pañcame 'pi cāhani tathaiva vratakāle purataḥ prādurabhūt / so 'pi cainaṃ pramuditataramanāstathaiva pratipūjayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s> appeared before him in the same way at the time of his observance on the second, third, fourth, and fifth days as well. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind even more delighted, honored him just as before each time.

children.text: dānābhilāṣaḥ sādhūnāṃ kṛpābhyāsavivardhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The desire to give among the virtuous, nourished by the practice of compassion,

children.text: naiti saṃkocadīnatvaṃ duḥkhaiḥ prāṇāntikairapi // Jm_7.8 //
children.translated_text: does not shrink into wretchedness even through sufferings that threaten life itself. || Jm 7.8 ||

body.text: atha śakraḥ paramavismayāviṣṭahṛdayastapaḥprakarṣādasya prārthanāmātrāpekṣaṃ tridaśapatilakṣmīsaṃparkamavagamya samutpatitabhayāśaṅkaḥ svameva vapurdivyādbhutaśobhamabhiprapadya tapaḥprayojanamenaṃ paryapṛcchat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his heart seized with the utmost wonder, perceiving that through the intensity of his austerities the splendor of the lord of the thirty gods was within the mere reach of his aspiration, alarmed and anxious, assumed his own divine form of wondrous beauty and asked him the purpose of his austerity:

children.text: bandhūnpriyānaśrumukhānvihāya parigrahānsaukhyaparigrahāṃśca /
children.translated_text: "Having left behind kinsmen, beloved ones with tear-stained faces,

children.text: āśāṅkuśaṃ nu vyavasṛjya kutra tapaḥparikleśamimaṃ śrito 'si // Jm_7.9 //
children.translated_text: and possessions — those possessions that are [but the possession of] pleasure — casting away the goad of desire, to what end have you resorted to this toil of austerity? || Jm 7.9 ||

children.text: sukhopapannānparibhūya bhogāṃcchokākulaṃ bandhujanaṃ ca hitvā /
children.translated_text: Having spurned pleasures accompanied by comfort and having abandoned a grieving circle of kinsmen,

children.text: na hetunālpena hi yānti dhīrāḥ sukhoparodhīni tapovanāni // Jm_7.10 //
children.translated_text: for the steadfast do not enter hermitages — which obstruct comfort — without a great reason. || Jm 7.10 ||

children.text: vaktavyametanmayi manyase cetkautūhalaṃ no 'rhasi tadvinetum /
children.translated_text: If you consider me worthy, this should be told; you should not dismiss our curiosity.

children.text: kiṃ nāma tadyasya guṇapraveśavaśīkṛtaivaṃ bhavato 'pi buddhiḥ // Jm_7.11 //
children.translated_text: What is that [goal], by whose entry into the domain of virtues your mind too is thus captivated?" || Jm 7.11 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - śrūyatāṃ mārṣa yannimitto 'yaṃ mama prayatnaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Listen, noble sir, to the reason for this effort of mine.

children.text: punaḥ punarjātiratīva duḥkhaṃ jarāvipadvayādhivirūpatāśca /
children.translated_text: "The perpetual cycle of birth is exceedingly painful, and old age, calamity, disease, and deformity —

children.text: martavyamityākulatā ca buddherlokānatastrātumiti sthito 'smi // Jm_7.12 //
children.translated_text: and the agitation of the mind at the thought 'I must die' — I am resolved to rescue beings from all this." || Jm 7.12 ||

body.text: atha śakro devendro nāyamasmadgatāṃ śriyamabhikāmayata iti samāśvāsitahṛdayaḥ subhāṣitena tena cābhiprasāditamatiryuktamityabhipūjya tadasya vacanaṃ varapradānena bodhisattvamupanimantrayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, his heart reassured that 'this one does not covet the prosperity belonging to us,' his mind won over by that fine speech, having honored his words with 'Well said!', invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with the offer of a boon:

children.text: atra te tāpasajanapratirūpe subhāṣite /
children.translated_text: "In this fine speech of yours, befitting an ascetic,

children.text: dadāmi kāśyapa varaṃ tadvṛṇīṣva yadicchasi // Jm_7.13 //
children.translated_text: I grant you a boon, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>; choose whatever you wish." || Jm 7.13 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo bhavabhogasukheṣvanāsthaḥ prārthanāmeva duḥkhamavagacchansātmībhūtasaṃtoṣaḥ śakramuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, indifferent to the pleasures of worldly existence, understanding desire itself as suffering, and contentment having become second nature, said to <s>Śakra</s>:

children.text: dātumicchasi cenmahyamanugrahakaraṃ varam /
children.translated_text: "If you wish to give me a boon that confers a blessing,

children.text: vṛṇe tasmādahamimaṃ devānāṃ pravaraṃ varam // Jm_7.14 //
children.translated_text: then I choose this, the foremost boon among the gods: || Jm 7.14 ||

children.text: dārānmano 'bhilaṣitāṃstanayānprabhutva marthānabhīpsitaviśālatarāṃśca labdhvā /
children.translated_text: "Having obtained wives desired by the mind, sons, sovereignty, and riches vast and longed for,

children.text: yenābhitaptamatireti na jātu tṛptiṃ lobhānalaḥ sa hṛdayaṃ mama nābhyupeyāt // Jm_7.15 //
children.translated_text: may that fire of greed — by which the afflicted mind never attains satisfaction — never approach my heart!" || Jm 7.15 ||

body.text: atha śakrastayā tasya saṃtoṣapravaṇamānasatayā subhāṣitābhivyañjitayā bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃprasāditamatiḥ punarbodhisattvaṃ sādhu sādhviti praśasya vareṇopacchandayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, his mind won over to an even greater degree by that inclination of his heart toward contentment, as revealed through his fine speech, again praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with 'Excellent! Excellent!' and offered him yet another boon:

children.text: atrāpi te munijanapratirūpe subhāṣite /
children.translated_text: "In this fine speech too, befitting a sage,

children.text: pratiprābhṛtavatprītyā prayacchāmyaparaṃ varam // Jm_7.16 //
children.translated_text: I grant you, as a reciprocal gift out of delight, another boon." || Jm 7.16 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kleśaviyogasyaiva durlabhatāmasya pradarśayanvarayācñāpadeśena punarapyasmai dharmaṃ deśayāsāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, showing the difficulty of separation from the afflictions, under the pretext of requesting a boon, taught him the <s>Dharma</s> once again:

children.text: dadāsi me yadi varaṃ sadguṇāvāsa vāsava /
children.translated_text: "If you grant me a boon, O <s>Vāsava</s>, abode of good qualities,

children.text: vṛṇe tenemamaparaṃ devendrānavaraṃ varam // Jm_7.17 //
children.translated_text: then I choose this other boon, no less than one from the lord of the gods: || Jm 7.17 ||

children.text: arthādapi bhraṃśamavāpnuvanti varṇaprasādādyaśasaḥ sukhācca /
children.translated_text: "People fall even from wealth, from the grace of their complexion, from fame, and from happiness;

children.text: yenābhibhūtā dviṣateva sattvāḥ sadveṣavahnirmama dūrataḥ syāt // Jm_7.18 //
children.translated_text: may that fire of hatred — by which beings, as if overpowered by an enemy, are overcome — be far from me!" || Jm 7.18 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā śakro devānāmadhipatirvismayavaśāt sādhu sādhvityenamabhipraśasya punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, overcome with wonder, praised him saying 'Excellent! Excellent!' and spoke again:

children.text: sthāne pravrajitānkīrtiranurakteva sevate /
children.translated_text: "It is fitting that fame attends the renunciants as if enamored;

children.text: tadvaraṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva madatrāpi subhāṣite // Jm_7.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore accept this boon from me for this fine speech as well." || Jm 7.19 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kleśaprātikūlyāt kliṣṭasattvasaṃparkavigarhāṃ vratisaṃpratigrahāpadeśena kurvannityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, expressing his aversion to association with afflicted beings due to his opposition to the afflictions, under the pretext of a vow-keeper's choice, spoke thus:

children.text: śṛṇuyāmapi naiva jātu bālaṃ na ca vīkṣeya na cainamālapeyam /
children.translated_text: "May I never even hear a fool, nor see one, nor be smeared by contact with one,

children.text: na ca tena nivāsakhedaduḥkhaṃ samupeyāṃ varamityahaṃ vṛṇe tvām // Jm_7.20 //
children.translated_text: nor endure the suffering of the weariness of dwelling with one — this is the boon I choose from you." || Jm 7.20 ||

body.text: śakra uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: anukampyo viśeṣeṇa satāmāpadgato nanu /
children.translated_text: "Is not one who has fallen into misfortune especially deserving of compassion from the virtuous?

children.text: āpadāṃ mūlabhūtatvādbālyaṃ cādhamamiṣyate // Jm_7.21 //
children.translated_text: And foolishness, being the very root of calamities, is regarded as the lowest [condition]. || Jm 7.21 ||

children.text: karuṇāśrayabhūtasya bālasyāsya viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Why, then, being compassionate,

children.text: kṛpālurapi sankasmānna darśanamapīcchasi // Jm_7.22 //
children.translated_text: do you not wish even to see this fool, who is especially deserving of compassion? || Jm 7.22 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - agatyā mārṣa / paśyatvatrabhavān /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Out of helplessness, noble sir. Let your honor observe:

children.text: kathaṃcidapi śakyeta yadi bālaścikitsitum /
children.translated_text: "If a fool could somehow be cured,

children.text: taddhitodyoganiryatnaḥ kathaṃ syāditi madvidhaḥ // Jm_7.23 //
children.translated_text: how could one such as I fail to exert himself in the effort toward his welfare? || Jm 7.23 ||

body.text: itthaṃ caiṣa cikitsāprayogasyāpātramiti gṛhyatām /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, let it be understood that this [fool] is not a fit vessel for the application of cure:

children.text: sunayavadanayaṃ nayatyayaṃ paramapi cātra niyoktumicchati /
children.translated_text: He considers non-policy as policy, and even wishes to compel others therein."

children.text: anucitavinayārjavakramo hitamapi cābhihitaḥ prakupyati // Jm_7.24 //
children.translated_text: and one unaccustomed to the order of humility and rectitude grows angry even when told what is beneficial." || Jm 7.24 ||

children.text: iti paṇḍitamānamohadagdhe hitavādiṣvapi roṣarūkṣabhāve /
children.translated_text: "Thus, when one is scorched by the delusion of thinking himself learned, and is harsh with anger even toward those who speak for his good,

children.text: rabhase vinayābhiyogamāndyādvada kastatra hitārpaṇābhyupāyaḥ // Jm_7.25 //
children.translated_text: and is impetuous due to sluggishness in the practice of discipline — tell me, what means is there to bestow benefit upon him?" || Jm 7.25 ||

children.text: ityagatyā suraśreṣṭha karuṇāpravaṇairapi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, O best of gods, even by those inclined to compassion, being helpless,

children.text: bālasyādravyabhūtasya na darśanamapīṣyate // Jm_7.26 //
children.translated_text: the very sight of a fool who is an unfit vessel is not desired." || Jm 7.26 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā śakraḥ sādhu sādhvityenamabhinandya subhāṣitābhiprasāditamatiḥ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Śakra</s>, saying "Excellent, excellent!" and congratulating him, his mind gladdened by the well-spoken words, said again —

children.text: na subhāṣitaratnānāmarghaḥ kaścana vidyate /
children.translated_text: "There is no price for the gems of well-spoken words;

children.text: kusumāñjalivatprītyā dadāmyatrāpi te varam // Jm_7.27 //
children.translated_text: like an offering of flowers, with joy I grant you a boon here too." || Jm 7.27 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sarvāvasthāsukhatāṃ sajjanasya pradarśayañchakramuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating that a good person finds happiness in every condition, said to <s>Śakra</s> —

children.text: vīkṣeya dhīraṃ śṛṇuyāṃ ca dhīraṃ syānme nivāsaḥ saha tena śakra /
children.translated_text: "May I behold the steadfast and hear the steadfast; may my dwelling be with such a one, O <s>Śakra</s>;

children.text: saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ tena sahaiva bhūyādetaṃ varaṃ devavara prayaccha // Jm_7.28 //
children.translated_text: may I have conversation with him alone — grant me this boon, O best of gods." || Jm 7.28 ||

body.text: śakra uvāca - atipakṣapāta iva khalu te dhīraṃ prati / taducyatāṃ tāvat /
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: "Your partiality toward the steadfast is indeed excessive. But let it be said —

children.text: kiṃ nu dhīrastavākārṣīdvada kāśyapa kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: "What has the steadfast one done for you? Speak the reason, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>;

children.text: adhīra iva yenāsi dhīradarśanalālasaḥ // Jm_7.29 //
children.translated_text: why is it that, as if unsteady yourself, you are so eager for the sight of the steadfast?" || Jm 7.29 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sajjanamāhātmyamasya pradarśayannuvāca - śrūyatāṃ mārṣa, yena me dhīradarśanamevābhilaṣate matiḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, demonstrating to him the greatness of the virtuous, said: "Hear, O noble sir, the reason my mind longs for the sight of the steadfast:

children.text: vrajati guṇapathena ca svayaṃ nayati parānapi tena vartmanā /
children.translated_text: "He himself walks the path of virtue and also leads others along that road;

children.text: vacanamapi na rūkṣamakṣamāṃ janayati tasya hitopasaṃhitam // Jm_7.30 //
children.translated_text: and even his speech, though directed toward benefit, does not generate harshness or impatience." || Jm 7.30 ||

children.text: aśaṭhavinayabhūṣaṇaḥ sadā hitamiti lambhayituṃ sa śakyate /
children.translated_text: "Adorned with guileless humility, he can always be trusted to bestow what is beneficial;

children.text: iti mama guṇapakṣapātinī namati matirguṃṇapakṣapātini // Jm_7.31 //
children.translated_text: thus my mind, partial to virtues, bows to him who is partial to virtues." || Jm 7.31 ||

body.text: athainaṃ śakraḥ sādhūpapannarūpamidamiti cābhinandya samabhivṛddhaprasādaḥ punarvareṇopanimantrayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, congratulating him with "Well done, this is fitting!" and with his favor greatly increased, again invited him with a boon —

children.text: kāmaṃ saṃtoṣasātmatvātsarvatra kṛtameva te /
children.translated_text: "Indeed, because of your nature of contentment, you are satisfied everywhere;

children.text: madanugrahabuddhyā tu grahītuṃ varamarhasi // Jm_7.32 //
children.translated_text: but out of regard for my wish to favor you, you ought to accept a boon." || Jm 7.32 ||

children.text: upakārāśayā bhaktyā śaktyā caiva samastayā /
children.translated_text: "When earnest affection is offered with a desire to help, with devotion, and with one's full capacity,

children.text: prayuktasyātiduḥkho hi praṇayasyāpratigrahaḥ // Jm_7.33 //
children.translated_text: its non-acceptance is truly most painful." || Jm 7.33 ||

body.text: atha tasya parāmupakartukāmatāmavekṣya bodhisattvastatpriyahitakāmatayā pradānānutarṣaprābalyamasmai prakāśayannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving his desire to benefit others, and wishing what was dear and beneficial to him, revealed to him the intensity of his thirst for giving, and said —

children.text: tvadīyamannaṃ kṣayadoṣavarjitaṃ manaśca ditsāpratipattipeśalam /
children.translated_text: "May your food be free from the fault of exhaustion, and may my mind be skilled in the determination to give;

children.text: viśuddhaśīlābharaṇāśca yācakā mama syuretāṃ varasaṃpadaṃ vṛṇe // Jm_7.34 //
children.translated_text: and may the supplicants be adorned with pure moral conduct — I choose this excellent boon." || Jm 7.34 ||

body.text: śakra uvāca - subhāṣitaratnākaraḥ khalvatrabhavān / api ca -
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: "Your honor is truly a mine of gems of well-spoken words. Moreover —

children.text: yadabhiprārthitaṃ sarvaṃ tattathaiva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: "All that you have desired shall come to pass just so;

children.text: dadāmi ca punastubhyaṃ varamasminsubhāṣite // Jm_7.35 //
children.translated_text: and I give you yet another boon for this beautiful speech." || Jm 7.35 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: varaṃ mamānugrahasaṃpadākaraṃ dadāsi cetsarvadivaukasāṃ vara /
children.translated_text: "If you grant a boon that is a source of the wealth of your favor, O best of all celestials,

children.text: na mābhyupeyāḥ punarityabhijvalannimaṃ varaṃ dainyanisūdanaṃ vṛṇe // Jm_7.36 //
children.translated_text: may you not visit me again — blazing forth, I choose this boon that destroys wretchedness." || Jm 7.36 ||

body.text: atha śakraḥ sāmarṣavadenamativismayamāna uvāca - mā tāvadbhoḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, as if indignant, said with extreme astonishment: "Wait, sir!

children.text: japavratejyāvidhinā tapaḥśramairjano 'yamanvicchati darśanaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: "People seek my audience through prayer, vows, sacrificial rites, and the toil of austerities;

children.text: bhavānpunarnecchati kena hetunā varapraditsābhigatasya me sataḥ // Jm_7.37 //
children.translated_text: but you, on the other hand, do not desire it — for what reason, when I have come wishing to grant boons?" || Jm 7.37 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - alaṃ te manyupraṇayena / samanuneṣyāmyahamatrabhavantaṃ devarāja na hyasāvadākṣiṇyānuvṛttirna cāpyabahumānaviceṣṭitamasamavadhānakāmyatā vā bhavati bhavatām / kiṃ tu
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Enough of this indignation born of affection. I shall conciliate your honor, O king of gods. For this is neither an act of discourtesy nor a gesture of disrespect, nor a desire for inattention toward you. Rather —

children.text: nirīkṣya te rūpamamānuṣādbhutaṃ prasannakānti jvalitaṃ ca tejasā /
children.translated_text: "Beholding your superhuman, wondrous form, radiant with serene beauty and blazing with splendor,

children.text: bhavetpramādastapasīti me bhayaṃ prasādasaumyādapi darśanāttava // Jm_7.38 //
children.translated_text: there might be negligence in my austerities — this is my fear, even from your gracious and gentle appearance." || Jm 7.38 ||

body.text: atha śakraḥ praṇamya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ tatraivāntardadhe / prabhātāyāṃ ca rajanyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ śakraprabhāvopahṛtaṃ prabhūtaṃ divyamannapānaṃ dadarśa / śakropanimantraṇāhūtāni cānekāni pratyekabuddhaśatāni vyāyatābaddhaparikarāṃśca pariveṣaṇasajjānanekāṃśca devakumārān /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, having bowed to him and circumambulated him, vanished right there. And when night had passed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> beheld an abundance of divine food and drink brought by <s>Śakra</s>'s power. And many hundreds of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, summoned by <s>Śakra</s>'s invitation, [had arrived], along with many divine princes, girded and ready, prepared for serving.

children.text: tenānnapānavidhinā sa munirmaharṣīn saṃtarpayanmudamudāratarāmavāpa /
children.translated_text: Satisfying the great sages with that provision of food and drink, the sage attained a most exalted joy;

children.text: vṛttyā ca tāpasajanocitayābhireme dhyānāpramāṇaniyamena śamena caiva // Jm_7.39 //
