children.translated_text: and he delighted in a livelihood proper for ascetics, in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurable meditations), restraint, and tranquility. || Jm 7.39 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ tapovanasthānāmapyalaṃkārastyāgaśauryaṃ prāgeva gṛhasthānāmiti tyāgaśauryeṇālaṃkartavya evātmā satpuruṣeṇeti / dānapatisaṃpraharṣaṇāyāmapyunneyaṃ lobhadveṣamohabālyavigarhāyāṃ kalyāṇamitrasaṃparkaguṇe saṃtoṣakathāyāṃ tathāgatamāhātmye ca / evaṃ pūrvajanmasvapi subhāṣitaratnātiśayākaraḥ sa bhagavān prāgeva saṃbuddha iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, the valor of generosity is an ornament even for those dwelling in ascetic groves, let alone for householders — therefore the virtuous person should adorn himself with the valor of generosity. This [story] is also to be cited for inspiring the lord of giving, for condemning greed, hatred, delusion, and folly, for [teaching] the virtue of association with a spiritual friend, in a discourse on contentment, and in [describing] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, even in former births, the Blessed One was a mine of the excellence of gems of well-spoken words — how much more so when fully awakened.

body.text: ityagastyajātakaṃ saptamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh [story], the <s>Agastya Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 8. Maitrībalajātakam
body.translated_text: 8. The <s>Maitrībala Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Power of Loving-Kindness)

body.text: na paraduḥkhāturāḥ svasukhamavekṣante mahākāruṇikāḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Those of great compassion, afflicted by the suffering of others, do not regard their own happiness. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila svamāhātmyakāruṇyābhiprapanno jagatparitrāṇādhyāśayaḥ, pradānadamaniyamasauratyādibhirlokānugrahānukūlairguṇātiśayairabhivardhamānaḥ sarvasattvamaitramanā maitrabalo nāma rājā babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with his own greatness and compassion, with the aspiration to protect the world, ever increasing in extraordinary virtues favorable to the welfare of beings — such as giving, self-restraint, discipline, and gentleness — a mind of loving-kindness toward all beings, became a king named <s>Maitrībala</s> (Power of Loving-Kindness).

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ vā yadabhūtprajānāṃ tasyāpi rājñastadabhūttathaiva /
children.translated_text: Whatever suffering or happiness befell his subjects, that same [suffering or happiness] befell that king as well;

children.text: ataḥ prajārakṣaṇadakṣiṇo 'sau śastraṃ ca śāstraṃ ca parāmamarśa // Jm_8.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore, skilled in the protection of his people, he mastered both arms and the sacred sciences. || Jm 8.1 ||

children.text: narendracūḍādhṛtaśāsanasya tasya tvalaṅkāravadāsa śastram /
children.translated_text: For him whose authority was upheld by the crowns of other kings, weaponry served as an ornament;

children.text: vispaṣṭarūpaṃ dadṛśe ca śāstraṃ nayeṣu lokasya hitodayeṣu // Jm_8.2 //
children.translated_text: and the sacred sciences were clearly manifested in his policies conducive to the welfare of the world. || Jm 8.2 ||

children.text: vinigrahapragrahayoḥ pravṛttirdharmoparodhaṃ na cakāra tasya /
children.translated_text: His exercise of punishment and reward did not cause any obstruction of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: hitāśayatvānnayanaipuṇācca parīkṣakasyeva pituḥ prajāsu // Jm_8.3 //
children.translated_text: because of his benevolent intention and his skill in statecraft — like a discerning father toward his children. || Jm 8.3 ||

body.text: tasyaivaṃ dharmeṇa prajāḥ pālayataḥ satyatyāgopaśamaprajñādibhiśca parahitapariṇāmanātsaviśeṣodāttakramairbodhisambhāravidhibhirabhivardhamānasya kadācitkasmiṃścidaparādhe yakṣāṇāmadhipatinā svaviṣayātpravrājitā ojohārāḥ pañca yakṣāḥ paravadhadakṣāstadviṣayamabhijagmuḥ / vyapagatasarvopadravatvācca nityapravṛttavividhotsavaṃ parayā sampadā samupetarūpaṃ pramuditatuṣṭapuṣṭajanamabhisamīkṣya tadviṣayaṃ tannivāsināṃ puruṣāṇāmojāṃsyapahartuṃ teṣāmabhilāṣo babhūva /
body.translated_text: As he thus governed his subjects through <s>Dharma</s>, ever increasing through the practices for accumulating the requisites of enlightenment (<s>bodhisambhāra</s>) — truth, generosity, tranquility, wisdom, and the like — devoted to the welfare of others in an especially exalted manner, at a certain time, five <s>Yakṣas</s> who consumed vital essences, skilled in killing others, having been banished from his own territory by the lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s> for some offense, came to that [king's] domain. And seeing that domain — free from all calamities, with various festivals perpetually in progress, endowed with supreme prosperity, its people delighted, contented, and thriving — they conceived the desire to steal the vital essences of the people dwelling there.

children.text: te pareṇāpi yatnena sampravṛttāḥ svakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Though they exerted themselves with utmost effort in their task,

children.text: naiva tadviṣayasthānāṃ hartumojaḥ prasehire // Jm_8.4 //
children.translated_text: they were unable to steal the vital essence of any dwelling in that territory. || Jm 8.4 ||

children.text: tasya prabhāvātiśayānnṛpasya mameti yatraiva babhūva buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the surpassing power of that king, wherever his thought was "this is mine,"

children.text: saivāsya rakṣā paramāsa tasmādojāṃsi hartuṃ na viṣehire te // Jm_8.5 //
children.translated_text: that very [thought] served as the supreme protection; therefore they were unable to steal the vital essences. || Jm 8.5 ||

body.text: yadā ca paramapi prayatnaṃ kurvanto naiva śaknuvanti sma kasyacidviṣayanivāsino janasyaujo 'pahartumatha teṣāṃ parasparamavekṣyaitadabhūt / kiṃ nu khalvidaṃ mārṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: And when, despite exerting the utmost effort, they were utterly unable to steal the vital essence of any person dwelling in that territory, they looked at one another and thought: "What indeed is this, noble sirs?

children.text: asmatprabhāvapratighātayogyā vidyātapaḥsiddhimayā viśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Special powers derived from the perfection of knowledge, austerities, and supernatural attainments, capable of resisting our power —

children.text: na santi caiṣāmatha cādya sarve vyarthābhidhānatvamupāgatāḥ smaḥ // Jm_8.6 //
children.translated_text: these people do not possess such; yet today we have all become utterly ineffective." || Jm 8.6 ||

body.text: atha te yakṣā brāhmaṇavarṇamātmānamabhinirmāya samanucaranto dadṛśuḥ pratyaraṇyacaramanyatamaṃ gopālakaṃ saśādvale chāyādrumamūle sopānatkaṃ saṃniṣaṇṇaṃ sapallavairvanatarukusumairviracitāṃ mālāmudvahantaṃ dakṣiṇato vinyastadaṇḍaparaśumekākinaṃ rajjuvartanavyāpṛtaṃ prakṣveḍitavilāsena gāyantamāsīnam / samupetya cainamūcuḥ - thathathadadakākākākā / bho gavāṃ saṃrakṣādhikṛta evaṃ vivikte nirjanasampāte 'sminnaraṇye vicarannevamekākī kathaṃ na bibheṣīti / sa tānālokyābravīt - kuto vā bhetavyamiti / yakṣā ūcuḥ - kiṃ tvayā na śrūtapūrvā yakṣarākṣasānāṃ piśācānāṃ vā nisargaraudrā prakṛtiriti?
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Yakṣas</s>, having transformed themselves into the appearance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, wandering about, saw at the edge of the forest a certain cowherd, seated on lush grass at the foot of a shady tree, wearing a garland woven from blossoming forest-tree flowers, with his staff and axe placed to his right, alone, occupied with twisting a rope, singing with a playful whistle. Approaching him, they said — "Blah blah blah!" "O you who are charged with the care of cattle, wandering alone like this in the forest, in this deserted and secluded wilderness — how are you not afraid?" He looked at them and said: "What is there to fear?" The <s>Yakṣas</s> said: "Have you not heard of the naturally fierce disposition of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s>?

children.text: sahāyamadhye 'pi hi vartamāno vidyātapaḥsvastyayanairupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even one surrounded by companions, equipped with the protections of knowledge, austerities, and benedictions,

children.text: yebhyaḥ kathañcitparimokṣameti śauryādavajñātabhayo 'pi lokaḥ // Jm_8.7 //
children.translated_text: from whom the world, though disdaining danger through courage, scarcely obtains escape — || Jm 8.7 ||

children.text: tebhyo nṛmedaḥpiśitāśanebhyaḥ kathaṃ bhayaṃ te 'sti na rākṣasebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "From those devourers of human fat and flesh, the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, how is it you have no fear,

children.text: viviktagambhīrabhayānakeṣu sahāyahīnasya vanāntareṣu // Jm_8.8 //
children.translated_text: alone and without companions, in the depths of the forest, desolate, profound, and terrifying?" || Jm 8.8 ||

body.text: ityukte sa gopālakaḥ prahasyainānuvāca -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, that cowherd laughed and said to them —

children.text: janaḥ svastyayanenāyaṃ mahatā paripālyate /
children.translated_text: "These people are protected by a great talisman;

children.text: devendreṇāpyaśakyo 'yaṃ kiṃ punaḥ piśitāśanaiḥ // Jm_8.9 //
children.translated_text: even <s>Indra</s>, lord of gods, cannot [overpower] them — what then of flesh-eaters?" || Jm 8.9 ||

children.text: tena geha ivāraṇye rātrāvapi yathā divā /
children.translated_text: "Because of him, in the forest as in a house, at night as in day,

children.text: janānta iva caiko 'pi nirbhayo vicarāmyaham // Jm_8.10 //
children.translated_text: and alone as if among people — I wander without fear." || Jm 8.10 ||

body.text: athainaṃ te yakṣāḥ kutūhalaprābalyātsādaramutsāhayanta ivocuḥ - tatkathaya kathaya tāvadbhada kīdṛśo 'yaṃ yuṣmākaṃ svastyayanaviśeṣa iti / sa tānprahasannuvāca - śrūyatāṃ yādṛśo 'yamasmākamatyadbhūtaḥ svastyayanaviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Yakṣas</s>, from the intensity of their curiosity, as if encouraging him with respect, said: "Then tell us, good fellow, what manner of special talisman is this of yours?" He replied to them with a laugh: "Hear what kind of extraordinary talisman ours is:

children.text: kanakagiriśilāviśālavakṣāḥ śaradamalendumanojñavaktraśobhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whose chest is broad as the rocks of a golden mountain, whose facial beauty is lovely as the spotless moon of autumn,

children.text: kanakaparighapīnalambabāhurvṛṣabhanibhekṣaṇavikramo narendraḥ // Jm_8.11 //
children.translated_text: whose long arms are stout as golden bars, whose prowess of gaze is like that of a bull — [such is] our king." || Jm 8.11 ||

body.text: īdṛśo 'smākaṃ svastyayanaviśeṣaḥ / ityuktvā sāmarṣavismayastān yakṣānavekṣamāṇaḥ punaruvāca - āścaryaṃ batedam /
body.translated_text: "Such is our special talisman." Having spoken thus, looking at the <s>Yakṣas</s> with indignant wonder, he spoke again: "This is indeed amazing!

children.text: evaṃ prakāśo nṛpatiprabhāvaḥ kathaṃ nu vaḥ śrotrapathaṃ na yātaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The power of this king is so well-known — how has it not reached the path of your ears?

children.text: atyadbhutatvādathavā śruto 'pi bhavatsu vipratyayato na rūḍhaḥ // Jm_8.12 //
children.translated_text: Or perhaps, because of its extraordinary nature, even though heard, it has not taken root in you due to disbelief." || Jm 8.12 ||

children.text: śaṅke guṇānveṣaṇaviklavo vā deśī jano 'sāvakutūhalo vā /
children.translated_text: "I suspect that the people of your country are either distressed in searching for virtues, or lacking in curiosity,

children.text: vivarjito bhāgyaparikṣayādvā kīrtyā narendrasya yato 'bhyupaita // Jm_8.13 //
children.translated_text: or bereft due to the exhaustion of their fortune — since you have come here [knowing nothing of] the king's fame." || Jm 8.13 ||

body.text: tadasti vo bhāgyaśeṣaṃ yattādṛśāddeśakāntārādihāgatāḥ stha / yakṣā ūcuḥ - bhadramukha kathaya kiṃkṛto 'yamasya rājñaḥ prabhāvo yadasyāmānuṣā na prasahante viṣayavāsinaṃ janaṃ hiṃsitumiti / gopālaka uvāca - svamāhātmyādhigataḥ prabhāvo 'yamasmākaṃ mahārājasya / paśyata mahābrāhmaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: "It is the remnant of your good fortune that from such a wilderness of a country you have come here." The <s>Yakṣas</s> said: "Fair-faced one, tell us — what is the source of this king's power, that even non-human beings cannot dare to harm the people dwelling in his territory?" The cowherd said: "This power of our great king is attained through his own greatness. Behold, O great <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> —

children.text: maitrī tasya balaṃ dhvajāgraśabalaṃ tvācāramātraṃ balaṃ
children.translated_text: "Loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) is his power, his banner's crest-mark; mere conduct is his [only] force;

children.text: nāsau vetti rūṣaṃ na cāha paruṣaṃ samyak ca gāṃ rakṣati /
children.translated_text: he knows not anger, nor speaks harshly, and he rightly protects the earth;

children.text: dharmastasya nayo na nītinikṛtiḥ pūjārthamarthaḥ satām
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is his statecraft, not the guile of politics; his wealth is for the worship of the virtuous —

children.text: ityāścaryamayo 'pi durjanadhanaṃ garvaṃ ca nālambate // Jm_8.14 //
children.translated_text: thus, though wondrous, he does not grasp at pride, which is the wealth of the wicked." || Jm 8.14 ||

body.text: evamādiguṇaśatasamudito 'yamasmākaṃ svāmī / tenāsya na prasahante viṣayanivāsinaṃ janaṃ hiṃsitumupadravāḥ / api ca / kiyadahaṃ vaḥ śakṣyāmi vaktum / nṛpatiguṇaśravaṇakautūhalaistu bhavadbhirnagarameva yuktaṃ praveṣṭuṃ syāt / tatra hi bhavantaḥ svadharmānurāgādvyavasthitāryamaryādaṃ nityakṣemasubhikṣatvātpramuditasamṛddhamanuddhatodāttaveṣamabhyāgatātithijanaviśeṣavatsalaṃ nṛpatiguṇākṣiptahṛdayaṃ tatkīrtyāśrayāḥ stutīrmaṅgalamiva svastyayanamiva ca praharṣādabhyasyantaṃ janaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājño guṇavistaramanumāsyante / satyāṃ ca guṇabahumānodbhāvanāyāṃ taddidṛkṣayā yūyamavaśyaṃ tadguṇapratyakṣiṇo bhaviṣyatheti /
body.translated_text: "Our master is endowed with hundreds of such virtues. Therefore, calamities cannot overpower the people dwelling in his realm. Moreover, how much can I tell you? But if you are curious to hear about the king's virtues, it would be fitting for you to enter the city itself. For there, having seen the people — who observe the noble customs established through devotion to their own <s>dharma</s> (duty), who are joyful and prosperous due to the perpetual security and abundance, whose dress is dignified without being ostentatious, who are especially hospitable to visiting guests, whose hearts are captivated by the king's virtues, and who, taking refuge in his fame, repeat praises like benedictions and blessings with great delight — you will infer the full extent of the king's virtues. And once your esteem for his virtues is aroused, through your desire to see him, you will surely become direct witnesses of those virtues."

body.text: atha te yakṣāḥ svaprabhāvapratighātāttasminnājani sāmarṣahṛdayā bhāvaprayuktayāpi yuktayā tayā tadguṇakathayā naiva mārdavamupajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Now those <s>yakṣas</s> (demons), their hearts filled with resentment at the thwarting of their own power, were not at all softened by that account of his virtues, even though it was delivered with genuine reasoning.

children.text: prāyeṇa khalu mandānāmamarṣajvalitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, the minds of the foolish, blazing with indignation,

children.text: yasminvastuni tatkīrtyā tadviśeṣeṇa dahyate // Jm_8.15 //
children.translated_text: burn all the more at the very thing whose glory is extolled.

body.text: pradānapriyatāṃ tu samabhivīkṣya tasya rājñaste yakṣāstadapakāracikīrṣavaḥ samabhigamya rājānaṃ sandarśanakāle bhojanamayācanta / atha sa rājā pramuditamanāstadadhikṛtānpuruṣānsamādideśakṣipramabhirucitaṃ bhojanaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dīyatāmiti / atha te yakṣāḥ samupahṛtaṃ rājārhamapi bhojanaṃ haritatṛṇamiva vyāghrā naiva pratyagṛhṇannaivaṃvidhaṃ bhojanaṃ vayamaśnīma iti / tacchrutvā sa rājā samabhigamyainānabravīt - atha kīdṛśaṃ bhojanaṃ yuṣmākamupaśete? yāvattādṛśamanviṣyatāmiti / yakṣā ūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: But observing that king's love of giving, those <s>yakṣas</s>, wishing to do him harm, approached the king at the time of audience and begged for food. Then that king, his mind delighted, instructed the officials in charge: "Let the food they desire be given to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (priests) at once." But those <s>yakṣas</s>, like tigers turning away from green grass, did not accept even the food worthy of a king that was brought to them, saying, "We do not eat this kind of food." Hearing this, the king approached them and said: "Then what kind of food suits you? Let such food be sought out." The <s>yakṣas</s> said:

children.text: pratyagroṣmāṇi māṃsāni narāṇāṃ rudhirāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: "Fresh, warm flesh of humans and their blood —

children.text: ityannapānaṃ padmākṣa yakṣāṇāmakṣatavrata // Jm_8.16 //
children.translated_text: this, O lotus-eyed one of unbroken vows, is the food and drink of <s>yakṣas</s>."

body.text: ityuktvā daṃṣṭrākarālavadanāni dīptapiṅgala kekararaudranayanāni sphuṭitacipiṭavirūpaghoṇāni jvaladanalakapilakeśaśmaśrūṇi sajalajaladharāndhakārāṇi vikṛtabhīṣaṇāni svānyeva vapūṃṣi pratyapadyanta / samabhivīkṣya cainānsa rājāpiśācāḥ khalvime na mānuṣāstenāsmadīyamannapānaṃ nābhilaṣantīti niścayamupajagāma /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, they assumed their own true forms — terrifying and grotesque, with faces gaping with fearsome fangs, eyes blazing tawny-yellow, squinting and dreadful, noses flat and split and misshapen, hair and beards like blazing copper-brown fire, dark as rain-clouds heavy with water. And seeing them, that king arrived at the certain conclusion: "These are indeed <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons), not humans — that is why they do not desire our food and drink."

children.text: atha tasya narendrasya prakṛtyā karuṇātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then in that lord of men, compassionate by nature,

children.text: bhūyasī karuṇā teṣu samabhūcchuddhacetasaḥ // Jm_8.17 //
children.translated_text: there arose an even greater compassion for them, his mind being pure.

body.text: karuṇaikatānahṛdayaśca tānyakṣānanuśocanniyatamīdṛśamarthaṃ cintayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: His heart overwhelmed by compassion alone, he grieved for those <s>yakṣas</s> and reflected on the matter with firm resolve:

children.text: dayāvatastāvadidamannapānaṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: "For one who is compassionate, such food and drink is extremely difficult to obtain,

children.text: pratyahaṃ ca tadanveṣyaṃ kinnu duḥkhamataḥ param // Jm_8.18 //
children.translated_text: and it must be sought out every day — what suffering could be greater than this?

children.text: nirdayasyāpyaśaktasya vighātaikarasaḥ śramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even for one devoid of compassion, the toil whose sole flavor is destruction is futile if one lacks the power;

children.text: śaktasyāpyahitābhyāsāt kiṃsvitkaṣṭataraṃ tataḥ // Jm_8.19 //
children.translated_text: and even for one who has the power, what could be more wretched than the habitual practice of harm?

children.text: evaṃvidhāhāraparāyaṇānāṃ kārūṇyaśūnyāśivamānasānām /
children.translated_text: For beings such as these, devoted to this kind of sustenance, devoid of compassion, with inauspicious minds,

children.text: pratyāhameṣāṃ dahatāṃ svamarthaṃ duḥkhāni yāsyanti kadā nu nāśam // Jm_8.20 //
children.translated_text: burning away their own merit every day — when will their sufferings ever come to an end?

body.text: tatkathamidānīmahameṣāmīdṛśāhārasampādanādekāhamapi tāvatparahiṃsāprāṇavighātaṃ kuryām?
body.translated_text: How then could I, even for a single day, cause harm to others or destroy their lives for the sake of procuring such food for these beings?

children.text: na hi smarāmyarthitayāgatānāmāśāviparyāsahataprabhāṇi /
children.translated_text: For I do not recall ever having caused the faces of those who came as supplicants

children.text: himānilamlāpitapaṅkajānāṃ samānadainyāni mukhāni kartum // Jm_8.21 //
children.translated_text: to become like lotuses withered by frost and wind — faces dejected with the disappointment of dashed hopes.

body.text: bhavatu / dṛṣṭam /
body.translated_text: So be it. The course is clear.

children.text: svataḥ śarīrātsthirapīvarāṇi dāsyāmi māṃsāni saśoṇitāni /
children.translated_text: From my own body I shall give firm and ample flesh, together with blood;

children.text: ato 'nyathā ko hi mama kramaḥ syādityāgateṣvarthiṣu yuktarūpaḥ // Jm_8.22 //
children.translated_text: for what other course of action would be proper for me when supplicants have come thus?

children.text: svayaṃmṛtānāṃ hi nirūṣmakāṇi bhavanti māṃsāni viśoṇitāni /
children.translated_text: For the flesh of those who have died naturally is cold and devoid of blood,

children.text: priyāṇi caiṣāṃ na hi tāni samyag bubhukṣayā pīḍitavigrahāṇām // Jm_8.23 //
children.translated_text: and such flesh is not pleasing to these beings, whose bodies are afflicted with hunger.

body.text: jīvato 'pi ca kuto 'hamanyasmānmāṃsamādāsye māmabhigamya caite tathaiva kṣuttarṣaparikṣāmanayanavadanā niṣphalāśāpraṇayatvādadhikataravighātāturamanasaḥ kathaṃ nāma pratiyāsyanti? tadidamatra prāptakālam /
body.translated_text: And even from a living person, from whom else would I take flesh? If these beings come to me and must return with the same gaunt faces, eyes hollow with hunger and thirst, their hopes fruitless and their affection unrequited, their minds distressed by even greater affliction — how could that be? Therefore, this is the course that is timely here:

children.text: duṣṭavraṇasyeva sadāturasya kaḍe(le)varasyāsya rujākarasya /
children.translated_text: "Of this body, which like a festering wound is perpetually afflicted and pain-producing,

children.text: karomi kāryātiśayopayogādatyartharamyaṃ pratikārakhedam // Jm_8.24 //
children.translated_text: I shall make the remedy exceedingly delightful through its application to an extraordinary purpose."

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahātmā praharṣodgamasphītīkṛtanayanavadanaśobhaḥ svaṃ śarīramupadarśayaṃstānyakṣānuvāca -
body.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that great-souled one, the beauty of his eyes and face expanded with a surge of joy, displaying his own body, said to those <s>yakṣas</s>:

children.text: amūni māṃsāni saśoṇitāni dhṛtāni lokasya hitārthameva /
children.translated_text: "These limbs of flesh with blood are maintained solely for the benefit of the world;

children.text: yadyātitheyatvamupeyuradya mahodayaḥ so 'bhyudayo mama syāt // Jm_8.25 //
children.translated_text: if today they attain the status of a gift to guests, that great fortune would be my supreme prosperity."

body.text: atha te yakṣā jānanto 'pi tasya rājñastamadhyāśayamatyadbhutatvādaśraddadhānā rājānamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Now those <s>yakṣas</s>, though they knew the king's intention, were incredulous because of its extraordinary nature, and said to the king:

children.text: arthinātmagate duḥkhe yācñādainyena darśite /
children.translated_text: "When a supplicant has revealed his own suffering and the humility of his request,

children.text: jñātumarhati dātaiva prāptakālamataḥ param // Jm_8.26 //
children.translated_text: the giver himself should know what is timely beyond that."

body.text: atha rājā - anumatamidameṣāmiti pramuditamanāḥ sirāmokṣaṇārthaṃ vaidyā ājñāpyantāmiti samādideśa / atha tasya rājño 'mātyāḥ svamāṃsaśoṇitapradānavyavasāyamavetya sambhramāmarṣavyākulahṛdayā vyaktamīdṛśaṃ kañcidarthaṃ snehavaśādūcuḥ - nārhati devaḥ pradānaharṣātiśayādanuraktānāṃ prajānāṃ hitāhitakramamanavekṣitum / na caitadaviditaṃ devasya / yathā -
body.translated_text: Then the king, his mind delighted thinking "This has their consent," gave the order: "Let physicians be summoned for the opening of veins." Now when the king's ministers learned of his resolve to give his own flesh and blood, their hearts agitated with alarm and indignation, they spoke words to this effect, impelled by affection: "Your Majesty should not, out of excessive delight in giving, neglect to consider what is beneficial and harmful for your devoted subjects. Nor is this unknown to Your Majesty. For:

children.text: yadyatprajānāmahitodayāya tattatpriyaṃ mānada rākṣasānām /
children.translated_text: "Whatever brings harm to the subjects, that is dear to the <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), O bestower of honor;

children.text: paroparodhārjitavṛttituṣṭirevaṃsvabhāvānagha jātireṣām // Jm_8.27 //
children.translated_text: their nature is to find satisfaction in livelihoods gained through the oppression of others — such, O sinless one, is the character of this race.

children.text: sukheṣvasaktaśca bibharṣi deva rājyaśramaṃ lokahitārthameva /
children.translated_text: Unattached to pleasures, you bear the burden of kingship solely for the benefit of the world, Your Majesty;

children.text: svamāṃsadānavyavasāyamasmātsvaniścayonmārgamimaṃ vimuñca // Jm_8.28 //
children.translated_text: therefore abandon this resolve to give your own flesh, which strays from the proper path of your own determination.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ na prasahanta ete tvadvīryaguptaṃ naradeva lokam /
children.translated_text: Without doubt, these beings cannot overpower the people guarded by your valor, O lord of men;

children.text: anarthapāṇḍityahatāstathā hi nayena vāñchantyanayaṃ prajānām // Jm_8.29 //
children.translated_text: for, ruined by their perverse cleverness, they seek through stratagem to bring calamity upon your subjects.

children.text: medovasādyaistridaśā makheṣu prītiṃ hutāśābhihutairvrajanti /
children.translated_text: The gods are gratified in sacrifices by offerings of fat, marrow, and the like, cast into the consecrated fire;

children.text: satkārapūtaṃ bhavadīyamannaṃ sampannameṣāṃ kila naiva rucyam // Jm_8.30 //
children.translated_text: yet the excellent food of yours, purified by proper hospitality, is apparently not to their taste!

body.text: kāmaṃ nāsmadvidhajanādheyabuddhayo devapādāḥ / svakāryānurāgastvayamasmānevamupacārapathād bhraṃśayati / pañcānāmamīṣāmarthe sakalaṃ jagadanarthīkartavyamiti ko 'yaṃ dharmamārgo devasya? api ca / kiṃkṛteyamasmāsvevaṃ niṣpraṇayatā, kena vāsmākaṃ svāmyarthe viniyojyamānāni vinigūḍhapūrvāṇi māṃsaśoṇitāni yadaparikṣīṇeṣvevāmīṣu svāni devo dātumicchatīti / atha sa rājā tānamātyānuvāca -
body.translated_text: Admittedly, Your Majesty's wisdom is not to be instructed by people like us. But our attachment to your cause compels us to deviate from the path of decorum. What kind of <s>dharma</s>-path is this of Your Majesty — that the entire world should be harmed for the sake of these five? Moreover, why this lack of affection toward us? For what reason does Your Majesty wish to give away his own flesh and blood, which have never before been disclosed, while ours remain undiminished?" Then that king said to his ministers:

children.text: saṃvidyamānaṃ nāstīti brūyādasmadvidhaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: "How could one such as I say 'it does not exist' of something that exists?

children.text: na dāsyāmītyasatyaṃ vā vispaṣṭamapi yācitaḥ // Jm_8.31 //
children.translated_text: Or, when clearly asked, utter the falsehood 'I will not give'?

children.text: dharmavyavasthāsu puraḥsaraḥ san svayaṃ vrajeyaṃ yadi kāpathena /
children.translated_text: If I, who should be the forerunner in matters of <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct), were myself to take a wrong path,

children.text: asmadgatācārapathānugānāṃ bhavedavasthā mama kā prajānām // Jm_8.32 //
children.translated_text: what would be the condition of my subjects, who follow the path of conduct set by me?

children.text: yataḥ prajā eva samīkṣamāṇaḥ sāraṃ śarīrādahamuddhariṣye /
children.translated_text: Since it is for the sake of the subjects themselves that I shall extract the essence from this body,

children.text: kaśca prabhāvo jagadarthasādhurmātsaryahāryālpahṛdo mama syāt // Jm_8.33 //
children.translated_text: what power to accomplish the world's welfare could belong to me if I were small-hearted enough to be overcome by selfishness?

body.text: yadapi cāsmatpremabahumānāvarjitaṃ praṇayavisrambhagarbhamabhidhīyate bhavadbhiḥ - kiṃkṛteyamasmāsvevaṃ niṣpraṇayatā yadaparikṣīṇeṣveva no māṃsaśoṇiteṣu svāni devo dātumicchatīti / atra vo 'nuneṣyāmi / na khalu me yuṣmāsu pratihataviṣayaḥ praṇayamārgo visrambhavirahātpariśaṅkāgahanaduravagāho vā / kintu -
body.translated_text: As for what you say, impelled by affection and esteem for me, with the confidence born of intimacy — 'Why this lack of affection toward us, that Your Majesty wishes to give away his own flesh and blood while ours remain undiminished?' — in this I shall reassure you. It is not that my path of affection toward you has been obstructed, nor that through lack of trust it has become impenetrably overgrown with suspicion. Rather:

children.text: dhane tanutvaṃ kramaśo gate vā bhāgyānuvṛttyā kṣayamāgate vā /
children.translated_text: When wealth has gradually diminished, or when following the course of fortune it has come to exhaustion,

children.text: vijṛmbhamāṇapraṇayaḥ suhṛtsu śobheta na sphītadhanaḥ kṛśeṣu // Jm_8.34 //
children.translated_text: one who displays affection toward friends when they are reduced would not shine if he himself were wealthy.

children.text: vivardhiteṣvarthijanārthameva saṃvidyamāneṣu ca me bṛhatsu /
children.translated_text: While my limbs remain enlarged, well-nourished, and swelling with flesh,

children.text: gātreṣu māṃsopacayonnateṣu yuṣmāsvapi syātpraṇayo virūpaḥ // Jm_8.35 //
children.translated_text: maintained precisely for the benefit of supplicants, even my affection for you would be unseemly.

children.text: asaṃstutānāmapi na kṣameya pīḍāṃ kathaṃ kaiva kathā bhavatsu /
children.translated_text: I could not endure the suffering even of strangers — how much less, then, of you!

children.text: svānyeva māṃsāni yato 'smi ditsurmāṃ caiva yācanta ime na yuṣmān // Jm_8.36 //
children.translated_text: Since it is my own flesh that I wish to give, and since these beings ask me, not you.

body.text: tadalamasmadatisnehāddharmavighnaniḥsādhvasatayā / anucitaḥ khalvayamatrabhavatāmasmadarthiṣu samudācāraḥ / mīmāṃsitavyamapi ca tāvadetatsyāt -
body.translated_text: Therefore, enough of this obstruction to <s>dharma</s> born of excessive affection for me, with no fear of its consequences! This behavior of yours toward those who come to me as supplicants is truly improper. And consider this further —

children.text: svārthamannādi ditsantaṃ kathaṃ syātpratiṣedhayan /
children.translated_text: How could one who restrains another wishing to give away his own possessions, such as food and the like,

children.text: sādhuvṛttirasādhurvā prāgevaivaṃvidhaṃ vidhim // Jm_8.37 //
children.translated_text: be considered virtuous — or even not-vicious — especially in a matter of this kind?

body.text: tadalamanenātra vo nirbandhena / nyāyopaparīkṣayā kriyatāmasmatsācivyasadṛśamunmārgāvaraṇaṃ manasaḥ / anumodanānuguṇavacasaḥ khalvatrabhavantaḥ śobherannevamadhīranayanāḥ / kutaḥ -
body.translated_text: Therefore, enough of this insistence. Through examination of what is just, perform the duty befitting my counselors — the guarding of the mind from wrong paths. You would shine here with words suited to approval, not with such timid counsel. For:

children.text: naikopayogasya dhanasya tāvanna pratyahaṃ yācanakā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Wealth that can be used only once — for that, supplicants do not come every day;

children.text: evaṃvidhastvarthijano 'dhigantuṃ na devatārādhanayāpi śakyaḥ // Jm_8.38 //
children.translated_text: and supplicants of this kind cannot be obtained even through the propitiation of the gods.

children.text: evaṃvidhe cārthijane 'bhyupete dehe vināśinyasukhāspade ca /
children.translated_text: And when such supplicants have arrived, and considering that the body is perishable and the abode of suffering,

children.text: vimarśamārgo 'pyanudāttatā syānmātsaryadainyaṃ tu parā tamisrā // Jm_8.39 //
children.translated_text: even deliberation would be a lack of nobility — and reluctance born of selfishness would be utter darkness."

body.text: tanna mā vārayatumarhantyatrabhavanta ityanunīya sa rājā svāṃ parṣadamāhūya vaidyānpañca sirāḥ svaśarīre mokṣayitvā tān yakṣānuvāca -
body.translated_text: "Therefore, let your honors not restrain me." Having thus conciliated his assembly, the king summoned physicians, had five veins opened in his own body, and said to those <s>yakṣas</s>:

children.text: dharmakarmaṇi sācivyaṃ prītiṃ ca paramāṃ mama /
children.translated_text: "You should do me the kindness of assisting in this act of <s>dharma</s>

children.text: bhavantaḥ kartumarhanti deyasyāsya pratigrahāt // Jm_8.40 //
children.translated_text: and granting me the highest joy, by accepting this gift."

body.text: te tathetyuktvāñjalipuṭaireva rājño raktacandanarasābhitāmraṃ rudhiraṃ pātumupacakramire /
body.translated_text: They said "So be it," and with cupped hands began to drink the king's blood, coppery-red like the juice of red sandalwood.

children.text: sa pīyamānakṣatajaḥ kṣitīśaḥ kṣapācarairhemavapuścakāśe /
children.translated_text: That lord of the earth, his blood being drunk by the night-wanderers, shone with a golden body

children.text: sandhyānuraktairjalabhāranamraiḥ payodharairmerurivopagūḍhaḥ // Jm_8.41 //
children.translated_text: like Mount <s>Meru</s> embraced by rain-clouds, heavy with water and reddened by twilight.

children.text: prītiprakarṣāddhṛtisampadā ca vapurguṇādeva ca tasya rājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the intensity of his joy, the firmness of his composure, and the very excellence of his bodily constitution,

children.text: mamlau na gātraṃ na mumūrcha cetaḥ saṃcikṣipe na kṣatajaṃ kṣaradvā // Jm_8.42 //
children.translated_text: that king's limbs did not wither, his mind did not faint, and his flowing blood did not diminish.

body.text: vinītatarṣaklamāstu te yakṣāḥ paryāptamaneneti rājānamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: The <s>yakṣas</s>, their thirst and fatigue relieved, said to the king, "This is sufficient" —

children.text: anekaduḥkhāyatane śarīre sadā kṛtadhne 'pi narādhipasya /
children.translated_text: "Though the body is an abode of manifold sufferings and ever ungrateful,

children.text: gate 'rthisaṃmānanasādhanatvaṃ harṣānukūlaṃ grahaṇaṃ babhūva // Jm_8.43 //
children.translated_text: the king's body, having attained the capacity to honor supplicants, was received with joy."

body.text: atha sa rājā harṣaprabodhādadhikataranayanavadanaprasādo nīlotpaladalanīlavimalapatraṃ ratnaprabhodbhāsuraruciratsaruṃ niśitaṃ nistriṃśamādāya svamāṃsāni cchittvā tebhyaḥ prāyacchat /
body.translated_text: Then that king, with the radiance of his eyes and face heightened by the awakening of joy, took up a sharp sword — its blade dark-blue and spotless like the petal of a blue lotus, its beautiful hilt gleaming with the splendor of jewels — and cutting his own flesh, offered it to them.

children.text: hriyamāṇāvakāśaṃ tu dānaprītyā punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: But his delight in giving, seizing every opportunity again and again,

children.text: na prasehe manastasya cchedaduḥkhaṃ vigāhitum // Jm_8.44 //
children.translated_text: did not allow his mind to dwell upon the pain of the cutting.

children.text: ākṛṣyamāṇaṃ śitaśasrapātaiḥ prītyā punardūṃramapāsyamānam /
children.translated_text: The pain, drawn forth by the blows of the sharp blade yet cast away again by his joy,

children.text: khedālasatvādiva tasya duḥkhaṃ manaḥsamutsarpaṇamandamāsīt // Jm_8.45 //
children.translated_text: was slow to rise to his mind, as though sluggish from weariness.

children.text: sa prītimāneva niśācarāṃstānsantarpayansvaiḥ piśitaistathāsīt /
children.translated_text: He remained joyful even as he satiated those night-wanderers with his own flesh;

children.text: krūrāṇi teṣāmapi mānasāni yenāsurāviṣkṛtamārdavāni // Jm_8.46 //
children.translated_text: so much so that even their cruel minds were made to reveal a hidden tenderness.

children.text: dharmapriyatvātkaruṇāvaśādvā tyajan parārthe priyamātmadeham /
children.translated_text: Whether from love of <s>dharma</s> or compelled by compassion, abandoning his dear body for the sake of others,

children.text: dveṣāgnidagdhānyapi mānasāni prasādasauvarṇyanavāni kuryāt // Jm_8.47 //
children.translated_text: could make even minds burnt by the fire of hatred newly golden with serenity. // Jm_8.47 //

body.text: atha te yakṣāstaṃ rājānaṃ svamāṃsotkartanaparaṃ tathaivāskhalitavadanaprasādamavikampyamānaṃ māṃsacchedavedanābhirabhivīkṣya prasādaṃ vismayaṃ copajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, seeing that king devoted to cutting his own flesh, yet with his facial serenity utterly unfaltering, unshaken by the pain of flesh being cut, were filled with faith and wonder.

children.text: āścaryamadbhutamaho bata kiṃsvidetat satyaṃ na veti samudīrṇavicāraharṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: "How marvelous! How wondrous! Ah, what can this be? Is it real or not?" — thus with deliberation and joy aroused,

children.text: rājanyamarṣamupamṛdya manaḥprasādaṃ tatsaṃstutipraṇatibhiḥ prathayāmbabhūvuḥ // Jm_8.48 //
children.translated_text: suppressing their hostility toward the king, they began to display their heartfelt serenity through praises and obeisances to him. // Jm_8.48 //

body.text: alamalaṃ deva viramyatāṃ svaśarīrapīḍāprasaṅgāt / santarpitāḥ smastavānayādbhutayā yācanakajanamanoharayā pratipattyeti sasambhramāḥ sapraṇāmaṃ vinivārya rājānaṃ prasādāśrupariṣiktavadanāḥ sabahumānamudīkṣamāṇāḥ punarūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: "Enough, enough, Your Majesty! Please desist from this occasion of bodily suffering! We are satisfied by this wondrous conduct of yours that captivates the minds of supplicants." Thus, in agitation, with bows, restraining the king, their faces bathed in tears of devotion, gazing at him with great respect, they spoke again:

children.text: sthāne bhaktivaśena gacchati janastvatkīrtivācālatāṃ
children.translated_text: "It is fitting that people, compelled by devotion, become eloquent in proclaiming your fame;

children.text: sthāne śrīḥ paribhūya paṅkajavanaṃ tvatsaṃśrayaślāghinī /
children.translated_text: it is fitting that <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), scorning the lotus grove, takes pride in dwelling with you;

children.text: vyaktaṃ śakrasanāthatāmapi gatā tvadvīryaguptāmimāṃ
children.translated_text: clearly even heaven, though protected by the might of <s>Śakra</s> himself, gazes upon

children.text: dyauḥ paśyatyuditaspṛhā vasumatīṃ no cedaho vañcyate // Jm_8.49 //
children.translated_text: this earth, guarded by your valor, with longing aroused — unless indeed it is being deceived! // Jm_8.49 //

body.text: kiṃ bahunā? evaṃvidhajanābhyupapannaḥ sabhāgyaḥ khalu manuṣyalokaḥ / yuṣmadāyāsābhyanumodanāttu vayamevātra dagdhāḥ / bhavadvidhajanāpaśrayācchakyamitthaṅgatairapyātmānaṃ samuddhartumiti svaduṣkarapratīghātāśayā bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmaḥ -
body.translated_text: What more need be said? The human world is truly fortunate to be graced by persons such as you. But it is we who are burned here by approving your exertions. Since even those who have fallen to such a state as ours can uplift themselves by taking refuge in persons like you" — thus, wishing to dissuade him from his difficult undertaking, they asked him:

children.text: anādṛtya sukhaprāptāmanuraktāṃ nṛpaśriyam /
children.translated_text: "Disregarding the royal splendor that came easily and was devoted to you,

children.text: kiṃ tadatyadbhutaṃ sthānaṃ pathānena yadīpsasi // Jm_8.50 //
children.translated_text: what is that supremely wondrous station you seek by this path? // Jm_8.50 //

children.text: sarvakṣitipatitvaṃ nu dhaneśatvamathendratām /
children.translated_text: Is it sovereignty over all the earth, or the lordship of <s>Kubera</s> (god of wealth), or the rank of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: brahmabhūyaṃ vimokṣaṃ vā tapasānena vāñchasi // Jm_8.51 //
children.translated_text: or the state of <s>Brahma</s>, or <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) that you desire by this <s>tapas</s> (austerity)? // Jm_8.51 //

children.text: asya hi vyavasāyasya na dūrataramīpsitam /
children.translated_text: For there is no goal too distant for such resolve as this;

children.text: śrotavyaṃ caitadasmābhirbaktumarhati no bhavān // Jm_8.52 //
children.translated_text: and we ought to hear it — pray tell us, Your Majesty! // Jm_8.52 //"

body.text: rājovāca - śrūyatāṃ yadartho 'yaṃ mamābhyudyamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The king said: "Hear the purpose of this, my endeavor.

children.text: prayatnalabhyā yadayatnanāśinī na tṛptisaukhyāya kutaḥ praśāntaye /
children.translated_text: That which is gained with effort yet destroyed without effort, which brings no satisfaction and still less peace —

children.text: bhavāśrayā sampadato na kāmaye surendralakṣmīmapi kimvathetarām // Jm_8.53 //
children.translated_text: such worldly prosperity, rooted in <s>bhava</s> (existence), I do not desire, not even the splendor of the lord of gods, let alone anything less. // Jm_8.53 //

children.text: na cātmaduḥkhakṣayamātrakeṇa me prayāti santoṣapathena mānasam /
children.translated_text: Nor does my mind proceed on the path of contentment with the mere cessation of my own suffering,

children.text: amūnanāthānabhivīkṣya dehinaḥ prasaktatīvravyasanaśramāturān // Jm_8.54 //
children.translated_text: when I behold these helpless embodied beings, afflicted by the weariness of incessantly intense misfortune. // Jm_8.54 //

children.text: anena puṇyena tu sarvadarśitāmavāpya nirjitya ca doṣavidviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Rather, by this merit, having attained omniscience and having conquered the faults that are one's enemies,

children.text: jarārujāmṛtyumahormisaṅkulātsamuddhareyaṃ bhavasāgarājjagat // Jm_8.55 //
children.translated_text: may I lift the world out of the ocean of <s>bhava</s> (existence), turbulent with the great waves of old age, disease, and death. // Jm_8.55 //"

body.text: atha te yakṣāḥ prasādasaṃharṣitatanuruhāḥ praṇamya rājānamūcuḥ - upapannarūpamevaṃvidhasya vyavasāyātiśayasyedaṃ karma / tanna dūre bhavadvidhānāmabhiprāyasampada iti niścitamanaso vijñāpayāmaḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, their body hair bristling with devotion, bowed to the king and said: "This deed is a fitting expression of such extraordinary resolve. We are convinced that the fulfillment of the aspirations of persons like you is not far off, and so we inform you:

children.text: kāmaṃ lokahitāyaiva tava sarvo 'yamudyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Assuredly, all this effort of yours is for the welfare of the world alone;

children.text: svahitātyādaraṃ tveṣāṃ smartumarhasi nastadā // Jm_8.56 //
children.translated_text: but please remember at that time your excessive solicitude for our welfare too. // Jm_8.56 //

children.text: ajñānācca yadasmābhirevamāyāsito bhavān /
children.translated_text: And that we, out of ignorance, have thus tormented you,

children.text: svamapyarthamapaśyadbhirmṛṣyatāmeva tacca naḥ // Jm_8.57 //
children.translated_text: not seeing even our own good — please forgive us for that. // Jm_8.57 //

children.text: ājñāmapi ca tāvannastvamanugrahapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: And now, please give us your command, as a path of grace,

children.text: sacivānāmiva sveṣāṃ visrabdhaṃ dātumarhasi // Jm_8.58 //
children.translated_text: as you would trustingly give it to your own ministers. // Jm_8.58 //"

body.text: atha sa rājā prasādamṛdūkṛtahṛdayānmatvainānuvāca - upakāraḥ khalvayaṃ nāyāso mametyalamatra vo 'kṣamāśaṅkayā / api ca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, judging their hearts to have been softened by devotion, said to them: "This is truly a service to me, not a hardship — so enough of your apprehension of offense. Moreover:

body.text: evaṃvidhe dharmapathe sahāyānkiṃ vismariṣyāmyadhigamya bodhim /
body.translated_text: "When I attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), how could I forget companions on such a path of <s>dharma</s>?

body.text: yuṣmākameva prathamaṃ kariṣye vimokṣadharmāmṛtasaṃvibhāgam // Jm_8.59 //
body.translated_text: To you first I shall distribute the nectar of the <s>dharma</s> of <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation). // Jm_8.59 //

children.text: asmatpriyaṃ cābhisamīkṣamāṇairhiṃsā bhavadbhirviṣavadvivarjyā /
children.translated_text: And considering what is dear to us, you should shun <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) as you would poison,

children.text: lobhaḥ paradravyaparigraheṣu vāggarhitā madyamayaśca pāpmā // Jm_8.60 //
children.translated_text: as well as greed in seizing others' property, blameworthy speech, and the sin of intoxication. // Jm_8.60 //"

body.text: atha te yakṣāstathetyasmai pratiśrutya praṇamya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya cainaṃ tatraivāntardadhire / svamāṃsaśoṇitapradānaniścayasamakālameva tu tasya mahāsattvasya /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, having promised him "So be it," having bowed and circumambulated him, vanished right there. And at the very moment of that great being's resolve to give his own flesh and blood,

children.text: vikampamānā bahudhā vasundharā vidhūrṇayāmāsa suvarṇaparvatam /
children.translated_text: the earth, trembling in many ways, shook the golden mountain <s>Meru</s>;

children.text: prasasvanurdundubhayaśca tadgatā drumāśca puṣpaṃ sasṛjurvikampanāt // Jm_8.61 //
children.translated_text: celestial drums resounded there, and trees shed their blossoms from the trembling. // Jm_8.61 //

children.text: tadabhravadvyomani māruteritaṃ patatriseneva vitānavatkvacit /
children.translated_text: In the cloudless sky, driven by the wind, a canopy of flowers, as if from a flock of birds,

children.text: visṛtya mālā grathiteva kutracitsamaṃ samantānnṛpatervyakīryata // Jm_8.62 //
children.translated_text: spreading out like a strung garland in some places, was scattered evenly on all sides over the king. // Jm_8.62 //

children.text: nivārayiṣyanniva medinīpatiṃ samuddhatāvegatayā mahārṇavaḥ /
children.translated_text: As if to restrain the lord of the earth, the great ocean, with upraised velocity,

children.text: jalaiḥ prakṛtyabhyadhikakramasvanaiḥ prayāṇasaujaskavapurvyarocata // Jm_8.63 //
children.translated_text: with waves whose crashing surpassed their natural measure, displayed a form suggestive of the energy of departure. // Jm_8.63 //

children.text: kimetadityāgatasambhramastataḥ surādhipastatra vicintya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: "What is this?" — alarmed thus, the lord of the gods (<s>Śakra</s>), pondering the cause,

children.text: nṛpātyayāśaṅkitatūrṇamāyayau nṛpālayaṃ śokabhayākulākulam // Jm_8.64 //
children.translated_text: fearing danger to the king, came swiftly to the royal palace, agitated with grief and fear. // Jm_8.64 //

children.text: tathāgatasyāpi tu tasya bhūpatermukhaprasādātsaviśeṣavismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But upon seeing the serenity on the face of that king even in such a state, filled with particular wonder,

children.text: upetya taktarma manojñayā girā prasādasaṃharṣavaśena tuṣṭuve // Jm_8.65 //
children.translated_text: he approached and praised him with charming words, overcome by devotion and delight. // Jm_8.65 //

children.text: aho prakarṣo bata sajjanasthiteraho guṇābhyāsanidherudāratā /
children.translated_text: "Oh, the excellence of the conduct of the virtuous! Oh, the nobility born of the cultivation of virtues!

children.text: aho parānugrahapeśalā matistvadarpaṇānnāthavatī bata kṣitiḥ // Jm_8.66 //
children.translated_text: Oh, the mind skilled in benefiting others! With you as its protector, the earth truly has a lord! // Jm_8.66 //"

body.text: ityabhipraśasyainaṃ śakro devendraḥ sadyaḥkṣatarohaṇasamarthairdivyairmānuṣyakairoṣadhiviśeṣairnirvedanaṃ yathāpaurāṇaṃ śarīraṃ kṛtvā dākṣiṇyavinayopacāramadhuraṃ pratipūjitastena rājñā svamāvāsaṃ pratijagāma /
body.translated_text: Having thus praised him, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, with divine and human medicinal herbs capable of instantly healing wounds, restored his body to its former state free of pain, and, having been honored by that king with courtesy sweet with gracious and respectful attentions, returned to his own abode.

body.text: tadevaṃ paraduḥkhāturā nātmasukhamavekṣante mahākāruṇikā iti / ko nāma dhanamātrake 'pyapekṣāṃ notsraṣṭumarhatīti dāyakajanasamuttejanāyāṃ vācyam / karuṇāvarṇe 'pi tathāgatamāhātmye satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ca / yaccoktaṃ bhagavatā 'bahukaraḥ khalvete pañcakā bhikṣavaḥ ' iti syādetatsandhāya / tena hi samayena te pañca yakṣā babhūvuḥ / teṣāṃ bhagavatā yathāpratijñātameva prathamaṃ dharmāmṛtasaṃvibhāgaḥ kṛta iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, those of great compassion, distressed by others' suffering, do not regard their own happiness — this is the moral. Who, then, would not be willing to relinquish even mere wealth? This should be told to encourage those who give. It is also relevant to the glorification of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> (Buddha's) greatness in the context of compassion, and to listening to the <s>dharma</s> with reverence. And what was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) — "These five, O monks, are indeed of great service" — this may refer to that occasion. For at that time, those five <s>yakṣas</s> existed. And to them, just as promised, the <s>Bhagavān</s> first distributed the nectar of the <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: iti maitrībalajātakamaṣṭamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>jātaka</s>, the story of <s>Maitrībala</s>.

body.text: 9. Viśvantarajātakam
body.translated_text: 9. <s>Viśvantara-jātaka</s>

body.text: na bodhisattvacaritaṃ sukhamanumoditumapyalpasattvaiḥ prāgevācaritum / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not easy even to appreciate for those of little spirit, let alone to practice. As the tradition relates:

body.text: sātmībhūtendriyajayaḥ parākramanayavinayasaṃpadā samadhigatavijayaśrīrvṛddhopāsananiyamāt trayyānvīkṣikyorupalabdhārthatattvaḥ svadharmakarmānuraktābhiranudvignasukhocitābhiranuraktābhiḥ prakṛtibhiḥ prakāśyamānadaṇḍanītiśobhaḥ samyakpravṛttavārttāvidhiḥ saṃjayo nāma śibīnāṃ rājā babhūva /
body.translated_text: There was a king of the <s>Śibis</s> named <s>Saṃjaya</s>, who had made mastery of the senses his own nature, who had attained the glory of victory through excellence in valor, statesmanship, and discipline, who had grasped the truth of matters from the <s>Trayī</s> (three Vedas) and <s>Ānvīkṣikī</s> (logic) through the practice of attending elders, whose splendor of governance was made manifest by subjects who were devoted to their own duties, delighting in them, enjoying undisturbed happiness, and who had properly set in motion the methods of economic activity.

children.text: guṇodayairyasya nibaddhabhāvā kulāṅganevāsa narādhipaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: The royal fortune of that king, her affection bound by the arising of his virtues, was like a wife of noble family,

children.text: atarkaṇīyānyamahīpatīnāṃ siṃhābhigupteva guhā mṛgāṇām // Jm_9.1 //
children.translated_text: unimaginable for other kings, like a cave guarded by a lion is for wild animals. // Jm_9.1 //

children.text: tapassu vidyāsu kalāsu caiva kṛtaśramā yasya sadābhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who had always attended upon him, having labored in <s>tapas</s> (austerities), learning, and the arts,

children.text: viśeṣayuktaṃ bahumānamīyuḥ pūjābhirāviṣkriyamāṇasārāḥ // Jm_9.2 //
children.translated_text: showed him distinguished respect, their worth displayed through acts of honor. // Jm_9.2 //

body.text: tasya rājñaḥ pratipattyanantaraṃ prathitaguṇagaṇanirantaro viśvaṃtaro nāma putro yuvarājo babhūva / [ayameva bhagavāñchākyamunistena samayena /]
body.translated_text: That king had a son and heir-apparent named <s>Viśvantara</s>, whose succession of renowned virtues was uninterrupted. [This was the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> himself at that time.]

children.text: yuvāpi vṛddhopaśamābhirāmastejasvyapi kṣāntisukhasvabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though young, he was charming with the calm of an elder; though spirited, his nature was the gentleness of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience);

children.text: vidvānapi jñānamadānabhijñaḥ śriyā samṛddho 'pyavalepaśūnyaḥ // Jm_9.3 //
children.translated_text: though learned, he was a stranger to the pride of knowledge; though prosperous in fortune, he was free from arrogance. // Jm_9.3 //

children.text: dṛṣṭaprayāmāsu ca dikṣu tasya vyāpte ca lokatritaye yaśobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And when his fame had spread to the farthest reaches of the directions and pervaded the three worlds,

children.text: babhūva naivānyayaśolavānāṃ prasartumutsāha ivāvakāśaḥ // Jm_9.4 //
children.translated_text: there was no room, as it were, for the ambition of rivals in glory to advance. // Jm_9.4 //

children.text: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ sa jagadgatānāṃ duḥkhodayānāṃ prasṛtāvalepam /
children.translated_text: Unable to endure the spreading insolence of the world's sufferings,

children.text: dāneṣuvarṣī karuṇorucāpastairyuddhasaṃrambhamivājagāma // Jm_9.5 //
children.translated_text: he, raining gifts, his great bow being compassion, entered into battle-fury against them, as it were. // Jm_9.5 //

body.text: sa pratyahamabhigatamarthijanamabhilaṣitādhikairakliṣṭairarthavisargaiḥ priyavacanopacāramanoharairatīva prahlādayāmāsa / parvadivaseṣu ca poṣadhaniyamapraśamavibhūṣaṇaḥ śiraḥsnātaḥ śuklakṣaumavāsā
body.translated_text: Each day he delighted the supplicants who came to him exceedingly, with effortless distributions of wealth exceeding their desires, made charming by kind words and courteous treatment. And on festival days, adorned with the observance of <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting) vows and tranquility, having bathed his head, wearing white linen garments

body.text: himagiriśikharasaṃnikāśaṃ madalekhābhyalaṃkṛtamukhaṃ lakṣaṇavinayajavasattvasaṃpannaṃ gandhahastinaṃ samājñātamaupavāhyaṃ dviradavaramabhiruhya samantato nagarasyābhiniviṣṭānyarthijananipānabhūtāni svāni sattrāgārāṇi pratyavekṣate sma / tathā ca prītiviśeṣamabhijagāma /
body.translated_text: he would mount the finest of elephants — a noble <s>gandhahastin</s> (rutting elephant) well-known as his state mount, resembling a peak of the snowy <s>Himālaya</s>, its face adorned with lines of ichor, endowed with excellent marks, discipline, speed, and strength — and inspect his alms-halls stationed on all sides of the city, serving as watering places for the multitude of supplicants. And thus he experienced a special joy.

children.text: na hi tāṃ kurute prītiṃ bibhūtirbhavanāśritā /
children.translated_text: For prosperity that remains confined within one's own palace does not produce that joy

children.text: saṃkramyamāṇārthijane saiva dānapriyasya yām // Jm_9.6 //
children.translated_text: which it produces for one who delights in giving when it passes to the hands of supplicants. // Jm_9.6 //

body.text: atha kadācittasyaivaṃvidhaṃ dānaprasaṅgaṃ pramuditahṛdayairarthibhiḥ samantato vikīryamāṇamupalabhyānyatamo bhūmyanantarastasya rājā śakyamayamabhisaṃdhātuṃ dānānurāgavaśagatvāditi pratarkya dviradavarāpaharaṇārthaṃ brāhmaṇāṃstatra praṇidadhe / atha te brāhmaṇā viśvaṃtarasya svāni sattrāgārāṇi pratyavekṣamāṇasya pramodādadhikataranayanavadanaśobhasya jayāśīrvādamukharāḥ samucchritābhiprasāritadakṣiṇāgrapāṇayaḥ purastāt samatiṣṭhanta / sa tato vinigṛhya dviradavaramupacārapuraḥsaramabhigamanaprayojanamenān paryapṛcchadājñāpyatāṃ kenārtha iti / brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Now once, a certain neighboring king, observing this manner of his generosity being celebrated on all sides by supplicants with gladdened hearts, reckoned that he could be exploited on account of his passion for giving, and dispatched <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> there to seize the best of elephants. Then those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, as <s>Viśvantara</s> was inspecting his alms-halls, his eyes and face radiant with heightened delight, stood before him, loudly proclaiming blessings of victory, their right hands raised and extended. Thereupon, reining in the lordly elephant, he inquired of them, preceded by courteous welcome, what the purpose of their visit was: "Let it be made known — what is your need?" The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said:

children.text: amuṣya tava nāgasya gatilīlāvilambinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "We have come as supplicants, drawn by the virtues of this elephant of yours, graceful in its swaying gait,

children.text: guṇairarthitvamāyātā dānaśauryācca te vayam // Jm_9.7 //
children.translated_text: and by your fame for generosity and valor. // Jm_9.7 //

children.text: kailāsaśikharābhasya pradānādasya dantinaḥ /
children.translated_text: By giving away this tusked one, resembling the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,

children.text: kuruṣva tāvallokānāṃ vismayaikarasaṃ manaḥ // Jm_9.8 //
children.translated_text: make the minds of the world a single <s>rasa</s> (essence) of wonder! // Jm_9.8 //"

body.text: ityukte bodhisattvaḥ prītyā samāpūryamāṇahṛdayaścintāmāpede / cirasya khalūdārapraṇayasumukhamarthijanaṃ paśyāmi / kaḥ punarartha evaṃvidhena dviradapatinaiṣāṃ brāhmaṇānām? vyaktamayaṃ lobherṣyādveṣaparyākulamanasaḥ kasyāpi rājñaḥ kārpaṇyaprayogaḥ /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his heart brimming with joy, fell into reflection: "At long last I see supplicants with a noble and gracious request! But what purpose could these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> truly have for such a lord of elephants? Clearly this is the doing of some king whose mind is troubled by greed, envy, and hatred, an act of meanness.

children.text: āśāvighātadīnatvaṃ tanmā bhūttasya bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: "Let there not be, then, the wretchedness of disappointed hope for that king,

children.text: anādṛtya yaśodharmau yo 'smaddhita ivodyataḥ // Jm_9.9 //
children.translated_text: who, disregarding both fame and <s>dharma</s>, has risen up as if for our benefit! // Jm_9.9 //"

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahātmā tvaritamavatīrya dviradavarāt pratigṛhyatāmiti samudyatakāñcanabhṛṅgārasteṣāṃ purastādavatasthe /
body.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that great soul swiftly dismounted from the lordly elephant and, golden pitcher raised, stood before them saying, "Let it be accepted!"

children.text: tataḥ sa vidvānapi rājaśāstramarthānuvṛttyā gatadharmamārgam /
children.translated_text: Then, though learned in the science of statecraft — which in its pursuit of advantage had departed from the path of <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: dharmānurāgeṇa dadau gajendraṃ nītivyalīkena na saṃcakampe // Jm_9.10 //
children.translated_text: out of devotion to <s>dharma</s> he gave the lordly elephant and did not tremble at the transgression of policy. // Jm_9.10 //

children.text: taṃ hemajālarucirābharaṇaṃ gajendraṃ vidyutpinaddhamiva śāradamabhrarāśim /
children.translated_text: Having given away that lordly elephant, splendid with ornaments of golden netting, like an autumn mass of clouds laced with lightning,

children.text: dattvā parāṃ mudamavāpa narendrasūnuḥ saṃcukṣubhe ca nagaraṃ nayapakṣapātāt // Jm_9.11 //
children.translated_text: the prince experienced supreme joy; but the city was thrown into turmoil out of partisanship for statecraft. // Jm_9.11 //

body.text: atha dviradapatipradānaśravaṇāt samudīrṇakrodhasaṃrambhāḥ śibayo brāhmaṇavṛddhā mantriṇo yodhāḥ pauramukhyāśca kolāhalamupajanayantaḥ saṃjayaṃ rājānamabhigamya sasaṃbhramāmarṣasaṃrambhāt pariśithilopacārayantraṇamūcuḥ - kimiyaṃ deva rājyaśrīrvilupyamānaivamupekṣyate? nārhati devaḥ svarājyopaplavamevamabhivardhamānamupekṣitum / kimetaditi ca sāvegamuktā rājñā punarevamūcuḥ - kasmād devo na jānīte

children.text: niṣevya mattabhramaropagītaṃ yasyānanaṃ dānasugandhi vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "He whose face exhales a fragrance of <s>dāna</s> (rut-fluid), served by the singing of intoxicated bees,

children.text: madāvalepaṃ paravāraṇānāmāyāsaduḥkhena vinā pramārṣṭi // Jm_9.12 //
children.translated_text: whose very wind effortlessly wipes away the arrogance of rival elephants, sparing them the pain of exertion — || Jm 9.12 ||

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Śibis</s> — elder <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, ministers, warriors, and leading citizens — their fury of anger inflamed at the report of the gift of the lord of elephants, creating an uproar, approached King <s>Saṃjaya</s> and, with the restraint of their decorum loosened by agitation, indignation, and rage, said: "Why, O lord, is this royal fortune allowed to be plundered through such indifference? Your majesty ought not to disregard this growing upheaval of his own kingdom." And when asked with alarm, "What is this?" they spoke again to the king: "Why does your majesty not know —

children.text: yattejasākrāntabalaprabhāvāḥ saṃsuptadarpā iva vidviṣaste /
children.translated_text: "He by whose prowess and power the enemies' pride lies dormant as if asleep,

children.text: viśvaṃtareṇaiṣa gajaḥ sa datto rūpī jayaste hriyate 'nyadeśam // Jm_9.13 //
children.translated_text: that elephant has been given away by <s>Viśvantara</s>! The embodied [form of] your victory is being led away to another land! || Jm 9.13 ||

children.text: gāvaḥ suvarṇaṃ vasanāni bhojyamiti dvijebhyo nṛpa deyarūpam /
children.translated_text: "Cows, gold, garments, and food — such are the proper things for a king to give to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: yasmiñjayaśrīrniyatā dvipendre deyaḥ sa nāmetyatidānaśauryam // Jm_9.14 //
children.translated_text: but that the elephant on whom victory's fortune depends should be given away — this is excessive daring in giving!" || Jm 9.14 ||

children.text: nayotpathenainamiti vrajantaṃ kathaṃ samanveṣyati rājalakṣmīḥ /
children.translated_text: "How will royal fortune follow him who walks thus on the wrong path of statecraft?

children.text: nopekṣaṇaṃ deva tavātra yuktaṃ purāyamānandayati dviṣaste // Jm_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Neglect is not fitting for you here, O lord, lest this [prince] gladden your enemies!" || Jm 9.15 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā sa rājā putrapriyatvāt kiṃcittāneva pratyaprītamanāḥ kāryānurodhāt sāvegavadevamityuktvā samanuneṣyañchibīnuvāca - jāne dānaprasaṅgavyasanitāṃ nītikramānapekṣāṃ viśvaṃtarasya na caiṣa kramo rājyadhuri saṃniyuktasya / dattaṃ tvanena svaṃ hastinaṃ vāntakalpaṃ kaḥ pratyāhariṣyati? api tu tathāhameva kariṣye yathā dāne mātrāṃ jñāsyati viśvaṃtaraḥ / tadalamatra vaḥ saṃrambheṇeti / śibaya ūcuḥ - na khalu mahārāja paribhāṣāmātrasādhyo 'sminnarthe viśvaṃtara iti / saṃjaya uvāca - atha kimanyadatra mayā śakyaṃ kartum?
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the king, somewhat displeased with them out of his love for his son, yet constrained by the necessity of the situation, said as if distressed, 'Very well, so be it,' and seeking to conciliate the <s>Śibis</s>, spoke: "I know <s>Viśvantara</s>'s obsession with the indulgence of giving, heedless of the course of statecraft, and this is not the conduct befitting one yoked to the burden of kingship. But who will take back what he has given — his own elephant, which is as if vomited forth? However, I shall act so that <s>Viśvantara</s> learns the proper measure in giving. Therefore enough of your agitation." The <s>Śibis</s> said: "Indeed, great king, in this matter <s>Viśvantara</s> is not to be dealt with by mere verbal reprimand." <s>Saṃjaya</s> said: "Then what else am I able to do here?

children.text: doṣapravṛttervimukhasya yasya guṇaprasaṅgā vyasanīkriyante /
children.translated_text: "For one who is averse to the path of wrongdoing, whose attachment to virtues is made into an addiction,

children.text: bandho vadho vātmasutasya tasya kiṃ niṣkrayaḥ syād dviradasya tasya // Jm_9.16 //
children.translated_text: should imprisonment or execution of one's own son be the ransom for that elephant?" || Jm 9.16 ||

body.text: tadalamatra vaḥ saṃrambheṇa / nivārayiṣyāmyahamato viśvantaramiti / atha śibayaḥ samudīrṇamanyavo rājānamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: "Therefore enough of your agitation. I shall remove <s>Viśvantara</s> from this [situation]." Then the <s>Śibis</s>, their wrath inflamed, spoke to the king:

children.text: ko vā vadhaṃ bandhanatāḍanaṃ vā sutasya te rocayate narendra /
children.translated_text: "Who indeed, O lord of men, would approve imprisonment, beating, or execution of your son?

children.text: dharmātmakastveṣa na rājyabhārakṣobhasya soḍhā karuṇāmṛdutvāt // Jm_9.17 //
children.translated_text: But he, being of righteous nature, will not endure the burden of kingship, because of his compassionate gentleness. || Jm 9.17 ||

children.text: siṃhāsanaṃ tejasi labdhaśabdāstrivargasevānipuṇā bhajante /
children.translated_text: "The lion-throne is occupied by those who have earned renown in power, who are skilled in the pursuit of the three aims of life;

children.text: dharmānurāgānnayanirvyapekṣastapovanādhyāsanayogya eṣaḥ // Jm_9.18 //
children.translated_text: but this one, out of love for <s>Dharma</s>, is indifferent to statecraft — he is fit for residing in a hermitage. || Jm 9.18 ||

children.text: phalanti kāmaṃ vasudhādhipānāṃ durnītidoṣāstadupāśriteṣu /
children.translated_text: "The faults of bad statecraft of kings do indeed bear fruit among their dependents;

children.text: sahyāsta eṣāṃ tu tathāpi dṛṣṭā mūloparodhānna tu pārthivānām // Jm_9.19 //
children.translated_text: but these [faults] have been seen to be endurable — what cannot be endured is the destruction of the very root of kingship. || Jm 9.19 ||

children.text: kimatra vā vahvabhidhāya niścayastvayaṃ śibīnāṃ tvadabhūtyamarṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "Why say much here? This is the determination of the <s>Śibis</s>, who cannot bear your ruin:

children.text: prayātu vaṅkaṃ tapaso 'bhivṛddhaye nṛpātmajaḥ siddhaniṣevitaṃ girim // Jm_9.20 //
children.translated_text: let the prince depart to Mount <s>Vaṅka</s>, frequented by sages, for the growth of his austerities." || Jm 9.20 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā snehapraṇayavisrambhavaśādanayāpāyadarśinā hitodyatena tena janena pariniṣṭhuramityabhidhīyamānaḥ prakṛtikopād vrīḍāvanatavadanaḥ putraviyogacintāparigatahṛdayaḥ sāyāsamabhiniśvasya śibīnuvāca - yadyeṣa bhavatāṃ nirbandhastadekamapyahorātramasya mṛṣyatām / prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāmabhipretaṃ vo 'nuṣṭhātā viśvantara iti / evamastviti ca pratigṛhītānunayaḥ śibibhiḥ sa rājā kṣattāramuvāca - gacchemaṃ vṛttāntaṃ viśvantarāya nivedayeti / sa tatheti pratiśrutya śokāśrupariṣiktavadano viśvantaraṃ svabhavanagatamupetya śokaduḥkhāvegāt sasvaraṃ rudan pādayorasya nyapatat / api kuśalaṃ rājakulasyeti ca sasaṃbhramaṃ viśvantareṇānuyuktaḥ samavasīdannaviśadapadākṣaramenamuvāca - kuśalaṃ rājakulasyeti / atha kasmādevamadhīro 'sīti ca punaranuyukto viśvantareṇa kṣattā bāṣpavegoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ śvāsaviskhalitalulitākṣaraṃ śanairityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king, being addressed quite harshly by those people who, though well-intentioned and acting out of concern, saw calamity [ahead] — out of the power of affection, love, and trust — his face bowed as if with shame at the anger of his subjects, his heart seized by the thought of separation from his son, sighing with effort, said to the <s>Śibis</s>: "If this is your firm resolve, then bear with him for just one more day and night. When the night has passed, <s>Viśvantara</s> shall fulfill your wish." And having his conciliatory [gesture] accepted by the <s>Śibis</s> with 'So be it,' the king said to the chamberlain: "Go and inform <s>Viśvantara</s> of this matter." He, having assented with 'As you command,' his face drenched with tears of grief, approached <s>Viśvantara</s> at his own residence and, from the onrush of grief and sorrow, fell at his feet weeping aloud. And when <s>Viśvantara</s> anxiously asked, "Is all well with the royal family?" the chamberlain, sinking down, his throat choked with the onslaught of tears, his syllables faltering and trembling with sighs, spoke slowly thus:

children.text: sāntvagarbhāmanādṛtya nṛpājñāmapyadakṣiṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Disregarding the king's command, though it contained conciliatory words, the <s>Śibis</s>, ungracious,

children.text: rāṣṭrātpravrājayanti tvāṃ kupitāḥ śibayo nṛpa // Jm_9.21 //
children.translated_text: are banishing you from the kingdom, O prince, in their anger." || Jm 9.21 ||

body.text: viśvantara uvāca - māṃ śibayaḥ pravrājayanti kupitā iti kaḥ saṃbandhaḥ?
body.translated_text: <s>Viśvantara</s> said: "The <s>Śibis</s> are banishing me in anger — what connection does this have [with me]?

children.text: rame na vinayonmārge dveṣmi cāhaṃ pramāditām /
children.translated_text: "I do not delight in the path of transgressing propriety, and I despise negligence;

children.text: kutra me śibayaḥ kruddhā yanna paśyāmi duṣkṛtam // Jm_9.22 //
children.translated_text: in what matter are the <s>Śibis</s> angered with me, that I do not see my misdeed?" || Jm 9.22 ||

body.text: kṣattovāca - atyudāratāyām /
body.translated_text: The chamberlain said: "In your excessive generosity.

children.text: alobhaśubhrā tvayi tuṣṭirāsīllobhākulā yācakamānaseṣu /
children.translated_text: "Your contentment was bright with the absence of greed, while the minds of supplicants were agitated with desire;

children.text: datte tvayā mānada vāraṇendre dhairyāṇi kopastvaharacchibīnām // Jm_9.23 //
children.translated_text: but when you gave away the lord of elephants, O bestower of honor, anger stole the <s>Śibis</s>' composure." || Jm 9.23 ||

children.text: ityatītāḥ svamaryādāṃ rabhasāḥ śibayastvayi /
children.translated_text: "Thus the <s>Śibis</s>, having overstepped their proper bounds in their impetuosity toward you,

children.text: yena pravrājitā yānti pathā tena kila vraja // Jm_9.24 //
children.translated_text: [say that] by the same road by which the banished go, you should go, they say." || Jm 9.24 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kṛpābhyāsarūḍhāṃ yācanakajanavatsalatāṃ dhairyātiśayasaṃpadaṃ ca svāmudbhāvayannuvāca - capalasvabhāvāḥ khalu śibayo 'nabhijñā iva cāsmatsvabhāvasya /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, displaying his tenderness toward supplicants — rooted in the practice of compassion — and the supreme wealth of his fortitude, said: "Truly the <s>Śibis</s> are fickle by nature and seem unaware of my character.

children.text: dravyeṣu bāhyeṣu ka eva vādo dadyāmahaṃ sve nayane śiro vā /
children.translated_text: "What need to speak of external possessions? I would give my own eyes or my head!

children.text: imaṃ hi lokārthamahaṃ bibharmi samucchrayaṃ kimvatha vastravāhyam // Jm_9.25 //
children.translated_text: For I bear this body only for the welfare of the world — what more then about things merely borne externally?" || Jm 9.25 ||

children.text: yasya svagātrairapi yāvakānāṃ vacāṃsi saṃpūjayituṃ manīṣā /
children.translated_text: "He whose mind is set on honoring the words of suppliants even with his own limbs —

children.text: bhayānna dadyātsa iti pratarkaḥ prakāśanā bāliśacāpalasya // Jm_9.26 //
children.translated_text: the conjecture that he would not give out of fear — this is a display of childish fickleness." || Jm 9.26 ||

children.text: kāmaṃ māṃ śibayaḥ sarve ghnantu pravrājayantu vā /
children.translated_text: "Let all the <s>Śibis</s> strike me or banish me as they wish;

children.text: na tvevāhaṃ na dāsyāmi gacchāmyeṣa tapovanam // Jm_9.27 //
children.translated_text: but never shall I not give — I now go to the hermitage." || Jm 9.27 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo vipriyaśravaṇaviklavamukhīṃ patnīmuvāca - śruto 'trabhavatyā śibīnāṃ niścayaḥ? madryuvāca - śruto 'yaṃ deva / viśvantara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> spoke to his wife, whose face was distressed at the unpleasant report: "Has your ladyship heard the decision of the <s>Śibis</s>?" <s>Madrī</s> said: "I have heard it, my lord." <s>Viśvantara</s> said:

children.text: tadyadasti dhanaṃ kiṃcidasmatto 'dhigataṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: "Then whatever wealth you have received from me,

children.text: nidhehi tadanindyākṣi yacca te paitrikaṃ dhanam // Jm_9.28 //
children.translated_text: deposit that, O lady of blameless eyes, and also your paternal wealth." || Jm 9.28 ||

body.text: madryuvāca - kutraitaddeva nidadhāmīti? viśvantara uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Madrī</s> said: "Where, my lord, shall I deposit this?" <s>Viśvantara</s> said:

children.text: śīlavadbhyaḥ sadā dadyā dānaṃ satkāraśībharam /
children.translated_text: "One should always give gifts to the virtuous, laden with honor and respect;

children.text: tathā hi nihitaṃ dravyamahāryamanugāmi ca // Jm_9.29 //
children.translated_text: for wealth so deposited is both unassailable and accompanies [one hereafter]." || Jm 9.29 ||

children.text: priyaṃ śvaśurayoḥ kuryāḥ putrayoḥ paripālanam /
children.translated_text: "Please your parents-in-law; care for our two sons;

children.text: dharmamevāpramādaṃ ca śokaṃ madvirahāttu mā // Jm_9.30 //
children.translated_text: attend to <s>Dharma</s> and diligence — but do not grieve at separation from me." || Jm 9.30 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā madrī saṃtaptahṛdayāpi bharturadhṛtiparihārārthamanādṛtya śokadainyamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madrī</s>, though her heart was burning, disregarding the misery of her grief in order to remove her husband's despondency, spoke thus:

children.text: naiṣa dharmo mahārāja yadyāyā vanamekakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is not righteous, O great king, that you should go to the forest alone;

children.text: tenāhamapi yāsyāmi yena kṣatriya yāsyasi // Jm_9.31 //
children.translated_text: therefore I too shall go by whichever path you go, O <s>Kṣatriya</s>." || Jm 9.31 ||

children.text: tvadaṅgaparivartinyā mṛtyurutsava eva me /
children.translated_text: "For me, who revolves around your person, death itself would be a celebration;

children.text: mṛtyorduḥkhataraṃ tatsyājjīveyaṃ yattvayā vinā // Jm_9.32 //
children.translated_text: more painful than death would be that I should live without you." || Jm 9.32 ||

body.text: naiva ca khalu me deva vanavāso duḥkha iti pratibhāti / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: "Nor indeed, my lord, does forest-dwelling appear as suffering to me. For indeed —

children.text: nirdurjanānyanupabhuktasarittarūṇi nānāvihaṃgavirutāni mṛgākulāni /
children.translated_text: "Free from wicked people, with rivers and trees yet unenjoyed, resounding with the songs of various birds, teeming with deer,

children.text: vaiḍūryakuṭṭimamanoharaśādvalāni krīḍāvanādhikasukhāni tapovanāni // Jm_9.33 //
children.translated_text: with lawns charming as pavements of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gems — hermitages are more delightful than pleasure-groves!" || Jm 9.33 ||

body.text: api ca deva /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, my lord:

children.text: alaṃkṛtāvimau paśyankumārau mālabhāriṇau /
children.translated_text: "Seeing these two princes adorned, bearing garlands,

children.text: krīḍantau vanagulmeṣu na rājyasya smariṣyasi // Jm_9.34 //
children.translated_text: playing among the forest thickets — you will not remember the kingdom." || Jm 9.34 ||

children.text: ṛtuprayatnaracitā vanaśobhā navā navāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The beauty of the forest, fashioned by the effort of the seasons, ever new and new,

children.text: vane tvāṃ ramayiṣyanti saritkuñjāśca sodakāḥ // Jm_9.35 //
children.translated_text: will delight you in the woods, along with watered bowers and streams." || Jm 9.35 ||

children.text: citraṃ virutavāditraṃ pakṣiṇāṃ ratikāṅkṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "The wondrous music of calls from birds longing for love,

children.text: madācāryopadiṣṭāni nṛttāni ca śikhaṇḍinām // Jm_9.36 //
children.translated_text: and the dances of peacocks as if taught by an intoxicated dancing-master — || Jm 9.36 ||

children.text: mādhuryānavagītaṃ ca gītaṃ madhupayoṣitām /
children.translated_text: "And the songs of the bee-maidens, sung with honeyed sweetness,

children.text: vaneṣu kṛtasaṃgītaṃ harṣayiṣyati te manaḥ // Jm_9.37 //
children.translated_text: making music together in the forests, will delight your heart." || Jm 9.37 ||

children.text: āstīryamāṇāni ca śarvarīṣu jyotsnādukūlena śilātalāni /
children.translated_text: "And in the nights, the rocky surfaces spread with the fine cloth of moonlight,

children.text: saṃvāhamāno vanamārutaśca labdhādhivāsaḥ kusumadrumebhyaḥ // Jm_9.38 //
children.translated_text: and the forest breeze, massaging [the body], having acquired its fragrance from blossoming trees — || Jm 9.38 ||

children.text: calopalapraskhalitodakānāṃ kalā virāvāśca saridvadhūnām /
children.translated_text: "And the artful murmurings of the river-brides, their water stumbling over shifting rocks,

children.text: vibhūṣaṇānāmiva saṃninādāḥ pramodayiṣyanti vane manaste // Jm_9.39 //
children.translated_text: like the tinkling of ornaments, will gladden your heart in the forest." || Jm 9.39 ||

body.text: ityanunīyamānaḥ sa dayitayā vanaprayāṇaparyuṃtsukamatirarthijanāpekṣayā mahāpradānaṃ dātumupacakrame /
body.translated_text: Thus consoled by his beloved, his mind eagerly set on the journey to the forest, he began to make a great distribution to supplicants in consideration of the needy.

body.text: athemāṃ viśvantarapravrājanapravṛttimupalabhya rājakule tumula ākrandaśabdaḥ prādurabhūta / śokaduḥkhāvegānmūrcchāparīta ivārthijano mattonmatta iva ca tattadbahuvidhaṃ vilalāpa /
body.translated_text: Then, when the news of <s>Viśvantara</s>'s banishment spread, a tumultuous sound of wailing arose in the royal palace. The suppliants, as if overcome by fainting from the onslaught of grief and sorrow, and as if intoxicated or mad, lamented in many and various ways:

children.text: chāyātaroḥ svāduphalapradasya cchedārthamāgūrṇaparaśvadhānām /
children.translated_text: "That the earth, its nurse, does not feel shame when axes are whirled for the felling

children.text: dhātrī na lajjāṃ yadupaiti bhūmirvyaktaṃ tadasyā hatacetanatvam // Jm_9.40 //
children.translated_text: of a shade-tree that bears sweet fruit — this clearly shows her to be devoid of consciousness." || Jm 9.40 ||

children.text: śītāmalasvādujalaṃ nipānaṃ bibhitsatāmasti na cenniṣeddhā /
children.translated_text: "If there is no one to prevent those who would destroy a watering-place of cool, pure, sweet water,

children.text: vyarthābhidhānā bata lokapālā viproṣitā vā śrutimātrakaṃ vā // Jm_9.41 //
children.translated_text: then alas, the so-called world-guardians are mere empty names — either gone away, or only heard of!" || Jm 9.41 ||

children.text: adharmo bata jāgarti dharmaḥ supto 'thavā mṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Alas, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is awake, and <s>Dharma</s> is asleep — or dead!

children.text: yatra viśvantaro rājā svasmādrājyānnirasyate // Jm_9.42 //
children.translated_text: since King <s>Viśvantara</s> is cast out from his own kingdom." || Jm 9.42 ||

children.text: ko 'narthapaṭusāmarthyo yācñānūrjitavṛttiṣu /
children.translated_text: "Who has such power for causing harm against those whose livelihood is sustained by supplication,

children.text: asmāsvanaparādheṣu vadhābhyudyamaniṣṭhuraḥ // Jm_9.43 //
children.translated_text: such cruelty of murderous intent against us who have committed no offense?" || Jm 9.43 ||
