body.text: atha bodhisattvo naikaśatasahasrasaṃkhyaṃ maṇikanakarajataparipūrṇakośaṃ vividhadhanadhānyanicayavanti kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi dāsīdāsayānavāhanavasanaparicchadādi ca sarvamarthibhyo yathārhamatisṛjya, śokaduḥkhābhibhūtadhairyayormātāpitroścaraṇāvabhipraṇamya saputradāraḥ syandanavaramabhiruhya puṇyāhaghoṣeṇaiva mahato janakāyasyākranditaśabdena puravarānniragacchat / anurāgavaśagamanuyāyinaṃ ca janaṃ śokāśrupariklinnavadanaṃ prayatnādvinivartya svayameva rathapragrahān pratigṛhya yena vaṅkaḥ parvatastena prāyāt / vyatītya cāviklavamatirudyānavanaruciramālinaṃ puravaropacāramanupūrveṇa praviralacchāyadrumaṃ vicchidyamānajanasaṃpātaṃ pravicaritamṛgagaṇasaṃbādhadigālokaṃ cīrīvirāvonnāditamaraṇyaṃ pratyapadyata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, releasing to the supplicants as was fitting everything — the treasury filled with gems, gold, and silver, numbering many hundreds of thousands; the storehouses and granaries containing heaps of various riches and grains; and slave-women, slaves, vehicles, draft-animals, garments, and equipment — and bowing at the feet of his mother and father, whose composure was overcome by grief and sorrow, together with his sons and wife, ascended the finest chariot and departed from the chief city accompanied by the auspicious benedictions [of priests], even as the great crowd of people [accompanied him with] cries of lamentation. And having with effort turned back the people who followed out of devotion, their faces wet with tears of grief, he himself took the chariot-reins and set out toward Mount <s>Vaṅka</s>. And passing beyond the area around the chief city — charming with its garden-groves, rich in offerings — with its gradually thinning shade-trees, its diminishing traffic of people, its horizons crowded with herds of roaming deer, resounding with the cries of crickets, he entered the wilderness.

body.text: athainaṃ yadṛcchayābhigatā brāhmaṇā rathavāhāṃsturagānayācanta /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had arrived by chance begged him for the horses yoked to his chariot.

children.text: sa vartamāno 'dhvani naikayojane sahāyahīno 'pi kalatravānapi /
children.translated_text: Though he was on the road, still many <s>yojanas</s> away, without companions, yet with his wife and children,

children.text: pradānaharṣādanapekṣitāyatirdadau dvijebhyaścaturasturaṃgamān // Jm_9.44 //
children.translated_text: from the joy of giving, without regard for consequences, he gave the four horses to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || Jm 9.44 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya svayameva rathadhuryatāmupagantukāmasya gāḍhataraṃ parikaramabhisaṃyacchamānasya rohitamṛgarūpiṇaścatvāro yakṣakumārāḥ suvinītā iva sadaśvāḥ svayameva rathayugaṃ skandhapradeśaiḥ pratyapadyanta / tāṃstu dṛṣṭvā harṣavismayaviśālatarākṣīṃ madrīṃ bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself wished to take up the yoke of the chariot and was tightly girding his waist-band, four <s>Yakṣa</s> princes in the form of red deer, like well-trained horses, of their own accord placed their shoulders into the chariot-yoke. And seeing them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to <s>Madrī</s>, whose eyes had grown wider with delight and wonder:

children.text: tapodhanādhyāsanasatkṛtānāṃ paśya prabhāvātiśayaṃ vanānām /
children.translated_text: "Behold the surpassing power of the forests, sanctified by the dwelling of those rich in austerity,

children.text: yatraivamabhyāgatavatsalatvaṃ saṃrūḍhamūlaṃ mṛgapuṃgaveṣu // Jm_9.45 //
children.translated_text: where such hospitable tenderness has taken deep root even in the lordly deer!" || Jm 9.45 ||

body.text: madryuvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Madrī</s> said:

children.text: tavaivāhamimaṃ manye prabhāvamatimānuṣam /
children.translated_text: "I consider this superhuman power to be yours alone;

children.text: rūḍho 'pi hi guṇābhyāsaḥ sarvatra na samaḥ satām // Jm_9.46 //
children.translated_text: for though the practice of virtues is well-established, it is not equal in all good persons everywhere." || Jm 9.46 ||

children.text: toyeṣu tārāpratibimbaśobhā viśeṣyate yatkumudaprahāsaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "That the beauty of the reflected stars in the waters is surpassed by the radiance of the water-lilies —

children.text: kautūhalābhiprasṛtā ivendorhetutvamatrāgrakarāḥ prayānti // Jm_9.47 //
children.translated_text: these [lilies], as if reaching out with curiosity, attain the status of being the cause [of the moon's beauty]." || Jm 9.47 ||

body.text: iti tayoranyonyānukūlyātparasparaṃ priyaṃ vadatoradhvānaṃ gacchatorathāparo brāhmaṇaḥ samabhigamya bodhisattvaṃ rathavaramayācata /
body.translated_text: As the two thus spoke pleasantly to each other in mutual harmony while traveling along the road, another <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> approached and begged the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for his excellent chariot.

children.text: tataḥ svasukhaniḥsaṅgo yācakapriyabāndhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, free from attachment to his own comfort and a kinsman devoted to the joy of supplicants,

children.text: pūrayāmāsa viprasya sa rathena manoratham // Jm_9.48 //
children.translated_text: fulfilled the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s wish with the chariot. || Jm 9.48 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ prītamanā rathādavatārya svajanānniryātya rathavaraṃ brāhmaṇāya jālinaṃ kumāramaṅkenādāya padbhyāmevādhvānaṃ pratyapadyata / avimanaskaiva ca madrī kṛṣṇājināṃ kumārīmaṅkenādāya pṛṣṭhato 'nvagacchadenam /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, joyful in mind, alighting from the chariot, sending away his attendants, and giving the excellent chariot to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, took the prince <s>Jālin</s> on his hip and continued on foot. And <s>Madrī</s>, not at all disheartened, took the princess <s>Kṛṣṇājinā</s> on her hip and followed behind him.

children.text: nimantrayāmāsuriva drumāstaṃ hṛdyaiḥ phalairānamitāgraśākhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The trees, with their topmost branches bowed under delightful fruits, seemed to invite him;

children.text: puṇyānubhāvādabhivīkṣamāṇāḥ śiṣyā vinītā iva ca praṇemuḥ // Jm_9.49 //
children.translated_text: beholding [him] through the power of his merit, they bowed like well-trained disciples. || Jm 9.49 ||

children.text: haṃsāṃsavikṣobhitapaṅkajāni kiñjalkareṇusphuṭapiñjarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Lakes appeared with lotuses stirred by the wings of swans,

children.text: prādurbabhūvuśca sarāṃsi tasya tatraiva yatrābhicakāṅkṣa vāri // Jm_9.50 //
children.translated_text: yellowish-golden with pollen-dust, right there wherever he desired water. || Jm 9.50 ||

children.text: vitānaśobhāṃ dadhire payodāḥ sukhaḥ sugandhiḥ pravavau nabhasvān /
children.translated_text: The clouds assumed the beauty of canopies; a pleasant, fragrant breeze blew;

children.text: pariśramakleśamamṛṣyamāṇā yakṣāśca saṃcikṣipurasya mārgam // Jm_9.51 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Yakṣas</s>, not tolerating his fatigue and distress, shortened his path. || Jm 9.51 ||

body.text: iti bodhisattva udyānagata iva pādacāravinodanasukhamanubhavanmārgaparikhedarasamanāsvādya saputradāraḥ prānta eva tu vaṅkaparvatamapaśyat / tatra ca puṣpaphalapallavālaṃkṛtasnigdhavividharucirataruvaranicitaṃ madamuditavihaṃgabahuvidharutavinadaṃ pravṛttanṛttabarhigaṇopaśobhitaṃ pravicaritanaikamṛgakulaṃ kṛtaparikaramiva vimalanīlasalilayā saritā kusumarajo 'ruṇasukhapavanaṃ tapovanaṃ vanacarakādeśitamārgaḥ praviśya viśvakarmaṇā śakrasaṃdeśāt svayamabhinirmitāṃ manojñadarśanāṃ sarvartusukhāṃ tatra praviviktāṃ parṇaśālāmadhyāvasat /
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, experiencing the pleasure of walking as if strolling in a garden, without tasting the weariness of the road, together with his sons and wife, soon beheld Mount <s>Vaṅka</s>. Having entered the ascetic grove there — adorned with groves of smooth and beautifully varied excellent trees decked with flowers, fruits, and shoots, resounding with the manifold cries of joyous and delighted birds, graced by groups of peacocks performing their dances, frequented by many herds of deer, bordered by a river of pure blue water, with a pleasant breeze tinged with flower-pollen — guided on the path by a forest-dweller, he settled in a hermitage of delightful appearance, comfortable in all seasons, secluded, which had been constructed there by <s>Viśvakarman</s> himself at <s>Śakra</s>'s command.

children.text: tasminvane dayitayā paricaryamāṇaḥ śṛṇvannayatnamadhurāṃśca sutapralāpān /
children.translated_text: In that forest, attended by his beloved, hearing the effortlessly sweet prattle of his sons,

children.text: udyānasaṃstha iva vismṛtarājyacintaḥ saṃvatsarārdhamadhikaṃ sa tapaścacāra // Jm_9.52 //
children.translated_text: as if dwelling in a pleasure-garden, oblivious of royal cares, he practiced austerities for more than a year and a half. || Jm 9.52 ||

body.text: atha kadācinmūlaphalārthaṃ gatāyāṃ rājaputryāṃ putrayoḥ paripālananimittamāśramapadamaśūnyaṃ kurvāṇe rājaputre mārgareṇuparuṣīkṛtacaraṇaprajaṅghaḥ pariśramakṣāmanayanavadano daṇḍakāṣṭhāvabaddhaskandhāvasaktakamaṇḍalurbrāhmaṇaḥ patnyāḥ paricārakānayanārthaṃ samarpitadṛḍhasaṃdeśastaṃ deśamupajagāma / atha bodhisattvaścirasyārthijanaṃ dṛṣṭvā 'bhigataṃ manaḥpraharṣāt samupajāyamānanayanavadanaprasādaḥ pratyudgamya svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsaraṃ praveśya cainamāśramapadaṃ kṛtātithisatkāramāgamanaprayojanamapṛcchat / atha sa brāhmaṇo bhāryānurāgādutsāritadhairyalajjaḥ pratigrahamātrasajjo niyatamarthamīdṛśamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then once, when the princess had gone to gather roots and fruits, while the prince was keeping the hermitage occupied for the sake of guarding the children, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — his feet and shins roughened by the dust of the road, his face gaunt with the fatigue of travel, his water-pot hanging from a staff-stick slung over his shoulder — having been sent with a firm message to procure attendants for his wife, arrived at that place. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing after a long time a supplicant who had come, with joy of mind producing clarity of countenance and eyes, went out to meet him, led him into the hermitage with kind words beginning with welcome, performed the hospitality due to a guest, and asked the purpose of his coming. Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his steadiness and shame cast aside by devotion to his wife, prepared merely to receive, spoke his fixed purpose thus —

children.text: āloko bhavati yataḥ samaśca mārgo loko 'yaṃ vrajati tato na durgameṇa /
children.translated_text: "From where there is light and the path is level, the world goes there, not by a difficult route;

children.text: prāyo 'smiñjagati tu matsarāndhakāreṇānye na praṇayapadāni me vahanti // Jm_9.53 //
children.translated_text: but in this world, generally blinded by the darkness of selfishness, others do not bear the footsteps of my affection." || Jm 9.53 ||

children.text: pradānaśauryoditayā yaśaḥśriyā gataṃ ca gantavyamaśeṣatastava /
children.translated_text: "By the glorious fame born of the valor of your giving, your [reputation] has gone — and remains to go — everywhere without remainder;

children.text: ato 'smi yācñāśramamabhyupeyivānprayaccha tanme paricārakau sutau // Jm_9.54 //
children.translated_text: therefore I have undertaken the toil of supplication — give me your two sons as attendants." || Jm 9.54 ||

body.text: ityukte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that great being,

children.text: dānaprītau kṛtābhyāsaḥ pratyākhyātumaśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: well-practiced in the joy of giving, untrained in refusal,

children.text: dadāmītyavadad dhṛṣṭaṃ dayitau tanayāvapi // Jm_9.55 //
children.translated_text: boldly said "I give" — even his beloved children. || Jm 9.55 ||

body.text: svastyastu / tatkimidānīmāsyata iti ca brāhmaṇenābhihitaḥ sa mahāsattvaḥ pradānakathāśravaṇotpatitaviṣādaviplutākṣayoḥ sutayoḥ snehāvegādavalambamānahṛdayo bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: "May all be well! Then why do you sit waiting?" — thus addressed by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, that great being, his heart clinging [to his sons] through the force of affection as his two children's eyes were flooded with the distress that arose upon hearing of the gift, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: dattāvetau mayā tubhyaṃ kiṃ tu mātānayorgatā /
children.translated_text: "These two have been given by me to you; however, their mother has gone

children.text: vanaṃ mūlaphalasyārthe sāyamadyāgamiṣyati // Jm_9.56 //
children.translated_text: to the forest for roots and fruits — she will return this evening. || Jm 9.56 ||

children.text: tayā dṛṣṭāvupāghrātau mālināvabhyalaṃkṛtau /
children.translated_text: "Let them be seen by her, embraced, garlanded, and adorned;

children.text: ihaikarātraṃ viśramya śvo netāsi sutau mama // Jm_9.57 //
children.translated_text: rest here one night, and tomorrow you shall take my sons away." || Jm 9.57 ||

body.text: brāhmaṇa uvāca - alamanenātrabhavato nirbandhena /
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: "Enough of this insistence of your honor!

children.text: gauṇametaddhi nārīṇāṃ nāma vāmā iti sthitam /
children.translated_text: "For it is a well-known secondary quality of women — they are called 'perverse';

children.text: syāccaiva dānavighnaste tena vāsaṃ na rocaye // Jm_9.58 //
children.translated_text: and there may well be an obstruction to the gift — therefore a stay does not please me." || Jm 9.58 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - alaṃ dānavighnaśaṅkayā / sahadharmacāriṇī mama sā / yathā vātrabhavate rocate / api ca mahābrāhmaṇa,
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Enough of this suspicion of an obstruction to the gift. She is my partner in the righteous life. But as it pleases your honor. Moreover, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: sukumāratayā bālyātparicaryāsvakauśalāt /
children.translated_text: "Because of their tenderness, their youth, and their inexperience in service,

children.text: kīdṛśīṃ nāma kuryātāṃ dāsaprītimimau tava // Jm_9.59 //
children.translated_text: what manner of satisfaction in slaves could these two give you?" || Jm 9.59 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tvitthaṃgatāvetau śibirājaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
children.translated_text: "King <s>Śibi</s>, the grandfather, seeing these two in such a state,

children.text: addhā dadyādyadiṣṭaṃ te dhanaṃ niṣkrayametayoḥ // Jm_9.60 //
children.translated_text: would surely give whatever wealth you desire as ransom for them." || Jm 9.60 ||

children.text: yatastadviṣayaṃ sādhu tvamimau netumarhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore it is well for you to take them to his territory;

children.text: evaṃ hyarthena mahatā dharmeṇa ca sameṣyasi // Jm_9.61 //
children.translated_text: for thus you will meet with great wealth and with <s>Dharma</s> as well." || Jm 9.61 ||

body.text: (brāhmaṇa uvāca) - na śakṣyāmyahamāśīviṣadurāsadaṃ vipriyopāyanena rājānamabhigantum /
body.translated_text: (The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said:) "I am unable to approach the king, who is as unapproachable as a venomous serpent, with an unpleasant gift.

children.text: ācchindyānmadimau rājā daṇḍaṃ vā praṇayenmayi /
children.translated_text: "The king might seize them from me or impose punishment upon me;

children.text: yato neṣyāmyahamimau brāhmaṇyāḥ paricārakau // Jm_9.62 //
children.translated_text: therefore I shall take them as attendants for my wife." || Jm 9.62 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo yatheṣṭamidānīmitvaparisamāptārthamuktvā sānunayamanuśiṣya tanayau paricaryānukūlye pratigrahārthamabhiprasārite brāhmaṇasya pāṇau kamaṇḍalumāvarjayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having said "As you wish" — [the conversation] having thus reached its conclusion — affectionately instructing his sons in fitness for service, poured water from his water-pot into the outstretched hand of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> extended to receive the gift.

children.text: tasya yatnānurodhena papātāmbu kamaṇḍaloḥ /
children.translated_text: By his effort to restrain [himself], water fell from the water-pot,

children.text: padmapatrābhitāmrābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ svayameva tu // Jm_9.63 //
children.translated_text: but from his own eyes, copper-red as lotus petals, [tears fell] of their own accord. || Jm 9.63 ||

body.text: atha sa brāhyaṇo lābhātiharṣāt saṃbhramākulitamatirbodhisattvatanayāpaharaṇatvarayā saṃkṣiptapadamāśīrvacanamuktvā nirgamyatāmityājñākarkaśena vacasā kumārāvāśramapadānniṣkrāmayitumārebhe / atha kumārau viyogaduḥkhātibhāravyathitahṛdayau pitaramabhipraṇamya bāṣpoparudhyamānanayanāvūcatuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his mind agitated with excessive delight at his gain, in his haste to take away the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s children, having uttered a brief blessing in abridged words, began to drive the princes out of the hermitage with harsh commanding words: "Come out!" Then the two princes, their hearts agonized by the overwhelming pain of separation, bowed to their father, and with their eyes choked with tears, said —

children.text: ambā ca tāta niṣkrāntā tvaṃ ca nau dātumicchasi /
children.translated_text: "Mother has gone out, and you, father, wish to give us away;

children.text: yāvattāmapi paśyāvastato dāsyati nau bhavān // Jm_9.64 //
children.translated_text: let us at least see her — after that you may give us." || Jm 9.64 ||

body.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaḥ purā mātānayorāgacchati, asya vā putrasnehāt paścāttāpaḥ saṃbhavatīti vicintya padmakalāpamivānayorhastānābadhya latayā saṃtarjayanviceṣṭamānau pitaraṃ prati vyāvartitavadanau prakṛtisukumārau kumārau pracakarṣa / atha kṛṣṇājinā kumāryapūrvaduḥkhopanipātāt sasvaraṃ rudatī pitaramuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, thinking, "Before their mother returns, or before regret arises in him from love for his sons," bound their hands together like a bunch of lotuses with a creeper, and threatening, dragged along the two struggling princes, their faces turned back toward their father, tender by nature. Then <s>Kṛṣṇājinā</s>, the princess, stricken by this unprecedented blow of suffering, crying aloud, said to her father —

children.text: ayaṃ māṃ brāhmaṇastāta latayā hanti nirdayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This merciless <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> beats me with a creeper, father!

children.text: na cāyaṃ brāhmaṇo vyaktaṃ dhārmikā brāhmaṇāḥ kila // Jm_9.65 //
children.translated_text: He is surely no <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are righteous, they say." || Jm 9.65 ||

children.text: yakṣo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇacchadmā nūnaṃ harati khāditum /
children.translated_text: "This is a <s>Yakṣa</s> in the guise of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, surely carrying us off to devour!

children.text: nīyamānau piśācena tāta kiṃ nāvupekṣase // Jm_9.66 //
children.translated_text: As we are being led away by a <s>Piśāca</s>, father, why do you not look upon us?" || Jm 9.66 ||

body.text: atha jālī kumāro mātaramanuśocayannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Jālin</s>, lamenting on account of his mother, said —

children.text: naivedaṃ me tathā duḥkhaṃ yadayaṃ hanti māṃ dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is not so much this suffering to me that this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> beats me;

children.text: nāpaśyamambāṃ yattvadya tadvidārayatīva mām // Jm_9.67 //
children.translated_text: but that I did not see mother today — that is what tears me apart." || Jm 9.67 ||

children.text: rodiṣyati ciraṃ nūnamambā śūnye tapovane /
children.translated_text: "Mother will surely weep for a long time in the empty ascetic grove,

children.text: putraśokena kṛpaṇā hataśāveva cātakī // Jm_9.68 //
children.translated_text: wretched with grief for her children, like a female <s>cātaka</s> bird whose young have been killed." || Jm 9.68 ||

children.text: asmadarthe samāhṛtya vanānmūlaphalaṃ bahu /
children.translated_text: "Having gathered abundant roots and fruits from the forest for our sake,

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nvambā dṛṣṭvā śūnyaṃ tapovanam // Jm_9.69 //
children.translated_text: how will mother feel upon seeing the hermitage empty?" || Jm 9.69 ||

children.text: ime nāvaśvakāstāta hastikā rathakāśca ye /
children.translated_text: "These toy horses, father, and these little elephants and chariots of ours —

children.text: ato 'rdhaṃ deyamambāyai śokaṃ tena vineṣyati // Jm_9.70 //
children.translated_text: half should be given to mother; by that she will dispel her grief." || Jm 9.70 ||

children.text: vandyāsmadvacanādambā vāryā śokācca sarvathā /
children.translated_text: "Salute mother on our behalf, and by all means restrain her from grief;

children.text: durlabhaṃ hi punastāta tava tasyāśca darśanam // Jm_9.71 //
children.translated_text: for it will be difficult, father, to see you and her again." || Jm 9.71 ||

children.text: ehi kṛṣṇe mariṣyāvaḥ ko nvartho jīvitena nau /
children.translated_text: "Come, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, we shall die — what use is life to us?

children.text: dattāvāvāṃ narendreṇa brāhmaṇāya dhanaiṣiṇe // Jm_9.72 //
children.translated_text: We have been given away by the king to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who seeks wealth." || Jm 9.72 ||

body.text: ityuktvā jagmatuḥ /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, they departed.

body.text: atha bodhisattvastenātikaruṇena tanayapralāpenākampitamatirapi ka idānīṃ dattvānutāpaṃ kariṣyatīti niṣpratīkāreṇa śokāgninā vinirdahyamānahṛdayo viṣavegamūrcchāparigata iva samuparudhyamānacetāstatraiva niṣasāda / śītalānilavyajanapratilabdhasaṃjñaśca niṣkūjamivāśramapadaṃ tanayaśūnyamabhivīkṣya bāṣpagadgadasaṃniruddhakaṇṭha ityātmagatamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though his mind was shaken by the exceedingly pitiable prattle of his children, thinking, "Who, having given, would indulge in regret?" — his heart being burned by the fire of grief for which there was no remedy, his consciousness overwhelmed as if by the swooning of poison — sat down right there. Having regained consciousness through the fanning of a cool breeze, and seeing the hermitage empty of his children, as if mute, his throat choked with tears and sobs, he spoke thus within his mind —

children.text: putrābhidhāne hṛdaye samakṣaṃ praharanmama /
children.translated_text: "Striking my heart directly, in the part named 'children,'

children.text: nāśaṅkata kathaṃ nāma dhigalajjo bata dvijaḥ // Jm_9.73 //
children.translated_text: how was [that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] not ashamed? Shame on the shameless wretch!" || Jm 9.73 ||

children.text: pattikāvanupānatkau saukumāryātklamāsahau /
children.translated_text: "Having no little shoes, barefoot, unable to bear fatigue because of their tenderness,

children.text: yāsyataḥ kathamadhvānaṃ tasya ca preṣyatāṃ gato // Jm_9.74 //
children.translated_text: how will they travel the road, reduced to his servitude?" || Jm 9.74 ||

children.text: mārgaśramaparimlānau ko 'dya viśrāmayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: "Wilted with the weariness of the road, who will give them rest today?

children.text: kṣuttarṣaduḥkhābhihatau yāciṣyete kametya vā // Jm_9.75 //
children.translated_text: Stricken by the suffering of hunger and thirst, to whom will they go begging?" || Jm 9.75 ||

children.text: mama tāvadidaṃ duḥkhaṃ dhīratāṃ kartumicchataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even for me, who wishes to be steadfast, this grief is [such];

children.text: kā tvavasthā mama tayoḥ sutayoḥ sukhavṛddhayoḥ // Jm_9.76 //
children.translated_text: what then will be the condition of those two sons of mine, raised in comfort?" || Jm 9.76 ||

children.text: aho putraviyogāgnirnirdahatyeva me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ah, the fire of separation from my children truly burns my mind;

children.text: satāṃ tu dharmaṃ saṃsmṛtya ko 'nutāpaṃ kariṣyati // Jm_9.77 //
children.translated_text: but recalling the <s>Dharma</s> of the virtuous, who would indulge in regret?" || Jm 9.77 ||

body.text: atha madrī vipriyopanipātaśaṃsibhiraniṣṭernimittairupajanitavaimanasyā mūlaphalānyādāya kṣiprataramāgantukāmāpi vyālamṛgoparudhyamānamārgā ciratareṇāśramapadamupajagāma / ucitāyāṃ ca pratyudgamanabhūmāvākrīḍāsthāne ca tanayāvapaśyantī bhṛśataramarativaśamagāt /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Madrī</s>, her mind disturbed by inauspicious omens portending misfortune, having gathered roots and fruits, though wishing to return more quickly, her path obstructed by wild animals and beasts of prey, arrived at the hermitage after a longer time. And not seeing the children in their usual place of welcome, the playground, she fell into even greater distress.

children.text: anīpsitāśaṅkitajātasaṃbhramā tataḥ sutānveṣaṇacañcalekṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Trembling with alarm at the suspicion of what she did not desire, her eyes darting about in search of her sons,

children.text: prasaktamāhvānamasaṃparigrahaṃ tayorviditvā vyalapacchucāturā // Jm_9.78 //
children.translated_text: realizing that her continuous calling received no response, the poor woman was consumed with grief. || Jm 9.78 ||

children.text: samājavadyatpratibhāti me purā sutapralāpapratināditaṃ vanam /
children.translated_text: "That this forest, which formerly appeared to me like a festive gathering, resounded with the prattle of my children —

children.text: adarśanādadya tayostadeva me prayāti kāntāramivāśaraṇyatām // Jm_9.79 //
children.translated_text: that same [forest], now that I cannot see them, approaches for me the desolation of a wilderness without refuge." || Jm 9.79 ||

body.text: kiṃ nu khalu tau kumārau -
body.translated_text: "What indeed has happened to the princes?

children.text: krīḍāprasaṅgaśramajātanidrau suptau nu naṣṭau gahane vane vā /
children.translated_text: "Are they asleep, drowsy from the fatigue of play, or lost in the dense forest?

children.text: cirānmadabhyāgamanādatuṣṭau syātāṃ kvacid bālatayā nilīnau // Jm_9.80 //
children.translated_text: Or, displeased at my long absence, have they hidden somewhere in their childishness?" || Jm 9.80 ||

children.text: ruvanti kasmācca na pakṣiṇo 'pyamī samākulāstadvadhasākṣiṇo yadi /
children.translated_text: "And why do even these birds not cry out? Are they troubled, as if witnesses to their slaughter?

children.text: taraṃgabhaṅgairavinītakopayā hṛtau nu kiṃ nimnagayātivegayā // Jm_9.81 //
children.translated_text: Or have they been swept away by the swift-flowing river, unruly with the crests of its waves?" || Jm 9.81 ||

body.text: apīdānīṃ me vitathā mithyāvikalpā bhaveyuḥ / api rājaputrāya saputrāya svasti syāt / apyaniṣṭanivedināṃ nimittānāṃ maccharīra eva vipāko bhavet / kiṃ nu khalvidamanimittāpavṛttapraharṣamaratitamisrayāvacchādyamānaṃ vidravatīva hṛdayam / visrasyanta iva me gātrāṇi / vyākulā iva digvibhāgāḥ / bhramatīva cedaṃ paridhvastalakṣmīkaṃ vanamiti /
body.translated_text: "May these groundless, false imaginings of mine prove untrue! May it be well with the prince and his sons! May the fruition of these inauspicious omens fall upon my body alone! What indeed is this — my heart, robbed of joy and shrouded in the darkness of sorrow, seems to melt away; my limbs seem to collapse; the quarters seem confused; and this forest, its beauty ruined, seems to spin."

body.text: athānupraviśyāśramapadamekānte nikṣipya mūlaphalaṃ yathopacārapuraḥsaraṃ bhartāramabhigamya kva dārakāviti papraccha / atha bodhisattvo jānānaḥ snehadurbalatāṃ mātṛhṛdayasya durnivadyatvācca vipriyasya naināṃ kiṃcidvaktuṃ śaśāka /
body.translated_text: Then, having entered the hermitage and set down the fruits and roots in one place, she approached her husband with proper courtesy and asked, "Where are the children?" Now the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (one destined for awakening), knowing the tender weakness of a mother's heart and that the unwelcome news was impossible to speak gently, was unable to say anything to her.

children.text: janasya hi priyārhasya vipriyākhyānavahninā /
children.translated_text: For when one approaches a person deserving of love with the fire of unwelcome tidings,

children.text: upetya manasastāpaḥ saghṛṇena suduṣkaraḥ // Jm_9.82 //
children.translated_text: the anguish of mind that arises is, for a compassionate person, exceedingly difficult to bear.

body.text: atha madrī vyaktamakuśalaṃ me putrayoḥ, yadayamevaṃ tūpṇīṃbhūtaḥ śokadainyānuvṛttyaivetyavadhārya samantataḥ kṣiptacitteva vilokyāśramapadaṃ tanayāvapaśyantī sabāṣpagadgadaṃ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Madrī</s>, concluding, "Surely some misfortune has befallen my sons, since he remains silent like this, overcome by grief and dejection," looked around the hermitage grounds in every direction as if her mind were scattered, and not seeing her two sons, spoke again, her voice choked with tears:

children.text: dārakau ca na paśyāmi tvaṃ ca māṃ nābhibhāṣase /
children.translated_text: "I do not see the children, and you do not speak to me —

children.text: hatā khalvahaṃ kṛpaṇā vipriyaṃ hi na kathyate // Jm_9.83 //
children.translated_text: I am surely slain, wretched one that I am, for the unwelcome is left unspoken!"

body.text: ityuktvā śokāgninā parigatahṛdayā chinnamūleva latā nipapāta / patantīmeva caināṃ parigṛhya bodhisattvastṛṇaśayanamānīya śītābhiradbhiḥ pariṣicya pratyāgataprāṇāṃ samāśvāsayannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Having said this, her heart consumed by the fire of grief, she fell to the ground like a vine whose roots have been severed. Catching her even as she fell, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> brought her to a bed of grass, sprinkled her with cool water, and when her breath returned, consoling her, he said:

children.text: sahasaiva na te madri duḥkhamākhyātavānaham /
children.translated_text: "I did not tell you the sorrowful news all at once, O <s>Madrī</s>,

children.text: na hi saṃbhāvyate dhairyaṃ manasi snehadurbale // Jm_9.84 //
children.translated_text: for steadfastness cannot be expected in a heart weakened by love."

children.text: jarādāridryaduḥkhārto brāhmaṇo māmupāgamat /
children.translated_text: "A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, afflicted by the suffering of old age and poverty, came to me;

children.text: tasmai dattau mayā putrau samāśvasihi mā śucaḥ // Jm_9.85 //
children.translated_text: to him I have given our two sons. Take heart and do not grieve!"

children.text: māṃ paśya madri mā putrau paridevīśca devi mā /
children.translated_text: "Look at me, <s>Madrī</s>, not at the sons — do not lament, O queen!

children.text: putraśokasaśalye me prahārṣīriva mā hṛdi // Jm_9.86 //
children.translated_text: Do not drive the shaft of grief for our sons deeper into my heart!"

children.text: yācitena kathaṃ śakyaṃ na dātumapi jīvitam /
children.translated_text: "How can one who is asked refuse to give, even if it be one's own life?

children.text: anumodasva tad bhadre putradānamidaṃ mama // Jm_9.87 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O noble one, rejoice in this gift of my sons!"

body.text: tacchrutvā madrī putravināśaśaṅkāvyathitahṛdayā putrayorjīvitapravṛttiśravaṇāt pratanūbhūtaśokaklamā bharturadhṛtiparihārārthaṃ pramṛjya nayane savismayamudīkṣamāṇā bhartāramuvāca - āścaryaṃ / kiṃ bahunā
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Madrī</s>, whose heart had been tormented by the fear of her sons' death, felt her grief and exhaustion diminish upon learning that her sons were alive. Wiping her eyes for the sake of dispelling her husband's distress, she gazed at him with wonder and said: "How astonishing! What more can be said —"

children.text: nūnaṃ vismayavaktavyacetaso 'pi divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Surely even the heaven-dwellers, whose minds are accustomed to marvels, must be amazed

children.text: yadityalabdhaprasarastava cetasi matsaraḥ // Jm_9.88 //
children.translated_text: that selfishness has found so little purchase in your heart!"

children.text: tathā hi dikṣu prasṛtapratisvanaiḥ samantato daivatadundubhisvanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "For with the sounds of divine drums resounding and echoing in every direction,

children.text: prasaktavispaṣṭapadākṣaraṃ nabhastavaiva kīrtigrathanādarādabhūt // Jm_9.89 //
children.translated_text: the sky itself became, as it were, zealously engaged in weaving garlands of your fame, with words and syllables ringing out clearly and continuously."

children.text: prakampiśailendrapayodharā dharā madādivābhūdabhivṛddhavepathuḥ /
children.translated_text: "The earth, with its mountains and clouds, trembled with ever-increasing quaking, as if from exhilaration;

children.text: divaḥ patadbhiḥ kusumaiśca kāñcanaiḥ savidyududyotamivābhavannabhaḥ // Jm_9.90 //
children.translated_text: and with golden flowers falling from heaven, the sky shone as though illuminated by flashes of lightning."

children.text: tadalaṃ śokadainyena dattvā cittaṃ prasādaya /
children.translated_text: "So enough of grief and dejection — having given, let your mind be at peace,

children.text: nipānabhūto lokānāṃ dātaiva ca punarbhava // Jm_9.91 //
children.translated_text: and be once again a reservoir of generosity for the world!"

body.text: atha śakro devendraḥ kṣititalacalanādākampite vividharatnaprabhodbhāsini sumerau parvatarāje kimidamiti samutpannavimarśo vismayotphullanayanebhyo lokapālebhyaḥ pṛthivīkampakāraṇaṃ viśvantaraputradānamupalabhya praharṣavismayāghūrṇitamanāḥ prabhātāyāṃ tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ brāhmaṇarūpī viśvantaramarthivadabhyagacchat / kṛtātithisatkāraśca bodhisattvena kenārtha ityupanimantrito bhāryāmenamayācata -
body.translated_text: Now <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>Devas</s> (gods), when Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, blazing with the radiance of manifold jewels, trembled at the shaking of the earth, wondered "What is this?" and learning from the world-guardians, whose eyes were wide with astonishment, that the cause of the earthquake was <s>Viśvantara</s>'s gift of his sons, his mind reeled with joy and wonder. When that night had passed, he approached <s>Viśvantara</s> in the guise of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, as if a supplicant. Having been received with hospitality by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and asked "What do you seek?", he requested his wife:

children.text: mahāhradeṣvambha ivopaśoṣaṃ na dānadharmaḥ samupaiti satsu /
children.translated_text: "The <s>dharma</s> (virtue) of giving never diminishes among the virtuous, just as water in great lakes never runs dry.

children.text: yāce tatastvāṃ surasannibhā yā bhāryāmimāmahaṃsi tatpradātum // Jm_9.92 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you: this wife of yours, who resembles a goddess — please give her to me!"

children.text: avimanā eva tu bodhisattvastathetyasmai pratiśuśrāva /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without any trace of reluctance, promised him, "So be it."

children.text: tataḥ sa vāmena kareṇa madrīmādāya savyena kamaṇḍaluṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Then, taking <s>Madrī</s> with his left hand and the water-vessel with his right,

children.text: nyapātayattasya jalaṃ karāgre manobhuvaścetasi śokavahnim // Jm_9.93 //
children.translated_text: he poured the water upon the other's hand, extinguishing the fire of grief in the heart of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love).

children.text: cukopa madrī na tu no ruroda viveda sā tasya hi taṃ svabhāvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Madrī</s> grew angry but did not weep, for she understood his nature well;

children.text: apūrvaduḥkhātibharāturā tu taṃ prekṣamāṇā likhiteva tasthau // Jm_9.94 //
children.translated_text: yet, overwhelmed by the unbearable weight of unprecedented suffering, she stood gazing at him, motionless as a painted figure.

body.text: tad dṛṣṭvā paramavismayākrāntahṛdayaḥ śakro devānāmindrastaṃ mahāsattvamabhiṣṭuvannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Seeing this, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>Devas</s>, his heart seized by the utmost wonder, praised that great being and said:

children.text: aho vikṛṣṭāntaratā sadasaddharmayoryathā /
children.translated_text: "Ah, how far apart indeed are the depths of virtue and vice!

children.text: śraddhātumapi karmedaṃ kā śaktirakṛtātmanām // Jm_9.95 //
children.translated_text: What capacity have the undisciplined even to believe in such a deed?"

children.text: avītarāgeṇa satā putradāramatipriyam /
children.translated_text: "That one who has not yet transcended passion should give away sons and wife, so exceedingly dear,

children.text: niḥsaṅgamiti dātavyaṃ kā nāmeyamudāttatā // Jm_9.96 //
children.translated_text: without any attachment — what nobility is this!"

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ tvadguṇaraktasaṃkathaiḥ prakīryamāṇeṣu yaśassu dikṣu te /
children.translated_text: "Without doubt, when your glories are proclaimed in every direction through tales celebrating your virtues,

children.text: tirobhaviṣyantyaparā yaśaḥśriyaḥ pataṃgatejassu yathānyadīptayaḥ // Jm_9.97 //
children.translated_text: the fame of others will vanish, like lesser lights when the stars lose their brilliance."

children.text: tasya te 'bhyanumodante karmedamatimānuṣam /
children.translated_text: "This superhuman deed of yours is applauded by

children.text: yakṣagandharvabhujagāstridaśāśca savāsavāḥ // Jm_9.98 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), and the Thirty Gods together with <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra)."

body.text: ityuktvā śakraḥ svameva vapurabhijvaladāsthāya śakro 'hamasmīti ca nivedyātmānaṃ bodhisattvamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s> resumed his own radiant form, announced "I am <s>Śakra</s>," and said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: tubhyameva prayacchāmi madrīṃ bhāryāmimāmaham /
children.translated_text: "I give <s>Madrī</s>, this wife, back to you yourself,

children.text: vyatītya na hi śītāṃśuṃ candrikā sthātumarhati // Jm_9.99 //
children.translated_text: for moonlight cannot remain after passing beyond the moon."

children.text: tanmā cintāṃ putrayorviprayogādrājyabhraṃśānmā ca saṃtāpamāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Do not worry about separation from your sons, nor grieve over the loss of your kingdom —

children.text: sārdhaṃ tābhyāmabhyupetaḥ pitā te kartā rājyaṃ tvatsanāthaṃ sanātham // Jm_9.100 //
children.translated_text: your father, together with them, will come to you, and will make your kingdom secure and enduring under your protection."

body.text: ityuktvā śakrastatraivāntardadhe / śakrānubhāvācca sa brāhmaṇo bodhisattvatanayau śibiviṣayameva saṃprāpayāmāsa / atha śibayaḥ saṃjayaśca śibirājastadatikaruṇamatiduṣkaraṃ ca bodhisattvasya karma śrutvā samākleditahṛdayā brāhmaṇahastānniṣkrīya bodhisattvatanayau prasādyānīya ca viśvantaraṃ rājya eva pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śakra</s> vanished right there. And by <s>Śakra</s>'s power, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> brought the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s two sons back to the <s>Śibi</s> territory. Then the <s>Śibis</s> and King <s>Saṃjaya</s>, the <s>Śibi</s> king, hearing of that supremely compassionate and exceedingly difficult deed of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, their hearts melted, ransomed the two sons from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s hands, and having propitiated and brought back <s>Viśvantara</s>, established him once more in the kingdom.

body.text: tadevamatyadbhutā bodhisattvacaryeti tadunmukheṣu sattvaviśeṣeṣu nāvajñā pratīghāto vā karaṇīyaḥ / tathāgatavarṇe satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe copaneyam /
body.translated_text: Thus the conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is most wondrous indeed. Therefore, toward those distinguished beings who are devoted to it, one should show neither contempt nor hostility. And one should attend respectfully to hearing the <s>Dharma</s> (Teaching) when the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (the Thus-Gone One) are being praised.

body.text: iti viśvantarajātakaṃ navamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>Jātaka</s> (birth-story), that of <s>Viśvantara</s>.

body.text: 10. Yajñajātakam
body.translated_text: 10. The <s>Jātaka</s> of the Sacrifice (<s>Yajña-jātaka</s>)

body.text: na kalyāṇāśayāḥ pāpapratāraṇāmanuvidhīyanta ityāśayaśuddhau prayatitavyam / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Those of noble disposition do not follow the deceptions of the wicked — therefore one should strive for purity of intention. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila svapuṇyaprabhāvopanatāmānatasarvasāmantāṃ praśāntasvaparacakrādyupadravatvādakaṇṭakāmasapatnāmekātapatrāṃ dāyādyakramāgatāṃ pṛthivīṃ pālayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, ruled the earth, which had come to him by right of inheritance — an earth over which all neighboring kings bowed, free from the disturbances of hostile armies and the like, without thorns or rivals, sheltered under a single royal umbrella — all attained through the power of his own merit.

children.text: nāthaḥ pṛthivyāḥ sa jitendriyārirbhuṃktāvagīteṣu phaleṣvasaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the lord of the earth, having conquered his senses and inner enemies, partaking without attachment of pleasures that none could disparage,

children.text: prajāhiteṣvāhitasarvabhāvo gharmaikakāryo munivad babhūva // Jm_10.1 //
children.translated_text: devoted his entire being to the welfare of his subjects and, like a sage, was solely dedicated to the performance of his duties.

children.text: viveda lokasya hi sa svabhāvaṃ pradhānacaryānukṛtipradhānam /
children.translated_text: For he understood the nature of the world, in which people chiefly follow the conduct of their leaders;

children.text: śreyaḥ samādhitsurataḥ prajāsu viśeṣato dharmavidhau sasañje // Jm_10.2 //
children.translated_text: therefore, wishing to establish the good among his people, he especially devoted himself to the observance of <s>Dharma</s> (righteous law).

children.text: dadau dhanaṃ śīlavidhiṃ samādade kṣamāṃ niṣeve jagadarthamaihata /
children.translated_text: He gave wealth, upheld the discipline of moral conduct, practiced forbearance, and strove for the welfare of the world;

children.text: prajāhitādhyāśayasaumyadarśanaḥ sa mūrtimāndharma iva vyarocata // Jm_10.3 //
children.translated_text: with a countenance made gentle by his intention to benefit his subjects, he shone like <s>Dharma</s> (Righteousness) incarnate.

body.text: atha kadācittadbhujābhiguptamapi taṃ viṣayaṃ sattvānāṃ karmavaiguṇyātpramādavaśagatvācca varṣakarmādhikṛtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ durvṛṣṭiparyākulatā kvacitkvacidabhidudrāva / atha sa rājā vyaktamayaṃ mama prajānāṃ vā dharmāpacārātsamupanato 'nartha iti niścitamatiḥ saṃrūḍhahitādhyāśayatvātprajāsu tadduḥkhamamṛṣyamāṇo dharmatattvajñasaṃmatānpurohitapramukhānbrāhmavṛddhānmatisacivāṃśca taduddharaṇopāyaṃ papraccha / atha te vedavihitamanekaprāṇiśatavadhārambhabhīṣaṇaṃ yajñavidhiṃ suvṛṣṭihetuṃ manyamānāstasmai saṃvarṇayāmāsuḥ / viditavṛttāntastu sa rājā yajñavihitānāṃ prāṇivaiśasānāṃ karuṇātmakatvānna teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ bhāvenābhyanandat / vinayānuvṛttyā cainānpratyākhyānarūkṣākṣaramanuktvā prastāvāntareṇaiṣāṃ tāṃ kathāṃ tiraścakāra / te punarapi taṃ rājānaṃ dharmasaṃkathāprastāvalabdhāvasarā gāmbhīryāvagūḍhaṃ tasya bhāvamajānānā yajñapravṛttaye samanuśaśāsuḥ -
body.translated_text: Now, once upon a time, although that realm was protected by his might, drought and calamity assailed it here and there, owing to the adverse <s>karma</s> (actions) of beings and the negligence of the <s>Devaputras</s> (divine beings) charged with rainfall. Then that king, having firmly resolved, "Surely this calamity has come upon my subjects or myself because of some lapse in <s>Dharma</s>," and being unable to endure that suffering of his people on account of his deeply rooted benevolent disposition, consulted the senior <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> led by the royal chaplain — those approved by knowers of the truth of <s>Dharma</s> — and his ministers of counsel, asking them for a remedy. They, believing that a Vedic sacrificial rite — terrifying in its commencement with the slaughter of hundreds of living creatures — was the means to bring good rainfall, recommended it to him. But the king, having understood the matter and being compassionate by nature, did not inwardly approve of their words regarding the slaughter of animals prescribed for the sacrifice. And without uttering the harsh words of outright refusal, out of courtesy, he deflected their proposal on another occasion. But they, finding an opportunity again during a discussion of <s>Dharma</s> and not comprehending the depth of his concealed intention, once more urged the king to undertake the sacrifice:

children.text: kāryāṇi rājñāṃ niyatāni yāni lābhe pṛthivyāḥ paripālane ca /
children.translated_text: "The duties prescribed for kings — those pertaining to the acquisition and protection of the earth —

children.text: nātyeti kālastava tāni nityaṃ teṣāṃ kramo dharmasukhāni yadvat // Jm_10.4 //
children.translated_text: time does not pass beyond these for you, just as the sequence of those duties brings both <s>Dharma</s> (merit) and happiness."

children.text: trivargasevānipuṇasya tasya prajāhitārthaṃ dhṛtakārmukasya /
children.translated_text: "For one so skilled in the pursuit of the three aims of life, who has taken up the bow for the welfare of his people,

children.text: yajñābhidhāne suralokasetau pramādatandreva kathaṃ matiste // Jm_10.5 //
children.translated_text: how is it that sloth and indifference have entered your mind regarding the sacrifice, which is a bridge to the world of the gods?"

children.text: bhṛtyairivājñā bahu manyate te sākṣādiyaṃ siddhiriti kṣitīśaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your command is honored by your subjects as much as by servants; kings regard this very accomplishment as paramount.

children.text: śreyāṃsi kīrtijvalitāni cetuṃ yajñairayaṃ te ripukāla kālaḥ // Jm_10.6 //
children.translated_text: This is the time, O destroyer of foes, for you to reap glories blazing with fame through sacrificial rites!"

children.text: kāmaṃ sadā dīkṣita eva ca tvaṃ dānaprasaṅgānniyamādarācca /
children.translated_text: "Indeed, you are always consecrated, as it were, by your devotion to giving and your dedication to vows of restraint;

children.text: vedaprasiddhaiḥ kratubhistathāpi yuktaṃ bhavenmoktumṛṇaṃ surāṇām // Jm_10.7 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, it would be fitting to discharge the debt to the gods through the rituals established in the <s>Vedas</s>."

children.text: sviṣṭyābhituṣṭāni hi daivatāni bhūtāni vṛṣṭyā pratimānayanti /
children.translated_text: "For the deities, gratified by well-performed offerings, repay living beings with rain.

children.text: iti prajānāṃ hitamātmanaśca yaśaskaraṃ yajñavidhiṃ juṣasva // Jm_10.8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, embrace the sacrificial rite, which is beneficial to your people, to yourself, and brings glory!"

body.text: tasya cintā prādurabhavat - atidurnyasto batāyaṃ parapratyayahāryapelavamatiramīmāṃsako dharmapriyaḥ śraddadhāno jano yatra hi nāma -
body.translated_text: A thought arose in him: "Alas, how badly misled are the people — susceptible to the influence of others, soft in judgment, lacking critical inquiry, fond of <s>Dharma</s>, and trusting — when indeed:

children.text: ya eva lokeṣu śaraṇyasammatāsta eva hiṃsāmapi dharmato gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those very ones who are regarded in the world as worthy of refuge have themselves sanctioned violence as righteous —

children.text: vivartate kaṣṭamapāyasaṅkaṭe janastadādeśitakāpathānugaḥ // Jm_10.9 //
children.translated_text: how grievous it is that the people, following the wrong path pointed out by them, wander in the straits of ruin!"

children.text: ko hi nāmābhisambandho dharmasya paśuhiṃsayā /
children.translated_text: "What connection indeed is there between <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) and the slaughter of animals,

children.text: suralokādhivāsasya daivataprīṇanasya vā // Jm_10.10 //
children.translated_text: or between residence in the heavenly world and the gratification of the gods?"

children.text: viśasyamānaḥ kila mantraśaktibhiḥ paśurdivaṃ gacchati tena tadvadhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is said that the sacrificial animal, slain by the power of <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae), goes to heaven, and that therefore its killing

children.text: upaiti dharmatvamitīdamapyasatparaiḥ kṛtaṃ ko hi paratra lapsyate // Jm_10.11 //
children.translated_text: attains the status of a righteous act — but this is false. A deed performed by others — who indeed will reap its fruit in the hereafter?"

children.text: asatpravṛtteranivṛttamānasaḥ śubheṣu karmasvavirūḍhaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One whose mind has not turned away from wrongdoing, in whom no firm conviction in virtuous deeds has taken root —

children.text: paśurdivaṃ yāsyati kena hetunā hato 'pi yajñe svakṛtāśrayādvinā // Jm_10.12 //
children.translated_text: by what reason would a sacrificial animal go to heaven when slain, unless through the result of its own past actions?"

children.text: hataśca yajñe tridivaṃ yadi vrajennanu vrajeyuḥ paśutāṃ svayaṃ dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And if the animal slain in sacrifice were truly to reach heaven, would not the priests themselves eagerly seek the condition of being the sacrificial animal?

children.text: yatastu nāyaṃ vidhirīkṣyate kvacidvacastadeṣāṃ ka iva grahīṣyati // Jm_10.13 //
children.translated_text: But since this practice is nowhere observed, who indeed would accept their words?"

children.text: atulyagandharddhirasaujasaṃ śubhāṃ sudhāṃ kilotsṛjya varāpsarodhṛtām /
children.translated_text: "Would the heaven-dwellers truly abandon the divine nectar — auspicious, of incomparable fragrance, potency, flavor, and vitality, offered by the finest <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) —

children.text: mudaṃ prayāsyanti vapādikāraṇādvadhena śocyasya paśordivaukasaḥ // Jm_10.14 //
children.translated_text: and find delight on account of the sacrificial fat and such offerings obtained through the slaughter of a pitiable animal?"

body.text: tadidamatra prāptakālamiti viniścitya sa rājā yajñārambhasamutsuka iva nāma tatteṣāṃ vacanaṃ pratigṛhyāvocadenan - sanāthaḥ khalvahamanugrahavāṃśca yadevaṃ me hitāvahitamanaso 'trabhavantaḥ / tadicchāmi puruṣamedhasahasreṇa yaṣṭum / anviṣyatāṃ tadupayogyasambhārasamudānayanārthaṃ yathādhikāramamātyaiḥ / parīkṣyatāṃ satrāgāraniveśanayogyo bhūmipradeśastadanuguṇaśca tithikaraṇamuhūrtanakṣatrayoga iti /
body.translated_text: Having thus determined, "This is now the appropriate course of action," that king, as if eager to commence the sacrifice, accepted their proposal and said to them: "I am indeed fortunate and favored that your honors are so devoted to my welfare. Therefore, I wish to perform a thousand human sacrifices (<s>puruṣamedha</s>). Let the ministers, each according to his authority, seek out and gather the requisite materials for this purpose. Let a suitable tract of land be examined for the erection of the sacrificial hall, along with a fitting conjunction of lunar day, astronomical sign, auspicious moment, and constellation!"

body.text: athainaṃ purohita uvāca - īpsitārthasiddhaye snātu tāvanmahārāja ekasya yajñasya samāptāvavabhṛthe / athottareṣāmārambhaḥ kariṣyate krameṇa / yugapatpuruṣapaśavaḥ sahasraśo hi parigṛhyamāṇā vyaktamudvegadoṣāya prajānāṃ te syuriti / astyetaditi brāhmaṇairuktaḥ sa rājā tānuvāca - alamatrabhavatāṃ prakṛtikopāśaṅkayā / tathā hi saṃvidhāsye yathodvegaṃ me prajā na yāsyantīti / atha sa rājā paurajānapadānsaṃnipātyāvravīt - icchāmi puruṣamedhasahasreṇa yaṣṭum / na ca mayārhaḥ kaścidakāmaḥ puruṣaḥ paśutve niyoktumaduṣṭaḥ / tadyaṃ yamataḥ prabhṛti vo drakṣyāmi vyavadhūtapramādanidreṇa vimalena cāracakṣuṣā śīlamaryādātivartinamasmadājñāṃ paribhavantaṃ taṃ taṃ svakulapāṃsanaṃ deśakaṇṭakamahaṃ yajñapaśunimittamādāsya ityetadvo viditamastviti / atha teṣāṃ mukhyatamāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvainamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Purohita</s> (royal priest) said to him: "For the accomplishment of your desired aim, first bathe, O great king, in the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) at the completion of one sacrifice; then the commencement of the subsequent ones shall be undertaken in due order. For if human victims are seized by the thousands all at once, they would clearly cause alarm among the people." When the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said "So be it," that king addressed them: "Let there be no apprehension on your part regarding the discontent of the populace. For I shall arrange matters in such a way that my subjects will not be alarmed." Then that king, having assembled the citizens and countryfolk, declared: "I wish to perform a sacrifice with a thousand human sacrifices. But I am not able to consign any unwilling and innocent person to the status of a sacrificial victim. Therefore, whomever among you I shall henceforth observe through my spotless eye of surveillance — one who has shaken off the sleep of negligence — transgressing the bounds of virtuous conduct, flouting my command, that disgrace to his own family, that thorn of the realm, him I shall seize as a sacrificial victim. Let this be known to you." Then the most eminent among them, joining their palms in reverence, said to him:

children.text: sarvāḥ kriyāstava hitapravaṇāḥ prajānāṃ tatrāvamānanavidhernaradeva ko 'rthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "All your actions are inclined toward the welfare of your people; therein, O lord of men, what purpose is served by the rite of disrespect?

children.text: brahmāpi te caritamabhyanumantumarhaḥ sādhupramāṇa paramatra bhavānpramāṇam // Jm_10.15 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> should approve of your conduct; where the virtuous are the standard, you, O Lord, are the supreme authority." || Jm 10.15 ||

children.text: priyaṃ yadeva devasya tadasmākamapi priyam /
children.translated_text: "Whatever is dear to the sovereign, that is dear to us as well;

children.text: asmatpriyahitādanyad dṛśyate na hi te priyam // Jm_10.16 //
children.translated_text: for nothing other than what promotes our welfare and happiness appears to be dear to you." || Jm 10.16 ||

body.text: iti pratigṛhītavacanaḥ paurajanāpadaiḥ sa rājā janaprakāśenāḍambareṇa pratyayitānamātyānpāpajanopagrahaṇārthaṃ janapadaṃ nagarāṇi ca preṣayāmāsa samantataśca pratyahamiti ghoṣaṇāḥ kārayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Thus, having received the assent of the citizens and countryfolk, that king, with public fanfare, dispatched trusted ministers to the countryside and cities for the apprehension of evildoers, and had proclamations made everywhere, day after day:

children.text: abhayamabhayado dadāti rājā sthiraśuciśīladhanāya sajjanāya /
children.translated_text: "The king, giver of safety, grants fearlessness to the virtuous, whose conduct is steadfast and pure, whose wealth is good character;

children.text: avinayanirataiḥ prajāhitārthaṃ narapaśubhistu sahasraśo yiyakṣuḥ // Jm_10.17 //
children.translated_text: but he desires to sacrifice by the thousands with human victims — those devoted to misconduct — for the welfare of the people." || Jm 10.17 ||

children.text: tadyaḥ kaścidataḥ prabhṛtyavinayaślāghānuvṛttyudbhavāt
children.translated_text: "Whoever, from this day forth, born of devotion to boasting of misconduct,

children.text: sāmantakṣitipārcitāmapi nṛpasyājñāmavajñāsyati /
children.translated_text: shall disregard the king's command, honored even by neighboring sovereigns,

children.text: sa svaireva viṣahya yajñapaśutāmāpāditaḥ karmabhir
children.translated_text: he, brought to the status of a sacrificial victim by his own deeds, freely enduring [the consequence],

children.text: yūpābaddhatanurviṣādakṛpaṇaḥ śuṣyañjanairdrakṣyate // Jm_10.18 //
children.translated_text: shall be seen by the people, his body bound to the sacrificial post, pitiable with despair, withering away." || Jm 10.18 ||

body.text: atha tadviṣayanivāsinaḥ puruṣā yajñapaśunimittaṃ duḥśīlapuruṣānveṣaṇādaraṃ tamanvavekṣya rājñastāṃ ca ghoṣaṇāmatibhīṣaṇāṃ pratyahamupaśrṛṇvantaḥ pāpajanopagrahāvahitāṃśca rājapuruṣānsamantataḥ samāpatato 'bhivīkṣya tyaktadauḥśīlyānurāgāḥ śīlasaṃvarasamādānaparā vairaprasaṅgaparāṅmukhāḥ parasparapremagauravasumukhāḥ praśāntavigrahavivādā gurujanavacanānuvartinaḥ saṃvibhāgaviśāradāḥ priyātithayo vinayanaibhṛtyaślāghinaḥ kṛta iva yuge babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the men dwelling in that realm, observing the king's diligent search for ill-conducted persons as sacrificial victims, hearing day after day that most terrifying proclamation, and seeing the king's officers vigilantly engaged in seizing evildoers dispatched in all directions — they abandoned their attachment to misconduct, became devoted to the adoption of moral discipline, turned away from involvement in enmity, became disposed toward mutual affection and respect, their quarrels and disputes pacified, obedient to the words of their elders, skilled in sharing, hospitable to guests, taking pride in modesty and self-restraint — as though the <s>Kṛta</s> age had come into being.

children.text: bhayena mṛtyoḥ paralokacintayā kulābhimānena yaśo 'nurakṣayā /
children.translated_text: Through fear of death, through reflection upon the next world, through pride in their family, through solicitude for their reputation,

children.text: suśuklabhāvācca viruḍhayā hriyā janaḥ saḥ śīlāmalabhūṣaṇo 'bhavat // Jm_10.19 //
children.translated_text: and through a most pure nature from which modesty flourished, those people became adorned with the spotlessness of good conduct. || Jm 10.19 ||

children.text: yathā yathā dharmaparo 'bhavajjanastathā tathā rakṣijano viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: The more the people became devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, the more the king's officers, with special zeal,

children.text: cakāra duḥśīlajanābhimārgaṇāmataśca dharmānna cacāla kaścana // Jm_10.20 //
children.translated_text: conducted their search for persons of ill conduct — and therefore no one wavered from righteousness. || Jm 10.20 ||

children.text: svadeśavṛttāntamathopaśuśruvānimaṃ nṛpaḥ prītiviśeṣabhūṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, adorned with supreme delight, heard this account of the state of his own realm;

children.text: carānpriyākhyānakadānavistaraiḥ santarpayitvā sacivānsamanvaśāt // Jm_10.21 //
children.translated_text: and having gratified his agents with lavish gifts of pleasing news, he instructed his ministers: || Jm 10.21 ||

children.text: parā manīṣā mama rakṣituṃ prajā gatāśca tāḥ samprati dakṣiṇīyatām /
children.translated_text: "My highest purpose is to protect my subjects, and they have now attained the status of worthy recipients of gifts.

children.text: idaṃ ca yajñāya dhanaṃ pratarkitaṃ yiyakṣurasmīti yathāpratarkitam // Jm_10.22 //
children.translated_text: This wealth has been set aside for the sacrifice; I wish to sacrifice — let it be as planned." || Jm 10.22 ||

children.text: yadīpsitaṃ yasya sukhendhanaṃ dhanaṃ prakāmamāpnotu sa tanmadantikāt /
children.translated_text: "Whatever is desired by whomever — wealth that readily fuels happiness — let him obtain it to his heart's content from my presence,

children.text: itīyamasmadviṣayopatāpinī daridratā nirviṣayā yathā bhavet // Jm_10.23 //
children.translated_text: so that this poverty which afflicts those in my domain may become without a domain of its own." || Jm 10.23 ||

children.text: mayi prajārakṣaṇaniścayasthite sahāyasampatparivṛddhasādhane /
children.translated_text: "While I stand firm in my resolve to protect my subjects, with the means of accomplishment enriched by the wealth of able allies,

children.text: iyaṃ janārtirmadamarṣadīpanī muhurmuṃhurme jvalatīva cetasi // Jm_10.24 //
children.translated_text: this affliction of the people, which inflames pride and indignation, burns again and again, as it were, in my heart." || Jm 10.24 ||

body.text: atha te tasya rājñaḥ sacivāḥ paramamiti pratigṛhya tadvacanaṃ sarveṣu grāmanagaranigameṣu mārgaviśrāmapradeśeṣu ca dānaśālāḥ kārayitvā yathāsandiṣṭaṃ rājñā pratyahamarthijanamabhilaṣitairarthavisargaiḥ santarpayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those ministers of the king, accepting his words with "Excellent!", having caused gift-halls to be built in all villages, cities, market-towns, and at resting places along the roads, gratified the supplicants day after day with disbursements of desired goods, as the king had commanded.

children.text: atha vihāya janaḥ sa daridratāṃ samamavāptavasurvasudhādhipāt /
children.translated_text: Then those people, having abandoned their poverty, having obtained wealth equally from the lord of the earth,

children.text: vividhacitraparicchadabhūṣaṇaḥ pravitatotsavaśobha ivābhavat // Jm_10.25 //
children.translated_text: adorned with various and splendid possessions and ornaments, appeared as though a festival had been spread out in all its beauty. || Jm 10.25 ||

children.text: pramuditārthijanastutisañcitaṃ pravitatāna nṛpasya diśo yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fame of the king, swelled by the praises of the delighted supplicants, spread to all the quarters,

children.text: tanutaraṅgavivardhitavistaraṃ sara ivāmbujakesarajaṃ rajaḥ // Jm_10.26 //
children.translated_text: like the pollen born of lotus filaments on a lake, its expanse increased by slender waves. || Jm 10.26 ||

body.text: iti nṛpasya sunītiguṇāśrayātsucaritābhimukhe nikhile jane /
body.translated_text: Thus, through the king's excellent conduct grounded in wise policy, when all the people had become inclined toward virtuous behavior,

body.text: samabhibhūtabalāḥ kuśalocchrayairvilayamīyurasaṅgamupadravāḥ // Jm_10.27 //
body.translated_text: the calamities, their strength overwhelmed by the rising tide of virtue, went to dissolution without resistance. || Jm 10.27 ||

children.text: aviṣamatvasukhā ṛtavo 'bhavannavanṛpā iva dharmaparāyaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The seasons became equable and pleasant, like new kings devoted to <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: vividhasasyadharā ca vasundharā sakamalāmalanīlajalāśayā // Jm_10.28 //
children.translated_text: and the earth bore various crops, with its lakes pure, blue-watered, and adorned with lotuses. || Jm 10.28 ||

children.text: na janamabhyarujanprabalā rujaḥ paṭutaraṃ guṇamoṣadhayo dadhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Powerful diseases did not afflict the people; medicinal herbs yielded their potency more abundantly;

children.text: ṛtuvaśena vavau niyato 'nilaḥ pariyayuśca śubhena pathā grahāḥ // Jm_10.29 //
children.translated_text: the wind blew regularly according to the seasons, and the planets traversed their auspicious courses. || Jm 10.29 ||

children.text: na paracakrakṛtaṃ samabhūdbhayaṃ na ca parasparajaṃ na ca daivikam /
children.translated_text: There was no fear caused by foreign armies, nor any arising from one another, nor from divine sources;

children.text: niyamadharmapare nibhṛte jane kṛtamivātra yugaṃ samapadyata // Jm_10.30 //
children.translated_text: among the people, who were restrained and devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, a <s>Kṛta</s> age, as it were, came to pass. || Jm 10.30 ||

body.text: athaivaṃ pravṛttena dharmayajñena rājñā praśamiteṣvarthijanaduḥkheṣu sārdhamupadravaiḥ pramuditajanasambādhāyāmabhyudayaramyadarśanāyāṃ vasundharāyāṃ nṛpaterāśīrvacanādhyayanasavyāpāre loke vitanyamāne samantato rājayaśasi prasādāvarjitamatiḥ kaścidamātyamukhyo rājānamityuvāca - suṣṭhu khalvidamucyate -
body.translated_text: Then, when through this <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice conducted by the king the sufferings of the supplicants had been allayed along with all calamities, when the earth, thronged with joyful people, was lovely to behold in its prosperity, and when the king's fame was being spread in all directions as the world was occupied with reciting benedictions and praises — a certain chief minister, his mind won over by admiration, spoke thus to the king: "Truly it is well said:

children.text: uttamādhamamadhyānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ nityadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: "From constantly observing affairs of the highest, lowest, and middling sort,

children.text: uparyupari buddhīnāṃ carantīśvarabuddhayaḥ // Jm_10.31 //
children.translated_text: the minds of rulers move ever higher and higher." || Jm 10.31 ||

body.text:
iti / devena hi paśuvaiśasavācyadoṣavirahitena dharmayajñena prajānāmubhayalokahitaṃ sampāditamupadravāśca praśamaṃ nītā dāridryaduḥkhāni ca śīle pratiṣṭhāpitānām /
kiṃ bahunā? sabhāgyāstāḥ prajāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, by His Majesty, through a <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice free from the reproachable fault of animal slaughter, the welfare of the subjects in both worlds has been accomplished, calamities have been brought to an end, and the sufferings of poverty have been allayed for those established in virtuous conduct. What more need be said? Those subjects are indeed fortunate.

children.text: lakṣmeva kṣaṇadākarasya vitataṃ gātre na kṛṣṇājinaṃ
children.translated_text: Like the splendor of the moon — no black antelope skin spread upon your body,

children.text: dīkṣāyantraṇayā nisargalalitā ceṣṭā na mandodyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: no sluggish effort restraining your naturally graceful movements through the constraint of consecration,

children.text: mūrdhnaśchatranibhasya keśaracanā śobhā tathaivātha ca
children.translated_text: the beauty of the hair-arrangement upon your head, which resembles a parasol, remains just as it is — and yet

children.text: tyāgaiste śatayajvano 'pyapahṛtaḥ kīrtyāśrayo vismayaḥ // Jm_10.32 //
children.translated_text: your liberality has surpassed even those who have performed a hundred sacrifices; wonder indeed takes refuge in your fame! || Jm 10.32 ||

children.text: hiṃsāviṣaktaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ phalepsoḥ prāyeṇa lokasya nayajña yajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sacrifice of ordinary folk, O knower of policy, is generally attached to violence, pitiable in its desire for reward;

children.text: yajñastu kīrtyābharaṇaḥ samaste śīlasya nirdoṣamanoharasya // Jm_10.33 //
children.translated_text: but your sacrifice is an ornament of fame to all — the sacrifice of faultless and captivating virtue. || Jm 10.33 ||

children.text: aho prajānāṃ bhāgyāni yāsāṃ gopāyitā bhavān /
children.translated_text: "Ah, the fortunes of those subjects whose protector you are!

children.text: prajānāmapi hi vyaktaṃ naivaṃ syād gopitā pitā // Jm_10.34 //
children.translated_text: For clearly, not even a father would protect his subjects in this manner." || Jm 10.34 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another [minister] said:

children.text: dānaṃ nāma dhanodaye sati jano datte tadāśāvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: "Giving, it is true, people practice when wealth arises — impelled by the hope it brings;

children.text: syācchīle 'pi ca lokapaṃktyabhimukhaḥ svarge ca jātaspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: and one might observe good conduct too, conforming to the ways of the world, with desire for heaven aroused;

children.text: yā tveṣā parakāryadakṣiṇatayā tadvatpravṛttistayor
children.translated_text: but this activity of yours, characterized by such skillfulness in attending to the welfare of others, proceeding in both [giving and conduct] —

children.text: nāvidvatsu na sattvayogavidhureṣveṣā samālakṣyate // Jm_10.35 //
children.translated_text: this is not observed among the unlearned, nor among those devoid of the strength of true character." || Jm 10.35 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ kalyāṇāśayā na pāpapratāraṇāmanuvidhīyanta ityāśayaśuddhau prayatitavyam /
body.translated_text: "Therefore, those of virtuous disposition do not follow the deceptions of the wicked — thus one should strive for purity of intention."

children.text: iti prajāhitodyogaḥ śreyaḥkīrtisukhāvahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the exertion for the welfare of subjects, which brings glory, fame, and happiness,

children.text: yannṛpāṇāmato nālaṃ tamanādṛtya vartitum // Jm_10.36 //
children.translated_text: is such that kings cannot afford to disregard it and carry on otherwise. || Jm 10.36 ||

body.text: evaṃ rājāpavāde 'pi vācyam / dharmābhyāsaḥ prajānāṃ bhūtimāvahatīti bhūtikāmena dharmānuvartinā bhavitavyamityevamapyunneyam / na paśuhiṃsā kadācidabhyudayāya dānadamasaṃyamādayastvabhyudayāyeti tadarthinā dānādipareṇa bhavitavyamityevamapi vācyam / lokārthacaryāpravaṇamatirevaṃ pūrvajanmasvapi bhagavāniti tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, even when disparaging a king, this [story] should be told. That the practice of <s>Dharma</s> brings prosperity to the people — therefore one who desires prosperity should be a follower of <s>Dharma</s>: this too should be inferred. That animal slaughter never leads to prosperity, while generosity, self-control, and restraint do lead to prosperity — therefore one who seeks that end should be devoted to giving and the rest: this too should be stated. That the Blessed One's disposition was inclined toward conduct for the welfare of the world even in former births — this should also be stated when extolling the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: iti yajñajātakaṃ daśamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth [story], the <s>Yajña Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Sacrifice).

body.text: 11. Śakrajātakam
body.translated_text: 11. The <s>Śakra Jātaka</s> (The Story of <s>Śakra</s>)

body.text: āpadapi mahātmanāmaiśvaryasampadvā sattveṣvanukampāṃ na śithilīkaroti / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even adversity, or the attainment of sovereign power, does not weaken the compassion of great souls toward living beings. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānalpakālasvabhyastapuṇyakarmā sātmībhūtapradānadamasaṃyamakaruṇaḥ parahitaniyatakriyātiśayaḥ kadācicchakro devānāmindro babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having long practiced meritorious deeds, with generosity, self-control, restraint, and compassion having become second nature to him, surpassing all in his deeds devoted to the welfare of others, once became <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>Devas</s>.

children.text: surendralakṣmīradhikaṃ rarāja tatsaṃśrayātsphītataraprabhāvā /
children.translated_text: The splendor of the lord of the <s>Devas</s> shone all the more, its power magnified through association with him,

children.text: harmye sudhāsekanavāṅgarāge niṣaktarūpā śaśinaḥ prabheva // Jm_11.1 //
children.translated_text: like the radiance of the moon clinging to a palace wall freshly coated with white plaster. || Jm 11.1 ||

children.text: yasyāḥ kṛte ditisutā rabhasāgatāni diṅnāgadantamusalānyurasābhijagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: That sovereign glory, for whose sake the sons of <s>Diti</s> impetuously charged, striking their chests against the tusk-pestles of the elephants of the quarters —

children.text: saubhāgyavistarasukhopanatāpi tasya lakṣmīrna darpamalinaṃ hṛdayaṃ cakāra // Jm_11.2 //
children.translated_text: even that <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), offered up by the abundance of good fortune, did not make his heart sullied with pride. || Jm 11.2 ||

body.text: tasya divaspṛthivyoḥ samyakparipālanopārjitāṃ sarvalokānuvyāpinīṃ kīrtisampadaṃ tāṃ ca lakṣmīmatyadbhutāmamṛṣyamāṇā daityagaṇāḥ kalpanāṭopabhīṣaṇataradviradarathaturagapadātinā kṣubhitasāgaraghoranirghoṣeṇa jājvalyamānavividhapraharaṇāvaraṇadurnirīkṣyeṇa mahatā balakāyena yuddhāyainamabhijagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Unable to endure his fame and prosperity, which pervaded all the worlds, earned through the just governance of heaven and earth, and that most wondrous sovereign splendor — the hosts of <s>Daityas</s> marched against him for battle with a vast army, made terrifying by elephants, chariots, horses, and foot-soldiers arrayed in fearsome battle-formation, whose tumult was dreadful as the churning of the ocean, and which was difficult to behold because of the blazing array of various weapons and armor.

children.text: dharmātmano 'pi tu sa tasya parābalepaḥ krīḍāvighātavirasaṃ ca bhayaṃ janasya /
children.translated_text: Yet the insolence of the enemy forces, and the fear of the people — distasteful as an interruption of play —

children.text: tejasvitā nayapathopanataḥ kramaśca yuddhodbhavābhimukhatāṃ hṛdayasya cakruḥ // Jm_11.3 //
children.translated_text: together with his innate valor and the course presented by the path of statecraft, turned his heart toward readiness for the onset of battle. || Jm 11.3 ||

body.text: atha sa mahāsattvasturagavarasahasrayuktamabhyucchritārhadvasanacihnaruciradhvajaṃ vividhamaṇiratnadīptivyavabhāsitamatijvaladvapuṣaṃ kalpanāvibhāgopaniyataniśitajvalitavividhāyudhavirājitobhayapārśvaṃ pāṇḍukambalinaṃ haimaṃ rathavaramabhiruhya mahatā hastyaśvarathapadātivicitreṇa devānīkena parivṛtastadasurasainyaṃ samudratīrānta eva pratyujjagāma /
body.translated_text: Then that great being, mounting a supreme golden chariot yoked to a thousand excellent horses, beautiful with its lofty banner bearing worthy emblems and banners, blazing with the radiance of various gems and jewels, its body exceedingly resplendent, both its flanks adorned with various sharp and gleaming weapons fitted in battle-formation compartments, covered with white woolen blankets — surrounded by a great and varied army of <s>Devas</s> consisting of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry — went forth to meet that <s>Asura</s> army right at the shore of the ocean.

children.text: atha pravavṛte tatra bhīrūṇāṃ dhṛtidāraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then there commenced a battle that shattered the courage of the timid,

children.text: anyonyāyudhaniṣpeṣajarjarāvaraṇo raṇaḥ // Jm_11.4 //
children.translated_text: with armor battered by the mutual clash of weapons. || Jm 11.4 ||

children.text: tiṣṭha naivamitaḥ paśya kvedānīṃ manna mokṣyase /
children.translated_text: "Stand! Not that way! Look here! Where will you escape me now?

children.text: praharāyaṃ na bhavasītyevaṃ te 'nyonyamārdayan // Jm_11.5 //
children.translated_text: Strike! You are no match for this one!" — thus they assailed one another. || Jm 11.5 ||

children.text: tataḥ pravṛtte tumule sphūrjatpraharaṇe raṇe /
children.translated_text: Then, when the tumultuous battle raged with weapons flashing,

children.text: paṭahadhvaninotkruṣṭaiḥ sphuṭatīva nabhastalam // Jm_11.6 //
children.translated_text: the firmament seemed to burst apart from the war-cries and the thunder of drums. || Jm 11.6 ||

children.text: dānagandhoddhatāmarṣeṣvāpatatsu parasparam /
children.translated_text: As elephants, maddened with fury aroused by the scent of rut, rushed at one another,

children.text: yugāntavātākalitaśailabhīmeṣu dantiṣu // Jm_11.7 //
children.translated_text: terrible as mountains tossed by the winds at the end of an age, || Jm 11.7 ||

children.text: vidyullolapatākeṣu prasṛteṣu samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: as chariots, their banners fluttering like lightning, advanced in all directions,

children.text: ratheṣu paṭunirghoṣeṣūtpātāmbudhareṣviva // Jm_11.8 //
children.translated_text: thundering loudly like portentous storm-clouds, || Jm 11.8 ||

children.text: pātyamānadhvajacchatraśastrāvaraṇamauliṣu /
children.translated_text: as sharp arrows of one another struck down the banners, parasols, weapons, armor, and crowns

children.text: devadānavavīreṣu śitairanyonyasāyakaiḥ // Jm_11.9 //
children.translated_text: of the heroes of the <s>Devas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>, || Jm 11.9 ||

children.text: atha prataptāsuraśastrasāyakairbhayātpradudrāva surendravāhinī /
children.translated_text: then the army of the lord of the <s>Devas</s>, scorched by the <s>Asura</s> weapons and arrows, fled in fear;

children.text: rathena viṣṭabhya balaṃ tu vidviṣāṃ surendra ekaḥ samare vyatiṣṭhata // Jm_11.10 //
children.translated_text: but the lord of the <s>Devas</s> alone, holding firm against the enemy forces with his chariot, stood his ground in battle. || Jm 11.10 ||

body.text: abhyudīrṇaṃ tvāsuraṃ balamatiharṣātpaṭutarotkruṣṭakṣveḍitasiṃhanādamabhipatitamabhisamīkṣya mātalirdevendrasārathiḥ svaṃ ca balaṃ palāyanaparamavetyāpayānamatra prāptakālamiti matvā devādhipateḥ syandanamāvartayāmāsa / atha śakro devendraḥ samutpatato ratheṣāgrābhimukhānyabhighātapathāgatāni śālmalīvṛkṣe garuḍanīḍānyapaśyat / dṛṣṭvaiva ca karuṇayā samālambyamānahṛdayo mātaliṃ saṃgrāhakamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mātali</s>, the charioteer of the lord of the gods, seeing the <s>Asura</s> army surging forward, charging with sharpened war-cries, roars, and lion-roars due to their excessive delight, and perceiving that his own forces were intent on fleeing, thinking 'The time for retreat has come,' turned around the chariot of the lord of the gods. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, saw <s>Garuḍa</s>-nests upon a <s>Śālmalī</s> tree directly in the path of the chariot-pole, having come into the line of impact. And upon seeing them, his heart gripped by compassion, he said to <s>Mātali</s> the charioteer:

children.text: ajātapakṣadvijapotasaṅkulā dvijālayāḥ śālmalipādapāśrayāḥ /
children.translated_text: "These bird-dwellings, sheltered in the <s>Śālmalī</s> tree, are teeming with fledglings whose wings have not yet grown;

children.text: amī pateyurna yathā ratheṣayā vicūrṇitā vāhaya me rathaṃ tathā // Jm_11.11 //
children.translated_text: drive my chariot so that they may not fall, crushed by the chariot-pole!" || Jm 11.11 ||

body.text: mātaliruvāca - amī tāvanmārṣa samabhiyānti no daityasaṃghā iti / śakra uvāca - tataḥ kim? pariharaitāni samyaggaruḍanīḍānīti / athainaṃ mātaliḥ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Mātali</s> said: "But noble sir, those hosts of <s>Daityas</s> are bearing down upon us!" <s>Śakra</s> said: "What of it? Avoid these <s>Garuḍa</s>-nests properly!" Then <s>Mātali</s> spoke to him again:

children.text: nivartanādasya rathasya kevalaṃ śivaṃ bhavedamburuhākṣa pakṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: "By merely turning this chariot around, there would be safety for the birds, O lotus-eyed one;

children.text: cirasya labdhaprasarā sureṣvasāvabhidravatyeva tu no dviṣaccamūḥ // Jm_11.12 //
children.translated_text: but the enemy army, having long gained its advance against the gods, is charging upon us all the more!" || Jm 11.12 ||

body.text: atha śakro devendraḥ svamadhyāśayātiśayaṃ sattvaviśeṣaṃ ca kāruṇyaviśeṣāt prakāśayannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, displaying the extraordinary depth of his inner nature and his special compassion, out of exceptional compassion, said:

children.text: tasmānnivartaya rathaṃ varameva mṛtyurdaityādhipaprahitabhīmagadābhighātaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore turn the chariot! Better indeed is death by the blows of terrible maces hurled by the lord of <s>Daityas</s>;

children.text: dhigvādadagdhayaśaso na tu jīvitaṃ me sattvānyamūni bhayadīnamukhāni hatvā // Jm_11.13 //
children.translated_text: but not for me a life whose glory has been burned by the fire of censure — not by killing these beings whose faces are wretched with fear!" || Jm 11.13 ||

body.text: atha mātalistatheti pratiśrutya turagasahasrayuktaṃ syandanamasya nivartayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mātali</s>, having assented with 'So be it,' turned around his chariot yoked with a thousand horses.

children.text: dṛṣṭāvadānā ripavastu tasya yuddhe samālokya rathaṃ nivṛttam /
children.translated_text: But the enemies, who had witnessed his [past] exploits, seeing his chariot turn back in battle,

children.text: bhayadrutāḥ praskhalitāḥ praṇemurvātābhinunnā iva kālameghāḥ // Jm_11.14 //
children.translated_text: fled in terror, stumbling, and bowed down — like storm-clouds driven by the wind. || Jm 11.14 ||

children.text: bhagne svasainye vinivartamānaḥ panthānamāvṛtya ripudhvajinyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Though his own army was broken, he, turning back alone, blocking the path of the enemy forces,

children.text: saṅkocayatyeva madāvalepameko 'pyasambhāvyaparākramatvāt // Jm_11.15 //
children.translated_text: contracted their swollen pride — even single-handedly, because of his inconceivable valor. || Jm 11.15 ||

children.text: nirīkṣya bhagnaṃ tu tadāsuraṃ balaṃ surendrasenāpyatha sā nyavartata /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the <s>Asura</s> army broken, that army of the gods also turned back;

children.text: babhūva naiva praṇayaḥ suradviṣāṃ bhayadrutānāṃ vinivartituṃ yataḥ // Jm_11.16 //
