children.translated_text: for indeed the enemies of the gods, fleeing in terror, had no inclination to turn and fight. || Jm 11.16 ||

children.text: saharṣalajjaistridaśaiḥ surādhipaḥ sabhājyamāno 'tha raṇājirācchanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the lord of the gods, being honored by the <s>Tridaśas</s> (the thirty gods) with joy and bashfulness, slowly [returning] from the battlefield,

children.text: abhijvalaccāruvapurjayaśriyā samutsukāntaḥpuramāgamat puram // Jm_11.17 //
children.translated_text: his beautiful form blazing with the glory of victory, entered his city, whose inner court was filled with eagerness. || Jm 11.17 ||

body.text: evaṃ sa eva tasya saṃgrāmasya vijayo babhūva / tasmāducyate -
body.translated_text: Thus that very [act] became the victory of that battle. Therefore it is said:

children.text: pāpaṃ samācarati vītaghṛṇo jaghanyaḥ prāpyāpadaṃ saghṛṇa eva tu madhyabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "The wretched person, devoid of compassion, commits evil; the one of middling mind does so even when stricken by misfortune, from fellow-feeling;

children.text: prāṇātyaye 'pi tu na sādhujanaḥ svavṛttiṃ velāṃ samudra iva laṅghayituṃ samarthaḥ // Jm_11.18 //
children.translated_text: but the virtuous person, even in mortal danger, is unable to transgress his own conduct — just as the ocean [cannot transgress] its shore." || Jm 11.18 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ devarājyaṃ prāṇānapi parityajya dīrgharātraṃ paripālitāni bhagavatā sattvāni / teṣviha prājñasyāghāto na yuktarūpaḥ prāgeva vipratipattiriti prāṇiṣu dayāyattenāryeṇa bhavitavyam / tathā hi dharmo ha vai rakṣati dharmacāriṇamityatrāpyunneyam / tathāgatavarṇe satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus the Blessed One, even abandoning his own life, protected beings for a long time during his reign over the gods. Against such beings, aggression by a wise person is not fitting, let alone open hostility — therefore the noble person should be devoted to compassion toward living beings. For this too is to be inferred: 'Dharma indeed protects one who practices Dharma.' This [story is to be cited] in the description of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s [virtues] and in hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence.

body.text: iti śakrajātakamekādaśam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh [story], the <s>Śakra Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 12. Brāhmaṇajātakam
body.translated_text: 12. The <s>Brāhmaṇa Jātaka</s>

body.text: ātmalajjayaiva satpuruṣā nācāravelāṃ laṅghayanti / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Virtuous persons do not transgress the bounds of right conduct, precisely because of their own sense of shame. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃścidanupakruṣṭagotracāritre svadharmānuvṛttiprakāśayaśasi vinayācāraślāghini mahati brāhmaṇakule janmaparigrahaṃ cakāra / sa yathākramaṃ garbhādhānapuṃsavanasīmantonnayanajātakarmādibhiḥ kṛtasaṃskārakramo vedādhyayananimittaṃ śrutābhijanācārasampanne gurau prativasati sma /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took birth in a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family — one whose lineage and conduct were unblemished, whose fame was made manifest by adherence to its own duties, and which was distinguished for the propriety of its deportment. He, having undergone the sequence of sacraments in due order — <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite), <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for a male child), <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair), <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite), and the rest — dwelt with a teacher who was endowed with learning, noble birth, and good conduct, for the purpose of Vedic study.

children.text: tasya śrutagrahaṇadhāraṇapāṭavaṃ ca bhaktyanvayaśca satataṃ svakulaprasiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: His skill in grasping, retaining, and reciting what he had learned, his devotion well known in his own family,

children.text: pūrve vayasyapi śamābharaṇā sthitiśca premaprasādasumukhaṃ gurumasya cakruḥ // Jm_12.1 //
children.translated_text: and even in his early youth, his steadfastness adorned by tranquility — these made his teacher favorably disposed toward him with affection and grace. || Jm 12.1 ||

children.text: vaśīkaraṇamantrā hi nityamavyāhatā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: For virtues are unfailing spells of enchantment,

children.text: api dveṣāgnitaptānāṃ kiṃ punaḥ svasthacetasām // Jm_12.2 //
children.translated_text: [winning over] even those burned by the fire of hatred — how much more those whose minds are at ease! || Jm 12.2 ||

body.text: atha tasyādhyāpakaḥ sarveṣāmeva śiṣyāṇāṃ śīlaparīkṣānimittaṃ svādhyāyaviśrāmakāleṣvātmano dāridryaduḥkhānyabhīkṣṇamupavarṇayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then his teacher, in order to test the character of all his pupils, during the intervals of study, repeatedly described his own miseries of poverty.

children.text: svajane 'pi nirākrandamutsave 'pi hatānandam /
children.translated_text: "Even among one's own people, without a cry [of sympathy]; even at a festival, robbed of joy;

children.text: dhikpradānakathāmandaṃ dāridryamaphalacchandam // Jm_12.3 //
children.translated_text: shame on poverty — slow to utter the word 'giving,' rendering desire fruitless!" || Jm 12.3 ||

children.text: paribhavabhavanaṃ śramāspadaṃ sukhaparivarjitamatyanūrjitam /
children.translated_text: "An abode of humiliation, a seat of toil, devoid of happiness, utterly powerless,

children.text: vyasanamiva sadaiva śocanaṃ dhanavikalatvamatīva dāruṇam // Jm_12.4 //
children.translated_text: always a cause for lamentation like a calamity — the state of being destitute of wealth is exceedingly cruel!" || Jm 12.4 ||

body.text: atha te tasya śiṣyāḥ pratodasaṃcoditā iva sadaśvā gurusnehātsamupajātasaṃvegāḥ sampannataraṃ prabhūtataraṃ ca bhaikṣamupasaṃharanti sma / sa tānuvāca - alamanenātrabhavatāṃ pariśrameṇa / na bhaikṣopahārāḥ kasyaciddāridryakṣāmatāṃ kṣapayanti / asmatparikleśāmarṣibhistu bhavadbhirayameva yatno dhanāharaṇaṃ prati yuktaḥ karttuṃ syāt / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: Then those students of his, urged as if by a goad like good horses, moved by affection for their teacher, began to bring in alms that were more ample and more abundant. He said to them: "Enough of this exertion on your part. Alms-offerings do not extinguish anyone's emaciation from poverty. Rather, if you who cannot bear our hardship wish to make an effort, it should be directed toward acquiring wealth. Why?

children.text: kṣudhamannaṃ jalaṃ tarṣaṃ mantravāksāgadā gadān /
children.translated_text: "Food destroys hunger, water [destroys] thirst, incantations and medicinal words [destroy] diseases;

children.text: hanti dāridryaduḥkhaṃ tu santatyārādhanaṃ dhanam // Jm_12.5 //
children.translated_text: but it is wealth, continuously cultivated, that destroys the suffering of poverty." || Jm 12.5 ||

body.text: śiṣyā ūcuḥ - kiṃ kariṣyāmo mandabhāgyā vayaṃ yadetāvānnaḥ śaktiprayāmaḥ / api ca
body.translated_text: The students said: "What can we do, ill-fated as we are, when our effort extends only this far? Moreover —

children.text: bhaikṣavadyadi labhyerarannupādhyāya dhanānyapi /
children.translated_text: "If, teacher, wealth could be obtained as easily as alms,

children.text: nedaṃ dāridryaduḥkhaṃ te vayamevaṃ sahemahi // Jm_12.6 //
children.translated_text: we would not have you endure this suffering of poverty!" || Jm 12.6 ||

children.text: pratigrahakṛśopāyaṃ viprāṇāṃ hi dhanārjanam /
children.translated_text: "For the means of acquiring wealth for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is slender, limited to accepting gifts;

children.text: apradātā janaścāyamityagatyā hatā vayam // Jm_12.7 //
children.translated_text: and the people are unwilling to give — so we are defeated, helpless." || Jm 12.7 ||

body.text: adhyāpaka uvāca - santyanye 'pi śāsraparidṛṣṭā dhanārjanopāyāḥ / jarāniṣpītasāmarthyāstu vayamayogyarūpāstatpratipattau / śiṣyā ūcuḥ - vayamupādhyāya jarayānupahataparākramāḥ / tadyadi nasteṣāṃ śāstravihitānāmupāyānāṃ pratipattisahatāṃ manyase, taducyatām / yāvadadhyāpanapariśramasyānṛṇyaṃ te gacchāma iti / adhyāpaka uvāca - taruṇairapi vyavasāyaśithilahṛdayairdurabhisambhavāḥ khalvevaṃvidhā dhanārjanopāyāḥ / yadi tvayamatra bhavatāṃ nirbandhaḥ / tacchruyatāṃ sādhuḥ katama eko dhanopārjanakramaḥ /
body.translated_text: The teacher said: "There are other means of acquiring wealth prescribed by the treatises. But we, whose strength has been drained by old age, are unfit for undertaking them." The students said: "We, teacher, have our vigor unimpaired by old age. If you consider us capable of undertaking those means prescribed by the treatises, then let them be stated. Let us discharge our debt of gratitude for the toil of your teaching." The teacher said: "Even for the young, such means of acquiring wealth are hard to accomplish if their hearts are slack in resolve. But if this is your firm determination, then listen well. There is one particular method of wealth-acquisition:

children.text: āpaddharmaḥ steyamiṣṭaṃ dvijānāmāpaccāntyā niḥsvatā nāma loke /
children.translated_text: "Theft is the sanctioned emergency-<s>dharma</s> (duty in extremity) for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; and the ultimate extremity in the world is destitution itself;

children.text: tasmād bhojyaṃ svaṃ pareṣāmaduṣṭaiḥ sarvaṃ caitad brāhmaṇānāṃ svameva // Jm_12.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore the property of others may be enjoyed by the blameless; indeed, everything is the property of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>." || Jm 12.8 ||

children.text: kāmaṃ prasahyāpi dhanāni hartuṃ śaktirbhavedeva bhavadvidhānām /
children.translated_text: "Such people as yourselves would certainly have the power to take wealth even by force;

children.text: na tveṣa yogaḥ svayaśo hi rakṣyaṃ śūnyeṣu tasmādvyavaseyameva // Jm_12.9 //
children.translated_text: but this method [should not be used openly], for one's reputation must be protected — therefore one should operate [only] in empty [houses]." || Jm 12.9 ||

body.text: iti muktapragrahāstena te chātrāḥ paramamiti tattasya vacanamayuktamapi yuktamiva pratyaśrauṣuranyatra bodhisattvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus given free rein by him, those students accepted his words — however improper, as though proper — saying 'Excellent!' — all except the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: sa hi prakṛtibhadratvāttannotsehe 'numoditum /
children.translated_text: For he, being noble by nature, could not bring himself to approve,

children.text: kṛtyavatpratipannaṃ tairvyāhantuṃ sahasaiva tu // Jm_12.10 //
children.translated_text: but neither [did he dare] to abruptly oppose what they had accepted as if it were their duty. || Jm 12.10 ||

body.text: vrīḍāvanatavadanastu bodhisattvo mṛdu viniśvasya tūṣṇīmabhūt /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his face bowed with shame, sighing softly, remained silent.

body.text: atha sa teṣāmadhyāpako bodhisattvamavekṣya taṃ vidhimanabhinandantamapratikrośantaṃ niviṣṭaguṇasambhāvanastasminmahāsattve kiṃ nu khalvayamavyavasitatvānniḥsnehatayā vā mayi steyaṃ na pratipadyate, utādharmasaṃjñayeti samutpannavimarśastatsvabhāvavyaktīkaraṇārthaṃ bodhisattvamuvāca - bho mahābrāhmaṇa
body.translated_text: Then that teacher of theirs, observing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who neither approved of that injunction nor protested against it, with his esteem for that great being's virtues firmly established, wondering, 'Why indeed does he not undertake theft — is it from irresolution, or from lack of affection for me, or from the recognition that it is unrighteous?' — and having developed an inquiry [into his nature], in order to make his true character manifest, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: amī dvijā madvyasanāsahiṣṇavaḥ samāśritā vīramanuṣyapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: "These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, unable to endure my misfortune, have taken up the path of heroic men;

children.text: bhavānanutsāhajaḍastu labhyate na nūnamasmadvyasanena tapyate // Jm_12.11 //
children.translated_text: but you are found to be sluggish through lack of enterprise — surely you are not afflicted by our misfortune!" || Jm 12.11 ||

children.text: pariprakāśe 'pyanigūḍhavistare mayātmaduḥkhe vacasā vidarśite /
children.translated_text: "When my personal suffering, quite manifest and not at all concealed, has been displayed in words,

children.text: kathaṃ nu niḥsambhramadīnamānaso bhavāniti svasthavadeva tiṣṭhati // Jm_12.12 //
children.translated_text: how then do you stand as if at ease, with a mind devoid of agitation and distress?" || Jm 12.12 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sasambhramo 'bhivādyopādhyāyamuvāca - śāntaṃ pāpam / na khalvahaṃ niḥsnehakaṭhinahṛdayatvādaparitapyamāno guruduḥkhairevamavasthitaḥ, kintvasambhavādupādhyāyapradarśitasya kramasya / na hi śakyamadṛśyamānena kvacitpāpamācaritum / kutaḥ? raho 'nupapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, flustered, bowing to his teacher, said: "Heaven forfend! It is not out of heartless insensitivity that I remain unmoved by my teacher's sufferings; rather, it is because the method proposed by the teacher is impossible [for me]. For one cannot commit a sin unseen anywhere. Why? Because there is no such thing as true secrecy:

children.text: nāsti loke raho nāma pāpaṃ karma prakurvataḥ /
children.translated_text: "There is no such thing as secrecy in the world for one who does an evil deed;

children.text: adṛśyāni hi paśyanti nanu bhūtāni mānuṣān // Jm_12.13 //
children.translated_text: for do not unseen beings see human beings?" || Jm 12.13 ||

children.text: kṛtātmānaśca munayo divyonmiṣitacakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And sages who have mastered themselves, whose eyes are opened with divine vision —

children.text: tānapaśyanrahomānī bālaḥ pāpe pravartate // Jm_12.14 //
children.translated_text: the fool, imagining himself in secrecy, not seeing them, engages in sin." || Jm 12.14 ||

children.text: ahaṃ punarna paśyāmi śūnyaṃ kvacana kiñcana /
children.translated_text: "But I do not see any place anywhere that is empty;

children.text: yatrāpyanyaṃ na paśyāmi nanvaśūnyaṃ mayaiva tat // Jm_12.15 //
children.translated_text: where I do not see another, is not that place un-empty by virtue of myself?" || Jm 12.15 ||

children.text: pareṇa yacca dṛśyeta duṣkṛtaṃ svayameva vā /
children.translated_text: "Whether a misdeed be seen by another or by oneself,

children.text: sudṛṣṭatarametatsyād dṛśyate svayameva yat // Jm_12.16 //
children.translated_text: more clearly seen would be that which is seen by oneself." || Jm 12.16 ||

children.text: svakāryaparyākulamānasatvātpaśyenna vānyaścaritaṃ parasya /
children.translated_text: "Another, his mind preoccupied with his own affairs, may or may not see one's conduct;

children.text: rāgārpitaikāgramatiḥ svayaṃ tu pāpaṃ prakurvanniyamena vetti // Jm_12.17 //
children.translated_text: but one who commits sin oneself, with mind single-pointedly fixed [on the act], inevitably knows it." || Jm 12.17 ||

body.text: tadanena kāraṇenāhamevaṃ vyavasthita iti / atha bodhisattvaḥ samabhiprasāditamanasamupādhyāyamavetya punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: "For this reason I have taken this position." Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that his teacher's mind had become well-pleased, spoke again:

children.text: na cātra me niścayameti mānasaṃ dhanārthamevaṃ prataredbhavānapi /
children.translated_text: "Moreover, my mind cannot reach the conclusion that you too would deceive for the sake of wealth;

children.text: avetya ko nāma guṇāguṇāntaraṃ guṇopamardaṃ dhanamūlyatāṃ nayet // Jm_12.18 //
children.translated_text: for who, having understood the difference between virtue and vice, would lead [others] to the destruction of virtue at the cost of wealth?" || Jm 12.18 ||

body.text: svābhiprāyaṃ khalu nivedayāmi -
body.translated_text: "Let me indeed declare my own view:

body.text: kapālamādāya vivarṇavāsasā varaṃ dviṣadveśmasamṛddhirīkṣitā /
body.translated_text: "Better to take up a begging-bowl, clad in faded garments, beholding the prosperity of an enemy's house,

body.text: vyatītya lajjāṃ na tu dharmavaiśase surendratārthe 'pyupasaṃhṛtaṃ manaḥ // Jm_12.19 //
body.translated_text: than to set one's mind, even for the throne of <s>Surendra</s> (Indra), upon the slaughter of <s>Dharma</s>, transgressing the bounds of shame." || Jm 12.19 ||

body.text: atha tasyopādhyāyaḥ praharṣavismayākṣiptahṛdaya utthāyāsanātsampariṣvajyainamuvāca - sādhu sādhu putraka sādhu sādhu mahābrāhmaṇa pratirūpametatte praśamālaṅkṛtasyāsya medhāvikasya /
body.translated_text: Then his teacher, his heart seized with delight and wonder, rising from his seat and embracing him, said: "Well done, well done, my child! Well done, well done, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! This is fitting for one such as you, adorned with tranquility and endowed with intelligence.

children.text: nimittamāsādya yadeva kiñcana svadharmamārgaṃ visṛjanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Fools, seizing upon whatever pretext, abandon the path of their own duty;

children.text: tapaḥśrutajñānadhanāstu sādhavo na yānti kṛcchre parame 'pi vikriyām // Jm_12.20 //
children.translated_text: but the virtuous, whose wealth is austerity, learning, and wisdom, do not undergo transformation even in the most extreme adversity." || Jm 12.20 ||

children.text: tvayā kulaṃ samamalamabhyalaṅkṛtaṃ samudyatā nabha iva śāradendunā /
children.translated_text: "You have adorned your family perfectly,

children.text: tavārthavatsucaritaviśrutaṃ śrutaṃ sukhodayaḥ saphalatayā śramaśca me // Jm_12.21 //
children.translated_text: as the autumn moon [adorns] the risen sky; your learning, made famous through good conduct, is fruitful; and my toil bears fruit in its success." || Jm 12.21 ||

body.text: tadevamātmalajjayaiva satpuruṣā nācāravelāṃ laṅghayantīti hrībalenāryeṇa bhavitavyam / evaṃ hrīparikhāsampanna āryaśrāvako 'kuśalaṃ prajahāti kuśalaṃ ca bhāvayatītyevamādiṣu sūtreṣūpaneyam / hrīvarṇapratisaṃyukteṣu lokādhipateyeṣu ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus, virtuous persons do not transgress the bounds of right conduct precisely because of their own sense of shame — therefore the noble person should possess the strength of modesty (<s>hrī</s>). [This story is] to be cited thus: 'A noble disciple endowed with the moat of modesty abandons the unwholesome and cultivates the wholesome,' and in <s>Sūtras</s> of this kind, and in those connected with the description of modesty (<s>hrī</s>) and the qualities of world-sovereignty (<s>lokādhipateya</s>).

body.text: iti brāhmaṇajātakaṃ dvādaśam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth [story], the <s>Brāhmaṇa Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 13. Unmādayantījātakam
body.translated_text: 13. The <s>Unmādayantī Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Maddening One)

body.text: tīvraduḥkhāturāṇāmapi satāṃ nīcamārganiṣpraṇayatā bhavati svadhairyāvaṣṭambhāt / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even when afflicted by intense suffering, the virtuous have no inclination toward base paths, because of the support of their own fortitude. As tradition relates —

body.text: satyatyāgopaśamaprajñādibhirguṃṇātiśayairlokahitārthamudyacchamānaḥ kila bodhisattvaḥ kadācicchibīnāṃ rājā babhūva sākṣāddharma iva vinaya iva piteva prajānāmupakārapravṛttaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, striving for the welfare of the world through surpassing virtues such as truth, renunciation, tranquility, and wisdom, once became the king of the <s>Śibis</s> — devoted to the benefit of his subjects like <s>Dharma</s> incarnate, like Discipline personified, like a father.

children.text: doṣapravṛtterviniyamyamāno niveśyamānaśca guṇābhijātye /
children.translated_text: Restrained from the course of vice and established in the nobility of virtues,

children.text: pitreva putraḥ kṣitipena tena nananda lokadvitaye 'pi lokaḥ // Jm_13.1 //
children.translated_text: the people rejoiced under that king as a son does under a father, in both this world and the next. // Jm_13.1 //

children.text: samaprabhāvā svajane jane ca dharmānugā tasya hi daṇḍanītiḥ /
children.translated_text: For his administration of justice was impartial toward his own people and others alike, and followed <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: adharmyamāvṛtya janasya mārgaṃ sopānamāleva divo babhūva // Jm_13.2 //
children.translated_text: blocking the path of unrighteousness for the people, it became as it were a stairway to heaven. // Jm_13.2 //

children.text: dharmānvayaṃ lokahitaṃ sa paśyaṃstadekakāryoṃ naralokapālaḥ /
children.translated_text: That protector of the world of men, seeing the welfare of the world as flowing from <s>Dharma</s>, and making that his sole purpose,

children.text: sarvātmanā dharmapathe 'bhireme tasyopamardaṃ ca parairna sehe // Jm_13.3 //
children.translated_text: delighted with his whole being in the path of <s>Dharma</s>, and could not endure its violation by others. // Jm_13.3 //

body.text: atha tasya rājñaḥ pauramukhyasya duhitā śrīriva vigrahavatī sākṣādratirivāpsarasāmanyatameva parayā rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpadopetā paramadarśanīyā strīratnasaṃmatā babhūva /
body.translated_text: Now there was a daughter of a leading citizen of that king's realm — like <s>Śrī</s> in bodily form, verily like <s>Rati</s> herself, or like any one of the <s>Apsarases</s> — endowed with supreme beauty and loveliness, most fair to behold, regarded as a jewel among women.

children.text: avītarāgasya janasya yāvatsā locanaprāpyavapurbabhūva /
children.translated_text: As long as she, whose beauty was attained only by the eyes, came within the sight of anyone not free from passion,

children.text: tāvatsa tadrūpaguṇāvabaddhāṃ na dṛṣṭimutkampayituṃ śaśāka // Jm_13.4 //
children.translated_text: so long was he unable to tear away his gaze, bound fast by the qualities of her form. // Jm_13.4 //

body.text: ataśca tasyā unmādayantītyeva bāndhavā nāma cakruḥ /
body.translated_text: And for this reason her kinsmen gave her the name <s>Unmādayantī</s> ("She who drives mad").

body.text: atha tasyāḥ pitā rājñaḥ saṃviditaṃ kārayāmāsastrīratnaṃ te deva viṣaye prādurbhūtam / yatastatpratigrahaṃ visarjanaṃ vā prati devaḥ pramāṇamiti / atha sa rājā strīlakṣaṇavido brāhmaṇān samādideśapaśyantvenāṃ tatrabhavantaḥ kimasāvasmadyogyā na veti / atha tasyāḥ pitā tānbrāhmaṇān svabhavanamabhinīyonmādayantīmuvāca - bhadre svayameva brāhmaṇān pariveṣayeti / sā tatheti pratiśrutya yathākramaṃ brāhmaṇān pariveṣayitumupacakrame / atha te brāhmaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Then her father had the king informed: "A jewel among women, O Lord, has appeared in your realm. Therefore the Lord is the authority regarding her acceptance or dismissal." Thereupon the king instructed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> learned in the marks of women: "Let the venerable ones examine her — whether she is suitable for us or not." Then her father, having conducted those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to his own house, said to <s>Unmādayantī</s>: "Good girl, serve the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> yourself in person." She assented with "So be it" and began to serve the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in due order. Then those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> —

children.text: tadānanodvīkṣaṇaniścalākṣā manobhuvā saṃhriyamāṇadhairyāḥ /
children.translated_text: their eyes fixed and motionless from gazing upon her face, their composure being overwhelmed by the god of love,

children.text: anīśvarā locanamānasānāmāsurmadeneva viluptasaṃjñāḥ // Jm_13.5 //
children.translated_text: no longer masters of their eyes or minds, they became as if bereft of consciousness through intoxication. // Jm_13.5 //

body.text: yadā ca naiva śaknuvanti sma pratisaṃkhyānadhīranibhṛtamavasthātuṃ, kuta eva bhoktum / athaiṣāṃ cakṣuṣpathādutsārya svāṃ duhitaraṃ sa gṛhapatiḥ svayameva brāhmaṇān pariveṣya visarjayāmāsa / atha teṣāṃ buddhirabhavat - kṛtyārūpamiva khalvidamatimanoharamasyā dārikāyā rūpacāturyam / yato naināṃ rājā draṣṭumapyarhati kutaḥ punaḥ patnītvaṃ gamayitum / anayā hi rūpaśobhayā niyatamasyonmāditahṛdayasya dharmārthakāryapravṛttervisrasyamānotsāhasya rājakāryakālātikramāḥ prajānāṃ hitasukhodayapathamupapīḍayantaḥ parābhavāya syuḥ /
body.translated_text: And when they were utterly unable to remain steady, composed through self-reflection and self-control — let alone to eat — the householder removed his daughter from their sight and himself served and dismissed the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Then they concluded: "The beauty and charm of this girl is truly something like a supernatural power. Therefore the king should not even look upon her, much less make her his wife. For through this splendor of her form, his heart would surely be maddened, his resolve for the conduct of <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Artha</s> would slacken, and the resulting delays in royal duties, obstructing the path to the welfare and happiness of his subjects, would lead to ruin.

children.text: iyaṃ hi saṃdarśanamātrakeṇa kuryānmunīnāmapi siddhivighnam /
children.translated_text: For she, by mere sight alone, could cause obstruction to the spiritual attainments even of sages,

children.text: prāgeva bhāvārpitadṛṣṭivṛṣṭeryūnaḥ kṣitīśasya sukhe sthitasya // Jm_13.6 //
children.translated_text: how much more so of a young king established in pleasure, upon whom the rain of her glances would fall with desire. // Jm_13.6 //

body.text: tasmādidamatra prāptakālamiti yathāprastāvamupetya rājñe nivedayāmāsuḥ - dṛṣṭāsmābhirmahārāja sā kanyakā / asti tasyā rūpacāturyamātrakamapalakṣaṇopaghātaniḥśrīkaṃ tu / yato naināṃ draṣṭumapyarhati devaḥ, kiṃ punaḥ patnītvaṃ gamayitum /
body.translated_text: Therefore this is the fitting course here." And approaching the king at an opportune moment, they reported: "We have seen the maiden, O great king. She possesses beauty and charm alone, but these are rendered inauspicious by unfavorable marks. Therefore the Lord should not even look upon her, much less make her his wife.

children.text: kuladvayasyāpi hi ninditā strī yaśo vibhūtiṃ ca tiraskaroti /
children.translated_text: For a woman of ill marks brings disgrace upon both families, obscuring their fame and prosperity,

children.text: nimagnacandreva niśā sameghā śobhāṃ vibhāgaṃ ca divaspṛthivyoḥ // Jm_13.7 //
children.translated_text: like a night with clouds and a sunken moon, obscuring the beauty and distinction of heaven and earth. // Jm_13.7 //

body.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sa rājā - apalakṣaṇā kilāsau, na ca me kulānurūpeti tasyāṃ vinivṛttābhilāṣo babhūva / anarthitāṃ tu vijñāya rājñaḥ sa gṛhapatistāṃ dārikāṃ tasyaiva rājño 'mātyāyābhipāragāya prāyacchat /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king thought, "She is of ill marks, it seems, and not suitable for my lineage," and his desire for her ceased. But the householder, learning that the king had no interest, gave that maiden to <s>Abhipāraga</s>, a minister of that very king.

body.text: atha kadācitsa rājā kramāgatāṃ kaumudīṃ svasminpuravare niṣaktaśobhāṃ draṣṭumutsukamanā rathavaragataḥ siktasaṃmṛṣṭarathyāntarāpaṇamucchritavicitradhvajapatākaṃ samantataḥ puṣpopahāraśabalabhūmibhāgadhavalaṃ pravṛttanṛttagītahāsyalāsyavāditraṃ puṣpadhūpacūrṇavāsamālyāsavasnānānulepanāmodaprasṛtasurabhigandhi prasāritavividharucirapaṇyaṃ tuṣṭapuṣṭojjvalataraveṣapaurajānapadasaṃbādharājamārgaṃ puravaramanuvicaraṃstasyāmātyasya bhavanasamīpamupajagāma / athonmādayantyapalakṣaṇā kilāhamityanena rājñāvadhūteti samutpannāmarṣā rājadarśanakutūhalena nāma saṃdṛśyamānarūpaśobhā vidyudiva ghanaśikharaṃ
body.translated_text: Then one day the king, eager to behold the <s>Kaumudī</s> festival whose splendor had settled upon his capital, mounted his finest chariot and traversed the royal city — its streets sprinkled and swept, its shops adorned with raised and variegated banners and pennants, its grounds everywhere dappled white with offerings of flowers, alive with dancing, singing, jesting, graceful movement, and music, fragrant with the sweet scent of flowers, incense, powders, perfumes, garlands, liquors, baths, and unguents wafting forth, displaying various attractive wares, its royal thoroughfare thronging with citizens and country folk in resplendent festive attire — and he drew near the residence of that minister. Then <s>Unmādayantī</s>, indignant that she had been rejected by the king on account of being supposedly ill-marked, curious to see the king, displaying her beauty of form as lightning illumines

body.text: harmyatalamavabhāsayantī vyatiṣṭhata / śaktirasyedānīmastvapalakṣaṇādarśanādavicalitadhṛtismṛtimātmānaṃ dhārayitumiti / atha tasya rājñaḥ puravaravibhūtidarśanakutūhalaprasṛtā dṛṣṭirabhimukhasthitāyāṃ sahasaiva tasyāmapatat / atha sa rājā -
body.translated_text: the summit of a cloud, stood resplendent upon the terrace of her mansion. "Let him now have the power to maintain his composure and presence of mind, unmoved by beholding one of ill marks!" she thought. Then the king's gaze, wandering forth in curiosity to behold the splendor of his capital, suddenly fell upon her as she stood directly before him. Then that king —

children.text: prakāmamantaḥpurasundarīṇāṃ vapurvilāsaiḥ kalitekṣaṇo 'pi /
children.translated_text: though his eye was well-trained by the beauty and grace of the women of his own inner chambers,

children.text: anuddhato dharmapathānurāgādudyogavānindriyanirjaye 'pi // Jm_13.8 //
children.translated_text: though he was not haughty, and through devotion to the path of <s>Dharma</s> was diligent even in the conquest of the senses, // Jm_13.8 //

children.text: vipuladhṛtiguṇo 'pyapatrapiṣṇuḥ parayuvatīkṣaṇaviklavekṣaṇo 'pi /
children.translated_text: though possessed of the virtue of great steadfastness, though modest, though his glance would falter at the sight of another's wife,

children.text: uditamadanavismayaḥ striyaṃ tāṃ ciramanimeṣavilocano dadarśa // Jm_13.9 //
children.translated_text: he gazed upon that woman with unblinking eyes for a long time, wonder and desire arising within him. // Jm_13.9 //

children.text: kaumudī kiṃ nviyaṃ sākṣādbhavanasyāsya devatā /
children.translated_text: "Is this the <s>Kaumudī</s> festival itself in person? Is she the deity of this mansion?

children.text: svargastrī daityayoṣidvā na hyetanmānuṣaṃ vapuḥ // Jm_13.10 //
children.translated_text: A celestial woman? A wife of the <s>Daityas</s>? For this form is surely not human." // Jm_13.10 //

body.text: iti vicārayata eva tasya rājñastaddarśanāvitṛptanayanasya sa rathastaṃ deśamativartamāno na manorathānukūlo babhūva / atha sa rājā śūnyahṛdaya iva tadgataikāgramanāḥ svabhavanamupetya manmathākṣiptadhṛtiḥ sunandaṃ sārathiṃ rahasi paryapṛcchat -
body.translated_text: Even as the king was thus deliberating, his eyes unsated by the sight of her, his chariot passed beyond that place and did not oblige his heart's desire. Then the king, as if his heart had been emptied, his mind single-pointedly fixed upon her, returned to his own palace, and his composure shattered by the god of love, he privately questioned his charioteer <s>Sunanda</s>:

children.text: sitaprākārasaṃvītaṃ vetsi kasya nu tadgṛham /
children.translated_text: "Do you know whose house that is, enclosed by white ramparts?

children.text: kā sā tatra vyarociṣṭa vidyutsita ivāmbude // Jm_13.11 //
children.translated_text: Who was she that shone there, like lightning in a white cloud?" // Jm_13.11 //

body.text: sārathiruvāca - asti devasyābhipārago nāmāmātyamukhyaḥ / tasya tadgṛhaṃ tasyaiva ca sā bhāryā kirīṭavatsasya duhitā unmādayantī nāmeti / tadupaśrutya sa rājā parabhāryeti vitānībhūtahṛdayaścintāstimitanayano dīrghamuṣṇamabhiniśvasya tadarpitamanāḥ śanairātmagatamuvāca -
body.translated_text: The charioteer replied: "Your Majesty has a chief minister named <s>Abhipāraga</s>. That is his house, and she is his wife, the daughter of <s>Kirīṭavatsa</s>, called <s>Unmādayantī</s>." Upon hearing this, the king — his heart stricken by the thought "another man's wife" — his eyes frozen with anxious reflection, having heaved a long, hot sigh, his mind fixed upon her, slowly said to himself:

children.text: anvartharamyākṣarasaukumāryamaho kṛtaṃ nāma yathedamasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ah, how fittingly made is this name of hers, with its syllables lovely and delicate in meaning —

children.text: unmādayantīti śucismitāyāstathā hi sonmādamivākaronmām // Jm_13.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Unmādayantī</s>, 'She who drives mad,' of the radiant smile — for so indeed she has driven me to madness. // Jm_13.12 //

children.text: vismartuṃmenāmicchāmi paśyāmīva ca cetasā /
children.translated_text: I wish to forget her, yet I see her still with my mind's eye;

children.text: sthitaṃ tasyāṃ hi me cetaḥ sā prabhutvena tatra vā // Jm_13.13 //
children.translated_text: for my heart remains fixed upon her — or rather, she holds sovereign power over it. // Jm_13.13 //

children.text: parasya nāma bhāryāyāṃ mamāpyevamadhīratā /
children.translated_text: That even I should feel such loss of composure toward another man's wife —

children.text: tadunmatto 'smi saṃtyakto lajjayevādya nidrayā // Jm_13.14 //
children.translated_text: surely I am maddened, forsaken this day by shame as if by sleep. // Jm_13.14 //

children.text: tasyā vapurvilasitasmitavīkṣiteṣu saṃrāganiścalamateḥ sahasā svanantī /
children.translated_text: As my mind dwells immovably in passionate attachment upon her form, her playful gestures, her smile, and her glances,

children.text: kāryāntarakramanivedanadhṛṣṭaśabdā vidveṣamuttudati cetasi nālikā me // Jm_13.15 //
children.translated_text: the water-clock, its sound intruding boldly to announce the passage of other duties, stirs only resentment in my heart. // Jm_13.15 //

body.text: iti sa rājā madabalavicalitadhṛtirvyavasthāpayannapyātmānamāpāṇḍukṛśatanuḥ pradhyānaviniśvasitavijṛmbhaṇaparaḥ pravyaktamadanākāro babhūva /
body.translated_text: Thus the king, his composure shaken by the force of infatuation, though he tried to steady himself, grew pale and thin of body, given over to brooding, sighing, and yawning, and his condition of lovesickness became plainly manifest.

children.text: dhṛtyā mahatyāpi niguhyamānaḥ sa bhūpatestasya manovikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Though concealed by great fortitude, that disturbance of the king's mind

children.text: mukhena cintāstimitekṣaṇena kārśyena ca vyaktimupājagāma // Jm_13.16 //
children.translated_text: became evident through his face with its gaze frozen in thought, and through his emaciation. // Jm_13.16 //

body.text: atheṅgitākāragrahaṇanipuṇamatirabhipārago 'mātyastaṃ rājño vṛttāntaṃ sakāraṇamupalabhya snehāttadatyayāśaṅko jānānaścātibalatāṃ madanasya rahasi rājānaṃ saṃviditaṃ samupetya kṛtābhyanujño vijñāpayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Abhipāraga</s>, the minister, skilled in discerning gestures and expressions, having perceived the full circumstances of the king's condition together with its cause, out of affection fearing the worst outcome, and knowing the overwhelming power of the god of love, approached the king in private, received his permission, and respectfully informed him:

children.text: adyārcayantaṃ naradeva devānsākṣādupetyāmburuhākṣa yakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O lord of men, today as you were worshipping the gods, a <s>Yakṣa</s> came to me in person, O lotus-eyed one,

children.text: māmāha nāvaiṣi nṛpasya kasmādunmādayantyāṃ hṛdayaṃ niviṣṭam // Jm_13.17 //
children.translated_text: and said, 'Do you not know that the king's heart is fixed upon <s>Unmādayantī</s>?' // Jm_13.17 //

children.text: ityevamuktvā sahasā tiro 'bhūdvimarśavānityahamabhyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he suddenly vanished. I have come to you upon reflection.

children.text: taccettathā deva kimetadevamasmāsu te niṣpraṇayatvamaunam // Jm_13.18 //
children.translated_text: If this be so, O Lord, then what is this silence of yours toward us, as though devoid of trust? // Jm_13.18 //

body.text: tatpratigrahītumenāmarhati madanugrahārthaṃ deva iti / atha rājā pratyādeśāllajjāvanatavadano madanavaśagato 'pi svabhyastadharmasaṃjñatvādaviklavībhūtadhairyaḥ pratyākhyānaviśadākṣaramenamuvāca - naitadasti / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: Therefore may the Lord deign to accept her, as a favor to me." Then the king, his face bowed in shame at being discovered, though subject to the power of love, yet undaunted in his fortitude owing to his habitual devotion to <s>Dharma</s>, spoke to him in words clear with refusal: "This must not be. Why?

children.text: puṇyāccyutaḥ syāmamaro na cāsmi vidyācca naḥ pāpamidaṃ jano 'pi /
children.translated_text: I would fall from merit — yet I am no immortal; and the people too would learn of this sin of ours;

children.text: tadviprayogācca mano jvalaṃtsvāṃ vahniḥ purā kakṣamiva kṣiṇoti // Jm_13.19 //
children.translated_text: and separation from her would cause the mind to burn, as fire consumes dry grass beforehand. // Jm_13.19 //

children.text: yaccobhayorityahitāvahaṃ syālloke parasminniha caiva karma /
children.translated_text: That which would bring harm in both this world and the next —

children.text: tadyasya hetorabudhā bhajante tasyaiva hetorna budhā bhajante // Jm_13.20 //
children.translated_text: the very thing for whose sake the unwise pursue it, for that very reason the wise do not. // Jm_13.20 //

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca - alamatra devasya dharmātikramāśaṅkayā /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: "Let the Lord have no apprehension of transgressing <s>Dharma</s> in this matter.

children.text: dāne sāhāyyadānena dharma eva bhavettava /
children.translated_text: By the gift of rendering assistance through giving, it would be <s>Dharma</s> itself for you;

children.text: dānavighnāttvadharmaḥ syāttāṃ matto 'pratigṛhṇataḥ // Jm_13.21 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Adharma</s> would arise from obstructing a gift, by your not accepting her from me. // Jm_13.21 //

body.text: kīrtyuparodhāvakāśamapi cātra devasya na paśyāmi / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: Nor do I see any occasion here for harm to the Lord's reputation. Why?

children.text: āvābhyāmidamanyaśca ka eva jñātumarhati /
children.translated_text: Who indeed is able to know of this matter besides ourselves?

children.text: janāpavādādāśaṅkāmato manasi mā kṛthāḥ // Jm_13.22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore do not harbor in your mind any apprehension of public reproach. // Jm_13.22 //

body.text: anugrahaścaiṣa mama syānna pīḍā / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: And this would be a favor to me, not an affliction. Why?

children.text: svāmyarthacaryārjitayā hi tuṣṭyā nirantare cetasi ko vighātaḥ /
children.translated_text: For when the heart is filled with satisfaction earned through service to one's master's purpose, what disturbance can there be?

children.text: yataḥ sukāmaṃ kuru deva kāmamalaṃ madutpīḍanaśaṅkayā te // Jm_13.23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore freely fulfill your desire, O Lord, and let there be no apprehension on your part of causing me suffering. // Jm_13.23 //

body.text: rājovāca - śāntaṃ pāpam /
body.translated_text: The king said: "Avert this evil!

children.text: vyaktamasmadatisnehānna tvayaitadapekṣitam /
children.translated_text: Clearly, out of excessive affection for me, you have not considered

children.text: yathā dāne na sarvasminsācivyaṃ dharmasādhanam // Jm_13.24 //
children.translated_text: that assistance in giving is not in every case the means of <s>Dharma</s>. // Jm_13.24 //

children.text: yo madarthamatisnehātsvān prāṇānapi nekṣate /
children.translated_text: He who out of excessive affection for my sake does not regard even his own life —

children.text: tasya bandhuviśiṣṭasya sakhyurbhāryā sakhī mama // Jm_13.25 //
children.translated_text: the wife of such a one, dearer than a kinsman, my friend, is as a friend to me. // Jm_13.25 //

body.text: tadayuktaṃ māmatīrthe pratārayitum / yadapi ceṣṭaṃ naitadanyaḥ kaścijjñāsyatīti, kimevamidamapāpaṃ syāt?
body.translated_text: Therefore it is wrong to lead me astray at a fordless crossing. And as for the claim that 'no one else will ever know of this' — would that make it free of sin?

children.text: adṛśyamāno 'pi hi pāpamācaranviṣaṃ niṣevyeva kathaṃ samṛdhnuyāt /
children.translated_text: For even one who commits sin unseen — how can he prosper, any more than one who consumes poison?

children.text: na taṃ na paśyanti viśuddhacakṣuṣo divaukasaścaiva narāśca yoginaḥ // Jm_13.26 //
children.translated_text: Those of purified vision do not fail to see him — both the celestial beings and the sages among men. // Jm_13.26 //

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: śraddadhīta ka etacca yathāsau tava na priyā /
children.translated_text: who would believe that she is not dear to you?

children.text: tāṃ parityajya sadyo vā vighātaṃ na samāpnuyāḥ // Jm_13.27 //
children.translated_text: Or that you would not immediately come to grief upon giving her up? // Jm_13.27 //

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said:

children.text: saputradāro dāso 'haṃ svāmī tvaṃ daivataṃ ca me /
children.translated_text: "I am your slave, together with my wife and children; you are my master and my deity.

children.text: dāsyāmasyāṃ yato deva kaste dharmavyatikramaḥ // Jm_13.28 //
children.translated_text: Since she is a slave's possession, O Lord, what transgression of <s>Dharma</s> can there be for you in this? // Jm_13.28 //

body.text: yadapi ceṣṭaṃ priyā mameyamiti kim?
body.translated_text: And as for the claim that she is dear to me — what of it?

children.text: mama priyā kāmada kāmameṣā tenaiva ditsāmi ca tubhyamenām /
children.translated_text: She is indeed dear to me, O granter of desires, and for that very reason I wish to give her to you;

children.text: priyaṃ hi dattvā labhate paratra prakarṣaramyāṇi janaḥ priyāṇi // Jm_13.29 //
children.translated_text: for by giving what is dear, a person obtains in the next world pleasures surpassingly delightful. // Jm_13.29 //

body.text: yataḥ pratigṛhṇātvevaināṃ deva iti / rājovāca - mā maivam / akrama eṣaḥ / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: Therefore let the Lord accept her." The king said: "Do not speak thus. This is improper. Why?

children.text: ahaṃ hi śastraṃ niśitaṃ viśeyaṃ hutāśanaṃ visphuradarciṣaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: I would sooner enter a sharpened blade, or a blazing fire with flickering flames,

children.text: na tveva dharmādadhigamya lakṣmīṃ śakṣyāmi tatraiva punaḥ prahartum // Jm_13.30 //
children.translated_text: than, having attained sovereignty through <s>Dharma</s>, be able to strike at that very <s>Dharma</s> again. // Jm_13.30 //

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca - yadyenāṃ madbhāryeti devo na pratigrahītumicchatyayamahamasyāḥ sarvajanaprārthanāviruddhaveśyāvratamādiśāmi / tata enāṃ devaḥ pratigṛhṇīyāditi / rājovāca - kimunmatto 'si?
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: "If Your Majesty does not wish to accept her because she is my wife, then I shall assign her the vow of a courtesan, open to the desires of all men. Then may Your Majesty accept her." The king said: "Are you mad?

children.text: aduṣṭāṃ saṃtyajanbhāryāṃ matto daṇḍamavāpnuyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Abandoning your innocent wife, you, a madman, would incur punishment;

children.text: sa dhigvādāspadībhūtaḥ paratreha ca dhakṣyase // Jm_13.31 //
children.translated_text: Having become an object of reproach, you will burn both here and in the next world."

body.text: tadalamakāryanirbandhitayā / nyāyābhiniveśī bhaveti / abhiupāraga uvāca -
body.translated_text: "Therefore, enough of this insistence on what is improper. Be devoted to what is right." <s>Abhipāraga</s> said:

children.text: dharmātyayo me yadi kaścidevaṃ janāpavādaḥ sukhaviplavo vā /
children.translated_text: "If any transgression of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) befalls me thus, or public censure, or loss of happiness,

children.text: pratyudgamiṣyāmyurasā tu tattattvatsaukhyalabdhena manaḥsukhena // Jm_13.32 //
children.translated_text: I shall face it with my breast, through the joy of mind born from your pleasure."

children.text: tvattaḥ paraṃ cāhavanīyamanyaṃ loke na paśyāmi mahīmahendra /
children.translated_text: "I see no other <s>āhavanīya</s> (sacred fire) in the world greater than you, O great lord of the earth;

children.text: unmādayantī mama puṇyavṛddhyai tāṃ dakṣiṇāmṛtvigiva pratīccha // Jm_13.33 //
children.translated_text: Accept <s>Unmādayantī</s> as a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial gift) for the increase of my merit, as a priest accepts his fee."

body.text: rājovāca - kāmamasmadatisnehādanavekṣitātmahitāhitakramo madarthacaryāsamudyogastavāyam / ata eva tu tvāṃ viśeṣato nopekṣitumarhāmi / naiva khalu lokāpavādaniḥśaṅkena bhavitavyam / paśya,
body.translated_text: The king said: "Clearly, this effort of yours in service to me proceeds from excessive affection for me, without regard for what is beneficial or harmful to yourself. But precisely for this reason I cannot neglect you. Indeed, one must not be indifferent to public censure. Consider:

children.text: lokasya yo nādriyate 'pavādaṃ dharmānapekṣaḥ parataḥ phalaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: He who disregards the censure of the world, heedless of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and its fruits in the hereafter,

children.text: jano na viśvāsamupaiti tasmindhruvaṃ ca lakṣmyāpi vivarjyate saḥ // Jm_13.34 //
children.translated_text: in him people place no trust, and he is surely abandoned even by <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune)."

body.text: yatastvāṃ bravīmi
body.translated_text: "Therefore I say to you:

children.text: mā te rociṣṭa dharmasya jīvitārthe vyatikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let not a transgression of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) for the sake of life appeal to you,

children.text: niḥsaṃdigdhamahādoṣaḥ sasandehakṛśodayaḥ // Jm_13.35 //
children.translated_text: for it brings great fault beyond all doubt, while its gain is meager and uncertain."

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ,
body.translated_text: "Moreover,

children.text: nindādiduḥkheṣu parānnipātya neṣṭā satāmātmasukhapravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having cast others into sufferings such as censure and the like, the pursuit of one's own pleasure is not desired by the virtuous;

children.text: eko 'pyanutpīḍya parānato 'haṃ dharme sthitaḥ svārthadhuraṃ prapatsye // Jm_13.36 //
children.translated_text: Even alone, without oppressing others, I, steadfast in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), shall pursue the burden of my own purpose."

body.text: abhipāraga uvāca - svāmyarthaṃ bhaktivaśena carato mama tāvadatra ka evādharmāvakāśaḥ syāddevasya vā dīyamānāmenāṃ pratigṛhṇataḥ / yataḥ sanaigamajānapadāḥ śibayaḥ kimatrādharma iti brūyuḥ / tat pratigṛhṇātvevaināṃ deva iti / rājovāca - addhā madarthacaryāpraṇayimatirbhavān / idaṃ tvatra cintayitavyam - sanaigamajānapadānāṃ vā śibīnāṃ tava mama vā ko 'smākaṃ dharmavittama iti / athābhipāragaḥ sasaṃbhramo rājānamuvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Abhipāraga</s> said: "What occasion for <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) could there be for me, who acts out of devotion for the sake of my lord, or for Your Majesty, who accepts what is freely given? For the <s>Śibis</s>, including townspeople and country folk, would say 'What unrighteousness is there in this?' Therefore, may Your Majesty accept her." The king said: "Truly, your mind is inclined to devoted service toward me. But consider this: who among us — the <s>Śibis</s> with their townspeople and country folk, or you, or I — is the most learned in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness)?" Then <s>Abhipāraga</s>, alarmed, said to the king:

children.text: bṛddhopasevāsu kṛtaśramatvācchrutādhikārānmatipāṭavācca /
children.translated_text: "Through your diligence in attending upon elders, your mastery of the scriptures, and your sharpness of intellect,

children.text: trivargavidyātiśayārthatattvaṃ tvayi sthitaṃ deva bṛhaspatau ca // Jm_13.37 //
children.translated_text: the essential truth of the science of the three aims of life resides in you, O Lord, and in <s>Bṛhaspati</s>."

body.text: rājovāca - tena hi na māmatra pratārayitumarhasi / kutaḥ?

children.text: narādhipānāṃ cariteṣvadhīnaṃ lokasya yasmādahitaṃ hitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Since the welfare and harm of the people depend upon the conduct of kings,

children.text: bhaktiṃ prajānāmanucintya tasmātkīrtikṣame satpatha eva raṃsye // Jm_13.38 //
children.translated_text: therefore, reflecting on the devotion of my subjects, I shall delight only in the righteous path that bears fair fame."

body.translated_text: The king said: "Then you should not try to deceive me in this matter. For what reason?

children.text: jihmaṃ śubhaṃ vā vṛṣabhapracāraṃ gāvo 'nugā yadvadanuprayānti /
children.translated_text: "Just as cows follow the lead of a bull, going along whichever way he goes, whether crooked or virtuous,

children.text: utkṣiptaśaṅkāṅkaśanirvighaṭṭaṃ prajāstathaiva kṣitipasya vṛttim // Jm_13.39 //
children.translated_text: so too do subjects follow the conduct of their king, free from any apprehension of raised doubt or rebuke."

body.text: api paśyatu tāvadbhavān /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, let your lordship consider:

children.text: ātmānamapi cecchaktirna syātpālayituṃ mama /
children.translated_text: If I should lack the power to govern even myself,

children.text: kā nvavasthā janasyāsya matto rakṣābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ // Jm_13.40 //
children.translated_text: what would be the condition of these people who look to me for protection?"

children.text: iti prajānāṃ hitamīkṣamāṇaḥ svaṃ caiva dharmaṃ vimalaṃ yaśaśca /
children.translated_text: "Thus, considering the welfare of my subjects, my own stainless <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and my fame,

children.text: necchāmi cittasya vaśena gantumahaṃ hi netā vṛṣavatprajānām // Jm_13.41 //
children.translated_text: I do not wish to act at the whim of my mind, for I am the leader of my people, like a bull."

body.text: athābhipārago 'mātyastena rājño 'vasthānena prasāditamanāḥ praṇamya rājānaṃ prāñjalirityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the minister <s>Abhipāraga</s>, his heart won over by the king's steadfastness, bowed to the king and spoke with palms joined:

children.text: aho prajānāmatibhāgyasampadyāsāṃ tvamevaṃ naradeva goptā /
children.translated_text: "Oh, what a great fortune for the subjects, that you, O lord of men, are their protector!

children.text: dharmānurāgo hi sukhānapekṣastapovanastheṣvapi mṛgya eva // Jm_13.42 //
children.translated_text: For such devotion to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), heedless of personal comfort, is rare to find even among forest-dwelling ascetics."

body.text: mahacchabdo mahārāja tvayyevāyaṃ virājate

children.text: viguṇeṣu guṇoktirhi kṣeparūkṣatarākṣarā // Jm_13.43 //
children.translated_text: for praise of virtues applied to those who lack them sounds harsh and mocking."

body.translated_text: "The great title 'Mahārāja' (Great King) truly shines in you alone, O great king,

children.text: vismayo 'nibhṛtatvaṃ vā kiṃ mamaitāvatā tvayi /
children.translated_text: "What wonder or agitation could I feel toward you, even by this much,

children.text: samudra iva ratnānāṃ guṇānāṃ yastvamākaraḥ // Jm_13.44 //
children.translated_text: you who are a mine of virtues, as the ocean is a mine of gems?"

body.text: tadevaṃ tīvraduḥkhāturāṇāmapi satāṃ nīcamārganiṣpraṇayatā bhavati svadhairyāvaṣṭambhāt svabhyastadharmasaṃjñatvācceti dhairyadharmābhyāse ca yogaḥ kārya iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, even when afflicted by intense suffering, the virtuous feel no inclination toward base paths, owing to their firm resolve and their habitual recognition of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). Therefore, one should strive to cultivate both steadfastness and the practice of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: ityunmādayantījātakaṃ trayodaśam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth <s>jātaka</s> (birth story), the story of <s>Unmādayantī</s>.

body.text: 14. Supāragajātakam
body.translated_text: 14. The <s>Jātaka</s> (Birth Story) of <s>Supāraga</s>

body.text: dharmāśrayaṃ satyavacanamapyāpadaṃ nudati prāgeva tatphalamiti dharmānuvartinā bhavitavyam / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: A truthful word grounded in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) dispels calamity — how much more so its fruit. Therefore one should be a follower of <s>dharma</s>. As it is heard in tradition:

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kila mahāsattvaḥ paramanipuṇamatirnausārathirbabhūva / dharmatā hyeṣā bodhisattvānāṃ prakṛtimedhāvitvādyaduta yaṃ yaṃ śāstrātiśayaṃ jijñāsante kalāviśeṣaṃ vā tasmiṃstasminnadhikatarā bhavanti medhāvino jagataḥ / atha sa mahātmā viditajyotirgatitvāddigvibhāgeṣvasammūḍhamatiḥ parividitaniyatāgantukautpātikanimittaḥ kālākālakramakuśalo mīnatoyavarṇabhaumaprakāraśakuniparvatādibhiścihnaiḥ sūpalakṣitasamudradeśaḥ smṛtimānvijitatandrīnidraḥ śītoṣṇavarṣādiparikhedasahiṣṇurapramādī dhṛtimānāharaṇāpaharaṇakuśalatvādīpsitaṃ deśaṃ prāpayitā vaṇijāmāsīt / tasya paramasiddhayātratvātsupāraga ityeva nāma babhūva / tadadhyuṣitaṃ ca pattanaṃ supāragamityevākhyātamāsīt / yadetarhi sūpāragamiti jñāyate / so 'pi maṅgalasammatatvād vṛddhatve 'pi sāṃyātrikairyātrāsiddhikāmairvahanamabhyarthanasatkārapuraḥsaramāropyate sma /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, possessed of supremely keen intellect, was a master navigator. For it is the nature of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that, owing to their innate wisdom, in whatever branch of learning or special art they wish to master, they surpass all intelligent beings. Now this great soul, having knowledge of the movements of the stars, was unerring in his understanding of the directions, fully conversant with the fixed, seasonal, and portentous signs, skilled in the sequence of favorable and unfavorable times, well able to identify regions of the sea by marks such as fish, water-color, terrain-type, birds, mountains, and the like, mindful, having conquered sloth and sleep, patient of the hardships of cold, heat, rain and more, vigilant, resolute, and skilled in steering and navigating — he would bring merchants to their desired destination. Because of his supremely successful voyages, his name became <s>Supāraga</s> ("He of excellent crossings"). And the port where he dwelt came to be known as <s>Supāraga</s>, which is now known as <s>Sūpāraga</s>. Even in his old age, because he was regarded as auspicious, seafarers desiring success on their voyages would invite him with honors and entreaties to board their vessel.

body.text: atha kadācidbharukacchādabhiprayātāḥ suvarṇabhūmivaṇijo yātrāsiddhikāmāḥ supāragaṃ pattanamupetya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ vahanārohaṇārthamabhyarthayāmāsuḥ / sa tānuvāca -
body.translated_text: Now once, merchants who had set out from <s>Bharukaccha</s> (Bharuch), desiring success on their voyage to <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> (the Land of Gold), came to the port of <s>Supāraga</s> and requested the great being to board their ship. He said to them:

children.text: jarājñayā saṃhriyamāṇadarśane śramābhipātaiḥ pratanūkṛtasmṛtau /
children.translated_text: "When my sight is being diminished by the command of old age, my memory made feeble by the assaults of exertion,

children.text: svadehakṛtye 'pyavasannavikrame sahāyatā kā pariśaṅkyate mayi // Jm_14.1 //
children.translated_text: and my vigor enfeebled even for the tasks of my own body, what companionship can be expected from me?"

body.text: vaṇija ūcuḥ - viditeyamasmākaṃ yuṣmaccharīrāvasthā / satyapi ca vaḥ parākramāsahatve naiva vayaṃ karmaviniyogena yuṣmānāyāsayitumicchāmaḥ / kiṃ tarhi?
body.translated_text: The merchants said: "We are aware of the condition of your body. And even though your strength has waned, we have no wish to burden you with the assignment of tasks. Rather:

children.text: tvatpādapaṅkajasamāśrayasatkṛtena maṅgalyatāmupagatā rajasā tviyaṃ nauḥ /
children.translated_text: This ship has become auspicious through the dust hallowed by the shelter of your lotus feet;

children.text: durge mahatyapi ca toyanidhāvamuṣmin svasti vrajediti bhavantamupāgatāḥ smaḥ // Jm_14.2 //
children.translated_text: and even in a great perilous passage of this ocean, she would travel safely — it is for this that we have come to you."

body.text: atha sa mahātmā teṣāmanukampayā jarāśithilaśarīro 'pi tadvahanamāruroha / tadadhirohaṇācca pramuditamanasaḥ sarva eva te vaṇijo babhūvurniyatamasmākamuttamā yātrāsiddhiriti / krameṇa cāvajagāhire vividhamīnakulavicaritamanibhṛtajalakalakalārāvamanilabalavilāsapravicalitataraṅgaṃ bahuvidharatnairbhūmiviśeṣairarpitaraṅgaṃ phenāvalīkusumadāmavicitramasurabalabhujagabhavanaṃ durāpapātālamaprameyatoyaṃ mahāsamudram /
body.translated_text: Then the great soul, out of compassion for them, though his body was frail with age, boarded their vessel. And at his boarding, the hearts of all those merchants became joyful, thinking "Surely we shall have the most excellent success on our voyage." And gradually they entered the great ocean, teeming with the movements of various fish and sea creatures, resounding with the ceaseless murmur of its waters, its waves tossed about by the sport of the wind's force, its expanse adorned with manifold jewels from various regions of its bed, adorned with garlands of foam-flowers, the abode of <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Balas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>, with unfathomable depths and immeasurable waters.

children.text: athendranīlaprakarābhinīlaṃ sūryāṃśutāpādiva khaṃ vilīnam /
children.translated_text: Then, into waters dark as a mass of sapphires, as though the sky had melted from the heat of the sun's rays,

children.text: samantato 'ntarhitatīralekhamagādhamammonidhimadhyamīyuḥ // Jm_14.3 //
children.translated_text: with the shoreline vanished on all sides, they entered the fathomless mid-ocean, the treasury of waters.

body.text: teṣāṃ tatrānuprāptānāṃ sāyāhnasamaye mṛdūbhūtakiraṇacakraprabhāve savitari mahadautpātikaṃ paramabhīṣaṇaṃ prādurabhūt /
body.translated_text: When they had arrived there, in the evening time, as the sun's circle of rays grew gentle, a great and supremely terrifying portent appeared:

children.text: vibhidyamānormivikīrṇaphenaścaṇḍānilāsphālanabhīmanādaḥ /
children.translated_text: With waves splitting apart and scattering foam, roaring dreadfully from the lashing of fierce winds,

children.text: naibhṛtyanirmuktasamagratoyaḥ kṣaṇena raudraḥ samabhūt samudraḥ // Jm_14.4 //
children.translated_text: all its waters hurled up in restless fury, the ocean became terrible in an instant.

children.text: utpātavātākalitairmahadbhistoyasthalairbhīmarayairbhramadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With great masses of water whipped up by storm-winds, terrifying in their roar, whirling about,

children.text: yugāntakālapracalācaleva bhūmirbabhūvogravapuḥ samudraḥ // Jm_14.5 //
children.translated_text: the ocean assumed a fearsome form, as though the earth were quaking with its mountains at the end of an age.

children.text: vidyullatodbhāsuralolajihvā nīlā bhujaṅgā iva naikaśīrṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Storm clouds, dark as serpents with many heads, their flickering tongues flashing with lightning,

children.text: āvavrurādityapathaṃ payodāḥ prasaktabhīmastanitānunādāḥ // Jm_14.6 //
children.translated_text: covered the path of the sun, resounding with continuous, dreadful thunder.

children.text: ghanairghanairāvṛtaraśmijālaḥ sūryaḥ krameṇāstamupāruroha /
children.translated_text: The sun, its web of rays obscured by cloud upon cloud, gradually climbed toward its setting;

children.text: dināntalabdhaprasaraṃ samantāttamo ghanībhāvamivājagāma // Jm_14.7 //
children.translated_text: and the darkness, gaining free scope at the end of day, seemed to thicken on all sides into a solid mass.

children.text: dhārāśarairācchuritormicakre mahodadhāvutpatatīva roṣāt /
children.translated_text: In the great ocean, its ring of waves pelted with showers of rain-arrows, rising as if in fury,

children.text: bhīteva naurabhyadhikaṃ cakampe viṣādayantī hṛdayāni teṣām // Jm_14.8 //
children.translated_text: the ship trembled ever more violently, as if in fear, filling their hearts with despair.

children.text: te trāsadīnāśca viṣādamūkā dhīrāḥ pratīkārasasambhramāśca /
children.translated_text: Some, wretched with terror, were struck dumb with dejection; the steadfast ones busied themselves with counter-measures;

children.text: svadevatāyācanatatparāśca bhāvānyathā sattvaguṇaṃ vivavruḥ // Jm_14.9 //
children.translated_text: and others, intent on praying to their own deities — the change in their states revealed each one's quality of <s>sattva</s> (character).

body.text: atha te sāṃyātrikāḥ pavanabalacalitasalilavegavaśagayā nāvā paribhramyamāṇā bahubhirapyahobhirnaiva kutaścittīraṃ dadṛśurna ca yathepsitāni samudracihnāni / apūrvaireva tu samudracihnairabhivardhamānavaimanasyā bhayaviṣādavyākulatāmupajagmuḥ / athaitān supārago bodhisattvo vyavasthāpayannuvāca - anāścaryaṃ khalu mahāsamudramadhyamavagāḍhānāmautpātikakṣobhaparikleśaḥ / tadalamatrabhavatāṃ viṣādānuvṛttyā / kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: Then those seafarers, carried about by the ship which was at the mercy of the rush of waters driven by the force of the wind, even after many days saw no shore anywhere, nor the sea-marks they desired. Beset by unfamiliar sea-marks, their distress ever growing, they fell into bewilderment overwhelmed by fear and despair. Then <s>Supāraga</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, reassuring them, said: "It is no wonder that those who have plunged into the midst of the great ocean should suffer the affliction of storms and portents. Therefore, enough of this indulgence in despair. For:

children.text: nāpatpratīkāravidhirviṣādastasmādalaṃ dainyaparigraheṇa /
children.translated_text: Despair is not a remedy against misfortune; therefore, enough of yielding to despondency;

children.text: dhairyāttu kāryapratipattidakṣāḥ kṛcchrāṇyakṛcchreṇa samuttaranti // Jm_14.10 //
children.translated_text: through steadfastness, those skilled in purposeful action overcome hardships without hardship."

children.text: viṣādadainyaṃ vyavadhūya tasmātkāryāvakāśaṃ kriyayā bhajadhvam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, shaking off the despondency of despair, devote yourselves to action when the occasion for action arises;

children.text: prājñasya dhairyajvalitaṃ hi tejaḥ sarvārthasiddhigrahaṇāgrahastaḥ // Jm_14.11 //
children.translated_text: for the splendor of the wise, blazing with steadfastness, has its foremost hand ready to seize the accomplishment of every aim."

body.text: tadyathādhikārāvahitā bhavantu bhavantaḥ / iti te sāṃyātrikāstena mahātmanā dhīrīkṛtamanasaḥ kūladarśanotsukamatayaḥ samudramavalokayanto dadṛśuḥ puruṣavigrahānāmuktarūpyakavacānivonmajjato nimajjataśca / samyak caiṣāmākṛtinimittamupadhārya savismayāḥ supāragāya nyavedayanta - apūrvaṃ khalvidamiha mahāsamudre cihnamupalabhyate / ete khalu
body.translated_text: "So let your honors be attentive to your duties." Thus, with their minds steadied by that great soul, those seafarers, their thoughts eager to catch sight of the shore, gazed upon the ocean and saw beings of human form, clad as it were in silver armor, rising and sinking. Having carefully noted the appearance and significance of these creatures, they reported to <s>Supāraga</s> with astonishment: "A strange sign is observed here in the great ocean! Indeed,

children.text: āmuktarūpyakavacā iva daityayodhā ghorekṣaṇāḥ khuranikāśavirūpaghoṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: clad as if in silver armor, like demon warriors, with terrible eyes and misshapen snouts resembling hooves,

children.text: unmajjanāvataraṇasphuraṇaprasaṃgāt krīḍāmivārṇavajale 'nubhavanti ke 'pi // Jm_14.12 //
children.translated_text: some beings seem to be sporting in the waters of the ocean, plunging, surfacing, and darting about."

body.text: supāraga uvāca - naite mānuṣā amānuṣā vā / mīnāḥ khalvete / yato na bhetavyamebhyaḥ / kintu -
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: "These are neither human nor non-human. They are fish. There is nothing to fear from them. However:

children.text: sudūrapamakṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ pattanadvitayādapi /
children.translated_text: We have been carried very far from both ports;

children.text: khuramālī samudro 'yaṃ tadyatadhvaṃ nivartitum // Jm_14.13 //
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Khuramālī</s> ocean — make every effort to turn back."

body.text: caṇḍavegavāhinā salilanivahenaikāntahareṇa ca pāścāttyena vāyunā samākṣiptayā nāvā na te sāṃyātrikāḥ śekurvinivartitum / athāvagāhamānāḥ krameṇa rūpyaprabhāvabhāsitamanīlaphenanicayapāṇḍuramaparaṃ samudramālokya savismayāḥ supāragamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: But carried by the ship, driven by the rush of waters propelled by fierce winds and by a relentless westerly gale, the seafarers were unable to turn back. Then, as they drifted further, they beheld another ocean, gleaming with a silvery radiance, pale white with masses of blue-green foam, and they said to <s>Supāraga</s> in astonishment:

children.text: svaphenamagnairiva ko 'yamambubhirmahārṇavaḥ śukladukūlavāniva /
children.translated_text: "What is this ocean that seems submerged in its own foam, as though robed in white silk,

children.text: dravānivendoḥ kiraṇānsamudvahansamantato hāsa iva prasarpati // Jm_14.14 //
children.translated_text: bearing what seem to be the melted rays of the moon, spreading laughter as it were on all sides?"

body.text: supāraga uvāca - kaṣṭam / atidūraṃ khalvavagāhyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: "Alas! We have drifted far too deep indeed.

children.text: kṣīrārṇava iti khyāta udadhirdadhimālyasau /
children.translated_text: This ocean is called the <s>Kṣīrārṇava</s> (Milk Ocean), the sea garlanded with curds;

children.text: kṣamaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ gantuṃ śakyate cennivartitum // Jm_14.15 //
children.translated_text: it is not safe to go beyond this point — turn back if you can."

body.text: vaṇija ūcuḥ - na khalu śakyate vilambayitumapi vahanaṃ kuta eva sannivartayitumatiśīghravāhitvādvahanasya pratikūlatvācca mārutasyeti / atha vyatītya tamapi samudraṃ suvarṇaprabhānurañjitapracalormimālamagnijvālakapilasalilamaparaṃ samudramālokya savismayakautūhalāste vaṇijaḥ supāragaṃ papracchuḥ -
body.translated_text: The merchants said: "It is not possible even to slow down the vessel, let alone turn it back, because of the extreme swiftness of the current and the adverse wind." Then, having passed beyond that ocean too, upon beholding another ocean whose water was tawny like the glow of fire, its restlessly rippling garlands of waves tinged with the radiance of gold, they questioned <s>Supāraga</s> with wonder and curiosity:

children.text: bālārkalakṣmyeva kṛtāṅgarāgaiḥ samunnamadbhiḥ salilairanīlaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "With its upwelling waters, not blue but as if adorned with the splendor of the young sun,

children.text: jvalanmahānagnirivāvabhāti ko nāma tasmācca mahārṇavo 'yam // Jm_14.16 //
children.translated_text: gleaming like a great blazing fire — what, pray, is this great ocean?" || Jm 14.16 ||

body.text: supāraga uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said:

children.text: agnimālīti vikhyātaḥ samudro 'yaṃ prakāśate /
children.translated_text: "This ocean is renowned as <s>Agnimālī</s> (Garlanded-with-Fire);

children.text: atīva khalu sādhu syānnivartemahi yadyataḥ // Jm_14.17 //
children.translated_text: it would be exceedingly good indeed if we could turn back from here." || Jm 14.17 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā nāmamātramakathayattasya saritpaterna toyavaivarṇyakāraṇaṃ dīrghadarśitvāt / atha te sāṃyātrikāstamapi samudramatītya puṣparāgendranīlaprabhodyotitasalilaṃ paripakvakuśavananikāśavarṇaṃ samudramālokya kautūhalajātāḥ supāragaṃ papracchuḥ -
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul mentioned only the name of that lord of rivers, and not the cause of the discoloration of the water, out of farsightedness. Then those voyagers, having passed beyond that ocean too, upon beholding an ocean whose water gleamed with the radiance of topaz and sapphire, of a color resembling mature <s>kuśa</s> grass, asked <s>Supāraga</s>, their curiosity aroused:

children.text: pariṇatakuśaparṇavarṇatoyaḥ salilanidhiḥ katamo nvayaṃ vibhāti /
children.translated_text: "What is this body of water that shines with water the color of ripened <s>kuśa</s> leaves,

children.text: sakusuma iva phenabhakticitrairanilajavākalitaistaraṅgabhaṅgaiḥ // Jm_14.18 //
children.translated_text: as if blossoming, with its breaking waves tossed by the swift wind, mottled with offerings of foam?" || Jm 14.18 ||

body.text: supāraga uvāca - bhoḥ sārthavāhā nivartanaṃ prati yatnaḥ kriyatām / na khalvataḥ kṣamate paraṃ gantum /
body.translated_text: <s>Supāraga</s> said: "O caravan-leaders, let every effort be made to turn back! It is certainly not possible to proceed further than this.

children.text: kuśamālī samudro 'yamatyaṅkaśa iva dvipaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This ocean, <s>Kuśamālī</s> (Garlanded-with-Kuśa-Grass), is like an elephant beyond the goad;

children.text: prasahyāsahyasalilo haranharati no ratim // Jm_14.19 //
children.translated_text: irresistibly powerful in its waters, it forcibly carries away our delight." || Jm 14.19 ||

body.text: atha te vāṇijakāḥ pareṇāpi yatnena nivartayitumaśaknuvantastamapi samudramatītya vaṃśarāgavaiḍūryaprabhāvyatikaraharitasalilamaparaṃ samudramālokya supāragamapṛcchan -
body.translated_text: Then those merchants, unable to turn back even with the utmost effort, having passed beyond that ocean too, upon beholding another ocean whose water was green from the intermingling of the radiance of bamboo-hue and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), asked <s>Supāraga</s>:

children.text: marakataharitaprabhairjalairvahati navāmiva śādvalaśriyam /
children.translated_text: "Bearing what seems like a new beauty of meadow-grass with waters green as the luster of emerald,

children.text: kumudaruciraphenabhūṣaṇaḥ salilanidhiḥ katamo 'yamīkṣyate // Jm_14.20 //
children.translated_text: adorned with foam beautiful as <s>kumuda</s> lotuses — what is this body of water that is seen?" || Jm 14.20 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā tena vaṇigjanasya vyasanopanipātena dahyamānahṛdayo dīrghamuṣṇamabhiniśvasya śanairuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, his heart burning at the calamity that had befallen the merchant-folk, sighing long and hot, spoke slowly:

children.text: atidūramupetāḥ stha duḥkhamasmānnivartitum /
children.translated_text: "You have come exceedingly far; it will be difficult to turn back from here.

children.text: paryanta iva lokasya nalamālyeṣa sāgaraḥ // Jm_14.21 //
children.translated_text: This ocean, <s>Nalamālī</s> (Garlanded-with-Reeds), is as if the boundary of the world." || Jm 14.21 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā te vāṇijakā viṣādoparudhyamānamanaso visrasyamānagātrotsāhā niśvasitamātraparāyaṇāstatraiva niṣeduḥ / vyatītya ca tamapi samudraṃ sāyāhnasamaye vilambamānaraśmimaṇḍale salilanidhimiva praveṣṭukāme divasakare samudvartamānasyeva salilanidheraśanīnāmiva ca sampatatāṃ veṇuvanānāmiva cāgniparigatānāṃ visphuṭatāṃ tumulamatibhīṣaṇaṃ śrutihṛdayavidāraṇaṃ samudradhvanimaśrauṣuḥ / śrutvā ca santrāsavaśagāḥ sphuranmanasaḥ sahasaivotthāya samantato 'nuvilokayanto dadṛśuḥ prapāta iva śvabhra iva ca mahati tamudakaughaṃ nipatantam / dṛṣṭvā ca paramabhayaviṣādavihvalāḥ supāragamupetyocuḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the merchants, their minds obstructed by despair, their bodily energy collapsing, able to do nothing but sigh, sat down right there. And having passed beyond that ocean too, in the evening hour — when the sun-god, with his garland of rays hanging low, seemed about to enter the body of water — they heard a tumultuous, exceedingly terrifying sound of the ocean, rending the ears and the heart, as if of the ocean swelling up, as if of thunderbolts crashing, as if of bamboo groves splitting apart when engulfed by fire. And upon hearing it, seized by terror, their minds trembling, rising up suddenly and looking all around, they saw that great mass of water plunging down as if into a precipice, as if into an abyss. And upon seeing it, utterly distraught with supreme fear and despair, they approached <s>Supāraga</s> and said:

children.text: nirbhindanniva naḥ śrutīḥ pratibhayaścetāṃsi mathnanniva
children.translated_text: "As if splitting our ears asunder, terrifying, as if churning our hearts,

children.text: kruddhasyeva saritpaterdhvanirayaṃ dūrādapi śrūyate /
children.translated_text: this sound as of the enraged lord of rivers is heard even from afar!

children.text: bhīme śvabhra ivārṇavasya nipatatyetatsamagraṃ jalaṃ
children.translated_text: All this water of the ocean is plunging into what seems a terrifying abyss —

children.text: tatko 'sāvudadhiḥ kimatra ca paraṃ kṛtyaṃ bhavānmanyate // Jm_14.22 //
children.translated_text: what, then, is that ocean, and what further course of action do you deem [fit]?" || Jm 14.22 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā sasambhramaḥ kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭamityuktvā samudramālokayannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, alarmed, having said 'Alas, alas!', gazing at the ocean, spoke:

children.text: yatprāpya na nivartante mṛtyormukhamivāmukham /
children.translated_text: "That from which [none] return, like the open mouth of death itself —

children.text: aśivaṃ samupetāḥ stha tadetadvaḍavāmukham // Jm_14.23 //
children.translated_text: you have reached that inauspicious [place]: this is the <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s> (the Mare's Mouth)." || Jm 14.23 ||

body.text: tadupaśrutya te vāṇijakā vaḍavāmukhamupetā vayamiti tyaktajīvitāśā maraṇabhayaviklavībhūtamanasaḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the merchants — realizing 'We have reached the <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>!' — having abandoned all hope of life, their minds bewildered by the fear of death,

children.text: sasvaraṃ ruruduḥ kecidvilepuratha cukruśuḥ /
children.translated_text: some wept aloud, some lamented, some shrieked;

children.text: na kiñcitpratyapadyanta kecittrāsavicetasaḥ // Jm_14.24 //
children.translated_text: and some, their minds bewildered with terror, could not do anything at all. || Jm 14.24 ||

children.text: viśeṣataḥ kecidabhipraṇemurdevendramārtiprahatairmanobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some in particular bowed down to <s>Devendra</s> (Indra), their minds stricken with anguish;

children.text: ādityarudrāṃśca marudvasūṃśca prapedire sāgarameva cānye // Jm_14.25 //
children.translated_text: some took refuge in the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s>; and others [took refuge] in the ocean itself. || Jm 14.25 ||

children.text: jepuśca mantrānapare vicitrānanye tu devīṃ vidhivatpraṇemuḥ /
children.translated_text: Others recited various <s>mantras</s>, and others bowed reverently to the goddess [of fortune];

children.text: supāragaṃ kecidupetya tattadviceṣṭamānāḥ karuṇaṃ vilepuḥ // Jm_14.26 //
children.translated_text: and some, approaching <s>Supāraga</s>, performing various gestures, wept piteously: || Jm 14.26 ||

children.text: āpadgatatrāsaharasya nityaṃ parānukampāguṇasambhṛtasya /
children.translated_text: "This is the time for the deployment of that surpassing power of yours,

children.text: ayaṃ prabhāvātiśayasya tasya tavābhyupeto viniyogakālaḥ // Jm_14.27 //
children.translated_text: who always removes the fear of those in distress, who is endowed with the virtue of compassion for others. || Jm 14.27 ||

children.text: ārtānanāthāñcharaṇāgatānnastvaṃ trātumāvarjaya dhīra cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Bend your mind, O steadfast one, to rescue us — distressed, helpless, [and] come to you for refuge;

children.text: ayaṃ hi kopādvaḍavāmukhena cikīrṣati grāsamivārṇavo 'smān // Jm_14.28 //
children.translated_text: for this ocean, with its <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>, in its fury, wishes to make a morsel of us, as it were!" || Jm 14.28 ||

children.text: nopekṣituṃ yuktamayaṃ janaste vipadyamānaḥ salilaughamadhye /
children.translated_text: "It is not right for you to be indifferent to these people of yours, perishing in the midst of the flood;

children.text: nājñāṃ tavātyeti mahāsamudrastadvāryatāmapraśamo 'yamasya // Jm_14.29 //
children.translated_text: the great ocean does not transgress your command — therefore let this restlessness of his be restrained!" || Jm 14.29 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā mahatyā karuṇayā samāpīḍyamānahṛdayastānvāṇijakānvyavasthāpayannuvāca - astyatrāpi naḥ kaścitpratikāravidhiḥ pratibhāti / tattāvatprayokṣye / yato muhūrtaṃ dhīrāstāvad bhavantu bhavanta iti / atha te vāṇijakā astyatrāpi kila pratīkāravidhirityāśayā samupastambhitadhairyāstadavahitamanasastūṣṇīṃbabhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, his heart pressed by immense compassion, steadying the merchants, said: "There is even here a certain method of remedy that occurs to me. I shall now employ it. Therefore be steadfast for a moment, good people." Then the merchants, their courage fortified by the hope that 'there is indeed a method of remedy,' became silent with attentive minds.

body.text: atha supārago bodhisattva ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇena jānumaṇḍalenādhiṣṭhāya nāvaṃ samāvarjitasarvabhāvaḥ praṇamya tathāgatebhyastānsāṃyātrikānāmantrayate sma - śrṛṇvantvatrabhavantaḥ sāṃyātrikāḥ salilanidhivyomāśrayāśca devaviśeṣāḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Supāraga</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, resting upon his right knee on the ship, having concentrated his entire being, bowing to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, addressed those voyagers: "Let their honors the voyagers listen — and the special deities who dwell in the ocean and the sky:

children.text: smarāmi yata ātmānaṃ yataḥ prāpto 'smi vijñatām /
children.translated_text: "From the time I recall myself, from the time I attained understanding,

children.text: nābhijānāmi sañcintya prāṇinaṃ hiṃsutuṃ kvacit // Jm_14.30 //
children.translated_text: I do not remember ever having intentionally harmed any living being." || Jm 14.30 ||

children.text: anena satyavākyena mama puṇyabalena ca /
children.translated_text: "By this truthful utterance and by the power of my merit,

children.text: vaḍavāmukhamaprāpya svasti naurvinivartatām // Jm_14.31 //
children.translated_text: may the ship turn back safely without reaching the <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>!" || Jm 14.31 ||

body.text: atha tasya mahātmanaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānabalātpuṇyatejasā saha salilajavena sa māruto vyāvartamānastāṃ nāvaṃ nivartayāmāsa / nivṛttāṃ tu tāṃ nāvamabhisamīkṣya te vāṇijakāḥ paramavismayapraharṣoddhatamānasā nivṛttā nauriti praṇāmasabhājanapuraḥsaraṃ supāragāya nyavedayanta / atha sa mahātmā tānvāṇijakānuvāca - sthirībhavantu bhavantaḥ / śīghramāropyantāṃ śītāni / iti ca tena samādiṣṭāḥ pramodādudbhūtabalotsāhāste tadadhikṛtāstathā cakruḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, by the power of that great soul's truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), together with the force of his merit, the wind reversed itself along with the current and turned the ship around. And perceiving the ship had turned back, the merchants, their minds uplifted with supreme wonder and joy, announced to <s>Supāraga</s>, preceded by bowing and homage: 'The ship has turned back!' Then that great soul said to the merchants: "Steady yourselves! Let the sails be hoisted quickly!" And those in charge, commanded by him, their strength and enthusiasm surging with delight, did so.

children.text: atha muditajanaprahāsanādā pravitatapāṇḍuraśītacārupakṣā /
children.translated_text: Then, with its people joyful and laughing, with its fair white sails beautifully spread,

children.text: salilanidhigatā rarāja sā naurgatajalade nabhasīva rājahaṃsī // Jm_14.32 //
children.translated_text: that ship, moving across the ocean, was resplendent — like a royal swan in a cloudless sky. || Jm 14.32 ||
