body.text: nivṛttāyāṃ tu tasyāṃ nāvyanukūlasalilamārutāyāṃ vimānalīlayā svecchayaiva cābhiprayātāyāṃ nātiśyāmībhūtasandhyāṅgarāgāsu pravitanyamānatamovitānāsvālakṣitanakṣatrabhūṣaṇāsu dikṣu kiñcidavaśeṣaprabhe divasakaramārge pravṛttakṣaṇadādhikāre supāragastānvāṇijakānuvāca - bhoḥ sārthavāhā nalamāliprabhṛtibhyo yathādṛṣṭebhyaḥ samudrebhyo vālukāḥ pāṣāṇāśca vahanamāropyantāṃ yāvatsahate / evamidaṃ yānapātraṃ nirghātabharīkrāntaṃ na ca pārśvāni dāsyati, maṅgalasammatāścaite vālukāpāṣāṇā niyataṃ lābhasiddhaye vo bhaviṣyantīti / atha te sāṃyātrikāḥ supāragapremabahumānāvarjitamatibhirdevatābhiranupradarśitebhyaḥ sthalebhya ādāya vālukāpāṣāṇabuddhyā vaiḍūryādīni ratnāni vahanamāropayāmāsuḥ / tenaiva caikarātreṇa sā naurbharukacchamupajagāma /
body.translated_text: And when the ship had turned back, proceeding as if at pleasure, like an aerial chariot, with current and wind in its favor, at a time when the evening-glow had not yet fully darkened, with the canopy of darkness gradually spreading, with the stars' ornaments becoming visible in the quarters, and with a little light remaining on the sun's path and night beginning to assume sovereignty, <s>Supāraga</s> said to the merchants: "O caravan-leaders, let sand and stones from the oceans [we passed through], beginning with the <s>Nalamālī</s>, be loaded onto the ship in accordance with what was observed, to the extent it can bear. Loaded with cargo from the storms in this manner, the vessel will not list to the sides; and these sands and stones, considered auspicious, will surely serve for the fulfillment of your profit." Then those voyagers, whose minds were won over by the deities — well-disposed toward <s>Supāraga</s> out of affection and respect — taking from the places indicated by the deities what they supposed to be sand and stones, loaded the ship with gems such as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and others. And within that very single night, the ship arrived at <s>Bharukaccha</s> (Bharuch).

children.text: atha prabhāte rajatendranīlavaiḍūryahemapratipūrṇanaukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at dawn, with their ship filled with silver, sapphire, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and gold,

children.text: svadeśatīrāntamupāgatāste prītyā tamānarcurudīrṇaharṣāḥ // Jm_14.33 //
children.translated_text: having arrived at the shore of their own country, they honored him with joy, their delight surging forth. || Jm 14.33 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ dharmāśrayaṃ satyavacanamapyāpadaṃ nudati prāgeva tatphalamiti dharmānuvartinā bhavitavyam / kalyāṇamitrāśrayavarṇe 'pi vācyamevaṃ kalyāṇamitrāśritāḥ śreyaḥ prāpnuvantīti /
body.translated_text: Thus, truthful speech rooted in <s>Dharma</s> dispels even calamity — how much more so its fruit! Therefore one should follow <s>Dharma</s>. This [story] is also to be cited in the description of the value of a spiritual friend: 'Those who rely on a spiritual friend attain well-being.'

body.text: iti supāragajātakaṃ caturdaśam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth [story], the <s>Supāraga Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 15. Matsyajātakam
body.translated_text: 15. The <s>Matsya Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Fish)

body.text: śīlavatāmihaivābhiprāyāḥ kalyāṇāḥ samṛdhyanti prāgeva paratreti śīlaviśuddhau prayatitavyam / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The good intentions of the virtuous are fulfilled right here in this world, let alone in the next — therefore one should strive for purity of conduct. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃścinnātimahati kahlāratāmarasakamalakuvalayavibhūṣitarucirasalile haṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākamithunopaśobhite tīrāntaruhatarukusumāvakīrṇe sarasi matsyādhipatirbabhūva / svabhyastabhāvācca bahuṣu janmāntareṣu parārthacaryāyāstatrastho 'pi parahitasukhapratipādanavyāpāro babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> became the king of fish in a certain not-very-large lake, whose lovely water was adorned with white lotuses, red lotuses, and blue lotuses, graced by pairs of geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds, and strewn with flowers fallen from trees growing along its banks. And owing to his habitual disposition, cultivated over many previous births, toward acting for the welfare of others, even in that [animal] state he was engaged in the task of promoting the happiness and well-being of others.

children.text: abhyāsayogāddhi śubhāśubhāni karmāṇi sātmyena bhavanti puṃsām /
children.translated_text: For through the force of habitual practice, both wholesome and unwholesome actions become second nature for people;

children.text: tathāvidhānyeva yadaprayatnājjanmāntare svapna ivācaranti // Jm_15.1 //
children.translated_text: thus in another birth, without effort, they perform such deeds as if in a dream. || Jm 15.1 ||

body.text: iṣṭānāmiva ca sveṣāmapatyānāmupari niviṣṭahārdo mahāsattvasteṣāṃ mīnānāṃ dānapriyavacanārthacaryādikramaiḥ paramanugrahaṃ cakāra /
body.translated_text: And that great being, his affection fixed upon those fish as upon his own beloved children, bestowed the highest favor upon them through the practices of giving, kind speech, beneficial action, and the like.

children.text: anyonyahiṃsāpraṇayaṃ niyacchanparasparaprema vivardhayaṃśca /
children.translated_text: Restraining their inclination toward mutual harm and fostering mutual affection,

children.text: yogādupāyajñatayā ca teṣāṃ vismārayāmāsa sa matsyavṛttam // Jm_15.2 //
children.translated_text: through effort and through his knowledge of skillful means, he caused them to forget the ways of fish. || Jm 15.2 ||

children.text: tattena samyakparipālyamānaṃ vṛddhiṃ parāṃ mīnakulaṃ jagāma /
children.translated_text: Thus, properly cared for by him, the fish-community attained supreme growth,

children.text: puraṃ vinirmuktamivopasargairnyāyapravṛttena narādhipena // Jm_15.3 //
children.translated_text: like a city freed from calamities by a righteous king. || Jm 15.3 ||

body.text: atha kadācitsattvānāṃ bhāgyasampadvaikalyātpramādācca varṣādhikṛtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ na samyagdevo vavarṣa / athāsamyagvarṣiṇi deve tatsaraḥ phullakadambakusumagaureṇa navasalilena na yathāpuramāpupūre / krameṇa copagate nidāghakālasamaye paṭutaradīptibhiḥ khedālasagatibhiriva ca dinakarakiraṇaistadabhitaptayā ca dharaṇyā jvālānugateneva ca hlādābhi lāṣiṇā mārutena tarṣavaśādiva pratyahamāpīyamānaṃ tatsaraḥ palvalībabhūva /
body.translated_text: Then, at a certain time, due to the deficiency of the beings' collective fortune and due to the negligence of the divine princes charged with rain, the gods did not rain properly. And as the gods did not rain properly, that lake was not filled with fresh water as before — water pale as the blossoms of the <s>Kadamba</s> tree in full bloom. And gradually, as the hot season arrived, with the sun's rays — more piercingly bright and moving as if sluggishly from the heat — and with the earth baking under them, and with the wind following the flames as if longing for coolness, that lake, as if being drunk daily out of thirst, became a puddle.

children.text: nidāghakāle jvalito vivasvāñjvālābhivarṣīva paṭuśca vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: In the hot season, the blazing sun, as if pouring down flames, and the fierce wind,

children.text: jvarāturevāśiśirā ca bhūmistoyāni roṣādiva śoṣayanti // Jm_15.4 //
children.translated_text: and the earth, hot as if from fever — they dry up the waters as if in rage. || Jm 15.4 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo vāyasagaṇairapi paritarkyamāṇaṃ prāgeva salilatīrāntacāribhiḥ pakṣigaṇairviṣādadainyavaśagaṃ vispanditamātraparāyaṇaṃ mīnakulamavekṣya karuṇāyamānaścintāmāpede / kaṣṭā bateyamāpadāpatitā mīnānām /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing the fish-community being eyed even by flocks of crows — let alone by the waterbirds walking along the shore — fallen under the sway of despair and dejection, able only to twitch, was moved to compassion and fell into reflection: "Alas, what a terrible calamity has befallen the fish!

children.text: pratyahaṃ kṣīyate toyaṃ spardhamānamivāyuṣā /
children.translated_text: "The water diminishes day by day, as if vying with [our] lifespan;

children.text: adyāpi ca cireṇaiva lakṣyate jaladāgamaḥ // Jm_15.5 //
children.translated_text: and even now, the arrival of rain-clouds is seen [to be] a long way off. || Jm 15.5 ||

children.text: apayānakramo nāsti netāpyanyatra ko bhavet /
children.translated_text: "There is no course of retreat, nor is there any other leader;

children.text: asmadvyasanasaṃkṛṣṭāḥ samāyānti ca no dviṣaḥ // Jm_15.6 //
children.translated_text: and our enemies, drawn by our distress, approach us. || Jm 15.6 ||

children.text: asya niḥsaṃśayamime toyaśeṣasya saṃkṣayāt /
children.translated_text: "Without a doubt, as the remainder of this water is exhausted,

children.text: sphuranto bhakṣayiṣyante śatrubhirmama paśyataḥ // Jm_15.7 //
children.translated_text: these [fish], thrashing about, will be devoured by enemies before my very eyes. || Jm 15.7 ||

body.text: tatkimatra prāptakālaṃ syāditi vimṛśansa mahātmā satyādhiṣṭhānamekamārtāyanaṃ dadarśa / karuṇayā ca samāpīḍyamānahṛdayo dīrghamuṣṇamabhiniśvasya nabhaḥ samullokayannavāca -

children.text: smarāmi na prāṇivadhaṃ yathāhaṃ sañcintya kṛcchre parame 'pi kartum /
anena satyena sarāṃsi toyairāpūrayanvarṣatu devarājaḥ // Jm_15.8 //

body.text: atha tasya mahātmanaḥ puṇyopacayaguṇātsatyādhiṣṭhānabalāttadabhiprasāditadevanāgayakṣānubhāvācca samantatastoyābalambibimbā gambhīramadhuranirghoṣā vidyullatālaṅkṛtanīlavipulaśikharā vijṛmbhamāṇā iva pravisarpibhiḥ śikharabhujaiḥ pariṣvajamānā iva cānyonyamakālameghāḥ kālameghāḥ prādurabhavan /

children.text: diśāṃ pramiṇvanta iva prayāmaṃ śṛṅgairvitanvanta ivāndhakāram /
nabhastalādarśagatā virejuśchāyā girīṇāmiva kālameghāḥ // Jm_15.9 //
saṃsaktakekaiḥ śikhibhiḥ prahṛṣṭaiḥ saṃstūyamānā iva nṛttacitraiḥ /
prasaktamandrastanitā virejurdhīraprahāsādiva te ghanaughāḥ // Jm_15.10 //
muktā vimuktā iva tairvimuktā dhārā nipetuḥ praśaśāma reṇuḥ /
gandhaścacārānibhṛto dharaṇyāṃ vikīryamāṇo jaladānilena // Jm_15.11 //
nidāghasamparkavivardhito 'pi tirobabhūvārkakaraprabhāvaḥ /
phenāvalīvyākulamekhalāni toyāni nimnābhimukhāni sasruḥ // Jm_15.12 //
muhurmuhuḥ kāñcanapiñjarābhirbhābhirdigantānanurañjayantī /
payodatūryasvanalabdhaharṣā vidyullatā nṛttamivācacāra // Jm_15.13 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samantato 'bhiprasṛtairāpāṇḍubhiḥ salilapravāhairāpūryamāṇe sarasi dhārānipātasamakālameva vidrute vāyasādye pakṣigaṇe pratilabdhajīvitāśe ca pramudite mīnagaṇe prītyābhisāryamāṇahṛdayo varṣanivṛttisāśaṅkaḥ punaḥ punaḥ parjanyamābabhāṣe -

children.text: udgarja parjanya gabhīradhīraṃ pramodamudvāsaya vāyasānām /
ratnāyamānāni payāṃsi varṣansaṃsaktavidyujjvalitadyutīni // Jm_15.14 //

body.text: tadupaśrutya śakro devānāmindraḥ paramavismitamanāḥ sākṣādabhigamyainamabhisaṃrādhayannuvāca -

children.text: tavaiva khalveṣa mahānubhāva matsyendra satyātiśayaprabhāvaḥ /
āvarjitā yatkalaśā iveme kṣaranti ramyastanitāḥ payodāḥ // Jm_15.15 //
mahatpramādaskhalitaṃ tvidaṃ me yannāma kṛtyeṣu bhavadvidhānām /
lokārthamabhyudyatamānasānāṃ vyāpārayogaṃ na samabhyupaimi // Jm_15.16 //
cintāṃ kṛthā mā tadataḥ paraṃ tvaṃ satāṃ hi kṛtyodvahane 'smi dhuryaḥ /
deśo 'pyayaṃ tvadguṇasaṃśrayeṇa bhūyaśca naivaṃ bhavitārtivaśyaḥ // Jm_15.17 //

body.text: ityevaṃ priyavacanaiḥ saṃrādhya tatraivāntardadhe / tacca saraḥ parāṃ toyasamṛddhimavāpa /
tadevaṃ śīlavatāmihaivābhiprāyāḥ kalyāṇāḥ samṛdhyanti prāgeva paratreti śīlaviśuddhau prayatitavyam /
iti matsyajātakaṃ pañcadaśam /
16. Vartakāpītakajātakam
satyaparibhāvitāṃ vācamagnirapi na prasahate laṅghayitumiti satyavacane 'bhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvaḥ kilānyatamasminnaraṇyāyatane vartakāpotako bhavati sma / sa katipayarātrodbhinnāṇḍakośaḥ pravirokṣyamāṇataruṇapakṣaḥ paridurbalatvādalakṣyamāṇāṅgapratyaṅgapradeśaḥ svamātāpitṛprayatnaracite tṛṇagahanopagūḍhe gulmalatāsaṃniśrite nīḍe saṃbahulairbhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ prativasati sma / tadavastho 'pi cāpariluptadharmasaṃjñatvānmātāpitṛbhyāmupahṛtānprāṇino necchati smābhyavahartum / yadeva tvasya tṛṇabījanyagrodhaphalādyupajahraturmātāpitarau tenaiva vartayāmāsa / tasya tayā rūkṣālpāhāratayā na kāyaḥ puṣṭimupayayau / nāpi pakṣau samyakpravirurohatuḥ / itare tu vartakāpotakā yathopanītamāhāramabhyavaharanto balavantaḥ sañjātapakṣāśca babhūvuḥ / dharmatā hyeṣā yaduta -

children.text: dharmādharmanirāśaṅkaḥ sarvāśī sukhamedhate /
dharmyāṃ tu vṛttimanvicchanvicitāśīha duḥkhitaḥ // Jm_16.1 //

body.text: [api coktaṃ bhagavatā - sujīvitamahrīkeṇeti gāthādvayam /

children.text: sujīvitamahrīkeṇa dhvāṅkṣeṇāśucikarmaṇā /
praskandinā pragalbhena susaṃkliṣṭaṃ tu jīvitam // Jm_16.2 //
hrīmatā tviha durjīvaṃ nityaṃ śucigaveṣiṇā /
saṃlīnenāpragalbhena śuddhājīvena jīvatā // Jm_16.3 //

body.text: iti gāthādvayametadāryasthāvirīyakanikāye paṭhyate / teṣāmevamavasthānāṃ nātidūre mahānvanadāvaḥ pratibhayaprasaktaninado vijṛmbhamāṇadhūmarāśirvikīryamāṇajvālāvalīlolavisphuliṅgaḥ santrāsano vanacarāṇāmanayo vanagahanānāṃ prādurabhavat /

children.text: sa mārutādhūrṇitaviprakīrṇairjvālābhujairnṛttaviśeṣacitraiḥ /
valganniva vyākuladhūmakeśaḥ sasvāna teṣāṃ dhṛtimādadānaḥ // Jm_16.4 //
caṇḍānilāsphālanacañcalāni bhayadrutānīva vane tṛṇāni /
so 'gniḥ sasaṃrambha ivābhipatya sphuratsphuliṅgaprakaro dadāha // Jm_16.5 //
bhayadrutodbhrāntavihaṅgasārthaṃ paribhramadbhītamṛgaṃ samantāt /
dhūmaughamagnaṃ paṭuvahniśabdaṃ vanaṃ tadārtyeva bhṛśaṃ rarāsa // Jm_16.6 //

body.text: krameṇa cotpīḍyamāna iva sa vahniḥ paṭunā mārutena tṛṇagahanānusārī teṣāṃ nīḍasamīpamupajagāma / atha te vartakāpotakā bhayavirasavyākulavirāvāḥ parasparanirapekṣāḥ sahasā samutpetuḥ / paridurbalatvādasañjātapakṣatvācca bodhisattvastu notpatituṃ prayatnaṃ cakāra / viditātmaprabhāvastvasaṃbhrānta eva sa mahāsattvaḥ sarabhasamivopasarpantamagniṃ sānunayamityuvāca -

children.text: vyarthābhidhānacaraṇo 'smyavirūḍhapakṣastvatsambhramācca pitarāvapi me praḍīnau /
tvadyogyamasti na ca kiñcidihātitheyamasmānnivartitumatastava yuktamagne // Jm_16.7 //

body.text: ityukte satyaparibhāvitavacasā tena mahāsattvena -

children.text: udīryamāṇo 'pyanilena so 'gnirviśuṣkasaṃsaktatṛṇe 'pi kakṣe /
nadīmiva prāpya vivṛddhatoyāṃ tadvācamāsādya śaśāma sadyaḥ // Jm_16.8 //
adyāpi taṃ himavati prathitaṃ pradeśaṃ dāvāgniruddhataśikho 'pi samīraṇena /
mantrābhiśapta iva naikaśirā bhujaṅgaḥ saṅkocamandalulitārcirupaiti śāntim // Jm_16.9 //

body.text: tatkimidamupanītamiti? ucyate -

children.text: velāmiva pracalitormiphaṇaḥ samudraḥ śikṣāṃ munīndravihitāmiva satyakāmaḥ /
satyātmanāmiti na laṅghayituṃ yadājñāṃ śaktaḥ kṛśānurapi satyamato na jahyāt // Jm_16.10 //

body.text: tadevaṃ satyavacanaparibhāvitāṃ vācamagnirapi na prasahate laṅghayitumiti satyavacane 'bhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyamiti /
iti vartakāpotakajātakaṃ ṣoḍaśam /
17. Kumbhajātakam
anekadoṣopasṛṣṭamatikaṣṭaṃ madyapānamiti sādhavaḥ paramapyasmādvārayanti prāgevātmānamiti / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvaḥ kila karuṇātiśayaparibhāvitamatiḥ parahitasukhopapādanaparaḥ puṇyāṃ pratipadamudbhāvayandānadamasaṃyamādibhiḥ kadācicchakrā devānāmindro babhūva / sa prakarṣiṇāmapi divyānāṃ viṣayasukhānāṃ nikāmalābhī sannapi karuṇāvaśagatvānnaiva lokārthacaryāsamudyogaśithilaṃ manaścakāra /

children.text: prāyeṇa lakṣmīmadiropayogājjāgarti naivātmahite 'pi lokaḥ /
surendralakṣmyāpi tu nirmado 'sāvabhūtparārtheṣvapi jāgarūkaḥ // Jm_17.1 //
anekatīvravyasanātureṣu sattveṣu bandhuṣviva jātahārdaḥ /
dhairyātsvabhāvajñatayāśritaśca nāsau visasmāra parārthacaryām // Jm_17.2 //

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahātmā manuṣyalokamavalokayannanukampāsamāvarjitena maitrasnigdhena svabhāvamahatā cakṣuṣā dadarśa sarvamitraṃ nāma rājānamakalyāṇamitrasaṃparkadoṣāt sapaurajānapadaṃ madyapānaprasaṅgābhimukham / tatra cāsyādoṣadarśitāmavekṣya mahādoṣatāṃ ca madyapānasya sa mahātmā mahatyā karuṇayā samāpīḍyamānahṛdayaścintāmāpede / kaṣṭā bateyamāpadāpatitā lokasya /

children.text: pramukhasvādu pānaṃ hi doṣadarśanaviklavān /
śreyaso 'paharatyeva ramaṇīyamivāpatham // Jm_17.3 //

body.text: tatkimatra prāptakālaṃ syāt? bhavatu dṛṣṭam /

children.text: pradhānabhūtasya viceṣṭitāni jano 'nukartuṃ niyatasvabhāvaḥ /
ityatra rājaiva cikitsanīyaḥ śubhāśubhaṃ tatprabhavaṃ hi loke // Jm_17.4 //

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahāsattvastaptakāñcanavarṇamāparuṣodgrathitajaṭāviṭapadharaṃ valkalājinasaṃvītamojasvi brāhmaṃ vapurabhinirmāya surāpūrṇaṃ ca vāmapārśvasthaṃ nātibṛhantaṃ kumbhaṃ sarvamitrasya rājñaḥ

pariṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇasya prastāvopanatāsu pravṛttāsu surāsavaśīdhumaireyamadhukathāsu purato 'ntarikṣe prādurabhūt / vismayabahumānāvarjitena ca prāñjalinā tena janenābhyutthāya pratyarcyamānaḥ sajala iva jaladharo gambhīramabhi dannuccairuvāca -

children.text: puṣpamālāhasatkaṇṭhamimaṃ bharitamākaṇṭham /
avataṃsakṛtākumbhaṃ kretumicchati kaḥ kumbham // Jm_17.5 //
savalayamiva puṣpamālayā pravitatayānilakampalīlayā /
kisalayaracanāsamutkaṭaṃ ghaṭamimamicchati kaḥ krayeṇa vaḥ // Jm_17.6 //

body.text: athainaṃ sa rājā vismayāvarjitakautūhalaḥ sabahumānamīkṣamāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliruvāca -

children.text: dīptyā navārka iva cārutayā śaśīva saṃlakṣyase ca vapuṣānyatamo munīnām /
tadvaktumarhasi yathā vidito 'si loke saṃbhāvanā hi guṇatastvayi no vicitrā // Jm_17.7 //

body.text: śakra uvāca -

children.text: paścādapi jñāsyasi yo 'hamasmi ghaṭaṃ tvidaṃ kretumito ghaṭasva /
na ced bhayaṃ te paralokaduḥkhādihaiva tīvravyasanāgamādvā // Jm_17.8 //

body.text: rājovāca - apūrvaḥ khalvayamatrabhavataḥ paśya vikrayārambhaḥ /

children.text: guṇasaṃvarṇanaṃ nāma doṣāṇāṃ ca nigūhanam /
prasiddha iti lokasya paṇyānāṃ vikrayakramaḥ // Jm_17.9 //
yukto vānṛtabhīrūṇāṃ tvadvidhānāmayaṃ vidhiḥ /
na hi kṛcchre 'pi saṃtyaktuṃ satyamicchanti sādhavaḥ // Jm_17.10 //
tadācakṣva mahābhāga pūrṇaḥ kasya ghaṭo nvayam /
kiṃ vā vinimaye prāpyamasmattastvādṛśairapi // Jm_17.11 //

body.text: śakra uvāca - śrūyatāṃ mahārāja

nāyaṃ toyadavicyutasya payasaḥ pūrṇo na tīrthāmbhasaḥ
kaiñjalkasya sugandhino na madhunaḥ sarpirviśeṣasya vā /
na kṣīrasya vijṛmbhamāṇakumudavyabhrendupādacchaveḥ
pūrṇaḥ pāpamayasya yasya tu ghaṭastasya prabhāvaṃ śṛṇu // Jm_17.12 //

children.text: yatpītvā madadoṣavihvalatayā svatantraścaran
deśeṣvaprapateṣvapi prapatito mandaprabhāvasmṛtiḥ /
bhakṣyābhakṣyavicāraṇāvirahitastattatsamāsvādayet
tatsaṃpūrṇamimaṃ gataṃ krayapathaṃ krīṇīta kumbhādhamam // Jm_17.13 //
anīśaḥ sve citte vicarati yayā saṃhṛtamatir
dviṣāṃ hāsāyāmaṃ samupajanayangauriva jaḍaḥ /
sadomadhye nṛtyetsvamukhapaṭahenāpi ca yayā
krayārhā seyaṃ vaḥ śubhavirahitā kumbhanihitā // Jm_17.14 //
pītvocitāmapi jahāti yathātmalajjāṃ
nirgranthavadvasanasaṃyamakhedamuktaḥ /
dhīraṃ caretpathiṣu paurajanākuleṣu
sā paśyatāmupagatā nihitātra kumbhe // Jm_17.15 //
yatpītvā vamathusamudgatānnaliptā
niḥśaṅkaiḥ śvabhiravalihyamānavaktrāḥ /
niḥsaṃjñā nṛpatipathiṣvapi svapanti
prakṣiptaṃ krayasubhagaṃ tadatra kumbhe // Jm_17.16 //
upayujya yanmadabalādabalā vinibandhayedapi tarau pitarau /
gaṇayecca sā dhanapatiṃ na patiṃ tadidaṃ ghaṭe vinihitaṃ nihitam // Jm_17.17 //
yāṃ pītavanto madaluptasaṃjñā vṛṣṇyandhakā vismṛtabandhubhāvāḥ /
parasparaṃ niṣpipiṣurgadābhirunmādanī sā nihiteha kumbhe // Jm_17.18 //
yatra prasaktāni kulāni neśurlakṣmīniketānyuditoditāni /
ucchedanī vittavatāṃ kulānāṃ seyaṃ ghaṭe krayyatayādhirūḍhā // Jm_17.19 //
aniyataruditasthitavihasitavāgjaḍagurunayano grahavaśaga iva /
paribhavabhavanaṃ bhavati ca niyataṃ yadupahatamatistadidamiha ghaṭe // Jm_17.20 //
pravayaso 'pi yadākulacetanāḥ svahitamārgasamāśrayakātarāḥ /
bahu vadantyasamīkṣitaniścayaṃ krayapathena gataṃ tadidaṃ ghaṭe // Jm_17.21 //
yasyā doṣātpūrvadevāḥ pramattā lakṣmīmoṣaṃ devarājādavāpya /
trāṇāpekṣāstoyarāśau mamajjustasyāḥ pūrṇaṃ kumbhametaṃ vṛṇīta // Jm_17.22 //
brūyādasatyamapi satyamiva pratītaḥ kuryādakāryamapi kāryamiva prahṛṣṭaḥ /
yasyā guṇena sadasatsadasacca vidyācchāpasya mūrtiriva sā nihiteha kumbhe // Jm_17.23 //
unmādavidyāṃ vyasanapratiṣṭhāṃ sākṣādalakṣmīṃ jananīmaghānām /
advaitasiddhāṃ kalipaddhatiṃ tāṃ krīṇīta ghorāṃ manasastamistrām // Jm_17.24 //
parimuṣitamatiryayā nihanyādapi pitaraṃ jananīmanāgasaṃ vā /
avigaṇitasukhāyatiryatiṃ vā krayavidhinā nṛpa tāmito gṛhāṇa // Jm_17.25 //
evaṃvidhaṃ madyamidaṃ narendra sureti loke prathitaṃ surābha /
na pakṣapāto 'sti guṇeṣu yasya sa kretumudyogamidaṃ karotu // Jm_17.26 //
niṣevya yadduścaritaprasaktāḥ patanti bhīmānnarakaprapātān /
tiryaggatiṃ pretadaridratāṃ ca ko nāma taddraṣṭumapivyavasyet // Jm_17.27 //
laghurapi ca vipāko madyapānasya yaḥ syānmanujagatigatānāṃ śīladṛṣṭīḥ sa hanti /
jvalitadahanaraudre yena bhūyo 'pyavīcau nivasati pitṛloke hīnatiryakṣu caiva // Jm_17.28 //
śīlaṃ nimīlayati hanti yaśaḥ prasahya lajjāṃ nirasyati matiṃ malinīkaroti /
yannāma pītamupahanti guṇāṃśca tāṃstāṃstatpātumarhasi kathaṃ nṛpa madyamadya // Jm_17.29 //

body.text: atha sā rājā taistasya hṛdayagrāhakairhetumadbhirvacobhiravagamitamadyapānadoṣo madyaprasaṅgādapavṛttābhilāṣaḥ śakramityuvāca -

children.text: snigdhaḥ pitā vinayabhaktiguṇād gururvā yadvaktumarhati nayānayavinmunirvā /
tāvattvayā svabhihitaṃ hitakāmyayā metatkarmaṇā vidhivadarcayituṃ yatiṣye // Jm_17.30 //

body.text: idaṃ ca tāvatsubhāṣitapratipūjanamarhati no 'trabhavān pratigrahītum /

children.text: dadāmi te grāmavarāṃśca pañca dāsīśataṃ pañca gavāṃ śatāni /
sadaśvayuktāṃśca rathāndaśemānhitasya vaktā hi gururmamāsi // Jm_17.31 //

body.text: yadvā mayānyatkaraṇīyaṃ tatsaṃdeśādarhatyatrabhavānbhūyo 'pi māmanugrahītum /
śakra uvāca -

children.text: artho 'sti na grāmavarādinā me surādhipaṃ māmabhigaccha rājan /
saṃpūjanīyastu hitasya vaktā vākpragraheṇa pratipanmayena // Jm_17.32 //
ayaṃ hi panthā yaśasaḥ śriyaśca paratra saukhyasya ca tasya tasya /
apāsya tasmānmadirāprasaṅgaṃ dharmāśrayānmadviṣayaṃ bhajasva // Jm_17.33 //

body.text: ityuktvā śakrastatraivāntardadhe / sa ca rājā sapaurajānapado madyapānādvirarāma /
tadevamanekadoṣopasṛṣṭamatikaṣṭaṃ madyapānamiti sādhavaḥ paramasmādvārayanti prāgevātmānamiti / evaṃ lokahitaḥ pūrvajanmasvapi sa bhagavāniti tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyam /
iti kumbhajātakaṃ saptadaśam /
18. Aputrajātakam
śīlapraśamapratipakṣasaṃbādhaṃ gārhasthyamityevamātmakāmā na rocayante / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃścidibhyakule ślāghanīyavṛttacāritrasaṃpanne prārthanīyasaṃbandhe kulodbhavānāṃ nipānabhūte śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ kośakoṣṭhāgāranirviśeṣe mitrasvajanānāmabhigamanīye kṛpaṇavanīpakānāmupajīvye śilpijanasyāspadabhūte lakṣmyā dattānugrahasatkāre rājño lokābhisaṃmate janma pratilebhe / sa kālānāmatyayenābhivṛddhaḥ kṛtaśramo lokābhimateṣu vidyāsthāneṣvaparokṣabuddhirvividhavikalpāśrayāsu kalāsu jananayanakāntena ca vapuṣā dharmāvirodhinyā ca lokajñatayā svajana iva lokasya hṛdayeṣu paryavartata /

children.text: na hi svajana ityeva svajano bahu manyate /
jano vā jana ityeva svajanād dṛśyate 'nyathā // Jm_18.1 //
guṇadoṣābhimarśāttu bahumānāvamānayoḥ /
vrajatyāspadatāṃ lokaḥ svajanasya janasya vā // Jm_18.2 //

body.text: kṛtapravrajyāparicayatvāttu tasya mahāsattvasya

children.text: paryeṣṭiduḥkhānugatāṃ viditvā gṛhasthatāṃ dharmavirodhinīṃ ca /
sukhodayatvaṃ ca tapovanānāṃ na gehasaukhyeṣu manaḥ sasañje // Jm_18.3 //

body.text: sa mātāpitroḥ kālakriyayā saṃvignahṛdayastamanekaśatasahasrasaṃkhyaṃ gṛhavibhavasāraṃ mitrasvajanakṛpaṇaśramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo yathārhamatisṛjya pravavrāja / so 'nupūrveṇa grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣvanuvicarannanyatamanagaramupaśritya kasmiṃścidvanaprasthe nivasati sma / sa dhyānaguṇābhyāsāt sātmībhūtenākṛtakenendriyaprasādena śrutihṛdayāhlādinā ca vidvattāsūcakenānutsiktena vigatalābhāśākārpaṇyadainyena vinayaujasvinā yathārhamadhuropacārasauṣṭhavena dharmādharmavibhāganipuṇena ca vacasā pravrajitācāraśībharayā (ca) sajjaneṣṭayā ceṣṭayā tatrābhilakṣito babhūva / kautūhalinā ca janena samupalabdhakulapravrajyākramaḥ suṣṭhutaraṃ lokasaṃmatastatrābhūt /

children.text: ādeyataratāṃ yānti kularūpaguṇād guṇāḥ /
āśrayātiśayeneva candrasya kiraṇāṅkarāḥ // Jm_18.4 //

body.text: athāsya tatrābhigamanamupalabhya pitṛvayasyaḥ samabhigamya cainaṃ guṇabahumānāt kuśalaparipraśnapūrvakaṃ cāsmai nivedyātmānaṃ pitṛvayasyatāṃ ca saṃkathāprastāvāgatamenaṃ snehāduvāca - cāpalamiva khalvidamanuvartitaṃ bhadantenānapekṣya kulavaṃśamasmin vayasi pravrajatā /

children.text: ārādhyate satpratipattimadbhirdharmo yadāyaṃ bhavane vane vā /
śrīmanti hitvā bhavanānyatastvaṃ kasmādaraṇyeṣu matiṃ karoṣi // Jm_18.5 //
paraprasādārjitabhaikṣavṛttiragaṇyamānaḥ khalavajjanena /
kucelabhṛdbandhusuhṛdvihīno vanāntabhūmāvapaviddhakāyaḥ // Jm_18.6 //
mūrtaṃ daridratvamivopaguhya kathaṃ nu śokasya vaśaṃ prayāsi /
imāmavasthāṃ hi tavekṣamāṇā dviṣo 'pi bāṣpāpihitekṣaṇāḥ syuḥ // Jm_18.7 //
tadehi pitryaṃ bhavanaṃ tavedaṃ śrutārthasāraṃ bhavatāpi nūnam /
saṃpādayethā nivasaṃstvamatra dharmaṃ ca satputramanorathaṃ ca // Jm_18.8 //

body.text: lokapravādaḥ khalvapi caiṣaḥ

children.text: parakarmakarasyāpi sve nipānasukhā gṛhāḥ /
kiṃ punaḥ sukhasaṃprāptāḥ samṛddhijvalitaśriyaḥ // Jm_18.9 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pravivekasukhāmṛtarasaparibhāvitamatistatpravaṇahṛdayaḥ samupalabdhaviśeṣo gṛhavanavāsayoḥ kāmopabhoganimantraṇāyāṃ tṛpta iva bhojanakathāyāmasukhāyamāna uvāca -

children.text: idaṃ snehodgatatvātte kāmamalpātyayaṃ vacaḥ /
sukhasaṃjñāṃ tu mā kārṣīḥ kadācidgṛhacārake // Jm_18.10 //
gārhasthyaṃ mahadasvāsthyaṃ sadhanasyādhanasya vā /
ekasya rakṣaṇāyāsāditarasyārjanaśramāt // Jm_18.11 //
yatra nāma sukhaṃ naiva sadhanasyādhanasya vā /
tatrābhiratisaṃmohaḥ pāpasyaiva phalodayaḥ // Jm_18.12 //

body.text: yadapi ceṣṭaṃ gṛhasthenāpi śakyamayamārādhayituṃ dharma iti kāmamevametat / atiduṣkaraṃ tu me pratibhāti dharmapratipakṣasaṃbādhatvācchramabāhulyācca gṛhasya / paśyatu bhavān /

children.text: gṛhā nānīhamānasya na caivāvadato mṛṣā /
na cānikṣiptadaṇḍasya pareṣāmanikurvataḥ // Jm_18.13 //

body.text: tadayaṃ gṛhasukhāvabaddhahṛdayastatsādhanodyatamatirjanaḥ /

children.text: yadi dharmamupaiti nāsti gehamatha gehābhimukhaḥ kuto 'sya dharmaḥ /
praśamaikaraso hi dharmamārgo gṛhasiddhiśca parākramakrameṇa // Jm_18.14 //
iti dharmavirodhadūṣitatvād gṛhavāsaṃ ka ivātmavān bhajeta /
paribhūya sukhāśayā hi dharmaṃ niyamo nāsti sukhodayaprasiddhau // Jm_18.15 //
children.translated_text: for by disregarding <s>Dharma</s> out of desire for happiness, there is no certainty of obtaining happiness." || Jm 18.15 ||

children.text: niyataṃ ca yaśaḥparābhavaḥ syādanutāpo manasaśca durgatiśca /
children.translated_text: "And there would certainly be destruction of fame, remorse of mind, and a wretched destiny;

children.text: iti dharmavirodhinaṃ bhajante na sukhopāyamapāyavannayajñāḥ // Jm_18.16 //
children.translated_text: thus, those ignorant of statecraft embrace what is opposed to <s>Dharma</s>, not as a means to happiness, but as one leading to ruin." || Jm 18.16 ||

body.text: api ca, sukho gṛhavāsa iti śraddhāgamyamidaṃ me pratibhāti /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, 'household life is pleasant' — this seems to me a matter to be accepted on faith alone;

children.text: niyatārjanarakṣaṇādiduḥkhe vadhabandhavyasanaikalakṣyabhūte /
children.translated_text: "in what is certainly filled with the suffering of acquiring, guarding, and the like, and is the sole target of slaughter, bondage, and calamity,

children.text: nṛpaterapi yatra nāsti tṛptirvibhavaistoyanidherivāmbuvarṣaiḥ // Jm_18.17 //
children.translated_text: where even a king finds no satisfaction with his riches, like the ocean with rainfalls —" || Jm 18.17 ||

children.text: sukhamatra kutaḥ kathaṃ kadā vā parikalpapraṇayaṃ na cedupaiti /
children.translated_text: "whence, how, and when could there be happiness here, unless one approaches it with the affection of imagination?

children.text: viṣayopaniveśane 'pi mohād vraṇakaṇḍūyanavatsukhābhimānaḥ // Jm_18.18 //
children.translated_text: Even in the indulgence of sense-pleasures, through delusion, there is a conceit of happiness, like the scratching of a wound." || Jm 18.18 ||

body.text: bāhulyena ca khalu bravīmi -
body.translated_text: "And I say this at length —

children.text: prāyaḥ samṛddhyā madameti gehe mānaṃ kulenāpi balena darpam /
children.translated_text: "Generally, in the household, prosperity leads to intoxication, family to pride, strength to arrogance,

children.text: duḥkhena roṣaṃ vyasanena dainyaṃ tasminkadā syātpraśamāvakāśaḥ // Jm_18.19 //
children.translated_text: suffering to anger, misfortune to wretchedness — when would there be any occasion for tranquility in it?" || Jm 18.19 ||

body.text: ataśca khalvahamatrabhavantamanunayāmi -
body.translated_text: "And therefore indeed I entreat your honor —

children.text: madamānamohabhujagopalayaṃ praśamābhirāmasukhavipralayam /
children.translated_text: "Who would resort to a dwelling that is a den of the serpents of intoxication, pride, and delusion, that is the destruction of the happiness delightful in tranquility,

children.text: ka ivāśrayedabhimukhaṃ vilayaṃ bahutīvraduḥkhanilayaṃ nilayam // Jm_18.20 //
children.translated_text: that faces dissolution, and is an abode of much intense suffering?" || Jm 18.20 ||

children.text: saṃtuṣṭajanagehe tu praviviktasukhe vane /
children.translated_text: "But in the forest, where the contented dwell, in the happiness of solitude,

children.text: prasīdati yathā cetastridive 'pi tathā kutaḥ // Jm_18.21 //
children.translated_text: the mind finds such serenity as is not found even in heaven." || Jm 18.21 ||

children.text: paraprasādārjitavṛttirapyato rame vanānteṣu kucelasaṃvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, though living on alms obtained by the grace of others, I delight in the forest's edge, clad in rags;

children.text: adharmamiśraṃ tu sukhaṃ na kāmaye viṣeṇa saṃpṛktamivānnamātmavān // Jm_18.22 //
children.translated_text: but happiness mixed with unrighteousness I do not desire, like a self-possessed person [does not desire] food mixed with poison." || Jm 18.22 ||

body.text: ityavagamitamatiḥ sa tena pitṛvayasyo hṛdayagrāhakeṇa vacasā bahumānameva tasminmahāsattve satkāraprayogaviśeṣeṇa pravedayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Having had his mind thus informed, that friend of his father, through those captivating words, expressed his esteem for that great being through extraordinary acts of reverence.

body.text:
tadevaṃ śīlapraśamapratipakṣasaṃbādhaṃ gārhasthyamityevamātmakāmāḥ parityajantīti /
labdhāsvādāḥ praviveke, na kāmeṣvāvartanta iti pravivekaguṇakathāyāmapyupaneyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, those who care for their own welfare renounce household life, which is hemmed in by the adversaries of moral conduct and tranquility. Those who have tasted the flavor of solitude do not turn back to sense-pleasures — this [story] is also to be cited in a discourse on the virtues of solitude.

body.text: ityaputrajātakamaṣṭādaśam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth [story], the <s>Aputra Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 19. Bisajātakam
body.translated_text: 19. The <s>Bisa Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Lotus-Root)

body.text: pravivekasukharasajñānāṃ viḍambaneva vihiṃseva ca kāmāḥ pratikūlā bhavanti / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: For those who know the flavor of the happiness of solitude, sense-pleasures are repugnant, like mockery or injury. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila kasmiṃścinmahati guṇaprakāśayaśasi vācyadoṣavirahite brāhmaṇakule janmaparigrahaṃ cakāra / tasya yatra kanīyāṃsaḥ ṣaḍapare bhrātarastadanurūpaguṇāḥ snehabahumānaguṇānnityānuguṇā babhūvuḥ, saptamī ca bhaginī / sa kṛtaśramaḥ sāṅgeṣu sopavedeṣu vedeṣu samadhigatavidyāyaśāḥ saṃmato jagati daivatavanmātāpitarau parayā bhaktyā paricarannācārya iva piteva tānbhrātṝnvidyāsu vinayannayavinayakuśalo gṛhamāvasati sma / sa kālakramānmātāpitroḥ kālakriyayā saṃvignahṛdayaḥ kṛtvā tayoḥ pretakṛtyāni vyatīteṣu śokamayeṣviva keṣucideva divaseṣu tānbhrātṝn saṃnipātyovāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took birth in a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family of illustrious virtue-born fame, free from any fault of reproach. He had six younger brothers of corresponding virtues, who through the qualities of affection and respect were always in harmony with him, and also a seventh, a sister. Having completed his studies, learned in the <s>Vedas</s> together with their limbs and auxiliary texts, having attained fame for his learning, honored by the world, attending to his parents with supreme devotion as if they were deities, instructing those brothers in the sciences like a teacher and like a father, skilled in the training of conduct and policy — he dwelt in the household. In the course of time, upon the death of his parents, his heart filled with spiritual urgency, and having performed the funeral rites for them, after some days — which seemed steeped in grief — he gathered his brothers together and said —

children.text: eṣa lokasya niyataḥ śokātivirasaḥ kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This is the fixed course of the world, exceedingly bitter with grief:

children.text: saha sthitvāpi suciraṃ mṛtyunā yadviyojyate // Jm_19.1 //
children.translated_text: that even after dwelling together for a very long time, one is separated by death." || Jm 19.1 ||

children.text: tatpravrajitumicchāmi śreyaḥślādhyena vartmanā /
children.translated_text: "Therefore I wish to go forth on the praiseworthy path of spiritual welfare,

children.text: purā mṛtyuripurhanti gṛhasaṃraktameva mām // Jm_19.2 //
children.translated_text: before death, the enemy, strikes me down while still attached to the household." || Jm 19.2 ||

body.text: yataḥ sarvāneva bhavataḥ sambodhayāmi / astyatra brāhmaṇakule dharmeṇa yathādhigatā vibhavamātrā / śakyamanayā vartitum / tatsarvaireva bhavadbhiḥ parasparaṃ snehagauravābhimukhaiḥ śīlasamudācāreṣvaśithilādarairvedādhyayanaparairmitrātithisvajanapraṇayavatsalairdhamaparāyaṇairbhūtva samyaggṛhamadhyāvastavyam /
body.translated_text: "Wherefore I inform all of you. There is in this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family a modest fortune rightfully acquired. It is possible to live on this. Therefore, let all of you, facing one another with affection and respect, unrelenting in the observance of moral conduct, devoted to the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, tender toward friends, guests, and kinsmen, devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, dwell properly in the household.

children.text: vinayaślāghibhirnityaṃ svādhyāyādhyayanodyataiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who take pride in discipline, ever devoted to study and recitation,

children.text: pradānābhirataiḥ samyakparipālyo gṛhāśramaḥ // Jm_19.3 //
children.translated_text: delighting in giving — by them the household life should be properly maintained." || Jm 19.3 ||

children.text: evaṃ hi vaḥ syādyaśasaḥ samṛddhirdharmasya cārthasya sukhāspadasya /
children.translated_text: "For thus you shall have an abundance of fame, of <s>Dharma</s> that is the foundation of happiness,

children.text: sukhāvagāhaśca paro 'pi lokastadapramattā gṛhamāvaseta // Jm_19.4 //
children.translated_text: and even the highest world shall be accessible — therefore dwell in the household without negligence." || Jm 19.4 ||

body.text: athāsya bhrātaraḥ pravrajyāsaṅkīrtanādviyogāśaṅkāvyathitamanasaḥ śokāśrudurdinamukhāḥ praṇamyainamūcuḥ - nārhatyatrabhavānpitṛviyogaśokaśalyavraṇamasaṃrūḍhameva no ghaṭṭayitumapareṇa duḥkhābhinipātakṣāreṇa /
body.translated_text: Then his brothers, their minds anguished by the apprehension of separation upon hearing the word 'renunciation,' their faces overcast with the clouds of tears of grief, bowing to him, said: "Your honor ought not to strike the wound of our grief at father's separation, not yet healed, with yet another poultice of suffering.

body.text: adyāpi tāvatpitṛśokaśalyakṣatāni rohanti na no manāṃsi /
body.translated_text: "Even now, the wounds of our grief for father have not healed in our hearts;

body.text: tatsādhvimāṃ saṃhara dhīra buddhiṃ mā naḥ kṣate kṣāramihopahārṣīḥ // Jm_19.5 //
body.translated_text: therefore, O steadfast one, well restrain this intention — do not apply salt to our wound here." || Jm 19.5 ||

children.text: athākṣamaṃ vetsi gṛhānurāgaṃ śreyaḥpathaṃ vā vanavāsasaukhyam /
children.translated_text: "But if you consider attachment to the household unbearable, or the path of spiritual welfare and the happiness of forest-dwelling [preferable],

children.text: asmānanāthānapahāya gehe kasmādvanaṃ vāñchasi gantumekaḥ // Jm_19.6 //
children.translated_text: why do you wish to go alone to the forest, abandoning us, protectorless, in the house?" || Jm 19.6 ||

body.text: tadyātrabhavato gatiḥ sāsmākam / vayamapi pravrajāma iti /
body.translated_text: "Wherever your honor goes, that is our [path] too. We too shall go forth."

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: anabhyāsādvivekasya kāmarāgānuvartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Because of unfamiliarity with solitude, and because of following the inclination of desire,

children.text: prapātamiva manyante pravrajyāṃ prāyaśo janāḥ // Jm_19.7 //
children.translated_text: people generally regard renunciation as a precipice." || Jm 19.7 ||

body.text: iti mayā nigṛhya nābhihitāḥ stha pravrajyāśrayaṃ prati jānatāpi gṛhavanavāsaviśeṣam / tadetaccedabhirucitaṃ bhavatāmeva pravrajāma iti / te saptāpi bhrātaro bhaginyaṣṭamāḥ sphītaṃ gṛhavibhavāsāramaśrumukhaṃ ca mitrasvajanabandhuvargaṃ vihāya tāpasapravrajyayā pravrajitāḥ / tadanuraktahṛdayaścainānsahāya eko dāsī dāsaścānupravrajitāḥ / te 'nyatarasminmahatyaraṇyāyatane jvalitamiva vikasitakamalavanaśobhayā vihasadiva ca phullakumudavanairanibhṛtamadhukaragaṇamamalanīlasalilaṃ mahatsaraḥ saṃniśritya praviviktamanojñāsu cchayādrumasamupagūḍhāsvasaṃnikṛṣṭaviniviṣṭāsu pṛthakpṛthakparṇaśālāsu vrataniyamaparā dhyānānuyuktamanaso vijahnaḥ / pañcame pañcame divase bodhisattvasamīpaṃ dharmaśravaṇārthamupajagmuḥ / sa caiṣāṃ dhyānopadeśapravṛttāṃ kāmādīnavadarśanīṃ saṃvejanīyāṃ pravivekasantoṣavarṇabahulāṃ kuhanalapanakausīdyādidoṣavigarhaṇīmupaśamaprasādapaddhatiṃ tāṃ tāṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ cakāra / sā cainān dāsī bahumānānurāgavaśā tathaiba paricacāra / sā tasmātsaraso bisānyuddhṛtya mahatsu padminīparṇeṣu śucau tīrapradeśe samānvinyasya ca bhāgānkāṣṭhasaṃghaṭṭanaśabdena kālaṃ nivedyāpakrāmati sma / tatasteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ kṛtajapahomavidhīnāṃ yathāvṛddhamekaiko 'bhigamya tato bisabhāgamekaikaṃ yathākramamādāya svasyāṃ svasyāṃ parṇaśālāyāṃ vidhivatparibhujya dhyānābhiyuktamatirvijahāra / ta evaṃ pravṛttā naiva parasparaṃ dadṛśuranyatra dharmaśravaṇakālāt /
body.translated_text: "It was with restraint that I did not address you regarding renunciation, even though I knew the distinction between household and forest life. But if this is agreeable to you — then let us all go forth." Then all seven brothers, with the sister as the eighth, abandoning the prosperous but insubstantial household wealth, and the tear-faced circle of friends, kinsmen, and relatives, went forth as ascetics. Following them, their hearts attached, one manservant and one maidservant also went forth. They settled near a great lake in a certain vast forest tract — a lake that seemed ablaze with the beauty of beds of blooming lotuses, that seemed to laugh with groves of blossoming night-lilies, its pure blue waters alive with swarms of bees — dwelling in separate leaf-huts, delightfully secluded, each nestled close together beneath shade-trees. Devoted to vows and discipline, their minds intent on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), they lived [there]. Every fifth day they came to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hermitage for the hearing of <s>Dharma</s>. And he delivered to them various discourses on the <s>Dharma</s>: teachings on <s>dhyāna</s>, expositions of the faults of sense-pleasures, discourses promoting spiritual urgency, rich in the praise of the contentment of solitude, and reproaching the faults of hypocrisy, idle talk, sloth, and the like — the path of tranquility and serenity. And that maidservant, moved by esteem and affection, served them in like manner. She would extract lotus-roots from that lake, arrange them in equal portions on large lotus-leaves on a clean spot on the bank, announce the time by the sound of striking sticks together, and then withdraw. Then those sages, having completed their recitations and fire-oblations, one by one in order of seniority, would come and take each one his portion of lotus-root, and having eaten it properly in his own leaf-hut, would dwell with his mind intent on meditation. Living thus, they never saw one another except at the time of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: teṣāmevaṃvidhena niravadyena śīlavṛttasamudācāreṇa pravivekābhiratyā dhyānapravaṇamānasatayā ca sarvatra yaśaḥ samupaśrutya śakro devānāmindrastatparīkṣānimittaṃ tatrābhijagāma / taccaiṣāṃ dhyānābhimukhatvaṃ kukāryeṣvaprasaṅgamanutkaṇṭhāṃ praśamābhirāmaṃ cāvasthānamavekṣya sthirataraguṇasambhāvanastatparīkṣānimittamavahitamanā babhūva /
body.translated_text: Having heard of their blameless conduct and moral observance, their delight in solitude, and their minds inclined toward meditation, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, came there to test them. And observing their devotion to meditation, their non-involvement in wrongful activities, their freedom from discontent, and their state of delighting in tranquility, esteeming them as possessing well-established virtues, he became attentive with the purpose of testing them.

children.text: anutsuko vanānteṣu vasañchamaparāyaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One who dwells without discontent in the forests, devoted to tranquility,

children.text: āropayati sādhūnāṃ guṇasambhāvanāṃ hṛdi // Jm_19.8 //
children.translated_text: causes the esteem of virtuous qualities to rise in the hearts of the good." || Jm 19.8 ||

body.text: atha dvipakalabhadaśanapāṇḍukomalāni samuddhṛtya prakṣālya ca bisāni marakataharitaprabheṣu padminīpatreṣu kamaladalakesaropahārālaṃkṛtānviracayya samānbhāgānkāṣṭhasaṃghaṭṭanaśabdena nivedya kālaṃ teṣāmṛṣīṇāmapasṛtāyāṃ tasyāṃ dāsyāṃ bodhisattvaparīkṣārthaṃ śakro devānāmindraḥ prathamameva bisabhāgamantardhāpayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, after that maidservant — having extracted lotus-roots as pale and soft as the tusks of a young elephant, washed them, arranged them in equal portions on lotus-leaves green as emerald, adorned with offerings of lotus-petal filaments, and having announced the time by the sound of striking sticks — had withdrawn, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in order to test the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, first of all made his portion of lotus-root disappear.

children.text: pravartane hi duḥkhasya tiraskāre sukhasya ca /
children.translated_text: "For in the occurrence of suffering and the removal of happiness,

children.text: dhairyaprayāmaḥ sādhūnāṃ visphuranniva gṛhyate // Jm_19.9 //
children.translated_text: the exertion of steadfastness in the virtuous is grasped as if flashing forth." || Jm 19.9 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo 'bhigataḥ prathame bisabhāgasthāne bisabhāgavirahitaṃ padminīpatraṃ parivyākulīkṛtopahāramabhisamīkṣya gṛhītaḥ kenāpi me bisapratyaṃśa ityavadhṛtamatirapetacetaḥsaṃkṣobhasaṃrambhastata eva pratinivṛtya praviśya parṇaśālāyāṃ yathocitaṃ dhyānavidhimārebhe / vaimanasyaparihārthaṃ cetareṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ tamarthaṃ na nivedayāmāsa / itare tvasya bhrātaro nūnamanena gṛhītaḥ pratyaṃśa iti manyamānā yathocitāneva svānsvānanukrameṇa bisabhāgānādāya yathāsvaṃ parṇaśālāsu paribhujya dhyāyanti sma / evaṃ dvitīye tṛtīye caturthe pañcame ca divase śakrastasya taṃ bisapratyaṃśamupanidadhe / bodhisattvo 'pi ca mahāsattvastathaiva niḥsaṃkṣobhapraśāntacitto babhūva /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having come to the place of the first portion and seeing the lotus-leaf bereft of its lotus-root portion, its offering disturbed, having concluded 'my lotus-root share has been taken by someone,' with his mind free from the agitation of disturbance and anger, turned back from that very place, entered his leaf-hut, and began his meditation practice as was his custom. To prevent distress among the other sages, he did not report the matter to them. The other brothers, thinking 'surely he has taken his share,' took their own lotus-root portions one after another in due order, ate them properly in their respective huts, and meditated. Thus on the second, third, fourth, and fifth day, <s>Śakra</s> concealed his lotus-root portion. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that great being, remained just as undisturbed and serene in mind.

children.text: manaḥsaṃkṣobha eveṣṭo mṛtyurnāyuḥkṣayaḥ satām /
children.translated_text: "Disturbance of mind itself is the death that matters to the virtuous, not the expiration of life;

children.text: jīvitārthe 'pi nāyānti manaḥkṣobhamato budhāḥ // Jm_19.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore, even for the sake of their life, the wise do not submit to mental agitation." || Jm 19.10 ||

body.text: athāparāhṇasamaye dharmaśravaṇārthamṛṣayaste yathocittaṃ bodhisattvasya parṇaśālāṃ samabhigatā dadṛśvāṃsaścainaṃ kṛśataraśarīraṃ parikṣāmakapolanayanaṃ parimlānavadanaśobhamasampūrṇasvaragāmbhīryaṃ parikṣīṇamapyaparikṣīṇadhairyapraśamaguṇamabhinavendupriyadarśanamupetyopacārapuraḥsaraṃ sasambhramāḥ kimidamiti kārśyanimittamenamapṛcchan / tebhyo bodhisattvastamarthaṃ yathānubhūtaṃ nivedayāmāsa / atha te tāpasāḥ parasparamīdṛśamanācāramasambhāvayantastatpīḍayā ca samupajātasaṃvegāḥ kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭamityuktvā vrīḍāvanatavadanāḥ samatiṣṭhanta / śakraprabhāvācca samāvṛtajñānagativiṣayāḥ kuta idamiti na niścayamupajagmuḥ / atha bodhisattvasyānujo bhrātā svamāvegamātmaviśuddhiṃ ca pradarśayañchapathātiśayamimaṃ cakāra -
body.translated_text: Then in the afternoon, those sages came as usual to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s leaf-hut for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and they saw him with an emaciated body, sunken cheeks and eyes, faded facial beauty, and with the depth of his voice diminished — yet though diminished [in body], his virtues of steadfastness and tranquility were undiminished, and he was lovely to behold like a new moon. Approaching with due courtesy, they asked him with alarm: "What is this?" — inquiring about the cause of his emaciation. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reported the matter to them just as he had experienced it. Then those ascetics, unable to imagine such misconduct among themselves, yet filled with distress at his suffering, saying "Alas, alas!" stood with their faces bowed in shame. And because their range of knowledge was obscured by <s>Śakra</s>'s power, they could not arrive at a certainty as to the source [of the theft]. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s next younger brother, displaying his own agitation and his innocence, made this extraordinary oath —

children.text: samṛddhicihnābharaṇaṃ sa gehaṃ prāpnotu bhāryāṃ ca mano 'bhirāmām /
children.translated_text: "May he obtain a house adorned with the marks of prosperity, and a wife delightful to the mind,

children.text: samagratāmetu ca putrapautrairbisāni te brāhmaṇa yo hyahārṣīt // Jm_19.11 //
children.translated_text: and may he be complete with sons and grandsons — he, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who has stolen your lotus-roots!" || Jm 19.11 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another said —

children.text: mālāḥ srajaścandanamaṃśukāni bibhradvibhūṣāśca sutābhimṛṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Wearing garlands, wreaths, sandalwood paste, and fine garments, and ornaments polished by the hands of women,

children.text: kāmeṣu tīvrāṃ sa karotvapekṣāṃ bisānyahārṣīddvijamukhya yaste // Jm_19.12 //
children.translated_text: may he feel intense longing for sense-pleasures — he, O foremost of sages, who stole your lotus-roots!" || Jm 19.12 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another said —

children.text: kṛṣyāśrayāvāptadhanaḥ kuṭumbī pramodamānastanayapralāpaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "A householder, possessing wealth obtained through agriculture, delighting in the prattle of children,

children.text: vayo 'pyapaśyanramatāṃ sa gehe bisāni yaste sakṛdapyahārṣīt // Jm_19.13 //
children.translated_text: heedless of passing age, may he take pleasure in the household — he who even once stole your lotus-roots!" || Jm 19.13 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another said —

children.text: narādhipairbhṛtyavinītaceṣṭairabhyarcyamāno natalolacūḍaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Honored by kings, with servants performing disciplined gestures, their crests bowing low,

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ mahīṃ pātu sa rājavṛttyā lobhādahārṣīttava yo bisāni // Jm_19.14 //
children.translated_text: may he rule the entire earth in royal splendor — he who out of greed stole your lotus-roots!" || Jm 19.14 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another said —

children.text: purohitaḥ so 'stu narādhipasya mantrādinā svastyayayena yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "May he be the royal chaplain of a king, endowed with the benediction of <s>mantras</s> and the like,

children.text: satkāramāpnotu tathā ca rājñastavāpi yo nāma bisānyahārṣīt // Jm_19.15 //
children.translated_text: and may he obtain such honor from the king — he who has stolen your lotus-roots!" || Jm 19.15 ||

body.text: apara uvāca -
body.translated_text: Another said —

children.text: adhyāpakaṃ samyagadhītavedaṃ tapasvisambhāvanayā mahatyā /
children.translated_text: Let the people of the country come together and honor him as a teacher who has properly studied the <s>Vedas</s>, with great reverence for his austerity —

children.text: arcantu taṃ jānapadāḥ sametya biseṣu lubdho na guṇeṣu yaste // Jm_19.16 //
children.translated_text: he who is greedy for lotus roots, not for virtues! // Jm_19.16 //

body.text: sahāya uvāca -
body.translated_text: The companion said:

children.text: catuḥśataṃ grāmavaraṃ samṛddhaṃ labdhvā narendrādupayātu bhoktum /
children.translated_text: Having obtained from the king a prosperous village of four hundred, let him go to enjoy it —

children.text: avītarāgo maraṇaṃ sa caitu lobhaṃ biseṣvapyajayanna yaste // Jm_19.17 //
children.translated_text: let him who has not abandoned passion meet death, he who could not conquer greed even for lotus roots! // Jm_19.17 //

body.text: dāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: The servant said:

children.text: sa grāmaṇīrastu sahāyamadhye strīnṛttagītairupalāpyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let him be a village headman among companions, entertained by women's dancing and singing —

children.text: mā rājataśca vyasanāni labdha bisārthamātmārthamaśīśamadyaḥ // Jm_19.18 //
children.translated_text: and let him not obtain misfortunes from the king, he who today destroyed himself for the sake of lotus roots! // Jm_19.18 //

body.text: bhaginyuvāca -
body.translated_text: The sister said:

children.text: vidyotamānāṃ bapuṣā śriyā ca patnītvamānīya narādhipastām /
children.translated_text: Let the king take as wife a woman radiant in beauty and splendor,

children.text: yoṣitsahasrāgrasarīṃ karotu yastvadvidhasyāpi bisānyahārṣīt // Jm_19.19 //
children.translated_text: and make her foremost among a thousand women — she who stole lotus roots even from one such as you! // Jm_19.19 //

body.text: dāsyuvāca -
body.translated_text: The female servant said:

children.text: ekākinī sā samatītya sādhūnsvādūpabhoge praṇayaṃ karotu /
children.translated_text: Let her, alone, surpassing virtuous women, indulge in the enjoyment of sweet pleasures —

children.text: satkāralabdhāṃ mudamudvahantī bisānyapaśyattava yā na dharmam // Jm_19.20 //
children.translated_text: bearing the joy obtained through honor, she who did not see your <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) but saw only lotus roots! // Jm_19.20 //

body.text: atha tatra dharmaśravaṇārthaṃ samāgatāstadvanādhyuṣitā yakṣadviradavānarāstāṃ kathāmupaśrutya parāṃ vrīḍāṃ saṃvegaṃ copajagmuḥ / atha yakṣa ātmaviśuddhipradarśanārthamiti śapathameṣāṃ purataścakāra -
body.translated_text: Now the <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit), elephant, and monkey who dwelt in that forest and had gathered there to hear the <s>dharma</s> (teaching), upon overhearing that conversation, were overcome with extreme shame and agitation. Then the <s>yakṣa</s>, in order to demonstrate his own purity, made this oath before them:

children.text: āvāsikaḥ so 'stu mahāvihāre kacaṅgalāyāṃ navakarmikaśca /
children.translated_text: Let him be a resident monk in the great <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) at <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, and a supervisor of construction work —

children.text: ālokasandhiṃ divasaiḥ karotu yastvayyapi praskhalito bisārtham // Jm_19.21 //
children.translated_text: let him spend his days making window-openings, he who has stumbled even regarding you for the sake of lotus roots! // Jm_19.21 //

body.text: hastyuvāca -
body.translated_text: The elephant said:

children.text: ṣaḍbhirdṛḍhaiḥ pāśaśataiḥ sa bandhaṃ prāpnotu ramyācca vanājjanāntam /
children.translated_text: Let him be bound with six hundred firm ropes, and driven from the lovely forest to a settlement of people,

children.text: tīkṣṇāṅkaśākarṣaṇajā rujaśca yaste muniśreṣṭha bisānyahārṣīt // Jm_19.22 //
children.translated_text: and suffer the pains caused by the pulling of sharp goads — he who stole your lotus roots, O best of sages! // Jm_19.22 //

body.text: vānara uvāca -
body.translated_text: The monkey said:

body.text: sa puṣpamālī trapughṛṣṭakaṇṭho yaṣṭayā hataḥ sarpamukhaṃ paraitu /
body.translated_text: Let him, wearing a garland of flowers and with his throat rubbed with a gourd, be struck with a stick and go to the serpent's mouth —

body.text: vaikakṣyabaddhaśca vased gṛheṣu laulyādahārṣīttava yo bisāni // Jm_19.23 //
body.translated_text: and let him live in houses, bound with a cord around his waist, he who out of greed stole your lotus roots! // Jm_19.23 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastānsarvānevānunayavinītākṣaraṃ śāntigāmbhīryasūcakamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, addressing all of them in words gentle with conciliation, indicative of peace and depth, said:

children.text: yo naṣṭamityāha na cāsya naṣṭamiṣṭānsa kāmānadhigamya kāmam /
children.translated_text: He who says something is lost when it is not lost — let him, having obtained his desired pleasures,

children.text: upaitu gehāśrita eva mṛtyuṃ bhavatsu yaḥ śaṅkata īdṛśaṃ vā // Jm_19.24 //
children.translated_text: meet death while still attached to the household life; or whoever among you harbors such suspicion! // Jm_19.24 //

body.text: atha śakro devendrastena teṣāṃ kāmopabhogaprātikūlyasūcakena śapathātiśayena samutpāditavismayabahumānaḥ svenaiva vapuṣābhijvalatā tānṛṣīnabhigamya sāmarṣavaduvāca - mā tāvadbhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s> (gods), astonished and filled with admiration by that extraordinary oath which indicated their aversion to the enjoyment of sense-pleasures, approached those <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) in his own radiant form and spoke as if with indignation: 'Hold, sirs!'

children.text: yatprāptiparyutsukamānasānāṃ sukhārthināṃ naiti manāṃsi nidrā /
children.translated_text: That which deprives sleep from the minds of those eager for its attainment,

children.text: yānprāptumicchanti tapaḥśramaiśca tānkena kāmāniti kutsayadhve // Jm_19.25 //
children.translated_text: those pleasures which they seek to obtain even through the toil of <s>tapas</s> (austerities) — why do you revile them? // Jm_19.25 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - anantādīnavā mārṣa kāmāḥ / saṃkṣepatastu śrūyatāṃ yadabhisamīkṣya kāmānna praśaṃsanti munayaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'The dangers of <s>kāma</s> (sense-pleasures) are endless, dear sir. But hear in brief the reason why the sages do not praise them:'

children.text: kāmeṣu bandhamupayāti vadhaṃ ca lokaḥ śokaṃ klamaṃ bhayamanekavidhaṃ ca duḥkham /
children.translated_text: For the sake of pleasures, the world falls into bondage, slaughter, grief, exhaustion, fear, and manifold suffering;

children.text: kāmārthameva ca mahīpatayaḥ patanti dharmopamardarabhasā narakaṃ paratra // Jm_19.26 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of pleasures alone, kings fall into <s>naraka</s> (hell) hereafter through the violence of trampling upon <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). // Jm_19.26 //

children.text: yatsauhṛdāni sahasā virasībhavanti yannītiśāṭhyamalinena pathā prayānti /
children.translated_text: That friendships suddenly become bitter, that people walk on paths defiled by the wickedness of false policy,

children.text: kīrtyā viyogamasukhaiḥ parataśca yogaṃ yatprāpnuvanti nanu kāraṇamatra kāmāḥ // Jm_19.27 //
children.translated_text: that they lose their fame and encounter sufferings hereafter — are not <s>kāmas</s> (sense-pleasures) the cause of all this? // Jm_19.27 //

children.text: iti hīnavimadhyamottamānāmiha cāmutra ca yadvadhāya kāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, since <s>kāmas</s> (sense-pleasures) lead to the destruction of the low, the middling, and the high, both in this world and the next,

children.text: kupitānbhujagānivātmakāmā munayastāniti śakra nāśrayante // Jm_19.28 //
children.translated_text: the sages who desire their own welfare do not resort to them, O <s>Śakra</s>, just as one does not resort to angry serpents. // Jm_19.28 //

body.text: atha śakro devānāmindrastasya tadvacanaṃ yuktamityabhinandya tena caiteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ māhātmyenābhiprasāditamanāstebhyaḥ svamaparādhamāviścakāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, applauded those words as fitting, and with his mind propitiated by the greatness of those <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), confessed his own offense to them:

children.text: guṇasambhāvanāvyaktiryatparīkṣyopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: 'The manifestation of esteem for virtues is verified when it is tested;

children.text: mayā vinihitānyasmātparīkṣārthaṃ bisāni vaḥ // Jm_19.29 //
children.translated_text: therefore your lotus roots were hidden by me for the purpose of testing you. // Jm_19.29 //

children.text: tatsanāthaṃ jagaddiṣṭayā munibhistathyakīrtibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Fortunately, the world is protected by sages of truthful renown;

children.text: viśuddhiḥ sthiracāritre tadetāni bisāni te // Jm_19.30 //
children.translated_text: your purity in steadfast conduct is confirmed — here are your lotus roots.' // Jm_19.30 //

body.text: ityuktvā tāni bisāni bodhisattvasya samupajahāra / atha bodhisattvastadasyāsamudācāradhāṣṭaryaṃ tejasvinibhṛtena vacasā pratyātideśa -
body.translated_text: Having said this, he presented those lotus roots to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rebuked his improper audacity with words that were dignified yet restrained:

children.text: na bāndhavā naiva vayaṃ sahāyā na te naṭā nāpi viḍambakāḥ smaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We are not your relatives, nor are we your companions; we are not your actors, nor your jesters;

children.text: kasminnavaṣṭabhya nu devarāja krīḍāpathenaivamṛṣīnupaiṣi // Jm_19.31 //
children.translated_text: on what grounds, O king of the <s>devas</s>, do you approach these <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) as though they were objects of sport? // Jm_19.31 //'

body.text: ityukte śakro devendraḥ sasambhramāpāstakuṇḍalakirīṭavidyudbhāsuravadanaḥ sabahumānamabhipraṇamyainaṃ kṣamayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, flustered, with his earrings and crown set aside, his face radiant like lightning, bowed with great respect and asked forgiveness:

children.text: uktaprayojanamidaṃ cāpalaṃ mama nirmama /
children.translated_text: 'This impulsiveness of mine had the purpose I stated, and was without malice;

children.text: pitevācārya iva ca kṣantumarhati tadbhavān // Jm_19.32 //
children.translated_text: may your honor forgive it, as a father or a teacher would. // Jm_19.32 //

children.text: nimīlitajñānabilocanānāṃ svabhāva eṣa skhalituṃ same 'pi /
children.translated_text: It is the nature of those whose eyes of wisdom are closed to stumble, even of one like me;

children.text: kṣamāṃ ca tatrātmavatāṃ prapattumato 'pyadaścetasi mā sma kārṣīḥ // Jm_19.33 //
children.translated_text: and it is for the self-controlled to grant forgiveness in such cases — therefore, please do not hold this offense in your heart.' // Jm_19.33 //

body.text: iti kṣamayitvā śakrastatraivāntardadhe /
body.translated_text: Having thus asked forgiveness, <s>Śakra</s> vanished right there.

body.text: tadevaṃ pravivekasukharasajñānāṃ viḍambaneva vihiṃseva ca kāmāḥ pratikūlā bhavanti / [taccedaṃ jātakaṃ bhagavānvyākārṣīt -
body.translated_text: Thus, for those who know the joy of the taste of seclusion, <s>kāmas</s> (sense-pleasures) are repugnant, like mockery and like injury. [The Blessed One narrated this <s>jātaka</s> (birth story) thus:]

children.text: ahaṃ śāradvatīputro maudgalyāyanakāśyapau /
children.translated_text: 'I was <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra), <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> and <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: pūrṇāniruddhāvānanda ityāsurbhrātarastadā // Jm_19.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and <s>Ānanda</s> — these were the brothers at that time. // Jm_19.34 //

children.text: bhaginyutpalavarṇāsīddāsī kubjottarābhavat /
children.translated_text: The sister was <s>Utpalavarṇā</s>, the female servant was <s>Kubjottarā</s>,

children.text: citro gṛhapatirdāso yakṣaḥ sātāgiristadā // Jm_19.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Citra</s> the householder was the servant, and the <s>yakṣa</s> was <s>Sātāgiri</s> at that time. // Jm_19.35 //

children.text: pārileyo 'bhavannāgo madhudātaiva vānaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Pārileya</s> was the elephant, and <s>Madhudāta</s> was the monkey,

children.text: kālodāyī ca śakro 'bhūddhāryatāmiti jātakam // Jm_19.36 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kālodāyin</s> was <s>Śakra</s> — may this <s>jātaka</s> (birth story) be cherished.' // Jm_19.36 //

body.text: iti bisajātakamekonaviṃśatitamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the Bisa-jātaka, the nineteenth.

body.text: 20. Śreṣṭhijātakam
body.translated_text: 20. The <s>Śreṣṭhi-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Merchant)

body.text: abhūtaguṇasaṃbhāvanā pratodasaṃcodaneva bhavati sādhūnāmiti guṇasaṃpādane prayatitavyam / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The attribution of virtues one does not actually possess acts like a goad spurring on the virtuous — therefore one should strive to acquire those virtues. As is heard in tradition:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila śrutakulavinayamahānakṣudranipuṇamatiraviṣamavyavahāraratiranekaśāstrābhyāsādālakṣitavacanasauṣṭhabaḥ karuṇānuvṛttyā samantato visyandamānadhanasamṛddhirmahāpradānairmahādhanatvād gṛhapatiratnasaṃmato 'nyatamasya rājñaḥ śreṣṭhī babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, was a man of keen and subtle intellect acquired through learning, family training, and discipline, delighting in fair dealing, whose eloquence was refined through the study of many <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), whose wealth flowed abundantly in all directions out of compassion, and who, being a great donor and a man of great wealth, was esteemed as a jewel among householders — he was the chief merchant of a certain king.

children.text: sa prakṛtyaiva dharmātmā śrutādiguṇabhūṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who was virtuous by nature, adorned with qualities such as learning,

children.text: abhūtprāyeṇa lokasya bahumānaikabhājanam // Jm_20.1 //
children.translated_text: became almost the sole object of the people's high esteem. // Jm_20.1 //

body.text: atha kadācittasminmahāsattve rājakulamabhigate kenacideva karaṇīyena tasya śvaśrūrduhitaramavalokayituṃ tadgṛhamabhijagāma / kṛtābhyāgamanasatkārā ca saṃkathāprastāvāgataṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ bodhisattvabhāryāṃ rahasi kuśalaparipraśnapūrvakaṃ paryapṛcchatkaccittvāṃ tāta bhartā nāvamanyate / kaccidvā vetti paricaryāguṇam / na vā duḥkhaśīlatayā prabādhata iti / sā vrīḍāvanatavadanā lajjā 'pragalbhaṃ śanakairuvāca - yādṛśo 'yaṃ śīlaguṇasamudācāreṇa, pravrajito 'pi durlabhaḥ ka idānīṃ tādṛśaḥ / atha sā tasyā mātā jaropahataśrutismṛtitvāllajjāsaṃkucitākṣaraṃ tanayayā tadvacanamabhidhīyamānaṃ na samyagupadhārayāmāta / pravrajitasaṃkīrtanāttu pravrajito me jāmāteti niścayamupajagāma / sā sasvaramabhiruditā svāṃ duhitaramanuśocantī duḥkhāvegavaśātparidevanaparā babhūva / kīdṛśastasya śīlaguṇasamudācāro ya evamanuraktaṃ svaṃ janamapahāya pravrajitaḥ? kiṃ vā tasya pravrajyayā?
body.translated_text: Now once, when that great being had gone to the royal court on some business, his mother-in-law came to his house to visit her daughter. Having been received with the hospitality due to a guest, and in the course of conversation, she privately asked her daughter, the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> wife, beginning with inquiries about her welfare: 'Dear child, does your husband not look down upon you? Does he recognize the merit of your devoted service? Does he not trouble you with a harsh temperament?' She, with her face bashfully lowered, said softly and with modest hesitation: 'Given his excellence of character and conduct, even as a <s>pravrajita</s> (renunciant) such a man would be hard to find — who then could be such while remaining a householder?' But her mother, whose hearing and memory were impaired by old age, did not properly grasp those words spoken by her daughter in syllables curtailed by modesty. However, from the mention of '<s>pravrajita</s>' (renunciant), she arrived at the conclusion: 'My son-in-law has become a renunciant!' She burst into loud weeping, lamenting for her daughter, and overcome by the force of grief, became absorbed in lamentation: 'What kind of excellence of character and conduct is his, that he has abandoned his own devoted people and become a renunciant? And what use is his renunciation?'

children.text: taruṇasya vapuṣmataḥ sataḥ sukumārasya sukhocitātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: How has the mind of one so young, handsome, noble,

children.text: kṣitipābhimatasya tasya vai vanavāse praṇatā matiḥ katham // Jm_20.2 //
children.translated_text: delicate, and accustomed to comfort, esteemed by the king, turned toward dwelling in the forest? // Jm_20.2 //

children.text: svajanādanavāpya vipriyaṃ jarayā vopahṛtāṃ virūpatām /
children.translated_text: Without receiving any offense from his own people, nor having been disfigured by old age,

children.text: kathamekapade rujaṃ vinā vibhavodgāri gṛhaṃ sa muktavān // Jm_20.3 //
children.translated_text: how has he suddenly, without illness, abandoned his home that overflowed with wealth? // Jm_20.3 //

body.text: vinayābharaṇena dhīmatā priyadharmeṇa parānukampinā /
body.translated_text: By one wise, adorned with discipline, devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and compassionate toward others —

body.text: kathamabhyupapannamīdṛśaṃ svajane niṣkaruṇatvacāpalam // Jm_20.4 //
body.translated_text: how has such heartless fickleness been committed toward his own people? // Jm_20.4 //

children.text: śramaṇadvijamitrasaṃśritānsvajanaṃ dīnajanaṃ ca mānayan /
children.translated_text: He who honored <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, dependents, his own kin, and the destitute —

children.text: śuciśīladhanaḥ kimāpnuyānna sa geheṣu vane yadīpsati // Jm_20.5 //
children.translated_text: what could he obtain in the forest, rich in pure conduct and virtue, that he could not obtain at home? // Jm_20.5 //

children.text: aparādhavivarjitāṃ tyajannanukūlāṃ sahadharmacāriṇīm /
children.translated_text: In abandoning a faithful wife, free from fault,

children.text: yatidharmaparaḥ sa nekṣate kimimaṃ dharmapathavyatikramam // Jm_20.6 //
children.translated_text: devoted and a companion in <s>dharma</s> (the religious life), he who is intent on the ascetic's path — does he not see this transgression of the path of <s>dharma</s>? // Jm_20.6 //

children.text: dhigaho bata daivadurnayādyadi bhaktaṃ janamevamujjhatām /
children.translated_text: Alas, shame upon him! If through the cruelty of fate he thus abandons his devoted people,

children.text: na ghṛṇāpathameti mānasaṃ yadi vā dharmalavo 'pi sidhyati // Jm_20.7 //
children.translated_text: does his mind not enter the path of compassion, even if some small portion of <s>dharma</s> is thereby accomplished? // Jm_20.7 //

body.text: atha sā bodhisattvasya patnī tena mātuḥ karuṇenākṛtakena paridevitena patipravrajyābhisaṃbandhena strīsvabhāvād vyathitahṛdayā sasaṃbhramā viṣādaviklavamukhī śokaduḥkhābhinipātasaṃkṣobhādvismṛtakathāprastāvasaṃbandhā pravrajito me bharteti madvyavasthāpanārthamambā gṛhamidamabhigatā vipriyaśravaṇāditi niścayamupetya saparidevitaṃ sasvaraṃ rudatī mohamupajagāma bālā / tadupaśrutya gṛhajanaḥ parijanavargaśca śokaduḥkhāvegādākrandanaṃ cakāra / tacchrutvā prātiveśyamitrasvajanabandhuvargaḥ saṃśritajano brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaśca tasya gṛhapateranurāgavaśānugāḥ prāyaśaśca paurāstadgṛhamabhijagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> wife, her heart wounded by woman's nature at her mother's piteous and unsolicited lamentation that implied her husband's renunciation, was flustered, her face stricken with despondency, and her mind having lost the thread of the conversation due to the shock of the onslaught of grief and sorrow, she arrived at the conclusion: 'My mother has come to this house to inform me that my husband has become a renunciant, upon hearing the unpleasant news.' Weeping aloud with lamentation, the young woman fainted. Hearing this, the household servants and the retinue burst into wailing from the force of grief and sorrow. Hearing that, the neighbors, friends, kinsmen, relatives, dependents, and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and householder communities, who were devoted to that householder, and most of the townspeople, came to his house.

children.text: prāyeṇa lokasya babhūva yasmāttulyakramo 'sau sukhaduḥkhayoge /
children.translated_text: Since for the most part the people shared equally in his joys and sorrows,

children.text: ato 'sya loko 'pyanuśikṣayeva tulyakramo 'bhūtsukhaduḥkhayoge // Jm_20.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore the people too, as if following his example, shared equally in joy and sorrow. // Jm_20.8 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo rājakulāt svabhavanasamīpamupagataḥ sākrandaśabdaṃ svabhavanamavetya mahataśca janakāyasya saṃnipātaṃ svaṃ puruṣamanvādideśa jñāyatāṃ kimetaditi / sa taṃ vṛttāntamupalabhya samupetyāsmai nivedayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having returned from the royal court to the vicinity of his own house and perceiving the sounds of wailing from his home and the gathering of a great multitude, dispatched his own man saying: 'Find out what this is about.' He, having learned the circumstances, came back and informed him:

children.text: utsṛjya bhavanaṃ sphītamāryaḥ pravrajitaḥ kila /
children.translated_text: 'The noble master has abandoned his splendid mansion and become a renunciant, it seems —

children.text: iti śrutvā kuto 'pyeṣa snehādevaṃgato janaḥ // Jm_20.9 //
children.translated_text: hearing this from somewhere, the people have come to this state out of affection.' // Jm_20.9 //

body.text: atha sa mahāsattvaḥ prakṛtyā śuddhāśayaḥ pratyādiṣṭa iva tena vacasā samupajātavrīḍasaṃvegaścintāmāpede / bhadrā bata mayi janasya saṃbhāvanā /
body.translated_text: Then that great being, pure-hearted by nature, as if admonished by those words, was seized with shame and reflection and thought: 'Noble indeed is the people's esteem for me!'

children.text: ślāghanīyāmavāpyaitāṃ guṇasaṃbhāvanāṃ janāt /
children.translated_text: 'Having obtained from the people this praiseworthy attribution of virtues,

children.text: gṛhābhimukha eva syāṃ yadi kiṃ mama pauruṣam // Jm_20.10 //
children.translated_text: if I were to simply turn back toward the household life, what would be my manliness? // Jm_20.10 //

children.text: syāddoṣabhaktiḥ prathitā mayaivaṃ guṇeṣvavajñāvirasā ca vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: My devotion to faults would thus become well-known, and my conduct would be one of disdainful indifference toward virtues;

children.text: yāyāmataḥ sādhujane laghutvaṃ ki jīvitaṃ syācca tathāvidhasya // Jm_20.11 //
children.translated_text: I would thereby fall into disrepute among the virtuous — and what would be the life of such a person? // Jm_20.11 //

children.text: saṃbhāvanāmasya janasya tasmātkriyāguṇena pratipūjayāmi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I shall honor the esteem of these people through the virtue of my actions,

children.text: asatparikleśamayaṃ vimuñcaṃstapovanapremaguṇena geham // Jm_20.12 //
children.translated_text: releasing myself from my home — which is full of unworthy afflictions — through the noble qualities of the ascetic grove.' // Jm_20.12 //

body.text: iti vicintya sa mahātmā tata eva pratinivṛtya rājñaḥ pratihārayāmāsa - śreṣṭhī punardraṣṭumicchati devamiti / kṛtābhyanujñaśca praviśya yathopacāraṃ rājasamīpamupajagāma / kimidamiti ca rājñā paryanuyukto 'bravīt - icchāmi pravrajitum, tadabhyanujñātumarhati māṃ deva iti /
body.translated_text: Having thus reflected, that great soul turned back from there and sent word to the king through the doorkeeper: 'The merchant wishes to see his majesty once more.' And having received permission, he entered and approached the king with due ceremony. When the king asked 'What is this about?', he said: 'I wish to become a renunciant; may your majesty be pleased to grant me permission.'

body.text: athainaṃ sa rājā sasaṃbhramāvegaḥ snehādityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king, flustered and agitated, said to him out of affection:

children.text: mayi sthite bandhusuhṛdviśiṣṭe tvaṃ kena duḥkhena vanaṃ prayāsi /
children.translated_text: 'While I am here, distinguished as your kinsman and friend, by what sorrow do you go to the forest?'

children.text: yannāpahartuṃ prabhutā mama syāddhanena nītyā balasaṃpadā vā // Jm_20.13 //
children.translated_text: that which cannot be taken from me by wealth, policy, or the power of arms.

children.text: artho dhanairyadi gṛhāṇa dhanāni mattaḥ pīḍā kutaścidatha tāṃ pratiṣedhayāmi /
children.translated_text: If your purpose is wealth, then accept wealth from me; if there is some affliction, then I shall remove it.

children.text: māṃ yācamānamiti bandhujanaṃ ca hitvā kiṃ vā tvamanyadabhivīkṣya vanaṃ prayāsi // Jm_20.14 //
children.translated_text: Why do you, abandoning me who am asking you, and your kinsmen too, look to something else and set forth for the forest?

body.text: iti sa mahātmā sasnehabahumānamabhihito rājñā sānunayamenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed by the king with affection and respect, the great-souled one spoke to him gently in reply:

children.text: pīḍā kutastvadbhujasaṃśritānāṃ dhanodayāvekṣaṇadīnatā vā /
children.translated_text: What affliction could there be for those sheltered by your arm, or what wretchedness of depending on the prospect of wealth?

children.text: ato na duḥkhena vanaṃ prayāmi yamarthamuddiśya tu taṃ nibodha // Jm_20.15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not from suffering that I go to the forest; but hear the purpose for which I do so.

children.text: dīkṣāmupāśrita iti prathito 'smi deva śokāśrudurdinamukhena mahājanena /
children.translated_text: O lord, I have become known as one who has undertaken <s>dīkṣā</s> (religious initiation), by the great multitude of people whose faces are overcast with clouds of tears of grief.

children.text: icchāmi tena vijaneṣu vaneṣu vastuṃ śraddheyatāmupagato 'smi guṇābhipattau // Jm_20.16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I wish to dwell in the solitary forests; I have attained credibility in the pursuit of virtues.

body.text: rājovāca - nārhati bhavāñjanapravādamātrakeṇāsmān parityaktum / na hi bhavadvidhānāṃ janapravādasaṃpādanābhirādhyā guṇavibhūtistadasaṃpādanavirādhyā vā /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Your honor should not abandon us merely on account of public talk. For those like yourself cannot achieve the splendor of virtues by conforming to popular opinion, nor can it be obstructed by not conforming to it.'

children.text: svecchāvikalpagrathitāśca tāstā niraṅkuśā lokakathā bhramanti /
children.translated_text: Those popular tales wander unchecked, strung together by the threads of arbitrary fancy.

children.text: kurvīta yastā hṛdaye 'pi tāvatsyātso 'pahāsyaḥ kimuta prapattā // Jm_20.17 //
children.translated_text: One who would even take them to heart would be an object of ridicule — how much more so one who submits to them!

body.text:
bodhisattva uvāca - mā maivaṃ mahārāja / na hi kalyāṇo janapravādo nānuvidheyaḥ /
paśyatu devaḥ,
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Do not say so, O great king! For virtuous public opinion is not to be disregarded. Let your majesty consider:

children.text: kalyāṇadharmeti yadā narendra saṃbhāvanāmeti manuṣyadharmā /
children.translated_text: When a person attains the reputation of being of virtuous character, O lord of men,

children.text: tasyā na hīyeta naraḥ sadharmā hriyāpi tāvaddhuramudvahettām // Jm_20.18 //
children.translated_text: a man of good conduct should not fall away from that; out of a sense of shame at least, he should bear that burden.

children.text: saṃbhāvanāyāṃ guṇabhāvanāyāṃ saṃdṛśyamāno hi yathā tathā vā /
children.translated_text: For one who is seen, rightly or wrongly, as living up to the reputation of cultivating virtues,

children.text: viśeṣato bhāti yaśaḥprasiddhyā syāttvanyathā śuṣka ivodapānaḥ // Jm_20.19 //
children.translated_text: shines especially through the fame of his renown; otherwise he would be like a dried-up well.

children.text: guṇapravādairayathārthavṛddhairvimarśapātākulitaiḥ patadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the body of one's fame is shattered by reports of virtue that are untruthfully inflated, tottering when subjected to scrutiny and falling,

children.text: vicūrṇitā kīrtitanurnarāṇāṃ duḥkhena śaknoti punaḥ prasartum // Jm_20.20 //
children.translated_text: it can only painfully spread again.

children.text: tadvarjanīyānparivarjayantaṃ parigrahānvigrahahetubhūtān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when I am renouncing possessions that should be renounced, possessions that are the cause of strife,

children.text: krodhocchiraskāniva kṛṣṇasarpānyukto 'si māṃ deva na saṃniṣeddhum // Jm_20.21 //
children.translated_text: like black serpents with raised hoods of anger — you ought not to restrain me, O lord.

body.text: snehena bhaktijñatayā ca kāmaṃ yukto vidhirbhṛtyajane tavāyam /
body.translated_text: This course of action toward your servants is fitting indeed, out of affection and recognition of their devotion;

body.text: vittena tu pravrajitasya kiṃ me parigrahakleśaparigraheṇa // Jm_20.22 //
body.translated_text: but what use is wealth to me, a renunciant — that grasping of the affliction of possessions?

body.text: ityanunīya sa mahātmā taṃ rājānaṃ kṛtābhyanujñastena tata eva vanāya pratasthe /
body.translated_text: Having thus persuaded that king, the great-souled one, having received his permission, set forth from that very place toward the forest.

body.text: athainaṃ suhṛdo jñātayaḥ saṃśritāścābhigamya śokāśrupariplutanayanāḥ pādayoḥ saṃpariṣvajya nivārayitumīṣuḥ / kecidañjalipragrahapuraḥsaraṃ mārgamasyāvṛtya samavātiṣṭhanta / sapariṣvaṅgasaṃgatānunayamapare gṛhābhimukhamenaṃ netumīṣuḥ / yatkiñcanakāritākṣepakarkaśākṣaramanye praṇayādenamūcuḥ / mitrasvajanāpekṣākāruṇyapradarśanamapare 'sya pracakruḥ / gṛhāśrama eva puṇyatama ityevamanye śrutiyuktisaṃgrathitaṃ grāhayitumīhāṃ cakrire / tapovanavāsaduḥkhatāsaṃkīrtanaiḥ kāryaśeṣaparisamāptyā yācñayā paralokaphalasaṃdehakathābhistaistaiśca vārttāviśeṣairnivartayitumenaṃ vyāyacchanta / tasya tān pravrajyāśrayavimukhān vanagamananivāraṇadhīramukhān nayanajalārdramukhān suhṛdo 'bhivīkṣya vyaktamiti cintā babhūva -
body.translated_text: Then his friends, relatives, and dependents approached him, their eyes flooded with tears of grief, and embracing his feet, sought to prevent him. Some blocked his path, standing before him with hands joined in supplication. Others tried to lead him back toward his home with affectionate embraces and entreaties. Some spoke to him out of love in harsh words expressing the reproach of one reduced to destitution. Others made a display of compassion born of concern for friends and kinsmen.
