Some endeavored to convince him with arguments woven from scripture and reason that the householder's life is the most meritorious. They exerted themselves to turn him back by recounting the hardships of forest life, by requesting him to complete his remaining duties, by raising doubts about the fruits of the next world, and by various other arguments. Seeing those friends — averse to the path of renunciation, resolute in their determination to prevent his going to the forest, their faces moist with tears — he clearly reflected thus:

children.text: suhṛtpratijñaiḥ suhṛdi pramatte nyāyyaṃ hitaṃ rūkṣamapi prayoktum /
children.translated_text: For those who profess friendship, it is proper to administer beneficial advice to a heedless friend, even if it be harsh;

children.text: rūḍhaḥ satāmeṣa hi dharmamārgaḥ prāgeva rūcyaṃ ca hitaṃ ca yatsyāt // Jm_20.23 //
children.translated_text: for this is the established path of the virtuous — how much more so when the advice is both agreeable and beneficial!

children.text: vanād gṛhaṃ śreya idaṃ tvamīṣāṃ svastheṣu citteṣu kathaṃ nu ruḍham /
children.translated_text: How has this notion taken root in their undisturbed minds that the household life is better than the forest,

children.text: yannirviśaṅkā vanasaṃśrāyānmāṃ pāpaprasaṅgādiva vārayanti // Jm_20.24 //
children.translated_text: so that they restrain me from resorting to the forest without hesitation, as if from involvement in sin?

children.text: mṛto mariṣyannapi vā manuṣyaścyutaśca dharmāditi roditavyam /
children.translated_text: One should weep for a person who has died, or who is about to die, or who has fallen from <s>dharma</s> (righteousness);

children.text: kayā nu buddhyā vanavāsakāmaṃ māmeva jīvantamamī rudanti // Jm_20.25 //
children.translated_text: with what understanding, then, do these people weep for me, who am alive and desirous of forest life?

children.text: madviprayogastvatha śokaheturmayā samaṃ kiṃ na vane vasanti /
children.translated_text: If separation from me is the cause of their grief, why do they not dwell with me in the forest?

children.text: gehāni cetkāntatarāṇi mattaḥ ko nvādaro bāṣpaparivyayena // Jm_20.26 //
children.translated_text: And if their homes are dearer to them than I am, what is the point of this expenditure of tears?

body.text: atha tvidānīṃ svajanānurāgaḥ karoti naiṣāṃ tapase 'bhyanujñām /
body.translated_text: But if their attachment to kinsmen does not permit them to give their consent to my austerities,

body.text: sāmarthyamāsītkathamasya naiva byūḍheṣvanīkeṣvapi tatra tatra // Jm_20.27 //
body.translated_text: how is it that this attachment had no power at all when armies were deployed here and there in battle?

children.text: dṛṣṭāvadāno vyasanodayeṣu bāṣpodgamānmūrta ivopalabdha /
children.translated_text: Witnessed in times of calamity, and perceived as if embodied through the welling up of tears,

children.text: saṃrūḍhamūlo 'pi suhṛtsvabhāvaḥ śāṭhyaṃ prayātyatra vinānuvṛttyā // Jm_20.28 //
children.translated_text: the nature of friendship, even when deeply rooted, turns to duplicity without compliance.

children.text: nivāraṇārthāni sagadgadāni vākyāni sāśrūṇi ca locanāni /
children.translated_text: These faltering words meant to dissuade me, these tear-filled eyes,

children.text: praṇāmalolāni śirāṃsi caiṣāṃ mānaṃ samānasya yathā karoti // Jm_20.29 //
children.translated_text: these heads bowing low — how they flatter the pride of an equal!

children.text: snehastathaivārhati kartumeṣāṃ ślādhyāmanupravrajane 'pi buddhim /
children.translated_text: Their affection deserves equally to produce in them a praiseworthy resolve to follow me into renunciation.

children.text: mā bhūnnaṭānāmiva vṛttametad vrīḍākaraṃ sajjanamānasānām // Jm_20.30 //
children.translated_text: Let not this conduct be like that of actors — shameful to noble-minded persons.

children.text: dvitrāṇi mitrāṇi bhavantyavaśyamāpadgatasyāpi sunirguṇasya /
children.translated_text: Even a person in distress and utterly devoid of merit will inevitably have two or three friends;

children.text: sahāya eko 'pyatidurlabhastu guṇoditasyāpi vanaprayāṇe // Jm_20.31 //
children.translated_text: but even for one endowed with virtues, a single companion on the journey to the forest is exceedingly hard to find.

children.text: ye me haranti sma puraḥsaratvaṃ raṇeṣu mattadvipasaṃkaṭeṣu /
children.translated_text: Those who used to seize the lead for me in battles crowded with maddened elephants,

children.text: nānuvrajantyadya vanāya te māṃ kiṃsvitsa evāsmi ta eva ceme // Jm_20.32 //
children.translated_text: do not follow me today as I go to the forest — am I still the same person, and are these still the same people?

children.text: smarāmi naiṣāṃ viguṇaṃ prayātuṃ snehasya yatsaṃkṣayakāraṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: I do not recall any fault of theirs that could be the cause of diminished affection;

children.text: suhṛjjanasyaivamiyaṃ sthitirme kaccidbhavetsvastinimittato 'smāt // Jm_20.33 //
children.translated_text: yet such is the conduct of my friends toward me — surely this must be for my own good.

children.text: mamaiva vā nirguṃṇabhāva eṣa nānuvrajantyadya vanāya yanmām /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps it is my own lack of merit that they do not follow me today to the forest;

children.text: guṇāvabaddhāni hi mānasāni kasyāsti viśleṣayituṃ prabhutvam // Jm_20.34 //
children.translated_text: for when hearts are bound by virtues, who has the power to separate them?

children.text: ye vā prakāśānapi gehadoṣānguṇānna paśyanti tapovane vā /
children.translated_text: Or those who do not see the manifest faults of household life, nor the virtues of the ascetic forest,

children.text: nimīlitajñānavilocanāṃstānkimanyathāhaṃ paritarkayāmi // Jm_20.35 //
children.translated_text: whose eyes of knowledge are shut — what else can I think of them?

children.text: paratra caiveha ca duḥkhahetūnkāmānvihātuṃ na samutsahante /
children.translated_text: They cannot bring themselves to abandon sensual pleasures, which are the cause of suffering both here and hereafter,

children.text: tapovanaṃ tadviparītamete tyajanti māṃ cādya dhigastu moham // Jm_20.36 //
children.translated_text: yet they abandon the ascetic forest, which is the opposite of that, and abandon me today — alas for delusion!

children.text: yairvipralabdhāḥ suhṛdo mamaite na yānti śāntiṃ nikhilāśca lokāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those very faults by which my friends here have been deceived, and by which all the worlds find no peace —

children.text: tapovanopārjitasatprabhāvastāneva doṣānprasabhaṃ nihanmi // Jm_20.37 //
children.translated_text: those very faults I shall forcefully destroy, having acquired the noble power obtained in the ascetic forest.

children.text: iti sa parigaṇayya niścitātmā praṇayamayāni suhṛdviceṣṭitāni /
children.translated_text: Thus having reflected with firm resolve upon the affection-filled gestures of his friends,

children.text: anunayamadhurākṣarairvacobhirviśadamapāsya tapovanaṃ jagāma // Jm_20.38 //
children.translated_text: he clearly dispelled them with words of gentle and sweet syllables, and departed for the ascetic forest.

body.text: tadevamabhūtaguṇasaṃbhāvanā pratodasaṃcodaneva bhavati sādhūnāmiti guṇasaṃpādane prayatitavyam / yato bhikṣurityupāsaka iti guṇataḥ saṃbhāvyamānena sādhunā tadbhāvasādhubhirguṇairabhyalaṃkartavya evātmā / evaṃ durlabhā dharmapratipattisahāyā ityevamapyunneyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, even undeserved attribution of virtues acts as a goad spurring on the virtuous — therefore one should strive to cultivate virtues. Since one who is honored as a good <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) or a good <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee) on account of his qualities must adorn himself with virtues befitting that status. From this one should also understand that companions on the path of <s>dharma</s> (righteous practice) are exceedingly rare.

body.text: // iti śreṣṭhijātakaṃ viṃśatitamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth story, the <s>Śreṣṭhi-jātaka</s> (Story of the Merchant).

body.text: 21. Cuḍḍabodhijātakam
body.translated_text: 21. <s>Cuḍḍabodhi-jātaka</s> (Story of Cuḍḍabodhi)

body.text: krodhavinayācchatrūnupaśamayati, vardhayatyeva tvanyathā / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: By subduing anger one pacifies enemies, but by acting otherwise one only increases them. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila mahāsattvaḥ kasmiṃścinmahati brāhmaṇakule guṇābhyāsamāhātmyādativṛddhayaśasi pratiniyatasamṛddhiguṇe rājasatkṛte daivatasaṃmate lokasya janma pratileme / kālānāmatyayenābhivṛddhaḥ kṛtasaṃskārakarmā śrutaguṇābhyāsādacireṇaiva vidvatsadassu prakāśanāmā babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, took birth in a certain great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family — one whose fame had grown exceedingly through the greatness of cultivated virtues, possessing a fixed endowment of excellent qualities, honored by the king, and esteemed by the people as divine. In the course of time, having grown up and completed the purificatory rites, through the practice of learning he quickly became renowned in the assemblies of the learned.

children.text: kītirvidvatsadassveva viduṣāṃ pravijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: The fame of the learned shines forth only in assemblies of the learned,

children.text: ratnajñeṣviva ratnānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ samareṣviva // Jm_21.1 //
children.translated_text: just as the splendor of gems shines among connoisseurs of gems, and that of heroes in battle.

body.text: atha sa mahātmā pravrajyākṛtaparicayatvātpūrvajanmasu svabhyastadharmasaṃjñatvātprajñāvadātamatitvacca na gehe ratimupalebhe / sa kāmān vigrahavivādamadavairasyaprācuryādrājacaurodakadahanavipriyadāyādasādhāraṇatvādatṛptijanakatvādanekadoṣāyatanatvācca saviṣamivānnamātmakāmaḥ parityajya saṃhṛtakeśaśmaśruśobhaḥ kāṣāyavivarṇavāsāḥ parityaktagṛhaveṣavibhramaḥ pravrajyāvinayaniyamaśriyamaśiśriyam / tadanurāgavaśagā cāsya patnī keśānavatāryāhāryavibhūṣaṇodvahananirvyāpāraśarīrā svarūpaguṇaśobhāvibhūṣitā kāṣāyavastrasaṃvītatanuranupravavrāja / atha bodhisattvastapovanānugamanavyavasāyamasya vidtvā tapovanādhyāsanāyogyatāṃ ca strīsaukumāryasyāvocadenāṃ - bhadre darśitastvayāyamasmadanurāgasvabhāvaḥ / tadalamasmadanugamanaṃ pratyanena vyavasāyena te / yatraiva tvanyāḥ pravrajitāḥ prativasanti tatra bhavatyāstābhireva sārdha pratirūpaṃ vastuṃ syāt / durabhisaṃbhavāni hyaraṇyāyatanāni / paśya -
body.translated_text: Then that great-souled one, because of his familiarity with renunciation in previous births, because of his habitual acquaintance with the teachings of <s>dharma</s> (the righteous path) practiced in former lives, and because of the purity of his discerning intellect, found no delight in household life. Desiring his own welfare, he abandoned sensual pleasures — which, like poisoned food, abound in quarrels, disputes, intoxication, and hostility, are shared in common with kings, thieves, water, fire, and hostile heirs, are incapable of producing satisfaction, and are the source of countless faults — and with his hair and beard shorn of their beauty, wearing the dull saffron robes, having cast off the ornamental display of the householder's attire, he assumed the grace of the discipline and restraint of the renunciant life. And his wife, drawn by her attachment to him, having let down her hair, her body no longer occupied with wearing ornamental adornments, adorned only by the natural beauty of her own form, her body wrapped in saffron cloth, followed him into renunciation. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, learning of her resolve to follow him to the ascetic forest, and considering the unsuitability of the delicacy of a woman for forest life, said to her: 'Noble lady, you have shown your nature of devotion to me. But enough of this resolve to follow me. It would be proper for you to dwell with other renunciant women wherever they reside. For forest hermitages are difficult to endure. Consider:

children.text: śamaśānaśūnyālayaparvateṣu vaneṣu ca vyālamṛgākuleṣu /
children.translated_text: In cremation grounds, deserted dwellings, and mountains, and in forests teeming with wild beasts and serpents,

children.text: niketahīnā yatayo vasanti yatraiva cāstaṃ ravirabhyupaiti // Jm_21.2 //
children.translated_text: ascetics dwell without shelter, wherever the sun sets.

children.text: dhyānodyamādekacarāśca nityaṃ stridarśanādapyapavṛttabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of their devotion to <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), they always wander alone, their disposition turned away even from the sight of women.

children.text: nivartituṃ tena matiṃ kuruṣva ko 'rthastabānena paribhrameṇa // Jm_21.3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore set your mind on turning back — what is the purpose of this wandering with me?'

body.text: sā niyatamenamanugamanakṛtaniścayā bāṣpoparudhyamānanayanā kiṃcidīdṛśaṃ pratyuvāca -
body.translated_text: She, firmly resolved to follow him, her eyes obstructed by tears, replied somewhat thus:

children.text: yadi me śramabuddhiḥ syattavānugamanotsave /
children.translated_text: 'If I had a thought of hardship in the joy of following you,

children.text: kimityevaṃ prapadyeya duḥkha tava ca vipriyam // Jm_21.4 //
children.translated_text: why would I undertake in this way what is painful and displeasing to you?

children.text: yattu naiva samarthāsmi vartituṃ rahitā tvayā /
children.translated_text: But since I am simply unable to live apart from you,

children.text: ityājñātikramamimaṃ tvaṃ mama kṣantumarhasi // Jm_21.5 //
children.translated_text: you should forgive this transgression of your command on my part.'

body.text: iti sā dvitrirapyucyamānāyadā necchati sma nivartitum, tato bodhisattva upekṣānibhṛtamatirasyāṃ babhūva /
body.translated_text: Though she was told thus two or three times, when she would not consent to turn back, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> became composed in a spirit of equanimity toward her.

body.text: sa tayānugamyamānaścakravāka iva cakravākyā grāmanagaranigamānanuvicaran kadācitkṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ kasmiṃścitpravivikte śrimati nānātarugahanopaśobhite ghanapracchāye kṛtopakāra iva kvacitkvaciddinakarakiraṇacandrakairnānukusumarajo 'vakīrṇadharaṇitale śucau vanoddeśe dhyānavidhimanuṣṭhāya sāyānhasamaye vyutthāya samādheḥ pāṃsukūlāni sivyati sma / sāpi pravrajitā tasyaiva nātīdūre vṛkṣamūlamupaśobhayamānā devateva svena vapuṣaḥ prabhāveṇa virājamānā tadupadiṣṭena manaskāravidhinā dhyāyati sma /
body.translated_text: Accompanied by her, like a <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) by his mate, he wandered through villages, towns, and market-towns. Once, having completed his meal, in a certain secluded and beautiful spot adorned with dense groves of various trees, deep in shade, its ground strewn here and there with the pollen of various flowers by the rays of the sun as if doing it a favor, in a pure forest clearing, he practiced the method of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and in the late afternoon, having risen from <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), he was sewing his <s>pāṃsukūla</s> (rag-robes). She too, the renunciant woman, not far from him, adorning the foot of a tree, radiant like a goddess by the splendor of her own form, was meditating according to the method of mental contemplation he had taught her.

body.text: atha tatratyo rājā vasantakālajanitābhyadhikakisalayaśobhāni bhramadbhramaramadhukarīgaṇopakūjitāni pramattakokilakulakilakilāni prahasitakamalakuvalayālaṃkṛtābhilaṣaṇiyajalāśayāni vividhakusumasaṃmodagandhādhivāsitasukhapavanānyupavanāni samanuvicaraṃstaṃ deśamupajagāma /
body.translated_text: Then the king of that region, wandering through the pleasure gardens — whose beauty of fresh sprouts was heightened by the spring season, humming with swarms of wandering bees and female bees, resounding with the calls of intoxicated cuckoo flocks, adorned with blooming lotuses and blue water-lilies making the pools inviting, perfumed by pleasant breezes carrying the fragrance of various flowers — came upon that place.

children.text: vicitrapuṣpastabakojjvalāni kṛtacchadānīva vasantalakṣmyā /
children.translated_text: Resplendent with clusters of colorful blossoms, as if canopied by the goddess of spring,

children.text: vācālapuṃskokilabarhiṇāni saroruhākīrṇajalāśayāni // Jm_21.6 //
children.translated_text: with vocal male cuckoos and peacocks, and pools strewn with lotuses —

children.text: samudbhavatkomalaśādvalāni vanāni mattabhramarārutāni /
children.translated_text: with tender young grass freshly sprouting, and forests humming with intoxicated bees,

children.text: ākrīḍabhūtāni manobhavasya draṣṭuṃ bhavatyeva manaḥpraharṣaḥ // Jm_21.7 //
children.translated_text: these were the pleasure grounds of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love, Kāma) — merely to behold them fills the heart with delight.

body.text: atha sa rājā savinayamabhigamya bodhisattvaṃ kṛtapratisaṃmodanakathastatraikānte nvaṣidata / sa tāṃ pravrajitāmatimanoharadarśanāmabhivīkṣya tasyā rūpaśobhayā samākṣipyamāgahṛdayo nūnamasyeyaṃ sahadharmacāriṇītyavetya lolasvabhavatvāttadapaharaṇopāyaṃ vimamarśa /
body.translated_text: Then that king, approaching the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with courtesy, having exchanged words of greeting, sat down to one side nearby. He, gazing upon that renunciant woman of exceedingly enchanting appearance, his heart being drawn by the beauty of her form, surmising 'Surely this is his companion in the religious life,' and being fickle by nature, deliberated upon a stratagem for taking her away.

children.text: śrutaprabhāvaḥ sa tapodhanānāṃ śāpārciṣaḥ kroṣahutāśanasya /
children.translated_text: He, knowing the reputed power of ascetics — the fiery arrows of the curse, the fire of the jackal's [howl] —

children.text: saṃkṣiptadhairyo 'pi manobhavena nāsminnavajñārabhaso babhūva // Jm_21.8 //
children.translated_text: though his composure was diminished by passion, did not give way to the rashness of contempt toward him. || Jm 21.8 ||

body.text: tasya buddhirabhavat - tapaḥprabhāvamasya jñātvā śakyamatra tadyuktaṃ pravartituṃ nānyathā / yadyayamasyāṃ saṃrāgavaktavyamatirvyaktamasminna tapaḥprabhāvo 'sti / atha vītarāgaḥ syānmandāpekṣo vā
body.translated_text: He thought: 'Only by knowing the extent of his ascetic power can one act fittingly here, not otherwise. If he is inclined to speak of his passion for her, then clearly there is no ascetic power in him. But if he is free from passion or has little regard [for her],

body.text: tato 'smin saṃbhāvyaṃ tapaḥprabhavamāhātmyam / iti vicintya sa rājā tapahprabhāvajijñāsayā bodhisattvaṃ hitaiṣivaduvāca - bhoḥ pravrajita pracuradhūrtasāhasikapuruṣe 'smiṃlloke na yuktamatrabhavato nirākrandeṣu vaneṣvevaṃ pratirūpayānayā sahadharmacāriṇyā saha vicaritum / asyāṃ hi te kaścidaparādhyamāno niyatasmānapyupakrośabhājanīkuryāt / paśya
body.translated_text: then the greatness born of ascetic power should be attributed to him.' Having reflected thus, the king, with a desire to test his ascetic power, spoke to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as if with good intentions: 'O renunciant, in this world full of rogues and bold villains, it is not proper for your honor to wander thus with this fitting companion in the religious life in these defenseless forests. For someone might do her wrong and thereby make even blameless you an object of reproach. Behold —

children.text: evaṃ vivikteṣu tapaḥkṛśaṃ tvāṃ dharmeṇa sārdhaṃ paribhūya kaścit /
children.translated_text: "If someone, in such secluded places, having overpowered you, emaciated by austerity, along with [your] <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: imāṃ prasahyāpaharedyadā te śokātparaṃ kiṃ bata tatra kuryāḥ // Jm_21.9 //
children.translated_text: were to carry her off by force — what more, alas, could you do then beyond grieving?" || Jm 21.9 ||

children.text: roṣaprasaṅgo hi manaḥprayāthī dharmopamardādyaśasaśca hantā /
children.translated_text: "For the impulse of anger is painful to the mind and is the destroyer of <s>Dharma</s> and fame;

children.text: vasatviyaṃ tena janānta eva strīsaṃnikarṣeṇa ca kiṃ yatīnām // Jm_21.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore let her dwell among people — and what use is the company of women to ascetics?" || Jm 21.10 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - yuktamāha mahārājaḥ / api tu śrūyatāṃ yadevaṃgate 'rthe prapadyeya -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "What the great king says is fitting. But let what I would resort to in such a case be heard:

children.text: syādatra me yaḥ pratikūlavartī darpodbhavādapratisaṃkhyayā vā /
children.translated_text: "He who would act against me here, whether from arrogance or from thoughtlessness,

children.text: vyaktaṃ na mucyeta sa jīvato me dhārādhanasyeva dhanasya reṇuḥ // Jm_21.11 //
children.translated_text: would clearly not escape while I live — as a speck of dust does not escape from a downpour of water." || Jm 21.11 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā tīvrāpekṣo 'yamasyāṃ tapaḥprabhāvahīna ityavajñāya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ tadapāyanirāśaṅkaḥ kāmarāgavaśagaḥ strīsaṃdarśanādhikṛtān puruṣān samādideśa - gacchataitāṃ pravrajitāmantaḥpuraṃ praveśayateti / tadupaśrutya sā pravrajitā vyālamṛgābhidruteva vanamṛgī bhayaviṣādaviklavamukhī bāṣpoparudhyamānanayanā gadgadāyamānakaṇṭhī tattadārtivaśādvilalāpa -
body.translated_text: Then the king, concluding that 'he is deeply attached to her and devoid of ascetic power,' contemptuous of that great being, without apprehension of any counter-measure from him, under the sway of passion, commanded the men appointed for showing women [to the palace]: 'Go and escort this renunciant woman into the inner palace.' Hearing that, the renunciant woman, like a wild doe pursued by a fierce beast, her face distressed with fear and despair, her eyes filling with tears, her throat choking with sobs, lamented in various ways under the power of her anguish:

children.text: lokasya nāmārtiparājitasya parāyaṇaṃ bhūmipatiḥ piteva /
children.translated_text: "The king is the refuge of the world that is defeated by suffering, like a father;

children.text: sa eva yasya tvanayābahuḥ syādākrandanaṃ kasya nu tena kāryam // Jm_21.12 //
children.translated_text: but he, of all people, to whom injustice should be unthinkable — before whom, then, should one cry for help?" || Jm 21.12 ||

children.text: bhraṣṭādhikārā bata lokapālā na santi vā mṛtyuvaśaṃ gatā vā /
children.translated_text: "Alas, the world-guardians have either been removed from office, or do not exist, or have passed under death's sway;

children.text: na trātumārtāniti ye sayatnā dharmo 'pi manye śrutimātrameva // Jm_21.13 //
children.translated_text: since they do not strive to rescue those in distress — I think <s>Dharma</s> too is merely a word, nothing more." || Jm 21.13 ||

children.text: kiṃ vā surairme bhagavān yadevaṃ madbhāgadheyairdhṛtamauna eva /
children.translated_text: "But what use are the gods to me, since this revered lord, even in the face of what [my] destiny demands, maintains silence?

children.text: paro 'pi tāvannau rakṣaṇīyaḥ pāpātmabhirvipratikṛṣyamāṇaḥ // Jm_21.14 //
children.translated_text: Even a stranger being dragged away by wicked people ought to be protected!" || Jm 21.14 ||

children.text: naśyeti śāpāśaninābhimṛṣṭaḥ syādyasya śailaḥ smaranīyamūrtiḥ /
children.translated_text: "He at whose curse, like a thunderbolt, a mountain would become a mere memory —

children.text: itthaṃgatāyāmapi tasya maunaṃ tathāpi jīvāmi ca mandabhāgyā // Jm_21.15 //
children.translated_text: that he is silent even when things have come to this pass — and yet I, ill-fated, still live!" || Jm 21.15 ||

children.text: pāpā kṛpāpātatarā na vāhamevaṃbidhāmāpadamabhyupetā /
children.translated_text: "Am I so sinful that I do not deserve compassion — having encountered such a calamity?

children.text: ārteṣu kārūṇyamayī pravṛttistapodhanānāṃ kimayaṃ na mārgaḥ // Jm_21.16 //
children.translated_text: Is not compassionate action toward the afflicted the very path of those rich in austerity?" || Jm 21.16 ||

children.text: śaṅke tavādyāpi tadeva citte nivartyamānāsmi na yannivṛttā /
children.translated_text: "I suspect that even now, that very [thought] is in your mind — the reason I was not turned away though I should have been;

children.text: tavāpriyeṇāpi mayepsitaṃ yadātmapriyaṃhā tadidaṃ kathaṃ me // Jm_21.17 //
children.translated_text: but that what is desired by me through even your displeasure — how can that, which destroys what is dear to oneself, be [desired] for me?" || Jm 21.17 ||

body.text: iti tāṃ pravrajitā karunavilāpākranditaruditamātraparāyaṇāṃ te rājasamādiṣṭāḥ puruṣā yānamāropya paśyata eva tasya mahasattvasyāntaḥpurāya ninyuḥ / bodhisattvo 'pi pratisaṃkhyānabalātpratinudya krodhabalaṃ tathaiba pāṃsukūlāni niḥsaṃkṣobhaḥ praśāntacetāḥ sīvyati sma / athainaṃ sa rājovāca -
body.translated_text: Thus, the men commanded by the king placed the renunciant woman — who could do nothing but pitifully wail, lament, and weep — upon a vehicle and carried her to the inner palace, right before the eyes of that great being. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, repelling the force of anger through the power of reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>), unperturbed, with a tranquil mind, continued to sew his patchwork robe. Then the king said to him:

children.text: amarṣaroṣābhinipātitākṣaraṃ taduccakairgarjitamūrjitaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: "That fierce thundering of yours — with words hurled as if by fury and wrath —

children.text: hṛtāṃ ca paśyannapi tāṃ varānanāmaśaktidīnapraśamo 'syavasthitaḥ // Jm_21.18 //
children.translated_text: yet seeing even that beautiful-faced one being carried away, you stand with the tranquility of one powerless and wretched!" || Jm 21.18 ||

children.text: taddarśaya svāṃ bhujayo ruṣaṃ vā tejastapaḥsaṃśrayasaṃbhṛtaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: "Then show your arms' fury, or the power nourished by your refuge in austerity;

children.text: ātmapramāṇagrahaṇānabhijño vyarthapratijño hyadhikaṃ na bhāti // Jm_21.19 //
children.translated_text: for one who, ignorant of the measure of his own capacity, makes empty boasts, does not shine well!" || Jm 21.19 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - avyarthapratijñameva māṃ viddhi mahārāja /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Know me to be one whose boast is not empty, O great king.

children.text: yo 'bhūnmamātra pratikūlavartī vispandamāno 'pi sa me na muktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who was my adversary here — even while thrashing about, he was not released by me;

children.text: prasahya nītaḥ praśamaṃ mayā tu tasmādyathārthaiva mama pratijñā // Jm_21.20 //
children.translated_text: he was forcibly led to peace by me — therefore my boast is true to its word." || Jm 21.20 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā tena bodhisattvasya dhairyātiśayavyañjakena praśamena samutpāditatapasviguṇasaṃbhāvanaścintāmāpede - anyadevānena brāhmaṇenābhisaṃdhāya bhāṣitam, tadaparijñāyāsmābhiścāpalakṛtamidamiti jātapratyavamarśo bodhisattvamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, his esteem for the ascetic's virtues aroused by that tranquility which revealed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s extraordinary steadfastness, fell into thought: 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> spoke with a different intention; and not having understood it, we have acted rashly.' Having come to this realization, he said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: ko 'nyastavābhūtpratikūlavartī yo visphuranneva na te vimuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Who then was that other adversary of yours who, even while struggling, was not released by you?

children.text: reṇuḥ samudyanniva toyadena kaścopanītaḥ praśamaṃ tvayātra // Jm_21.21 //
children.translated_text: Who was led to peace by you here — like a speck of dust rising before a rain-cloud?" || Jm 21.21 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu mahārāja jāte na dṛśyate yasminnajāte sādhu dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: "Listen, O great king — that which, when arisen, nothing good is seen, but when not arisen, good is clearly seen:

children.text: abhūnme sa na muktaśca krodhaḥ svāśrayabādhanaḥ // Jm_21.22 //
children.translated_text: that was my adversary and was not released by me — anger (<s>krodha</s>), which torments its own abode. || Jm 21.22 ||

children.text: yena jātena nandanti narāṇāmahitaiṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "That in which, when it arises, the ill-wishers of men rejoice —

children.text: so 'bhūnme na vimuktaśca krodhaḥ śātravanandanaḥ // Jm_21.23 //
children.translated_text: that was my adversary and was not released by me — anger, the delight of enemies. || Jm 21.23 ||

children.text: utpadyamāne yasmiṃśca sadarthaṃ na prapadyate /
children.translated_text: "That upon whose arising, good purpose does not succeed —

children.text: tamandhīkaraṇaṃ rājannahaṃ krodhamaśīśamam // Jm_21.24 //
children.translated_text: that blinding [force], O king — anger — I did not let loose. || Jm 21.24 ||

children.text: yenābhibhūtaḥ kuśalaṃ jahāti prāptādapi bhraśyata eva cārthāt /
children.translated_text: "He who, when overpowered by it, abandons what is wholesome and falls even from attained goals —

children.text: taṃ roṣamugragrahavaikṛtābhaṃ sphurantamevānayamantamantaḥ // Jm_21.25 //
children.translated_text: that fury, hideous as the deformation wrought by a fierce planetary seizure — even as it surged, I brought it to an end within." || Jm 21.25 ||

children.text: kāṣṭhādyathāgniḥ parimathyamānādudeti tasyaiva parābhavāya /
children.translated_text: "Just as fire rises from wood being churned, only for the destruction of that very [wood],

children.text: mithyāvikalpaiḥ samudīryamāṇastathā narasyātmavadhāya roṣaḥ // Jm_21.26 //
children.translated_text: so anger, stirred up by false imaginings, [leads] to the destruction of the very person [who harbors it]." || Jm 21.26 ||

children.text: dahanamiva vijṛmbhamāṇaraudraṃ śamayati yo hṛdayajvaraṃ na roṣam /
children.translated_text: "He who does not extinguish anger — the fever of the heart — as it swells forth terrifyingly like a fire,

children.text: laghurayamiti hīyate 'sya kīrtiḥ kumudasakhīva śaśiprabhā prabhāte // Jm_21.27 //
children.translated_text: his fame diminishes as 'this one is frivolous' — like the moon's glow, the friend of <s>kumuda</s> lotuses, [wanes] at dawn." || Jm 21.27 ||

children.text: parajanaduritānyacintayitvā ripumiva paśyati yastu roṣameva /
children.translated_text: "But he who, not dwelling on the wrongdoings of others, regards anger itself as the enemy,

children.text: vikasati niyamena tasya kīrtiḥ śaśina ivābhinavasya maṇḍalaśrīḥ // Jm_21.28 //
children.translated_text: his fame inevitably blossoms forth — like the beauty of the orb of the new moon." || Jm 21.28 ||

body.text: iyamaparā ca roṣasya mahādoṣatā -
body.translated_text: "And this is yet another great fault of anger:

children.text: na bhātyalaṃkāraguṇānvito 'pi krodhāgninā saṃhṛtavarṇaśobhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Even though endowed with the virtues of adornment, one whose beauty of complexion has been consumed by the fire of anger does not shine;

children.text: saroṣaśalye hṛdaye ca duḥkhaṃ mahārhaśayyāṅkagato 'pi śete // Jm_21.29 //
children.translated_text: and with the dart of anger in his heart, he lies in pain even upon a costly bed." || Jm 21.29 ||

children.text: vismṛtya cātmakṣamasiddhipakṣaṃ roṣātprayātyeva tadutpathena /
children.translated_text: "And forgetting the cause of his own success through self-control, he proceeds by the wrong path because of anger;

children.text: nihīyate yena yaśo 'rthasiddhyā tāmisrapakṣendurivātmalakṣmyā // Jm_21.30 //
children.translated_text: whereby his fame wanes, along with the attainment of his goals — like the moon in the dark fortnight [wanes] in its own splendor." || Jm 21.30 ||

children.text: roṣeṇa gacchatyanayaprapātaṃ nivāryamāṇo 'pi suhṛjjanena /
children.translated_text: "Through anger one falls into the precipice of ruin, even though restrained by well-wishing friends;

children.text: prāyeṇa vairasya jaḍatvameti hitāhitāvekṣaṇamandabuddhiḥ // Jm_21.31 //
children.translated_text: mostly one becomes hardened in enmity, dull-witted in discerning benefit from harm." || Jm 21.31 ||

children.text: krodhācca sātmīkṛtapāpakarmā śocatyapāyeṣu samāśatāni /
children.translated_text: "And through anger, having made evil deeds one's own, one grieves for hundreds [of lifetimes] in the realms of woe;

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ ripavaśca kuryustīvrāpakāroddhatamanyavo 'pi // Jm_21.32 //
children.translated_text: what more could enemies do, even with their wrath aroused by grievous offenses?" || Jm 21.32 ||

children.text: antaḥsapatnaḥ kopo 'yaṃ tadevaṃ viditaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: "This anger is an enemy within one's own breast — this I know full well;

children.text: tasyāvalepaprasaraṃ kaḥ pumān marṣayiṣyati // Jm_21.33 //
children.translated_text: what man would tolerate the spread of its arrogance?" || Jm 21.33 ||

children.text: ato na muktaḥ kopo me visphurannapi cetasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore anger was not released by me, even as it surged in my mind;

children.text: ityanarthakaraṃ śatruṃ ko hyupekṣitumarhati // Jm_21.34 //
children.translated_text: for who indeed should disregard an enemy that causes such harm?" || Jm 21.34 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā tena tasyādbhutena praśamaguṇena hṛdayagrāhakeṇa ca vacasābhiprasāditamatiruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king, his mind won over by that wondrous virtue of tranquility and by speech that captivated the heart, said:

children.text: anurūpaḥ śamasyāsya tavāyaṃ vacanakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This manner of speech of yours is fitting for such tranquility;

children.text: bahunā tu kimuktena vañcitāstvadadarśinaḥ // Jm_21.35 //
children.translated_text: but what need of much talk — those who do not see you are deceived!" || Jm 21.35 ||

body.text: ityabhipraśasyainamabhisṛtyaivāsya pādayonryapatat atyayadeśanāṃ ca cakre / tāṃ ca pravrajitāṃ kṣamayitvā vyavasarjayat, paricāraka cātmānaṃ bodhisattvasya niryātayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Having thus praised him and approaching, the king fell at his feet and made a confession of his transgression. And having appeased the renunciant woman with requests for forgiveness, he released her, and surrendered himself as an attendant of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: tadevaṃ krodhavinayācchatrūnupaśamayati, vardhayatyeva tvanyathā, iti krodhavinaye yatnaḥ kāryaḥ / evamavaireṇa vairāṇi śāmyanti, saṃyamataśca vairaṃ na cīyate / evaṃ cobhayorarthaṃ caratyakrodhana ityevamādiṣu kṣamānuśaṃsāpratisaṃyukteṣu sūtreṣu vācyam / krodhādīnavakathāyāṃ tathāgatamāhātmye ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus, through the restraint of anger, one pacifies enemies; but otherwise, one only increases them — therefore effort should be made in the restraint of anger. Likewise, 'through non-enmity, enmities are pacified; and through self-restraint, enmity does not accumulate.' And 'thus the non-angry one acts for the benefit of both [parties]' — this [story] should be cited in <s>Sūtras</s> connected with the praise of patience (<s>kṣamā</s>). Also in a discourse on the dangers of anger, and in [describing] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: // iti cuḍḍabodhijātakamekaviṃśatitamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first [story], the <s>Cuḍḍabodhi Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 22. Haṃsajātakam
body.translated_text: 22. The <s>Haṃsa Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Geese)

body.text: vinipātagatānāmapi satāṃ vṛttaṃ nālamanugantumasatpuruṣāḥ, prāgeva sugatisthānām / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even when fallen into ruin, the virtuous do not deviate from their conduct — wicked persons are unable to follow it, let alone those established in fortunate states. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila mānase mahāsarasi naikaśatasahasrasaṃkhyasya mahato haṃsayūyasyādhipatirdhṛtarāṣṭro nāma haṃsarājo babhūva / tasya nayānayaparijñānanipuṇamatirviprakṛṣṭagocarasmṛtiprabhāvaḥ ślāghanīyakulatilakabhūto dākṣyadākṣiṇyavinayabhūṣaṇaḥ sthiraśuciśīlavṛttacāritraśūraḥ khedasahiṣṇurapramādī samaravīvadhaviśāradaḥ svāmyanurāgasumukhaḥ sumukho nāma senāpatirbabhūva [āryānandasthavirastena samayena] / tau parasparapremaguṇāśrayājjvalitataraprabhāvāvāryaśiṣyamukhyāviva pariśeṣaṃ śiṣyagaṇaṃ pitṛjyeṣṭhaputrāviva ca śreṣṭhaśeṣaṃ putragaṇaṃ taddhaṃsayūthamubhayalokahitodayeṣvartheṣu samyagniveśayamānau tatpratyakṣiṇāṃ devanāgayakṣavidyādharatapasvināṃ paraṃ vismayamupajahratuḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> was the king of geese named <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the lord of a great flock of geese numbering many hundreds of thousands, at the great lake <s>Mānasa</s>. His general, named <s>Sumukha</s>, was skilled in distinguishing what is and is not in accordance with propriety, possessed the power of memory extending to far-distant ranges, was the crest-jewel of a praiseworthy family, was adorned with skill, courtesy, and deportment, was heroic in steadfast and pure conduct and character, patient under fatigue, vigilant, expert in military strategy and tactics, and favorably disposed to loyalty toward his lord — [this was the elder <s>Ānanda</s> at that time]. Those two, shining with enhanced splendor because of their mutual affection and reliance on each other's virtues, like a chief teacher and disciple, and like an elder brother and father's son [guiding] the remaining disciples and sons respectively, properly instructed that flock of geese in matters conducive to the welfare of both worlds, and aroused the utmost wonder of the gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and ascetics who witnessed them.

children.text: tāvāsaturhaṃsagaṇasya tasya śreyaḥśarīrodvahanaikakāryau /
children.translated_text: Those two served that flock of geese, their sole purpose being to bear the body of well-being,

children.text: nabhogatasyeva vihaṃgamasya pakṣau śarīrodvahanaikakāryau // Jm_22.1 //
children.translated_text: like the two wings of a bird moving through the sky, whose sole purpose is to bear the body. || Jm 22.1 ||

body.text: evaṃ tābhyāṃ tadanugṛhyamāṇaṃ haṃsayūthaṃ jagadivaṃ dharmārthavistarābhyāṃ parāṃ vṛddhimavāpa / tena ca tatsaraḥ parāṃ śobhāṃ babhāra /
body.translated_text: Thus, favored by those two, the flock of geese, like the world [blessed] by the abundance of <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Artha</s>, attained supreme growth. And through them, that lake bore supreme beauty.

children.text: kalanūpuranādena haṃsayūthena tena tat /
children.translated_text: With that flock of geese, whose anklet-like cries were melodious, wandering about,

children.text: puṇḍarīkavaneneva reje saṃcārīṇā saraḥ // Jm_22.2 //
children.translated_text: the lake was resplendent, as if with a grove of white lotuses in motion. || Jm 22.2 ||

children.text: kvacitpravisṛtairhaṃsaiḥ kvacidviṣamasaṃhataiḥ /
children.translated_text: With geese sometimes spread about, sometimes clustered in uneven groups,

children.text: chinnābhralavacitrasya jahāra nabhasaḥ śriyam // Jm_22.3 //
children.translated_text: [the lake] stole the beauty of a sky dappled with broken fragments of cloud. || Jm 22.3 ||

body.text: atha tasya haṃsādhipateḥ sarvasattvahitasumukhasya ca senāpaterguṇātiśayaprabhāvavismitamanasaḥ siddharṣividyādharadaivatagaṇāstayoḥ kīrtyāśrayābhiḥ kathābhistatra tatrābhiremire /
body.translated_text: Then the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, sages, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and deities, their minds struck with wonder at the surpassing excellence of virtues of that king of geese and his general, who was favorably disposed to the welfare of all beings, delighted everywhere in stories that took refuge in the fame of those two.

children.text: uttaptacāmīkarasaṃnikāśaṃ śrīmadvapurvyaktapadākṣarā vāk /
children.translated_text: "A body resplendent as refined gold, speech with clearly articulated syllables,

children.text: dharmābhijāto vinayo nayaśca kāvapyamū kevalahaṃsaveṣau // Jm_22.4 //
children.translated_text: nobility of birth in <s>Dharma</s>, deportment, and statecraft — are these two really mere geese in form?" || Jm 22.4 ||

body.text: guṇaprakāśairapamatsaraiḥ sā kīrtistayordikṣu vitanyamānā /
body.translated_text: That fame of theirs, displaying their virtues without jealousy, spreading through the quarters,

body.text: średdheyatāmityagamannṛpāṇāṃ sadassu yatprābhṛtavaccacāra // Jm_22.5 //
body.translated_text: gained credibility among kings, for it circulated in the assemblies as if it were a tribute-offering. || Jm 22.5 ||

body.text: tena ca samayena brahmadatto nāmānyatamo vārāṇasyāṃ rājā babhūva / sa tāṃ haṃsādhipateḥ sasenādhipaterguṇātiśayāśrayāṃ kathāṃ prātyayikāmātyadvijavṛddhaiḥ sadasi saṃstūyamānāmasakṛdupaśrutya tayordarśanaṃ pratyabhivṛddhakautūhalo naikaśāstrābhyāsanipuṇamatīn sacivānuvāca - parimṛśyatāṃ tāvadbhoḥ prasṛtanipuṇamatayaḥ kaścidupāyo yena nāstau haṃsavaryau darśanapathamapi tāvadupagacchetāmiti / atha te 'mātyāḥ svaiḥ svairmatiprabhāvairanusṛtya nītipathaṃ rājānamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Now at that time, there was a certain king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Having repeatedly heard in his court the trustworthy account of the extraordinary virtues of the lord of geese together with his commander — an account celebrated by reliable ministers and elder brahmins — his curiosity to see them both having greatly increased, he addressed his counselors, whose intellects were sharpened by study of many treatises: "Come now, gentlemen, apply your far-reaching keen minds and devise some means by which those two most excellent geese might come at least within the range of my sight." Then those ministers, each having followed the path of statecraft with their respective powers of intellect, said to the king:

children.text: sukhāśā deva bhūtāni vikarṣati tatastataḥ /
children.translated_text: The desire for pleasure, O lord, draws beings hither and thither;

children.text: sukhahetuguṇotkarṣaśrutistāvānayedyataḥ // Jm_22.6 //
children.translated_text: therefore, let the report of the excellence of pleasurable qualities bring them here. || Jm 22.6 ||

body.text: tadyādṛśe sarabhi tāvabhiratarūpāvanuśrūyete tadutkṛṣṭaraguṇaśobhamiha saraḥ kasmiṃścidaraṇyapradeśe kārayitumarhati devaḥ, pratyahaṃ ca sarvapakṣiṇāmabhayapradānaghoṣaṇām / api nāma kautūhalotpādinyā sukhahetuguṇātiśayaśrutyā tāvihākṛṣyeyātām / paśyatu devaḥ,
body.translated_text: Since those two are heard to delight in a lake of such a kind, Your Majesty should have a lake constructed in some forest region here, possessing beauty of qualities surpassing that one, and should proclaim daily the grant of safety to all birds. Perhaps through the report of the surpassing excellence of pleasurable qualities, which arouses curiosity, those two might be drawn here. Let Your Majesty consider:

children.text: prāyeṇa prāptivirasaṃ sukhaṃ deva na gaṇyate /
children.translated_text: Generally, O lord, pleasure that is readily available is not valued;

children.text: parokṣatvāttu harati śrutiramyaṃ sukhaṃ manaḥ // Jm_22.7 //
children.translated_text: but because it is remote, pleasure that is delightful to hear about captivates the mind. || Jm 22.7 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā astvetadityalpena kālena nātisaṃnikṛṣṭaṃ nagaropavanasya mānasasarasaḥ pratispardhiguṇavibhavaṃ padmotpalakumudapuṇḍarīkasaugandhikatāmarasakalhārasamūpagūḍhaṃ vimalasalilamatimanoharaṃ mahatsaraḥ kārayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then that king, saying "so be it," in a short time had a great lake constructed — not too close to the royal gardens — rivaling <s>Mānasa</s> lake in the splendor of its qualities, densely covered with lotuses, blue lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, fragrant water-plants, red lotuses, and water-lilies, with pure waters, and exceedingly enchanting:

children.text: drumaiḥ kusumasaṃchanaiścalatkisalayojjvalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With trees covered in blossoms, gleaming with trembling fresh shoots,

children.text: tatprekṣārthamivotpatraiḥ kṛtatīraparigraham // Jm_22.8 //
children.translated_text: as if stretching upward to gaze upon it, forming a border along its banks; || Jm 22.8 ||

children.text: vihasadbhirivāmbhojaistaraṃgotkampakampibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With lotuses seeming to laugh, trembling with the tremor of waves,

children.text: vilobhyamānākulitabhramadbhramarasaṃkulam // Jm_22.9 //
children.translated_text: thronged with buzzing bees bewildered as if being enticed; || Jm 22.9 ||

children.text: jyotsnāsaṃvāhanonnirdairvicitrakumudaiḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Here and there with variegated water-lilies, their petals opened by the caress of moonlight,

children.text: tarucchāyāparicchinnaiścandrikāśakalairiva // Jm_22.10 //
children.translated_text: like fragments of moonbeams bordered by the shadows of trees; || Jm 22.10 ||

children.text: taraṃgāṅgalisaṃkṣiptaiḥ kamalotpalareṇubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here and there with pollen of lotuses and blue lotuses gathered by the fingers of the waves,

children.text: abhyalaṃkṛtatīrāntaṃ hemasūtrairiva kvacit // Jm_22.11 //
children.translated_text: adorning the edges of the banks as if with threads of gold; || Jm 22.11 ||

children.text: citraiḥ padmotpaladalaistatra tatra sakesaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Bearing here and there a spread-out splendor as if made of offerings,

children.text: śriyaṃ pravitatāṃ bibhradupahāramayīmiva // Jm_22.12 //
children.translated_text: with variegated petals of lotuses and blue lotuses along with their filaments; || Jm 22.12 ||

children.text: prasannastimitāmbutvādvyaktacitravapurguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of its clear and still waters, the qualities of the colorful forms being clearly visible,

children.text: vyomnīva paridhāvadbhirmīnavṛndairalaṃkṛtam // Jm_22.13 //
children.translated_text: adorned with schools of fish darting about as if in the sky; || Jm 22.13 ||

children.text: vicchinnamuktāhārābhiḥ kvacid dviradaśīkaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here and there, with sprays from elephants resembling scattered pearl necklaces,

children.text: upalāsphālanotkīrṇamūrmicūrṇāmivodvahat // Jm_22.14 //
children.translated_text: seeming to bear powdered spray of waves struck up from striking against rocks; || Jm 22.14 ||

children.text: vidyādharavadhūsnānairmadasekaiśca dantinām /
children.translated_text: In some places, from the bathing of <s>Vidyādhara</s> maidens, from the rut-water of elephants,

children.text: rajobhiḥ kusumānāṃ ca savāsamiva kutracit // Jm_22.15 //
children.translated_text: and from the pollen of flowers, as if imbued with fragrance; || Jm 22.15 ||

children.text: tārāṇāṃ candradārāṇāṃ sāmānyamiva darpaṇam /
children.translated_text: Like a common mirror for the stars, the wives of the Moon,

children.text: muditadvijasaṃkīrṇa tadrutapratināditam // Jm_22.16 //
children.translated_text: filled with joyful birds, resounding with their calls echoing back. || Jm 22.16 ||

body.text: tadevaṃvidhaṃ saraḥ kārayitvā sarvapakṣigaṇasya cānāvṛtasukhopabhogyametaddattvā pratyahaṃ sarvapakṣiṇā viśvāsanārthamityabhayadānaghoṣaṇāṃ kārayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Having had such a lake constructed, and having given to the entire flock of birds the unrestricted enjoyment of its pleasures, he had a daily proclamation of safety made for the purpose of winning the trust of all birds:

children.text: eṣa padmotpaladalacchannatoyamidaṃ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: "This lake, its waters covered with lotus and blue lotus petals,

children.text: dadāti rājā pakṣibhyaḥ prītyā sābhayadakṣiṇam // Jm_22.17 //
children.translated_text: the king gives to the birds with affection, together with the gift of safety." || Jm 22.17 ||

body.text: atha kadācitsaṃhṛtameghāndhakārayavanikāsu śaradguṇopahṛdaśobhāsvālokanakṣamāsu dikṣu prabaddhakamalavanaśobheṣu prasannasalilamanohareṣu sarassu paraṃ kāntiyauvanamupagate praceyakiraṇa iva candramasi vividhasasyasaṃpadvibhūṣaṇadharāyāṃ vasuṃdharāyāṃ pravṛtte haṃsataruṇajanasaṃpāte mānasātsarasaḥ śaratprasannāni digantarāṇyanuvicaradanupūrveṇānyatamaṃ haṃsamithunaṃ tasmādeva haṃsayūthāttasya rājño viṣayamupajagāma / tatra ca pakṣigaṇakolāhalonnāditamanibhṛtamadhukaragaṇaṃ taraṃgamālāvicaraṇakṛtavyāpāraiḥ sukhaśiśirairmṛdubhiranilaiḥ samantato vikṣiptamāṇakamalakuvalayareṇugandhaṃ jvaladiva vikacaiḥ kamalairhasadiva vikasitaiḥ kumudaistatsaro dadarśa / tasya mānasasaraḥsamucitasyāpi haṃsamithunasya tāmatimanoharāṃ sarasaḥ śriyamabhivīkṣya prādurabhūt - aho bata tadapi haṃsayūthamihāgacchediti /
body.translated_text: Then once, when the curtains of darkness formed by the rainy-season clouds had been withdrawn, when the quarters were graced with the beauties brought by the qualities of autumn and were fit for gazing upon, when the lakes were lovely with their clear waters and adorned with groves of blooming lotuses, when the moon had attained the height of beauty and youth as if gathering rays, when the earth wore the ornament of abundant harvests of various grains, and when the season of the young geese's migration had commenced — a certain pair of geese from that very flock of the goose-king, wandering in due course through the autumn-clear regions of the sky from <s>Mānasa</s> lake, arrived in the territory of that king. There they beheld that lake, resounding with the clamor of flocks of birds, humming with restless swarms of bees, its fragrance of lotus and water-lily pollen scattered in all directions by gentle, pleasantly cool breezes whose occupation was to set the garlands of waves in motion — blazing as it were with fully-opened lotuses, laughing as it were with blooming water-lilies. Upon beholding the exceedingly enchanting beauty of that lake — worthy even of <s>Mānasa</s> lake — the goose-pair thought: "Oh, if only that flock of geese too would come here!"

children.text: prāyeṇa khalu lokasya prāpya sādhāraṇaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: Generally indeed, when beings obtain a common pleasure,

children.text: smṛtiḥ snehānusāreṇa pūrvameti suhṛjjanam // Jm_22.18 //
children.translated_text: their memory, following the course of affection, goes first to their dear ones. || Jm 22.18 ||

body.text: atha tatra taddhaṃsamithunaṃ yathākāmaṃ vihṛtya pravṛtte jaladasamaye vidyudvisphuritaśastravikṣepeṣu nātighanavicchinnāndhakārarūpeṣu samabhivartamāneṣu daityānīkeṣviva jaladharavṛndeṣu paripūrṇabarhakalāpaśobheṣu prasaktakekāninādotkruṣṭairjaladharavijayamiva saṃrādhayatsu nṛttapravṛtteṣu citreṣu barhigaṇeṣu vācālatāmupagateṣu stokaśukaniṣu pravicaratsu kadambasarjārjunaketakīpuṣpagandhādhivāsiteṣu sukhaśiśireṣu kānanaviniścasiteṣvivānileṣu meghadaśanapaṃktiṣvivālakṣyamāṇarūpāsu balākāyuvatiṣu gamanautsukyamṛdunikūjiteṣu prayāṇavyākuleṣu haṃsayūtheṣu taddhaṃsamithunaṃ mānasameva saraḥ pratyājagāma / samupetya ca haṃsādhipatisamīpaṃ prastutāsu digdeśakathāsu taṃ tasya saraso guṇaviśeṣaṃ varṇayāmāsa - asti deva dakṣiṇena himavato vārāṇasyāṃ brahmadatto nāma narādhipatiḥ / tenātyadbhūtarūpaśobhamanirvarṇyaguṇasaundaryaṃ mahatsaraḥ pakṣibhyaḥ svacchandasukhopabhogyaṃ dattam /
body.translated_text: Then, after that goose-pair had sported there as they pleased, when the rainy season had set in — when the massed clouds were like advancing armies of <s>Daityas</s> with weapons flashing as lightning, their forms of dense, scarcely-broken darkness — when the splendid peacocks with their fully-spread tail-plumes were engaged in dancing, as if celebrating the victory of the rain-clouds with their persistent cries of exultation — when the <s>Śuka</s> (parrot) birds had become talkative — when the breezes, cool and pleasant, perfumed with the fragrance of <s>Kadamba</s>, <s>Sarja</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and <s>Ketakī</s> flowers, wandered about like the murmuring of forests — when the rows of cranes, barely visible, were like rows of teeth of the clouds — when the flocks of geese were restless for departure, cooing softly with the eagerness to travel — that goose-pair returned to <s>Mānasa</s> lake itself. And having approached the lord of the geese, when conversations about various lands and regions had begun, they described to him the special qualities of that lake: "O lord, to the south of the <s>Himavat</s>, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there is a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s>. He has given to the birds a great lake of astonishingly beautiful form and indescribable beauty of qualities, to be enjoyed at their own pleasure.

body.text: abhayaṃ ca pratyahamavaghuṣyate / ramante cātra pakṣiṇaḥ svagṛha iva prahīnabhayāśaṅkā / tadarhati devo vyatītāsu varṣāsu tatra gantumiti / tacchrutvā sarva eva te haṃsāstatsaṃdarśanasamutsukā babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: And safety is proclaimed daily. The birds sport there free from fear and apprehension, as if in their own homes. Therefore, Your Majesty should deign to go there when the rains have passed." Having heard this, all those geese became eager to see that lake.

body.text: atha bhodhisattvaḥ sumukhaṃ senāpatiṃ praśanavyaktākāraṃ pratataṃ dadarśa, kathaṃ paśyasīti cāvocat / atha sumukhaḥ praṇamyainamuvāca - na prāptaṃ tatra devasya gamanamiti paśyāmi / kutaḥ? amūni tāvallobhanīyāni manoharāṇyāmiṣabhūtāni rūpāṇi / na ca naḥ kiṃcidiha parihīyate / kṛtakamadhuropacāravacanapracchannatīkṣṇadaurātmyāni ca prāyeṇa pelavaghṛṇāni śaṭhāni mānuṣahṛdayāni / paśyatu svāmī,
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> noticed that <s>Sumukha</s>, the commander, had a calm but clearly thoughtful expression, and asked: "What is your view?" Then <s>Sumukha</s>, bowing to him, said: "I see that it is not fitting for Your Majesty to go there. Why? These are indeed alluring, captivating forms that serve as bait. And nothing here is lacking for us. Moreover, human hearts are generally of fickle compassion and deceitful, their sharp malice concealed beneath artfully contrived sweet words of hospitality. Let my lord consider:

children.text: vāśitārthasvahṛdayaḥ prāyeṇa mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Animals and birds generally have hearts devoted to their own desires;

children.text: manuṣyāḥ punarekīyāstadviparyayanaipuṇāḥ // Jm_22.19 //
children.translated_text: but humans, belonging to another order, are skilled in the very opposite. || Jm 22.19 ||

children.text: ucyate nāma madhuraṃ svanubandhi niratyayam /
children.translated_text: Sweet words are spoken that seem harmless and without consequence,

children.text: vaṇijo 'pi hi kurvanti lābhasiddhyāśayā vyayam // Jm_22.20 //
children.translated_text: for even merchants incur expenditure with the hope of gaining profit. || Jm 22.20 ||

children.text: yato naitāvatā deva visrambhaḥ kṣamate kvacit /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O lord, confidence is never warranted by such things alone;

children.text: kāryārthamapi na śreyaḥ sātyayāpanayaḥ kramaḥ // Jm_22.21 //
children.translated_text: even for a worthy purpose, a course of action that courts danger is not beneficial. || Jm 22.21 ||

body.text: yadi tvavaśyameva tatra gantavyam, gatvānubhūya ca tasya saraso guṇavibhūtirasaṃ na nastatra ciraṃ vicarituṃ kṣamaṃ nivāsāya vā cittamabhināmayitumiti paśyāmi / atha bodhisattvaḥ prāptāyāṃ vimalacandrakṣatratārāvibhūṣaṇāyāṃ rajanyāṃ śaradi tena haṃsayūthena vārāṇasīsaraḥsaṃdarśanaṃ pratyabhivṛddhakautūhalena tadabhigamanārthaṃ punaḥ punarvijñāpyamānasteṣāṃ haṃsānāmanuvṛttyā sumukhapramukheṇa mahatā haṃsagaṇena parivṛttaścandramā iva śaradabhṛvṛdena tatrābhijagāma /
body.translated_text: If, however, we absolutely must go there, I think that having gone and experienced the delightful qualities of that lake, it would not be proper for us to linger there long or to incline our minds toward settling there." Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when the autumn arrived with its nights adorned by the pure moon, constellations, and stars, being repeatedly entreated by that flock of geese — whose curiosity to see the lake of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> had greatly increased — to go there, in compliance with those geese, surrounded by a great flock of geese led by <s>Sumukha</s>, traveled there like the moon encircled by an autumn mass of clouds.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva lakṣmī sarasastu tasya teṣāṃ praharṣākulavismayānām /
children.translated_text: Upon seeing the splendor of that lake, their wonder was agitated with joy;

children.text: citraprakārā rucisaṃniveśāstatsaṃśraye tulyaguṇā babhūvuḥ // Jm_22.22 //
children.translated_text: the various arrangements of beauty became, upon taking shelter there, equal in quality to their own. || Jm 22.22 ||

children.text: yanmānasādabhyadhikaṃ babhūva taistairavasthātiśayaiḥ sarastat /
children.translated_text: That lake surpassed <s>Mānasa</s> in those various degrees of excellence,

children.text: ataściraṃ tadgatamānasānāṃ na mānase mānasamāsa teṣām // Jm_22.23 //
children.translated_text: and therefore, their minds being fixed upon it, their thoughts were no longer on <s>Mānasa</s>. || Jm 22.23 ||

body.text: tatra te tāmabhayaghoṣaṇāmupalabhya svacchandatāṃ ca pakṣigaṇasya tasya ca saraso vibhūtsā pramuditahṛdayāstatrodyānayātrāmivānubhavantaḥ parāṃ prītisaṃpadamupajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: There, having heard that proclamation of safety and observing the freedom of the flocks of birds and the splendor of that lake, their hearts delighted, they experienced the highest attainment of joy as if enjoying a pleasure excursion in a royal garden.

body.text: atha tasmin sarasyadhikṛtāḥ puruṣāsteṣāṃ haṃsānāṃ tatrāgamanaṃ rājñe pratyavedayanta - yādṛśaguṇarūpau
body.translated_text: Then the men appointed over that lake reported to the king the arrival of those geese there: "Those two most excellent geese, whose qualities and form are heard to be such

body.text: deva tau haṃsavaryāvanuśrūyete tadṛśāveva [haṃsavaryau]kanakāvadātarucirapatrau tapanīyojjvalataravadanacaraṇaśobhāvadhikatarapramāṇau susaṃsthitadehau naikahaṃsaśatasahasraparivārau devasya saraḥ śobhayitumivānuprāptāviti / atha sa rājā śākunikakarmaṇi prasiddhaprakāśanaipuṇaṃ śākunikagaṇe samanvipya tadgrahaṇārthaṃ sādaramanvādideśa / sa tatheti pratiśrutya taryorhaṃsayorgocaravihārapradeśaṃ samyagupalabhya tatra tatra dṛḍhānnigūḍhān pāśān nyadadhāt / atha teṣāṃ haṃsānāṃ viśvāsādapāyanirāśaṅkānāṃ pramododdhatamanasāṃ vicaratāṃ sa haṃsādhipatiḥ pāśena caraṇe nyabadhyata /
body.translated_text: — O lord, those two foremost geese are exactly as described: with beautiful plumage of golden radiance, with beaks and feet of even more brilliant golden luster, of surpassing stature, well-proportioned in body, attended by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of geese — they have arrived as if to adorn Your Majesty's lake." Then that king, having searched among his guild of fowlers for one renowned and skilled in the craft of bird-catching, dispatched him with eager respect to capture those two. He, having assented with "so be it," carefully ascertained the feeding and sporting grounds of those two geese, and there and there laid strong, concealed snares. Then, as those geese wandered about free from suspicion of danger due to their trust, their minds elated with joy, the lord of the geese was caught by the foot in a snare.

children.text: vismṛtātyayaśaṅkānāṃ sūkṣmairviśvāsanakramaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through subtle means of building trust, for those who have forgotten the apprehension of danger,

children.text: vikarotyeva viśrambhaḥ pramādāpanayākaraḥ // Jm_22.24 //
children.translated_text: confidence, which is a source of negligence, inevitably brings about calamity. || Jm 22.24 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo mā bhūdanyasyāpi kasyacittatraivaṃvidho vyasanopanipāta iti rutaviśeṣeṇa sapratibhayatāṃ sarasaḥ prakāśayāmāsa / atha te (haṃsā) haṃsādhipatibandhādvyathitahṛdayā bhayavirasavyākulavirāvāḥ parasparanirapekṣā hatapravīrā iva sainikā divaṃ samutpetuḥ / sumukhastu haṃsasenādhipatirhaṃsādhipatisamīpānaiva vicacāla /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thinking "let no other suffer such a misfortune here," made known the danger of the lake by a distinctive cry. Then those geese, their hearts distressed by the capture of their lord, uttering cries confused with fear and dismay, heedless of one another, flew up into the sky like soldiers whose champion has been slain. But <s>Sumukha</s>, the commander of the geese, did not stir from the side of the goose-king.

children.text: snehāvabaddhāni hi mānasāni prāṇatyayaṃ svaṃ na vicintayanti /
children.translated_text: For minds bound by affection do not consider the loss of their own lives;

children.text: prāṇātyayād duḥkhataraṃ yadeṣāṃ suhṛjjanasya vyasanārtidainyam // Jm_22.25 //
children.translated_text: since more painful than the loss of their own lives is the misery and wretchedness of their dear ones in calamity. || Jm 22.25 ||

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to him:

children.text: gaccha gacchaiva sumukha kṣamaṃ neha vilambitum /
children.translated_text: "Go, go at once, <s>Sumukha</s>! It is not proper to linger here,

children.text: sāhāyyasyāvakāśo hi kastavetthaṃgate mayi // Jm_22.26 //
children.translated_text: for what scope is there for assistance when I am in such a state?" || Jm 22.26 ||

body.text: sumukha uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Sumukha</s> said:

children.text: naikāntiko mṛtyuriha sthitasya na gacchataḥ syādajarāmaratvam /
children.translated_text: "Death is not certain for one who stays, nor will immortality and freedom from old age come to one who departs;

children.text: sukheṣu ca tvāṃ samupāsya nityamāpadgataṃ mānada kena jahyām // Jm_22.27 //
children.translated_text: having always attended upon you in happiness, O bestower of honor, by what reason should I abandon you in misfortune? || Jm 22.27 ||

children.text: svaprāṇatantumātrārthaṃ tyajatastvāṃ khagādhipa /
children.translated_text: For those who would abandon you, O lord of birds, merely to preserve the thread of their own lives —

children.text: dhigvādavṛṣṭyāvaraṇaṃ katamanme bhaviṣyati // Jm_22.28 //
children.translated_text: shame upon them! What shield against reproach will there be for me? || Jm 22.28 ||

children.text: naiṣa dharmo mahārāja tyajeyaṃ tvāṃ yadāpadi /
children.translated_text: It is not <s>Dharma</s> (righteous duty), O great king, that I should abandon you in adversity;

children.text: yā gatistava sā mahyaṃ rocate vihagādhipa // Jm_22.29 //
children.translated_text: whatever fate is yours, that same fate is pleasing to me, O lord of birds. || Jm 22.29 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kā nu pāśena baddhasya gatiranyā mahānasāt /
children.translated_text: "What fate other than the cooking-fire is there for one bound in a snare?

children.text: sā kathaṃ svasthacittasya muktasyābhimatā tava // Jm_22.30 //
children.translated_text: How then can that same fate be desired by you, who are free and of sound mind? || Jm 22.30 ||

children.text: paśyasyevaṃ kamarthaṃ vā tvaṃ mamātmana eva vā /
children.translated_text: Consider — for whose sake do you do this? For mine, or for yourself,

children.text: jñātīnāṃ vāvaśeṣāṇāmubhayorjīvitakṣaye // Jm_22.31 //
children.translated_text: or for the remaining kinsmen, when both our lives would be lost? || Jm 22.31 ||

children.text: lakṣyate ca na yatrārthastamasīva samāsamam /
children.translated_text: And where no purpose can be discerned, that is like meeting darkness with darkness."

children.text: tādṛśe saṃtyajan prāṇān kamarthaṃ dyotayedbhavān // Jm_22.32 //
children.translated_text: Why would you, in such circumstances, abandoning your life, illuminate the purpose? // Jm_22.32 //

body.text: sumukha uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Sumukha</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ nu patatāṃ śreṣṭha dharme 'rthaṃ na samīkṣase /
children.translated_text: How is it, O best of birds, that you do not perceive the purpose in <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: dharmo hyupacitaḥ samyagāvahatyarthamuttamam // Jm_22.33 //
children.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s>, when properly cultivated, yields the highest good. // Jm_22.33 //

children.text: so 'haṃ dharmaṃ ca saṃpaśyan dharmāccārthaṃ samutthitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore I, perceiving <s>dharma</s> and the good that arises from <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tava mānada bhaktyā ca nābhikāṅkṣāmi jīvitam // Jm_22.34 //
children.translated_text: and out of devotion to you, O bestower of honor, do not long for life. // Jm_22.34 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: addhā dharmaḥ satāmeṣa yatsakhā mitramāpadi /
children.translated_text: Truly, this is the <s>dharma</s> of the virtuous: that a companion should not abandon a friend in adversity,

children.text: na tyajejjīvitasyāpi hetordharmamanusmaran // Jm_22.35 //
children.translated_text: not even for the sake of life, remembering <s>dharma</s>. // Jm_22.35 //

children.text: tadarcitastvayā dharmo bhaktirmayi ca darśitā /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dharma</s> has been honored by you, and devotion to me has been shown.

children.text: yācñjāmantyāṃ kuruṣvemāṃ gacchaivānumato mayā // Jm_22.36 //
children.translated_text: Fulfill this, my final request: go forth, with my permission. // Jm_22.36 //

children.text: api caivaṃgate kārye yadūnaṃ suhṛdāṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in this state of affairs, whatever remains unfulfilled by me toward our companions,

children.text: tattvayā matisaṃpanna bhavetparamasaṃbhṛtam // Jm_22.37 //
children.translated_text: let that be most perfectly attended to by you, O wise one. // Jm_22.37 //

children.text: paraspapremaguṇāditi saṃjalpatostayoḥ /
children.translated_text: As the two were thus conversing, by virtue of their mutual affection,

children.text: pratyadṛśyata naiṣādaḥ sākṣānmṛtyurivāpatan // Jm_22.38 //
children.translated_text: the fowler appeared, swooping down like Death himself. // Jm_22.38 //

body.text: atha tau haṃsavaryau niṣādamāpatantamālokya tūṣṇīṃ babhūvatuḥ / sa ca taddhaṃsayūthaṃ vidrutamālokya nūnamatra kaścidvaddha iti niścitamatiḥ pāśasthānānyanuvicaraṃstau haṃsavaryau dadarśa / sa tadrūpaśobhayā vismitamanā baddhāviti manyamānastatsamāpannau pāśāvudghaṭṭayāmāsa / athaikaṃ baddhamabaddhenetareṇa svasthenopāsyamānamavekṣya vismitatarahṛdayaḥ sumukhamupetyovāca -
body.translated_text: Then those two lordly geese, seeing the fowler approaching, fell silent. And he, seeing the flock of geese scattered, concluded that surely one must be trapped here, and searching through the snare-sites, he beheld those two lordly geese. Astonished in mind at their beauty of form, thinking them both bound, he tried to loosen the two snares that had caught them. Then, observing that one was bound while the other, unbound and unharmed, was attending upon its companion, his heart struck with even greater wonder, he approached <s>Sumukha</s> and said:

children.text: ayaṃ pāśena mahatā dvijaḥ saṃhṛtavikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: This bird has been subdued by a great snare, his power restrained;

children.text: vyoma nāsmatprapadyeta mayyapyantikamāgate // Jm_22.39 //
children.translated_text: he could not take to the sky, even with me approaching. // Jm_22.39 //

children.text: avaddhastvaṃ punaḥ svasthaḥ sajjapatrarathī balī /
children.translated_text: But you are unbound, sound, with wings and pinions ready, and strong.

children.text: kasmātprāpte 'pi mayyevaṃ vegānna bhajase nabhaḥ // Jm_22.40 //
children.translated_text: Why, even though I have arrived, do you not swiftly take to the sky? // Jm_22.40 //

body.text: tadupaśrutya sumukhaḥ pravyaktākṣarapadavinyāsena svabhāvavarṇanādhairyaguṇaujasvinā svareṇa mānuṣīṃ vācamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Sumukha</s>, with clearly articulated syllables and words, in a voice resplendent with the qualities of natural eloquence and steadfast courage, spoke in human speech:

children.text: śaktisthaḥ sanna gacchāmi yadidaṃ tatra kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Though possessing the ability, I do not go; and the reason for that is this:

children.text: ayaṃ pāśaparikleśaṃ vihaṃgaḥ prāptavāniti // Jm_22.41 //
children.translated_text: this bird has fallen into the affliction of the snare. // Jm_22.41 //

children.text: ayaṃ pāśena mahatā saṃyataścaraṇe tvayā /
children.translated_text: This one has been bound at the feet by you with a great snare,

children.text: guṇairasyatu baddho 'hamato dṛdhatarairhṛdi // Jm_22.42 //
children.translated_text: but I am bound in my heart by his virtues, which are far stronger. // Jm_22.42 //

body.text: atha sa naiṣādaḥ paramavismitamatiḥ saṃhṛṣitatanūruhaḥ sumukhaṃ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that fowler, supremely astonished in mind, his hair standing on end, said again to <s>Sumukha</s>:

children.text: tyaktvainaṃ madbhayadanye diśo haṃsāḥ samaśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: The other geese, abandoning him out of fear of me, have fled to every direction.

children.text: tvaṃ punarna tyajasyenaṃ ko nvayaṃ bhavato dvija // Jm_22.43 //
children.translated_text: Yet you do not forsake him — who then is this to you, O bird? // Jm_22.43 //

body.text: sumukha uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Sumukha</s> said:

children.text: rājā mama prāṇasamaḥ sakhā ca sukhasya dātā viṣamasthitaśca /
children.translated_text: He is my king, dear as my very life, my companion, the giver of happiness, and steadfast in adversity;

children.text: naivotsahe yena vihātumenaṃ svajīvitasyāpyanurakṣaṇārtham // Jm_22.44 //
children.translated_text: therefore I cannot bring myself to abandon him, even for the sake of preserving my own life. // Jm_22.44 //

body.text: atha sumukhaḥ prasādavismayāvarjitamānasaṃ taṃ naiṣādamavetya punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sumukha</s>, perceiving that the fowler's mind had been won over by grace and wonder, spoke again:

children.text: apyasmākamiyaṃ bhadra saṃbhāṣā syātsukhodayā /
children.translated_text: May this conversation of ours, good sir, prove to be the occasion of happiness.

children.text: apyasmān visṛjannadya dharmyāṃ kīrtimavāpnuyāḥ // Jm_22.45 //
children.translated_text: May you, by releasing us today, attain righteous fame. // Jm_22.45 //

body.text: naiṣāda uvāca -
body.translated_text: The fowler said:

children.text: naiva te duḥkhamicchāmi na ca baddho bhavān mayā /
children.translated_text: I do not wish suffering upon you, nor is it you who has been bound by me.

children.text: sa tvaṃ gaccha yathākāmaṃ paśya bandhūṃśca nandaya // Jm_22.46 //
children.translated_text: Go as you please, behold your kinsmen, and bring them joy. // Jm_22.46 //

body.text: sumukha uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Sumukha</s> said:

children.text: no cedicchasi me duḥkhaṃ tatkuruṣva mamārthanām /
children.translated_text: If you do not wish my suffering, then fulfill my entreaty:

children.text: ekena yadi tuṣṭo 'si tattyajainaṃ gṛhāṇaṃ mām // Jm_22.47 //
children.translated_text: if you are satisfied with one, then release him and take me instead. // Jm_22.47 //

children.text: tulyārohaparīṇāhau samānau vayasā ca nau /
children.translated_text: We are equal in size and girth, and alike in age;

children.text: viddhi niṣkraya ityasya na te 'haṃ lābhahānaye // Jm_22.48 //
children.translated_text: know me to be his ransom — I am not to your loss or disadvantage. // Jm_22.48 //

children.text: tadaṅga samavekṣasva gṛddhirbhavatu te mayi /
children.translated_text: Come then, consider this: let your desire be directed toward me.

children.text: māṃ badhnātu bhavān pūrvaṃ paścānmuñceda dvijādhipam // Jm_22.49 //
children.translated_text: Let your honor bind me first, and afterward release the lord of birds. // Jm_22.49 //

children.text: tāvāneva ca lābhaste kṛtā syānmama cārthanā /
children.translated_text: Your gain would be just the same, my entreaty would be fulfilled,

children.text: haṃsayūthasya ca prītirmaitrī tena tathaiva ca // Jm_22.50 //
children.translated_text: and the flock of geese would be gladdened, and friendship with him likewise preserved. // Jm_22.50 //

children.text: paśyantu tāvadbhavatā vimuktaṃ haṃsādhipaṃ haṃsagaṇāḥ pratītāḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the flocks of geese, trusting and joyful, behold the lord of geese released by your hand,

children.text: virocamānaṃ nabhasi prasanne daityendranirmuktamivoḍurājam // Jm_22.51 //
children.translated_text: shining in the clear sky, like the lord of stars freed from the demon-king. // Jm_22.51 //

body.text: atha sa naiṣādaḥ krūratābhyasakaṭhinahṛdayo 'pi tena tasya jīvitanirapekṣeṇa svāmyanurāgaślāghinā kṛtajñatāgunaujasvinā dhairyamādhuryālaṃkṛtavacasā samāvarjitahṛdayo vismayagauravavaśāṭsamānītāñjaliḥ sumukhamuvāsa - sādhu sādhu mahābhāga
body.translated_text: Then that fowler, though his heart was hardened by habitual cruelty, had his heart won over by <s>Sumukha</s>'s words — heedless of his own life, glorying in devotion to his lord, resplendent with the quality of gratitude, adorned with steadfastness and sweetness — and, brought to joined palms by the force of wonder and reverence, said to <s>Sumukha</s>: "Well done, well done, O greatly fortunate one!

children.text: mānuṣeṣvapyayaṃ dharma āścaryo daivateṣu vā /
children.translated_text: Even among humans or among the gods, this <s>dharma</s> would be wondrous —

children.text: svāmyarthaṃtyajatā prāṇān yastvayātra pradarśitaḥ // Jm_22.52 //
children.translated_text: that which you have displayed here, sacrificing your life for the sake of your lord. // Jm_22.52 //

children.text: tadeṣa te vimucāmi rājanamanumānayan /
children.translated_text: Therefore I release this king of yours, showing him due honor.

children.text: ko hi prāṇāpriyatare tavāsmin vipriyaṃ carat // Jm_22.53 //
children.translated_text: For who could act with unkindness toward one dearer to you than life itself? // Jm_22.53 //

body.text: ityuktvā sa naiṣādastasya nṛapteḥ saṃdeśamanādṛtya haṃsarājaṃ samanumānayan dayāsumukhaṃ pāśānmumoca /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that fowler, disregarding the king's commission, showing honor to the king of geese and compassion to <s>Sumukha</s>, released him from the snare.

body.text: atha sumukhaḥ senāpatirhaṃsarājavimokṣātparamānanditahṛdayaḥ prītyabhisnigdhamudīkṣamāṇo naiṣādamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Sumukha</s> the general, his heart supremely overjoyed at the liberation of the king of geese, gazing at the fowler with eyes moist with affection, said:

children.text: yathā suhṛnnandana nandito 'smi tvayādya haṃsādhipatervimokṣāt /
children.translated_text: Just as I have been delighted today, O joy of friends, by your release of the lord of geese,

children.text: evaṃ suhṛjjñātigaṇena bhadra śaratsahastrāṇi bahūni nanda // Jm_22.54 //
children.translated_text: so may you rejoice for many thousands of autumns, good sir, surrounded by friends and kinsmen. // Jm_22.54 //

children.text: tanmā tavāyaṃ viphalaḥ śramo bhūdādāya māṃ haṃsagaṇādhipaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let not this effort of yours be in vain — taking me along with the lord of the goose-flock,

children.text: svasthāvabaddhāvadhiropya kācamantaḥpure darśaya bhūmipāya // Jm_22.55 //
children.translated_text: place us both, unharmed and unbound, upon a palanquin and present us to the king in his inner palace. // Jm_22.55 //

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ prītamanāḥ sa rājā haṃsāvipaṃ sānucaraṃ samīkṣya /
children.translated_text: Without doubt, that king, his mind delighted upon beholding the lord of geese with his minister,

children.text: dāsyatyasaṃbhāvitavistarāṇi dhānāni te prītivivardhanāni // Jm_22.56 //
children.translated_text: will bestow upon you gifts of unimaginable magnitude, increasing your joy. // Jm_22.56 //

body.text: atha naiṣādastasya nirbandhāt paśyatu tāvadatyadbhutamidaṃ haṃsayutaṃ sa rājeti kṛtvā te haṃsamukhyau kācenādaya svasthāvabaddhau rājñe darśayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the fowler, at his insistence, thinking "Let the king behold this most wondrous pair of geese," took those two lordly geese upon a palanquin, unharmed and unbound, and presented them to the king.

children.text: upāyanāścaryamidaṃ draṣṭumarhasi mānada /
children.translated_text: "Deign to behold this wondrous offering, O bestower of honor:

children.text: sasenāpatirānītaḥ so 'yaṃ haṃsapatirmayā // Jm_22.57 //
children.translated_text: this lord of geese has been brought by me, together with his general." // Jm_22.57 //

body.text: atha sa rājā praharṣavismayāpūrṇamatirdṛṣṭvā tī haṃsapradhānī kāñcanapuñjāvivaśriyābhijvalanmanohararūpau taṃ naiṣādamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, his mind filled with delight and wonder, beholding those two foremost geese, resplendent in beauty like heaps of gold, with captivating forms that blazed with splendor, said to the fowler:

children.text: svasthāvabaddhāvamukau vihaṃgau bhūmicāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: These two birds are unharmed, unbound, and free, walking upon the ground;

children.text: tava hastamanuprāptau kathaṃ kathaya vistaram // Jm_22.58 //
children.translated_text: how did they come into your hands? Tell me in full detail. // Jm_22.58 //

body.text: ityukte sa naiṣādaḥ praṇamya rājānamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the fowler, bowing before the king, said:

children.text: nihitā bahavaḥ pāśā mayā dāruṇadāruṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many snares, exceedingly cruel, were laid by me

children.text: vihagākriḍadeśeṣu palvaleṣu sarassu ca // Jm_22.59 //
children.translated_text: in the pleasure-grounds of birds, in marshes, and in lakes. // Jm_22.59 //

children.text: atha visrambhaniḥśaṅko haṃsavaryaścarannayam /
children.translated_text: Then this lordly goose, roaming about in trusting fearlessness,

children.text: paricchannena pāśena caraṇe samabadhyata // Jm_22.60 //
children.translated_text: was caught at the feet by a concealed snare. // Jm_22.60 //

children.text: abaddhastamupāsīno māmayaṃ samayācata /
children.translated_text: Seeing this one, <s>Sumukha</s>, unbound yet standing as though bound, out of affection for him,

children.text: ātmānaṃ tiṣkrayaṃ kṛtvā haṃsarājasya jīvitam // Jm_22.61 //
children.translated_text: he addressed him with gentle words alone, filled with curiosity and wonder. // Jm_22.61 //

children.text: visṛjanmānuṣīṃ vācaṃ vispaṣṭamadhurākṣarām /
children.translated_text: Uttering human speech with distinctly sweet syllables,

children.text: svajīvitaparityāgādyācñāmapyūrjitakramām // Jm_22.62 //
children.translated_text: and a plea made powerful by the willingness to sacrifice his own life, // Jm_22.62 //

children.text: tenāsya vākyena supeśalena svāmyarthadhīreṇa ca ceṣṭitena /
children.translated_text: by his graceful words and by his conduct, steadfast for the sake of his lord,

children.text: tathā prasanno 'smi yathāsya bhartā mayā samaṃ krūratayaiva muktaḥ // Jm_22.63 //
children.translated_text: I was so moved that his master was released by me, along with my cruelty itself. // Jm_22.63 //

children.text: atha vihagapaterayaṃ vimokṣānmuditamatirbahudhā vadan priyāṇi /
children.translated_text: Then, his mind gladdened by the liberation of the lord of birds, speaking many kind words,

children.text: tvadabhiṃgama iti nyayojayanmāṃ viphalaguruḥ kila mā mama śramo bhūt // Jm_22.64 //
children.translated_text: he directed me to come before you, saying 'Let not my effort be in vain.' // Jm_22.64 //

children.text: tadevamatidhārmikaḥ khagavarākṛtiḥ ko 'pyasau
children.translated_text: Thus, that supremely righteous one, whoever he may be, in the form of a bird,

children.text: mamāpi hṛdi mārdavaṃ janitavān kṣaṇenaiva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: who in an instant produced tenderness even in my heart —

children.text: khagādhipatimokṣaṇaṃ kṛtamanusmaran matkṛte
children.translated_text: remembering the release of the bird-lord accomplished for my sake,

children.text: sahādhipatināgataḥ svayamayaṃ ca te 'ntaḥpuram // Jm_22.65 //
