children.translated_text: he has come of his own accord, together with his chief, to your inner palace. // Jm_22.65 //

body.text: tadupaśrutya sa rājā sapramodavismayena manasā vividharatnaprabhodbhāsurasurucirapādaṃ parārdhyāstaraṇaracanābhirāmaṃ śrimatsukhopāśrayasāṭopamupahitapādapīṭhaṃ rājādhyāsanayogyaṃ kāñcanamāsanaṃ haṃsarājāya samādideśaḥ, amātyamukhyādhyāsanayogyaṃ ca vetrāsanaṃ sumukhāya /
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, with a mind full of delight and wonder, directed that a golden seat be given to the king of geese — one fit for a sovereign, with a beautiful footstool placed before it, resplendent with the radiance of various gems, charming with the arrangement of costly coverlets, and possessing the splendor of a magnificent and comfortable resting place — and a cane seat worthy of a chief minister for <s>Sumukha</s>.

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kāla idānīṃ pratisaṃmoditumiti nūpurārāvamadhureṇa svareṇa rājānamābabhāṣe -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thinking "Now is the time to return the greeting," addressed the king in a voice as sweet as the tinkling of anklets:

children.text: dyutikāntiniketane śarīre kuśalaṃ te kuśalārha kaccidasmin /
children.translated_text: "Is all well with you, O worthy of welfare, in this body that is the abode of radiance and beauty?

children.text: api dharmaśarīramavraṇaṃ te vipulairucchvasitīva vākpradānaiḥ // Jm_22.66 //
children.translated_text: Is your body of <s>dharma</s> without wounds, and does it breathe freely, as it were, through abundant gifts of speech? // Jm_22.66 //

children.text: api rakṣaṇadīkṣitaḥ prajānāṃ samayānugrahavigrahapravṛttyā /
children.translated_text: Consecrated to the protection of your subjects, through the exercise of treaties, favors, and force,

children.text: abhivardhayase svakīrtiśobhamanurāgaṃ jagato hitodayaṃ ca // Jm_22.67 //
children.translated_text: do you increase the luster of your fame, the affection of the world, and the arising of its welfare? // Jm_22.67 //

children.text: api śuddhatayopadhāsvasaktairanuraktairnipuṇakriyairamātyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With ministers who are devoted, free from treachery and self-interest, and skilled in their duties,

children.text: samavekṣayase hitaṃ prajānāṃ na ca tatrāsi parokṣabuddhireva // Jm_22.68 //
children.translated_text: do you look after the welfare of your subjects, and are you not merely one who relies on the judgment of others in this matter? // Jm_22.68 //

children.text: nayavikramasaṃhṛtapratāpairapi sāmantanṛpaiḥ prayācyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though entreated by vassal kings whose might has been subdued by your statecraft and valor,

children.text: upayāsi dayānuvṛttiśobhāṃ na ca viśvāsamayīṃ pramādanidrām // Jm_22.69 //
children.translated_text: do you practice the grace of compassion, yet not fall into the sleep of negligent trust? // Jm_22.69 //

children.text: api dharmasukhārthanirvirodhāstava ceṣṭā naravira sajjaneṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Are your undertakings free from conflict among <s>dharma</s>, pleasure, and profit, and pleasing to the virtuous, O hero among men?

children.text: vitatā iva dikṣu kīrtisiddhyā ripubhirniśvasitairasatkriyante // Jm_22.70 //
children.translated_text: Spread through the quarters by the accomplishment of fame, are they honored even by enemies with their sighs? // Jm_22.70 //

body.text: athainaṃ sa nṛpatiḥ pramodādabhivyajyamānendriyaprasādaḥ pratyuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, his senses suffused with manifest delight, replied to him:

children.text: adya me kuśalaṃ haṃsa sarvatra ca bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: "Today all is well with me, O goose, and shall be henceforth in every way,

children.text: cirābhilaṣitaḥ prāpto yadayaṃ satsamāgamaḥ // Jm_22.71 //
children.translated_text: for this long-desired meeting with the virtuous has now been attained. // Jm_22.71 //

children.text: tvayi pāśavaśaṃ prāpte praharṣaddhatacāpalaḥ /
children.translated_text: When you had fallen into the power of the snare, did this one, unsteadied by excitement,

children.text: kacinnāyamakāriṣītte daṇḍenābhirujan rujam // Jm_22.72 //
children.translated_text: perchance inflict pain upon you with his rod, causing you injury? // Jm_22.72 //

children.text: evaṃ hyamīṣāṃ jālmānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ vyasanodaye /
children.translated_text: For thus it is with these base fowlers: when misfortune befalls birds,

children.text: praharṣākulitā buddhirāpatatyeva kalmaṣam // Jm_22.73 //
children.translated_text: their minds, agitated by excitement, inevitably descend into wickedness. // Jm_22.73 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kṣemamāsīnmahārāja satyāmapyevamāpadi /
children.translated_text: "All was well, O great king, even in such adversity as this,

children.text: na cāyaṃ kiṃcidasmāsu śatruvatpratyapadyata // Jm_22.74 //
children.translated_text: nor did this man act toward us in any way as an enemy would. // Jm_22.74 //

children.text: abaddhaṃ baddhavadayaṃ matsnehātsumukhaṃ sthitam /
children.translated_text: Seeing this <s>Sumukha</s>, unbound yet standing as though bound, out of affection for me,

children.text: dṛṣṭvābhāṣata sāmnaiva sakautūhalavismayaḥ // Jm_22.75 //
children.translated_text: he addressed him with gentle words alone, filled with curiosity and wonder. // Jm_22.75 //

children.text: sūnṛtairasya vacanairathāvarjitamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, his mind won over by the kind words of this one,

children.text: māmayaṃ vyamucatpāśādvinayadanumānayan // Jm_22.76 //
children.translated_text: he released me from the snare, showing honor with humility. // Jm_22.76 //

children.text: ataśca sumukhenedaṃ hitamasya samīhitam /
children.translated_text: And therefore, this benefit to him has been contrived by <s>Sumukha</s>:

children.text: ihāgamanamasmakaṃ syadasyāpi sukhodayam // Jm_22.77 //
children.translated_text: our coming here should be the occasion of happiness for him as well. // Jm_22.77 //

body.text: nṛpatiruvāca -
body.translated_text: The king said:

children.text: ākāṅkṣitābhigamayoḥ svāgataṃ bhavatoriha /
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you both, whose arrival has been longed for!

children.text: atīva prīṇitaścāsmi yuṣmatsaṃdarśanotsavāt // Jm_22.78 //
children.translated_text: I am exceedingly delighted by the festive joy of beholding you. // Jm_22.78 //

children.text: ayaṃ ca mahatārthena naiṣādo 'dya sameṣyati /
children.translated_text: And this fowler shall today meet with a great reward,

children.text: ubhayeṣāṃ priyaṃ kṛtvā mahadarhatyayaṃ priyam // Jm_22.79 //
children.translated_text: for having done what is pleasing to both parties, he greatly deserves this favor. // Jm_22.79 //

body.text: ityuktvā sa rājā taṃ naiṣādaṃ mahatā dhanavistarapradānena samānya punarhaṃsarājamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the king honored that fowler with a lavish bestowal of wealth, and then said again to the king of geese:

children.text: imaṃ svamāvāsamupāgatau yuvāṃ visṛjyatāṃ tanmayi yantraṇāvratam /
children.translated_text: "You two have come to your own abode — therefore let the vow of restraint toward me be set aside.

children.text: prayojanaṃ yena yathā taducyatāṃ bhavatsahāyā hi vibhūtayo mama // Jm_22.80 //
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose there may be, and in whatever manner, let it be spoken, for my powers are at your service. // Jm_22.80 //

children.text: aśaṅkitoktaiḥ praṇayākṣaraiḥ suhṛt karoti tuṣṭiṃ vibhavasthitasya yām /
children.translated_text: The contentment that a friend produces for one established in prosperity through words of candid and trusting affection —

children.text: na tadvidhāṃ lambhayate sa tāṃ dhanairmahopakāraḥ praṇayaḥ suhṛtsvataḥ // Jm_22.81 //
children.translated_text: that same contentment cannot be procured by riches; the goodwill of friends, born of its own nature, is a great benefaction. // Jm_22.81 //

body.text: atha sa rājā sumukhasaṃbhāṣaṇakutūhalahṛdayaḥ savismayabhivīkṣya sumukhamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, his heart curious to converse with <s>Sumukha</s>, gazed at <s>Sumukha</s> with wonder and said:

children.text: alabdhagādhā navasaṃstave jane na yānti kāmaṃ praṇayapragalbhatām /
children.translated_text: "Those who have found no footing in the presence of new praise do not easily attain boldness of affection;

children.text: vacastu dākṣiṇyasamāhitākṣaraṃ na te na jalpantyupacāraśībharam // Jm_22.82 //
children.translated_text: yet your words, composed with syllables arranged by courtesy, are not spoken as a mere burden of formality. // Jm_22.82 //

children.text: saṃbhāṣaṇenāpi yataḥ kartumarhati no bhavān /
children.translated_text: Since even through conversation, Your Majesty is able to bring about

children.text: sāphalyaṃ praṇayāśāyāḥ prīteścopacayaṃ hṛdi // Jm_22.83 //
children.translated_text: the fulfillment of the hope born of affection, and an increase of joy in the heart.

body.text: ityukte sumukho haṃsasenāpatirvinayādabhipraṇamyainamuvāca -
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Sumukha</s>, the general of the geese, bowing respectfully before the king, spoke:

children.text: mahendrakalpena saha tvayā saṃbhāṣaṇotsavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The delight of conversing with you, who are like great <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: iti darśitasauhārde kasya nātimanorathaḥ // Jm_22.84 //
children.translated_text: when such friendliness has been shown, whose heart would not be filled with the highest aspiration?

children.text: saṃbhāṣamāṇe tu narādhipe ca sauhārdaramyaṃ vihagādhipe ca /
children.translated_text: While the king of men and the king of birds were conversing, delighting in mutual affection,

children.text: tatsaṃkathāmadhyamupetya dhārṣṭyānnanvakramaḥ preṣyajanasya vaktum // Jm_22.85 //
children.translated_text: a servant boldly intruded into the midst of their discourse and presumed to speak.

children.text: na heyṣa mārgo vinayabhijātastaṃ caiva jānan kathamabhyupeyām /
children.translated_text: This is not the way of one born of good conduct, and knowing this, how could I have approached? —

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ mahārāja yataḥ sthito 'haṃ tanmarṣaṇīyaṃ yadi marṣaṇīyam // Jm_22.86 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I stood in silence, O great king. May this be pardoned, if it is pardonable.

body.text: ityukte sa rājā sapraharṣavismayavadanaḥ saṃrādhayan sumukhamuvāca -
body.translated_text: When this was said, the king, his face beaming with delight and wonder, addressed <s>Sumukha</s> with gratification:

body.text: sthāne bhavadguṇakathā ramayanti lokaṃ sthāne 'si haṃsapatinā gamitaḥ sakhitvam / evaṃvidhaṃ hi vinayaṃ nayasauṣṭhavaṃ ca naivākṛtātmahṛdayāni samudvahanti // Jm_22.87 //
body.translated_text: Rightly do the accounts of your virtues delight the world; rightly have you been taken into friendship by the lord of geese — for such refinement and excellence of judgment are not borne by hearts that are unrefined.

children.text: tadiyaṃ prastutā prītirvicchidyeta yathā na naḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, may this affection that has arisen between us never be severed;

children.text: tathaiva mayi visrambha ajaryaṃ hyāryasaṃgatam // Jm_22.88 //
children.translated_text: therefore place your trust in me, for the company of the noble never grows old.

body.text: atha bodhisattvastasya rājñaḥ parāṃ prītikāmatāmavetya snehapravṛttisumukhatāṃ ca saṃrādhayannavocadenam -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving the king's supreme desire for affection and his tender-faced disposition born of love, gratified him and spoke:

children.text: yatkṛtyaṃ parame mitre kṛtamasmāsu tattvayā /
children.translated_text: What ought to be done for the dearest of friends — that you have done for us,

children.text: saṃstave hi nave 'pyasmin svamāhātmyānuvartinā // Jm_22.89 //
children.translated_text: even though this acquaintance is new, acting in accordance with your own greatness.

children.text: kaśca nāma mahārāja nāvalambyeta cetasi /
children.translated_text: And who indeed, O great king, would not be deeply moved in heart

children.text: saṃmānavidhinānena yastvayāsmāsu darśitaḥ // Jm_22.90 //
children.translated_text: by this manner of honoring that you have shown toward us?

children.text: prayojanaṃ nāma kiyatkimeva vā madāśrayaṃ mānada yattvamīkṣase /
children.translated_text: What purpose, and how great a one, O bestower of honor, do you see that depends on me?

children.text: priyātithitva guṇavatsalasya te pravṛttamabhyāsaguṇāditi dhruvam // Jm_22.91 //
children.translated_text: Surely your hospitality toward guests and fondness for virtue have arisen from habitual practice of good qualities.

children.text: na citrametattvayi vā jitātmani prajāhitārthaṃ dhṛtapārthivavrate /
children.translated_text: This is no wonder in you, who have conquered yourself, who uphold the royal vow for the welfare of your subjects;

children.text: tapaḥsamādhānapare munāviva svabhāvavṛttyā hi guṇāstvayi sthitāḥ // Jm_22.92 //
children.translated_text: as in a sage devoted to the practice of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), virtues abide in you by their very nature.

children.text: iti praśaṃsāsubhagāḥ sukhā guṇā na doṣadurgeṣu vasanti bhūtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, virtues that are graced with praise are pleasant; prosperity does not dwell in the rough terrain of faults.

children.text: imāṃ viditvā guṇadoṣadharmatāṃ sacetanaḥ kaḥ svahitotpathaṃ bhacet // Jm_22.93 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this law regarding virtues and faults, what sentient being would tread the wrong path against his own welfare?

children.text: na deśamāpnoti parākrameṇa taṃ na kośavīryeṇa na nitīsaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: A king does not attain that place by valor alone, nor by treasury and army, nor by excellence of policy —

children.text: śramavyayābhyāṃ nṛpatirvinaiva yaṃ guṇābhijātena pathadhigacchati // Jm_22.94 //
children.translated_text: without toil and expenditure, he reaches it through the path born of virtue.

children.text: surādhipaśrīrapi vīkṣate guṇān guṇoditāneva paraiti saṃnati /
children.translated_text: Even the glory of <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, regards virtues; reverence proceeds only toward those endowed with virtues.

children.text: guṇebhya eva prabhavanti kīrtayaḥ prabhāvamāhātmyamiti śritaṃ guṇān // Jm_22.95 //
children.translated_text: Renown arises from virtues alone; might and greatness rest upon virtues.

children.text: amarṣadarpodbhavakarkaśānyapi prarūḍhavairasthiramatsarāṇyapi /
children.translated_text: Even hearts of enemies that are harsh from indignation and pride,

children.text: prasādayantyeva manāṃsi vidviṣāṃ śaśiprakāśādhikakāntayo guṇāḥ // Jm_22.96 //
children.translated_text: that are hardened by deep-rooted enmity and envy — virtues, whose beauty exceeds the radiance of the moon, win them over.

children.text: tadevameva kṣitipāla pālayan mahīṃ pratāpānatadṛptapārthivām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O protector of the earth, continuing to guard the earth whose proud kings are humbled by your might,

children.text: amandaśobhairvinayadibhirguṇairguṇānurāgaṃ jagataṃ prabodhaya // Jm_22.97 //
children.translated_text: awaken in the world a love for virtues through your resplendent qualities such as modesty and the rest.

children.text: prajāhitaṃ kṛtyatamaṃ mahīpatestadanya panthā hyubhayatra bhūtaye /
children.translated_text: The welfare of subjects is the highest duty of a king; there is no other path to well-being in both worlds.

children.text: bhavecca tadrājani dharmavatsale nṛpasya vṛttaṃ hi jano 'nuvartate // Jm_22.98 //
children.translated_text: And that is possible when the king is devoted to <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), for people follow the conduct of their king.

children.text: praśādhi dharmeṇa vasuṃdharāmataḥ karotu rakṣāṃ tridaśādhipaśca te /
children.translated_text: Therefore govern the earth with <s>Dharma</s>; may the lord of the gods grant you his protection.

children.text: tvadantikātsaṃśritabhāvanādapi svayūthyaduḥkhaṃ tu vikarṣatīva mām // Jm_22.99 //
children.translated_text: But the suffering of my own flock draws me away even from the pleasure of dwelling near you.

body.text: atha sa rājā samabhinandya tattasya vacanaṃ saparṣatkaḥ saṃmānapriyavacanaprayogapuraḥsaraṃ tau haṃsamukhyau visasarja / atha bodhisattvaḥ samutpatya vimalakhaḍgābhinīlaṃ śaratprasannaśobhaṃ gaganatalaṃ pratibimbenevānugamyamānaḥ sumukhena haṃsasenāpatinā samupetya haṃsayūthaṃ saṃdarśanādeva pareṇa praharṣeṇa saṃyojayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the king, having joyfully approved those words, together with his court, preceded by gestures of honor and kind speech, released the two foremost geese. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, flying up into the sky — radiant with the dark blue beauty of stainless swords and the clear splendor of autumn — followed as if by a reflection by <s>Sumukha</s>, the general of the geese, rejoined the flock of geese and filled them with the greatest joy at the very sight of him.

children.text: kālena copetya nṛpaṃ sa haṃsaḥ parānukampavyasanī sahaṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in time, that goose, devoted to compassion for others, together with his geese,

children.text: jagāda dharmaṃ kṣitipena tena pratyarcyamāno vinayānatena // Jm_22.100 //
children.translated_text: visited the king and taught him <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), and was honored by that king of the earth with humility.

body.text: tadevaṃ vinipātagatānāmapi satāṃ vṛttaṃ nālamanugantumasatpuruṣāḥ prāgeva sugatiṣṭhānāmiti / evaṃ kalyāṇī vāgubhayahitāvahā bhavatīti kalyāṇavacanapraśaṃsāyāmapyupaneyam / kalyāṇamitravarṇe 'pi vācyam, evaṃ kalyāṇamitravatāṃ kṛcchre 'pyarthāḥ saṃsidhyantīti / sthavirāryānandapūrvasabhāgapradarśane ca, evamayaṃ sthaviraḥ sahacaritacaraṇo bodhisattvena cirakālābhyastapremabahumāno bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: Thus, even when fallen into ruin, the conduct of the virtuous cannot be matched by the wicked — much less when they are well-established. This also may be adduced in praise of good speech, that noble speech brings benefit to both parties. It may also be cited in praise of a good friend: thus for those who have a good friend, even in adversity their aims are accomplished. And in illustration of the elder <s>Ārya</s> <s>Ānanda</s> and those like him: thus this elder, having walked the path together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, has long-cultivated love and reverence.

body.text: // iti haṃsajātakaṃ dvāviśatitamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Haṃsa-jātaka</s> (Story of the Geese), the twenty-second.

body.text: 23. Mahābodhijātakam
body.translated_text: 23. <s>Mahābodhi-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Great Awakening)

body.text: asatkṛtānāmapi satpuruṣāṇāṃ pūrvopakāriṣvanukampā na śithilībhavati kṛtajñatvāt kṣamāsātmyācca / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The compassion of the virtuous toward those who formerly helped them does not slacken even when treated with disrespect, because of their gratitude and their familiarity with patience. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān mahābodhirnāma parivrājako babhūva / sa gṛhasthabhāva eva parividitakramavyāyāmo lokābhimatānāṃ vidyāsthānānāṃ kṛtajñānakautūhalaścitrāsu ca kalāsu pravrajyāśrayāllokahitodyogācca viśeṣavattaraṃ dharmaśāstreṣvavahitamatisteṣvācāryakaṃ padamavāpa / sa kṛtapuṇyatvājjñānamāhātmyāllokajñatayā pratipattiguṇasauṣṭhavācca yatra yatra gacchati sma tatra tatraiva viduṣāṃ vidvatpriyāṇāṃ ca rājñāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmanyatīrthikānāṃ ca pravrajitānāmabhigamanīyo bhāvanīyaśca babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the Blessed One, was in a former life a wandering ascetic named <s>Mahābodhi</s>. Even while still a householder, he had mastered the sequential disciplines, had explored with scholarly curiosity the various fields of learning esteemed by the world, and was accomplished in diverse arts. Through his renunciation, his dedication to the welfare of the world, and his especially profound attentiveness to the treatises on <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), he attained the rank of teacher in those subjects. Due to his accumulated merit, the greatness of his knowledge, his understanding of the world, and the excellence of his practical conduct, wherever he went, he became worthy of being approached and revered by the learned, by kings who loved learning, by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, and by ascetics of other schools.

children.text: guṇā hi puṇyāśrayalabdhadīptayo gatāḥ priyatvaṃ pratipattiśobhayā /
children.translated_text: For virtues, whose radiance is obtained through the abode of merit, having become dear through the beauty of practice,

children.text: api dviṣadbhyaḥ svayaśonurakṣayā bhavanti satkāraviśeṣabhāginaḥ // Jm_23.1 //
children.translated_text: even among enemies, through the preservation of their own fame, come to receive special honors.

body.text: atha sa mahātmā lokānugrahārthamanuvicaran grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhāṇīranyatamasya rājño viṣāyāntaramupajāgāma / śrutagunavistaraprabhavastu sa rājā tasyāgamanaṃ dūrata evopalabhya prītamanā ramaṇīye svasminnudyānavanapradeśe tasyāvasathaṃ kārayāmāsa / abhyudgamanādisatkārapuraḥsaraṃ cainaṃ praveśya svaviṣayaṃ śiṣya ivācāryaṃ paricaraṇaparyupāsanavidhinā saṃmānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, wandering for the benefit of the world through villages, cities, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, arrived in the territory of a certain king. That king, whose respect was born from hearing of the extent of his virtues, learning of his arrival from afar and being pleased at heart, had a dwelling prepared for him in a pleasant area of his own garden grove. Having received him with honors beginning with a formal welcome, he paid him respect as a pupil would a teacher, through attendance and devoted service.

children.text: vibhūtiguṇasaṃpannamupetaḥ praṇayād gṛham /
children.translated_text: When one possessed of virtues arrives at the house, endowed with the wealth of good qualities,

children.text: gunapriyasya gunavānutsavātiśayo 'tithiḥ // Jm_23.2 //
children.translated_text: of one who loves virtue, coming with affection — he is a guest who surpasses any festival.

body.text: bodhisattvo 'pi cainaṃ śrutihṛdayahlādinībhirdharmyābhiḥ kathābhiḥ śreyomārgamanupratipādayamānaḥ pratyahamanujagrāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, guiding him daily toward the path of the good through discourses on <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) that gladdened the heart and ears, continued to benefit him.

children.text: adṛṣṭabhaktiṣvapi dharmavatsalā hitaṃ vivakṣanti parānukampinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are compassionate toward others, devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, wish to speak what is beneficial even to those in whom devotion is not yet seen;

children.text: ka eva vādaḥ śucibhājanopame hitārthini premaguṇotsuke jane // Jm_23.3 //
children.translated_text: what need to speak then of one who is like a pure vessel, who seeks his own welfare, and who is eager with the quality of love?

body.text: atha tasya rājño 'mātyā labdhavidvatsaṃbhāvanā labdhasaṃmānāśca sadasyāḥ pratyahamabhivardhamānasatkārāṃ bodhisattvasya guṇasamṛddhimīrṣyopahatabuddhitvānna sehire /
body.translated_text: Now the ministers of that king, who had gained their standing through learning and their honor through courtly rank, could not endure the daily increasing abundance of honor shown to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, their minds being corrupted by envy.

children.text: svaguṇātiśayoditairyaśobhirjagadāvarjanadṛṣṭaśaktiyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose mastery is evident in his power to captivate the world through his fame, born from the surpassing excellence of his own virtues —

children.text: racanāgunamatrasatkṛteṣu jvalayatyeva pareṣvamarṣavahnim // Jm_23.4 //
children.translated_text: such a one kindles the fire of resentment in others who are honored merely for the quality of their literary composition.

body.text: prasahya cainaṃ śāstrakathāsvabhibhavitumaśaktā dharmaprasaṅgamamṛṣyamāṇāśca rājñastena tena krameṇa rājānaṃ bodhisattvaṃ prati vigrāhayāmāsuḥ - nārhati devo bodhiparivrājake viśvāsamupagantum / vyaktamayaṃ devasya guṇapriyatāṃ dharmābhimukhatāṃ copalabhya vyasanapratāraṇaślakṣṇaṭhamadhuravacanaḥ pravṛttisaṃcāraṇaheturabhūtaḥ kasyāpi pratyarthino rājño nipuṇaḥ praṇidhiprayogaḥ / tathā hi dharmātmako nāma bhūtvā devamekāntena kāruṇyapravṛttau hrīdainye ca samanuśāsti, arthakāmoparodhiṣu ca kṣatradharmabāhyeṣvāsannāpanayeṣu dharmasamādāneṣu dayānuvṛttyā ca nāma te kṛtyapakṣamāśvāsanavidhinopagṛṇīte priyasaṃstavaścānyarājadūtaiḥ / na cāyamaviditavṛttānto rājaśāstrāṇām / ataḥ sāśaṅkānyatra no hṛdayānīti / atha tasya rājñaḥ punaḥ punarbhedopasaṃhitaṃ hitamiva bahubhirucyamānasya bodhisattvaṃ prati pariśaṅkāsaṃkocitasnehagauravaprasaramanyādṛśaṃ cittamabhavat /
body.translated_text: Unable to overpower him openly in discussions of scripture, and unable to tolerate his prominence in matters of <s>Dharma</s>, they gradually turned the king against the <s>Bodhisattva</s> by various means: 'Your Majesty should not place trust in the wandering ascetic <s>Bodhi</s>. Clearly, having observed Your Majesty's love of virtue and inclination toward <s>Dharma</s>, this man, with his smooth, deceptive, and sweet words calculated to lead astray in times of crisis, has been planted as a cunning spy by some rival king. For while professing to be devoted to righteousness, he instructs Your Majesty exclusively in the practice of compassion and the virtue of humility, and through his advocacy of mercy, he endorses <s>Dharma</s> observances that obstruct wealth and pleasure, that are contrary to the duties of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> (warrior), and that lead to imminent ruin — and he flatters your party through reassuring counsel. Moreover, he is praised by the envoys of other kings. And this man is not ignorant of the contents of treatises on statecraft. Therefore our hearts are full of suspicion.' And as the king heard this counsel, framed as friendly advice but laced with divisiveness, repeated again and again by many, his mind toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> changed — his affection and respect contracted with suspicion, and his disposition became quite different.

children.text: paisunyavajrāśanisaṃnipāte bhīmasvane cāśanisaṃnipāte /
children.translated_text: Under the thunderbolt-like impact of slander, the terrible crash of calumny —

children.text: visrambhavānmānuṣamātradhairyaḥ syānnirvikāro yadi nāma kaścit // Jm_23.5 //
children.translated_text: if anyone with merely human fortitude and trust could remain unmoved, that would be remarkable indeed.

body.text: atha sa rājā visrambhavirahanmandībhutapremabahumānastasmin mahāsattve na yathāpūrvaṃ satkāraprayogasumukho babhūva / bodhisattvo 'pi śuddhasvabhāvatvāt bahukāryavyāsaṅgā rājāna iti tanmanasi cakāra / tatsamīpavartināṃ tu vinayopacāraśaithilyasaṃdarśanādviraktahṛdayamavetya rājānaṃ samādāya tridaṇḍāduṇḍikādyāṃ parivrājakabhāṇḍikāṃ prakramaṇasavyāpāraḥ samabhavat / tadupaśrutya sa rājā sāvaśeṣasnehatayā dākṣiṇyavinayanuvṛttyā cainamabhigamya pradarśitasaṃbhramo vinivartayitukāma iva tamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king, his affection and respect having grown feeble from the loss of trust, was no longer as cordial in his gestures of honor toward that great being as before. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, being pure in nature, reflected that 'kings are preoccupied with many affairs.' But observing the laxity of courteous behavior among those near the king, he understood that the king's heart had turned away. Taking up his triple staff, his water vessel, and the rest of his wandering ascetic's equipment, he began preparations for departure. When the king heard of this, still retaining some affection, and prompted by courtesy and good manners, he approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a show of concern, as if wishing to dissuade him, and said:

children.text: asmanakasmādapahāya kasmādgantavya eva praṇatā matiste /
children.translated_text: Why must you absolutely go, leaving us? For what reason is your mind set on departure?

children.text: vyalīkaśaṅkājanakaṃ nu kiṃcid dṛṣṭaṃ pramādaskhalitaṃ tvayā naḥ // Jm_23.6 //
children.translated_text: Have you perhaps observed some negligent lapse on our part that might give rise to suspicion of ill treatment?

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to him:

body.text: nākasmiko 'yaṃ gamanodyamo me nāsatkriyāmātrakarūkṣikatvāt /
body.translated_text: This resolve to depart of mine is not without cause, nor is it from mere irritation at any lack of courtesy.

body.text: abhajanatvaṃ tu gato 'si śāṭhyāddharmasya tenāhamito vrajāmi // Jm_23.7 //
body.translated_text: But through duplicity, you have come to abandon <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) — therefore I depart from here.

body.text: athāsya sarabhasabhaṣitamativivṛtavadanamabhidravantaṃ vallabhaṃ śvānaṃ tatrāgatamabhipradarśayan punaruvāca - ayaṃ cātra mahārāja amānuṣaḥ sākṣinirdeśo dṛśyatām /
body.translated_text: Then, pointing to his favorite dog that had come there, rushing toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with its mouth wide open, barking furiously, he said again: 'And here, O great king, let this non-human witness be observed:

children.text: ayaṃ hi pūrvaṃ paṭucāṭukarmā bhūtvā mayi śvā bhavato 'nuvṛttyā /
children.translated_text: This dog, who formerly was fawning and flattering toward me, following your lead,

children.text: ākāraguptyajñatayā tvidānīṃ tvadbhāvasūcāṃ bhaṣitaiḥ karoti // Jm_23.8 //
children.translated_text: now, not knowing how to conceal his expression, reveals your changed attitude through his barking.

children.text: tvattaḥ śrutaṃ kiṃcidanena nūnaṃ madantare bhaktivipattirukṣam /
children.translated_text: He has surely heard from you something harsh concerning a deterioration of devotion toward me;

children.text: ato 'nuvṛttaṃ dhruvamityanena tvatprītihetoranujīvivṛttam // Jm_23.9 //
children.translated_text: therefore he has certainly adopted this behavior accordingly, acting as a dependant does for the sake of his master's favor.'

body.text: atha sa rājā tatpratyadeśād vrīḍāvanāmitavadanastena cāsya matinaipuṇyena samāvarjitamatirjātasaṃvego nedānīṃ śāṭhyānuvṛttikāla iti bodhisattvamabhipraṇamyovāca -
body.translated_text: Then the king, his face bowed with shame at this rebuke, his mind won over by the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> acuteness of judgment, felt remorse, thinking 'This is no longer the time for following the path of duplicity,' and bowing before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, said:

children.text: tvadāśrayā kacidabhūtkathaiṣā saṃprastutā naḥ sadasi pragalbhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some story concerning you was raised in our assembly by certain bold courtiers,

children.text: upekṣitā kāryavaśānmayā ca tatkṣamyatāṃ tiṣṭha ca sādhu mā gāḥ // Jm_23.10 //
children.translated_text: and was neglected by me due to the pressure of affairs. Let that be forgiven — please stay, do not go.

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - naiva khalvahaṃ mahārāja asatkāraprakṛtatvādakṣamayā vā praṇudyamāṇo gacchāmi / na tvayaṃ mahārāja avasthānakāla iti na tiṣṭhāmi / paśyatu bhavān /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Indeed, O great king, I am not leaving because I am driven away by disrespect or by impatience. But I do not remain because, O great king, this is not the time for staying. Let Your Majesty consider:

children.text: vimadhyabhāvādapi hīnaśobhe yāyāṃ na satkāravidhau svayaṃ cet /
children.translated_text: Even if the ceremony of honor were merely diminished in its splendor, I myself would not leave;

children.text: saṅgādagatyā jaḍatābalādvā nanvardhacandrābhinayottaraḥ syām // Jm_23.11 //
children.translated_text: Whether through attachment to worldly life, through sluggishness, or through the force of dullness, surely I would end up performing the half-moon gesture of dismissal. [Jm 23.11]

children.text: prāptakramo 'yaṃ vidhiratra tena yāsyāmi nāprītyabhitaptacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: The proper course of action has arrived here; therefore I shall depart, my heart not scorched by displeasure,

children.text: ekāvamānābhihatā hi satsu pūrvopakārā na samībhavanti // Jm_23.12 //
children.translated_text: For among the virtuous, former services, once struck by a single insult, do not remain intact. [Jm 23.12]

body.text: asnigdhabhāvastu na paryupāsyastoyārthina śuṣka ivodapānaḥ /
body.translated_text: One who is devoid of affection should not be attended upon, like a dried-up well by one seeking water,

body.text: prayatnasādhyāpi tato 'rthasiddhiryasmādbhavedākaluṣā kṛśā ca // Jm_23.13 //
body.translated_text: Since even success in one's aims, though achievable through effort, would from such a person be meager and tainted. [Jm 23.13]

children.text: prasanna eva tvabhigamyarūpaḥ śaradviśuddhāmbumahāhradābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who is gracious is indeed worthy of approach, like a great lake of autumn-clear waters;

children.text: sukhārthinaḥ kleśaparāṅmukhasya lokaprasiddhaḥ sphuṭa eṣa mārgaḥ // Jm_23.14 //
children.translated_text: For one who seeks happiness and turns away from affliction, this path is well-known to the world and evident. [Jm 23.14]

children.text: bhaktyunmukhādyo 'pi parāṅmukhaḥ syātparāṅmukhe cābhimukhatvadīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who would turn away even from one devoted to him, and who depends on others turning toward him when he himself has turned away,

children.text: pūrvopakārasmaraṇālaso vā narākṛtiścintyaviniścayaḥ saḥ // Jm_23.15 //
children.translated_text: Or who is lazy in remembering former services — such a person, though bearing human form, is of uncertain resolve. [Jm 23.15]

children.text: asevanā cātyupasevanā ca yācñābhiyogāśca dahanti maitrīm /
children.translated_text: Both neglect and excessive attendance, as well as persistent begging, burn up friendship;

children.text: rakṣyaṃ yataḥ prītyavaśeṣametannivāsadoṣāditi yāmi tāvat // Jm_23.16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since this remnant of affection must be guarded against the fault of prolonged residence, I shall depart for now. [Jm 23.16]

body.text: rājovāca - yadyavaśyameva gantavyamiti niścitātrabhavato matiḥ, tatpunarapīdānīmihāgamanenāsmānanugrahītumarhati bhavān / asevanādapi hi prītiranurakṣitavyaiva / bodhisattva uvāca - bahvantarāyo mahārāja bahūpadravapratyarthikatvāllokasaṃniveśa iti na śakyametadavadhāraṇayā pratijñātumāgamiṣyāmīti / sati tvāgamanakāraṇasākalye 'pi nāma punarbhavantaṃ paśyema / ityanunīya sa māhatmā taṃ rājānaṃ kṛtābhyanujñāsatkārastena rājñā tadviṣayātpracakrāma / sa tena gṛhijanasaṃstavenākulitahṛdayo 'nyatamadaraṇyāyatanamupaśritya dhyānābhiyuktamatistatra viharannacireṇeva catvāri dhyānāni pañcābhijñāḥ pratilebhe /
body.translated_text: The king said: "If your honor's mind is firmly resolved that you must certainly go, then please grace us by coming here again hereafter. For even without constant attendance, affection must still be preserved." The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Great king, the course of worldly existence is full of many obstacles and beset with many calamities and adversaries; therefore I cannot promise with certainty 'I shall come.' But if all the conditions for returning are complete, may we indeed see your majesty again." Having thus consoled the king, that great soul, honored with a respectful farewell by the king, departed from his kingdom. With his heart disturbed by the lamentations of the household, he took refuge in a certain forest hermitage, and dwelling there with his mind devoted to <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he soon attained the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and the five <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges).

body.text: tasya samasvāditapraśamasukharasasya smṛtiranukampanusāriṇī taṃ rājānaṃ prati prādurabhūt - kā nu khalu tasya rājño 'vastheti / athainaṃ dadarśa tairamātyairyathābhiniviṣṭāni dṛṣṭigatāni prait pratāryamāṇam / kaścidenamamātyo durvibhāvyahetubhirnidarśanairahetuvādaṃ prati pracakarṣa -
body.translated_text: As he savored the bliss of tranquility, a recollection arose in him, guided by compassion, regarding that king: "What indeed is the condition of that king now?" Then he saw him being led astray by those ministers, each drawing him toward their own entrenched philosophical views. A certain minister was pulling him toward <s>ahetuvāda</s> (the doctrine of no causation) with arguments whose premises were difficult to discern —

children.text: kaḥ padmanāladalakesarakarṇikānāṃ saṃsthānavarṇaracanāmṛdutādihetuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Who is the cause of the form, color, arrangement, and softness of the stalk, petals, filaments, and pericarp of a lotus?

children.text: patrāṇi citrayati ko 'tra patatriṇāṃ vā svābhāvikaṃ jagadidaṃ niyataṃ tathaiva // Jm_23.17 //
children.translated_text: And who paints the feathers of birds here? This world is naturally so determined, just as it is." [Jm 23.17]

body.text: apara iśvarakāraṇamasmai svabuddhirucitamupavarṇayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Another described to him the doctrine that <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is the cause, fashioned according to his own intellectual preference —

children.text: nākasmikaṃ bhavitumarhati sarvametadastyatra sarvamadhi kaścidananta ekaḥ /
children.translated_text: "All this cannot come about without a cause; there exists over all this someone who is infinite and one,

children.text: svecchāviśeṣaniyamādya imaṃ vicitraṃ lokaṃ karoti ca punaśca samīkaroti // Jm_23.18 //
children.translated_text: Who by the determination of his own particular will creates this variegated world and again destroys it." [Jm 23.18]

body.text: sarvamidaṃ pūrvakarmakṛtaṃ sukhāsukham / na prayatnasāmarthyamastītyevamanya enaṃ vigrāhayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Yet another led him astray thus, arguing that all happiness and suffering is produced by <s>pūrvakarman</s> (past actions), and that effort has no power —

children.text: evaṃ kariṣyati kathaṃ nu samānakālaṃ bhinnāśrayān bahuvidhānamitāṃśca bhāvān /
children.translated_text: "How could one agent simultaneously produce the manifold, unlimited, and varied states located in different substrates?

children.text: sarvaṃ tu pūrvakṛtakarmanimittametat saukhyaprayatnanipuṇo 'pi hi duḥkhameti // Jm_23.19 //
children.translated_text: All this is rather caused by previously performed <s>karma</s> (actions), for even one skilled in the pursuit of happiness meets with suffering." [Jm 23.19]

body.text: apara ucchedavādakathābhirenaṃ kāmabhogaprasaṅga eva pratārayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Another misled him with discourses on <s>ucchedavāda</s> (annihilationism), directing him toward the enjoyment of sensual pleasures —

children.text: dārūṇi naikavidhavarṇaguṇākṛtīni karmātmakāni na bhavanti bhavanti caiva /
children.translated_text: "Pieces of wood, of various colors, qualities, and shapes, do not possess a self and yet they come into being;

children.text: naṣṭāni naiva ca yathā punarudbhavanti lokastathāyamiti saukhyaparāyaṇaḥ syāt // Jm_23.20 //
children.translated_text: And once destroyed, they never arise again — the world is likewise; therefore one should be devoted to pleasure." [Jm 23.20]

body.text: apara enaṃ kṣatravidyāparidṛṣṭeṣu nītikauṭilyaprasaṅgeṣu nairghṛṇyamalineṣu dharmavirodhiṣvapi rājadharmo 'yamiti samanuśaśāsa -
body.translated_text: Another instructed him in the practices of <s>nītikauṭilya</s> (political cunning), associated with the science of kingship — cruel, impure, and contrary to <s>dharma</s> — saying 'This is the duty of a king' —

children.text: chāyādrumeṣviva nareṣu kṛtāśrayeṣu tāvatkṛtajñacaritaiḥ svayaśaḥ parīpset /
children.translated_text: "Among men who have taken shelter, as under shade-trees, one should seek to enhance one's own fame through acts of apparent gratitude,

children.text: nārtho 'ti yāvadupabhoganayena teṣāṃ kṛtye tu yajña iva te paśavo niyojyāḥ // Jm_23.21 //
children.translated_text: So long as their usefulness has not been fully exploited; but when the task is done, they should be yoked like sacrificial animals at a <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice)." [Jm 23.21]

body.text: iti te 'mātyāstaṃ rājānaṃ tena tena dṛṣṭikṛtonmārgeṇa netumīṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus those ministers sought to lead the king astray, each along a wrong path fashioned by their own philosophical views.

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pāpajanasaṃparkavaśātparapratyayaneyabuddhitvācca dṛṣṭikṛtaprapātābhimukhamavekṣya rājānaṃ tadanukampāsamāvarjitahṛdayastannivartanopāyaṃ vimamarśa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing that the king — susceptible to the influence of evil companions and of a nature to be guided by the opinions of others — was heading toward the precipice created by false views, his heart moved by compassion for him, deliberated upon a means to turn him back.

children.text: guṇābhyāsena sādhūnāṃ kṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati cetasi /
children.translated_text: What is done by the virtuous through habitual cultivation of good qualities remains in the mind;

children.text: bhraśyatyapakṛtaṃ tasmājjalaṃ padmadalādiva // Jm_23.22 //
children.translated_text: Evil deeds fall away from it, like water from a lotus petal. [Jm 23.22]

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ idamatra prāptakālamiti viniścitya svasminnāśramapade mahāntaṃ vānaramabhinirmāya ṛddhiprabhāvāttasya carmāpanīya śeṣamantardhāpayāmāsa / sa tannirmitaṃ mahadvānaracarma
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having determined "This is the opportune moment," created a great monkey at his own hermitage through his supernatural power, removed its skin, and caused the rest to disappear. Bearing that conjured great monkey skin

body.text: bibhrattasya nṛpaterbhavanadvāre prādurabhūt / niveditābhyāgamanaśca dauvārikairyathākramamāyudhīyaguptaparyantāmamātyadvijayodhadūpapauramukhyābhikīrṇāṃ vinītadhīrodāttaveṣajanāṃ sāsiyaṣṭibhiḥ pratihārairadhiṣṭhitapradvārāṃ siṃhāsanāvaśtitanarādhipāmanākulāṃ rājaparṣadamavajagāhe / pratyudgamanādividhinā cātithijanopacāreṇa pratipūjyamānaḥ kṛtapratisaṃmodanakathāsatkārāsanābhinirhāraśca tena rājñā kautūhalānuvṛttyā vānaracarmapratilambhaṃ pratyanuyuktaḥ - kenedamāryāya vānaracarmopanayatā mahatānugraheṇātmā saṃyojita iti /
body.translated_text: , he appeared at the gate of that king's palace. When his arrival was announced by the doorkeepers, he entered in due order the royal assembly — filled with military officers, guards, ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, warriors, physicians, and leading citizens, attended by people of dignified and noble bearing, with its entrances guarded by attendants bearing swords and staffs, and with the king seated upon his throne, undisturbed. Honored with the customary hospitality of welcoming guests — rising to greet him and other courtesies — and after the exchange of greetings, the offering of a seat of honor, the king, prompted by curiosity, inquired about the acquisition of the monkey skin: "By what great favor has your honor come to possess this monkey skin? Who presented it?"

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - mayaivedaṃ mahārāja svayamadhigataṃ nānyena kenacidupahṛtam / kuśatṛṇamātrāstīrṇāyāṃ hi pṛthivyāṃ svabhāvakaṭhināyāṃ niṣaṇṇena svapatā vā pratapyamānaśarīreṇa na sukhaṃ dharmavidhiranuṣṭhiyate / ayaṃ ca mayāśramapade mahān vānaro dṛṣṭaḥ / tasya me buddhirabhavat - upapannaṃ bata me dharmasādhanamidamasya vānarasya carma / śakyamatra niṣaṇṇena svapatā vā parārdhyāstaraṇāstīrṇebhyo rājaśayanebhyo 'pi nivṛttaspṛheṇa svadharmavidhiranuṣṭhātumiti mayā tasyedaṃ carma pragṛhītam / sa ca praśamita iti / tacchrutvā sa rājā dākṣiṇyavinayānuvṛttyā na bodhisattvaṃ kiṃcitpratyuvāca / savrīḍahṛdayastu kiṃcidavāṅmukho babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "Great king, I myself obtained this; no one else presented it to me. For when sitting or sleeping on the bare ground, covered only with <s>kuśa</s> grass and naturally hard, one's body suffers, and the practice of <s>dharma</s> cannot be performed comfortably. Now, I saw a great monkey at my hermitage. The thought occurred to me: 'This monkey's skin would be a fitting aid for my religious practice. Seated or sleeping upon it, one could perform one's religious duties free from longing even for royal couches spread with the most exquisite coverings.' So I took this skin from it, and it was killed." Hearing this, the king, out of polite deference, said nothing in reply to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But his heart was filled with shame, and he hung his head slightly.

body.text: atha te 'mātyāḥ pūrvamapi tasmin mahāsattve sāmarṣahṛdayā labdhavacanāvakāśatvātpravikasitavadanā rājānamūdīkṣya bodhisattvamupadarśayanta ūcuḥ - aho bhagavato dharmanurāgaikarasā matiḥ / aho dhairyam / aho vyavasāyasādhusāmarthyam / āśramapadamabhigata eva mahānnāma vānara ekākinā tapaḥkṣāmaśarīreṇa praśamita ityāścaryam / sarvathā tapaḥsiddhirastu / athainānasaṃrabdha eva bodhisattvaḥ pratyuvāca - nārhantyatrabhavantaḥ svavādaśobhānirapekṣamityasmān vigarhitum / na hyayaṃ kramo vidvadyaśaḥ samudbhābayitum / pahsyantvatrabhavantaḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those ministers, who had already harbored resentment toward that great being, finding an opening for speech, their faces brightening, looked toward the king and said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in a mocking tone: "Ah, what single-minded devotion to <s>dharma</s> the reverend one has! What fortitude! What noble power of resolve! That a great monkey, no less, was killed single-handedly by one whose body is emaciated from <s>tapas</s> (ascetic practice), right at the hermitage — how astonishing! May the fruits of asceticism be yours indeed!" Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without any agitation, replied to them: "Your honors should not censure us so, without regard for the beauty of your own doctrines. For this is not the way to enhance a scholar's reputation. Let your honors consider —

children.text: svavādaghnena vacasā yaḥ parān vijugupsate /
children.translated_text: He who reviles others with words that undermine his own doctrine

children.text: sa khalvātmavadheneva parasyākirtīmicchati // Jm_23.23 //
children.translated_text: Truly desires the other's disgrace at the cost of destroying himself. [Jm 23.23]

body.text: iti sa mahātmā tānamātyān sāmānyenopālabhya pratyekaśaḥ punarupālabdhukāmastamahetuvādinamāmantryovāca -
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having reproved those ministers collectively, wishing to reprove each one individually, addressed the proponent of <s>ahetuvāda</s> (the no-cause doctrine) and said:

children.text: svābhāvikaṃ jagaditi pravikathase tvaṃ tattvaṃ ca tadyadi vikutsayasi kimasmān /
children.translated_text: "You proclaim that the world is naturally so — and if that is the truth, why do you reproach us?

children.text: śākhāmṛge nidhanamāpatite svabhāvāt pāpaṃ kṛto mama yataḥ suhato mayāyam // Jm_23.24 //
children.translated_text: Since the tree-dwelling monkey met its death by its own nature, what sin have I committed? For it was killed by me in accordance with my nature. [Jm 23.24]

children.text: atha pāpamasti mama tasya vadhānnanu hetutastaditi siddhamidam /
children.translated_text: Now, if there is sin in my killing of it, then surely the existence of causation is established by that very fact.

children.text: tadahetuvādamidamutsṛja vā vada vātra yattava na yuktamiva // Jm_23.25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore either abandon this doctrine of no causation, or state what in this matter you find inconsistent." [Jm 23.25]

children.text: yadi padmanālaracanādi ca yattadahetukaṃ nanu sadaiva bhavet /
children.translated_text: "If the arrangement of the lotus stalk and so forth is without a cause, then surely it should exist forever;

children.text: salilādībījakṛtameva tu tat sati tatra saṃbhavati na hyasati // Jm_23.26 //
children.translated_text: But in fact it is produced only from water and other seeds — it arises when those conditions are present, not when they are absent. [Jm 23.26]

body.text: api cāyuṣman, samyagupadhāraya tāvat,
body.translated_text: Moreover, friend, consider this carefully:

children.text: na heturastīti vadan sahetukaṃ nanu pratijñā svayameva hāpayet /
children.translated_text: He who says 'there is no cause' — does he not by that very statement, which itself has a cause, undermine his own thesis?

children.text: athāpi hetupraṇayālaso bhavet pratijñayā kevalayāsya kiṃ bhavet // Jm_23.27 //
children.translated_text: And if he is merely too lazy to trace the cause, what use is his bare assertion? [Jm 23.27]

children.text: ekatra kvacidanavekṣya yaśca hetuṃ tenaiva pravadati sarvahetvabhāvam /
children.translated_text: One who, without examining the cause in even a single case, declares on that very basis the absence of all causes —

children.text: prtyakṣaṃ nanu tadavetya hetusāraṃ taddveṣī bhavati virodhaduṣṭavākyaḥ // Jm_23.28 //
children.translated_text: Does he not, while directly perceiving what is essentially causation, become hostile to it, and thus contradict himself? [Jm 23.28]

children.text: na lakṣyate yadi kuhacicca kāraṇaṃ kathaṃ nu tad dṛḍhamasadeva bhāṣase /
children.translated_text: If in some cases a cause is not observed, how can you firmly assert that it simply does not exist?

children.text: na dṛśyate sadapi hi kāraṇāntarāddinātyaye vimalavivārkamaṇḍalam // Jm_23.29 //
children.translated_text: For even what exists is not always seen due to intervening conditions — as the spotless disc of the sun is not seen at nightfall. [Jm 23.29]

body.text: nanu ca bhoḥ
body.translated_text: And furthermore, sir:

children.text: sukhārthamiṣṭān viṣayān prapadyase niṣevituṃ necchasi tadvirodhinaḥ /
children.translated_text: You pursue desired sense-objects for the sake of happiness, and you do not wish to indulge in what opposes them;

children.text: nṛpasya sevāṃ ca karoṣi tatkṛte na heturastīti ca nāma bhāṣase // Jm_23.30 //
children.translated_text: You also perform service to the king for that purpose — yet you say 'there is no cause'! [Jm 23.30]

body.text: tadevamapi cedbhāvānanupaśyasyahetukān / ahetorvānaravadhe siddhe kiṃ māṃ vigarhase // Jm_23.31 //
body.translated_text: Even so, if you regard things as without cause, and the causeless killing of the monkey is established, then why do you censure me? [Jm 23.31]

body.text: iti sa mahātmā tamahetuvādinaṃ viśadairhetubhirniṣpratibhaṃ kṛtvā tamīśvakāraṇikamamantrayovāca -
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having rendered the proponent of <s>ahetuvāda</s> (the no-cause doctrine) speechless with clear arguments, addressed the advocate of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) as the cause and said:

body.text: āyuṣmānapyasmān nārhatyeva vigarhitum / īśvaraḥ sarvasya hi te kāraṇamabhimataḥ / paśya -
body.translated_text: "Your honor too should not censure us at all. For <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is, in your view, the cause of everything. Consider —

children.text: kurute yadi sarvamīśvaro nanu tenaiva hataḥ sa vānaraḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Īśvara</s> indeed does everything, then surely that monkey was killed by him alone.

children.text: tava keyamamaitracittatā paradoṣān mayi yanniṣiñcasi // Jm_23.32 //
children.translated_text: What is this hostility of yours, unfriendly in mind, that you pour the faults of another upon me? [Jm 23.32]

children.text: atha vānaravīravaiśasaṃ na kṛtaṃ tena dayānurodhinā /
children.translated_text: But if the slaughter of the heroic monkey was not done by him, out of his inclination toward compassion,

children.text: bṛhadityavaghuṣyate kathaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇamīśvarastvayā // Jm_23.33 //
children.translated_text: Then how can you loudly proclaim that <s>Īśvara</s> is the cause of the entire world? [Jm 23.33]

body.text: api ca bhadra sarvamīśvarakṛtamiti paśyataḥ -
body.translated_text: Moreover, good sir, for one who holds that everything is created by <s>Īśvara</s> —

children.text: īśvare prasādāśā kā stutipraṇāmādyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: What hope of favor from <s>Īśvara</s> can there be through praises, prostrations, and the like?

children.text: sa svayaṃ svayaṃbhūste yatkaroti tatkarma // Jm_23.34 //
children.translated_text: He himself is self-existent for you; whatever he does is his own action. [Jm 23.34]

children.text: tvatkṛtātha yadījyā na tvasau tadakartā /
children.translated_text: And if worship is your own act, then he is not the doer of that;

children.text: ātmano hi vibhūtyā yaḥ karoti sa karjā // Jm_23.35 //
children.translated_text: For he who acts by his own power is the agent of his own action. [Jm 23.35]

children.text: īśvaraḥ kurute cetpāpakānyakhilāni /
children.translated_text: If <s>Īśvara</s> creates all sinful deeds as well,

children.text: tatr abhaktiniveśaḥ kaṃ guṇaṃ nu samīkṣya // Jm_23.36 //
children.translated_text: Then having observed what virtue would justify devotion to him? [Jm 23.36]

children.text: tānyadharmabhayādvā yadyayaṃ na karoti /
children.translated_text: And if, out of fear of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), he does not create those evil deeds,

children.text: tena vaktumayuktaṃ sarvamīśvarasṛṣṭam // Jm_23.37 //
children.translated_text: Then it is improper to say that everything is created by <s>Īśvara</s>. [Jm 23.37]

children.text: tasya ceśvaratā syāddharmataḥ parato vā /
children.translated_text: And would his lordship derive from <s>dharma</s> (his own nature) or from another?

children.text: dharmato yadi na prāgīśvaraḥ sa tato 'bhūt // Jm_23.38 //
children.translated_text: If from his own nature, then he was not the Lord before that, and so became one only afterward. [Jm 23.38]

children.text: dāsataiva ca sā syādyā kriyeta pareṇa /
children.translated_text: And that lordship which is conferred by another would be mere servitude;

children.text: syādathāpi na hetoḥ kasyaneśvaratā syat // Jm_23.39 //
children.translated_text: Or if it arises without any cause, then whose lordship could it not be? [Jm 23.39]

body.text: evamapi tu gate bhaktirāgādavigaṇitayuktāyuktasya -
body.translated_text: Even granting all this, for one who, out of passionate devotion, disregards what is logical and illogical —

children.text: yadi kāraṇamīśvara eva vibhurjagato nikhilasya tavābhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Īśvara</s> alone, the all-pervading Lord, is in your view the cause of the entire world,

children.text: nanu nārhasi mayyadhiropayituṃ vihitaṃ vibhunā kapirājavadham // Jm_23.40 //
children.translated_text: Then surely you should not impute to me what was ordained by the Lord — the killing of the king of monkeys. [Jm 23.40]

body.text: iti sa mahātmā tamīśvakāraṇikaṃ suśliṣṭairhetubhirmūkatāmivopanīya taṃ pūrvakarmakṛtavādinamāmantraṇāsauṣṭhavenābhimukhīkṛtyovāca - bhavānapyasmānna śobhate vikutsayamānaḥ / sarvaṃ hi te pūrvakarmakṛtamityabhimānaḥ / tena ca tvāṃ bravīmi -
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having reduced the advocate of <s>Īśvara</s> as the cause to virtual silence with well-joined arguments, turned to the proponent of <s>pūrvakarma</s> (past actions) as the cause of all, and addressing him courteously, said: "Your honor too does not look well censuring us. For it is your conviction that everything is caused by <s>pūrvakarman</s> (past actions). And therefore I say to you —"

children.text: syātsarvameva yadi pūrvakṛtaprabhāvācchākhāmṛgaḥ suhata eva mayaiṣa tasmāt /
children.translated_text: If everything were indeed the result of prior deeds (<s>pūrvakṛta</s>), then this monkey was well slain by me; therefore,

children.text: dagdhe hi pūrvakṛtakarmadavāgnināsmin pāpaṃ kimatra mama yena vigarhase mām // Jm_23.41 //
children.translated_text: since he has been consumed by the forest-fire of previously accumulated <s>karma</s>, what sin is there in this for me, that you should reproach me? || Jm 23.41 ||

children.text: athāsti pāpaṃ mama vānaraṃ ghnataḥ kṛtaṃ mayā tarhi na pūrvakarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: But if there is sin in my killing the monkey, then it was done by me and not by prior <s>karma</s>;

children.text: yadiṣyate karma ca karmahetukaṃ na kaścidevaṃ sati mokṣameṣyati // Jm_23.42 //
children.translated_text: and if <s>karma</s> is said to be caused by [prior] <s>karma</s>, then no one in that case would ever attain liberation. || Jm 23.42 ||

children.text: bhavecca saukhyaṃ yadi duḥkhahetuṣu sthitasya duḥkhaṃ sukhasādhaneṣu vā /
children.translated_text: And if happiness results for one established in causes of suffering, or suffering for one engaged in means of happiness,

children.text: ato 'numīyeta sukhāsukhaṃ dhruvaṃ pravartate pūrvakṛtaikahetukam // Jm_23.43 //
children.translated_text: then it must be inferred that happiness and unhappiness certainly proceed from prior deeds as their sole cause. || Jm 23.43 ||

children.text: na dṛṣṭamevaṃ ca yataḥ sukhāsukhaṃ na pūrvakarmaikamato 'sya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: But since happiness and unhappiness are not seen to [operate] in this way, prior <s>karma</s> is not their sole cause;

children.text: bhavedabhāvaśca navasya karmaṇastadaprasiddhau ca purātanaṃ kutaḥ // Jm_23.44 //
children.translated_text: and there would be the non-existence of new <s>karma</s>, and if that is not established, whence the ancient? || Jm 23.44 ||

children.text: pūrvakarmakṛtaṃ sarvamathaivamapi manyase /
children.translated_text: If you hold that everything is indeed caused by prior <s>karma</s>,

children.text: vānarasya vadhaḥ kasmānmatkṛtaḥ parikalpyate // Jm_23.45 //
children.translated_text: then why is the killing of the monkey imagined to be done by me? || Jm 23.45 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā niranuyojyairhetubhistasya maunavratamivopadiśya tamucchedavādinaṃ smitapūrvakamuvāca - āyuṣmataḥ ko 'yamatyādaro 'smadvigarhāyāṃ yadi tattvamucchedavādaṃ manyase?
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having as it were taught him a vow of silence through irrefutable arguments, addressed that minister who was versed in the science of statecraft (<s>kṣatravidyā</s>), smiling: 'And why, sir, do you too revile us, if you hold as right the method prescribed in the treatises on statecraft (<s>arthaśāstra</s>)?

children.text: lokaḥ paro yadi na kaścana kiṃ vivarjyaṃ pāpaṃ śubhaṃ prati ca kiṃ bahumānamohaḥ /
children.translated_text: For in that [system], what is to be practiced for the sake of gain is approved, whether proper or improper;

children.text: svacchandaramyacarito 'tra vicakṣaṇaḥ syādevaṃ gate suhata eva ca vānaro 'yam // Jm_23.46 //
children.translated_text: and having raised oneself up through wealth, one will then practice <s>Dharma</s> — [so they say]. || Jm 23.51 ||

children.text: janavādabhayādathāśubhaṃ parivarjyaṃ śubhamārgasaṃśrayāt /
children.translated_text: If through separation from compassion such action is to be blamed, and its painful fruit is observed,

children.text: svavacaḥpratilomaceṣṭitairjanavādānapi nātiyātyayam // Jm_23.47 //
children.translated_text: yet in the very treatise where this [killing] is sanctioned, with what face do you profess truth? || Jm 23.53 ||

children.text: svakṛtāntapathāgataṃ sukhaṃ na samāpnoti ca lokaśaṅkayā /
children.translated_text: And if he does not attain happiness that has come upon the path of his own doctrine, out of fear of public opinion,

children.text: iti niṣphalavādavibhramaḥ paramo 'yaṃ nanu bāliśādhamaḥ // Jm_23.48 //
children.translated_text: then is not this the supreme fool among fools — one who is deceived by fruitless doctrine? || Jm 23.48 ||

body.text: yadapi ca bhavānāha -
body.translated_text: And as for what you said —

children.text: dārūṇi naikavidhavarṇaguṇākṛtīni karmātmakāni na bhavanti bhavanti caiva /
children.translated_text: Pieces of wood, of many varied colors, qualities, and shapes, which are by nature [products of] <s>karma</s>, both come into being and also do not come into being;

children.text: naṣṭāni naiva ca yathā punarudbhavanti lokastathāyamiti ko 'tra ca nāma hetuḥ // Jm_23.49 //
children.translated_text: and once destroyed, they do not arise again — the world is likewise — and what cause is there in this? || Jm 23.49 ||

children.text: ucchedavādavātsalyaṃ syādevamapi te yadi /
children.translated_text: Even if your attachment to the doctrine of annihilation (<s>ucchedavāda</s>) were thus,

children.text: vigarhaṇīyaḥ kiṃ hantā vānarasya narasya vā // Jm_23.50 //
children.translated_text: why should the slayer of a monkey — or of a man — be blamed? || Jm 23.50 ||

body.text: iti sa mahāsattvastamucchedavādinaṃ vispaṣṭaśobhenottarakrameṇa tūṣṇīṃbhāvaparāyaṇaṃ kṛtvā taṃ kṣatravidyāvidagdhamamātyamuvāca - bhavānapyasmān kasmāditi vikutsayate yadi nyāyyamarthaśāstraparidṛṣṭaṃ vidhiṃ manyase?
body.translated_text: Thus that great being, having reduced that annihilationist to silence through a sequence of brilliantly clear refutations, addressed that minister who was skilled in the science of statecraft: 'And why, sir, do you too despise us, if you consider the method prescribed in the treatises on statecraft to be right?

children.text: anuṣṭheyaṃ hi tatreṣṭamarthārthaṃ sādhvasādhu vā /
children.translated_text: For in that [system], what is to be practiced for the sake of gain is the approved [course], whether virtuous or not;

children.text: athoddhṛtya kilātmānamarthairdharmaṃ kariṣyate // Jm_23.51 //
children.translated_text: and then, having raised oneself up through wealth, one will practice <s>Dharma</s>. || Jm 23.51 ||

body.text: atastvāṃ bravīmi -
body.translated_text: Therefore I say to you:

children.text: prayojanaṃ prāpya na cedavekṣyaṃ snigdheṣu bandhuṣvapi sādhuvṛttam /
children.translated_text: If, upon achieving one's objective, proper conduct need not be observed even toward affectionate kinsmen,

children.text: hate mayā carmaṇi vānare 'smin kā śāstradṛṣṭe 'pi naye vigarhā // Jm_23.52 //
children.translated_text: then what blame is there, even in the method prescribed by the treatises, in my having killed this monkey for its skin? || Jm 23.52 ||

children.text: dayāviyogādatha garhaṇīyaṃ karmedṛśaṃ dūḥkhaphalaṃ ca dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: If through separation from compassion such an action is blameworthy and its painful fruit is observed,

children.text: yatrābhyanujñātamidaṃ na tantre prapadyase kena mukhena tattvam // Jm_23.53 //
children.translated_text: then in the very treatise where this is sanctioned — with what face do you embrace it as truth? || Jm 23.53 ||

children.text: iyaṃ vibhūtiśca nayasya yatra tatrānayaḥ kidṛśavibhramaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If this is the grandeur of [your] statecraft, then what kind of folly would the absence of statecraft be?

children.text: aho pragalbhaiḥ paribhūya lokamunnīyate śāstrapathairadharmaḥ // Jm_23.54 //
children.translated_text: Alas, by the bold, <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is elevated through the paths of the treatises, with contempt for the world! || Jm 23.54 ||

children.text: adṛṣṭamevātha tavaitadiṣṭaṃ śāstre kila spaṣṭapathopadiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Or if this is your cherished position — that it is clearly taught in the treatise as an open path —

children.text: śāstraprasiddhena nayena gacchan na garhaṇīyo 'smi kapervadhena // Jm_23.55 //
children.translated_text: then walking by the method established in the treatise, I should not be blamed for the killing of the monkey! || Jm 23.55 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā jitaparṣatkān paricitaprāgalbhyānapi ca tānamātyān prasahyābhibhūya samāvarjitahṛdayāṃ ca sarājikāṃ parṣadamavetya teṣāṃ vānaravadhahṛllekhavinayanārthaṃ rājānamābabhāṣe - naiva ca khalvahaṃ mahārāja prāṇinaṃ vānaraṃ hatavān / nirmāṇavidhirayam / nirmitasya hi vānarasyedaṃ carma mayā gṛhītamasyaiva kathākramasya prastāvārtham / tadalaṃ māmanyathā pratigrahītum / ityuktvā tamṛddhyābhisaṃskāraṃ pratisaṃhṛtya parayā ca mātrayābhiprasāditamānasaṃ rājānaṃ saparṣatkamavetyovāca -
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having forcibly overcome those ministers — who had conquered assemblies and were well-practiced in boldness — and perceiving that the assembly along with the king had had its heart won over, spoke to the king in order to remove the heart-stain [caused by] the killing of the monkey: 'In truth, O great king, I did not kill a living monkey. This was an act of magical creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>). For the skin I took was of a magically created monkey, for the purpose of providing an occasion for this very discourse.' Having said this, he withdrew the magical creation, and having fully pacified the mind of the king and his assembly with the utmost gentleness, he said:

children.text: saṃpaśyan hetutaḥ siddhiṃ svatantraḥ paralokavit /
children.translated_text: One who perceives success as arising from causes, who is self-reliant, who knows the next world,

children.text: sādhupratijñaḥ saghṛṇaḥ prāṇinaṃ ko haniṣyati // Jm_23.56 //
children.translated_text: who is devoted to right resolve and possessed of compassion — who [such a person] would kill a living being? || Jm 23.56 ||

body.text: paśya mahārāja,
body.translated_text: Behold, O great king:

children.text: ahetuvādī paratantradṛṣṭiranāstikaḥ kṣatranayānugo vā /
children.translated_text: That which one who advocates causelessness, who holds views dependent on others, who is a nihilist, or who follows the way of political expediency,

children.text: kuryānna yannāma yaśolavārthaṃ tannyāyavādī kathamabhyupeyāt // Jm_23.57 //
children.translated_text: would not do even for fame and gain — how would one who advocates right reasoning undertake it? || Jm 23.57 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭirnaraśreṣṭha śubhāśubhā vā sabhāgakarmapratipattihetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Right or wrong view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), O best of men, is the cause of engagement in corresponding actions;

children.text: dṛṣṭyanvayaṃ hi pravikalpya tattadvāgbhiḥ kriyābhiśca vidarśayanti // Jm_23.58 //
children.translated_text: for having determined this or that in accordance with their view, people display [their views] through words and deeds. || Jm 23.58 ||

children.text: saddṛṣṭirasmācca niṣevitavyā tyājyā tvasaddṛṣṭiranarthavṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore right view (<s>saddṛṣṭi</s>) should be cultivated, and wrong view (<s>asaddṛṣṭi</s>), which showers misfortune, should be abandoned;

children.text: labhyaśca satsaṃśrayiṇā kramo 'yamasajjanāddūracareṇa bhutvā // Jm_23.59 //
children.translated_text: and this course is attainable by one who resorts to the company of the good, having ranged far from the wicked. || Jm 23.59 ||

body.text: asaṃyatāḥ saṃyataveṣadhāriṇaścaranti kāmaṃ bhuvi bhikṣurākṣasāḥ /
body.translated_text: Unrestrained [persons] wearing the guise of the restrained wander at will upon the earth — mendicant-demons (<s>bhikṣurākṣasa</s>),

body.text: vinirdahantaḥ khalu bāliśaṃ janaṃ kudṛṣṭibhirdṛṣṭiviṣā ivoragāḥ // Jm_23.60 //
body.translated_text: burning indeed the foolish folk with wrong views, like serpents with poison in their gaze. || Jm 23.60 ||

children.text: ahetuvādādivirūkṣavāśitaṃ śṛgālavattatra viśeṣalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The distinguishing mark there [of such persons] is that their cry is harsh with doctrines of causelessness (<s>ahetuvāda</s>) and the like, like that of a jackal;

children.text: ato na tānarhati sevituṃ budhaścarettadarthaṃ tu parākrame sati // Jm_23.61 //
children.translated_text: therefore the wise person should not attend upon them, but should strive for their [right] purpose when he has the strength. || Jm 23.61 ||

children.text: loke virūḍhayaśasāpi tu naiva kāryā kāryārthamapyasadṛśena janena maitrī /
children.translated_text: Even with one of widespread fame, friendship should not be formed with an unworthy person, even for the sake of one's purpose;

children.text: hemantadurdinasamāgamadūṣito hi saubhāgyahānimupayāti niśākaro 'pi // Jm_23.62 //
children.translated_text: for even the moon, friend of <s>kumuda</s> lotuses, suffers loss of beauty when tainted by the advent of winter's foul weather. || Jm 23.62 ||

children.text: tadvarjanād guṇavivarjayiturjanasya saṃsevanācca guṇasevanapaṇḍitasya /
children.translated_text: By avoiding the company of those devoid of virtues and by cultivating the company of those wise in the service of virtues,

children.text: svāṃ kirtimujjvalaya saṃjanayan prajānāṃ doṣānurāgavilayaṃ guṇasauhṛdaṃ ca // Jm_23.63 //
children.translated_text: make your fame radiant, generating in the people the dissolution of attachment to faults and affection for virtues. || Jm 23.63 ||

children.text: tvayi ca carati dharma bhūyasāyaṃ nṛlokaḥ sucaritasumukhaḥ syātsvargamārgapratiṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when you, [O king], practice <s>Dharma</s> abundantly, this world of men,

children.text: jagadidamanupālyaṃ caivamabhyudyamaste vinayaruciramārgaṃ dharmamasmādbhajasva // Jm_23.64 //
children.translated_text: with faces turned toward good conduct, would be established on the path to heaven; this world must be protected thus — therefore embrace <s>Dharma</s>, whose path is adorned with discipline. || Jm 23.64 ||

children.text: śīlaṃ viśodhaya samarjaya dātṛkīrtiṃ maitraṃ manaḥ kuru jane svajane yathaiva /
children.translated_text: Purify your conduct, polish the fame of generosity, make your mind friendly toward people as toward your own kin;

children.text: dharmeṇa pālaya mahīṃ ciramapramādādevaṃ sameṣyasi sukhaṃ tridivaṃ yaśaśca // Jm_23.65 //
children.translated_text: protect the earth with <s>Dharma</s> for a long time, vigilantly — thus you shall attain happiness and glory in the three heavens. || Jm 23.65 ||

children.text: kṛṣipradhānān paśupālanodyatān mahīruhān puṣpaphalānvitāniva /
children.translated_text: Just as one whose livelihood depends on agriculture, who is engaged in tending cattle, [is like] a tree endowed with flowers and fruits,

children.text: apālayañjānapadān balipradān nṛpo hi sarvauṣadhibhirvirudhyate // Jm_23.66 //
children.translated_text: a king who does not protect his tribute-paying country-folk is antagonized by all [their] vital resources. || Jm 23.66 ||

children.text: vicitrapaṇyakrayavikrayāśrayaṃ vaṇigjanaṃ paurajanaṃ tathā nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The merchant class engaged in buying and selling various wares, and likewise the townspeople,

children.text: na pāti yaḥ śulkapathopakāriṇaṃ virodhamāyāti sa kośasaṃpadā // Jm_23.67 //
children.translated_text: a king who does not protect those who contribute through tolls and taxes becomes estranged from the prosperity of his treasury. || Jm 23.67 ||

body.text: adṛṣṭadoṣaṃ yudhi dṛṣṭavikramaṃ tathā balaṃ yaḥ prathitāsrakauśalam /
body.translated_text: And an army of proven valor in battle, free from [known] faults, renowned for its skill in arms —

body.text: vimānayed bhūpatiradhyupekṣayā dhruvaṃ viruddhaḥ sa raṇe jayaśriyā // Jm_23.68 //
body.translated_text: a king who dishonors it through neglect surely becomes estranged from the goddess of victory in battle. || Jm 23.68 ||

children.text: tathaiva śīlaśrutayogasādhuṣu prakāśamāhātmyaguṇeṣu sādhuṣu /
children.translated_text: Likewise, toward the holy ones who are righteous through conduct, learning, and spiritual practice, whose virtuous qualities of greatness are manifest —

children.text: carannavajñāmalinena vartmanā narādhipaḥ svargasukhervirudhyate // Jm_23.69 //
children.translated_text: a sovereign who behaves with contempt, walking a tainted path, becomes estranged from the happiness of heaven. || Jm 23.69 ||

children.text: drumadyathāmaṃ pracinoti yaḥ phalaṃ sa hanti bījaṃ na rasaṃ ca vindati /
children.translated_text: Just as one who plucks unripe fruit from a tree destroys the seed and does not obtain the juice,

children.text: adharmyamevaṃ balimuddharannṛpaḥ kṣiṇoti deśaṃ na ca tena nandati // Jm_23.70 //
children.translated_text: so a king who exacts unlawful tribute devastates the country and does not rejoice thereby. || Jm 23.70 ||

children.text: yathā tu saṃpūrṇaguṇo mahoruhaḥ phalodayaṃ pākavaśātprayacchati /
children.translated_text: But just as a great tree, full of virtues, yields fruit in due season through the power of ripening,

children.text: tathaiva deśaḥ kṣitipābhirakṣito yunakti dharmārthasukhairnarādhipam // Jm_23.71 //
children.translated_text: so a country protected by a king endows the sovereign with <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s> (wealth), and <s>Sukha</s> (happiness). || Jm 23.71 ||

children.text: hitānamātyānnipuṇārthadarśinaḥ śucīni mitrāṇi janaṃ svameva ca /
children.translated_text: Bind to your heart your beneficial ministers, skilled in discerning right policy, your trustworthy friends, and your own people,

children.text: badhāna cetassu tadiṣṭayā girā dhanaiśca saṃmānanayopapāditaiḥ // Jm_23.72 //
children.translated_text: through speech that is dear to them, and through wealth bestowed with respect. || Jm 23.72 ||

children.text: tasmāddharmaṃ tvaṃ puraskṛtya nityaṃ śreyaḥprāptau yuktacetāḥ prajānām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, always placing <s>Dharma</s> foremost, with your mind intent on the welfare of the people,

children.text: rāgadveṣonmuktayā daṇḍanītyā rakṣaṃllokānātmano rakṣa lokān // Jm_23.73 //
children.translated_text: protecting the worlds with a policy of punishment free from attachment and hatred — while protecting the worlds, protect yourself! || Jm 23.73 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā taṃ rājānaṃ dṛṣṭikṛtakāpathādvivecya samavatārya ca sanmārgaṃ saparṣatkaṃ tata eva gaganatalaṃ samutpatya prāñjalinā tena janena sabahumānapraṇatena pratyarcyamānastadevāraṇyāyatanaṃ pratijagāma /
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having turned that king away from the wrong path created by [false] views and guided him onto the right path, together with his assembly, flew up from that very place into the sky; honored by those people with their palms joined in reverence and respectful bows, he returned to that very forest hermitage.

body.text: tadevamasatkṛtānāmapi satpuruṣāṇāṃ pūrvopakāriṣvanukampā na śithilībhavati kṛtajñatvātkṣamāsātmyācca / iti nāsatkāramātrakeṇa pūrvakṛtaṃ vismartavyam / evaṃ sa bhagavānanabhisaṃbuddho 'pi paravādānabhibhūya sattvavinayaṃ kṛtavāniti buddhavarṇe 'pi vācyam / evaṃ mithyādṛṣṭirananuyogakṣamānupāśrayatvādasevyā ceti mithyādṛṣṭivigarhāyāmapyupaneyam / viparyayeṇa samyagdṛṣṭipraśaṃsāyāmiti /
body.translated_text: Thus the compassion of virtuous persons toward their former benefactors does not slacken, even when they are treated disrespectfully, because of their gratitude and their habituation to patience. Therefore, a former kindness should not be forgotten merely because of disrespectful treatment. Thus the Blessed One, even before his Enlightenment, overcame the doctrines of others and accomplished the training of beings — this should also be cited in the description of the <s>Buddha</s>'s [virtues]. Thus, false view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) should not be resorted to, since it cannot withstand examination — this should be adduced in the condemnation of wrong view as well. And conversely, in the praise of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: // iti mahābodhijātakaṃ trayoviṃśatitamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third [story], the <s>Mahābodhi Jātaka</s>.

body.text:
24. Mahākapijātakam
nātmaduḥkhena tathā santaḥ saṃtapyante yathāpakāriṇāṃ kuśalapakṣahānyā / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text:
24. The <s>Mahākapi Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Great Monkey)
The virtuous are not so much pained by their own suffering as by the loss of the wholesome course of those who wrong them. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila śrīmati himavatpārśve vividhadhāturuciracitrāṅgarāge nīlakauśeyaprāvārakṛtottarāsaṅga iva vanagahanalakṣmyā prayatnaracitairivānekavarṇasaṃsthānavikalpairvaiṣamyabhakticitrairvibhūṣitataṭāntadeśe pravisṛtanaikaprasravaṇajale gambhīrakandarāntaraprapātasaṃkule paṭutaramadhukaranināde manojñamārutopavījyamānavicitrapuṣpaphalapādape vidyādharākrīḍabhute mahākāyaḥ kapirekacaro babhuva / tadavasthamapi cainamapariluptadharmasaṃjñaṃ kṛtajñamakṣudrasvabhāvaṃ dhṛtyā mahatyā samanvitamanurāgavaśādiva karuṇā naiva mumoca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on the beautiful slopes of the <s>Himavat</s> — whose rocky surfaces were charmingly variegated with diverse mineral hues, as if wearing an outer garment of blue silk through the beauty of the dense forest, adorned at the edges of its terraces with manifold patterns of colors, forms, and designs as if carefully fashioned, with waters of numerous streams flowing far, teeming with deep ravines and precipitous waterfalls, resonant with the sharp buzzing of bees, with trees bearing delightful flowers and fruits fanned by pleasant breezes, frequented by <s>Vidyādharas</s> at play — was a great-bodied monkey living alone. And even in that state, with his awareness of <s>Dharma</s> undiminished, grateful, noble by nature, and endowed with great fortitude, compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) did not release him, as if drawn by affection.

children.text: sakānanā sādrivarā sasāgarā gatā vināśaṃ śataśo vasuṃdharā /
children.translated_text: The earth with its forests, mountains, and oceans has perished hundreds of times,

children.text: yugāntakāle salilānalānilairna bodhisattvasya mahākṛpālutā // Jm_24.1 //
children.translated_text: [consumed] by water, fire, and wind at the end of the <s>yuga</s> — but not the great compassion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. || Jm 24.1 ||

body.text: atha sa mahātmā tāpasa iva vanaruparṇaphalamātravṛttiranukampamānastena tena vidhinā gocarapatitān prāṇinastamaraṇyapradeśamadhyavasati sma /
body.translated_text: Then that great soul, subsisting on mere forest roots, leaves, and fruits like an ascetic, compassionately caring for the living beings that came within his range by various means, dwelt in that forest region.

body.text: athānyatamaḥ puruṣo gāṃ pranaṣṭāmanveṣituṃ kṛtodyogaḥ samantato 'nuvicaran mārgāpranaṣṭo digbhāgasaṃmūḍhamatiḥ paribhramaṃstaṃ deśamupajagāma / sa kṣutpipāsādharmaśramaparimlānatanurdaurmanasyavahninā cāntaḥpradīpyamāno viṣādātibhārādivānyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇo dadarśa paripākavaśādvicyutāni paripiñjarāṇi katicittindukīphalāni / sa tānyāsvādya kṣutparikṣāmatayā paramasvādūni manyamānastatprabhavānveṣaṇaṃ pratyabhivṛddhotsāhaḥ samantato 'nuvilokayan dadarśa prapātataṭāntavirūḍhaṃ paripakkaphalānamitapiñjarāgraśākhaṃ tindukīvṛkṣam / sa tatphalatṛṣṇayākṛṣyamāṇastaṃ giritaṭamadhiruhya tasya tindukīvṛkṣasya phaliniṃ śākhāṃ prapātābhinatāmadhyāruroha phalalobhena cāsyāḥ prāntamupajagāma /
body.translated_text: Then a certain man, having set out in search of a lost cow, wandering about in all directions, having lost his way and become confused about the cardinal directions, roaming about, came to that region. He, his body withered by hunger, thirst, weariness, and fatigue, and being inwardly consumed by the fire of despondency, as if weighed down by an excess of despair, sat down at the foot of a certain tree and saw some <s>tindukī</s> (persimmon) fruits, yellowish-brown from ripeness, that had fallen [to the ground]. Having tasted them and considering them supremely delicious because of the emaciation of his hunger, with his eagerness revived for seeking their source, looking about in all directions, he saw a <s>tindukī</s> tree growing at the edge of a precipice-cliff, with its topmost branches bending low, tawny with ripe fruits. Drawn by his craving for those fruits, he climbed up that mountain-cliff, ascended the fruit-bearing branch of that <s>tindukī</s> tree which bent over the precipice, and in his greed for the fruits reached its tip.

children.text: śākhātha sā tasya mahīruhasya bhārātiyogānnamitā kṛśatvāt /
children.translated_text: That branch of that great tree, bent by the excess of its burden and its slenderness,

children.text: paraśvadheneva nikṛttamūlā saśabdabhaṅgaṃ sahasā papāta // Jm_24.2 //
children.translated_text: As if its roots were cut by an axe, it suddenly fell with a loud crash. || Jm 24.2 ||
