body.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ mahati giridurge samantataḥ śailabhittiparikṣipte kūpa iva nyapatat / parṇasaṃcayaguṇāttvasya gāmbhīryācca salilasya na kiṃcidaṅgamabhajyata / sa tasmāduttīrya salilātsamantataḥ parisarpanna kutaściduttaraṇamārgaṃ dadarśa / sa nispratīkāraṃ martavyamiha mayā nacirāditi visrasyamānajīvitāśaḥ śokāśrupariṣiktadīnavadanastrīvreṇa daurmanasyaśalyena pratudyamānaḥ kātarahṛdayastattadārtivaśād vilalāp /
body.translated_text: He fell along with it into a great mountain gorge, enclosed on all sides by rock walls, like a well. But due to the cushioning mass of leaves and the depth of the water, none of his limbs were broken. Climbing out of the water, he searched all around but could not find any path of escape. Thinking 'I shall surely die here before long, with no remedy,' his hopes of survival slipping away, his miserable face drenched with tears of grief, pierced by the thorn of despondency as if by shame, his heart faint, he lamented in various ways according to his anguish:

children.text: kāntāre durge 'smijanasaṃpātarahite nipatitaṃ mām /
children.translated_text: I have fallen into this remote, inaccessible wilderness, devoid of human presence;

children.text: yatnādapi parimṛgayan mṛtyoranyaḥ ka iva paśyet // Jm_24.3 //
children.translated_text: Even if searching with great effort, who other than Death could find me? || Jm 24.3 ||

children.text: bandhujanamitravarjitamekanipānīkṛtaṃ maśakasaṃghaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Bereft of kinsmen and friends, made the sole drinking place of swarms of mosquitoes,

children.text: avapātānanamagnaṃ mṛgamiva ko 'bhyuddhariṣyati mām // Jm_24.4 //
children.translated_text: Sunk into this pit with face submerged, like a trapped animal — who will rescue me? || Jm 24.4 ||

children.text: udyānakānanavimānasaridvicitraṃ tārāvikīrṇamaṇiratnavirājitābhram /
children.translated_text: Beautiful with gardens, groves, palaces, and rivers, its sky radiant with scattered stars, gems, and jewels —

children.text: tāmisrapakṣarajanīva ghanāndhakārā kaṣṭaṃ jaganmama tiraskurute 'ntarātriḥ // Jm_24.5 //
children.translated_text: Alas, the midnight darkness, dense and black like a night of the dark fortnight, conceals the world from me. || Jm 24.5 ||

body.text: iti sa puruṣastattadvilapaṃstena salilena taiśca sahanipatitaistindukaphalairvartayamānaḥ katiciddināni tatrāvasat /
body.translated_text: Thus that man, lamenting in various ways, sustained himself for several days there on that water and on the <s>tinduka</s> (Diospyros) fruits that had fallen in with him.

body.text: atha sa mahākapirāhārahetostadvanamanuvicarannāhūyamān iva mārutākampitābhistasya tindukīvṛkṣasyāgraśākhābhistaṃ pradeśamabhijagāma / abhiruhya cainaṃ tatprapātamavalokayan dadarśa taṃ puruṣaṃ kṣutparikṣāmanayanavadanaṃ paripāṇḍukṛśadīnagātraṃ paryutsukaṃ tatra viceṣṭamānam / sa tasya paridyūnatayā samāvajitānukampo mahākapirnikṣiptāhāravyāpārastaṃ puruṣaṃ pratataṃ bikṣamāṇo mānuṣīṃ vācamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Now the great monkey, wandering through that forest in search of food, was drawn as if summoned by the topmost branches of that <s>tinduka</s> tree, swaying in the wind, and came to that place. Climbing up and looking down into the chasm, he saw that man — his eyes and face emaciated from hunger, his body pale, thin, wretched, and anxious — struggling about there. The great monkey, his compassion aroused by the man's enfeebled condition, set aside his own search for food and, gazing steadily at the man, spoke in a human voice:

children.text: mānuṣāṇāmagamye 'smin prapāte parivartase /
children.translated_text: In this chasm inaccessible to humans, you languish;

children.text: vaktumahaṃsi tatsādhu ko bhavāhina vā kutaḥ // Jm_24.6 //
children.translated_text: Please tell me then — who are you, sir, and from where have you come? || Jm 24.6 ||

body.text: atha sa puruṣastaṃ mahākapimārtatayā samabhipraṇamyodvīkṣamāṇaḥ sāñjaliruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that man, bowing reverently to the great monkey in his distress, looking up at him with palms joined, said:

children.text: mānuṣo 'smi mahābhāga pranaṣṭo vicaran vane /
children.translated_text: I am a human, O noble one, who became lost while wandering in the forest;

children.text: phalārthī pādapādasmādimāmāpadamāgamam // Jm_24.7 //
children.translated_text: Seeking fruits, I fell from a tree into this calamity. || Jm 24.7 ||

children.text: tatsuhṛdvandhuhīnasya prāptasya vyasanaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for one bereft of friends and kinsmen, who has met with great misfortune,

children.text: nātha vānarayūthānāṃ mamāpi śaraṇaṃ bhava // Jm_24.8 //
children.translated_text: O lord of the monkey troops, be a refuge for me as well. || Jm 24.8 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā sa mahāsattvaḥ parāṃ karuṇāmupajagāma /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>Mahāsattva</s> (Great Being) was overcome with the deepest compassion.

children.text: āpadgato bandhusuhṛdvihīnaḥ kṛtāñjalirdīnamudīkṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who has fallen into calamity, bereft of kinsmen and friends, with palms joined, gazing up pitifully —

children.text: karoti śatrūnapi sānukampānākampayatyeva tu sānukampān // Jm_24.9 //
children.translated_text: He makes even enemies compassionate, and how much more does he move those already disposed to compassion! || Jm 24.9 ||

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ karuṇāyamāṇastatkāladurlabhena snigdhena vacasā samāśvāsayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, filled with compassion, comforted him with tender words, rare to hear at such a time:

body.text: prapātasaṃkṣiptaparākramo 'hamabāndhavo veti kṛthāḥ śucaṃ mā /
body.translated_text: Do not grieve, thinking 'My strength is confined by this chasm' or 'I have no kinsmen';

body.text: yadbandhukṛtyaṃ tava kiṃcidatra kartāsmi tatsarvamalaṃ bhayena // Jm_24.10 //
body.translated_text: Whatever duty a kinsman would perform for you here, all that I shall do — have no fear. || Jm 24.10 ||

body.text: iti sa mahāsattvastaṃ puruṣamāśvāsya tataścāsmai tindukānyaparāṇi ca phalāni samupahṛtya taduddharaṇayogyayā puruṣabhāragurvyā śilayānyatra yogyāṃ cakāra / tataścātmano balapramāṇamavagamya śakto 'hamenametasmātprapātādurddhartumiti niścitamatiravatīrya prapātaṃ karuṇayā paricodyamānastaṃ puruṣamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Mahāsattva</s> (Great Being), having comforted that man and brought him <s>tinduka</s> fruits and other fruits as well, practiced elsewhere with a rock heavy enough to bear a man's weight, suitable for pulling him out. Then, having assessed the measure of his own strength, and determined 'I am able to lift this man out of this chasm,' he descended into the chasm, impelled by compassion, and said to the man:

children.text: ehi pṛṣṭhaṃ mamāruhya sulagno 'stu bhavān mayi /
children.translated_text: Come, climb upon my back and hold fast to me,

children.text: yāvadabhyuddharāmi tvāṃ svadehātsārameva ca // Jm_24.11 //
children.translated_text: While I pull you out, along with the very essence of my body. || Jm 24.11 ||

children.text: asārasya śarīrasya sāro hyeṣa mataḥ satām /
children.translated_text: For of this unsubstantial body, this is deemed its true essence by the virtuous —

children.text: yatpareṣāṃ hitārtheṣu sādhanīkriyate budhaiḥ // Jm_24.12 //
children.translated_text: That which the wise employ as an instrument for the benefit of others. || Jm 24.12 ||

body.text: sa tatheti pratiśrutyābhipraṇasya cainamadhyāruroha /
body.translated_text: He replied 'So be it,' bowed down to him, and climbed upon his back.

children.text: athābhirūḍhaḥ sa nareṇa tena bharātiyogena vihanyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with that man mounted upon him, impeded by the exertion of bearing his weight,

children.text: sattvaprakarṣādaviprannadhairyaḥ pareṇa duḥkhena tamujjahāra // Jm_24.13 //
children.translated_text: Yet unshaken in courage due to the excellence of his <s>sattva</s> (spiritual resolve), he lifted him out with supreme effort. || Jm 24.13 ||

children.text: uddhṛtya cainaṃ paramapratītaḥ khedātparivyākulakhelagāmī /
children.translated_text: Having lifted him out, utterly exhausted, his movement faltering with labored breathing,

children.text: śilātalaṃ toyadharābhinīlaṃ viśrāmahetoḥ śayanīcakāra // Jm_24.14 //
children.translated_text: He made a slab of rock, dark as a rain cloud, his bed for the sake of rest. || Jm 24.14 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ śuddhasvabhāvatayā kṛtopakāratvācca tasmātpuruṣādapāyanirāśaṅko visrambhādenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being of pure nature and having rendered a great service to that man, without suspecting any harm from him, spoke to him trustingly:

children.text: avyāhatavyālamṛgapraveśe vanapradeśe 'tra samantamārge /
children.translated_text: In this forest region, open to the unrestricted entry of wild beasts and serpents, with paths on every side,

children.text: khedaprasuptaṃ sahasā nihanti kaścitpurā māṃ svahitodayaṃ ca // Jm_24.15 //
children.translated_text: Let no one suddenly slay me while I sleep from exhaustion, before I have accomplished my own welfare and that of others. || Jm 24.15 ||

children.text: yato bhavān dikṣuṃ vikīrṇacakṣuḥ karotu rakṣāṃ mama cātmanaśca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, with eyes scanning all directions, please keep watch for my safety and your own;

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ śrameṇāsmi parītamūrtistatsvaptumicchāmi muhūrtamātram // Jm_24.16 //
children.translated_text: My body is thoroughly overcome with fatigue — I wish to sleep for just a moment. || Jm 24.16 ||

body.text: atha sa mithyāvinayapragalbhaḥ - svapitu bhavān yathākāmaṃ sukhaprabodhāya, sthito 'haṃ tvatsaṃrakṣaṇāyetyasmai pratiśuśrāva / atha sa puruṣastasmin mahāsattve śramabalānnidrāvaśamupagate cintāmaśivāmāpede -
body.translated_text: Then that man, bold in his false civility, promised him: 'May you sleep as you please for a pleasant awakening; I stand here for your protection.' But when that <s>Mahāsattva</s> (Great Being) had fallen asleep from the force of exhaustion, that man conceived an evil thought:

children.text: mūlaiḥ prayatnātiśayādhigamyairvanyairyadṛcchādhigataiḥ phalairvā /
children.translated_text: With wild roots obtainable only through extreme effort, or with fruits found by mere chance,

children.text: evaṃ parikṣīṇatanoḥ kathaṃ syādyātrāpi tāvatkuta eva puṣṭiḥ // Jm_24.17 //
children.translated_text: How can one so emaciated even continue the journey, let alone gain nourishment? || Jm 24.17 ||

children.text: idaṃ ca kāntāramasupratāraṃ kathaṃ tariṣyāmi balena hīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this wilderness is so difficult to cross — how shall I, bereft of strength, traverse it?

children.text: paryāptarūpaṃ tvidamasya māṃsaṃ kāntāradurgottaraṇāya me syāt // Jm_24.18 //
children.translated_text: But this monkey's flesh would be sufficient for me to cross through the difficulties of this wilderness. || Jm 24.18 ||

children.text: kṛtopakāro 'pi ca bhakṣya eva nisargayogaḥ sa hi tādṛśo 'sya /
children.translated_text: Even one who has rendered service is indeed food by nature — for such is his natural classification;

children.text: āpatprasiddhaśca kilaiṣa dharmaḥ pātheyatāmityupaneya eṣaḥ // Jm_24.19 //
children.translated_text: And this is a <s>dharma</s> (principle) well-established in times of distress — that he should be used as provisions. || Jm 24.19 ||

children.text: yāvacca visrambhasukhaprasuptastāvanmayā śakyamayaṃ nihantum /
children.translated_text: And while he sleeps deeply in the comfort of trust, I can slay him;

children.text: imaṃ hi yuddhābhimukhaṃ sametya siṃho 'pi saṃbhāvyaparājayaḥ syāt // Jm_24.20 //
children.translated_text: For even a lion, encountering this one face to face in battle, might well suffer defeat. || Jm 24.20 ||

body.text: tannāyaṃ vilambituṃ me kāla iti viniścitya sa durātmā lobhadoṣavyāmohitamatirakṛtajño vipannadharmasaṃjñaḥ pranaṣṭakāruṇyasaumyasvabhāvaḥ paridurbalo 'pyakāryātirāgānmahatīṃ śilāmudyamya tasya mahākapeḥ śirasi mumoca /
body.translated_text: Deciding 'This is no time for delay,' that vile-souled one, his mind deluded by greed and vice, ungrateful, his sense of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) destroyed, his natural compassion and gentleness extinguished, though exceedingly weak, driven by excessive attachment to a wrongful act, lifted a great rock and hurled it at the head of the great monkey.

children.text: śilātha sā durbalavihvalena kāryātirāgāttvaritena tena /
children.translated_text: That rock, released hastily by him, feeble and trembling,

children.text: atyantanidropagamāya muktā nidrāpravāsāya kaperbabhūva // Jm_24.21 //
children.translated_text: Thrown to bring about the deepest sleep, instead became the cause of the monkey's awakening. || Jm 24.21 ||

children.text: sarvātmanā sā na samāsasāda mūrdhānamasmānna vinispipeṣa /
children.translated_text: It did not fully strike his head, nor did it crush him;

children.text: koṭyekadeśena tu taṃ rujantī śīlā tale sāśanivatpapāta // Jm_24.22 //
children.translated_text: But grazing him on one edge, causing pain, the rock fell to the ground like a thunderbolt. || Jm 24.22 ||

children.text: śīlābhighātādavabhinnamūrdhā vegādavaplutya ca bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his head split open by the blow of the rock, leaping away swiftly,

children.text: kenāhato 'smīti dadarśa nānyaṃ tameva tu hrītamukhaṃ dadarśa // Jm_24.23 //
children.translated_text: Looked around thinking 'By whom was I struck?' — and saw no other, but saw only that very man with his face downcast in shame. || Jm 24.23 ||

children.text: vailakṣyapītaprabhamapragalbhaṃ viṣādadainyātparibhinnavarṇam /
children.translated_text: His complexion drained pale with embarrassment, timid, his color broken by dejection and misery,

children.text: trāsodayādāgatakaṅṭhaśoṣaṃ svedārdramudvīkṣitumapyaśaktam // Jm_24.24 //
children.translated_text: His throat parched from the onset of fear, moist with sweat, unable even to look up. || Jm 24.24 ||

body.text: atha sa mahākapirasyaiva tatkarmeti niscitamatiḥ svamabhighātaduḥkhamacintayitvā tena tasyātmahitanirapekṣeṇātikaṣṭena karmaṇā samupajātasaṃvegakāruṇyaḥ parityattakrodhasaṃrambhadoṣaḥ sabāspayanayanastaṃ puruṣamavekṣya samanuśocannuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the great monkey, certain that this was indeed that man's doing, disregarding the pain of his own wound, his compassion and alarm aroused by that man's exceedingly cruel act of utter disregard for his own welfare, free from the faults of anger and fury, his eyes brimming with tears, looking upon that man and lamenting for him, said:

children.text: mānuṣeṇa satā bhadra tvayedaṃ kṛtamīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: O good sir, that you, being a human, have done such a thing as this —

children.text: kathaṃ nāma vyavasitaṃ prārabdhaṃ kathameva vā // Jm_24.25 //
children.translated_text: How was it resolved upon? How indeed was it even undertaken? || Jm 24.25 ||

children.text: madabhidrohasaṃrabdhaṃ tvaṃ nāmāpatitaṃ param /
children.translated_text: You ought rather to have had the boldness and valor to restrain

children.text: vinivāraṇaśauṭīravikramo roddhumarhasi // Jm_24.26 //
children.translated_text: One who has fallen to the utmost depth, seized by the impulse of hostility toward me. || Jm 24.26 ||

children.text: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavānasmītyabhūnmānonnatirmama /
children.translated_text: I had a swelling of pride thinking 'I have done something difficult' —

children.text: tvayāpaviddhā sā duramatiduṣkarakāriṇā // Jm_24.27 //
children.translated_text: That has been cast far away by you, who have done something even more difficult. || Jm 24.27 ||

children.text: paralokādivānīto mṛtyorvaktrāntarādiva /
children.translated_text: As if brought back from the next world, as if from the jaws of death,

children.text: prapātāduddhṛto 'nyasmādanyatra patito hyasi // Jm_24.28 //
children.translated_text: You were pulled out of one chasm only to have fallen into another. || Jm 24.28 ||

children.text: dhigaho bata durvṛttamajñānamatidāruṇam /
children.translated_text: Alas, shame upon this wicked, terribly cruel ignorance,

children.text: yatpātayati duḥkheṣu sukhāśākṛpaṇaṃ jagat // Jm_24.29 //
children.translated_text: Which, wretched in its desire for happiness, casts the world into suffering! || Jm 24.29 ||

children.text: pātito durgatāvātmā kṣiptaḥ śokānalo mayi /
children.translated_text: You have cast your own self into a wretched state, hurled the fire of grief upon me,

children.text: nimīlitā yaśolakṣmīrguṇamaitrī virodhitā // Jm_24.30 //
children.translated_text: Dimmed the splendor of your reputation, and turned to enmity the friendship born of virtue. || Jm 24.30 ||

children.text: gatvā dhigvādalakṣatvaṃ hatā viśvasanīyatā /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the condition of one whose word cannot be trusted, you have slain your own trustworthiness —

children.text: kā nu khalvarthanispattirevamākāṅkṣitā tvayā // Jm_24.31 //
children.translated_text: What gain, pray, was so eagerly sought by you in this manner? || Jm 24.31 ||

children.text: dunoti māṃ naiva tathā tviyaṃ rujā yathaitadevātra manaḥ kṣiṇoti mām /
children.translated_text: This wound does not pain me so much as this very thing here torments my mind;

children.text: gato 'smi pāpe tava yannimittatāṃ na cāhamenastadapohituṃ prabhuḥ // Jm_24.32 //
children.translated_text: That I have become an occasion for your sin — and I am powerless to remove that evil from you. || Jm 24.32 ||

children.text: saṃdṛśyamānavapureva tu pārśvato māṃ tatsādhvanuvraja dṛḍhaṃ hyasi śaṅkanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But keeping my person visible at your side, follow me closely — for you are indeed to be regarded with suspicion;

children.text: yāvadbahupratibhayādgahanāditastvāṃ grāmāntapaddhatimanupratipādayāmi // Jm_24.33 //
children.translated_text: Until I guide you out of this dense forest, full of many terrors, to the path leading to a village. || Jm 24.33 ||

children.text: ekākinaṃ kṣāmaśarīrakaṃ tvāṃ mārganabhijñaṃ hi vane bhramantam /
children.translated_text: For if someone were to come upon you wandering alone in the forest, with emaciated body, ignorant of the way,

children.text: kaścitsamāsādya purā karoti tvatpīḍaṇādvyarthapariśramaṃ mām // Jm_24.34 //
children.translated_text: And were to harm you, it would render my own toil fruitless. || Jm 24.34 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā taṃ puruṣamanuśocañjanāntamānīya pratipādya cainaṃ tanmārgaṃ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Thus that great-souled one, lamenting for that man, led him to the edge of habitation and, having guided him there, spoke to him once more about the path:

children.text: prāpto janāntamasi kānta vanāntametat kāntāradurgabhayamutsṛja gaccha sādhu /
children.translated_text: You have reached the edge of habitation, dear one; leave behind this fear of the perilous wilderness and go well. And strive to renounce sinful deeds,

children.text: pāpaṃ ca karma parivarjayituṃ yatethā duḥkho hi tasya niyamena vipākakālaḥ // Jm_24.35 //
children.translated_text: For the time of their ripening is assuredly full of suffering. || Jm 24.35 ||

body.text: iti sa mahākapistaṃ puruṣamanukampayā śiṣyamivānuśiṣya tameva vanapradeśaṃ pratijagāma /
body.translated_text: Thus the great monkey, having instructed that man with compassion as if he were a disciple, returned to that very forest region.

body.text: atha sa puruṣastadatikasṭaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtvā paścāttāpavahninā saṃpradīpyamānacetāmahatā kuṣṭhavyādhinā rūpāntaramupanītaḥ kilāsacitracchaviḥ prabhidyamānavraṇavisravārdragātraḥ paramadurgandhaśarīraḥ sadyaḥ samapadyata / sa yaṃ yaṃ deśamabhijagāma tatastata evainamatibībhatsavikṛtataradarśanaṃ mānuṣa ityaśraddheyarūpaṃ bhinnadīnasvaramabhivīkṣya puruṣāḥ sākṣadayaṃ pāṣmeti manyamānāḥ samudyataloṣṭadaṇḍā nirbhartsanaparuṣavacasaḥ pravāsayāmāsuḥ / athainamanyatamo rājā mṛgayāmanuvicaran pretamivāraṇye paribhramantaṃ prakṣīṇamalinavasanaṃ nātipracchannakaupīnamatidurdaśanamabhivīkṣya sasādhvasakautūhalaḥ papraccha -
body.translated_text: Now that man, having committed that exceedingly cruel sin, his mind ablaze with the fire of remorse, was transformed in appearance by a severe case of leprosy — his skin mottled with white patches, his body moist with the discharge flowing from splitting wounds, his body emitting the most terrible stench — he became so at once. Wherever he went, people, seeing him in that excessively hideous and disfigured form, his appearance scarcely believable as human, his voice broken and pitiful, thinking 'This is surely a personification of disease,' drove him away with raised clods and sticks, with harsh words of rebuke. Then a certain king, wandering on a hunt, saw him roaming in the wilderness like a ghost — his garments worn and filthy, his loincloth barely concealing him, his appearance utterly wretched — and, struck with both alarm and curiosity, asked:

children.text: virūpitatanuḥ kuṣṭhaiḥ kilāsaśabalacchaviḥ /
children.translated_text: With body disfigured by leprosy, skin mottled with white patches,

children.text: pāṇḍuḥ kṛśatanurdīno rajorūkṣaśiroruhaḥ // Jm_24.36 //
children.translated_text: Pale, thin-bodied, wretched, with hair rough with dust — || Jm 24.36 ||

children.text: kastvaṃ pretaḥ piśāco vā mūrtaḥ pāṣmātha pūtanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are you? A ghost? A <s>piśāca</s> (flesh-eating demon)? An embodied pestilence? Or a <s>pūtana</s> (putrid demon)?

children.text: anekarogasaṃghātaḥ katamo vāsi yakṣmaṇām // Jm_24.37 //
children.translated_text: An assemblage of countless diseases — or which particular one among afflictions are you? || Jm 24.37 ||

body.text: sa taṃ dīnena kaṇṭhena samabhipraṇamannuvāca - mānuso 'smi mahārāja, nāmānuṣa iti / tatkathamimāmavasthāmanuprāpto 'sīti ca paryanuyukto rājñā tadasmai svaṃ duścaritamāviṣkṛtyovāca -
body.translated_text: He, bowing reverently to the king, replied in a feeble voice: 'I am a human, O great king, not a non-human.' And when pressed by the king, 'How then did you come to this condition?', he revealed his own misdeed to him and said:

children.text: mitradrohasya tasyedaṃ puṣpaṃ tāvadupasthitam /
children.translated_text: This is but the flower of that treachery against a friend that has appeared so far;

children.text: ataḥ kaṣṭhataraṃ vyaktaṃ phalamanyadbhaviṣyati // Jm_24.38 //
children.translated_text: Clearly, a fruit even more terrible than this will follow hereafter. || Jm 24.38 ||

children.text: tasmānmitreṣvabhidrohaṃ śatruvad draṣṭumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, regard treachery against friends as you would an enemy;

children.text: bhāvasnigdhamavekṣasva bhāvasnigdhaṃ suhṛjjanam // Jm_24.39 //
children.translated_text: Look upon your kindhearted, affectionate companions with genuine affection. || Jm 24.39 ||

children.text: mitreṣvamitracaritaṃ parigṛhya vṛttamevaṃbidhāṃ samupayānti daśāmihaiva /
children.translated_text: Those who adopt the conduct of an enemy toward friends meet with such a fate as this even in this very life;

children.text: lobhādidoṣamalinīkṛtamānasānāṃ mitradruhāṃ gatirataḥ parato 'numeyā // Jm_24.40 //
children.translated_text: The destiny of those who betray friends, whose minds are defiled by faults such as greed, can therefore be inferred to be still worse in the hereafter. || Jm 24.40 ||

children.text: vātsalyasaumyahṛdayastu suhṛtsu kīrtiṃ viśvāsabhāvamupakārasukhaṃ ca tebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But one whose heart is gentle with tender affection toward his friends obtains fame, trustworthiness, and the happiness of beneficence from them,

children.text: prāpnoti saṃnatiguṇaṃ manasaḥ praharṣaṃ durdharṣatāṃ ca pirubhistridaśālayaṃ ca // Jm_24.41 //
children.translated_text: as well as the joy of mind that is the reward of humility, invincibility by enemies, and [rebirth in] the abode of the gods. || Jm 24.41 ||

children.text: imaṃ viditvā nṛpa mitrapakṣe prabhāvasiddhī sadasatpravṛttyoḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing this efficacy in the realm of friends, O king, of good and bad conduct,

children.text: bhajasva mārga sujanābhipannaṃ tena prayātamanuyāti bhūtiḥ // Jm_24.42 //
children.translated_text: follow the path trodden by the virtuous — prosperity follows one who walks upon it. || Jm 24.42 ||

body.text: tadevaṃ nātmaduḥkhena tathā santaḥ saṃtapyante yathāpakāriṇāṃ kuśalapakṣahānyā / iti tathāgatamāhātmye vācyam / satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe kṣāntikathāyāṃ mitrānabhidrohe pāpakarmādinavapradarśane ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus the virtuous are not so much pained by their own suffering as by the loss of the wholesome course of those who wrong them. This should be cited in [describing] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; in hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence; in a discourse on patience (<s>kṣānti</s>); in [teaching] non-hostility toward friends; and in the demonstration of the danger of evil deeds.

body.text: iti mahākapijātakaṃ catuviṃśatitamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth [story], the <s>Mahākapi Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 25. Śarabhajātakam
body.translated_text: 25. The <s>Śarabha Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Śarabha Deer)

body.text: jighāṃsumapyāpadgatamanukampanta eva mahākārūṇikā nopekṣante / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The greatly compassionate do not neglect even one who seeks to kill them, but rather show compassion when he has fallen into distress. As tradition relates —

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānyatamasminnaraṇyavanapradeśe nirmānuṣasaṃpātanīrave vividhamṛgakulādhivāse tṛṇagahananimagnamūlavṛkṣakṣupabahule pathikayānavāhanacaraṇairavinyastamārgasimāntalekhe salilamārgavalmīkaśvabhraviṣamabhūbhāge balajavavarṇasattvasaṃpannaḥ saṃhananavatkāyopapannaḥ śarabho mṛgo babhūva / sa kāruṇyābhyāsādanabhidrugdhacittaḥ sattveṣu tṛṇaparṇasalilamātravṛttiḥ saṃtoṣaguṇādaraṇyavāsaniratamatiḥ pravivekakāma iva yogī tamaraṇyapradeśamabhyalaṃcakāra /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> was a <s>śarabha</s> deer in a certain uninhabited forest region — where no human footfall echoed, inhabited by herds of various wild animals, thick with shrubs and small trees whose roots were submerged in dense grass, with no trace of road-boundaries marked by the feet of travelers, vehicles, or draft animals, with uneven terrain of water-channels, anthills, and pits — endowed with strength, speed, beauty, and vitality, possessed of a well-knit body. He, with a mind free from hostility toward beings due to his habitual practice of compassion, subsisting on mere grass, leaves, and water, cherishing the virtue of contentment, with his mind devoted to forest-dwelling, adorned that forest region like a yogī desiring solitude.

children.text: mṛgākṛtirmānuṣadhīracetāstapasvivatprāṇiṣu sānukampaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the form of a deer, yet with a mind of human steadfastness and wisdom, compassionate toward living beings like an ascetic,

children.text: cacāra tasmin sa vane vivikte yogīva saṃtuṣṭamatistṛṇāgraiḥ // Jm_25.1 //
children.translated_text: he wandered in that secluded forest — like a yogī, content in mind with [mere] tips of grass. || Jm 25.1 ||

body.text: atha kadācidanyatamo rājā tasya viṣayasyādhipatisturagavarādhirūḍhaḥ sajyacāpabāṇavyagrapāṇirmṛgeṣvastrakauśalamātmano jijñāsamānaḥ saṃrāgavaśājjavena mṛgānanupatannuttamajavena vājinā dūrādapasṛtahastyaśvarathapadātikāyastaṃ pradeśamupajagāma / dūradeva cālokya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ hantumutpatitaniścayaḥ samutkṛṣṭaniśitasāyako yataḥ sa mahātmā tena turagavaraṃ saṃcodayāmāsa / atha bodhisattvaḥ samālokyaiva turagavaragataṃ sāyudhamabhipatantaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ śaktimānapi pratyavasthātuṃ nivṛttasāhasasaṃrambhatvātpareṇa javātiśayena samutpapāta / so 'nugamyamānastena turaṃgameṇānumārgāgataṃ mahacchvabhraṃ goṣpadamiva javena laṅghayitvā pradudrāva / atha turagavarastenaiva mārgeṇa taṃ śarabhamanupatannuttamena javapramāṇena tacchvabhramāsādya laṅgayitumanadhyavasitamatiḥ sahasā vyatiṣṭhata /
body.translated_text: Then, on one occasion, a certain king, the lord of that territory, mounted upon a fine horse, with a strung bow and arrows ready in his hands, wishing to test his own skill in archery against the deer, galloping after deer in the grip of passion, carried far from his elephant, horse, chariot, and infantry forces by the supreme speed of his steed, came to that region. Having spotted that great being from afar, his resolve to kill it leaping forth, he drew a sharp, well-whetted arrow and urged his fine horse toward where that great soul was. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upon seeing that king riding his fine horse and charging at him with weapon [drawn], though possessed of the strength to stand his ground, since his impulse toward violent resistance had been abandoned, sprang forth with a speed surpassing the other's. As he was being pursued by that horse, he leaped over a great pit that lay in his path as if it were a cow's hoofprint, and dashed away. Then the fine horse, pursuing that <s>śarabha</s> along the same path, upon reaching that pit at top speed, unable to resolve to leap over it, suddenly halted.

children.text: athāśvapṛṣṭhādudgīrṇaḥ sāyudhaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that lord of the earth, thrown from the horse's back, along with his weapons,

children.text: papāta mahati svabhre daityayodha ivodadhau // Jm_25.2 //
children.translated_text: fell into the great pit — like a <s>Daitya</s> warrior into the ocean. || Jm 25.2 ||

children.text: nibaddhacakṣuḥ śarabhe sa tasmin saṃlakṣayāmāsa na taṃ prapātam /
children.translated_text: With his eyes fixed upon that <s>śarabha</s>, he did not notice the precipice;

children.text: visrambhadoṣāccalitāsano 'tha drutāśvavegoparamātpapāta // Jm_25.3 //
children.translated_text: then, his seat dislodged through the fault of over-confidence, he fell when the swift horse's speed suddenly stopped. || Jm 25.3 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvasturagakhuraśabdapraśamātkiṃ nu khalu pratinivṛttaḥ syādayaṃ rājeti samutpannavitarkaḥ paścādāvarjitāvadanaḥ samālokayan dadarśa tamaśvamanārohakaṃ tasmin prapātoddeśe 'vasthitam / tasya buddhirabhavat - niyatamatra prapāte nipatitaḥ sa rājā / na hyatra kiṃcidviśramahetoḥ saṃśrayaṇīyarūpaṃ ghanapracchāyaṃ vṛkṣamūlamasti nīlotpaladalanīlavimalasalilamavagāhayogyaṃ vā saraḥ / na caiva vyālamṛgānuvicaritamaraṇyavanamavagāḍhena yatra kvacidupasṛjya turagavaraṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when the sound of the horse's hooves ceased, the thought arising in his mind, 'Has this king perhaps turned back?', looking backward with his face turned around, saw that horse without its rider, standing at the edge of that precipice. The thought occurred to him: 'Surely this king has fallen into this precipice. For there is nothing here in the nature of a shelter to rest at — no dense-shaded tree-root, no lake with clear water the color of blue lotus petals fit for bathing. Nor would one who has plunged into this wilderness forest, frequented by wild beasts, release his fine horse somewhere and rest, or conduct a hunt. And there is not even a thicket of grass here dense enough to conceal him. Therefore that king must clearly have fallen into this pit.' Then that great soul, having arrived at this conclusion, was filled with supreme compassion even for that hunter [who had pursued him].

body.text: viśramyate mṛgayā vānuṣṭhiyate / na cātra kiṃcittṛṇagahanamapi tadvidhaṃ yatra nilīnaḥ syāt / tadvyaktamātra śvabhre nipatitena tena rājñā bhavitavyamiti / tataḥ sa mahātmā niścayamupetya vadhake 'pi tasmin parāṃ karuṇāmupajagāma /
body.translated_text: He must clearly have fallen into this pit.' Then that great soul, having arrived at this conclusion, was filled with supreme compassion even for that would-be killer.

children.text: adyaiva citradhvajabhūṣaṇena vibhrājamānāvaraṇāyudhena /
children.translated_text: Just now, [attended] by an army resplendent with variegated banners and ornaments,

children.text: rathāśvapattidviradākulena vāditracitradhvaninā balena // Jm_25.4 //
children.translated_text: its armor and weapons gleaming, teeming with chariots, horses, infantry, and elephants, with the varied sounds of musical instruments, || Jm 25.4 ||

children.text: kṛtānuyātro rucirātapatraḥ parisphuraccāmarahāraśobhaḥ /
children.translated_text: escorted [in procession], beautiful with his parasol, adorned with the splendor of waving <s>cāmara</s> whisks and pearl garlands,

children.text: devendravatprāñjalibhirjanaughairabhyarcito rājasukhānyavāpya // Jm_25.5 //
children.translated_text: honored like <s>Devendra</s> (Indra) by throngs of people with palms joined, having enjoyed the pleasures of a king — || Jm 25.5 ||

children.text: adyaiva magno mahati prapāte nipātavegādabhirugṇagātraḥ /
children.translated_text: just now, submerged in a great precipice, his limbs shattered by the force of the fall,

children.text: murchānvitaḥ śokaparāyaṇo vā kaṣṭaṃ bata kleśamayaṃ prapannaḥ // Jm_25.6 //
children.translated_text: overwhelmed by fainting or given over to grief — alas, [how] he has fallen into a painful, wretched state! || Jm 25.6 ||

children.text: kiṇāṅkitānīva manāṃsi duḥkhairna hīnavargasya tathā vyathante /
children.translated_text: The minds of those of low estate, calloused as it were by sufferings, do not feel such anguish

children.text: adṛṣṭaduḥkhānyatisaukumāryādyathottamānāṃ vyasanāgameṣu // Jm_25.7 //
children.translated_text: as those of the exalted do when calamity arrives — unused to suffering because of their extreme delicacy. || Jm 25.7 ||

body.text: na cāyamataḥ śakṣyatei svayamuttartum / yadyapi sāvaśeṣaprāṇastannāyamupekṣituṃ yuktamiti vitarkayan sa mahātmā karuṇayā samākṛṣyamāṇahṛdayastaṃ prapātataṭāntamupajagāma / dadarśa cainaṃ tatra reṇusaṃsargānmṛditavārabāṇaśobhaṃ vyākulitoṣṇīṣavasanasaṃnāhaṃ prapātapatananighātasaṃjānītābhirvedanābhirāpīḍyamānahṛdayamāpatitavaitānyaṃ viceṣṭamānam /
body.translated_text: And he will not be able to climb out of here by himself. Even if his life still remains, it is not right to abandon him.' Reflecting thus, that great soul, his heart being drawn by compassion, approached the edge of that precipice. And he saw the king there — his splendor of fine garments and arrows dimmed by contact with dust, his turban, clothing, and armor in disarray, his heart tormented by the pains born of the impact of falling into the precipice, overcome by despair and writhing about.

children.text: dṛṣṭvāya taṃ tatra viceṣṭamānaṃ narādhipaṃ bāṣpaparītanetraḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that lord of men writhing there, his eyes brimming with tears,

children.text: kṛpāvaśādvismṛtaśatrusaṃjñastadduḥkhasāmānyamupājagāma // Jm_25.8 //
children.translated_text: under the sway of compassion, having forgotten the sense of 'enemy,' he entered into a sharing of his suffering. || Jm 25.8 ||

children.text: uvāca cainaṃ vinayābhijātamudbhāvayan sādhujanasvabhāvam /
children.translated_text: And he spoke to him, born of courtesy, bringing forth the nature of the virtuous,

children.text: āśvāsayan spaṣṭapadena sāmnā śiṣṭopacāreṇa manohareṇa // Jm_25.9 //
children.translated_text: consoling him with kindly words, clearly articulated, with the refined civility that captivates the heart: || Jm 25.9 ||

children.text: kaccinmahārāja na pīḍito 'si prapātapātālamidaṃ prapannaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Are you in pain, O great king, having fallen into this abyss of a precipice?

children.text: kaccinna te vikṣatamatra gātraṃ kaccidrujaste tanutāṃ gacchanti // Jm_25.10 //
children.translated_text: Are your limbs injured here? Are your pains diminishing? || Jm 25.10 ||

children.text: nāmānuṣaścāsmi manuṣyavarya mṛgo 'pyahaṃ tvadviṣayāntavāsī /
children.translated_text: I am no human, O best of men — I am merely an animal dwelling within your domain;

children.text: vṛddhamastvadīyena tṛṇodakena visrambhamityarhasi mayyupetum // Jm_25.11 //
children.translated_text: nourished by your grass and water, you should therefore place your trust in me. || Jm 25.11 ||

children.text: prapātapātādadhṛtiṃ ca mā gāḥ śakto 'hamuddhartumito bhavantam /
children.translated_text: And do not fall into despair because of the fall into the precipice — I have the strength to lift you out of here;

children.text: visrambhitavyaṃ mayi manyase cettatkipramājñāpaya yāvadaimi // Jm_25.12 //
children.translated_text: if you think I am to be trusted, then command me quickly, and I shall go [about it]. || Jm 25.12 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā tena tasyādbhatenābhivyāhāreṇa vismayāvarjitahṛdayaḥ saṃjāyamānavrīḍo niyatamiti cintāmāpede -
body.translated_text: Then that king, his heart won over with amazement by that wondrous utterance of his, feeling shame arise within him, inevitably fell into this thought:

children.text: dṛṣṭāvadāne dviṣati kā nāmāsya dayā mayi /
children.translated_text: "What compassion can this one have toward me, who was seen to be an enemy?

children.text: mama vipratipattiśca keyamasminnanāgasi // Jm_25.13 //
children.translated_text: And what is this offence of mine toward him, who has done no wrong? || Jm 25.13 ||

children.text: aho madhuratīkṣṇena pratyādiṣṭo 'smi karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Ah, I have been rebuked by a deed at once sweet and sharp!

children.text: ahameva mṛgo gaurvā ko 'pyayaṃ śarabhākṛtiḥ // Jm_25.14 //
children.translated_text: I am the animal, or rather a bull — while this one in the form of a <s>śarabha</s> is something more! || Jm 25.14 ||

body.text: tadarhatyayaṃ praṇayapratigrahasaṃpūjanamiti viniścityainamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Therefore he deserves to be honored by the acceptance of his offer of friendship.' Having resolved thus, he said to him:

children.text: vārabāṇāvṛtamidaṃ gātraṃ me nātivikṣatam /
children.translated_text: "This body of mine, covered with fine garments and arrows, is not greatly injured;

children.text: prapātaniṣpeṣakṛtāḥ sahyā eva ca me rujaḥ // Jm_25.15 //
children.translated_text: and the pains caused by the impact of falling into the precipice are bearable. || Jm 25.15 ||

children.text: prapātapanakleśānna tvahaṃ pīḍitastathā /
children.translated_text: I am not so much pained by the distress of falling into the precipice

children.text: iti kalyāṇahṛdaye tvayi praskhalanādyathā // Jm_25.16 //
children.translated_text: as by my stumbling against you, O noble-hearted one. || Jm 25.16 ||

children.text: ākṛtipratyayādyacca dṛṣṭo 'si mṛgavanmayā /
children.translated_text: And as for the fact that I regarded you as a [mere] animal, judging by outward form —

children.text: avijñāya svabhāvaṃ te tacca mā hṛdaye kṛthāḥ // Jm_25.17 //
children.translated_text: not knowing your true nature, do not take that to heart. || Jm 25.17 ||

body.text: atha śarabhastasya rājñaḥ prītisūcakena tenābhivyāhāreṇānumatamuddharaṇamavetya puruṣabhāragurvyā śīlayā taduddharaṇayogyāṃ kṛtvā viditātmabalapramāṇastaṃ nṛpatimuddhartuṃ vyavasitamatiravatīrya taṃ prapātaṃ savinayamabhigamyovāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>śarabha</s>, understanding from the king's speech indicative of affection that his rescue was approved, having made the [ground of the] pit suitable for his rescue through effort worthy of a man's burden, knowing the measure of his own strength, resolved to lift up that king. Descending into the precipice and approaching him with courtesy, he said:

body.text: madgātrasaṃsparśamimaṃ muhūrtaṃ kāryānurodhāttvamanukṣamasva /
body.translated_text: "Endure for a moment this contact with my body, for the sake of the task at hand;

body.text: yāvatkaromi svahitābhipattyā prītiprasādābhimukhaṃ mukhaṃ te // Jm_25.18 //
body.translated_text: while I make your face — inclining toward joy and grace — [rise upward] through the attainment of your own welfare. || Jm 25.18 ||

body.text: tadārohatu matpuṣṭhaṃ mahārājaḥ sulagnaśca mayi bhavatviti / sa tatheti pratiśrutyainamaśvavadāruroha /
body.translated_text: Let the great king mount upon my back and hold fast to me.' He, having assented with 'So be it,' mounted him as one would a horse.

children.text: tataḥ samabhyunnatapūrvakāyastenādhirūḍhaḥ sa narādhipena /
children.translated_text: Then, with his forequarters raised high, mounted upon by that lord of men,

children.text: samutpatannuttamasattvavegaḥ khe toraṇavyālakavad babhāse // Jm_25.19 //
children.translated_text: he leaped upward with the vigor of supreme strength — appearing in the sky like a serpent-figure upon a gateway arch. || Jm 25.19 ||

children.text: uddhṛtya durgādatha taṃ narendraṃ prītaḥ samānīya turaṃgameṇa /
children.translated_text: Having rescued that lord of men from the dangerous place, joyful, reuniting him with his horse,

children.text: nivedya cāsmai svapurāya mārgaṃ vanaprayāṇābhimukho babhūva // Jm_25.20 //
children.translated_text: and having pointed out to him the road to his city, he turned toward the forest [to depart]. || Jm 25.20 ||

body.text: atha sa rājā kṛtajñatvāttena tasya vinayamadhureṇopacāreṇa samāvartitahṛdayaḥ saṃpariṣvajya śarabhamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, out of gratitude and with his heart turned around by that graciously sweet courtesy, embracing the <s>śarabha</s>, said:

children.text: prāṇā amī me śarabha tvadīyāḥ prāgeva yatrāsti mama prabhutvam /
children.translated_text: "These lives of mine, O <s>Śarabha</s>, are yours — let alone that over which I have lordship;

children.text: tadarhasi draṣṭumidaṃ puraṃ me satyāṃ rucau tatra ca te 'stu vāsaḥ // Jm_25.21 //
children.translated_text: therefore deign to visit my city, and if it pleases you, let your dwelling be there. || Jm 25.21 ||

children.text: vyādhābhikīrṇe sabhaye vane 'smin śītoṣṇavarsādyupasargaduḥkhe /
children.translated_text: In this forest, infested with hunters, fraught with danger, painful with the afflictions of cold, heat, rain, and the like —

children.text: hitvā bhavantaṃ mama nanvayuktamekasya gehābhimukhasya gantum // Jm_25.22 //
children.translated_text: is it not unfit for me to go homeward alone, leaving you behind? || Jm 25.22 ||

body.text: tadehi gacchāva iti / athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ savinayamadhuropacāraṃ saṃrādhayan pratyuvāca -
body.translated_text: Therefore come, let us go.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gratifying him with courtesy and gentle civility, replied:

children.text: bhavadvidheṣveva manuṣyavarya yuktaḥ kramo 'yaṃ guṇavatsaleṣu /
children.translated_text: "This course [of action] is fitting indeed for those like you, O best of men, who are fond of virtues;

children.text: abhyāsayogena hi sajjanasya svabhāvatāmeva guṇā vrajanti // Jm_25.23 //
children.translated_text: for through the force of habitual practice, virtues become second nature for the virtuous. || Jm 25.23 ||

children.text: anugrahītavyamavaiṣi yattu vanocitaṃ māṃ bhavanāśrayeṇa /
children.translated_text: But in that you wish to favor me, a creature of the forest, with a dwelling in [your] palace —

children.text: tenālamanyaddhi sukhaṃ narāṇāmanyādṛśaṃ jātyucitaṃ mṛgāṇām // Jm_25.24 //
children.translated_text: enough of that, for the happiness of humans is one thing, and the happiness natural to the species of animals is another. || Jm 25.24 ||

children.text: cikīrṣite te yadi matpriyaṃ tu vyādhavrataṃ vīra vimuñca tasmāt /
children.translated_text: But if you wish to do what is dear to me, then abandon the practice of hunting, O hero;

children.text: tiryaktvabhavājjaḍacetaneṣu kṛpaiva śocyeṣu mṛgeṣu yuktā // Jm_25.25 //
children.translated_text: toward the animals who are pitiable through the misfortune of being born in animal form, with their dull minds, compassion alone is fitting. || Jm 25.25 ||

children.text: sukhāśraye duḥkhavinodane ca samānacittānavagaccha sattvān /
children.translated_text: Understand that beings are alike in their desire for happiness and their aversion to suffering;

children.text: ityātmanaḥ syādanabhīpsitaṃ yanna tatpareṣvācarituṃ kṣamaṃ te // Jm_25.26 //
children.translated_text: thus what would be undesirable for yourself — that is not fit for you to inflict upon others. || Jm 25.26 ||

children.text: kīrtikṣayaṃ sādhujanādvigarhāṃ duḥkhaṃ ca pāpaprabhavaṃ viditvā /
children.translated_text: Knowing the loss of fame, the reproach from the virtuous, and the suffering born of sin,

children.text: pāpaṃ dviṣatpakṣamivoddharasva nopekṣituṃ vyādhiriva kṣamaṃ te // Jm_25.27 //
children.translated_text: uproot sin as if it were the faction of your enemies — it is no more fit to be neglected than a disease. || Jm 25.27 ||

children.text: lakṣmīniketaṃ yadapāśrayeṇa prāpto 'si lokābhimataṃ nṛpatvam /
children.translated_text: That abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) — the merits by whose support you have attained kingship, esteemed by the world —

children.text: tānyeva puṇyāni vivardhayethā na karśanīyo hyupakāripakṣaḥ // Jm_25.28 //
children.translated_text: those very merits you should increase; for the party of one's benefactors should not be oppressed. || Jm 25.28 ||

children.text: kālopacārasubhagairvipulaiḥ pradānaiḥ śīlena sādhujanasaṃgataniścayena /
children.translated_text: Through generous gifts, grand and graced by timely bestowal, through conduct firmly established in the company of the virtuous,

children.text: bhūteṣu cātmani yathā hitabuddhisiddhyā puṇyāni saṃcinu yaśaḥ sukhasādhanāni // Jm_25.29 //
children.translated_text: and through the realization of a benevolent mind toward beings as toward oneself — accumulate merits, which are the means to fame and happiness. || Jm 25.29 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā taṃ rājānaṃ dṛḍhaṃ sāṃparāyikeṣvartheṣvanugṛhya saṃpratigṛhītavacanastena rājñā sabahumānamabhivīkṣyamāṇastameva vanāntaṃ praviveśa /
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having firmly benefited that king in matters pertaining to the next world, his words having been accepted, being gazed upon with reverence by that king, entered that very forest.

body.text: tadevaṃ jighāṃsumapyāpadgatamanukampanta eva mahākārūṇikā nopekṣanta iti karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyam / tathāgatamahātmye satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe / avaireṇa vairapraśamananidarśane ca kṣāntikathāyāmapyupaneyam / evaṃ tiryaggatānāmapi mahātmanāṃ vadhakeṣvapi sānukrodhā pravṛttirdṛṣṭā / ko manuṣyabhūtaḥ pravrajitapratijño vā sattveṣvanukrośavikalaṃ śobheteti prāṇiṣu sānukrośenāryeṇa bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, the greatly compassionate do not neglect even one who seeks to kill them, but rather show compassion when he has fallen into distress — this should be cited in the description of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>); in the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; in hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence; and in the demonstration of the pacification of enmity through non-enmity, it should be adduced in a discourse on patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) as well. Thus, even among those born in animal states, the conduct of great souls toward their very killers has been seen to be compassionate. Who, being a human, or one who has taken the vow of renunciation, would look well without compassion toward beings? — therefore a noble person should be compassionate toward living beings.

body.text: iti śarabhajātakaṃ pañcaviṃśatitamam /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth [story], the <s>Śarabha Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 26. Rurujātakam
body.translated_text: 26. The <s>Ruru Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Ruru Deer)

body.text: paraduḥkhameva duḥkhaṃ sāghūnām / taddhi na sahante nātmaduḥkham / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvaḥ kila sālabakulapiyālahintālatamālanaktamālavidulaniculakṣipabahule śiṃśapātiniśaśamīpalāśaśākakuśavaṃśaśaravaṇagahane kadambasarjārjunadhavakhadirakuṭajanicite vividhavallīpratānāvaguṇṭhitabahutaruviṭape rurupṛṣatasṛmaracamaragajagavaya mahiṣahariṇanyaṅkuvarāhadvīpitarakṣuvyāghravṛkasiṃharkṣādimṛgavicarite manuṣyasaṃpātavirahite mahatyaraṇyavanapradeśe tatpakāñcanojjvalavarṇaḥ sukumāraromā nānāvidhapadmarāgendranīlamarakatavaiḍūryaruciravarṇabinduvidyotitavicitragātraḥ snigdhābhinīlavimalavipulanayano manīmayairivāparuṣaprabhairviṣāṇakṣurapradeśaiḥ paramadarśanīyarūpo ratnākara iva pādacārī rurumṛgo babhūva / sa jānānaḥ svasya vapuṣo 'tilobhanīyatāṃ tanukāruṇyatāṃ ca janasya nirjanasaṃpāteṣu vanagahaneṣvabhireme, paṭuvijñānatvācca tatra tatra vyādhajanaviracitāni yantrakūṭavāgurāpāśāvapātalepakāṣṭhanivāpabhojanāni samyak pariharannanugāminaṃ ca mṛgasārthamavabodhayannācārya iva piteva ca mṛgāṇāmādhipatyaṃ cakāra /

children.text: rūpavijñānasaṃpattiḥ kriyāsauṣṭhavasaṃskṛtā /
svahitānveṣiṇi jane kutra nāma na pūjyate // Jm_26.1 //

body.text: atha sa kadācinmahātmā tasmin vanagahane vāsopagatastatsamīpavāhinyā navāmbupurṇayā mahavegayā nadyā hriyamāṇasya puruṣasyākranditaśabdaṃ śuśrāva /

children.text: hriyamāṇamanāthamaplavaṃ saritodīrṇajalaughavegayā /
abhidhāvata dīnavatsalāḥ kṛpaṇaṃ tārayituṃ javena mām // Jm_26.2 //
na vilambitumatra śakyate śramadoṣavidheyabāhunā /
na ca gādhamavāpyate kvacittadayaṃ māṃ samayo 'bhidhāvitum // Jm_26.3 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastena tasya karuṇenākranditaśabdena hṛdiva samabhihanyamāno mā bhairmā bhairiti janmaśatābhyastāṃ bhayaviṣādadainyaśramāpanodinīmāmreḍitābhiniṣpīḍitaspaṣṭapadāmuccairmānuṣīṃ vācaṃ visṛjaṃstasmādvanagahanādviniṣpapāt / dūrata eva ca taṃ puruṣamiṣṭamivopāyanamānīyamānaṃ salilaughena dadarśa /

children.text: tatastaduttāraṇaniścitātmā svaṃ prāṇasaṃdehamacintayitvā /
sa tāṃ nadīṃ bhīmarayāṃ jagāhevimokṣobhayan vīra ivārisenām // Jm_26.4 //
āvṛtya mārga vapuṣātha tasya māmāśrayasveti tamabhyuvāca /
trāsāturatvācchramavihvalāṅgaḥ sa pṛṣṭhamevādhiruroha tasya // Jm_26.5 //
saṃsādyamāno 'pi nareṇa tena vivartyamāno 'pi nadīrayeṇa /
sattvocchrayādaskhalitoruvīryaḥ kūlaṃ yayau tasya manonukūlam // Jm_26.6 //
prāpayya tīramatha taṃ puruṣaṃ pareṇa prītyudgamena vinivartitakhedaduḥkham /
svenoṣmaṇā samapanīya ca śītamasya gaccheti taṃ sa visasarja nivedya mārgam // Jm_26.7 //

body.text: atha sa puruṣaḥ snigdhabāndhavasuhṛjjanadurlabhena tena tasyādbhutenābhyupapattisaumukheyan samāvarjitahṛdayastayā cāsya rūpaśobhayā samutthāpyamānavismayabahumānaḥ praṇamyainaṃ tattatpriyamuvāca -

children.text: ā bālyātsaṃbhṛtasnehaḥ suhṛdvāndhava eva vā /
nālaṃ kartumidaṃ karma madarthe yatkṛtaṃ tvayā // Jm_26.8 //
tvadīyāstadime prāṇāstvadarthe yadi nāma me /
svalpe 'pi viniyujyeran sa me syadatyanugrahaḥ // Jm_26.9 //
tadājñāsaṃpradānena kartumarhasyanugraham /
viniyogakṣamatvaṃ me bhavān yatrāvagacchati // Jm_26.10 //

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃrādhayān pratyuvāca -

children.text: na citrarūpā sujane kṛtajñatā nisargasiddhaiva hi tasya sā sthitiḥ /
jagattu dṛṣṭvā samudīrṇavikriyaṃ kṛtajñatāpyadya guṇeṣu gaṇyate // Jm_26.11 //

body.text: yatastvāṃ bravīmi kṛtamidamanusmaratā bhavatā nāyamarthaḥ kasmaicinnivedyaḥ īdṛśenāsmi sattvaviśeṣeṇottārita iti / āmiṣabhūtamatilobhanīyamidaṃ hi me rūpam / paśya / tanughṛṇāni bahulaulyādanibhṛtāni ca prāyeṇa mānuṣahṛdayāni /

children.text: tadātmani guṇāṃścaiva māṃ ca rakṣitumarhasi /
na hi mitreṣvabhidrohaḥ kvacidbhavati bhūtaye // Jm_26.12 //

body.text: mā caivamucyamāno manyupraṇayavirasaṃ hṛdayaṃ kārṣiḥ / mṛgā hi vayamanabhyastamānusopacāraśāṭhyāḥ / api ca /

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ vañcanādakṣairmithyāvinayapaṇḍitaiḥ /
yena bhāvavinīto 'pi janaḥ sāśaṅkamīkṣyate // Jm_26.13 //

body.text: tadetatpriyaṃ bhavatā saṃpādyamānamicchāmīti / sa tatheti pratiśrutya praṇamya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca taṃ mahāsattvaṃ svagṛhamabhyajagāma /

tena khalu samayena tatrānyatamasya rājño devī satyasvapnā babhūva / sā yaṃ yamātiśayikaṃ svapnaṃ dadarśa, sa tathaivābhavat / sā kathācinnidrāvaśamupagatā pratyuṣasamaye svapnaṃ paśyati sma sarvaratnasamāhāramiva śriyā jvalantaṃ siṃhāsanasthaṃ rurumṛgaṃ sarājikayā parṣadā parivṛtaṃ vispaṣṭākṣarapadanyasena mānuṣeṇa vacasā dharmaṃ deśayantam / vismayā kṣiptahṛdayā ca bhartuḥ prabodhapaṭahadhvaninā saha sā vyabudhyata / yathāprastāvaṃ ca samupetya rājānaṃ labdhaprasarapraṇayasaṃmānā -

children.text: sā mismayotphullatarekṣaṇaśrīḥ prītyā samutkampikapolaśobhā /
upāyaneneva nṛpaṃ dadarśa tenādbhutasvapnanivedanena // Jm_26.14 //

body.text: nivedya ca taṃ svapnātiśayaṃ rājñe sādaraṃ punaruvāca -

children.text: tatsādhu tāvatkiryatāṃ mṛgasya tasyopalambhaṃ prati deva yatnaḥ /
antaḥpuraṃ ratnamṛgeṇa tena tārāmṛgeṇeva nabho virājet // Jm_26.15 //

body.text: atha sa rājā dṛṣṭapratyayastasyāḥ svapnadarśanasya pratigṛhya tadvacanaṃ tatpriyakāmyayā ratnamṛgādhigamalobhācca tasya mṛgasyānveṣaṇārthaṃ sarvaṃ vyādhagaṇaṃ samādideśa / pratyahaṃ ca puravare goṣaṇāmiti kārayāmāsa -

children.text: hemacchavirmaṇiśatairiva citragātraḥ khyāto mṛgaḥ śrutiṣu dṛṣṭacaraśca kaiścit /
yastaṃ pradarśayati tasya dadāti rājā grāmottamaṃ paridaśā rucirāḥ striyaśca // Jm_26.16 //

body.text: atha sa puruṣastāṃ ghoṣaṇāṃ punaḥ punarupaśrutya -

children.text: dāridryaduḥkhagaṇanaparikhinnacetāḥ smṛtvā ca taṃ rurumṛgasya mahopakāram /
lobhena tena ca kṛtena vikṛṣyamāṇo dolāyamānahṛdayo vimamarśa tattat // Jm_26.17 //

body.text: kiṃ nu khalu karomi? guṇaṃ paśyāmyuta dhanasamṛddhim? kṛtamanupālayāmyuta kuṭumbatantram? paralokamudbhāvayāmyatheyamam? sadvṛttamanugacchāmyutāho lokavṛttam? śriyamanugacchāmyutāhosvitsādhudayitāṃ śriyam? tadātvaṃ paśyāmyutāyatimiti / athāsya lobhākulitamaterevamabhūt - śakyamadhigatavipuladhanasamṛddhinā svajanamitrātithipraṇayijanasaṃmānanapareṇa sukhānyanubhavatā paro 'pi lokaḥ saṃpādayitum / iti niścitamatirvismṛtya taṃ rurumṛgasyopakāraṃ samupetya rājānamuvāca - ahaṃ deva taṃ mṛgavaramadhivāsaṃ cāsya jānāmi / tadājñāpaya kasmai pradarśayāmyenamiti / tacchrutvā sa rājā pramuditamanāḥ - mamaivainaṃ bhadra pradarśayetyuktvā mṛgayāprayāṇānurūpaṃ veṣamāsthāya mahatā balakāyena parivṛtaḥ puravarānnirgamya tena puruṣeṇādeśyamānamārgastaṃ nadītīramupajagāma / parikṣipya ca tadvanagahanaṃ samagreṇa balakāyena dhanvī hastāvāpi vyavasitāptapuruṣaparivṛtaḥ sa rājā tenaiva puruṣeṇādeśyamānamārgastadvanagahanamanupraviveśa / atha sa puruṣastaṃ rurumṛgaṃ viśvastasthitamālokya pradarśayāmāsa rājñe - ayamayaṃ deva sa mṛgavaraḥ / paśyatvenaṃ devaḥ, prayatnaśca bhavatviti /

children.text: tasyonnāmayato bāhuṃ mṛgasaṃdarśanādarāt /
prakoṣṭhānnyapatatpāṇirvinikṛtta ivāsinā // Jm_26.18 //
āsādya vastūni hi tādṛśāni kriyāviśeṣairabhisaṃskṛtāni /
labdhaprayāmāṇi vipakṣamāndyātkarmāṇi sadyaḥ phalatāṃ vrajanti // Jm_26.19 //

body.text: atha sa rājā tatpradarśitena mārgeṇa rurusaṃdarśanakutūhale nayane vicikṣepa /
vane 'tha tasminnavameghanīle jvalattanuṃ ratnanidhānalakṣmyā /
guṇairuruṃ taṃ sa ruruṃ dadarśa śātahnadaṃ vahnimivābhramakṣe // Jm_26.20 //

children.text: tadrūpaśobhāhṛtamānaso 'tha sa bhūmipastadgrahaṇātilobhāt /
kṛtvā dhanurbāṇavidaṣṭamaurvi bibhitsayā cainamupāruroha // Jm_26.21 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samantato janakolāhalamupaśrutya vyaktaṃ samantātparivṛtto 'smīti niścitamatirvyaddhukāmamupārūḍhaṃ cāvetya rājānaṃ nāyamapayānakāla iti viditvā viśadapadākṣareṇa mānuṣeṇa vacasā rājānamābabhāṣe -

children.text: tiṣṭha tāvanmahārāja mā māṃ vyātsīrnararṣabha /
kautūhalamidaṃ tāvadvinodayitumarhasi // Jm_26.22 //
asminnirjanasaṃpāte nirataṃ gahane vane /
asāvatra mṛgo 'stīti ko nu te māṃ nyavedayat // Jm_26.23 //

body.text: atha sa rājā tasyādbhūtena mānuṣeṇābhivyāhāreṇa bhṛśataramāvarjitahṛdayastamasmai puruṣaṃ śarāgreṇa nirdideśa - ayamasyātyadbhutasya no darśayiteti / atha bodhisattvastaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyabhijñāya vigarhamāṇa uvāca - kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ /

children.text: satya eva pravādo 'yamudakaughagataṃ kila /
dārveva varamuddhatu nākṛtajñamatiṃ janam // Jm_26.24 //
pariśramasya tasyeyamodṛśī pratyupakriyā /
ātmano 'pi na dṛṣṭo 'yaṃ hitasyāpanayaḥ katham // Jm_26.25 //

body.text: atha sa rājā kiṃ nu khalvayamevaṃ vijugupsata iti samutpannakautūhalaḥ sāvegastaṃ rurumuvāca -

children.text: anirbhinnārthagambhīramanārabhyavigarhitam /
tvadidaṃ samupaśrutya sākampamiva me manaḥ // Jm_26.26 //
mṛgātiśaya tadbrūhi kamārabhyeti bhāṣase /
manuṣyamamanuṣyaṃ vā pakṣiṇaṃ mṛgameva vā // Jm_26.27 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -

children.text: nāyaṃ vigarhādara eva rājan kutsārhametattvavagamya karma /
children.translated_text: This is not merely a matter of reproach, O king; having understood this deed to be worthy of censure,

children.text: nāyaṃ punaḥ kartumiti vyavasyettīkṣṇākṣaraṃ tena mayaivamuktam // Jm_26.28 //
children.translated_text: one should resolve never to do it again — it is with this intention that these sharp words were spoken by me. (26.28)

children.text: ko hi kṣate kṣāramivāvasiñced rūkṣākṣaraṃ viskhaliteṣu vākyam /
children.translated_text: For who would pour salt on a wound, or speak harsh words to one who has stumbled?

children.text: priye tu putre 'pi cikitsakasya pravartate vyādhivaśāccikitsā // Jm_26.29 //
children.translated_text: Yet even toward a beloved son, a physician's treatment proceeds according to the nature of the disease. (26.29)

children.text: yamuhyamānaṃ salilena hāriṇā kṛpavaśadabhyupapannavāhanam /
children.translated_text: This man, being swept away by the carrying current, was rescued by me out of compassion, providing him a vehicle of deliverance;

children.text: tato bhayaṃ māṃ nṛvaredamāgataṃ na khalvasatsaṃgatamasti bhūtaye // Jm_26.30 //
children.translated_text: from him, O lord of men, this danger has come to me — truly, association with the wicked never leads to well-being. (26.30)

body.text: atha sa rājā taṃ puruṣaṃ tīkṣṇayā dṛṣṭyā nirbhartsanarūkṣamavekṣyovāca - satyamare re purā tvamanenaivamāpanno 'bhyuddhṛta iti? atha sa puruṣaḥ samāpatitabhayaviṣādasvedavaivarṇyadainyo hrīmandaṃ satyamityavocat / atha sa rājā dhik tvāmityenamavabhartysayan dhanuṣi śaraṃ saṃdhāyābravīt - mā tāvadbhoḥ
body.translated_text: Then that king, fixing a sharp gaze upon that man and rebuking him harshly, said: 'Is it true, wretch, that you were once rescued by this very one when you had fallen into such distress?' And that man, overcome by fear, dejection, sweat, pallor, and misery, said shamefacedly, 'It is true.' Then the king, reproaching him with 'Shame on you!', fitted an arrow to his bow and said: 'Wait now, sirs —

children.text: evaṃvidhenāpi pariśrameṇa mṛdūkṛtaṃ yasya na nāma cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: one whose heart is not softened even by such extraordinary effort as this,

children.text: tulyākṛtīnāmayaśodhvajena kiṃ jīvatānena narādhamena // Jm_26.31 //
children.translated_text: this lowest of men, who brings disgrace upon those of similar form — what use is there in his living?' (26.31)

body.text: ityuktvā muṣṭimābadhya tadvadhārthaṃ dhanuḥ pracakarṣa / atha bodhisattvaḥ karuṇayā mahatyā samuparudhyamānahṛdayastadantarā sthitvā rājānamuvāca - alamalaṃ mahārāja hataṃ hatvā /
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he clenched his fist and drew the bow to slay him. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (being of awakening), his heart overwhelmed by great compassion, stood between them and said to the king: 'Enough, enough, great king! Do not kill one already destroyed.

children.text: yadeva lobhadviṣataḥ pratāraṇāṃ vigarhitāmapyayamabhyupeyivān /
children.translated_text: The very fact that he, out of greed and hatred, resorted to this contemptible betrayal —

children.text: hatastadeveha yaśaḥparikṣayād dhruvaṃ paratrāpi ca dharmasaṃkṣayāt // Jm_26.32 //
children.translated_text: by that alone he is already slain here through the destruction of his reputation, and surely hereafter too through the destruction of his <s>dharma</s> (merit). (26.32)

children.text: asahyaduḥkhodayapītamānasāḥ patanti caivaṃ vyasaneṣu mānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: People whose minds are consumed by the arising of unbearable suffering fall thus into calamities,

children.text: pralobhyamānāḥ phalasampadāśayā pataṃgamūrkhā iva dīpaśobhayā // Jm_26.33 //
children.translated_text: lured by the prospect of gaining rewards, like foolish moths by the splendor of a lamp. (26.33)

children.text: ataḥ kṛpāmatra kurūṣva mā ruṣaṃ yadīpsitaṃ caivamanena kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: Therefore, show compassion here, not anger; and whatever this man desires,

children.text: kiruṣva tenainamavandhyasāhasaṃ sthitaṃ tvadājñāpravaṇaṃ hi me śiraḥ // Jm_26.34 //
children.translated_text: grant it to him, so that his reckless act may not be in vain — for my head stands bowed, ready to obey your command. (26.34)

body.text: atha sa rājā tena tasyāpakāriṇyapi sadayatvenākṛtakena ca tatpratyupakārādareṇa paramavismitamatirjātaprasādaḥ sabahumānamudīkṣamāṇastaṃ ruruvaramuvāca - sādhu sādhu mahābhāga
body.translated_text: Then that king, supremely astonished at his compassionate nature even toward one who had wronged him, and at his genuine disregard for any return of the favor, was filled with faith and, gazing at that excellent <s>Ruru</s> deer with great respect, said: 'Well done, well done, O noble one!

children.text: pratyakṣogrāpakāre 'pi dayā yasyeyamīdṛśī /
children.translated_text: One whose compassion is such even toward a manifest and terrible offender —

children.text: guṇato mānuṣastvaṃ hi vayamākṛtimānuṣāḥ // Jm_26.35 //
children.translated_text: you are truly human in your virtues, while we are merely human in form. (26.35)

children.text: yenānukampyastu tavaiṣa jālmo hetuśca naḥ sajjanadarśanasya /
children.translated_text: Since this wretch is an object of your pity, and since he is the cause of our meeting a virtuous being,

children.text: dadāmi tenepsitamarthamasmai rājye tavāsmiṃśca yatheṣṭacāram // Jm_26.36 //
children.translated_text: I therefore grant him whatever he desires, and to you, freedom to roam as you wish in this kingdom. (26.36)

body.text: rururuvāca - pratigṛhīto 'yaṃ mayāvandhyo mahārājaprasādaḥ / tadājñāpaya yāvadiha saṃgamanaprayojanena tavopayogaṃ gacchāma iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Ruru</s> said: 'I accept this bountiful favor of the great king. Then command, so that having fulfilled the purpose of our meeting here, I may be of service to you.'

body.text: atha sa rājā taṃ ruruṃ gurumiva rathavaramāropya mahatā satkāreṇa puravaraṃ praveśya kṛtātithisatkāraṃ mahati siṃhāsane niveśya samutsāhayamānaḥ sāntaḥpuro 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ prītibahumānasaumyamudīkṣamāṇo dharmaṃ papraccha -
body.translated_text: Then that king, placing <s>Ruru</s> upon a splendid chariot as one would a teacher, brought him into the chief city with great honor, received him with the hospitality due a guest, seated him upon a great throne, and, encouraging him — surrounded by the inner circle and the assembly of ministers, gazing at him with affection and reverence — asked him about <s>dharma</s> (righteousness):

children.text: dharmaṃ prati manuṣyāṇāṃ bahudhā buddhayo gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Regarding <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), the minds of men have gone in many directions;

children.text: niścayastava dharme tu yathā taṃ vaktumarhasi // Jm_26.37 //
children.translated_text: please tell me what your settled conviction regarding <s>dharma</s> truly is.' (26.37)

body.text: atha bodhisattvastasya rājñaḥ saparṣatkasya sphuṭamadhuracitrākṣareṇa vacasā dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (being of awakening) taught <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) to that king and his assembly, in words clear, sweet, and eloquently varied:

children.text: dayāṃ sattveṣu manye 'haṃ dharmaṃ saṃkṣepato nṛpa /
children.translated_text: 'I consider compassion (<s>dayā</s>) toward all beings to be <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) in brief, O king,

children.text: hiṃsāsteyanivṛttyādiprabhedaṃ vividhakriyam // Jm_26.38 //
children.translated_text: with its various forms of practice such as abstention from violence, theft, and the like. (26.38)

body.text: paśya mahārāja,
body.translated_text: Consider, O great king:

children.text: ātmanīva dayā syāccetsvajane vā yathā jane /
children.translated_text: If one had compassion for others as for oneself, or for the people as for one's own family,

children.text: kasya nāma bhaveccittamadharmapraṇayāśivam // Jm_26.39 //
children.translated_text: whose mind would ever turn toward the inauspicious path of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness)? (26.39)

children.text: dayāviyogāttu janaḥ paramāmeti vikriyām /
children.translated_text: But separated from compassion, a person undergoes the most extreme degradation,

children.text: manovākkāyavispandaiḥ svajane 'pi jane yathā // Jm_26.40 //
children.translated_text: through the impulses of mind, speech, and body — toward the people at large just as toward one's own family. (26.40)

children.text: dharmārthī na tyajedasmād dayāmiṣṭaphalodayām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who seeks <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) should not abandon compassion, which yields the most cherished fruits;

children.text: suvṛṣṭiriva sasyāni guṇān sā hi prasūyate // Jm_26.41 //
children.translated_text: for like good rainfall upon crops, it brings forth virtues. (26.41)

children.text: dayākrāntaṃ cittaṃ na bhavati paradroharabhasaṃ
children.translated_text: A mind pervaded by compassion does not rush toward harming others;

children.text: śucau tasmin vāṇī vrajati vikṛtaṃ naiva ca tanuḥ /
children.translated_text: when the mind is pure, neither speech nor body goes astray;

children.text: vivṛddhā tasyaivaṃ parahitaruciḥ prītyanusṛtān
children.translated_text: thus, as one's delight in the welfare of others grows, it gives rise to

children.text: pradānakṣāntyādīñjanayati guṇān kīrtyanuguṇān // Jm_26.42 //
children.translated_text: virtues such as generosity and forbearance, born of love, and conducive to fame. (26.42)

children.text: dayālurnodvegaṃ janayati pareṣāmupaśamād
children.translated_text: The compassionate one does not cause agitation in others, for he is tranquil;

children.text: dayāvān viśvāsyo bhavati jagatāṃ bāndhava iva /
children.translated_text: the compassionate one becomes trustworthy, like a kinsman to the world;

children.text: na saṃrambhakṣobhaḥ prabhavati dayādhīrahṛdaye
children.translated_text: the turbulence of anger cannot prevail in a heart steadied by compassion;

children.text: na kopāgniścitte jvalati hi dayātoyaśiśire // Jm_26.43 //
children.translated_text: the fire of wrath does not blaze in a mind cooled by the water of compassion. (26.43)

children.text: saṃkṣepeṇa dayāmataḥ sthiratayā paśyanti dharmaṃ buddhāḥ
children.translated_text: In brief, the <s>Buddhas</s> (awakened ones), established in compassion, see it as the essence of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness);

children.text: ko nāmāsti guṇaḥ sa sādhudayito yo nānuyāto dayām /
children.translated_text: what virtue is there, cherished by the good, that does not follow from compassion?

children.text: tasmātputra ivātmanīva ca dayāṃ nītvā prakarṣaṃ jane
children.translated_text: Therefore, cultivating compassion to its utmost toward the people — as toward a son, as toward oneself —

children.text: sadvṛttena haranmanāṃsi jagatāṃ rājatvamudbhāvaya // Jm_26.44 //
children.translated_text: captivating the minds of the world through righteous conduct, make your kingship shine forth. (26.44)

body.text:
atha sa rājā samabhinandya tattasya vacanaṃ sayaurajānapado dharmaparāyaṇo babhūva /
abhayaṃ ca sarvamṛgapakṣiṇāṃ dattvān /
body.translated_text: Then that king, having joyfully accepted his words, together with his citizens and subjects, became devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). And he granted safety to all animals and birds.

body.text: tadevaṃ paraduḥkhameva duḥkhaṃ sādhūnām / taddhi na sahante nātmaduḥkhamiti / karuṇāvarṇe 'pi vācyam / sajjanamāhātmye khalajanakutsāyāmapyupaneyamiti /
body.translated_text: Thus, the suffering of others is the very suffering of the virtuous; for they cannot bear it — not even their own suffering. This should also be cited when praising compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). It should also be adduced when extolling the greatness of the virtuous and when condemning the wicked.

body.text: // iti rurujātakaṃ ṣaḍiṃvaśatitamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Ruru-jātaka</s>, the twenty-sixth story.

body.text: 27. Mahākapijātakam
body.translated_text: 27. <s>Mahākapi-jātaka</s> (The Story of the Great Monkey)

body.text: dviṣatāmapi mānasānyāvarjayanti sadvṛttānuvartinaḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Those who follow righteous conduct win over the minds even of enemies. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila śrīmati himavatkukṣau vividharasaviryavipākaguṇairbahubhiroṣadhiviśeṣaiḥ parigṛhītabhūmibhāge nāṇāvidhapuṣpaphalapallavapatraviṭaparaparacanairmahīruhaśatairākīrṇe sphaṭikadalāmalasalilaprasravaṇe vividhapakṣigaṇanādanādite vānarayūthādhipatirbabhūva / tadavasthamapi cainaṃ tyāgakāruṇyābhyāsātpratipakṣasevāvirodhitānīverṣyāmātsaryakrauryāṇi nopajagmuḥ / sa tatra mahāntaṃ nyagrodhapādapaṃ parvataśikharamiva vyomollikhantamadhipatimiva tasya vanasya meghasaṃghātamiva pratyandhakāraviṭapamākīrṇaparṇatayā tālaphalādhikatarapramāṇaiḥ paramasvādubhirmanojñavarṇagandhaiḥ phalaviśeṣairānamyamānaśākhaṃ niśritya vijahāra /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> (being of awakening) was, it is said, the leader of a troop of monkeys in a glorious region on the slopes of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), in a tract of land endowed with numerous exceptional herbs possessing manifold qualities of flavor, potency, and ripening, covered with hundreds of great trees adorned with various flowers, fruits, shoots, leaves, and spreading branches, with streams of water clear as crystal petals, resounding with the songs of diverse flocks of birds. Even in that state, the tendencies of jealousy, envy, and cruelty — which are opposed by the cultivation of their antidotes — did not arise in him, due to his habitual practice of generosity and compassion. There he dwelt at a great banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha</s>) that scratched the sky like a mountain peak, like the sovereign of that forest, with branches so thickly covered with leaves as to appear like a mass of dark clouds, its boughs bending under fruits of extraordinary sweetness and delightful color and fragrance, larger in size than ripe palmyra fruits.

children.text: tiryaggatānāmapi bhāgyaśeṣaṃ satāṃ bhavatyeva sukhāśrayāya /
children.translated_text: Even for those born in animal existence, the residue of their merit serves as a refuge of happiness,

children.text: kartavyasaṃbandhi suhṛjjanānāṃ videśagānāmiva vittaśeṣam // Jm_27.1 //
children.translated_text: like the remaining wealth of benefactors who have gone abroad, which is connected to their obligations. (27.1)

body.text: tasya tu vanaspaterekā śākhā tatsamīpagāṃ nimnagāmabhi praṇatābhavat / atha bodhisattvo dīrghadarśitvāttadvānarayūthaṃ samanuśaśāsa - asyāṃ nyogrodhaśākhāyāmaphalāyāmakṛtāyāṃ na vaḥ kena cidanyataḥ phalamupabhoktavyamiti /
body.translated_text: Now, one branch of that tree hung down toward a nearby river. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being far-sighted, instructed the monkey troop: 'On this branch of the banyan, even when it is fruitless and unattended, none of you should eat any fruit that falls from elsewhere.'

body.text: atha kadācittasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ pipīlikābhiḥ parṇapuṭāvacchāditaṃ taruṇatvānnātimahadekaṃ phalaṃ na te vānarā dadṛśuḥ / tatkrameṇābhivardhamānaṃ varṇagandharasamārdavopapannaṃ paripākavaśācchithilabandhanaṃ tasyāṃ nadyāṃ nipapāta / anupūrveṇa vāhyamāna nadīstrotasā 'nyatamasya rājñaḥ sāntaḥpurasya tasyāṃ nadyāṃ salilakrīḍāmanubhavato jālakaraṇḍakapārśve vyāsajyata /
body.translated_text: Now once, on that branch, there was a single fruit — small because it was still young, concealed within a fold of leaves by ants — which the monkeys did not notice. That fruit, gradually growing, acquiring color, fragrance, flavor, and tenderness, loosened from its stalk upon ripening, fell into that river. Carried along gradually by the river's current, it caught against the edge of a mesh basket near a certain king who, together with his inner circle, was enjoying water-sports in that river.

children.text: tatsnānamālyāsavavāsagandha saṃśleṣasaṃpiṇḍitamaṅganānām /
children.translated_text: Its fragrant excellence, mingling with the scents of the bath oils, garlands, wines, perfumes, and unguents

children.text: visarpiṇā svena tiraścakāra ghrāṇābhirāmeṇa guṇodayena // Jm_27.2 //
children.translated_text: of the women clustered together, overpowered all those with its spreading, nose-delighting quality. (27.2)

children.text: tadgandhamattāḥ kṣāṇamaṅganāstā dīrghīkṛtocchvāsavikuñcitākṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Intoxicated by that fragrance, those women for a moment, with prolonged inhalations and half-closed eyes,

children.text: bhutvātha kautūhalacañcalāni vicikṣipurdikṣu vilocanāni // Jm_27.3 //
children.translated_text: and then, their eyes restless with curiosity, cast their glances in every direction. (27.3)

body.text: kaūtuhalaprasṛtalolataranayanāstu tā yoṣitastannyagrodhaphalaṃ paripakvatālaphalādhikatarapramāṇaṃ jālakaraṇḍakapārśvato vilagnamavekṣya kimidamiti tadāvarjitanayanāḥ samapdyanta saha rājñā / atha sa rājā tatphalamānāyya prātyayikavaidyajanaparidṛṣṭaṃ svayamāsvādayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Those women, with their eager, darting, curious eyes, spotted that banyan fruit — larger in size than a ripe palmyra fruit — clinging to the side of the mesh basket, and with their gaze drawn to it, they turned toward it together with the king, wondering 'What is this?' Then that king had the fruit brought, had it examined by his trusted physicians, and tasted it himself.

children.text: adbhūtena rasenātha nṛpastasya visiṣmiye /
children.translated_text: The king was then astonished by the wondrous flavor of that fruit,

children.text: adbhūtena raseneva prayogaguṇahāriṇā // Jm_27.4 //
children.translated_text: by its wondrous taste, captivating in its effect and quality. (27.4)

children.text: apūrvavarṇagandhābhyāṃ tasyākalitavismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Amazed beyond measure by its unprecedented color and fragrance,

children.text: yayau tadrasasaṃrāgātparāṃ vismayavikriyām // Jm_27.5 //
children.translated_text: he was overcome by the most extreme wonderment due to his passion for its taste. (27.5)

body.text: atha tasya rājñaḥ svādurasabhojanasamucitasyāpi tadrasasaṃrāgavaśagasyaitada bhavat -
body.translated_text: Then that king, though accustomed to foods of delicious flavor, overpowered by his passion for that taste, thought thus:

children.text: yo nāma nāmūni phalāni bhuṅkte sa kāni rājyasya phalāni bhuṅkte /
children.translated_text: 'He who does not eat such fruits — what fruits of kingship does he truly enjoy?

children.text: yasyānnametattu ca eva rājā vinaiva rājatvapariśrameṇa // Jm_27.6 //
children.translated_text: But he whose food this is, he is the true king, even without the toil of ruling.' (27.6)

body.text: sa tatprabhavānveṣaṇakṛtamatiḥ svabuddhyā vimamarśavyaktamayaṃ taruvara ito nātidūre nadītīrasaṃniviṣṭaśca yasyedaṃ phalaṃ tathā hyanupahatavarṇagandharasamadīrghakālasalilasaṃparkādaparikṣatamajarjaraṃ ca yataḥ śakyamasya prabhavo 'dhigantumiti niścayamupetya tadrasatṛṣṇayā ākṛṣyamāṇo viramya jalakrīḍāyāḥ samyak puravare sve rakṣāvidhānaṃ saṃdiśya yātrāsajjena mahatā balakāyena parivṛtastāṃ nadīmanusasāra / krameṇa cotsādayan saśvāpadagaṇāni vanagahanāni samanubhavaṃ ścatrāṇi rasāntarāṇi paśyannakṛtrimaramaṇīyaśobhāni vanāntarāṇi saṃtrāsayan paṭaharasitairavanyagajamṛgān mānuṣajanadurgamaṃ tasya vanaspateḥ samīpamupajagāma /
body.translated_text: He, intent on discovering its origin, reasoned thus: 'Clearly, this must be an excellent tree situated not far from here on a riverbank, whose fruit this is; for its color, fragrance, and flavor are so unimpaired, and despite prolonged contact with water it is undamaged and intact — from this one can determine its source.' Having reached this conclusion, drawn by his craving for that taste, he ceased his water-sports and, having properly arranged the defense of his chief city, surrounded by a great force of troops equipped for a march, he followed the course of that river. And gradually, clearing away the dense forests along with their wild beasts, experiencing various other flavors along the way, beholding forest glades of artless and charming beauty, startling the wild elephants and deer of the forest with the rumble of his drums, he arrived near that lord of trees, in a place inaccessible to men.

children.text: taṃ meghavṛndamiva toyabharāvasannamāsannaśailamapi śailavadīkṣyamāṇam /
children.translated_text: That lord of trees, like a mass of clouds heavy with water, seeming like a mountain even when near a mountain,

children.text: dūrāddadarśa nṛpatiḥ sa vanaspatīndramullokyamānamadhirājamivānyavṛkṣaiḥ // Jm_27.7 //
children.translated_text: the king saw from afar — that sovereign among trees, looked up to by the other trees as though he were a supreme ruler. (27.7)

body.text: paripakvasahakāraphalasurabhitareṇa ca nirhāriṇā atimanojñena gandhena pratyudgata iva tasya pādapasya ayaṃ sa vanaspatiriti niścayamupajagāma / samupetya cainaṃ dadarśa tatphalopabhogavyāpṛtairanekavānaraśatairākīrṇaviṭapam /
body.translated_text: And greeted, as it were, by the irresistibly delightful fragrance issuing forth — more fragrant than ripe mango fruits — he arrived at the certainty: 'This is that lord of trees.' And approaching it, he beheld its branches teeming with many hundreds of monkeys busily enjoying its fruits.

body.text: atha sa rājā samabhilaṣitārthavipralopinastān vānarān pratyabhikruddhamatiḥ - hata hataitān / vidhvaṃsayata vināśayata sarvān vānarajālmāniti saparuṣākṣaraṃ svān puruṣānādideśa / atha te rājapuruṣāḥ sajyacāpabāṇavyagrakarāgrā vānarāvabhartsanamukharāḥ samudyataloṣṭadaṇḍaśastrāścāpare
body.translated_text: Then that king, his mind inflamed with anger against those monkeys who were plundering his coveted prize, commanded his men harshly: 'Kill them, kill them! Destroy them, annihilate all those wretched monkeys!' And his men, with hands grasping strung bows and arrows, loudly threatening the monkeys, and others raising stones, clubs, and weapons —

body.text: paradurgamivābhiroddhukāmāstaṃ vanaspatimabhisasruḥ / atha bodhisattvastumulaṃ tadrājabalamanilajavākalitamivārṇavajalamanibhṛtakalakalārāvamabhipatadālokyāśanivarṣeṇeva samantato vikīryamāṇaṃ taruvaraṃ śaraloṣṭadaṇḍaśastravarṣeṇa bhayavirasavirāvamātraparāyaṇaṃ ca vikṛtadīnamukhamunmukhaṃ vānaragaṇamavekṣya mahatyā karuṇayā samākramyamāṇacetāstyaktaviṣādadainyasaṃtrāsaḥ samāśvāsya tadvānarayūthaṃ tatparitrāṇavyavasitamatirabhiruhya tasya vanaspateḥ śikharaṃ tatsamāsannaṃ giritaṭaṃ laṅghayitumiyeṣa / athānekapraskandanakramaprāpyamapi taṃ giritaṭaṃ sa mahāsattvaḥ svavīryātiśayātkhaga ivādhiruroha /
body.translated_text: as if wishing to besiege an inaccessible fortress, they rushed toward that tree. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, beholding that tumultuous royal army—like ocean waters stirred by a swift wind, with a restless murmur of commotion—descending upon them, and seeing the noble tree being showered on all sides with a rain of arrows, stones, clubs, and weapons as if by a torrent of thunderbolts, and seeing too the monkey troop with faces distorted and pitiable, looking upward, their only recourse being cries of terror and distress, his heart overwhelmed by great compassion, casting aside dejection, despondency, and fear, he reassured that monkey troop; and with his mind resolved upon their rescue, he climbed to the summit of that tree and sought to leap across to the nearby mountain cliff. And that great being, though that cliff was reachable only through many successive leaps, through the supremacy of his own strength ascended it like a bird.

children.text: dvābhyāmapi laṅghanakramābhyāṃ gamyaṃ naiva tadanyavānarāṇām /
children.translated_text: That distance, traversable by two leaps combined, was utterly beyond the reach of other monkeys.

children.text: vegena yadantaraṃ tarasvī pratatārālpamivaikavikrameṇa // Jm_27.8 //
children.translated_text: The gap that the swift one crossed with speed, as though it were trifling, in a single bound— // Jm_27.8 //

children.text: kṛpayābhivivardhitaḥ sa tasya vyavasāyaḥ paṭutāṃ jagāma śauryāt /
children.translated_text: His resolve, augmented by compassion, attained keenness through valor;
