children.text: sa ca yatnaviśeṣamasya cakre manasaivātha jagāma yatnataikṣṇyāt // Jm_27.9 //
children.translated_text: And his effort reached a special intensity; then by the sharpness of that effort he accomplished it as if by mere thought alone. // Jm_27.9 //

body.text: adhiruhya ca gireruccataraṃ tātapradeśaṃ tadantarālādhikapramāṇayā mahatyā virūḍhayā 'śithilamūlayā dṛḍhayā vetralatayā gāḍhamābadhya caraṇau punastaṃ vanaspatiṃ pracaskandaḥ / viprakṛṣṭatvāttu tasyāntarālasya caraṇabandhanavyākulatvācca sa mahāsattvaḥ kathaṃcittasya vanaspateragraśākhāṃ karābhyāṃ samāsasāda /
body.translated_text: Having climbed to a higher ledge of the mountain, he firmly bound his feet with a great, well-rooted yet loosely hanging, strong cane creeper—one whose length exceeded the measure of that intervening gap—and leapt back toward that tree. But because of the great distance of that gap and the encumbrance of the binding upon his feet, that great being barely managed to grasp with his hands the topmost branch of that tree.

children.text: tataḥ samālambya dṛḍhaṃ sa śākhāmātatya tāṃ vetralatāṃ ca yatnāt /
children.translated_text: Then, holding fast to that branch and stretching that cane creeper taut with effort,

children.text: svasaṃjñayā yūthamathādideśa drumādataḥ śighramabhirpayāyāt // Jm_27.10 //
children.translated_text: He commanded his troop by his own signal: 'Cross swiftly from this tree to the mountain!' // Jm_27.10 //

body.text: atha te vānarā bhayāturatvādapayānamārgamāsādya capalataragatayastadākramaṇanirviśaṅkāstayā svastyapacakramuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those monkeys, being stricken with fear, having found a path of escape, with ever more nimble movement, without hesitation treading upon that crossing, departed safely.

children.text: bhayāturaistasya tu vānaraistairākramyamāṇaṃ caraṇaiḥ prasaktam /
children.translated_text: But as those fear-stricken monkeys trod ceaselessly upon his body with their feet,

children.text: gātraṃ yayau svaiḥ piśitairviyogaṃ na tveva dhairyātiśayena cetaḥ // Jm_27.11 //
children.translated_text: His limbs were stripped of their own flesh, yet his spirit was not stripped of its supreme fortitude. // Jm_27.11 //

body.text: taddṛṣṭvā sa rājā te ca rājapuruṣāḥ parāṃ vismayavaktavyatāmupajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Witnessing this, that king and those royal attendants were overcome with the utmost astonishment and speechlessness.

children.text: evaṃvidhā vikramabuddhisampadātmānapekṣā ca dayā pareṣu /
children.translated_text: Such a wealth of valor and wisdom, such disregard for oneself, and such compassion for others—

children.text: āścaryabuddhiṃ janayecchrutāpi pratyakṣataḥ kiṃ punarīkṣyamāṇā // Jm_27.12 //
children.translated_text: Even heard of, it would engender wonder; how much more so when witnessed with one's own eyes! // Jm_27.12 //

body.text: atha sa rājā tān puruṣān samādideśabhayodbhrāntavānaragaṇacaraṇakṣobhitakṣataśarīraściramekakramāvasthānācca dṛḍhaṃ pariśrānto vyaktamayaṃ vānarādhipatiḥ na cāya mataḥ śakṣyati svayamātmānaṃ saṃhartum, tacchrīghramasyādhaḥ paṭavitānaṃ vitatya vitralateyaṃ ca nyagrodhaśākhā śārābhyāṃ yugapatpracchidyetāmiti / te tathā cakruḥ / athainaṃ sa rājā śanakairvitānādavatārya murchayā vraṇavedanāklamopajātayā samākramyamāṇacetasaṃ mṛduni śayanīye saṃveśayāmāsa / sadyaḥkṣatapraśamanayogyaiśca sarpirādibhirasya vraṇānyabhyajya mandībhūtapariśramaṃ samāśvastamenamabhyupagamya sa rājā sakautūhalavismayabahumānaḥ kuśalaparipraśnapūrvakamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king gave orders to those men: 'His body is battered and wounded by the trampling feet of the panic-stricken monkey troop, and he is utterly exhausted from standing so long in that single posture. Clearly this is the chief of the monkeys, and he is no longer able to withdraw himself on his own. Therefore, quickly spread a cloth canopy beneath him, and let this creeper and the banyan branch be cut simultaneously with saws.' They did so. Then the king, gently lowering him from the canopy, his mind being overcome by a swoon born of wound-pain and fatigue, laid him upon a soft bed. And having anointed his wounds with ghee and other remedies suited to the immediate soothing of fresh injuries, when his exhaustion had subsided and he had regained composure, the king approached him with curiosity, astonishment, and deep respect, and after first inquiring about his welfare, spoke:

children.text: gatvā svayaṃ saṃkramatāmamīṣāṃ svajīvite tyaktadayena bhutvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself become a bridge for these to cross, with no mercy spared for your own life,

children.text: samuddhṛtā ye kapayastvayeme ko nu tvameṣāṃ tava vā ka ete // Jm_27.13 //
children.translated_text: These monkeys have been rescued by you—who then are you to them, or who are they to you? // Jm_27.13 //

children.text: śrotuṃ vayaṃ cedidamarharūpāstattāvadācakṣva kapipradhāna /
children.translated_text: If we are worthy to hear this, then pray tell us, O chief of monkeys!

children.text: na hyalpasauhārdanibandhanānāmevaṃ manāṃsi prataranti kartum // Jm_27.14 //
children.translated_text: For the hearts of those whose bonds of affection are slight do not venture forth to act in such a manner.' // Jm_27.14 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastasya rājñastadabhyupapattisaumukhyaṃ pratipūjayannātmanivedanamanuguṇena krameṇa cakāra -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, honoring that king's readiness to receive his account, made a self-disclosure in fitting order:

children.text: ebhirmadājñāpratipattidakṣairāropito mayyadhipatvabhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By these, who are skilled in carrying out my commands, the burden of sovereignty was placed upon me;

children.text: putreṣvivaitesṣvavabaddhahārdastaṃ voḍhumevāhamabhiprapannaḥ // Jm_27.15 //
children.translated_text: With my heart bound to them as to my own children, I undertook to bear that very burden. // Jm_27.15 //

children.text: iyaṃ mahārāja samaṃ mamaibhiḥ saṃbandhajātiścirakālarūḍhā /
children.translated_text: This bond between myself and them, O great king, is a friendship born of kinship, long nurtured over time,

children.text: samānajātitvamayī ca maitrī jñāteyajātā sahavāsayogāt // Jm_27.16 //
children.translated_text: A friendship rooted in our being of the same birth, and born among kin through the bond of living together. // Jm_27.16 //

body.text: tacchrutvā sa rājā paraṃ vismayamupetya punarenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Hearing this, that king, having arrived at the utmost astonishment, spoke to him again:

children.text: adhipārthamamātyādi na tadarthaṃ mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sovereign exists for the sake of the subjects, not the subjects for the sake of the sovereign—

children.text: iti kasmātsvabhṛtyārthamātmānaṃ tyaktavān bhavān // Jm_27.17 //
children.translated_text: Why then have you, for the sake of your own dependents, sacrificed yourself?' // Jm_27.17 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - kāmamevaṃ pravṛttā, mahārāja, rājanītiḥ / duranuvartyā tu māṃ pratibhāti /

children.text: asaṃstutasyāpyaviṣahyatīvramupekṣituṃ duḥkhamatīva duḥkham /
children.translated_text: Even for a stranger, to disregard suffering that is exceedingly acute is itself exceedingly painful;

children.text: prāgeva bhaktyunmukhamānasamya gatasya bandhupriyatāṃ janasya // Jm_27.18 //
children.translated_text: How much more so when one faces people who are devoted, who have attained the status of kinsmen and dear ones! // Jm_27.18 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Indeed, O great king, the science of statecraft (<s>rājanīti</s>) prescribes thus. Yet it seems to me difficult to follow.

children.text: idaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vyasanārtidainyaṃ śākhāmṛgān pratyabhivardhamānam /
children.translated_text: And seeing this wretchedness of calamity and anguish among the tree-dwelling monkeys (<s>śākhāmṛga</s>), ever increasing,

children.text: svakāryacintāvasaroparodhi prādudruvanmāṃ sahasaiva duḥkham // Jm_27.19 //
children.translated_text: A grief that overwhelmed any occasion for thinking of my own welfare burst upon me all at once. // Jm_27.19 //

children.text: ānamyamānāni dhanūṃsi dṛṣṭvā viniṣpataddīptaśilīmukhāni /
children.translated_text: Seeing the bows being drawn, the blazing arrows flying forth,

children.text: bhīmasvanajyānyavicintya vegādasmāttaroḥ śailamimaṃ gato 'smi // Jm_27.20 //
children.translated_text: Their bowstrings sounding terribly—without deliberation on the swiftness, I went from this tree to this mountain. // Jm_27.20 //

children.text: vaiśeṣikatrāsaparītacittairākṛṣyamāṇo 'hamatha svayūthyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Drawn by my own troop-fellows, whose hearts were gripped by an extraordinary terror,

children.text: ālakṣitāyāmaguṇāṃ sumūlāṃ svapādayorvetralatāṃ nibadhya // Jm_27.21 //
children.translated_text: Having spotted a firm, well-rooted cane creeper, I bound it to my feet. // Jm_27.21 //

children.text: prāskandamasmātpunareva śailādimaṃ drumaṃ tārayituṃ svayūthyān /
children.translated_text: I leapt again from this mountain back to this tree, in order to ferry my troop-fellows across;

children.text: tataḥ karābhyāṃ samavāpamasya prasāritaṃ prasāritaṃ pāṇimivāgraśākhām // Jm_27.22 //
children.translated_text: Then with my hands I grasped the outstretched topmost branch, like an extended hand. // Jm_27.22 //

children.text: samātatāṅgaṃ latayā tayā ca śākṣāgrahastena ca pādapasya /
children.translated_text: With my body stretched out along that creeper and holding the treetop in my grasp,

children.text: amī madadhyākramaṇe viśaṅkā niśritya māṃ svasti gatāḥ svayūthyāḥ // Jm_27.23 //
children.translated_text: These troop-fellows of mine, without fear of treading upon me, crossed over safely by relying on me. // Jm_27.23 //

body.text: atha sa rājā pramodyajātaṃ tasyāmapyavasthāyāṃ taṃ mahāsattvamavekṣya paraṃ vismayamudvahan punarenamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that king, beholding the great being filled with joy even in that condition, bearing the utmost astonishment, spoke to him again:

children.text: paribhūyātmanaḥ saukhyaṃ paravyasanamāpatat /
children.translated_text: 'Scorning your own comfort, you rushed toward the calamity of others—

children.text: ityātmani samāropya prāptaḥ ko bhavatā guṇaḥ // Jm_27.24 //
children.translated_text: What merit have you gained by thus taking it upon yourself?' // Jm_27.24 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kāmaṃ śarīraṃ kṣitipa kṣataṃ me manaḥ parasvāsthyamupāgataṃ tu /
children.translated_text: 'Granted, O lord of the earth, my body is wounded; yet my mind has attained tranquility through the well-being of others.

children.text: akāri yeṣāṃ ciramādhipatyaṃ teṣāṃ mayārtirvinivartiteti // Jm_27.25 //
children.translated_text: That the affliction of those over whom I long held sovereignty has been turned away by me— // Jm_27.25 //

children.text: jitvāhave vidviṣataḥ sadarpān gātreṣvalaṃkāravadudvahanti /
children.translated_text: Just as warriors, having conquered their proud enemies in battle, bear upon their limbs the splendor of valor's scars as if they were ornaments,

children.text: vīrā yathā vikramacihnaśobhāṃ prītyā tathemāṃ rujamudvahāmi // Jm_27.26 //
children.translated_text: So do I bear this pain with joy. // Jm_27.26 //

children.text: praṇāmasatkārapuraḥsarasya bhaktiprayuktasya samānajātyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the sovereignty obtained through the homage and respect offered by those of the same birth, united through devotion,

children.text: eśvaryalabdhasya sukhakramasya saṃprāptāmānṛṇyamidaṃ mayādya // Jm_27.27 //
children.translated_text: And the felicity that came with it—today I have attained full repayment of that debt. // Jm_27.27 //

children.text: tanmāṃ tapatyeṣa na duḥkhayogaḥ suhṛdviyogaḥ sukhaviplavo vā /
children.translated_text: Therefore this union with suffering does not torment me, nor separation from dear ones, nor the loss of comfort;

children.text: krameṇa cānena amabhyupeto mahotsavābhyāgama eṣa mṛtyuḥ // Jm_27.28 //
children.translated_text: And by this very course, death approaches me as the arrival of a great festival. // Jm_27.28 //

children.text: pūrvopakārānṛṇatātmatuṣṭiḥ saṃtāpaśāntirvimalaṃ yaśaśca /
children.translated_text: The repayment of past debts of kindness, self-satisfaction, the calming of remorse, unstained fame,

children.text: pūjā nṛpānnirbhayatā ca mṛtyoḥ kṛtajñabhāvād grahaṇaṃ ca satsu // Jm_27.29 //
children.translated_text: Honor from the king, fearlessness before death, and recognition among the virtuous through gratitude— // Jm_27.29 //

children.text: ete guṇāḥ sadguṇavāsavṛkṣa prāptā mayaitad vyasanaṃ prapadya /
children.translated_text: These merits, O tree of excellent virtues, have been gained by me through entering into this calamity;

children.text: eṣāṃ vipakṣāṃstu samabhyupaiti dayāvihīno nṛpatiḥ śriteṣu // Jm_27.30 //
children.translated_text: But their opposites befall a king devoid of compassion toward those who depend upon him. // Jm_27.30 //

children.text: guṇairvihīnasya vipannakīrterdoṣodayairāvasathīkṛtasya /
children.translated_text: For one bereft of virtues, whose fame is ruined, who has become a dwelling-place of faults arising from vice—

children.text: gatirbhavettasya ca nama kānyā jvālākulebhyo narakānalebhyaḥ // Jm_27.31 //
children.translated_text: What other destiny can there be for him than the blazing fires of hell? // Jm_27.31 //

children.text: taddarśito 'yaṃ guṇadoṣayoste mayā prabhāvaḥ prathitaprabhāva /
children.translated_text: Thus I have shown you, O one of renowned might, the power of virtue and vice;

children.text: dharmeṇa tasmādanuśādhi rājyaṃ strīcañcalapremaguṇā hi lakṣmīḥ // Jm_27.32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore govern your kingdom by <s>dharma</s>, for royal fortune (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) has the fickle quality of a woman's love.' // Jm_27.32 //

children.text: yugyaṃ balaṃ jānapadānamātyān paurānanāthāñchramaṇān dvijātīn /
children.translated_text: 'The army, the countryfolk, the ministers, the citizens, the helpless, the ascetics, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—

children.text: sarvān sukhena prayateta yoktuṃ hitānukūlena piteva rājā // Jm_27.33 //
children.translated_text: A king should strive to yoke them all to happiness, through what is beneficial and agreeable, like a father.' // Jm_27.33 //

children.text: evaṃ hi dharmārthayaśaḥsamṛddhiḥ syātte sukhāyeha paratra caiva /
children.translated_text: 'For thus shall the prosperity of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and fame be yours, for happiness both here and hereafter;

children.text: prajānukampārjitayā tvamasmādrājarṣilakṣmyā nararāja rāja // Jm_27.34 //
children.translated_text: Through the royal sage's majesty (<s>rājarṣilakṣmī</s>) earned by compassion for your subjects, O lord of men, you shall be truly a king.' // Jm_27.34 //

children.text: iti nṛpamanuśiṣya śisyavad bahumatavākprayatena tena saḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus having instructed the king, who, like a disciple, attended with reverent and respectful speech,

children.text: rugabhibhavanasaṃhṛtakriyāṃ tanumapahāya yayau triviṣṭapam // Jm_27.35 //
children.translated_text: He relinquished his body, its functions stilled by the overpowering of his wounds, and departed to <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven). // Jm_27.35 //

body.text: tedevaṃ dviṣatāmapi manāṃsyāvarjayanti sadvṛttānuvartinaḥ, iti lokaṃ samāvarjayitukāmena sadvṛttānuvartinā bhavitavyam / na samarthāstathā svārthamapi pratipattuṃ sattvā yathā parārthaṃ pratipannavān sa bhagavāniti tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyam / satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe karuṇāvarṇe rājāvavāde ca / evaṃ rājñā prajāsu dayāpannena bhavitavyam / kṛtajñakathāyāmapyupaneyam / evaṃ kṛtajñāḥ santo bhavantīti /
body.translated_text: Thus do those who follow righteous conduct win over the hearts even of their enemies. Therefore, one who wishes to win over the world should follow righteous conduct. This should also be told in praise of the <s>Tathāgata</s>: that beings are not able to pursue even their own welfare as effectively as that Blessed One pursued the welfare of others. It is also to be cited in connection with respectful listening to the <s>Dharma</s>, in praise of compassion, and in the admonition of kings. Thus should a king be compassionate toward his subjects. It may also be adduced in a narrative about gratitude: 'Thus are the virtuous grateful.'

body.text: // iti mahākapijātakaṃ saptaviṃśatitamam //
body.translated_text: // Thus ends the <s>Mahākapi-jātaka</s>, the twenty-seventh. //

body.text: 28. Kṣāntijātakam
body.translated_text: 28. <s>Kṣānti-jātaka</s> (The Story of Patience)

body.text: sātmībhūtakṣamāṇāṃ pratisaṃkhyānamahatāṃ nāviṣahyaṃ nāma kiṃcidasti / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: For those great ones in whom forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>) has become second nature, through their practice of analytical meditation (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>), there is truly nothing that is unendurable. As it is heard in tradition:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānekadoṣavyasanopasṛṣṭamarthakāmapradhānatvādanaupaśamikaṃ rāgadveṣamohāmarṣasaṃrambhamadamānamātsaryādidoṣarajasāmāpātaṃ pātanaṃ hrīdharmaparigrahasyāyatana lobhāsadgrāhasya kukāryasaṃbādhatvātkṛśavakāśaṃ dharmasyāvetya gṛhavāsaṃ parigrahaviṣayaparivarjanācca taddoṣavivekasukhāṃ pravrajyāmanupaśyan śīlaśrutapraśamavinayaniyamānasastāpaso babhūva / tamaskhalitasamādānaṃ kṣāntivarṇavādinaṃ tadanurūpadharmākhyānakramaṃ vyatītya sve nāmagotre kṣāntivādinamityeva lokaḥ svabuddhipūrvakaṃ saṃjajñe /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that household life is beset with many faults and afflictions—that it is unpeaceful on account of its predominant pursuit of wealth and pleasure, that it is the haunt where the dust of such vices as passion, hatred, delusion, impatience, agitation, pride, conceit, and jealousy descends, that it causes the loss of the virtue of modesty, that it is the ground of greed and false attachment, and that <s>dharma</s> has scant room in it on account of its congestion with wicked deeds—and perceiving also that renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>), through the relinquishment of possessions and the domain of sensory objects, brings the bliss of freedom from those very faults, became an ascetic (<s>tāpasa</s>), his mind devoted to moral conduct, learning, tranquility, humility, and restraint. Because his observances were faultless and because he was an advocate of the virtue of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), with his discourses on <s>dharma</s> conforming to that very ideal, the world, of its own understanding, passing over his proper name and lineage, came to know him simply as <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> ('Advocate of Patience').

children.text: eśvaryavidyātapasāṃ samṛddhirlabdhaprayāmaśca kalāsu saṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: The attainment of sovereignty, learning, and austerity, and the devoted pursuit of the arts once mastered,

children.text: śarīravākceṣṭitavikriyāśca nāmāparaṃ saṃjanayanti puṃsām // Jm_28.1 //
children.translated_text: And the distinctive conduct of one's body, speech, and behavior—these generate for a person a new name. // Jm_28.1 //

children.text: jānan sa tu kṣāntiguṇaprabhāvaṃ tenātmavallokamalaṃkariṣyan /
children.translated_text: But he, knowing the power of the virtue of patience, and wishing to adorn the world with it as he had adorned himself,

children.text: cakāra yatkṣāntikathāḥ prasaktaṃ tatkṣāntivādīti tato vijajñe // Jm_28.2 //
children.translated_text: Because he constantly delivered discourses on patience, he became known as <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>. // Jm_28.2 //

children.text: svabhāvabhūtā mahatī kṣamā ca parāpakāreṣvavikāradhīrā /
children.translated_text: His great forbearance, innate in nature, steadfast and unperturbed in the face of injuries by others,

children.text: tadarthayuktāśca kathāviśeṣāḥ kīrtyā muniṃ taṃ prathayāṃbabhūvuḥ // Jm_28.3 //
children.translated_text: And his distinctive discourses suited to that theme—these spread the fame of that sage far and wide. // Jm_28.3 //

body.text: atha sa mahātmā praviviktaramaṇīyaṃ samartusulabhapuṣpaphalaṃ padmotpalālaṃkṛtavimalasalilāśayamudyānaramyaśobhaṃ vanapradeśamadhyāsanāttapovanamaṅgalyatāmānināya /
body.translated_text: Then that great-souled one, by dwelling in a secluded and beautiful forest tract—rich with flowers and fruits according to the seasons, its pure waters adorned with lotuses and water-lilies, possessed of the lovely charm of a garden—elevated it to the sanctity of an ascetic grove (<s>tapovana</s>).

children.text: nivasanti hi yatraiva santaḥ sadguṇabhūṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Wherever the virtuous dwell, adorned with good qualities,

children.text: tanmaṅgalyaṃ manojñaṃ ca tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam // Jm_28.4 //
children.translated_text: That place is auspicious, that place is delightful, that is a holy site, that is an ascetic grove. // Jm_28.4 //

body.text: sa tatra bahumanyamānastadadhyuṣitairdevatāviśeṣairabhigamyamānaśca śreyobhilāṣiṇāguṇavatsalena janena kṣāntipratisaṃyuktābhiḥ śrutihṛdayalhādinībhirdharmyābhiḥ kathābhisatasya janakāyasya paramanugrahaṃ cakāra / atha kadācittatastyo rājā grīṣmakālaprabhāvādabhilaṣaṇīyatarāṃ salilakrīḍāṃ prati samutsukamatirudyānaguṇātiśayaniketabhūtaṃ taṃ vanapradeśaṃ sāntaḥpuraḥ samabhijagāma /
body.translated_text: There, held in high esteem by the divine beings who inhabited that place, and approached by people who yearned for spiritual welfare and were devoted to virtuous qualities, he bestowed the highest grace upon that assembly of people through his discourses on <s>dharma</s>—discourses connected with patience, gladdening to the ear and the heart. Now once, a certain king, his mind eager for water-sports made all the more desirable by the power of the summer season, came with his harem to that forest tract, which was the very abode of the garden's surpassing excellence.

body.text: sa tadvanaṃ nandanaramyaśobhamākīrṇamantaḥpurasundarībhiḥ /
body.translated_text: He, the playful one, wandering about with his lordly grace, as it were adorned

body.text: alaṃcakāreva caran vilāsī vibhūtimatyā lalitānuvṛttyā // Jm_28.5 //
body.translated_text: that forest, beautiful as <s>Nandana</s> (Indra's garden), filled with the beauties of the inner palace. || Jm 28.5 ||

children.text: vimānadeśeṣu latāgṛheṣu latāgṛheṣu puṣpaprahāseṣu mahīruheṣu /
children.translated_text: In the pavilion-terraces and in the bower-houses, in the trees abloom with flowers,

children.text: toyeṣu conmīlitapaṅkajeṣu reme svabhāvātiśayairvadhūnām // Jm_28.6 //
children.translated_text: and in the waters where lotuses had opened, he delighted in the surpassing natural charms of the women. || Jm 28.6 ||

children.text: mālyāsavasnānavilepanānāṃ saṃmodagandhākulitairdvirephaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By bees intoxicated with the scents of garlands, wine, bath-unguents, and perfumes swarming about [them],

children.text: dadarśa kāsāṃcidupohyamānā jātasmitastrāsavilāsaśobhāḥ // Jm_28.7 //
children.translated_text: he saw some of the women being assailed — their beauty [enhanced] by smiles of playful alarm. || Jm 28.7 ||

children.text: pratyagraśobhairapi karṇapūraiḥ paryāptamālyairapi mūrdhajaiśca /
children.translated_text: Even with fresh and beautiful ear-ornaments and with hair fully adorned with garlands,

children.text: tṛptiryathāsītkusumairna tāsāṃ tathaiva nāsāṃ lalitairnṛpasya // Jm_28.8 //
children.translated_text: those women were not satiated with flowers — and neither was the king satiated with their graceful movements. || Jm 28.8 ||

children.text: vimānadeśeṣu viṣajyamānā vilambamānāḥ kamalākareṣu /
children.translated_text: Lingering at the pavilion-terraces, tarrying at the lotus-ponds,

children.text: dadarśa rājā bhramarāyamāṇāḥ puṣpadrumeṣu pramadākṣimālāḥ // Jm_28.9 //
children.translated_text: the king beheld the garlands of the women's glances hovering bee-like about the flowering trees. || Jm 28.9 ||

children.text: madapragalbhānyapi kokilānāṃ rutāni nṛtyāni ca barhiṇānām /
children.translated_text: Even the bold cooing of the cuckoos, the dances of the peacocks,

children.text: dvirephagītāni ca nābhirejustatrāṅganājalpitanṛttagītaiḥ // Jm_28.10 //
children.translated_text: and the songs of the bees could not compete with the chattering, dancing, and singing of those women. || Jm 28.10 ||

children.text: payodadhīrastanitairmṛdaṅgairudīrṇakekāstatabarhacakrāḥ /
children.translated_text: With drums [sounding] like the deep thunder of rain-clouds, with their fully-spread tail-fans raised in display,

children.text: natā iva svena kalaguṇena cakrurmayūrāḥ kṣitipasya sevām // Jm_28.11 //
children.translated_text: the peacocks, as if bowing with their own melodious calls, performed service to the king. || Jm 28.11 ||

body.text: sa tatra sāntaḥpura udyānavanavihārasukhaṃ prakāmamanubhūya krīḍāprasaṅgaparikhedānmadapariṣvaṅgācca śrīmati vimānapradeśe mahārhaśayanīyavaragato nidrāvaśamupajagāma / atha tā yoṣitaḥ prastāvāntaragatamavetya rājānaṃ vanaśobhābhirākṣipyamāṇahṛdayāstaddarśanāvitṛptā yathāprītikṛtasamavāyāḥ samākulabhūṣaṇatinādasaṃmiśrakalapralāpāḥ samantataḥ prasasruḥ /
body.translated_text: He, together with the inner palace [women], having enjoyed to his heart's content the pleasures of strolling in the garden-grove, wearied by the exertions of play and dizzy from the embrace of intoxication, went to a beautiful pavilion-terrace and, reclining upon a supremely precious couch, fell under the sway of sleep. Then those women, perceiving that the king had passed into an interval of repose, their hearts captivated by the beauties of the forest, unsatiated with gazing at them, assembling in groups according to their preference, with their ornamental tinkling mingled with soft babble, streamed out in all directions.

children.text: tāścchatravālavyajanāsanādyaiḥ preṣyādhṛtaiḥ kāñcanabhakticitraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those women, attended by the insignia of sovereignty — parasols, fans, seats, and the like —

children.text: eśvaryacihnairanugamyamānāḥ striyaḥ svabhāvānibhṛtaṃ viceruḥ // Jm_28.12 //
children.translated_text: held by maidservants and adorned with designs of gold, wandered about with natural modesty. || Jm 28.12 ||

children.text: tāḥ prāpya rūpāṇi mahīruhāṇāṃ puṣpāṇi cārūṇi ca pallavāni /
children.translated_text: Reaching the beautiful forms of the trees and their fair blossoms and shoots,

children.text: preṣyāprayatnānatipatya lobhādālebhire svena parākrameṇa // Jm_28.13 //
children.translated_text: surpassing the efforts of their maidservants, they plucked them by their own daring out of eagerness. || Jm 28.13 ||

children.text: mārgopalabdhān kusumābhirāmān gulmāṃścalatpallavinaśca vṛkṣān /
children.translated_text: Charming flowering shrubs found along the paths, and trees with trembling foliage —

children.text: paryāptapuṣpābharaṇasrajo 'pi lobhādanālupya na tā vyatīyuḥ // Jm_28.14 //
children.translated_text: even with garlands and ornaments of flowers already sufficient, they did not pass by without plucking more, out of greed. || Jm 28.14 ||

body.text: atha tā vanaramaṇīyatayākṣipyamāṇahṛdayā rājayoṣitastadvanamanuvicarantyaḥ kṣāntivādina āśramapadamupajagmuḥ / viditatapaḥprabhāvamāhātmyāstu tasya muneḥ strījanādhikṛtā rājño vāllabhyād durāsadatvācca tāsāṃ naināstato vārayituṃ prasehire / abhisaṃskāraramaṇīyatarayā cāśramapadaśriyā samākṛṣyamāṇā iva tā yoṣitaḥ praviśyāśramapadaṃ dadṛśustatra taṃ munivaraṃ praśamasaumyadarśanamatigāmbhīryātiśayād durāsadamabhijvalantamiva tapaḥśriyā dhyānābhiyogādudāraviṣayasaṃnikarṣe 'pyakṣubhitendriyanaibhṛtyaśobhaṃ sākṣāddharmamiva maṅgalyaṃ puṇyadarśanaṃ vṛkṣamūle baddhāsanamāsīnam / atha tā rājastriyastasya tapastejasākrāntasattvāḥ saṃdarśanādeva tyaktavibhramavilāsauddhatyā vinayanibhṛtamabhigamyainaṃ paryupāsāṃcakrire / sa tāsāṃ svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsaramatithijanamanoharamupacāravidhiṃ pravartya tatparipraśnopapāditaprastāvābhiḥ strījanasukhagrahaṇārthābhirdṛṣṭāntavatībhiḥ kathābhirdharmātithyamāsāṃ cakāra /
body.translated_text: Then those royal women, their hearts captivated by the loveliness of the forest, while wandering through it, came to the hermitage of <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (the Preacher of Patience). But the attendants in charge of the women's quarters, knowing the greatness of that sage's ascetic power, yet unable to prevent them because of the king's affection for them and their unapproachability, did not dare to bar them. And those women, as if drawn by the beauty of the hermitage, made even more delightful by its refinement, entered the hermitage and there beheld that best of sages — serene and gentle in appearance, unapproachable because of his extraordinary depth, as if blazing with the splendor of austerity, his senses unperturbed despite proximity to sublime objects of sense through his absorption in meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), bearing the beauty of composure, like <s>Dharma</s> itself made visible — auspicious, a blessed sight — seated in cross-legged posture at the foot of a tree. Then those royal women, their courage subdued by the radiance of his austerity, at the very sight [of him] abandoning the boldness of flirtatious play, approached him with disciplined modesty and waited upon him. He, having offered them the hospitable treatment befitting guests, beginning with words of welcome and other endearments — captivating to the minds of guests — and through discourses illustrated with examples, prompted by their questions, intended for the easy comprehension of women, offered them the hospitality of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: agarhitāṃ jātimavāpya mānūṣīmanūnabhāvaṃ paṭubhistathendriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the blameless human birth, with faculties undiminished and sharp,

children.text: avaśyamṛtyurna karoti yaḥ śubhaṃ pramādabhākpratyahameṣa vañcyate // Jm_28.15 //
children.translated_text: one who, though subject to inevitable death, does not do good — such a one, partaking of heedlessness, is deceived each day. || Jm 28.15 ||

children.text: kulena rūpeṇa vayoguṇena vā balaprakarṣeṇa dhanodayena vā /
children.translated_text: By lineage, beauty, youth, virtue, eminence of strength, or rise of wealth —

children.text: paratra nāpnoti sukhāni kaścana pradānaśīlādiguṇairasaṃskṛtaḥ // Jm_28.16 //
children.translated_text: no one attains happiness in the next world who is not cultivated in the virtues of generosity and the like. || Jm 28.16 ||

children.text: kulādihīno 'pi hi pāpaniḥspṛhaḥ pradānaśīlādiguṇābhipattimān /
children.translated_text: Even one lacking lineage and the rest, if free from craving for evil, and endowed with the virtues of generosity and the like,

children.text: paratra saukhyairabhisāryate dhruvaṃ ghanāgame sindhujalairivārṇavaḥ // Jm_28.17 //
children.translated_text: is surely borne toward the pleasures of the next world — like the ocean by river-waters at the coming of the rains. || Jm 28.17 ||

children.text: kulasya rūpasya vayoguṇasya vā balaprakarṣasya dhanocchrayasya vā /
children.translated_text: Of lineage, beauty, youth, virtue, eminence of strength, and height of wealth,

children.text: ihāpyalaṃkāravidhirguṇādaraḥ samṛddhisūcaiva tu hemamālikā // Jm_28.18 //
children.translated_text: even in this world the ornament and adornment is respect for virtues — while a golden necklace merely announces prosperity. || Jm 28.18 ||

children.text: alaṃkriyante kusumairmahīruhāstaḍidguṇaistoyavilambino ghanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Trees are adorned by flowers, rain-bearing clouds by streaks of lightning,

children.text: sarāṃsi mattabhramaraiḥ saroruhairguṇairviśeṣādhigataistu dehinaḥ // Jm_28.19 //
children.translated_text: lakes by lotuses and intoxicated bees — but embodied beings by specially acquired virtues. || Jm 28.19 ||

children.text: arogatāyurdhanarūpajātibhirnikṛṣṭamadhyottamabhedacitratā /
children.translated_text: The variegated diversity — inferior, middling, and superior — in people's health, longevity, wealth, beauty, and birth

children.text: janasya ceyaṃ na khalu svabhāvataḥ parāśrayādvā trividhā tu karmaṇaḥ // Jm_28.20 //
children.translated_text: is certainly not by nature, nor from dependence on another, but is threefold from [one's own] <s>karma</s>. || Jm 28.20 ||

children.text: avetya caivaṃ niyatāṃ jagatsthitiṃ calaṃ vināśapravaṇaṃ ca jīvitam /
children.translated_text: And having understood this fixed order of the world, and that life is fleeting and prone to destruction,

children.text: jahīta pāpāni śubhakramāśayādayaṃ hi panthā yaśase sukhāya ca // Jm_28.21 //
children.translated_text: one should abandon sins, with a disposition inclined to the course of virtue — for this is the path to fame and happiness. || Jm 28.21 ||

children.text: manaḥpradoṣastu parātmanorhitaṃ vinirdahannagniriva pravartate /
children.translated_text: But the corruption of the mind proceeds like fire, burning the welfare of both others and oneself;

children.text: ataḥ prayatnena sa pāpabhīruṇā janena varjyaḥ pratipakṣaśaṃśrayāt // Jm_28.22 //
children.translated_text: therefore it should be zealously avoided by one who fears sin, through resort to its antidote. || Jm 28.22 ||

children.text: yathā sametya jvalito 'pi pāvakastaṭāntasaṃsaktajalāṃ mahānadīm /
children.translated_text: Just as even a blazing fire, upon reaching a great river whose banks are lapped by water,

children.text: praśāntimāyātimanojvalastathā śritasya lokadvitayakṣamāṃ kṣamām // Jm_28.23 //
children.translated_text: goes to extinction — so too the [fire of the] mind, for one who has resorted to patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), which is capable of [securing] both worlds. || Jm 28.23 ||

body.text:
iti kṣāntyā pāpaṃ pariharati taddhetvabhibhavād
ataścāyaṃ vairaṃ na janayati maitryāśrayabalāt /
body.translated_text: Thus through patience one avoids sin by overcoming its cause,

body.text: priyaḥ pūjyaścāsmādbhavati sukhabhāgeva ca tataḥ
body.translated_text: and thereby does not generate enmity, through the strength of resorting to loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>);

body.text: prayātyante ca dyāṃ svagṛhamiva puṇyāśrayaguṇāt // Jm_28.24 //
body.translated_text: and from this one becomes dear and honored, and thereby a partaker of happiness, and at the end goes to heaven as if to one's own home, through the merit of resorting to virtue. || Jm 28.24 ||

body.text: api ca bhavatyaḥ kṣāntirnāmaiṣā -
body.translated_text: Furthermore, dear ladies, this patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is:

children.text: śubhasvabhāvātiśayaḥ prasiddhaḥ puṇyena kīrtyā ca parā vivṛddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: A well-known superabundance of auspicious nature, supreme growth through merit and fame,

children.text: atoyasaṃparkakṛtā viśuddhistaistairguṇaughaiśca parā samṛddhiḥ // Jm_28.25 //
children.translated_text: a purity accomplished without the contact of water, and supreme prosperity through manifold floods of virtues. || Jm 28.25 ||

children.text: paroparodheṣu sadānabhijñā vyavasthitiḥ sattvavatāṃ manojñā /
children.translated_text: The steadfast comportment of the strong-willed, always unmindful of offenses by others, delightful,

children.text: guṇābhinirvārtitacārusaṃjñā kṣameti lokārthakarī kṛpājñā // Jm_28.26 //
children.translated_text: bearing the beautiful name fashioned by virtues — patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), which promotes the welfare of the world, [born of] the command of compassion. || Jm 28.26 ||

children.text: alaṃkriyā śaktisamanvitānāṃ tapodhanānāṃ balasapadagryā /
children.translated_text: The ornament of those endowed with power, the foremost companion of the strength of those rich in austerity,

children.text: vyāpādadāvānalavāridhārā pretyeha ca kṣāntiranarthaśāntiḥ // Jm_28.27 //
children.translated_text: a stream of water [to quench] the forest-fire of ill-will — patience is the pacification of misfortune, in this world and the next. || Jm 28.27 ||

children.text: kṣamāmaye varmaṇi sajjanānāṃ vikuṇṭhitā durjanavākyabāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Against the armor of patience worn by the virtuous, the arrows of the wicked's words are blunted;

children.text: prāyaḥ praśaṃsākusumatvametya tatkīrtimālāvayavā bhavanti // Jm_28.28 //
children.translated_text: they mostly come to be flowers of praise, becoming components of their garland of fame. || Jm 28.28 ||

children.text: hantīti yā dharmavipakṣamāyāṃ prāhuḥ sukhaṃ civa vimokṣamāyām /
children.translated_text: She who, they say, destroys the adversary of <s>Dharma</s>, and who is said [to lead] to happiness and to liberation —

children.text: tasmānna kuryātka iva kṣamāyāṃ prayatnamekāntahitakṣamāyām // Jm_28.29 //
children.translated_text: who, then, would not strive in patience, which is exclusively capable of benefiting? || Jm 28.29 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā tāsāṃ dharmātithyaṃ cakāra /
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul offered them the hospitality of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha sa rājā nidrāklamavinodanātprativibuddhaḥ sāvaśeṣamadagurunayano madanānuvṛttyā kutra devya iti śayanapālikāḥ sabhrūkṣepaṃ paryapṛcchat / etā deva vanāntarāṇyupaśobhayamānāstadvibhūtiṃ paśyantīti copalabhya śayanapālikābhyaḥ sa rājā devījanasya visrambhaniryantraṇahasitakathitadravaviceṣṭitadarśanotsukamatirutthāya śayanādyuvatidhṛtacchatravyajanottarīyakhaṅgaḥ sakañcukairvetradaṇḍapāṇibhirantapurāvacaraiḥ kṛtānuyātrastadvanamanuvicacāra / sa tatra yuvatijanānaibhṛtyaviracitāṃ vividhakusumastabakapallavanikaprapaddhatiṃ tāmbūlarasarāgavicitrāmanusaraṃstadāśramapadamabhijagāma / dṛṣṭaiva tu sa rājā kṣāntivādinaṃ tamṛṣivaraṃ devijanaparivṛtaṃ pūrvavairānuśayadoṣānmadaparibhramitasmṛtitvādīrṣyāparābhūtamatitvācca paraṃ kopamupajagāma / pratisaṃkhyānabalavaikalyācca
body.translated_text: Then that king, having awakened from the lassitude of sleep, his eyes still heavy with the residue of intoxication, in pursuit of amorous pleasures, asked the bedroom-attendants with a frown, 'Where are the queens?' And upon hearing from the bedroom-attendants that 'They are adorning the forest interiors, beholding its splendor,' that king, his mind eager to see the unrestrained laughter, talk, movements, and play of the queens' assembly, rising from his couch, with parasol, fan, upper garment, and sword held by young women, escorted by inner-palace attendants with cane-staves in hand, wandered through that forest. He, following the trail of various flower-clusters, sprays of blossoms, and rows of foliage artfully arranged by the young women, arrived at that hermitage. But that king, upon seeing <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>, that best of sages, surrounded by the queens, because of the taint of residual spite from former enmity, and because his memory was bewildered by intoxication, and because his mind was overcome by jealousy, was seized by extreme anger. And through the weakness of his power of reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>),

body.text: bhraṣṭavinayopacārasauṣṭhavaḥ saṃrambhapāpmābhibhavādāpatitasvedavaivarṇyavepathurbhrūbhaṅgajihmavivṛttasthirābhitāmranayano viraktakāntilāvaṇyaśobhaḥ pracalatkanakavalayau parimṛdnan sāṅgalivibhūṣaṇau pāṇī tamṛṣivaramadhikṣipaṃstattaduvāca / haṃho -
body.translated_text: his grace of disciplined civility was lost, and overwhelmed by the sin of rage, with sweat, pallor, and trembling setting in, his brow knitted, his eyes rolling askance, fixed, and reddish — his beauty, charm, and grace departed — rubbing his two hands adorned with golden bracelets and rings, he hurled various insults at that best of sages and said: 'Ha!

children.text: asmattejaḥ khalīkṛtya paśyannantaḥpurāṇi naḥ /
children.translated_text: "Making a mockery of our might, gazing upon our inner palace [women] —

children.text: muniveṣapraticchannaḥ ko 'yaṃ vaitaṃsikāyate // Jm_28.30 //
children.translated_text: who is this one, concealed in the garb of a sage, who plays the butcher? || Jm 28.30 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā varṣavarāḥ sasaṃbhramāvegā rājanamūcuḥ - deva mā maivam / cirakālasaṃbhṛtavrataniyamatapobhāvitātmā munirayaṃ kṣāntivādī nāmeti / upahatādhyāśayatvāttu sa rājā tatteṣāṃ vacanamapratigṛhṇannuvāca - kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Hearing that, the chief queens, with agitation and alarm, said to the king: 'Your Majesty, no, no! This sage is one named <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (Preacher of Patience), whose soul has been purified by observances, vows, and austerity cultivated over a long time!' But that king, his inner disposition being corrupted, not accepting their words, said: 'Alas!

children.text: cirātprabhṛti kolo 'yamevametena vañcyate /
children.translated_text: "For a long time these people have been deceived by this trickster,

children.text: kuhanājihmabhāvena tāpasākumbhasātmanā // Jm_28.31 //
children.translated_text: with his crooked, deceitful ways and his sham ascetic's nature! || Jm 28.31 ||

body.text: tadayamasya tāpasanepathyāvacchāditaṃ māyaśāṭhyasaṃbhṛtaṃ kuhakasvabhāvaṃ prakāṣayāmītyuktvā pratihārīhastādasimādāya hantumutpatitaniścayastamṛṣivaraṃ sapatnavacabhijagāma / atha tā devyaḥ parijananiveditābhyagamanamālokya rājānaṃ krodhasaṃkṣiptasaumyabhāvaṃ vitānībhūtahṛdayāḥ sasaṃbhramāvegacañcalanayanāḥ samutthāyābhivādya ca tamṛṣivaraṃ samudyatāñjalikuḍmalāḥ śarannalinya iva samudgataikapaṅkajānanamukulā rājānamabhijagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore I shall expose his hypocritical nature, concealed beneath his ascetic's costume and compounded of fraud and cunning!' Having said this, taking a sword from the hand of a female guard, his resolve to kill leaping forth, he approached that best of sages as if approaching a rival. Then the queens, seeing by the announcement of the attendants the approach of the king, whose gentle nature had been contracted by rage, their hearts becoming rigid with alarm, with eyes darting in agitation and panic, rising up and saluting that best of sages, with hands joined in lotus-bud gestures, like autumn lotuses with a single lotus-bud raised — approached the king.

children.text: tattāsāṃ samudācāralīlāvinayasauṣṭham /
children.translated_text: But the graceful propriety and courtesy of their conduct

children.text: na tasya śamayāmāsa krodhāgnijvalitaṃ manaḥ // Jm_28.32 //
children.translated_text: did not pacify his mind, ablaze with the fire of anger. || Jm 28.32 ||

body.text: labdhataraprāṇaprasarāstu tā devyaḥ sasaṃrambhavikārasamudācārarūkṣakramaṃ sāyudhamabhipatantaṃ tamudīkṣya rājānaṃ tamṛṣivaraṃ prati vivartitābhinivisṭadṛṣṭiṃ samāvṛṇvatya ūcuḥ - deva mā mā khalu sāhasaṃ kārṣīḥ / kṣāntivādī bhagavānayamiti / praduṣṭabhāvāttu sa rājā samāvarjitabhāvā nūnamanenemā iti suṣṭhutaraṃ kopamupetya sphuṭaraṃ bhrūbhaṅgairasūyāsamāveśatīkṣṇaistiryagavekṣitaistattāsāṃ praṇayaprāgalbhyamavabhartsya saroṣamavekṣamāṇaḥ strījanādhikṛtāñchiraḥkampādākampamānakuṇḍalamukuṭaviṭapastā yoṣito 'bhivīkṣamāṇa uvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the queens, having gained some latitude for their breath, seeing the king charging with weapon [drawn] in an onslaught of harsh, rage-distorted behavior toward that best of sages, upon whom his gaze was fixedly turned, interposing themselves, said: 'Your Majesty, you must not, you must not commit this rash act! This reverend one is <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>!' But that king, his disposition corrupted, [thinking] 'They have surely been won over by him,' growing even more angry, with his brow more conspicuously knit in expressions of jealous intensity and piercing sidelong glances, rebuking their bold familiarity, looking on wrathfully, the chief of the women's quarters, with his earrings and crown trembling from the shaking of his head, gazing at those women, said:

children.text: vadatyeva kṣamāmeṣa na tvenāṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: "He only speaks of patience but does not practice it;

children.text: tathā hi yoṣitsaṃparkatṛṣṇā na kṣāntavānayam // Jm_28.33 //
children.translated_text: for indeed, his thirst for the company of women shows that he has not practiced patience! || Jm 28.33 ||

children.text: vāganyathānyaiva śarīreceṣṭā duṣṭāśayaṃ mānasamanyathaiva /
children.translated_text: His speech is one thing, his bodily conduct another, and his wicked mind yet another —

children.text: tapovane ko 'yamasaṃyatātmā dambhavratāḍambaradhīramāste // Jm_28.34 //
children.translated_text: who is this unrestrained soul in the ascetic forest, sitting with the bold ostentation of a hypocrite's vow? || Jm 28.34 ||

body.text: atha tā devyastasmin rājani krodhasaṃrambhakarkaśahṛdaye pratyāhatapraṇayāḥ prajānānāśca tasya rājñaścaṇḍatāṃ duranuneyatāṃ ca vaimanasyadainyākrāntamanasaḥ strījanādhikṛtairbhayaviṣādavyākulitairhastasaṃjñābhirapasāryamāṇā vrīḍāvanatavadanāstamṛṣivaryaṃ samanuśocantyastato 'pacakramuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the queens, their affectionate overtures rebuffed by that king whose heart was hardened by the fury of anger, and knowing that king's ferocity and his being impossible to dissuade, their minds seized by despondency and dejection, being waved away by the agitated and alarmed attendants of the women's quarters with hand-signals, their faces bowed in shame, grieving for that best of sages, withdrew from that place.

children.text: asmannimittamaparādhavivarjite 'pi dānte tapasvini guṇapratite 'pyamuṣmin /
children.translated_text: "On account of us, against this blameless, disciplined ascetic, renowned for his virtues —

children.text: ko vetti kāmapi vivṛtya vikāralīlaṃ kenāpi yāsyapi pathā kṣitipasya roṣaḥ // Jm_28.35 //
kṣitīśavṛttiṃ pratilabdhakīrtiṃ tanuṃ munerasya tapastanuṃ ca /
amūnyanāgāṃsi ca no manāṃsi tulyaṃ hi hanyādapi nāma rājā // Jm_28.36 //

body.text: iti tāsu devīṣvanuśocitaviniḥśvasitamātraparāyaṇāsvapayātāsu sa rājā tamṛṣīvaraṃ saṃtarjayan roṣavaśanniṣkṛṣya khaṅgaṃ svayameva cchettumupacakrame / nirvikāradhīramasaṃbhrāntasvasthaceṣṭitaṃ ca taṃ mahāsattvamāsādyamānamapyavekṣya saṃrambhitaramenamuvāca -

children.text: dāṇḍājinikatānena prakarṣaṃ gamitā yathā /
udvahan kapaṭāṭopaṃ munivanmāmapīkṣate // Jm_28.37 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kṣāntiparicayādavicalitadhṛtistenāsatkāraprayogeṇa taṃ rājānaṃ roṣasaṃrambhavirūpaceṣṭitaṃ bhraṣṭavinayopacāraśriyaṃ vismṛtātmahitāhitapathamāgatavismayaḥ kṣaṇamabhivīkṣya karūṇāyamānaḥ samuneṣyanniyatamīdṛśaṃ kiṃciduvāca -

children.text: bhāgyāparādhajanito 'pyapamānayogaḥ saṃdṛśyate jagati tena na me 'tra cintā /
dūḥkhaṃ tu me yaducitābhigatesu vṛttirvācāpi na tvayi mayā kriyate yathārham // Jm_28.38 //

body.text: api ca mahārāja,

children.text: asatpravṛttān pathi saṃniyokṣyatā bhavadvidhānāṃ jagadarthakāriṇām /
na yuktarūpaṃ sahasā pravartituṃ vimarśamārgo 'pyanugamyatāṃ yataḥ // Jm_28.39 //
ayuktavatsādhvapi kiṃcidīkṣyate prakāśate 'sādhvapi kiṃcidanyathā /
na kāryatattvaṃ sahasaiva lakṣyate vimarśamaprāpya viśeṣahetubhiḥ // Jm_28.40 //
vimṛśya kāryaṃ tvavagamya tattvataḥ prapadya dharmeṇa ca nītivartmanā /
mahānti dharmārthasukhāni sādhayajanasya taireva na hīyate nṛpaḥ // Jm_28.41 //
vinīya tasmādaticāpalānmati yaśasyamevārhasi karma sevitum /
abhiprathante hyabhilakṣitātmanāmadṛṣṭapūrvāścariteṣvatikramāḥ // Jm_28.42 //
tapovane tvadbhujavīryarakṣite pareṇa yannāma kṛtaṃ na marṣayeḥ /
hitakramonmāthi yadāryagarhitaṃ svayaṃ mahīnātha kathaṃ vyavasyasi // Jm_28.43 //
striyo 'bhiyātā yadi te mamāśramaṃ yadṛcchayāntaḥpuraraikṣibhiḥ saha /
vyatikramastatra ca no bhavetkiyān ruṣāyadevaṃ gamito 'si vikriyām // Jm_28.44 //
athāpyayaṃ syādaparādha eva me kṣamā tu śobheta tathāpi te nṛpa /
kṣamā hi śaktasya paraṃ vibhūṣaṇaṃ guṇānurakṣānipūnatvasūcanāt // Jm_28.45 //
kapolaloladyutinīlakuṇḍale na mauliratnadyutayaḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ /
tathābhyalaṃkartumalaṃ nṛpānyathā kṣameti naināmavamantumarhasi // Jm_28.46 //
tyajākṣamāṃ nityamasaṃśrayakṣamāṃ kṣamāmivārakṣitumarhasi kṣamām /
tapodhaneṣvabhyuditā hi vṛttayaḥ kṣitīśvarāṇāṃ bahumānapeśalāḥ // Jm_28.47 //

body.text: ityanunīyamāno 'pi sa rājā tena munivareṇānārjavopahatamatistamanyathaivābhiśaṅkamānaḥ punaruvāca -

children.text: na tāpasacchadma bibharti cedbhavān sthito 'si vā sve niyamavrate yadi /
kṣamopadeśavyapadeśasaṃgataṃ kimarthamasmādabhayaṃ prayācase // Jm_28.48 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - śrūyatāṃ mahārāja yadartho 'yaṃ mama prayatnaḥ /

children.text: anāgasaṃ pravrajitamavadhīd brāhmaṇaṃ nṛpaḥ /
iti te matkṛte mā bhūdyaśo vācyavijarjaram // Jm_28.49 //
martavyamiti bhūtānāmayaṃ naiyamiko vidhiḥ /
iti me na bhayaṃ tasmātsvaṃ vṛttaṃ canupaśyataḥ // Jm_28.50 //
sukhodarkasya dharmasya pīḍā mā bhuttathaiva tu /
kṣamāmityavadaṃ tubhyaṃ śreyobhigamanakṣamām // Jm_28.51 //
guṇānāmākaratvācca doṣāṇāṃ ca nivāraṇāt /
prābhṛtātiśayaprītyā kathayāmi kṣamāmaham // Jm_28.52 //

body.text: atha sa rājā sūnṛtānyapi tānyanādṛtya tasya munervacanakusumāni sāsūyaṃ tamṛṣivaramuvāca - drakṣyāma idānīṃ te kṣāntyanurāgamityuktvā nivāraṇārthamiṣadabhiprasāritamabhyucchritapratanudīrghāṅgaliṃ tasya munerdakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ niśitenāsinā kamalamiva nāladeśād vyayojayat /

children.text: chinne 'grahaste 'pi tu tasya nāsīdduḥkhaṃ tathā kṣāntidṛḍhavratasya /
sukhocitasyāpratikāraghoraṃ chetturyathāgāmi samīkṣya duḥkham // Jm_28.53 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ kaṣṭamatikrānto 'yaṃ svahitamaryādāmapātrībhūto 'nunayasyeti vaidya pratyākhyātamānuramivainaṃ samanuśocaṃstūṣṇīṃbabhūva / athainaṃ sa rājā saṃtarjayan punaruvāca -

children.text: evaṃ cācchidyamānasya nāśameṣyati te tanuḥ /
muñca dambhavrataṃ cedaṃ khalabuddhipralambhanam // Jm_28.54 //

body.text: bodhisattvastvanunayākṣamamenaṃ viditvāyaṃ ca nāmāsya nirbandha iti nainaṃ kiṃciduvāca / atha sa rājā tasya mahātmano dvitīyaṃ pāṇibhūmau bāhu karṇanāsaṃ caraṇau tathaiva nicakarta /

children.text: patati tu niśite 'pyasau śarīre na munivaraḥ sa śuśoca no cukopa /
parividitaśarīrayantraniṣṭhaḥ paricitayā ca jane kṣamānuvṛttyā // Jm_28.55 //
gātracchede 'pyakṣatakṣāntidhīraṃ cittaṃ tasya prekṣamāṇasya sādhoḥ /
nāsīd duḥkhaṃ prītiyogānnṛpaṃ tu bhraṣṭaṃ dharmādvikṣya saṃtāpamāpa // Jm_28.56 //
pratisaṃkhyānamahatāṃ na tathā karuṇātmanām /
bādhate duḥkhamutpannaṃ parāneva yathāśritam // Jm_28.57 //
ghoraṃ tu tatkarmaḥ nṛpaḥ sa kṛtvā sadyo jvareṇānugato 'gnineva /
vinirgataścopavanāntadeśād gāṃ cāvadīrṇāṃ sahasā viveśa // Jm_28.58 //

body.text: nimagne tu tasmin rājani bhīmaśabdamavadīrṇāyāṃ vahnijvālākulāyāṃ samudbhūte mahati kolāhale samantataḥ prakṣubhite vyākule rājakule tasya rājño 'mātyā jānānāstasya munestapaḥprabhāvamāhātmyaṃ tatkṛtaṃ ca rājño dharaṇītalanimajjanaṃ manyamānāḥ purāyamṛṣivarastasya rājño doṣātsarvamidaṃ janapadaṃ nirdahatīti jātabhayāśaṅkāḥ samabhigamya tamṛṣivaramabhipraṇamya kṣamayamāṇāḥ kṛtāñjalayo vijñāpayāmāsuḥ -

children.text: imāmavasthāṃ gamito 'si yena nṛpeṇe mohādaticāpalena /
śāpānalasyendhanatāṃ sa eva prayātu te mā puramasya kṣākṣīḥ // Jm_28.59 //
strībālavṛddhāturavipradīnānanāgaso nārhasi dagdhumatra /
tatsādhu deśaṃ kṣitipasya tasya svaṃ caiva dharmaṃ guṇapakṣa rakṣa // Jm_28.60 //

body.text: athaitān bodhisattvaḥ samāśvāsayannuvāca - mā bhaiṣṭa āyuṣmantaḥ /

children.text: sapāṇipādamasinā karṇanāsamanāgasaḥ /
chinnavān yo 'pi tāvanme vane nivasata sataḥ // Jm_28.61 //
kathaṃ tasyāpi duḥkhāya cintayedapi madvidhaḥ /
ciraṃ jīvatvasau rājā mā cainaṃ pāpamāgamat // Jm_28.62 //
maraṇavyādhiduḥkhārte lobhadveṣavaśīkṛte /
dagdhe duścaritaiḥ śocye kaḥ kopaṃ kartumarhati // Jm_28.63 //

body.text: syāllabhyarūpastu yadi kramo 'yaṃ mayyeva pacyeta tadasya pāpam /
duḥkhānubandho hi sukhocitānāṃ bhavatyadīrgho 'pyaviṣahyatīkṣṇaḥ // Jm_28.64 //

children.text: trātuṃ na śakyastu mayā yadevaṃ vinirdahannātmahitaṃ sa rājā /
utsṛjya tāmātmagatāmaśaktiṃ rājñe kariṣyāmi kimityasūyām // Jm_28.65 //
ṛte 'pi rājño maraṇādiduḥkhaṃ jātena sarveṇa niṣevitavyam /
janmaiva tenātra na marṣaṇīyaṃ tannāsti cetkiṃ ca kutaśca duḥkham // Jm_28.66 //
kalpānanalpān bahudhā vinaṣṭaṃ śarīrakaṃ janmaparaṃparāsu /
jahyāṃ kathaṃ tatpralaye titikṣāṃ tṛṇasya hetoriva ratnajāṭam // Jm_28.67 //
vane vasan pravrajitapratijñaḥ kṣamābhidhāyī nacirānmariṣyan /
kimakṣamāyāṃ praṇayaṃ kariṣye tadbhaiṣṭa mā svasti ca vo 'stu yāt // Jm_28.68 //
iti sa munivaro 'nuśiṣya tān samamupanīya ca sādhuśiṣyatām /
avicalitadhṛtiḥ kṣamāśrayātsamadhiruroha divaṃ kṣamāśrayāt // Jm_28.69 //

body.text: tadevaṃ sātmībhūtakṣamāṇāṃ pratisaṃkhyānamahatāṃ nāviṣahyaṃ nāmāstīti kṣāntiguṇasaṃvarṇane munimupanīya vācyam / cāpalākṣāntidoṣanidarśane rājānamupanīya kāmādinavakathāyāmapi vācyam - evaṃ kāmahetorduścaritamāsevya vinipātabhāgino bhavantīti / saṃpadāmanityatāsaṃdarśane ceti /
// iti kṣāntijātakamaṣṭāviṃśatitamam //
29. Brahmajātakam
mithyādṛṣṭiparamāṇyavadyānīti viśesānukampyāḥ satāṃ dṛṣṭivyasanagatāḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān dhyānābhyāsopacitasya kuśalasya karmaṇo vipākaprabhāvād brahmaloke janma pratilebhe / tasya tanmahadapi dhyānaviśeṣādhigataṃ brāhmaṃ sukhaṃ pūrvajanmasu kāruṇyaparicayānnaiva parahitakaraṇavyāpāranirutsukaṃ manaścakāra /

children.text: viṣayasukhenāpi parāṃ pramādavaktavyatāṃ vrajati lokaḥ /
dhyānasukhairapi tu satāṃ na tiraskriyate parahitecchā // Jm_29.1 //

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahātmā karuṇāśrayabhūtaṃ vividhadūḥkhavyasanaśatopasṛṣṭamutkliṣṭavyāpādavihiṃsākāmadhātuṃ kāmadhātuṃ vyalokayan dadarśa videharājamaṅgadinnaṃ nāma kumitrasaṃparkadoṣādasanmanaskāraparicayācca mithyādṛṣṭigahane paribhramantam / nāsti paralokaḥ, kutaḥ śubhaśubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipāka ityevaṃ sa niścayamupetya praśāntadharmakriyautsukyaḥ pradānaśīlādisukṛtapratipattivimukhaḥ saṃrūḍhaparibhavabuddhirdhārmikeṣvaśraddhārūkṣamatirdharmaśāstreṣu parihāsacittaḥ parlokakathāsu śithilavinayopacāragauravabahumānaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇeṣu kāmasukhaparāyaṇo babhūva /

children.text: śubhāśubhaṃ karma sukhāsukhodayaṃ dhruvaṃ paratreti virūḍhaniścayaḥ /
apāsya pāpa yatate śubhāśrayo yatheṣṭamaśraddhatayā tu gamyate // Jm_29.2 //

body.text: atha sa mahātmā devarṣistasya rājñastena dṛṣṭivyasanopanipātenāpāyikena lokānarthākarabhūtena samāvarjitānukampastasya rājño viṣayasukhākalitamateḥ śrīmati pravivikte vimānadeśe 'vatiṣṭhamānasyābhijvalan brahmalokātpurastātsamavatatāra / atha sa rājā tamagniskandhamiva jvalantaṃ vidyutsamūhamiva cāvabhāsamānaṃ dinakarakīraṇasaṃghātamiva ca parayā dīptyā virocamānamabhivīkṣya tattejasābhibhūtamatiḥ sasaṃbhramaḥ prāñjalirena pratyutthāya sabahumānamudīkṣamāṇa ityuvāca -

children.text: karoti te bhūriva saṃparigrahaṃ nabho 'pi padmopamapāda pādayoḥ /
vibhāsi saurīmiva codvahan prabhāṃ vilocanānandanarūpa ko bhavān // Jm_29.3 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
jitvā dṛptau śāstravamukhyāviva saṃkhye rāgadveṣau cittasamādānabalena /
brāhmaṃ lokaṃ ye 'bhigatā bhūmipa teṣāṃ devarṣīṇāmanyatamaṃ māṃ tvamavehi // Jm_29.4 //
ityukte sa rājā svāgatādipriyavacanapuraḥsaraṃ pādyārghyasatkāramasmai samupahṛtya savismayamenamabhivīkṣamāṇa uvāca - āścaryarūpaḥ khalu te maharṣe ṛddhiprabhāvaḥ /

children.text: prāsādabhittiṣvaviṣajyamānaścaṃkramyase vyomni yathaiva bhūmau /
śatahradonmeṣasamṛddhadīpte pracakṣva tatkena taveyamṛddhiḥ // Jm_29.5 //

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -

children.text: dhyānasya śīlasya ca nirmalasya varasya caivendriyasaṃvarasya /
sātmīkṛtasyānyabhaveṣu rājannevaṃprakārā phalasiddhireṣā // Jm_29.6 //

body.text: rājovāca - kiṃ satyamevedamasti paraloka iti? brahmovāca - āma / asti mahārāja paralokaḥ / rājovāca - kathaṃ punaridaṃ mārṣa śakyamasmābhirapi śraddhātuṃ syāt? bodhisattva uvāca - sthūlametanmahārāja pratyakṣādipramāṇayuktigrāhyamāptajananidarśitakramaṃ parīkṣākramagamyaṃ ca / paśyatu bhavān /

children.text: candrārkanakṣatravibhūṣaṇā dyaustiryagvikalpāśca bahuprakārāḥ /
pratyakṣarūpaḥ paraloka eṣa mā te 'tra saṃdehajaḍā matirbhūt // Jm_29.7 //
jātismarāḥ santi ca tatra tatra dhyānābhiyogātsmṛtipāṭavācca /
ato 'pi lokaḥ parato 'numeyaḥ sākṣyaṃ ca nanvatra kṛtaṃ mayaiva // Jm_29.8 //
yadbuddhipūrvaiva ca buddhisiddhirlokaḥ paro 'stīti tato 'pyavehi /
ādyā hi yā garbhagatasya buddhiḥ sānantaraṃ pūrvakajanmabuddheḥ // Jm_29.9 //

body.text: jñeyāvabodhaṃ ca vadanti buddhiṃ janmādibuddherviṣayo 'sti tasmāt /
na caihiko 'sau nayanādyabhāvātsiddhau yadiyastu paraḥ sa lokaḥ // Jm_29.10 //

children.text: pitryaṃ svabhāvaṃ vyatiricya dṛṣṭaḥ śīlādibhedaśca yataḥ prajānām /
nākasmikasyāsti ca yatprasiddhirjātyantarābhyāsamayaḥ sa tasmāt // Jm_29.11 //
paṭutvahīne 'pi matiprabhāve jaḍaprakāreṣvapi cendriyeṣu /
vinopadeśātpratipadyate yatprasūtamātraḥ stanapānayatnam // Jm_29.12 //
āhārayogyāsu kṛtaśramatvaṃ taddarśayatyasya bhavāntareṣu /
abhyāsasiddhirhi paṭukaroti śikṣāgaṇaṃ karmasu teṣu teṣu // Jm_29.13 //

body.text: tatra cetparalokasaṃpratyayāparicayātsyādiyamāśaṅkā bhavataḥ -

children.text: yatsaṃkucanti vikasanti ca apṅkajāti kāmaṃ tadanyabhavaceṣṭisiddhireṣā /
no cettadiṣṭamatha kiṃ stanapānayatnaṃ jātyantarīyakapariśramajaṃ karoṣi // Jm_29.14 //

body.text: sā cāśaṅkā nānuvidheyā niyamāniyamadarśanātprayatnānupapattyupapattibhyāṃ ca /

children.text: dṛṣṭo hi kālaniyamaḥ kamalaprabodhe saṃmīlane ca na punaḥ stanapānayatne /
yatnaśca nāsti kamale stanape tu dṛṣṭaḥ sūryaprabhāva iti padmavikāsahetuḥ // Jm_29.15 //

body.text:
tadevaṃ mahārāja samyagupaparīkṣamāṇena śakyametacchraddhātum - asti paraloka iti /
atha sa rājā mithyādṛṣṭiparigrahābhiniviṣṭabuddhitvādupacitapāpatvācca tāṃ paralokakathāṃ śrutvā asukhāyamāna uvāca - bho maharṣe,

children.text: lokaḥ paro yadi na bālavibhīṣikaiṣā grāhyaṃ mayaitaditi vā yadi manyase tvam /
teneha naḥ pradiśa niṣkaśatāni pañca tatte sahasramahamanyabhave pradāsye // Jm_29.16 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastadasya prāgalbhyaparicayanirviśaṅkaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiviṣodgārabhūtamasamudācāravacanaṃ yukteneva krameṇa pratyuvāca -

children.text: ihāpi tāvaddhanasaṃpadarthinaḥ prayuñjate naiva dhanaṃ durātmani /
na ghasmare nānipuṇe na cālase gataṃ hi yattatra tadantameti tat // Jm_29.17 //
yameva paśyanti tu savyapatrapaṃ śamābhijātaṃ vyavahāranaipuṇam /
ṛṇaṃ prayacchanti raho 'pi tadvidhe tadarpaṇaṃ hyabhyudayāvahaṃ dhanam // Jm_29.18 //
kramaśca tāvadvidha eva gamyatāmṛṇaprayoge nṛpa pāralaukike /
tvayi tvasaddarśanaduṣṭaceṣṭite dhanaprayogasya gatirna vidyate // Jm_29.19 //
kudṛṣṭidoṣaprabhavairhi dāruṇairnipātitaṃ tvāṃ narake svakarmabhiḥ /
vicetasaṃ niṣkasahasrakāraṇādrujāturaṃ kaḥ praticodayettataḥ // Jm_29.20 //
na tatra candrārkakarairdigaṅganā vibhānti saṃkṣiptatamo 'vaguṇṭhanāḥ /
na caiva tārāgaṇabhūṣaṇaṃ nabhaḥ saraḥ prabuddhaiḥ kumudairivekṣyate // Jm_29.21 //
paratra yasminnivasanti nāstikā ghanaṃ tamastatra himaśca mārutaḥ /
karoti yo 'stīnyapi dārayan rujaṃ tamātmavān kaḥ praviśeddhanepsayā // Jm_29.22 //
dhanāndhakāre paṭudhūmadurdine bhramanti kecinnarakodare ciram /
svavadhracīrapravikarṣaṇāturāḥ parasparapraskhalanārtanādinaḥ // Jm_29.23 //
viśīryamāṇaiścarṇairmuhurmahurjvalatkukūle narake tathāpare /
diśaḥ pradhāvanti tadunmumukṣayā na cāntamāyāntyaśubhasya nāyuṣaḥ // Jm_29.24 //
ātakṣya takṣāṇa ivāpareṣāṃ gātrāni raudrā viniyamya yāmyāḥ /
nistakṣṇuvantyeva śitāgraśastrāḥ sārdreṣu dāruṣviva labdhaharṣāḥ // Jm_29.25 //
samutkṛttasarvatvaco vedanārtā vimāṃsīkṛtāḥ kecidapyasthiśeṣāḥ /
na cāyānti nāśaṃdhṛtā duṣkṛtaiḥ svaistathā cāpare khaṇḍaśaśchidyamānāḥ // Jm_29.26 //
jvalitapṛthukhalīnapūrṇavaktrāḥ sthiradahanāsu mahīṣvayomayīṣu /
jvalanakapilayoktratotravaśyāściramapare valato rathān vahanti // Jm_29.27 //

body.text: saṃghātaparvatasamāgamapiṣṭadehāḥ / kecittadākramaṇacūrṇitamūrtayo 'pi /

children.text: duḥkhe mahatyavikale 'pi ca no mriyante yāvatparikṣayamupaiti na karma pāpam // Jm_29.28 //
droṇiṣu kecijjvalanojjvalāsu lauhairmahadbhirmusalairjvaladbhiḥ /
samāni pañcāpi samāśatāni saṃcūrṇyamānā visṛjanti nāsūn // Jm_29.29 //
tīkṣṇāyasajvalitakaṇṭakakarkaśeṣu tapteṣu vidrumanibheṣvapare drumeṣu /
pāṭyanta ūrdhvamadha eva ca kṛṣyamāṇāḥ krūrai ravairapuruṣaiḥ puruṣairyamasya // Jm_29.30 //
jvaliteṣu taptatapanīyanibheṣvaṅgārarāśiṣu mahatsvapare /
upabhuñjate svacaritasya phalaṃ vispanditārasitamatrabalāḥ // Jm_29.31 //
kecittīkṣṇaiḥ śaṅkaśatairātatajihvā jvālāmālādīptatarāyāṃ vasudhāyām /
rāraṭyante tīvrarujāviṣṭaśarīrāḥ pratyāyyante te ca tadānīṃ paralokam // Jm_29.32 //
āveṣṭyante lohapaṭṭairjvaladbhirniṣkāthyante lohakumbhīṣvathānye /
kecittīkṣṇaiḥ śastravarṣaiḥ kṣatāṅgā nistvaṅmāṃsā vyālasaṃghaiḥ kriyante // Jm_29.33 //
kecitklāntā vahnisaṃsparśatīkṣṇaṃ kṣāraṃ toyaṃ vaitaraṇyāṃ viśanti /
saṃśīryante yatra māṃsāni teṣāṃ no tu prāṇā duṣkṛtairdhāryamāṇā // Jm_29.34 //
aśucikuṇapamabhyupeyivāṃso hradamiva dāhapariśramārtacittāḥ /
atulamanubhavanti tatra duḥkhaṃ krimiśatajarjaritāsthibhiḥ śarīraiḥ // Jm_29.35 //
jvalanaparigatā jvalaccharīrāściramapare 'nubhavanti dāhaduḥkham /
jvalanaparigatāyasaprakāśāḥ svakṛtadhṛtā na ca bhasmasādbhavanti // Jm_29.36 //
pāṭyante krakacairjvaladbhirapare kecinniśātaiḥ kṣuraiḥ
kecinmudgaravegapiṣṭaśirasaḥ kūjanti śokāturāḥ /
pacyante pṛthuśūlabhinnavapuṣaḥ kecidvidhūme 'nale
pāyyante jvalitāgnivarṇamapare lauhaṃ rasanto rasam // Jm_29.37 //
apare śvabhirbhṛśabalaiḥ śabalairabhipatya tīkṣṇadaśanairdaśanaiḥ /
pariluptamāṃsatanavastanavaḥ prapatanti dīnavirutā virutāḥ // Jm_29.38 //

body.text: evaṃprakāramasukhaṃ nirayeṣu ghoraṃ prāpto bhaviṣyati (bhavān) svakṛtapraṇunnaḥ /
śokāturaṃ śramaviṣādaparītacittaṃ yācedṛṇaṃ ka iva nāma tadā bhavantam // Jm_29.39 //

children.text: lauhīṣu durjanakalevarasaṃkulāsu kumbhīṣvabhijvalitavahnidurāsadāsu /
prakvāthavegavaśagaṃ vivaśaṃ bhramantaṃ yācedṛṇaṃ ka iva nāma tadā bhavantam // Jm_29.40 //
yaccāyasajvalitakilanibaddhadehaṃ nirdhūmavahnikapile vasudhātale vā /
nirdahyamānavapuṣaṃ karuṇaṃ rudantaṃ yācedṛṇaṃ ka iva nāma tadā bhavantam // Jm_29.41 //
prāptaṃ parābhavaṃ taṃ duḥkhāni mahānti kastadānubhavantam /
yācedṛṇaṃ bhavantaṃ prativacanamapi pradātumaprabhavantam // Jm_29.42 //
viśasyamānaṃ himamārutena vā nikūjitavye 'pi vipannavikramam /
vidāryamāṇa bhṛśamārtinādinaṃ paratra kastvārhati yācituṃ dhanam // Jm_29.43 //
vihiṃsyamāna puruṣairyamasya vā viceṣṭamānaṃ jvalite 'thavānale /
śvavāyasairvyāhṛtamāṃsaśoṇitaṃ paratra kastvā dhanayācñayā tudet // Jm_29.44 //
vadhavikartanatāḍanapāṭanairdahanatakṣaṇapeṣāṇabhedanaiḥ /
viśasanairvividhaiśca sadāturaḥ kathamṛṇaṃ pratidāsyasi me tadā // Jm_29.45 //

body.text: atha sa rājā, tāṃ nirayakathāmatibhīṣaṇāṃ samupaśrutya jātasaṃvegastyaktamithyādṛṣṭyanurāgo labdhasaṃpratyayaḥ paraloke, tamṛṣivaraṃ praṇamyovāca -

children.text: niśamya tāvannareṣu yātanāṃ bhayādidaṃ vidravatīva me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing now of the torments among men, my mind seems to flee in terror;

children.text: kathaṃ bhaviṣyāmi na tāṃ sameyivān vitakravahnirdahatīva māṃ punaḥ // Jm_29.46 //
children.translated_text: how shall I fare, having not escaped that [torment]? The fire of wrongdoing burns me again, as it were. || Jm 29.46 ||

children.text: mayā hyasaddarśananaṣṭacetasā kuvarmanā yātamadīrghadarśinā /
children.translated_text: For I, whose mind was ruined by wrong views, of poor conduct, short-sighted, have traveled [this far];

children.text: tadatra me sādhugatirgatirbhavān parāyaṇaṃ tvaṃ śaraṇaṃ ca me mune // Jm_29.47 //
children.translated_text: therefore here you are my good path and my refuge — you, O sage, are my final resort and shelter. || Jm 29.47 ||

children.text: yathaiva me dṛṣṭitamastvayoddhṛtaṃ divākareṇeva samudyatā tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the darkness of my wrong views has been dispelled by you, as darkness is dispelled by the risen sun,

children.text: tathaiva mārgaṃ tvamṛṣe pracakṣva me bhajeya yenāhamito na durgatim // Jm_29.48 //
children.translated_text: so too, O seer, point out to me the path by which I may not go from here to an evil destiny. || Jm 29.48 ||

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃvignamānasamṛjūbhūtadṛṣṭiṃ dharmapratipattipātrabhūtamavekṣya piteva putramācārya iva ca śiṣyamanukampamāna iti samanuśaśāsa -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing him agitated in mind and with his views set aright, having become a fit vessel for the practice of <s>Dharma</s>, with compassion like a father toward a son and a teacher toward a pupil, instructed him thus:

children.text: suśiṣyavṛttyā śramaṇadvijeṣu pūrve guṇaprema yathā vicakruḥ /
children.translated_text: As the kings of old, with devoted discipleship toward ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, cultivated love of virtues,

children.text: nṛpāḥ svavṛttyā ca dayāṃ prajāsu kīrtikṣamaḥ sa tridivasya panthāḥ // Jm_29.49 //
children.translated_text: and through their own conduct showed compassion toward their subjects — that path, worthy of fame, leads to heaven. || Jm 29.49 ||

children.text: adharmamasmād bhṛśadurjayaṃ jayan kadaryabhāvaṃ ca durutaraṃ taran /
children.translated_text: Therefore, conquering <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), which is exceedingly difficult to overcome, and crossing over miserliness, which is hard to traverse,

children.text: upaihi ratnātiśayojjvalaṃ jvalan divaspateḥ kāñcanagopuraṃ puram // Jm_29.50 //
children.translated_text: ascend, blazing with the surpassing splendor of jewels, to the golden-towered city of the Lord of Heaven. || Jm 29.50 ||

children.text: manasyasaddarśanasaṃstute 'stu te rucisthiraṃ sajjanasaṃmataṃ matam /
children.translated_text: Let there be in your mind a conviction that is firm in its inclination toward the good, approved by the virtuous, and praised by right views;

children.text: jahīhi taṃ bāliśarañjanaijanaiḥ pravedito 'dharmaviniścayaśca yaḥ // Jm_29.51 //
children.translated_text: and abandon that determination of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) which was proclaimed by people who delight the foolish. || Jm 29.51 ||

children.text: tvayā hi saddarśanasādhunādhunā narendra vṛttena yiyāsatā satā /
children.translated_text: For now by you, O king, who possess right views, who are of good conduct, who are virtuous, and who wish to advance,

children.text: yadaiva citte guṇarūkṣatā kṣatā tadaiva te mārgakṛtāspadaṃ padam // Jm_29.52 //
children.translated_text: the very moment harshness toward virtues is cut away in the mind, at that very moment your foot has found its place on the path. || Jm 29.52 ||

children.text: kuruṣva tasmād guṇasādhanaṃ dhanaṃ śivāṃ ca loke svahitodayāṃ dayām /
children.translated_text: Therefore make virtues your wealth and their cultivation your treasure; practice compassion in the world, which is auspicious and gives rise to one's own welfare;

children.text: sthiraṃ ca śīlendriyasaṃvaraṃ varaṃ paratra hi syādaśivaṃ na tena te // Jm_29.53 //
children.translated_text: and maintain firmly the excellent restraint of the senses through moral conduct — for thereby nothing inauspicious shall befall you in the hereafter. || Jm 29.53 ||

children.text: svapuṇyalakṣmyā nṛpa dīptayāptayā sukṛtsu śuklatvamanojñayājñayā /
children.translated_text: O king, with the radiance of your own merit, attained and shining, with the command that is white and delightful toward the virtuous,

children.text: carātmano 'rthapratisaṃhitaṃ hitaṃ jagadvyathāṃ kīrtimanoharaṃ haran // Jm_29.54 //
children.translated_text: practice what is beneficial and conducive to your own welfare, removing the suffering of the world in a manner captivating to fame and mind. || Jm 29.54 ||

children.text: tvamatra sanmānasasārathī rathī sva eva deho guṇasūratho rathaḥ /
children.translated_text: Herein you are the charioteer with a righteous mind, and you yourself are the chariot; your own body is the chariot adorned with the steeds of virtue,

children.text: arūkṣatākṣo damadānacakravān samanvitaḥ puṇyamanīṣayeṣayā // Jm_29.55 //
children.translated_text: with the axle of gentleness, with the wheels of self-control and generosity, equipped with merit through wise resolve. || Jm 29.55 ||

children.text: yatendriyāśvaḥ smṛtiraśmisaṃpadā matipratodaḥ śrutivistarāyudhaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the horses of restrained senses, with the wealth of the reins of mindfulness, with the goad of wisdom, with the weapons of extensive learning,

children.text: hrayupaskaraḥ saṃnaticārukūbaraḥ kṣamāyugo dākṣagatirdhṛtisthiraḥ // Jm_29.56 //
children.translated_text: with the accoutrements of modesty, with the beautiful yoke-pole of humility, yoked with patience, moving with the gait of skill, steady with fortitude. || Jm 29.56 ||

children.text: asadvacaḥsaṃyamanādakūjano manojñavāṅ mandagabhīranisvanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-creaking through the restraint of false speech, with speech that is pleasant, gentle, and deep in resonance,

children.text: amuktasaṃdhirniyamāvikhaṇḍanādasatkriyājihmavivarjanārjavaḥ // Jm_29.57 //
children.translated_text: with unbroken joints through the non-violation of vows, with the straightness of avoiding crooked and wicked deeds. || Jm 29.57 ||

children.text: anena yānena yaśaḥpatākinā dayānuyātreṇa śamoccaketunā /
children.translated_text: With this vehicle, bearing the banner of fame, attended by compassion, with the lofty standard of tranquility,

children.text: caran parātmārthamamohabhāsvatā na jātu rājannirayaṃ gamiṣyasi // Jm_29.58 //
children.translated_text: traveling for the welfare of both others and yourself, shining with the light of non-delusion — never, O king, shall you go to hell. || Jm 29.58 ||

body.text: iti sa mahātmā tasya rājñastadasaddarśanāndhakāraṃ bhāsvarairvacanakiraṇairvyavadhūya prakāśya cāsmai sugatimārgaṃ tatraivāntardadhe / atha sa rājā samupalabdhaparalokavṛttāntatattvaḥ pratilabdhasamyagdarśanacetāḥ sāmātyapaurajānapado dānadamasaṃyamaparāyaṇo babhūva /
body.translated_text: Thus that great soul, having dispelled the darkness of wrong views of that king with the radiant rays of his words, and having illuminated for him the path to a good destiny, vanished right there. Then that king, having grasped the truth about the affairs of the next world, his mind restored to right views, together with his ministers, citizens, and subjects, became devoted to generosity, self-control, and restraint.

body.text: tadevaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiparamāṇyavadyānīti viśeṣeṇānukampyāḥ satāṃ dṛṣṭivyasanagatāḥ / evaṃ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ paripūrṇāṃ śraddhāṃ paripūrayatītyevamapyupaneyam / evaṃ parato dharmaśravaṇaṃ samyagdṛṣṭyutpādapratyayo bhavatītyevamapyupaneyam / evamāsādanāmapi santastaddhitopadeśena pratinudanti kṣamāparicayānna pāruṣyeṇeti satpraśaṃsāyāṃ kṣāmāvarṇe 'pi vācyam / saṃvegādevamāśu śreyobhimukhatā bhavatīti saṃvegakathāyāmapi vācyamiti /
body.translated_text: Thus, because wrong views are the subtlest of faults, those who have fallen into the affliction of wrong views are especially to be pitied by the virtuous. It should also be adduced thus: hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> fulfills complete faith. It should also be adduced thus: hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from another becomes the cause for the arising of right views. It should also be stated in praise of the virtuous, even in a context of unfavorable description: thus even those who cause harm, the virtuous dispel through beneficial instruction, through the practice of patience and not through harshness. It should also be stated in a discourse on religious emotion: thus from spiritual urgency arises swift turning toward the good.

body.text: // iti brahmajātakamekonatriṃśattamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-ninth [story], the <s>Brahmā Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 30. Hastijātakam
body.translated_text: 30. The <s>Hasti Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Elephant)

body.text: parahitodarkaṃ duḥkhamapi sādhavo lābhamiva bahu manyante / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: The virtuous esteem even suffering that results in the welfare of others as highly as gain. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kila anyatamasmin nāgavane puṣpaphalapallavālakṣitaśikharairalaṃkṛta iva tatra taruvarataruṇairvividhavīruttarutṛṇapihitabhūmibhāge vanarāmaṇīyakanibaddhahṛdayairanutkaṇṭhitamadhyāsyamāna iva parvatasthalairāśrayabhūte vanacarāṇāṃ gambhīravipulasalilāśayasanāthe mahatā nirvṛkṣakṣupasalilena kāntāreṇa samantatastiraskṛtajanānte mahākāya ekacaro hastī babhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, was once a great-bodied, solitary elephant in a certain elephant-forest, whose peaks were adorned with flowers, fruits, and young shoots as if the place were decorated by the youthful trees, whose ground was covered with various creepers, bushes, and grasses, whose mountain plateaus — binding the heart with the forest's charm — served as dwelling places seemingly occupied without longing by the forest creatures, which was furnished with deep and vast reservoirs of water, and which was on all sides shut off from human habitation by a great waterless and treeless wilderness.

children.text: sa tatra taruparṇena bisena salilena ca /
children.translated_text: There, with the leaves of the trees, with lotus stalks, and with water,

children.text: abhireme tapasvīva saṃtoṣeṇa śamena ca // Jm_30.1 //
children.translated_text: he lived contentedly, like an ascetic, with satisfaction and tranquility. || Jm 30.1 ||

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahāsattvastasya vanasya paryante vicaran yatastatkāntāraṃ tato janaśabdamupaśuśrāva / tasya cintā prādurabhūt - kiṃ nu khalvidam? na tāvadanena pradeśena kaściddeśāntaragāmī mārgo 'sti / evaṃ mahatkāntāraṃ ca vyatītya mṛgayāpi na yujyate prāgeva mahāsamārambhaparikhedamasmatsayūthyagrahaṇam /
body.translated_text: Now once, that great being, while roaming at the border of that forest, heard the sound of people coming from the direction of the wilderness. A thought arose in him: 'What indeed is this? There is no road through this region leading to another country. And having crossed such a great wilderness, even hunting would not be feasible — much less the great exertion required to capture one of our herd.

children.text: vyaktaṃ tvete paribhraṣṭā mārgādvā mūḍhadaiśikā /
children.translated_text: Clearly these people have strayed from their path, or have been misled by their guides,

children.text: nirvāsitā vā kruddhena rājñā svenānayena vā // Jm_30.2 //
children.translated_text: or have been banished by an angry king, or by their own misfortune. || Jm 30.2 ||

children.text: tathā hyamanojasko naṣṭaharṣoddhavadravaḥ /
children.translated_text: For indeed, joyless, with their delight and enthusiasm gone,

children.text: kevalārtibalaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate rudatāmiva // Jm_30.3 //
children.translated_text: only the sound of anguish is heard, as if of people weeping.' || Jm 30.3 ||

body.text: tajjñāsyāmi tāvadenamiti sa mahāsattvaḥ karuṇayā samākṛṣyamāṇo yataḥ sa jananirghoṣo babhūva tataḥ prasasāra / viṣpaṣṭataravilāpaṃ ca viṣādadainyavirasaṃ tamākranditaśabdamupaśṛṇvan kāruṇyaparyutsukamanāḥ sa mahātmā drutataraṃ tato 'bhyagacchat / nirgamya ca tasmādvanagahanānnirvṛkṣakṣupatvāttasya deśasya dūra evāvalokayan dadarśa saptamātrāṇi puruṣaśatāni kṣuttarṣapariśramamandāni tadvanamabhimukhāni prārthayamānāni / te 'pi ca puruṣāstaṃ mahāsattvaṃ dadṛśurjaṅgamamiva himagiriśikharaṃ hīnārapuñjamiva śaradvalāhakamiva pavanabalāvarjitamabhimukhamāyāntam / dṛṣṭvā ca viṣādadainyaparītā hantedānīṃ naṣṭā vayamiti bhayagrastamanaso 'pi kṣuttarṣapariśramavihatotsāhā nāpayānaprayatnaparā babhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Thinking, 'Let me find out about this,' that great being, drawn by compassion, proceeded toward the source of that human clamor. Hearing that wailing sound ever more distinctly — disheartened, wretched, and dreary — that great soul, his mind agitated with pity, went there all the more swiftly. And emerging from the dense forest, because that region was devoid of trees and shrubs, looking from afar, he saw some seven hundred men, weakened by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, heading toward that forest with longing. Those men too saw that great being approaching like a moving peak of the snowy mountains, like a massive heap of cloud-banks, like an autumn cloud driven by the force of the wind, coming toward them. And seeing him, overcome with despondency and wretchedness, thinking 'Alas, now we are destroyed,' their minds seized with fear, yet their vigor sapped by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, they did not even make an effort to flee.

children.text: te viṣādaparītatvātkṣuttarṣaśramavihvalāḥ /
children.translated_text: Overcome by despair, bewildered by hunger, thirst, and exhaustion,

children.text: nāpayānasamudyogaṃ bhaye 'pi pratipedire // Jm_30.4 //
children.translated_text: they did not undertake the effort to flee, even in the face of danger. || Jm 30.4 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo bhītānavetyaitān - mā bhaiṣṭa, bhaiṣṭa na vo bhayamasti matta iti samucchritena snigdhābhitāmrapṛthupuṣkareṇa kareṇa samāśvāsayannabhigamya karuṇāyamāṇaḥ papraccha - ke 'trabhavantaḥ? kena cemāṃ daśāmanuprāptāḥ stha?
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, understanding that they were frightened, [called out:] 'Do not fear, do not fear — you have nothing to fear from me!' Reassuring them with his raised trunk, tender and broadly coppery, approaching them with compassion, he asked: 'Who are your honors? And by what [cause] have you arrived at this condition?

children.text: rajaḥsūryāṃśusaṃparkādvivarṇākṛtayaḥ kṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Discolored in form from contact with dust and sun's rays, emaciated,

children.text: śokaklamārtāḥ ke yūyamiha cābhigatāḥ kutaḥ // Jm_30.5 //
children.translated_text: afflicted by grief and fatigue — who are you, and whence have you come here? || Jm 30.5 ||

body.text: atha te puruṣāstasya tena mānuṣeṇābhivyāhāreṇābhayapradānābhivyañjakena cābhyupapattisaumukhyena pratyāgatahṛdayāḥ samabhipraṇamyainamūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those men, their hearts restored by his human speech, which conveyed the assurance of safety, and by his disposition of friendly approach, bowed to him reverently and said:

children.text: kopotpātānileneha kṣiptāḥ kṣitipatervayam /
children.translated_text: We have been cast here by the tempest of a king's anger,

children.text: paśyatāṃ śokadīnānāṃ bandhūnāṃ dviradādhipa // Jm_30.6 //
children.translated_text: while our kinsmen, wretched with grief, looked on, O lord of elephants. || Jm 30.6 ||

children.text: asti no bhāgyaśeṣastu lakṣmībhimukhī dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Yet there must be some remainder of our good fortune, and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) surely faces us again,

children.text: suhṛdvandhuviśiṣṭena yad dṛṣṭā bhavatā vayam // Jm_30.7 //
children.translated_text: since we have been seen by you, who surpass even a friend or kinsman. || Jm 30.7 ||

children.text: nistīrṇāmāpadaṃ cemāṃ vidmastvaddarśanotsavāt /
children.translated_text: And we know we have crossed beyond this calamity, from the joy of beholding you;

children.text: svapne 'pi tvadvidhaṃ dṛṣṭvā ko hi nāpadamuttaret // Jm_30.8 //
children.translated_text: for who, having seen one such as you even in a dream, would not surmount disaster? || Jm 30.8 ||

body.text: athainān sa dviradavara uvāca - atha kiyanto 'trabhavanta iti? manuṣyā ūcuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then that best of elephants said to them: 'And how many are your honors?' The men replied:

children.text: sahasrametadvasudhādhipena tyaktaṃ nṛṇāmatra manojñagātra /
children.translated_text: A thousand men were abandoned here by the lord of the earth, O one of lovely form;

children.text: adṛṣṭaduḥkhā bahavastatastu kṣuttarṣaśokābhibhavādvinaṣṭāḥ // Jm_30.9 //
children.translated_text: many of those, who had never known such suffering, have perished from the overwhelming force of hunger, thirst, and grief. || Jm 30.9 ||

children.text: etāni tu syurdviradapradhāna saptāvaśeṣāṇi nṛṇāṃ śatāni /
children.translated_text: But these seven hundred, O foremost of elephants, are the remnant of those men,

children.text: nimajjatāṃ mṛtyumukhe tu yeṣāṃ mūrtastvamāśvāsa ivābhyupetaḥ // Jm_30.10 //
children.translated_text: sinking into the jaws of death — to whom you have come as consolation incarnate. || Jm 30.10 ||

body.text: tacchrutvā tasya mahāsattvasya kāruṇyaparicayādaśrūṇi prāvartanta / samanuśocaṃścainānniyatamīdṛśaṃ kiṃ ciduvāca - kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Hearing this, tears flowed from that great being out of his habitual compassion. And lamenting over them, he inevitably spoke something like this: 'Alas!

children.text: ghṛṇāvimuktā bata nirvyapatrapā nṛpasya buddhiḥ paralokanirvyathā /
children.translated_text: Bereft of pity, utterly shameless is the mind of the king, indifferent to the next world!

children.text: aho taḍiccañcalayā nṛpaśriyā hṛtendriyāṇāṃ svahitānavekṣitā // Jm_30.11 //
