children.translated_text: Ah, how blind to their own welfare are those whose senses have been stolen by royal fortune, fickle as lightning! || Jm 30.11 ||

children.text: avaiti manye na sa mṛtyumagrataḥ śṛṇoti pāpasya na vā durantatām /
children.translated_text: He does not perceive death before him, I think, nor does he hear of the endlessness of sin;

children.text: aho batānāthatamā narāḍhipā vimarśamāndyādvacanakṣamā na ye // Jm_30.12 //
children.translated_text: alas, most pitiable are those rulers of men who, through dullness of judgment, are not amenable to counsel! || Jm 30.12 ||

children.text: dehasyaikasya nāmarthe rogabhūtasya nāśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the sake of a single body, which is like a disease and subject to destruction —

children.text: idaṃ sattveṣu nairghṛṇyaṃ dhigaho bata mūḍhatām // Jm_30.13 //
children.translated_text: this cruelty toward living beings! Shame! Alas, what delusion! || Jm 30.13 ||

body.text: atha tasya dviradapatestān puruṣān karuṇāsnigdhamavekṣamāṇasya cintā prādurabhūt evamamī kṣuttarṣaśramapīḍitāḥ paridurbalaśarīrā nirudakamapracchāyamanekayojanāyānaṃ kāntāramapathyādanāḥ kathaṃ vyatiyāsyanti? nāgavane 'pi ca kiṃ tadasti yenaiṣāmekāhamapi tāvadaparikleśena vārtā syāt? śakyeyuḥ punarete madīyāni māṃsāni pātheyatāmupanīya dṛtibhiriva ca mamāntraiḥ salilamādāya kāntārametannistarituṃ nānyathā /
body.translated_text: Then a thought arose in that lord of elephants as he gazed upon those men with compassion-moistened eyes: 'Thus these people, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and exhaustion, their bodies utterly weakened — how will they cross this waterless, shadeless wilderness of many <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), eating unwholesome food? And even in the elephant-forest, what is there by which they could sustain themselves even for a single day without suffering? But could they, taking my flesh as provisions and carrying water in my entrails as if in leather sacks, cross this wilderness? There is no other way.

children.text: karomi tadidaṃ dehaṃ bahurogaśatālayam /
children.translated_text: Therefore let me make this body, the abode of hundreds of diseases,

children.text: eṣāṃ duḥkhaparītānāmāpaduttaraṇaplavam // Jm_30.14 //
children.translated_text: a raft for these suffering ones to cross over their calamity. || Jm 30.14 ||

children.text: svargamokṣasukhaprāptisamarthaṃ janma mānuṣam /
children.translated_text: Human birth, capable of attaining the happiness of heaven and liberation,

children.text: durlabhaṃ ca tadeteṣāṃ maivaṃ vilayamāgamat // Jm_30.15 //
children.translated_text: is rare to obtain — let these [lives] not thus come to destruction! || Jm 30.15 ||

children.text: svagocarastasya mamābhyupetā dharmeṇa ceme 'tithayo bhavanti /
children.translated_text: They have come within my domain and by <s>Dharma</s> (righteous law) they are my guests;

children.text: āpadgatā bandhuvivarjitāśca mayā viśeṣeṇa yato 'nukampyāḥ // Jm_30.16 //
children.translated_text: fallen into distress and bereft of kinsmen — they are therefore especially to be pitied by me. || Jm 30.16 ||

children.text: cirasya tāvadvahurogabhājanaṃ sadāturatvādvividhaśramāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For a long time this receptacle of many diseases, the resting place of various afflictions due to perpetual infirmity —

children.text: śarīrasaṃjño 'yamanarthavistaraḥ parārthakṛtye viniyogameṣyati // Jm_30.17 //
children.translated_text: this expanse of misfortune called 'the body' — shall find its employment in service to others.' || Jm 30.17 ||

body.text: athainamanye kṣuttarṣaśramadharmaduḥkhāturaśarīrāḥ kṛtāñjalayaḥ sāśrunayanāḥ samabhipraṇamyārtatayā hastasaṃjñābhiḥ pānīyamayācanta /
body.translated_text: Then others among them, their bodies tormented by the suffering of hunger, thirst, fatigue, and heat, with palms joined and eyes filled with tears, bowed to him and, in their distress, begged for water with hand gestures.

children.text: tvaṃ no bandhurabandhūnāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ śaraṇaṃ ca naḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are the kinsman of us who are without kinsmen, you are our refuge and shelter;

children.text: yathā vetsi mahābhāga tathā nastrātumarhasi // Jm_30.18 //
children.translated_text: as you know [best], O most fortunate one, so you should endeavor to save us. || Jm 30.18 ||

body.text: ityenamanye sakaruṇamūcuḥ / apare tvenaṃ dhīrataramanasaḥ salilapradeśaṃ kāntāradurgottāraṇāya ca mārgaṃ papracchuḥ -
body.translated_text: Thus some spoke to him piteously. Others among them, being of steadier mind, asked him about a place with water and a path to cross the impassable wilderness:

children.text: jalāśayaḥ śītajalā saridvā yadyatra vā nairjharamasti toyam /
children.translated_text: 'Whether there be a lake, a river of cool water, or spring water here,

children.text: chāyādrumaḥ śādvalamaṇḍalaṃ vā tannod vipānāmadhipa pracakṣva // Jm_30.19 //
children.translated_text: or a shade tree, or a patch of green meadow — that, O lord of beasts, please point out to us. || Jm 30.19 ||

children.text: kāntāraṃ śakyametacca nistartuṃ manyase yataḥ /
children.translated_text: And if you think this wilderness can be crossed,

children.text: anukampāṃ puraskṛtya tāṃ diśaṃ sādhu nirdiśa // Jm_30.20 //
children.translated_text: then with compassion as your guide, kindly indicate that direction. || Jm 30.20 ||

body.text: saṃbahulāni hi dinānyatra naḥ kāntāre paribhramatām / tadarhasi naḥ svāminnistārayitumiti /
body.translated_text: For many days now we have been wandering in this wilderness. Therefore, O master, deign to rescue us.'

body.text: atha sa mahātmā taiḥ karuṇaiḥ prayācitaisteṣāṃ bhṛśataramākleditahṛdayo yatastatkāntāraṃ śakyaṃ nistartu babhūva, tata esāṃ parvatasthalaṃ saṃdarśayannabhyucchritena bhujagavarabhogapīvareṇa kareṇovāca - asya parvatasthalasyādhastātpadmotpalālaṃkṛtavimalasalilamasti mahatsaraḥ / tadanena mārgeṇa gacchata / tatna ca vyapanītagharmatarṣaklamāstasyaiva nātīdūre 'smātparvatasthalātpatitasya hastinaḥ śarīraṃ drakṣyatha / tasya māṃsāni pātheyatāmānīya dṛtibhiriva tasyāntraiḥ salilamupagṛhyānayaiva diśā yātavyam / evamalpakṛcchreṇa kāntāramidaṃ vyatiyāsyatha / iti sa mahātmā tān puruṣān samāśvāsanapūrvakaṃ tataḥ prasthāpya tato drutataramanyena mārgeṇa tadgiriśikharamāruhya tasya janakāyasya nistāraṇāpekṣayā svaśarīraṃ tato mumukṣurniyatamiti praṇidhimupabṛṃhayāmāsa -

children.text: nāyaṃ prayatnaḥ sugatiṃ mamāptuṃ naikātapatrāṃ manujendralakṣmīm /
sukhaprakarṣaikarasāṃ na ca dyāṃ brāhmīṃ śriyaṃ naiva na mokṣasaukhyam // Jm_30.21 //
yatvasti puṇyaṃ mama kiṃcidevaṃ kāntāramagnaṃ janamujjihīrṣoḥ /
saṃsārakāntāragatasya tena lokasya nistārayitā bhaveyam // Jm_30.22 //

body.text: iti viniścitya sa mahātmā pramodādagaṇitaprapātaniṣpeṣamaraṇaduḥkhaṃ svaśarīraṃ tasmād giritaṭādyathoddeśaṃ mumoca -

children.text: reje tataḥ sa nipatañcharadīva meghaḥ paryastabimba iva cāstagireḥ śaśāṅkaḥ /
tārkṣyasya pakṣapavanograjavāpaviddhaṃ śṛṇgaṃ gireriva ca tasya himottarīyam // Jm_30.23 //
ākampayannatha dharāṃ dharaṇīdharāṃśca mārasya ca prabhumadādhyuṣitaṃ ca cetaḥ /
nirghātapiṇḍitaravaṃ nipapāta bhūmāvāvarjayan vanalatā vanadevatāśca // Jm_30.24 //
asaṃśayaṃ tadvanasaṃśrayāstadā manassu visphāritavismayāḥ surāḥ /
vicikṣipurvyomni mudottanūruhāḥ samucchritaikāṅgulipallavān bhujān // Jm_30.25 //
sugandhibhiścandanacūrṇarañjitaiḥ prasaktamanye kusumairavākiran /
atāntavaiḥ kāñcanabhaktirājitaistamuttarīyairapare vibhūṣaṇaiḥ // Jm_30.26 //
stavaiḥ prasādagrathitaistathāpare samudyataiścāñjalipadmakuḍmalaiḥ /
śirobhirāvarjitacārumaulibhirnamaskiryābhiśca tamabhyapūjayan // Jm_30.27 //
sugandhinā puṣparajovikarṣaṇāttaraṃgamālāracanena vāyunā /
tamavyajan kecidathāmbare 'pare vitānamasyopadadhurghanairghanaiḥ // Jm_30.28 //
tamarcituṃ bhaktivaśena kecana vyarāsayan dyāṃ suradundubhisvanaiḥ /
akālajaiḥ puṣpaphalaiḥ sapallavairvyabhūṣayaṃstatra tarūnathāpare // Jm_30.29 //
diśaḥ saratkāntimayīṃ dadhuḥ śriyaṃ raveḥ karāḥ prāṃśutarā ivābhavan /
mudābhigantuṃ tamivāsa cārṇavaḥ kutūhalotkampitavīcivibhramaḥ // Jm_30.30 //

body.text: atha te puruṣāḥ krameṇa tatsaraḥ samupetya tasmin vinītadharmatarṣaklamā yathākathitaṃ tena mahātmanā tadavidūre hastiśarīraṃ naciramṛtaṃ dadṛśuḥ / teṣāṃ buddhirabhavat - aho yathāyaṃ sadṛśastasya dviradapaterhastī /
bhrātā nu tasyaiṣa mahādvipasya syād bāndhavo vānyatamaḥ suto vā /
tasyaiva khalvasya sitādriśobhaṃ saṃcūrṇitasyāpi vibhāti rūpam // Jm_30.31 //

children.text: kumudaśrīrivaikasya jyotsnā puñjīkṛteva ca /
chāyeva khalu tasyeyamādarśatalasaṃśritā // Jm_30.32 //

body.text: atha tatraikeṣāṃ nipuṇataramanupaśyatāṃ buddhirabhavat - yathā paśyāmaḥ sa eva khalvayaṃ digvāreṇendrapratispardhirūpātiśayaḥ kuñjaravara āpadgatānāmabandhusuhṛdāmasmākaṃ nistāraṇāpekṣayā giritaṭādasmānnipatita iti /

children.text: yaḥ sa nirghatavadabhūtkampayanniva medinīm /
vyaktamasyaiva patataḥ sa cāsmābhirdhvaniḥ śrutaḥ // Jm_30.33 //
etadvapuḥ khalu tadeva mṛṇālagauraṃ candraṃśuśuklatanujaṃ tanubinducitram /
kūrmopamāḥ sitanakhāścaraṇāsta ete vaṃśaḥ sa eva ca dhanurmadhurānato 'yam // Jm_30.34 //
tadeva cedaṃ madarājirājitaṃ sugandhivāyvāyatapīṇamānanam /
samunnataṃ śrimadanarpitāṅkaśaṃ śirastadetacca bṛhacchirodharam // Jm_30.35 //
viṣāṇayugmaṃ tadidaṃ madhuprabhaṃ sadarpacihnaṃ taṭareṇunāruṇam /
ādeśayan mārgamimaṃ ca yenaḥ sa eṣa dīrghāṅgalipuṣkaraḥ karaḥ // Jm_30.36 //

body.text: āścaryamatyadbhutarūpaṃ bata khalvidam /

children.text: adṛṣṭapūrvānvayaśīlabhaktiṣu kṣateṣu bhāgyairapariśruteṣvapi /
suhṛttvamasmāsu batedamīdṛśaṃ suhṛtsu vā bandhuṣu vāsya kīdṛśam // Jm_30.37 //

body.text: sarvathā namo 'stvasmai mahābhāgāya /
āpatparītān bhayaśokadīnānasmadvidhānabhyupapadyamānaḥ /
ko 'pyeṣa manye dviradāvabhāsaḥ siṣatsatāmudvahatīva vṛttam // Jm_30.38 //

children.text: kva śikṣito 'sāvatibhadratāmimāmupāsitaḥ ko nvamunā gururvane /
na rūpaśobhā ramate vinā guṇairjano yadityāha tadetadīkṣyate // Jm_30.39 //
aho svabhāvātiśayasya saṃpadā vidarśitānena yathārhabhadratā /
himādriśobhena mṛto 'pi khalvayaṃ kṛtātmatuṣṭirhasatīva varṣmaṇā // Jm_30.40 //

body.text: tatka idānīmasya snigdhabāndhavasuhṛtprativiśiṣṭavātsalyasyaivamabhyupapattisumukhasya svaiḥ prāṇairapyasmadarthamupakartumabhipravṛttasyāṭisādhuvṛttasya māṃsamupabhoktuṃ śakṣyati? yuktaṃ tvasmābhiḥ pūjāvidhipūrvakamagnisatkāreṇāsyānṛṇyamupagantumiti / atha tān bandhuvyasan eva śokānuvṛttipravaṇahṛdayān sāśrunayanān gadgadāyamānakaṇṭhānavekṣya kāryāntaramavekṣamāṇā dhīrataramanasa ūcuranye - na khalvevamasmābhirayaṃ dviradavaraḥ saṃpūjitaḥ satkṛto vā syāt / abhiprāyasaṃpādanena tvayamasmābhiryuktaḥ pūjayitumiti paśyāmaḥ /

children.text: āsmannistāraṇāpekṣī sa hyasaṃstutabāndhavaḥ /
śarīraṃ tyaktavānevamiṣṭamiṣṭatarātithiḥ // Jm_30.41 //
abhiprāyamatastvasya yuktaṃ samanuvartitum /
anyathā hi bhavedvyartho nanu tasyāyamudyamaḥ // Jm_30.42 //
snehādudyatamātithyaṃ sarvasvaṃ tena khalvidam /
apratigrahaṇādvyarthāṃ kuryātko nvasya satkriyām // Jm_30.43 //
guroriva yatastaya vacasaḥ saṃpratigrahāt /
satkriyāṃ kartumarhāmaḥ kṣemamātmana eva ca // Jm_30.44 //
nistīrya cedaṃ vyasanaṃ samagraiḥ pratyekaśo vā punarasya pūjā /
kariṣyate nāgavarasya sarvaṃ bandhoratītasya yathaiva kṛtyam // Jm_30.45 //

body.text: atha te puruṣāḥ kāntāranistāraṇāpekṣayā tasya dviradapaterabhiprāyamanusmarantastadvacanamapratikṣipya tasya mahāsattvasya māṃsānyādāya dṛtibhiriva ca tadantraiḥ salilaṃ tatpradarśitayā diśā svasti tasmātkāntārādviniryayuḥ /

tadevaṃ parihitodarkaṃ duḥkhamapi sādhavo lābhamiva bahu manyante, iti sādhu janapraśaṃsāyāṃ vācyam / tathāgatavarṇe 'pi, satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ca bhadraprakṛtiniṣpādanavarṇe 'pi vācyam - evaṃ bhadrā prakṛtirabhyastā janmāntareṣvanuvartata iti / tyāgaparicayaguṇanidarśane 'pi vācyam - evaṃ dravyatyāgaparicayādātmasnehaparityāgamapyakṛcchreṇa karotīti / yaccoktaṃ bhagavata parinirvāṇasamaye samupasthiteṣu divyakusumavāditrādiṣu - na khalu punarānanda etāvatā tathāgataḥ satkṛto bhavatīti, taccaivaṃ nidarśayitavyam / evamabhiprāyasaṃpādanātpūjā kṛtā bhavati na gandhamālyādyabhihāreṇeti /
// iti hastijātakaṃ triṃśattamam //
31. Sutasomajātakam
śreyaḥ samādhatte yathātathāpyupanataḥ satsaṃgama iti sajjanāpāśrayeṇa śreyo 'rthinā bhavitavyam / tadyathānuśrūyate -

bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān yaśaḥprakāśavaṃśe guṇaparigrahaprasaṅgātsātmībhūtaprajānurāge pratāpānatadṛptasāmante śrīmati kauravyarājakule janma pratilebhe tasya / guṇaśatakiraṇamālinaḥ somapriyadarśanasya sutasya sutasoma ityevaṃ pitā nāma cakre / sa śuklapakṣacandramā iva pratidinamabhivardhamānakāntilāvaṇyaḥ kālakramādavāpya sāṅgeṣu sopavedeṣu ca vedeṣu vaicakṣaṇyaṃ dṛṣṭakramaḥ sottarakalānāṃ kalānāṃ lokyānāṃ lokapremabahumānaniketabhūtaḥ samyagabhyupapattisaumukhyādabhivardhamānādarātparipālananiyamācca bandhuriva guṇānāṃ babhūva /

children.text: śīlaśrutatyāgadayādamānāṃ tejaḥkṣamādhīdhṛtisaṃnatīnām /
anunnatihrīmatikāntikīrtidākṣiṇyamedhābalaśuklatānām // Jm_31.1 //
teṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ sa guṇodayānāmalaṃkṛtānāmiva yauvanena /
viśuddhataudāryamanoharāṇāṃ candraḥ kalānāmiva saṃśrayo 'bhūt // Jm_31.2 //

body.text: ataścainaṃ sa rājā lokaparipālanasāmarthyādakṣudrabhadraprakṛtitvācca yauvarājyavibhūtyā saṃyojayāmāsa /

children.text: vidvattayā tvāsuratīva tasya priyāṇi dharmyāṇi subhāṣitāni /
ānarca pūjātiśayairatastaṃ subhāṣitairenamupāgamadyaḥ // Jm_31.3 //

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahātmā kusumamāsaprabhāvaviracitakisalayalakṣmīmādhuryāṇi pravikasatkusumamanojñaprahasitāni pravitatanavaśādvalakuthāstaraṇasanāthadharaṇītalāni kamalotpaladalāstīrṇanirmalanīlasalilāni bhramadbhramaramadhukarīgaṇopagītānyanibhṛtaparabhṛtabarhigaṇāni mṛdusurabhiśiśirasukhapavanāni manaḥprasādodbhāvanāni nagaropavanānyanuvicaran anyatamamudyānavanaṃ nātimahatā balakāyena parivṛtaḥ krīḍārthamupanirjagāma /

children.text: sa tatra puṃskokilanādite vane manoharodyānavimānabhūṣite /
cacāra puṣpānatacitrapādape priyāsahāyaḥ sukṛtīva nandane // Jm_31.4 //
gītasvanairmadhuratūryaravānuviddhairnṛtyaiśca hāvacaturairlalitāṅgahāraiḥ /
strīṇāṃ madopahṛtayā ca vilāsalakṣmyā reme sa tatra vanacārutayā tayā ca // Jm_31.5 //
children.translated_text: He delighted there with the beauty of the women, whose grace was heightened by the intoxication of passion, and with the loveliness of the forest. || Jm 31.5 ||

body.text: tatrasthaṃ cainamanyatamaḥ subhāṣitākhyāyī brāhmaṇaḥ samabhijagāma / kṛtopacārasatkāraśca tadrūpaśobhāpahṛtamanāstatropaviveśa / iti sa mahāsattvo yauvanānuvṛttyā puṇyasamṛddhiprabhāvopanataṃ krīḍāvidhimanubhavaṃstadāgamanādutpannabahumāna eva tasmin brāhmaṇe subhāṣitaśravaṇādanavāptāgamanaphale sahasaivotpatitaṃ gītavāditrasvanoparodhi kriḍāprasaṅgajanitapraharṣopahantṛ pramadājanabhayaviṣādajananaṃ kolāhalamupaśrutya jñāyatāṃ kimetamditi sādaramantaḥ purāvacarān samādideśa / athāsya dauvārikā bhayaviṣādadinavadanāḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ drutataramupetya nyavedayanta - eṣa sa deva puruṣādaḥ kalmāṣavādaḥ saudāsaḥ sākṣādivāntako naraśatakadanakaraṇaparicayādrākṣasādhikakrūrataramatiratimānuṣabalavīryadarpo rakṣaḥpratibhayaraudramūrtimūrtimāniva jagatsaṃtrāsa iti evābhivartate / vidrutaṃ ca nastatsaṃtrāsagrastadhairyamudbhrāntarathaturagadviradavyākulayodhaṃ balam / yataḥ pratiyatno bhavatu devaḥ, prāptakālaṃ vā saṃpradhāryatāmiti / atha sutasomo jānāno 'pi tānuvāca - bhoḥ ka eṣa saudāso nāma? te taṃ procuḥ - kimetaddevasya na viditaṃ yathā sudāso nāma rājā babhūva / sa mṛgayānirgato 'śvenāpahṛto vanagahanamanupraviṣṭaḥ siṃhyā sārdhaṃ yogamagamat / āpannasattvā ca sā siṃhī saṃvṛttā / kālāntareṇa ca kumāraṃ prasuṣuve / sa vanacarairgṛhītaḥ sudāsāyopanītaḥ / aputro 'hamiti ca kṛtvā sudāsena saṃvardhitaḥ / pitari ca surapuramupagate svaṃ rājyaṃ pratilebhe / sa mātṛdoṣādāmiṣeṣvabhisaktaḥ / idamidaṃ rasavaraṃ māṃsamiti sa mānuṣaṃ māṃsamāsvādya svapaurāneva ca hatvā hatvā bhakṣayitumupacakrame / atha paurāstadvadhāyodyogaṃ cakruḥ / yato 'sau bhītaḥ saudāso nararudhirapiśitabalibhugbhyo bhutebhya upaśuśrāva - asmātsaṃkaṭānmukto 'haṃ rājñāṃ kumāraśatena bhūtayajñaṃ kariṣyāmīti / so 'yaṃ tasmātsaṃkaṭānmuktaḥ / prasahya prasahya cānena rājakumārāpaharanaṃ kṛtam / so 'yaṃ devamapyapahartuṃmāyātaḥ / śrutvā devaṃ pramāṇamiti /
body.translated_text: While he was staying there, a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a reciter of wise sayings (<s>subhāṣita</s>), came to visit him. Having been received with due hospitality, his mind captivated by the beauty of <s>Sutasoma's</s> form, he sat down there. Thus the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), enjoying the pleasures brought about by the power of his accumulated merit in accordance with his youth, had already conceived great esteem for that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> upon his arrival, whose coming had not yet borne fruit through the hearing of wise sayings, when suddenly he heard a tumult — drowning out the sounds of songs and instruments, destroying the joy born of the occasion of merriment, and causing fear and dismay among the women — and he respectfully instructed the attendants of the inner palace: 'Let it be ascertained what this is.' Then his doorkeepers, their faces stricken with fear and dismay, came hurrying to him in great haste and reported: 'This, O lord, is the man-eater <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, <s>Saudāsa</s> — like <s>Antaka</s> (Death) himself in person; through his familiarity with slaughtering hundreds of men, his cruelty surpasses even that of <s>Rākṣasas</s>; proud of his superhuman strength and valor, embodying a form as terrifying and dreadful as that of a <s>Rakṣas</s>, he is the very incarnation of terror to the world — thus he is advancing. And our army, its courage seized by terror at him, with charioteers, horses, and elephants thrown into confusion, has been routed. Therefore let the lord take countermeasures, or let a suitable course of action be deliberated upon.' Then <s>Sutasoma</s>, though he already knew, said to them: 'Sirs, who is this person called <s>Saudāsa</s>?' They told him: 'Is this not known to the lord? There was a king named <s>Sudāsa</s>. He, having gone out hunting, was carried away by his horse into the depths of the forest, and there he mated with a lioness. And that lioness became pregnant. In due course she gave birth to a prince. He was found by forest-dwellers and brought to <s>Sudāsa</s>. Thinking "I am without a son," <s>Sudāsa</s> raised him. And when his father departed to the city of the gods, he obtained the kingdom. Due to the defect inherited from his mother, he became addicted to meat. Thinking "This, this is the finest-flavored meat," he tasted human flesh, and began killing and devouring his own citizens. Then the citizens organized an effort to kill him. Whereupon <s>Saudāsa</s>, frightened, made a vow to the spirits who feast on offerings of human blood and flesh: "Once freed from this crisis, I shall perform a sacrifice to the spirits with a hundred princes." And he has been freed from that crisis. And by force he has carried off prince after prince. He has come to abduct even the lord — having heard that the lord is [a king of] great stature.'

body.text: atha sa bodhisattvaḥ pūrvameva viditaśīladoṣavibhramaḥ saudāsasya kāruṇyāttaccikitsāvahitamatirāśaṃsamānaścātmani tacchīlavikṛtapraśamanasāmarthyaṃ priyākhyāna iva ca saudāsābhiyānanivedane prītiṃ pratisaṃvedayanniyatamityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who already knew of <s>Saudāsa's</s> moral corruption and aberration, his mind intent on curing it out of compassion, and hoping for the capacity within himself to pacify that corruption of character, feeling delight at the report of <s>Saudāsa's</s> approach as if at pleasant news, said: 'It is certain' —

children.text: rājyāccyute 'sminnaramāṃsalobhādunmādavaktavya ivāsvatantre /
children.translated_text: When this one has fallen from kingship due to his craving for human flesh, when he is to be spoken of as one deranged, bereft of self-control,

children.text: tyaktasvadharme hatapuṇyakīrtau śocyāṃ daśāmityanuvartamāne // Jm_31.6 //
children.translated_text: when he has abandoned his own <s>dharma</s> (duty), his merit and fame destroyed, and is following a pitiable course — || Jm 31.6 ||

children.text: ko vikramasyātra mamāvakāśa evaṃgatādvā bhayasaṃbhramasya /
children.translated_text: what occasion is there here for my valor, or for fear and panic at one who has come to such a state?

children.text: ayatnasaṃrambhaparākrameṇa pāpmānamasya prasabhaṃ nihanmi // Jm_31.7 //
children.translated_text: With effort, exertion, and prowess requiring no struggle, I shall forcibly slay the sin of this one. || Jm 31.7 ||

children.text: gatvāpi yo nāma mayānukampyo madgocaraṃ sa svayamabyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, having gone afar, was still an object of my compassion — he has come of his own accord within my reach;

children.text: yuktaṃ mayātithyamato 'sya kartumevaṃ hi santo 'tithiṣu pravṛttāḥ // Jm_31.8 //
children.translated_text: it is fitting, therefore, that I should offer him hospitality, for thus do the virtuous conduct themselves toward guests. || Jm 31.8 ||

body.text: tadyathādhikāramatrāvahitā bhavanti bhavantaḥ / iti sa tānantaḥ purāvacarānanuśiṣya viṣādavipulatarapāriplavākṣamāgadgadavilulitakaṅṭhaṃ mārgāvaraṇasodyamamāśvāsanapūrvakaṃ vinivartya yuvatijanaṃ yatastatkolāhalaṃ tataḥ prasasāra / dṛṣṭvaiva ca vyāyatābaddhamalinavasanaparikaraṃ valkalapaṭṭaviniyataṃ reṇuparuṣapralambavyākulaśiroruhe praruḍhaśmaśrujālāvanaddhāndhakāravadanaṃ roṣasaṃrambhavyāvṛttaraudranayanamudyatāsimacarmāṇaṃ saudāsaṃ vidravadanupatantaṃ rājabalaṃ vigatabhayasādhvasaḥ samājuhāva - ayamahamare sutasomaḥ / ita eva nivartasva / kimanena kṛpaṇajanakadanakaraṇaprasaṅgeneti / tatsamāhvānaśabdākalitadarpastu saudāsaḥ siṃha iva tato nyavartata / nirāvaraṇapraharaṇamekākinaṃ prakṛtisaumyadarśanamabhivīkṣya ca bodhisattvamahamapi tvāmeva mṛgayāmītyuktvā niviśaṅka sahasā saṃrambhadrutataramabhisṛtyainaṃ skandhamāropya pradudrāva / bodhisattvo 'pi cainaṃ saṃrambhadarpoddhatamānasaṃ sasaṃbhramākulitamatiṃ rājabalavidrāvaṇāduparūḍhapraharṣāvalepaṃ sābhiśaṅkamavetya nāyamasyānuśiṣṭikāla ityupekṣāṃcakre / saudāso 'pyabhimatārthaprasiddhyā paramiva lābhabhadhigamya pramuditamanāḥ svamāvāsadurgaṃ praviveśa /
body.translated_text: Therefore, let your honors be attentive here as befits your duties.' Having thus instructed the attendants of the inner palace, turning back the company of young women — whose eyes were all the more unsteady with dismay, whose throats were choked with sobs — who were striving to block his path, first consoling them, he proceeded toward the source of that tumult. And upon seeing <s>Saudāsa</s> — bound with a girdle of loose, soiled garments, wearing a strip of bark, his disheveled hair matted, rough with dust, and hanging low, his face obscured as if by darkness from a mass of overgrown beard, his fierce eyes rolling with rage and fury, holding aloft a sword and shield — pursuing the fleeing royal army, free from fear and alarm, he called out: 'Here I am, friend — I am <s>Sutasoma</s>! Turn back this way! What is the use of this business of slaughtering wretched people?' <s>Saudāsa</s>, his pride arrested by that call, turned back from there like a lion. And seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone, without weapon or armor, of naturally gentle appearance, he said, 'I am indeed seeking you,' and without hesitation, rushing forward suddenly with the swiftness of fury, he hoisted him upon his shoulder and ran off. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that his mind was agitated with the pride of fury, his wits flustered with haste, and his arrogance heightened by having routed the royal army, and regarding him with apprehension, thought, 'This is not the time for his instruction,' and exercised forbearance. <s>Saudāsa</s> too, as if having obtained the greatest gain through the attainment of his desired object, his mind delighted, entered his own fortress retreat.

children.text: hatapuruṣakalevarākulaṃ rudhirasamukṣitaraudrabhūtalam /
children.translated_text: Strewn with the corpses of slain men, its ground dreadful and besmeared with blood,

children.text: puruṣamiva ruṣāvabhartsayatsphuṭadahanairaśivaiḥ śivārutaiḥ // Jm_31.9 //
children.translated_text: as if threatening a man with anger — through the inauspicious howls of jackals, with fires blazing openly; || Jm 31.9 ||

body.text: gṛdhradhvāṅkṣādhyāsanarūkṣāruṇaparṇaiḥ kīrṇaṃ vṛkṣairnaikacitādhūmavivarṇaiḥ /
body.translated_text: covered with trees whose reddish-brown leaves were rough from the perching of vultures and crows, discolored by the smoke of many funeral pyres,

body.text: rakṣaḥpretānartanabibhatsamaśāntaṃ dūrād dṛṣṭaṃ trāsajaḍaiḥ sārthikanetraiḥ // Jm_31.10 //
body.translated_text: a place made horrifying by the dancing of <s>Rakṣas</s> and ghosts, and utterly desolate — seen from afar by the eyes of travelers, paralyzed with terror. || Jm 31.10 ||

body.text: samavatārya ca tatra bodhisattvaṃ tadrūpasaṃpadā vinibadhyamānanayanaḥ pratataṃ vīkṣamāṇo viśaśrāma / atha bodhisattvasya subhāṣitopāyanābhigataṃ brāhmaṇamakṛtasatkāraṃ tadudyānavinivartanapratīkṣiṇamāśāvabaddhahṛdayamanusmṛtya cintā prādurabhūt - kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Having set down the <s>Bodhisattva</s> there, his gaze held captive by the splendor of his form, he rested while gazing at him continually. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, remembering the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who had come with an offering of wise sayings (<s>subhāṣita</s>), to whom no hospitality had been shown, who was waiting for his return from the garden, his heart bound by hope, a thought arose: 'Alas!

children.text: ubhāṣitopāyanavānāśayā duramāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who came from afar with hope, bearing an offering of wise sayings —

children.text: sa maṃ hṛtamupaśrutya vipraḥ kiṃ nu kariṣyati // Jm_31.11 //
children.translated_text: having heard that I have been abducted, what will that twice-born one do? || Jm 31.11 ||

children.text: āśāvighātāgniparītacetā vaitānyatīvreṇa pariśrameṇa /
children.translated_text: His heart consumed by the fire of frustrated hope, and by the sharp pain of his journey's weariness,

children.text: viniśvasiṣyatyanuśocya vā māṃ svabhāgyanindāṃ pratipatsyate vā // Jm_31.12 //
children.translated_text: he will either sigh deeply while grieving for me, or he will resort to blaming his own fortune.' || Jm 31.12 ||

body.text: iti vicintayatastasya mahāsattvasya tadīyaduḥkhābhitaptamanasaḥ kāruṇyaparicayādaśrūṇi prāvartanta / atha saudāsaḥ sāśrūnayanamabhivīkṣya bodhisattvaṃ samabhiprahasannuvācamā tavadbhoḥ /
body.translated_text: As the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>) reflected thus, his mind scorched by the other's suffering, tears flowed from the force of habitual compassion. Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with tear-filled eyes, laughed mockingly and said: 'Enough now, sir!

children.text: dhīra ityasi vikhyātastaistaiśca bahubhirguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: You are renowned as steadfast, and for those many virtues of yours;

children.text: atha cāsmadvaśaṃ prāpya tvamapyaśrūṇi muñcasi // Jm_31.13 //
children.translated_text: yet, having fallen into my power, even you shed tears! || Jm 31.13 ||

body.text: suṣṭhu khalvidamucyate -
body.translated_text: Indeed, it is well said:

children.text: āpatsu viphalaṃ dhairyaṃ śoke śrutamapārthakam /
children.translated_text: In calamities, fortitude is useless; in sorrow, learning is of no avail;

children.text: na hi tadvidyate bhūtamāhataṃ yuanna kampate // Jm_31.14 //
children.translated_text: for there exists no being that, when struck, does not tremble.' || Jm 31.14 ||

body.text: iti / tatsatyaṃ tāvad brūhi -
body.translated_text: So then, tell me truly:

children.text: prāṇān priyānatha dhanaṃ sukhasādhanaṃ vā bandhūnnarādhipatitāmathavānuśocan /
children.translated_text: Is it your dear life that you mourn, or wealth — the means of happiness — or kinsmen, or sovereignty,

children.text: putrapriyaṃ pitaramaśrumukhān sutān vā smṛtveti sāśrūnayanatvamupāgato 'si // Jm_31.15 //
children.translated_text: or do you recall your father, dear to his sons, and your sons with tear-stained faces — is that why your eyes have become filled with tears?' || Jm 31.15 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: na prāṇān pitarau na caiva tanayān bandhūnna dārānna ca
children.translated_text: Not for my life, not for parents, not indeed for sons, not for kinsmen, nor for wife,

children.text: naivaiśvaryasukhāni saṃsmṛtavato bāṣpodgamo 'yaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: nor from remembering the pleasures of sovereignty does this surge of tears arise in me;

children.text: āśāvāṃstu subhāṣitairabhigataḥ śrutvā hṛtaṃ māṃ dvijo
children.translated_text: but a twice-born one came to me with hope, bearing wise sayings, and having heard that I was abducted,

children.text: nairāśyena sa dahyate dhruvamiti smṛtvāsmi sāsrekṣaṇaḥ // Jm_31.16 //
children.translated_text: he is surely being consumed by despair — remembering this, my eyes are filled with tears. || Jm 31.16 ||

children.text: tasmādvisarjayitumarhasi tasya yāvadāśāvighātamathitaṃ hṛdayaṃ dvijasya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, please release me, so that I may [relieve] the heart of that twice-born one, crushed by the frustration of his hope;

children.text: saṃmānanāmbupariṣekanavikaromi tasmātsubhāṣitamadhūni ca saṃbibharmi // Jm_31.17 //
children.translated_text: I shall sprinkle him with the water of honor, and I shall gather for him the nectar of wise sayings. || Jm 31.17 ||

children.text: prāpyaivamānṛṇyamahaṃ divjasya gantāsmi bhūyo 'nṛṇatāṃ tavāpi /
children.translated_text: Having thus discharged my debt to the twice-born one, I shall come again to discharge my debt to you as well,

children.text: ihāgamātprītikṛtakṣaṇābhyāṃ nirīkṣyamāṇo bhavadīkṣaṇābhyām // Jm_31.18 //
children.translated_text: being gazed upon by your eyes, through two moments — one of joy at my arrival, and one [of satisfaction at fulfilling my word]. || Jm 31.18 ||

children.text: mā cāpayātavyanayo 'yamasyetyevaṃ viśaṅkākulamānaso bhūḥ /
children.translated_text: And do not let your mind become agitated with suspicion, thinking "This one will not return — this would be his ruin."

children.text: anyo hi mārgo nṛpa madvidhānāmanyādṛśastvanyajanābhipannaḥ // Jm_31.19 //
children.translated_text: For the path of those like me is different, O king, and one of a different nature is differently disposed when others are in distress. || Jm 31.19 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

children.text: idaṃ tvayā hyādṛtamucyamānaṃ śraddheyatāṃ naiva kathaṃcideti /
children.translated_text: What you are saying with such earnestness does not in any way attain credibility;

children.text: ko nāma mṛtyorvadanādvimuktaḥ svasthaḥ sthitastatpunarabhyupeyām // Jm_31.20 //
children.translated_text: for who, having been released from the jaws of death, would calmly and of his own accord approach them again? || Jm 31.20 ||

children.text: duruttaraṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ vyatītya sukhe sthitaḥ śrīmati veśmani sve /
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond the fear of death, so hard to overcome, established in happiness, in your own splendid palace —

children.text: kiṃ nāma tatkāraṇamasti yena tvaṃ matsamīpaṃ punarabhyupeyāḥ // Jm_31.21 //
children.translated_text: what reason could there possibly be for which you would come back to my presence? || Jm 31.21 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - kathamevaṃ mahadapi mamāgamanakāraṇamatrabhavānnābabhudhyate? nanu mayā pratipannamāgamiṣyāmīti / tadalaṃ māṃ khalajanasamatayaivaṃ pariśaṅkitum / sutasomaḥ khalvaham /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'How is it that his honor does not perceive even so great a reason for my return? Did I not give my promise that I would come back? Therefore, do not suspect me as you would a dishonest person. I am <s>Sutasoma</s>!

children.text: lobhena mṛtyośca bhayena satyaṃ satyaṃ yadeke tṛṇavattyajanti /
children.translated_text: Out of greed and fear of death, some abandon truth — truth itself — as if it were a blade of grass;

children.text: satāṃ tu satyaṃ vasu jīvitaṃ ca kṛcchre 'pyatastanna parityajanti // Jm_31.22 //
children.translated_text: but for the virtuous, truth is [their] treasure and life itself — therefore, even in adversity, they do not abandon it. || Jm 31.22 ||

children.text: na jīvitaṃ yatsukhamaihikaṃ vā satyāccyutaṃ rakṣati durgatibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither life nor worldly happiness, when fallen from truth, protects one from evil destinies;

children.text: satyaṃ vijahyāditi kastadarthaṃ yaccākaraḥ stutiyaśaḥsukhānām // Jm_31.23 //
children.translated_text: who then, for the sake of that [life or happiness], would abandon truth — which is the cause of praise, fame, and happiness? || Jm 31.23 ||

children.text: saṃdṛśyamānavyabhicāramārge tvadṛṣṭakalyāṇaparākrame vā /
children.translated_text: When the path of transgression is clearly visible, or when the glorious prowess [of truth] is unseen,

children.text: śraddheyatāṃ naiti śubhaṃ tathā ca kiṃ vīkṣya śaṅkā tava mayyapīti // Jm_31.24 //
children.translated_text: virtue still does not lose its credibility — why then, seeing [my conduct], should there be suspicion toward me?' || Jm 31.24 ||

children.text: tvatto bhayaṃ yadi ca nāma mamābhaviṣyat saṅgaḥ sukheṣu karuṇāvikalaṃ mano vā /
children.translated_text: If I had had fear of you, or attachment to pleasures, or a mind weakened by compassion,

children.text: vikhyātaraudracaritaṃ nanu vīramānī tvāmudyatapraharaṇāvaraṇo 'bhyupaiṣyam // Jm_31.25 //
children.translated_text: would I not have approached you — who are famed for your dreadful deeds and pride yourself on valor — without weapon or shield? || Jm 31.25 ||

children.text: tvatsaṃstavastvayamabhīpsita eva me syāt tasya dvijasya saphalaśramatāṃ vidhāya /
children.translated_text: Your praise would indeed be my desired reward; having made the labor of that twice-born one fruitful,

children.text: eṣyāmyahaṃ punarapi svayamantikaṃ te nāsmadvidhā hi vitathāṃ giramudgiranti // Jm_31.26 //
children.translated_text: I shall come again of my own accord to your presence — for those like me do not utter a false word. || Jm 31.26 ||

body.text: atha saudāsastad bodhisattvavacanaṃ vikalpitamivāmṛṣyamāṇaścintāmāpede - suṣṭhu khalvayaṃ satyavāditayā ca dharmikatayā ca vikatthate / tatpaśyāmi tāvadasya satyānurāgaṃ dharmapriyatāṃ ca / kiṃ ca tāvanmamānena naṣṭenāpi syāt? asti hi me svabhujavīryapratāpādvaśīkṛtaṃ śatamātraṃ kṣatriyakumārāṇām / tairyathopayācitaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ kariṣyāmīti vicintya bodhisattvamuvāca - tena hi gaccha / drakṣyāmaste satyapratijñatāṃ dhārmikatāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, as though unable to tolerate the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> words being [merely] contrived, fell into thought: 'Truly, he boasts well of his truthfulness and righteousness. Let me then test his devotion to truth and his love of <s>dharma</s>. And besides, what loss would there be to me even if he is lost? For I have a hundred <s>Kṣatriya</s> princes already subdued by the prowess of my own arms. With them I shall perform the sacrifice to the spirits as promised.' Having reflected thus, he said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Then go. I shall observe your fidelity to your pledge and your righteousness.'

children.text: gatvā kṛtvā ca tasya tvaṃ dvijasya yadabhīpsitam /
children.translated_text: Having gone and done for that twice-born one what he desires,

children.text: śīghramāyāhi yāvatte citāṃ sajjīkaromyaham // Jm_31.27 //
children.translated_text: come back quickly, while I prepare the funeral pyre for you. || Jm 31.27 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvastathetyasmai pratiśrutya svabhavanamabhigataḥ pratinandyamānaḥ svena janena tamāhūya brāhmaṇaṃ tasmād gāthācatuṣṭayaṃ śuśrāva / tacchrutvā subhāṣitābhiprasāditamanāḥ sa mahāsattvaḥ saṃrādhayan priyavacanasatkārapuraḥsaraṃ sāhasrikīṃ gāthāṃ kṛtvā samabhilaṣitenārthena taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pratipūjayāmāsa / athainaṃ tasya pitā asthānātivyayanivāraṇodyatamatiḥ prastāvakramāgataṃ sānunayamityuvāca - tāta subhāṣitapratipūjane sādhu mātrāṃ jñātumarhasi / mahājanaḥ khalu te bhartavyaḥ, kośasaṃpadapekṣiṇī ca rājaśrīḥ / ataśca tvāṃ bravīmi -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having assented to him with 'So be it,' returned to his own palace. Welcomed by his own people, he summoned that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and listened to the four verses from him. Having heard them, that great being, his mind gladdened by the wise sayings (<s>subhāṣita</s>), gratifying [the Brahmin] with honor preceded by kind words and hospitality, reckoning each verse at a thousand, honored that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with the desired reward. Then his father, his mind set upon preventing such unseemly extravagance, spoke to him gently as the occasion arose, saying: 'Dear son, in honoring wise sayings you should know the proper measure. You have a great multitude to support, and royal splendor depends upon the fullness of the treasury. Therefore I say to you —'

children.text: śatena saṃpūjayituṃ subhāṣitaṃ paraṃ pramāṇaṃ na tataḥ paraṃ kṣamam /
children.translated_text: A hundred is the utmost limit for honoring a wise saying; beyond that is not fitting.

children.text: atipradāturhi kiyacciraṃ bhaveddhaneśvarasyāpi dhaneśvaradyutiḥ // Jm_31.28 //
children.translated_text: For how long can the splendor of the lord of wealth endure, if he gives excessively? || Jm 31.28 ||

body.text: samarthamarthaḥ paramaṃ hi sādhanaṃ na tadvirodhena yataścaretpriyam /
body.translated_text: Wealth is indeed the supreme instrument of accomplishment; one should not act in a manner contrary to it, however pleasing [the cause may be].

body.text: narādhipaṃ śrīrna hi kośasaṃpadā vivarjitaṃ veśavadhūrivekṣate // Jm_31.29 //
body.translated_text: For royal fortune does not regard a king lacking in treasury's fullness, just as a courtesan [does not regard a man without wealth]. || Jm 31.29 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: arghapramāṇaṃ yadi nāmaṃ kartuṃ śakyaṃ bhaveddeva subhāṣitānām /
children.translated_text: If it were possible, O lord, to set a price upon wise sayings,

children.text: vyaktaṃ na te vācyapathaṃ vrajeya tanniṣkrayaṃ rājyamapi prayacchan // Jm_31.30 //
children.translated_text: clearly even giving away one's kingdom would not reach the extent of their ransom. || Jm 31.30 ||

children.text: śrutvaiva yannāma manaḥ prasādaṃ śreyo 'nurāgaḥ sthiratāṃ ca yāti /
children.translated_text: That by merely hearing which the mind attains serenity, devotion to the good becomes firm,

children.text: prajñā vivṛddhyā vitamaskatāṃ ca krayyaṃ nanu syādapi tatsvamāṃsaiḥ // Jm_31.31 //
children.translated_text: and through the growth of wisdom, darkness is dispelled — would it not be worth purchasing even with one's own flesh? || Jm 31.31 ||

children.text: dīpaḥ śrutaṃ mohatamaḥpramāthī caurādyahāryaṃ paramaṃ dhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Sacred learning is a lamp that destroys the darkness of delusion, the supreme wealth that cannot be stolen by thieves and the like,

children.text: saṃmohaśatruvyathanāya śastraṃ nayopadeṣṭā paramaśca mantrī // Jm_31.32 //
children.translated_text: a weapon for striking down the enemy of bewilderment, and the supreme counselor who teaches right conduct. || Jm 31.32 ||

children.text: āpadgatasyāpyavikāri mitramapīḍanīśokarujaścikitsā /
children.translated_text: It is an unwavering friend even in times of adversity, a remedy for grief and sickness that causes no pain,

children.text: balaṃ mahaddoṣabalāvamardi paraṃ nidhānaṃ yaśasaḥ śriyaśca // Jm_31.33 //
children.translated_text: a great power that crushes the force of faults, and the supreme treasure of fame and prosperity. || Jm 31.33 ||

children.text: satsaṃgame prābhṛtaśībharasya sabhāsu vidvajjanarañjanasya /
children.translated_text: Of that [learning] which in the company of the good bears the weight of offerings, which in assemblies delights the learned,

children.text: parapravādadyutibhāskarasya spardhāvatāṃ kīrtimadāpahasya // Jm_31.34 //
children.translated_text: which like the sun outshines the brilliance of opponents' arguments, and which strips away the pride of rivals, || Jm 31.34 ||

children.text: prasannanetrānanavarṇarāgairasaṃskṛtairapyatiharṣalabdhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: whose surpassing excellence is made manifest by the clear eyes, radiant faces, and flushed complexions —

children.text: saṃrādnanavyagrakarāgradeśairvikhyāpyamānātiśayakramasya // Jm_31.35 //
children.translated_text: unfeigned, born of extreme delight — and by fingertips eagerly extended in applause, || Jm 31.35 ||

children.text: vispaṣṭahetvarthanidarśanasya vicitraśāstrāgamapeśalasya /
children.translated_text: which is clear in its reasoning, meaning, and illustrations, elegant through mastery of diverse scriptures and traditions,

children.text: mādhuryasaṃskāramanoharatvādakliṣṭamālyaprakaropamasya // Jm_31.36 //
children.translated_text: and which, through the charm of sweetness and refinement, is like a garland of unwilted flowers, || Jm 31.36 ||

children.text: vinītadīptapratibhojjvalasya prasahya kīrtipratibodhanasya /
children.translated_text: which blazes with disciplined and brilliant wit, and which forcefully awakens fame —

children.text: vāksauṣṭhavasyāpi viśeṣaheturyogātprasannārthagatiḥ śrutaśrīḥ // Jm_31.37 //
children.translated_text: even for one skilled in eloquent speech, the beauty of learning, with its lucid conveyance of meaning, is the special cause [of distinction] through [its proper] application. || Jm 31.37 ||

children.text: śrutvā ca vairodhikadoṣamuktaṃ trivagamārgaṃ samupāśrayante /
children.translated_text: And having heard it, people take refuge in the path of the triple goal (<s>trivarga</s>), freed from the faults of opposition,

children.text: śrutānusārapratipattisārāstarantyakṛcchreṇa ca janmadurgam // Jm_31.38 //
children.translated_text: and those whose essence is practice guided by what they have learned cross the perilous passage of rebirth without difficulty. || Jm 31.38 ||

children.text: guṇairanekairiti viśrutāni prāptānyahaṃ prābhṛtavacchrutāni /
children.translated_text: Thus, renowned for its many virtues, I have obtained these wise sayings as a gift;

children.text: śaktaḥ kathaṃ nāma na pūjayamājñāṃ kathaṃ vā tava laṅghayeyam // Jm_31.38 //
children.translated_text: how could I possibly fail to honor them, or how could I transgress your command? || Jm 31.39 ||

children.text: yāsyāmi saudāsasamīpamasmādartho na me rājyapariśrameṇa /
children.translated_text: I shall go from here to the presence of <s>Saudāsa</s> — I have no use for wealth obtained through the toil of kingship

children.text: nivṛttasaṃketaguṇopamarde labhyaśca yo doṣapathānuvṛttyā // Jm_31.40 //
children.translated_text: at the cost of destroying the merit of a fulfilled pledge, and which is obtainable only by following the path of vice. || Jm 31.40 ||

body.text: athainaṃ pitā snehātsamutpatitasaṃbhramaḥ sādaramuvāca - tavaiva khalu tāta hitāvekṣiṇā mayaivamabhihitam / tadalamatra te manyuvaśamanubhavitum / dviṣantaste saudāsavarśaṃ gamiṣyanti / athāpi pratijñātaṃ tvayā tatsamīpopagamanam, ataḥ satyānurakṣī tatsaṃpādayitumicchasi, tadapi te nāhamanujñāsyāmi / apātakaṃ hi svaprāṇaparirakṣānimittaṃ gurujanārthaṃ cānṛtamārgo vedavihita iti / tatparihāraśrameṇa tava ko 'rthaḥ? arthakāmābhyāṃ ca virodhidṛṣṭaṃ dharmasaṃśrayamanayamiti vyasanamiti ca rājñāṃ pracakṣate nītikuśalāḥ / tadalamanenāsmanmanastāpinā svārthanirapekṣeṇa te nirbandhena / athāpyayaśasyaṃ mārṣa dharmavirodhi ceti pratijñāvisaṃvādanamanucitatvānna vyavasyati te matiḥ, evamapīdaṃ tvadvimokṣaṇārthaṃ samudyaktaṃ sajjameva no hastyaśvarathapattikāyaṃ saṃpannamanuraktaṃ kṛtāstraśūrapuruṣamanekasamaranīrājitaṃ mahanmahaughabhīmaṃ balam / tadanena parivṛtaḥ samabhigamyainaṃ vaśamānaya, antakavaśaṃ vā prāpaya / evamavyarthapratijñatā saṃpāditā syādātmarakṣā ceti / bodhisattva uvāca - notsahe deva anyathā pratijñātumanyathā kartuṃ śocyeṣu vā vyasanapaṅkanimagneṣu narakābhimukheṣu suhṛtsu svajanapartiyakteṣvanātheṣu ca tadvidheṣu prahartum /
body.translated_text: Then his father, agitation arising from affection, said to him earnestly: 'It was out of concern for your welfare, dear son, that I spoke thus. So do not give way to anger over this. Your enemies shall go to <s>Saudāsa</s>'s abode [in your stead]. But if you wish to fulfill your promised visit to his presence because you are a guardian of truth, even that I shall not permit. For the path of untruth is prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> for the blameless purpose of protecting one's own life and for the sake of one's elders. So what use is the effort of fulfilling [that promise] to you? And those skilled in statecraft declare that adherence to <s>dharma</s> when it conflicts with wealth and pleasure is a calamity and ruin for kings. So enough of this obstinacy of yours that torments our minds and disregards your own interest. But if your mind does not resolve upon breaking your promise, considering it disgraceful and contrary to <s>dharma</s>, then even so — this army of ours, assembled for the purpose of freeing you, stands ready: a force of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, well-equipped, loyal, consisting of warriors skilled in arms and proven in many battles, vast and terrible as a great flood. Surrounded by this force, go to him and bring him under your power, or send him to the domain of death. Thus your promise will be kept without being rendered futile, and your own safety will be secured.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I cannot, O lord, promise one thing and do another, nor can I strike at those who are pitiable, sunk in the mire of calamity, headed toward the hells, abandoned by their own people, and thus helpless.'

body.text: api ca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: dukṣaraṃ puruṣādo 'sāvudāraṃ cākaronmayi /
children.translated_text: That man-eater did something difficult and noble toward me,

children.text: madvacaḥpratyayādyo māṃ vyasṛjadvaśamāgatam // Jm_31.41 //
children.translated_text: in that he released me, who had come into his power, trusting in my word. || Jm 31.41 ||

children.text: labdhaṃ tatkāraṇāccedaṃ mayā tāta subhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: If, dear father, I obtained these wise sayings because of him,

children.text: upakārī viśeṣeṇa so 'nukampyo mayā yataḥ // Jm_31.42 //
children.translated_text: then he is all the more deserving of my compassion, since he was my benefactor. || Jm 31.42 ||

body.text: alaṃ cātra devasya madatyayāśaṅkayā / kā hi tasya śaktirasti māmevamabhigataṃ vihiṃsitumiti / evamanunīya ca mahatmā pitaraṃ vinivāraṇasodyamaṃ ca vinivartya praṇayyijanamanuraktaṃ ca balakāyamekākī vigatabhayadainayaḥ satyānurakṣī lokahitārthaṃ saudāsamabhivineṣyaṃstanniketamabhijagāma /
body.translated_text: And let the lord have no anxiety about my perishing, for what power has he to harm me when I come to him thus?' Having thus reassured his father, the great soul turned aside the effort to restrain him, and bidding farewell to his devoted people and the loyal army, alone, free from fear and dejection, as a guardian of truth, for the welfare of the world, intending to guide <s>Saudāsa</s>, he went to his dwelling place.

body.text: dūrādevāvalokya saudāsastaṃ mahāsattvamativismayādabhivṛddhabahumānaprasādaścirābhyāsavirūḍhakruratāmalinamatirapi vyaktamiti cintāmāpede - ahahahaha
body.translated_text: Beholding that great being from afar, <s>Saudāsa</s>, his esteem and favor greatly increased by extreme astonishment, though his mind was stained by cruelty grown through long habit, clearly fell into this reflection: 'Ah, ah, ah, ah!

children.text: āścaryāṇāṃ batāścaryamadbhutānāṃ tathādbhatam /
children.translated_text: A marvel among marvels indeed! A wonder among wonders!

children.text: satyaudāryaṃ nṛpasyedamatimānuṣadaivatam // Jm_31.43 //
children.translated_text: This truthfulness and nobility of the king is beyond the human, it is divine! || Jm 31.43 ||

children.text: mṛtyuraudrasvabhāvaṃ māṃ vinītabhayasaṃbhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: To me, whose nature is terrible as death itself, he has come of his own accord, free from fear and alarm —

children.text: iti svayamupeto 'yaṃ hī dhairyaṃ sādhu satyatā // Jm_31.44 //
children.translated_text: truly, courage is [well joined with] truthfulness! || Jm 31.44 ||

children.text: sthāne khalvasya vikhyātaṃ satyavāditayā yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is fitting indeed that his fame is celebrated for truthfulness,

children.text: iti prāṇān svarājyaṃ ca satyārthaṃ yo 'yamatyajat // Jm_31.45 //
children.translated_text: for he has abandoned his life and his own kingdom for the sake of truth. || Jm 31.45 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ samabhigamyainaṃ vismayabahumānāvarjitamānasamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having approached him whose mind was won over by astonishment and admiration, said:

children.text: prāptaṃ subhāṣitadhanaṃ pratipūjito 'rthī prītiṃ manaśca gamitaṃ bhavataḥ prabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: 'The wealth of wise sayings has been obtained, the supplicant has been honored, and joy and contentment have been attained through your grace.

children.text: prāptastadasmyayamaśāna yathepsitaṃ māṃ yajñāya vā mama paśuvratamādiśa tvam // Jm_31.46 //
children.translated_text: I have therefore come, O eater of raw flesh — dispose of me as you wish, whether for your feast or as a sacrificial victim for your rite.' || Jm 31.46 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

children.text: nātyeti kālo mama khādituṃ tvāṃ dhūmākulā tāvadiyaṃ citāpi /
children.translated_text: 'The time to devour you has not yet passed — this funeral pyre is still smoking.',

children.text: vidhūmapakvaṃ viśitaṃ ca hṛdyaṃ śṛṇmastadetāni subhāṣitāni // Jm_31.47 //
children.translated_text: 'When the [meat] is cooked without smoke and the flesh is tender, [I shall eat] — but [meanwhile] let us hear these wise sayings.' || Jm 31.47 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca kastavārtha itthaṃgatasya subhāṣitaśravanena?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'What use is listening to wise sayings for one in such a state as yours?

children.text: imāmavasthāmudarasya hetoḥ prāpto 'si saṃtyaktaghṛṇaḥ prajāsu /
children.translated_text: You have reached this condition for the sake of your belly, having cast off compassion toward your subjects;

children.text: imāśca dharmaṃ pravadanti gāthāḥ sametyadharmeṇa yato na dharmaḥ // Jm_31.48 //
children.translated_text: and these verses proclaim <s>dharma</s> — since there is no <s>dharma</s> through <s>adharma</s>.' || Jm 31.48 ||

children.text: rakṣovikṛtavṛttasya saṃtyaktāryapathasya te /
children.translated_text: For one of demonic and corrupt conduct, who has abandoned the path of the noble,

children.text: nāṣti satyaṃ kuto dharmaḥ kiṃ śrutena kariṣyasi // Jm_31.49 //
children.translated_text: there is no truth — whence then <s>dharma</s>? What will you do with learning? || Jm 31.49 ||

body.text: atha saudāsastāmavasādanāmamṛṣyamāṇaḥ pratyuvāca - mā tāvadbhoḥ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, unable to bear that reproach, replied: 'Wait, sir!

children.text: ko 'sau nṛpaḥ kathaya yo na samudyatāstraḥ krīḍāvane vanamṛgīdayitānnihanti /
children.translated_text: Tell me, what king is there who, with weapons drawn in his pleasure garden, does not slay the wild deer, the darlings of the forest?

children.text: tdvannihanmi manujān yadi vṛttihetorādharmikaḥ kila tato 'smi na te mṛgaghnāḥ // Jm_31.50 //
children.translated_text: If I likewise kill humans for the sake of my sustenance, am I then sinful while those deer-slayers are not?' || Jm 31.50 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: dharme sthitā na khalu te 'pi namanti yeṣāṃ bhītadruteṣvapi mṛgeṣu śarāsanāni /
children.translated_text: 'Even they do not stand in <s>dharma</s>, those whose bows bend upon fleeing, terrified deer;

children.text: tebhyo 'pi nindyatama eva narāśanastu jātyucchritā hi puruṣā na ca bhakṣaṇīyāḥ // Jm_31.51 //
children.translated_text: but a man-eater is even more contemptible than they, for humans are of exalted birth and are not fit to be eaten.' || Jm 31.51 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ parikarkaśākṣaramapyabhidhīyamāno bodhisattvena tanmaitrīguṇaprabhāvādabhibhūtaraudrasvabhāvaḥ sukhāyamāna eva tadvacanamabhiprahasannuvāca - bhoḥ sutasoma
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, though addressed with rather harsh words by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his fierce nature subdued by the power of the latter's benevolence (<s>maitrī</s>), feeling pleased, said with a smile: 'O <s>Sutasoma</s>!

children.text: mukto mayā nāma sametya gehaṃ samantato rājyavibhūtiramyam /
children.translated_text: Released by me, having returned home to the splendor of your kingdom, resplendent on every side,

children.text: yanmatsamīpaṃ punarāgatastvaṃ na nītimārge kuśalo 'si tasmāt // Jm_31.52 //
children.translated_text: that you have come back to my presence — you are therefore not skilled in the ways of statecraft.' || Jm 31.52 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - naitadasti / ahameva tu kuśalo nītimārge yadenaṃ na pratipattumicchāmi /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'That is not so. It is I who am skilled in the ways of statecraft, in that I do not wish to follow that [path].

children.text: yaṃ nāma pratipannasya dharmādaikāntikī cyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: That [path] which, once undertaken, leads exclusively to a fall from <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: na tu prasiddhiḥ saukhyasya tatra kiṃ nāma kauśalam // Jm_31.53 //
children.translated_text: and which does not lead to the attainment of happiness — what skill is there in that?' || Jm 31.53 ||

body.text: kiṃ ca bhūyaḥ,
body.translated_text: Furthermore,

children.text: ye nītimārgapratipattidhīrāḥ prāyeṇa te pretya patantyapāyān /
children.translated_text: those who are resolute in following the ways of statecraft mostly fall into evil destinies after death;

children.text: apāsya jihmāniti nītimārgān satyānurakṣī punarāgato 'smi // Jm_31.54 //
children.translated_text: having cast aside those crooked ways of statecraft, I have returned as a guardian of truth. || Jm 31.54 ||

children.text: ataśca nītau kuśalo 'hameva tyaktvānṛtaṃ yo 'bhirato 'smi satye /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is I who am skilled in statecraft, who have abandoned falsehood and delight in truth;

children.text: na tatsunītaṃ hi vadanti rajjñā yannānubadhnanti yaśaḥsukhārthāḥ // Jm_31.55 //
children.translated_text: for they say that is not good governance for a king which does not secure fame, happiness, and prosperity. || Jm 31.55 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

body.text: prāṇān priyān svajanamaśrumukhaṃ ca hitvā rājyāśrayāṇi ca sukhāni mahoharāṇi /
body.translated_text: 'Having abandoned your dear life, your own people with tearful faces, and the great and splendid pleasures attendant upon kingship,

body.text: kāmarthasiddhimanupaśyasi satyavākye tadrakṣaṇārthamapi māṃ yadupāgato 'si // Jm_31.56 //
body.translated_text: you see the fulfillment of desire and purpose in truthful speech — since you have come to me for the sake of protecting it.' || Jm 31.56 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - bahavaḥ satyavacanāśrayā guṇātiśayāḥ / saṃkṣepastu śrūyatām -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Many are the surpassing virtues that rest upon truthful speech. Hear them in brief:

children.text: malyaśriyaṃ hṛdyatayātiśete sarvān rasān svādutayā ca satyam /
children.translated_text: Truth surpasses the beauty of garlands by its agreeableness, and all flavors by its sweetness;

children.text: śramādṛte puṇyaguṇaprasiddhyā tapāṃsi tīrthābhigamaśramāṃśca // Jm_31.57 //
children.translated_text: without effort it surpasses austerities and the toils of pilgrimage in establishing the glory of merit. || Jm 31.57 ||

children.text: kīrterjagadvyāptikṛtakṣaṇāyā mārgastrilokākramaṇāya satyam /
children.translated_text: Truth is the path for fame that pervades the world in an instant, for traversing the three worlds,

children.text: dvāraṃ praveśāya surālayasya saṃsāradurgottaraṇāya setuḥ // Jm_31.58 //
children.translated_text: the gateway to entering the abode of the gods, and the bridge for crossing the perilous passage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). || Jm 31.58 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ sādhu yuktamityabhipraṇamyainaṃ savismayamabhivīkṣamāṇaḥ punaruvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, saying 'Well and rightly spoken,' bowed to him, and gazing at him with wonder, said again:

children.text: anye na rā madvaśagā bhavanti dainyārpaṇāttrāsaviluptadhairyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Others who come under my power become devoid of courage, their firmness shattered by the surrender of wretchedness;

children.text: saṃtyajyase tvaṃ tu na dhairyalakṣmyā manye na te mṛtyubhayaṃ narendra // Jm_31.59 //
children.translated_text: but you are not forsaken by the grace of fortitude — I think you have no fear of death, O lord of men.' || Jm 31.59 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: mahatāpi prayatnena yacchaktyaṃ nātivartitum /
children.translated_text: 'That which cannot be overcome even by the greatest effort,

children.text: pratīkārāsamarthena bhayaklaibyena tatra kim // Jm_31.60 //
children.translated_text: of what use is the cowardice of fear when one is powerless to avert it?' || Jm 31.60 ||

body.text: iti parigaṇitalokasthitayo 'pi tu kāpuruṣāḥ
body.translated_text: Even those who have reckoned the ways of the world, yet are cowards,

children.text: pāpaprasaṅgādanutapyamānāḥ śubheṣu karmasvakṛtaśramaśca /
children.translated_text: tormented by remorse over their involvement with sin, and having made no effort in meritorious deeds,

children.text: āśaṅkamānāḥ paralokaduḥkhaṃ martavyasaṃtrāsajaḍā bhavanti // Jm_31.61 //
children.translated_text: fearing the suffering of the next world, become paralyzed with the terror of death. || Jm 31.61 ||

children.text: tadeva kartuṃ na tu saṃsmarāmi bhavedyato me manaso 'nutāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: But I do not recall having done anything on account of which my mind would feel remorse;

children.text: sātmīkṛtaṃ karma ca śuklamasmāddharmasthitaḥ ko maraṇādvibhīyāt // Jm_31.62 //
children.translated_text: and since virtuous <s>karma</s> has become my very nature, why would one established in <s>dharma</s> tremble at death? || Jm 31.62 ||

body.text: na ca smarāmyarthijanopayānaṃ yanna praharṣāya mamārthināṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Nor do I recall any approach of a supplicant that did not bring delight to me or to those in need;

body.text: iti pradānaiḥ samavāptatuṣṭirdharme sthitaḥ ko maraṇādbibhīyāt // Jm_31.63 //
body.translated_text: thus, having attained contentment through generosity, why would one established in <s>dharma</s> fear death? || Jm 31.63 ||

children.text: ciraṃ vicintyāpi ca naiva pāpe manaḥpadanyāsamapi smarāmi /
children.translated_text: And even after long reflection, I do not recall even a step of my mind toward evil;

children.text: viśodhitasvargapatho 'hamevaṃ mṛtyoḥ kimarthaṃ bhayamabhyupeyām // Jm_31.64 //
children.translated_text: having thus purified the path to heaven, why should I approach fear of death? || Jm 31.64 ||

children.text: vipreṣu bandhuṣu suhṛtsu samāṣriteṣu dīne jane yadiṣu cāśramabhūṣaṇeṣu /
children.translated_text: Toward <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kinsmen, friends, dependents, the wretched, and toward ascetics who are the ornaments of the hermitages —

children.text: nyastaṃ mayā bahu dhanaṃ dadatā yathārhaṃ kṛtyaṃ ca yasya yadabhūttadakāri tasya // Jm_31.65 //
children.translated_text: Much wealth was laid aside by me while giving as was fitting, and whatever duty was owed to whomever — that I performed for them. || Jm 31.65 ||

body.text: śrīmanti kīrtanaśatāni niveśitāni / satrājirāśramapadāni sabhāḥ prapāśca /

children.text: mṛtyorna me bhayamatastadavāptatuṣṭeryajñāya tatsamupaklpaya bhauṅkṣva vā mām // Jm_31.66 //
children.translated_text: I have no fear of death, and therefore, being one who has attained contentment, prepare me as an offering for the sacrifice, or simply devour me. || Jm 31.66 ||

body.translated_text: Glorious hundreds of charitable foundations were established — sacrificial grounds, hermitage sites, assembly halls, and watering stations;

body.text: tadupaśrutya saudāsaḥ prasādāśruvyāptanayanaḥ samudbhiyamānaromāñcapiṭako vismṛtapāpasvabhāvatāmisraḥ sabahumānamavekṣya bodhisattvamuvāca - śāntaṃ pāpam /
body.translated_text: Having heard that, <s>Saudāsa</s>, his eyes brimming with tears of faith, his body breaking out in goosebumps, the darkness of his evil nature forgotten, gazed upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with great respect and said: 'May evil be averted!'

children.text: adyādviṣaṃ sa khalu hāhahalaṃ prajānannāśīviṣaṃ prakupitaṃ jvaladāyasaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Indeed, from today onward, he who knowingly consumes poison, or provokes a venomous serpent, or handles burning iron —

children.text: mūrdhāpi tasya śatadhā hṛdayaṃ ca yāyād yastvadvidhasya nṛpapuṃgava pāpamicchet // Jm_31.67 //
children.translated_text: even his head would split into a hundred pieces and his heart would burst, if he should wish evil upon one such as you, O bull among kings! || Jm 31.67 ||

body.text: tadarhati bhavāṃstānyapi me subhāṣitāni vaktum / anena hi te vacanakusumavarṣeṇābhiprasāditamanasaḥ suṣṭutaramabhivṛddhaṃ ca teṣu me kautūhalam / api ca bhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, may Your Honor deign to recite those well-spoken verses to me as well. For through this shower of flowers that are your words, my mind has been greatly gladdened, and my curiosity regarding those [verses] has grown even more. Moreover, sir:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā me caritacchāyāvairūpyaṃ dharmadarpaṇe /
children.translated_text: Having seen in the mirror of <s>Dharma</s> the ugliness — the shadow of my past conduct —

children.text: api nāmāgatāvegaṃ syanme dharmotsukaṃ manaḥ // Jm_31.68 //
children.translated_text: may my mind, stirred with urgency, perhaps become eager for <s>Dharma</s>! || Jm 31.68 ||

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ patrīkṛtāśayaṃ dharmaśravaṇapravaṇamānasamavetyovāca - tena hi dharmārthinā tadanurūpasamudācārasauṣṭhavena dharmaḥ śrotuṃ yuktam / paśya /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving that his mind had become a vessel ready for <s>Dharma</s>-hearing, said: 'Then, as one who seeks <s>Dharma</s>, it is proper to hear <s>Dharma</s> with the grace of conduct befitting that [aspiration]. Observe:'

children.text: nīcaistarāsanasthānadvibodhya vinayaśriyam /
children.translated_text: Seated low upon one's seat, having awakened the beauty of discipline,

children.text: prītyarpitābhyāṃ cakṣurbhyāṃ vāṅmadhvāsvādayannivi // Jm_31.69 //
children.translated_text: with eyes offered in devotion, savoring the honey of the words — || Jm 31.69 ||

children.text: gauravāvarjitaikāgraprasannāmalamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: with a mind one-pointedly attentive, clear and pure, drawn by reverence,

children.text: satkṛtya dharmaṃ śṛṇuyādbhiṣagvākyamivāturaḥ // Jm_31.70 //
children.translated_text: one should hear the <s>Dharma</s> with respect — as a sick person [listens to] the words of a physician. || Jm 31.70 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ svenottarīyeṇa samāstīryoccaistaraṃ śilātalaṃ tatra cādhiropya bodhisattvaṃ svayamanāstaritāyamupaviśya bhūmau bodhisattvasya purastādānanodvīkṣaṇavyāpṛtanirīkṣaṇarataṃ mahāsattvamuvāca - brūhīdānīṃ mārṣeti / atha bodhisattvo navāmbhodharaninadamadhureṇa gambhīreṇāpūrayanniva tadvanaṃ vyāpinā svareṇovāca /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, having spread his own upper garment upon a high stone slab and having seated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> upon it, himself sat down on the bare ground before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gazing intently upward at his face, and said to the great being: 'Speak now, noble sir.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, filling that forest, as it were, with his deep voice, sweet as the rumbling of a fresh rain cloud, pervading all directions, said:

children.text: yadṛcchayāpyupānītaṃ sakṛtsajjanasaṃgatam /
children.translated_text: Even a single encounter with the virtuous, brought about by chance,

children.text: bhavatyacalamatyantaṃ nābhyāsakramamīkṣate // Jm_31.71 //
children.translated_text: becomes unshakeable and everlasting — it does not depend on the course of repeated practice. || Jm 31.71 ||

body.text: tadupaśrutya saudāsaḥ sādhu sādhviti svaśiraḥ prakampyāṅgalīvīkṣepaṃ bodhisattvamuvāca - tatastataḥ?
body.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Saudāsa</s>, nodding his head [and saying] 'Excellent, excellent!' and snapping his fingers, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Then what next?'

body.text: atha bodhisattvo dvitīyāṃ gāthāmudājahāra -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> uttered the second verse:

children.text: na sajjanād duracaraḥ kvacidbhavedbhajeta sādhūn vinayakramānugaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who associates with the virtuous, following the course of discipline, would never become evil-doer anywhere;

children.text: spṛśantyayatnena hi tatsamīpagaṃ visarpiṇastadguṇapuṣpareṇavaḥ // Jm_31.72 //
children.translated_text: for the spreading pollen-dust of their virtuous qualities effortlessly touches one who dwells near them. || Jm 31.72 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

children.text: subhāṣitānyarcayatā sādho sarvātmanā tvayā /
children.translated_text: O virtuous one, by honoring well-spoken words with your whole being,

children.text: sthāne khalu niyukto 'rthaḥ sthāne nāvekṣitaḥ śramaḥ // Jm_31.73 //
children.translated_text: your purpose is rightly fulfilled, and your toil is rightly disregarded. || Jm 31.73 ||

body.text: tatastataḥ? bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: 'Then what next?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: rathā nṛpāṇāṃ maṇihemabhūṣaṇā vrajanti dehāśca jarāvirūpatām /
children.translated_text: The chariots of kings, adorned with jewels and gold, fall into ruin, and bodies too [succumb to] the disfigurement of old age;

children.text: satāṃ tu dharmaṃ na jarābhivartate sthirānurāgā hi guṇeṣu sādhavaḥ // Jm_31.74 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>Dharma</s> of the virtuous is never overtaken by old age, for the good are steadfast in their devotion to virtues. || Jm 31.74 ||

body.text: amṛtavarṣaṃ khalvidam / aho saṃtarpitāḥ smaḥ / tatastataḥ? bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: 'This is truly a shower of nectar! Ah, we are satiated!' 'Then what next?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: nabhaśca dure vasudhātalācca pārādavāraṃ ca mahārṇavasya /
children.translated_text: The sky is far from the surface of the earth, and the far shore is distant from the near shore of the great ocean,

children.text: astācalendrādudayastato 'pi dharmaḥ satāṃ dūratare 'satāṃ ca // Jm_31.75 //
children.translated_text: and the place of rising from the mountain where the sun sets — yet the <s>Dharma</s> of the virtuous is even farther from that of the wicked. || Jm 31.75 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ prasādavismayābhyāmāvarjitapremabahumāno bodhisattvamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, his affection and respect won over by faith and wonder, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

body.text: citrābhidhānātiśayojjvalārthā gāthāstvadetā madhurā niśamya /
body.translated_text: Having heard these sweet verses, resplendent with marvelous expression and brilliant meaning,

body.text: ānanditastatpratipūjanārthaṃ varānahaṃ te caturo dadāmi // Jm_31.76 //
body.translated_text: I, delighted, grant you four boons in return for honoring them. || Jm 31.76 ||

body.text: tad vṛṇīṣva yadyanmatto 'bhikāṅkṣasīti /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore choose whatever you desire from me.'

body.text: athainaṃ bodhisattvaḥ savismayabahumāna uvāca kastvaṃ varapradānasya?
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with wonder and respect, said to him: 'Who are you to grant boons?'

children.text: yasyāsti nātmanayapi te prabhutvamakāryasaṃrāgaparājitasya /
children.translated_text: You who have no mastery even over yourself, defeated by your passion for wrongdoing —

children.text: sa tvaṃ varaṃ dāsyasi kaṃ parasmai śubhapravṛterapavṛttabhāvaḥ // Jm_31.77 //
children.translated_text: what boon will you, who have turned away from virtuous conduct, give to another? || Jm 31.77 ||

children.text: ahaṃ ca dehīti varaṃ vadeyaṃ manaśca ditsāthiśilaṃ tava syāt /
children.translated_text: And should I say 'Give!' as a boon, and should your mind then be inclined to generosity,

children.text: tamatyayaṃ kaḥ saghṛṇo 'bhyupeyādetāvadevālamalaṃ yato naḥ // Jm_31.78 //
children.translated_text: who that is compassionate would accept that transgression? This much alone suffices for us. || Jm 31.78 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ kiṃcid vrīḍāvanatavadano bodhisattvamuvāca - alamatrabhavato māmevaṃ viśaṅkitum /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, his face somewhat downcast with shame, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Let Your Honor not be so suspicious of me.'

children.text: prāṇānapi parityajya dāsyāmyetānahaṃ varān /
children.translated_text: Even at the cost of my life, I shall grant these boons;

children.text: visrabdhaṃ tad vṛṇīṣva tvaṃ yadyādicchasi bhūmipa // Jm_31.79 //
children.translated_text: therefore choose freely whatever you wish, O lord of the earth. || Jm 31.79 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - tena hi
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Then so be it —'

children.text: satyavarato bhava visarjaya sattvahiṃsāṃ bandīkṛtaṃ janamaśeṣamimaṃ vimuñca /
children.translated_text: Be devoted to truth, abandon the harming of beings, release all these people who have been made captive,

children.text: adyā na caiva naravīra manuṣyamāṃsametān varānanavarāṃścaturaḥ prayaccha // Jm_31.80 //
children.translated_text: and from this day forth, O hero among men, do not [eat] human flesh — grant these four peerless boons. || Jm 31.80 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

children.text: dadāmi pūrvān bhavate varāṃstrīnanyaṃ caturthaṃ tu varaṃ vṛṇīṣva /
children.translated_text: I grant you the first three boons; but choose another as the fourth boon —

children.text: avaiṣi kiṃ na tvamidaṃ yathāhamīśo virantuṃ na manuṣyamāṃsāt // Jm_31.81 //
children.translated_text: do you not know that I am unable to abstain from human flesh? || Jm 31.81 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - hanta tavaitatsaṃvṛttam / nanūktaṃ mayā kastvaṃ varapradānasyeti? api ca bhoḥ?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Alas, this is how it has turned out! Did I not say: Who are you to grant boons? Moreover, sir:'

children.text: satyavratatvaṃ ca kathaṃ syadahiṃsakatā ca te /
children.translated_text: How can there be truthfulness and non-violence for you,

children.text: aparityajato rājan manuṣyapaiśitāśitām // Jm_31.82 //
children.translated_text: O king, if you do not relinquish the eating of human flesh? || Jm 31.82 ||

body.text: āha -
body.translated_text: He (<s>Saudāsa</s>) said:

children.text: nanūktaṃ bhavatā pūrvaṃ dāsyāmyetānahaṃ varān /
children.translated_text: Did you not yourself say earlier, 'I shall grant these boons,

children.text: prāṇānapi parityajya tadidaṃ jāyate 'nyathā // Jm_31.83 //
children.translated_text: even at the cost of my life' — yet now this turns out otherwise? || Jm 31.83 ||

children.text: ahiṃsakatvaṃ ca kuto māṃsārthaṃ te ghnato narān /
children.translated_text: And where is non-violence when you slay men for their flesh?

children.text: satyevaṃ katame dattā bhavatā syurvarāstrayaḥ // Jm_31.84 //
children.translated_text: If this is the truth, which three boons have you [actually] granted? || Jm 31.84 ||

body.text: saudāsa uvāca -
body.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> said:

children.text: tyaktvā rājyaṃ vane kleśo yasya heturtādhṛto mayā /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned my kingdom, I have endured hardship in the forest for the sake of this [craving];

children.text: hato dharmaḥ kṣatā kīrtistyakṣyāmi tadahaṃ katham // Jm_31.85 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is destroyed, fame is ruined — how then shall I give that up? || Jm 31.85 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca - ata eva tadbhavāṃstyaktumarhati /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'For that very reason Your Honor ought to abandon it.'

children.text: dharmādarthātsukhātkīrtebhraṣṭo yasya kṛte bhavān /
children.translated_text: That on account of which you have been bereft of <s>Dharma</s>, of wealth, of happiness, and of fame —

children.text: anarthāyatanaṃ tādṛkkathaṃ na tyaktumarhasi // Jm_31.86 //
children.translated_text: such an abode of calamity, how can you not deserve to abandon it? || Jm 31.86 ||

children.text: dattānuśayitā ceyamanaudāryahate jane /
children.translated_text: And this regret after giving — unworthy of a noble person —

children.text: nīcata sā kathaṃ nāma tvāmapyabhibhavediti // Jm_31.87 //
children.translated_text: how could such baseness overpower even you? || Jm 31.87 ||

body.text: tadalaṃ te pāpmānamevānubhrāmitum / avaboddhumarhasyātmānam / saudāsaḥ khalvatrabhavān /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, enough of following sin! You should recognize yourself. Your Honor is indeed <s>Saudāsa</s>.'

children.text: vaidyekṣitāni kuśalairupakalpitāni grāmyāṇyanūpajalajānyatha jāṅgalāni /
children.translated_text: Meats examined by physicians, prepared by the skilled — domestic, marshy, aquatic, and also those from arid regions —

children.text: māṃsāni santi kuru tairhṛdayasya tuṣṭiṃ nindāvahādvirama sādhu manuṣyamāṃsāt // Jm_31.88 //
children.translated_text: these meats exist; satisfy your heart with them, and desist, good sir, from the blame-bringing [practice of eating] human flesh. || Jm 31.88 ||

children.text: tūryasvanāna sajalatoyadanādadhīrān gītasvanaṃ ca niśi rājyasukhaṃ ca tattat /
children.translated_text: The sounds of musical instruments, deep as the rumble of rain-laden clouds, the sound of singing, and all those various royal pleasures,

children.text: bandhūn sutān parijanaṃ ca manonukūlaṃ hitvā kathaṃ nu ramase 'tra vane vivikte // Jm_31.89 //
children.translated_text: your kinsmen, sons, and agreeable retinue — having abandoned all these, how can you delight in this solitary forest? || Jm 31.89 ||

children.text: cittasya nārhasi narendra vaśena gantuṃ dharmārthayoranuparodhapathaṃ bhajasva /
children.translated_text: O lord of men, you should not go at the bidding of your mind; follow the path that does not obstruct <s>Dharma</s> and prosperity.

children.text: eṃko nṛpān yudhi vijitya samastasainyān mā cittavigrahavidhau parikātaro bhūḥ // Jm_31.80 //
children.translated_text: You who alone in battle have conquered kings with their entire armies — do not be anxious in the battle against your own mind! || Jm 31.80 ||

children.text: lokaḥ paro 'pi manujādhipa nanvavekṣyastasmātpriyaṃ yadahitaṃ ca na tanniṣevyam /
children.translated_text: The next world too, O lord of men, must surely be considered; therefore what is pleasant but harmful should not be pursued;

children.text: yatsyāttu kīrtyanuparodhi manojñamārgaṃ tadvipriyaṃ sadapi bheṣajavadbhajasva // Jm_31.91 //
children.translated_text: but what would preserve fame and follow the path pleasing [to the virtuous] — that, even if unpleasant, should be embraced like medicine. || Jm 31.91 ||

body.text: atha saudāsaḥ prasādāśruvyāptanayano gadgadāyamānakaṅṭhaḥ samabhisṛtyaiva bodhisattvaṃ pādayoḥ saṃpariṣvajyovāca -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Saudāsa</s>, his eyes brimming with tears of faith, his throat choked with emotion, approaching the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and embracing his feet, said:

children.text: guṇakusumarajobhiḥ puṇyagandhiḥ samantājjagadidamavakīrṇaṃ kāraṇe tvadyaśobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The world is scattered all around with the pollen-dust of your virtuous qualities, fragrant with merit, and by the fame born of your deeds —

children.text: iti vicarati pāpe mṛtyudūtogravṛttau tvamiva hi ka ivānyaḥ sānukampo mayi syāt // Jm_31.92 //
children.translated_text: when [even] the fierce emissary of Death roams about in evil, who else but you could be so compassionate toward me? || Jm 31.92 ||

children.text: śastā guruśca mama daivatameva ca tvaṃ mūrdhnā vacāṃsyahamamūni tavārcayāmi /
children.translated_text: You are my teacher, my preceptor, and indeed my deity — with my head I honor these words of yours;

children.text: bhokṣye na caiva sutasoma manuṣyamāṃsaṃ yanmāṃ yathā vadasi tacca tathā kariṣye // Jm_31.93 //
children.translated_text: I shall never again eat human flesh, O <s>Sutasoma</s> — whatever you tell me, that I shall do. || Jm 31.93 ||

children.text: nṛpātmajā yaṅanimittamāhṛtā mayā ca ye bandhanakhedapīḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The princes who were brought here on my account, and who have been afflicted by the suffering of captivity,

children.text: hatatviṣaḥ śokaparītamānasāstadehi muñcāva sahaiva tānapi // Jm_31.94 //
children.translated_text: their splendor dimmed, their minds overwhelmed with grief — come, let us release even them together. || Jm 31.94 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvastathetyasmai pratiśrutya yatra te nṛpasutāstenāvaruddhāstatraivābhijagāma / dṛṣṭai va ca te nṛpasutāḥ sutasomaṃ hanta muktā vayamiti paraṃ harṣamupajagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having agreed with 'So be it,' went to where those princes were held captive. And upon seeing <s>Sutasoma</s>, those princes, [thinking] 'We are freed!' attained the utmost joy.

children.text: virejire te sutasomadarśanānnarendraputrāḥ sphuṭahāsakāntayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those princes shone at the sight of <s>Sutasoma</s>, radiant with blossoming smiles,

children.text: śaranmukhe candrakaropabṛhitā vijṛmbhamāṇāḥ kumudākarā iva // Jm_31.95 //
children.translated_text: like lotus ponds blooming, adorned with moonbeams at the onset of autumn. || Jm 31.95 ||

body.text: athainānabhigamya bodhisattvaḥ samāśvāsayan priyavacanapuraḥsaraṃ ca pratisaṃmodya saudāsasyādrohāya śapathaṃ kārayitvā bandhanādvimucya sārdhaṃ saudāsena taiśca nṛpatiputrairanugamyamānaḥ svaṃ rājyamupetya yathārhakṛtasaṃskārāṃstān rājaputrān saudāsaṃ ca sveṣu sveṣu rājyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having approached them, consoling them and greeting them cordially with kind words, having made <s>Saudāsa</s> take an oath of non-hostility, releasing them from bondage, accompanied by <s>Saudāsa</s> and those princes, returned to his own kingdom and, having honored those princes and <s>Saudāsa</s> with due ceremony, established them each in their respective kingdoms.

body.text: tadevaṃ śreyaḥ samādhatte yathātathāpyupanataḥ satsaṃgama iti śreyo 'rthinā sajjanasamāśrayeṇa bhavitavyam / evamasaṃstutahṛtpūrvajanmasvapyupakāraparatvād buddho bhagavāniti tathāgatavarṇe 'pi vācyam / evaṃ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ doṣāpacayāya guṇasamādhānāya ca bhavatīti saddharmaśravaṇe 'pi vācyam / śrutapraśaṃsāyāmapi vācyam - evamanekānuśaṃsaṃ śrutamiti / satyakathāyāmapi vācyam - evaṃ sajjaneṣṭaṃ puṇyakīrtyākaraṃ satyavacanamityevaṃ svaprāṇasukheśvaryanirapekṣāḥ satyamanurakṣanti satpuruṣā iti / satyapraśaṃsāyāmapyupaneyaṃ karuṇāvarṇe 'pi ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus, good fortune is accomplished [through] the company of the virtuous, however it may come about; therefore one who seeks welfare should resort to the company of the virtuous. Thus, because even in previous births, without prior acquaintance, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] was devoted to helping [others], this should be cited in praise of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as 'the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.' Thus, hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> leads to the diminution of faults and the attainment of virtues — this should be cited in [praise of] hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>.
