In praise of learning too it should be cited: 'Thus learning has manifold benefits.' In a discourse on truth too it should be cited: 'Thus truthful speech, dear to the virtuous, is a mine of merit and fame — in this manner, without regard for their own lives, comforts, or sovereignty, the virtuous guard the truth.' It should be adduced in praise of truth and also in the description of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>).

body.text: // iti sutasomajātakamekatriṃśattamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-first [story], the <s>Sutasoma Jātaka</s>.

body.text: 32. Ayogṛhajātakam
body.translated_text: 32. The <s>Ayogṛha Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Iron House)

body.text: rājalakṣmīrapi śreyomārgaṃ nāvṛṇoti saṃvignamānasānāmiti saṃvegaparicayaḥ kāryaḥ / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even royal splendor does not obstruct the path to spiritual welfare for those whose minds are stirred with spiritual urgency — therefore one should cultivate familiarity with <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency). As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvabhūtaḥ kilāyaṃ bhagavān vyādhijarāmaraṇapriyaviprayogādivyasanaśatopanipātaṃ duḥkhitamanāthamatrāṇamapariṇāyakaṃ lokamavekṣya karuṇayā samutsāhyamānastatparitrāṇavyavasitamatiratisādhusvabhāvastattatsaṃpādayamāno vimukhasyāsaṃstutasyāpi ca lokasya hitaṃ sukhaviśeṣa ca kadācidanyatamasmin rājakule prajānurāgasaumukhyādaskhalitābhivṛddhyā ca samṛddhyā samānatadṛptasāmantayā cābhivyajyamānamahābhāgye vinayaślāghini janma pratilebhe / sa jāyamāna eva tadrājakulaṃ tatsamānasukhaduḥkhaṃ ca puravaraṃ parayābhyudayaśriyā samyojayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One, when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, observing this world — assailed by hundreds of calamities such as disease, old age, death, and separation from loved ones — suffering, without protector, without refuge, without guide, his mind impelled by compassion, resolved upon its deliverance, being of exceedingly virtuous nature, accomplishing those [necessary deeds], once took birth in a certain royal family — achieving welfare and happiness even for a world that was averse and unacquainted [with him] — through the affection of the people, through the unfaltering increase of prosperity, and through the humbling of proud feudatory kings, [a birth] whose great fortune was manifest and worthy of praise for its discipline. Even as he was born, he united that royal house and that excellent city, which shared its joys and sorrows, with supreme glory and prosperity.

children.text: pratigrahavyākulatuṣṭavipraṃ madoddhatābhyujjvalaveṣabhṛtyam /
children.translated_text: With brahmins delighted and overwhelmed by gifts received, with servants whose splendid attire was resplendent with pride,

children.text: anekatūryasvanapūrṇakūjamānandanṛttānayavṛttābhāvam // Jm_32.1 //
children.translated_text: filled with the cries of numerous musical instruments, its festivities displaying graceful conduct and joyous dancing — || Jm 32.1 ||

children.text: saṃsaktagītadravahāsanādaṃ parasparāśleṣavivṛddhaharṣam /
children.translated_text: resounding with the mingled sounds of singing, flowing laughter, embraces exchanging heightened joy,

children.text: naraiḥ priyākhyānakadānatuṣṭairāśāsyamānābhyudayaṃ nṛpasya // Jm_32.2 //
children.translated_text: with people gladdened by the giving and telling of good news, wishing for the prosperity of the king — || Jm 32.2 ||

children.text: vighaṭṭitadvāravimuktabandhanaṃ samuchritāgradhvajacitracatvaram /
children.translated_text: its gates thrown open, its bonds released, its crossroads adorned with tall banners raised high and colorful [decorations],

children.text: vicūrṇapuṣpāsavasiktabhūtalaṃ babhāra ramyāṃ puramutsavaśriyam // Jm_32.3 //
children.translated_text: its ground strewn with crushed flowers and sprinkled with fragrant liquors — the city bore a delightful festival splendor. || Jm 32.3 ||

children.text: mahāgṛhebhyaḥ pravikīryamāṇairhiraṇyavastrābharaṇādivarṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With showers of gold, garments, ornaments, and the like being scattered from the great houses,

children.text: lokaṃ tadā vyāptumivodyatā śrīrunmattagaṅgālalitaṃ cakāra // Jm_32.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), as if striving to pervade the world, displayed the playful grace of an exuberant <s>Gaṅgā</s>. [Jm 32.4]

body.text: tena ca samayena tasya rājño jātā jātāḥ kumārā mriyante sma / sa taṃ vidhimamānuṣakṛtamiti manyamānastasya tanayasya rakṣārthaṃ maṇikāñcanarajatabhakticitre śrīmati sarvāyase prasūtibhavane bhūtavidyāparidṛṣṭena vedavihitena ca krameṇa vihitarakṣodhnapratīkāre samucitaiśca kautukamaṅgalaiḥ kṛtasvastyayanaparigrahe jātakarmādisaṃskāravidhiṃ saṃvardhanaṃ ca kārayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: At that time, the princes born to that king kept dying one after another. Considering this calamity to be the work of non-human beings, the king, for the protection of his son, had the birth-chamber — beautiful, adorned with designs in gems, gold, silver, and colored patterns, and made entirely of iron — furnished with rites for the repulsion of evil spirits as prescribed by the science of <s>bhūtavidyā</s> (demonology) and by Vedic procedure, and with appropriate auspicious ceremonies and blessings, and therein had the rites of <s>jātakarma</s> (birth-ceremony) and other <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacramental rites) and the rearing of the child performed.

body.text: tamapi ca mahāsattvaṃ sattvasaṃpatteḥ puṇyopacayaprabhāvātsusaṃvihitatvācca rakṣāyā nāmānuṣāḥ prasehire / sa kālakramādavāptasaṃskārakarmā śrutābhijanācāramahadbhyo labdhavidvadyaśaḥsaṃmānanebhyaḥ praśamavinayamedhāguṇāvarjitebhyo gurubhyaḥ samadhigatānekavidyaḥ pratyahamāpūryamāṇamūrtiryauvanakāntyā nisargasiddhena ca vinayānurāgeṇa paraṃ premāspadaṃ svajanasya janasya ca babhūva /
body.translated_text: And the non-human beings could not prevail against that great being either, due to the excellence of his innate goodness, the power of his accumulated merit, and the thorough arrangement of his protection. In due course of time, having received the prescribed sacramental rites, having obtained manifold learning from teachers who had earned the honor and esteem of scholars through their fame born of learning, noble lineage, and good conduct, and who captivated others by their qualities of tranquility, discipline, and intelligence — growing daily in stature, he became, through the beauty of youth and his naturally innate love of propriety, the supreme object of affection for both his own family and the people at large.

children.text: asaṃstutamasaṃbandhaṃ durasthamapi sajjanam /
children.translated_text: Even toward the virtuous who are unknown, unrelated, and far away,

children.text: jano 'nveti suhṛtprītyā guṇaśrīstatra karaṇam // Jm_32.5 //
children.translated_text: People are drawn with the affection of a friend — the splendor of their virtues is the cause of this. [Jm 32.5]

children.text: hāsabhūtena nabhasaḥ śaradvikacaraśminā /
children.translated_text: What real connection does the world have with the moon,

children.text: saṃbandhasiddhirlokasya kā hi candramasā saha // Jm_32.6 //
children.translated_text: Which wanders through the sky in autumn with its scattered rays, as though it were a jest? [Jm 32.6]

body.text: atha sa mahāsattvaḥ puṇyaprabhāvasukhopanatairdivyakalpairanalpairapi ca viṣayairupalālyamānaḥ snehabahumānasumukhena ca pitrā viśvāsananirviśaṅkaṃ dṛśyamānaḥ kadācitsvasmin puravare pravitataramaṇīyaśobhāṃ kalakramopanatāṃ kaumudīvibhūtiṃ didṛkṣuḥ kṛtābhyanujñaḥ pitrā kāñcanamaṇirajatabhakticitrālaṃkāraṃ samucchritanānāvidharāgapracalitojjvalapatākadhvajaṃ haimabhāṇḍābhyalaṃkṛtavinītacaturaturaṃgaṃ dakṣadākṣiṇyanipuṇaśucivinītadhīrasārathiṃ citrojjvalaveṣapraharaṇāvaraṇānuyātraṃ rathavaramadhiruhya manoṅatūryasvanapuraḥsarastatpuravaramanuvicaraṃstaddarśanākṣiptahṛdayasya kautūhalalolacakṣuṣaḥ stutisabhājanāñjalipragrahapraṇāmāśīrvacanaprayogasavyāparasyotsavaramyataraveṣaracanasya paurajānapadasya samudayaśobhāmālokya labdhapraharṣāvakāśe 'pi manasi kṛtasaṃvegaparicayatvātpūrvajanmasu smṛtiṃ pratilebhe /
body.translated_text: Now that great being, though attended upon by divine-like pleasures brought near by the power of his merit, and by no small share of sensory enjoyments, and though regarded with trusting confidence by his father, whose face was turned toward him with affection and respect — one day, wishing to see the splendor of the <s>kaumudī</s> (moonlight festival), whose lovely beauty had spread extensively through his capital city, brought about by the course of time, obtained his father's permission and mounted an excellent chariot — adorned with gold, gems, and silver in painted designs, bearing aloft various colored, fluttering, brilliant banners and flags, equipped with well-trained, swift horses adorned with golden trappings, driven by a charioteer who was skilled, courteous, dexterous, clean, disciplined, and steady, and attended by an escort brilliant in variegated dress and bearing arms and armor — and proceeded through that excellent city, preceded by the sounds of heart-delighting musical instruments. Beholding the collective splendor of the citizens and country-folk — whose hearts were captivated and whose eyes roved with curiosity at the sight, who were engaged in offering praises, salutations with joined palms, bowing, and words of blessing, and who were adorned in festive finery more beautiful than usual — though his mind found occasion for delight, because of his familiarity with spiritual urgency cultivated in former births, he attained recollection:

children.text: kṛpaṇā bata lokasya calatvavirasā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: "How pitiable is the condition of the world, unstable and devoid of lasting substance,

children.text: yadiyaṃ kaumudīlakṣmīḥ smartavyaiva bhaviṣyati // Jm_32.7 //
children.translated_text: If even this splendor of the moonlight festival is destined to become merely a memory! [Jm 32.7]

children.text: evaṃvidhāyāṃ ca jagatpravṛttāvaho yathā nirbhayatā janānām /
children.translated_text: And given the way things go in this world, alas, how fearless people are —

children.text: yanmṛtyunādhiṣṭhitasarvamārgā niḥsaṃbhramā harṣamanubhramanti // Jm_32.8 //
children.translated_text: That with death stationed on every path, they enjoy their pleasures without alarm! [Jm 32.8]

children.text: avāryavīryeṣvariṣu sthiteṣu jighāṃsayā vyādhijarāntakeṣu /
children.translated_text: While enemies of irresistible power stand ready — disease, old age, and death — intent on destruction,

children.text: avaśyagamye paralokadurge harṣāvakāśo 'tra sacetasaḥ kaḥ // Jm_32.9 //
children.translated_text: And with the perilous other world an inevitable destination, what occasion for joy is there here for one who possesses awareness? [Jm 32.9]

children.text: svanānukṛtyeva mahārṇavānāṃ saṃrambharaudrāṇi jalāni kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: As if imitating the roar of great oceans, rendering the waters turbulent and terrible,

children.text: meghāstaḍidbhāsurahemamālāḥ saṃbhūya bhūyo vilayaṃ vrajanti // Jm_32.10 //
children.translated_text: The clouds, adorned with garlands of lightning-bright gold, having gathered, dissolve once again. [Jm 32.10]

children.text: taṭaiḥ samaṃ tadvinibaddhamūlān hṛtvā tarūṃllabdhajavaiḥ payobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having uprooted trees whose roots were bound to the banks, carrying them away with swift-flowing waters,

children.text: bhavanti bhūyaḥ saritaḥ kramena śokopatāpādiva dinarūpāḥ // Jm_32.11 //
children.translated_text: Rivers gradually become shrunken in form, as if emaciated from grief and distress. [Jm 32.11]

children.text: hṛtvāpi śṛṅgāṇi mahīdharāṇāṃ vegena vṛndāni ca toyadānām /
children.translated_text: Having shattered the peaks of mountains and scattered the masses of rain-clouds with its force,

children.text: vighūrṇya codvartya ca sāgarāmbhaḥ prayāti nāśa pavanaprabhāvaḥ // Jm_32.12 //
children.translated_text: Having churned and upheaved the waters of the ocean, the power of the wind passes to naught. [Jm 32.12]

children.text: diptoddhatārcirvikasatsphuliṅgaḥ saṃkṣipya kakṣaṃ kṣayameti vahniḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire, with its blazing, upraised flames and bursting sparks, having consumed the brush, reaches extinction;

children.text: krameṇa śobhāśca vanāntarāṇāmudyanti bhūyaśca tirobhavanti // Jm_32.13 //
children.translated_text: And the beauties of the forest interiors arise in turn and again vanish. [Jm 32.13]

children.text: kaḥ saṃprayogo na viyoganiṣṭhaḥ kāḥ saṃpado yā na vipatparaiti /
children.translated_text: What union does not end in separation? What prosperity does not lead to misfortune?

children.text: jagatpravṛttāviti cañcalāyāmapratyavekṣyaiva janasya harṣaḥ // Jm_32.14 //
children.translated_text: In this flickering course of worldly existence, the joy of people is truly without reflection." [Jm 32.14]

body.text: iti sa parigaṇayan mahātmā saṃvegādvyāvṛttapramodauddhavena manasā ramaṇīyeṣvapi puravaravibhūṣārthamabhiprasāriṣu lokacitreṣvaviṣajyamānabuddhiḥ krameṇa svabhavanamanuprāptamevātmānamapaśyat / tadabhivṛddhasaṃvegaśca viṣayasukheṣvanāstho dharma ekaḥ śaraṇamiti tatpratipattiniścitamatiryathāprastāvamabhigamya rājānaṃ kṛtāñjalistapovanagamanāyānujñāmayācata -
body.translated_text: Thus reflecting, that great soul, his mind turned away from delight by the force of spiritual urgency, his intellect unattached even to the charming spectacles spread out to adorn that excellent city, gradually found himself having returned to his own palace. With his sense of urgency intensified, indifferent to the pleasures of the senses, his mind firmly resolved that <s>Dharma</s> alone is the refuge and that he must pursue it, he approached the king at a suitable occasion, and with hands joined in supplication, requested permission to go to the ascetic grove —

children.text: pravrajyāsaṃśrayātkartumicchāmi hitamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I wish to pursue my own welfare by taking refuge in the renunciant life;

children.text: kṛtāṃ tatrābhyanujñāṃ ca tvayānugrahapaddhatim // Jm_32.15 //
children.translated_text: May you grant your permission for that, which would be a path of grace. [Jm 32.15]

children.text: tacchratvā priyatanayaḥ sa tasya rājā digdhena dvirada iveṣuṇābhividdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king, who cherished his son, like an elephant struck by a poisoned arrow,

children.text: gambhīro 'pyudadhirivānilāvadhūtastacchokavyathitamanāḥ samācakampe // Jm_32.16 //
children.translated_text: Though deep like the ocean, shaken by the wind, his mind distressed by that grief, trembled. [Jm 32.16]

children.text: nivārayiṣyannatha taṃ sa rājā snehātpaṣvajya sabāṣpakaṇṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, wishing to dissuade him, embracing him with affection, his throat choked with tears,

children.text: uvāca kasmātsahasaiva tāta saṃtyaktumasmān matimityakārṣīḥ // Jm_32.17 //
children.translated_text: Said: 'Why, my child, have you suddenly formed the resolve to abandon us? [Jm 32.17]

children.text: tvadapriyeṇātmavināśahetuḥ kenāyamityākalitaḥ kṛtāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: By whom has this <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) — the cause of self-destruction — been invoked through some act displeasing to you?

children.text: śokāśruparyākulalocanāni bhavantu kasya svajanānanāni // Jm_32.18 //
children.translated_text: Whose family faces shall be clouded with tears of grief?' [Jm 32.18]

children.text: athāpi kiṃcitpariśaṅkitaṃ vā mayi vyalīkaṃ samupaśrutaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Or if there is some apprehension, or some falsehood heard regarding me,

children.text: tadbrūhi yāvadviramāmi tasmātpaśyāmi na tvātmani kiṃcidīdṛk // Jm_32.19 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, so that I may desist from it — though I do not see any such thing in myself. [Jm 32.19]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: ityabhisnehasumukhe vyalīkaṃ nāma kiṃ tvayi /
children.translated_text: 'What falsehood could there be in you, who are so graciously disposed with affection?

children.text: vipriyeṇa samarthaḥ syānmāmāsādayituṃ ca kaḥ // Jm_32.20 //
children.translated_text: And who would be capable of afflicting me with anything displeasing? [Jm 32.20]

body.text: atha kiṃ tarhi naḥ parityuaktumicchasīti cābhihitaḥ sāśrunayanena rājñā sa mahāsattvastamuvāca - mṛtyubhayāt / paśyatu devaḥ,
body.translated_text: Then why do you wish to leave us?' — asked by the king with tearful eyes, that great being said to him: 'Out of fear of death. Let your majesty consider:"

children.text: yāmeva rātriṃ prathamāmupaiti garbhe nivāsaṃ naravīra lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: "From the very first night that a being enters its dwelling in the womb, O hero among men,

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛtyaskhalitaprayāṇaḥ sa pratyahaṃ mṛtyusamīpameti // Jm_32.21 //
children.translated_text: From that moment onward, with unswerving course, it approaches death day by day. [Jm 32.21]

children.text: nītau suyukto 'pi bale sthito 'pi nātyeti kaścinmaraṇaṃ jarāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Even one well-versed in statecraft, even one established in strength, does not escape death or old age;

children.text: upadrutaṃ sarvamitīdamābhyāṃ dharmārthamasmādvanamāśrayiṣye // Jm_32.22 //
children.translated_text: All this is beset by these two — therefore, for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, I shall take refuge in the forest. [Jm 32.22]

children.text: vyūḍhānyudīrṇanaravājirathadvipāni sainyāni darparabhasāḥ kṣitipā jayanti /
children.translated_text: Kings, fierce in the impetuosity of their pride, conquer armies arrayed with spirited men, horses, chariots, and elephants;

children.text: jetuṃ kṛtā taripumekamapi tvaśaktāstanme matirbhavati dharmamabhiprapattum // Jm_32.23 //
children.translated_text: Yet they are unable to conquer even one enemy, death — therefore my mind turns to embracing <s>Dharma</s>. [Jm 32.23]

children.text: hṛṣṭāśvakuñjarapadātirathairanīkairguptā vimokṣamupayāni nṛpā dviṣadbhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings, protected by battalions of spirited horses, elephants, infantry, and chariots, escape from their foes;

children.text: sārdhaṃ balairatibalasya tu mṛtyuśatrormanvādayo 'pi vivaśā vaśamabhyupetāḥ // Jm_32.24 //
children.translated_text: But before death, that overpowering enemy, even <s>Manu</s> and the others have helplessly submitted to his power, together with their forces. [Jm 32.24]

children.text: saṃcūrṇya dantamusalaiḥ puragopurāṇi mattā dvipā yudhi rathāṃśca narān dvīpāṃśca /
children.translated_text: Maddened elephants, shattering the gate-towers of fortresses with their tusks like pestles, crushing chariots, men, and other elephants in battle —

children.text: naivāntakaṃ pratimukhābhigataṃ nudanti vaprāntalabdhavijayairapi tairviṣāṇaiḥ // Jm_32.25 //
children.translated_text: Even with those tusks that have won victory at the rampart's edge, they cannot repel Death when he approaches face to face. [Jm 32.25]

children.text: dṛḍhacitravarmakavacāvaraṇān yudhi dārayantyapi vidūracarān /
children.translated_text: Those skilled in weaponry, who with their arrows pierce even distant foes wearing hard, ornate armor and coats of mail in battle —

children.text: iṣubhistadastrakuśalā dviṣataściravairiṇaṃ na tu kṛtāntamarim // Jm_32.26 //
children.translated_text: They cannot [pierce] Death, their eternal enemy. [Jm 32.26]

children.text: siṃhā vikartanakarairnakharairdvipānāṃ kumbhāgramagnaśikharaiḥ praśamayya tejaḥ /
children.translated_text: Lions, having subdued the might of elephants with their claws — sharp instruments of tearing — whose tips sink into the frontal globes of elephants,

children.text: bhittvaiva ca śrutamanāṃsi ravaiḥ pareṣāṃ mṛtyuṃ sametya hatadarpabalāḥ svapanti // Jm_32.27 //
children.translated_text: And having shattered the courage of their foes with their roars, sleep with their pride and strength destroyed upon encountering death. [Jm 32.27]

children.text: doṣānurūpaṃ praṇayanti daṇḍaṃ kṛtāparādheṣu nṛpāḥ pareṣu /
children.translated_text: Kings inflict punishment upon transgressors proportionate to their offence;

children.text: mahāparādhe yadi mṛtyuśatrau na daṇḍanītipravaṇā bhavanti // Jm_32.28 //
children.translated_text: Yet against Death, the greatest transgressor, they do not exercise their punitive authority. [Jm 32.28]

children.text: nṛpāśca sāmādibhirapyupāyaiḥ kṛtaparādhaṃ vaśamānayanti /
children.translated_text: Kings bring even transgressors under their control through <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and other diplomatic means;

children.text: raudraścirābhyāsadṛḍhāvalepo mṛtyuḥ punarnānunayādisādhyaḥ // Jm_32.29 //
children.translated_text: But Death, terrible, his arrogance hardened through long practice, cannot be subdued by appeasement or other measures. [Jm 32.29]

children.text: krodhānalajvalitaghoraviṣāgnigarbhairdaṃṣṭrāṅkarairabhidaśanti narān bhujaṃgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Serpents bite men with their fangs — curved projections filled with the fire of terrible, blazing poison born of wrath;

children.text: daṃṣṭavyayatnavidhurāstu bhavanti mṛtyau vadhye 'pi nityamapakāravidhānadakṣe // Jm_32.30 //
children.translated_text: Yet their efforts to bite are futile against Death, who is ever skilled in causing harm even to those who are to be slain. [Jm 32.30]

children.text: daṣṭasya koparabhasairapi pannagaiśca mantrairviṣaṃ praśamayantyagadaiśca vaidyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the best physicians cure the poison of one bitten even by serpents furious with rage, through <s>mantras</s> (incantations) and antidotes;

children.text: āśīviṣastvativīṣo 'yamariṣṭadaṃṣṭro mantragadādibhirasādhyabalaḥ kṛtāntaḥ // Jm_32.31 //
children.translated_text: But this venomous serpent <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death), with his unfailing fangs, is one whose power cannot be overcome by incantations, antidotes, or any other means. [Jm 32.31]

body.text: pakṣānilairlalitamīnakulaṃ vyudasya meghaughabhīmarasitaṃ jalamarṇavebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Suparṇas</s> (Garuḍas), with widespread talons, sweeping aside the playful schools of fish with the wind of their wings, carry off serpents from the oceans with their terrible thundering like storm-clouds;

body.text: sarpān haranti vitatagrahaṇāḥ suparṇā mṛtyuṃ punaḥ pramathituṃ na tathotsahante // Jm_32.32 //
body.translated_text: Yet they are not so bold as to overpower Death. [Jm 32.32]

children.text: bhītadrutānapi javātiśayena jitvā saṃsādya caikabhujavajravilāsavṛttyā /
children.translated_text: Tigers, overtaking fleeing deer with their surpassing speed, seizing them with the playful ease of a single paw-stroke like a thunderbolt,

children.text: vyāghrāḥ pibanti rudhirāṇi vane mṛgāṇāṃ naivaṃpravṛttipaṭavastu bhavanti mṛtyau // Jm_32.33 //
children.translated_text: Drink their blood in the forest — yet they are not so skilled in their ways when it comes to Death. [Jm 32.33]

children.text: daṣṭrākarālamapi nāma mṛgaḥ sametya vaiyāghramānanamupaiti punarvimokṣam /
children.translated_text: A deer, having encountered even the terrible-fanged face of a tiger, may yet obtain release;

children.text: mṛtyormukhaṃ tu pṛthurogajarārtidaṃṣṭraṃ prāptasya kasya ca punaḥ śivatātirasti // Jm_32.34 //
children.translated_text: But for one who has entered the jaws of Death — wide, with the teeth of grievous disease, old age, and suffering — for whom is there any deliverance? [Jm 32.34]

children.text: pibanti nṝṇāṃ vikṛtogravigrahā śaujasāyūṃṣi dṛḍhagrahā grahāḥ /
children.translated_text: Demons of hideous and terrible form, with a firm grip, drink the life-forces of men with their ferocity;

children.text: bhavanti tu prastutamṛtyuvigrahā vipannadarpotkaṭatāparigrahāḥ // Jm_32.35 //
children.translated_text: Yet when confronted with the might of Death, they become bereft of their swollen arrogance and possessions. [Jm 32.35]

children.text: pūjāratadrohakṛte 'bhyupetān grahānniyacchanti sa siddhavidyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have perfected <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) subdue demons that have come, having committed offenses against worship or acts of malice;

children.text: tapobalasvastyayanauṣadhaiśca mṛtyugrahastvaprativāryaṃ eva // Jm_32.36 //
children.translated_text: But the demon Death cannot be warded off even by the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), benedictions, or medicines. [Jm 32.36]

children.text: māyāvidhijñāśca mahāsamāje janasya cakṣuṃṣi vimohayanti /
children.translated_text: Those skilled in magic and ritual arts bewilder the eyes of people in great assemblies;

children.text: ko 'pi prabhāvastvayamantakasyayadbhrāmyate tairapi nāsya cakṣuḥ // Jm_32.37 //
children.translated_text: Yet such is the incomparable power of Death that their vision too is not deluded by him. [Jm 32.37]

children.text: hatvā viṣāṇi ca tapobalasiddhamantrā vyādhīnnṛṇāmupaśamayya ca vaidyavaryāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having neutralized poisons and cured the diseases of men through <s>mantras</s> perfected by the power of <s>tapas</s>, even the greatest physicians,

children.text: dhanvantariprabhṛtayo 'pi gatā vināśaṃ dharmāya me namati tena matirvanānte // Jm_32.38 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Dhanvantari</s>, have gone to destruction — therefore my mind bows toward <s>Dharma</s> in the forest's end. [Jm 32.38]

children.text: āvirbhavanti ca punaśca tirobhavanti gacchanti vānilapathena mahīṃ viśanti /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vidyādharas</s> (bearers of sacred knowledge) appear and disappear, travel through the sky and enter the earth,

children.text: vidyādharā vividhamantrabalaprabhāvā mṛtyuṃ sametya tu bhavanti hataprabhāvāḥ // Jm_32.39 //
children.translated_text: Through the power of their various <s>mantras</s> — yet upon encountering Death, they become powerless. [Jm 32.39]

children.text: dṛptānapi pratinudantyasurān surendrā dṛptānapi pratinudantyasurāḥ surāṃśca /
children.translated_text: The lords of the <s>Suras</s> (gods) repel even the haughty <s>Asuras</s> (demons), and the <s>Asuras</s> repel even the haughty <s>Suras</s>;

children.text: mānādhirūḍhamatibhiḥ sumudīrṇasainyaistaiḥ saṃhatairapi tu mṛtyurajayya eva // Jm_32.40 //
children.translated_text: Yet even when all of them unite — their minds mounted on pride, with their armies fully arrayed — Death remains unconquerable. [Jm 32.40]

children.text: imāmavetyāprativāryaraudratāṃ kṛtāntaśatrorbhavane na me matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing this irresistible ferocity of the enemy Death, my mind is not set on remaining in the household;

children.text: na manyunā snehaparikṣayeṇa vā prayāmi dharmāya tu niścito vanam // Jm_32.41 //
children.translated_text: It is not out of anger or the decay of affection that I depart, but with firm resolve, for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, to the forest. [Jm 32.41]

body.text: rājovāca - atha vane tava ka āśvāsaḥ evamapratikriye mṛtyubhaye sati dharmaparigrahe ca /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Then what assurance do you have in the forest, when the fear of death is thus without remedy, and you are committed to <s>Dharma</s>?'

children.text: kiṃ tvā vane na samupaiṣyati mṛtyuśatrurdharme sthitāḥ kimṛṣayo na vane vinaṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Will not the enemy Death approach you in the forest as well? Have not the sages, established in <s>Dharma</s>, perished in the forest too?

children.text: sarvatra nāma niyataḥ krama eṣa tatra ko 'rtho vihāya bhavanaṃ vanasaṃśrayeṇa // Jm_32.42 //
children.translated_text: Since this succession is fixed everywhere, what is the purpose of forsaking the palace for refuge in the forest?' [Jm 32.42]

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kāmaṃ sthiteṣu bhavane ca vane ca mṛtyurdharmātmakesu viguṇeṣu ca tulyavṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Granted that death acts with equal force upon those in the palace and those in the forest, upon the righteous and the unrighteous alike;

children.text: dharmātmanāṃ bhavati na tvanutāpahetudharmaśca nāma vana eva sukha prapattum // Jm_32.43 //
children.translated_text: Yet for the righteous it does not become a cause of remorse — and <s>Dharma</s> is indeed easier to pursue in the forest. [Jm 32.43]

body.text: paśyatu devaḥ,
body.translated_text: Let your majesty consider:

children.text: pramādamadakandarpalobhadveṣāspade gṛhe /
children.translated_text: In the household, which is the abode of heedlessness, intoxication, passion, greed, and hatred —

children.text: tadviruddhasya dharmasya ko 'vakāśaparigrahaḥ // Jm_32.44 //
children.translated_text: what scope is there for <s>Dharma</s>, which is the very opposite of these? || Jm 32.44 ||

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇo bahubhiḥ kukarmabhiḥ parigrahopārjanarakṣaṇākulaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dragged about by numerous evil deeds, agitated by the acquisition, earning, and guarding of possessions,

children.text: aśāntacetā vyasanodayāgamaiḥ kadā gṛhasthaḥ śamamārgameṣyati // Jm_32.45 //
children.translated_text: his mind never at peace, beset by the arising of calamities — when will the householder ever reach the path of tranquility? || Jm 32.45 ||

children.text: vane tu saṃtyaktakukāryavistaraḥ parigrahakleśavivarjitaḥ sukhī /
children.translated_text: But in the forest, having abandoned the proliferation of evil activities, free from the affliction of possessions, happy,

children.text: śamaikakāryaḥ parituṣṭamānasaḥ sukhaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca yaśāṃsi cārcchati // Jm_32.46 //
children.translated_text: devoted solely to tranquility, with a contented mind, one attains happiness, <s>Dharma</s>, and renown. || Jm 32.46 ||

children.text: dharmaśca rakṣati naraṃ na dhanaṃ balaṃ vā dharmaḥ sukhāya mahate na vibhutisiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> protects a man, not wealth or strength; <s>Dharma</s> leads to great happiness, not the attainment of prosperity;

children.text: dharmātmanaśca mudameva karoti mṛtyurna hyasti durgatibhayaṃ niratasya dharme // Jm_32.47 //
children.translated_text: and for one whose soul is devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, death brings only joy — for there is no fear of an evil destiny for one who delights in <s>Dharma</s>. || Jm 32.47 ||

children.text: kriyāviśeṣaśca yathā vyavasthitaḥ śubhasya pāpasya ca bhinnalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the particular action of good and evil is established with distinct characteristics,

children.text: tathā vipāko 'pyaśubhasya durgatiścitrasya dharmasya sukhāśrayā gatiḥ // Jm_32.48 //
children.translated_text: so too is the ripening: for the unwholesome, an evil destiny; for the manifold <s>Dharma</s>, a course leading to happiness. || Jm 32.48 ||

body.text: ityanunīya sa mahātmā pitaraṃ kṛtābhyanujñaḥ pitrā tṛṇavadapāsya rājyalakṣmīṃ tapovanāśrayaṃ cakāra / tatra ca dhyānānyapramāṇāni cotpādya teṣu ca pratiṣṭhāpya lokaṃ brahmalokamadhiroha /
body.translated_text: Having thus persuaded his father, that great soul, given leave by his father, casting aside the splendor of kingship as if it were a blade of grass, took up residence in an ascetic grove. And there, having cultivated the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurable states), and having established the people in them, he ascended to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: tadevaṃ saṃvignamanasāṃ rājalakṣmīrapi śreyomārgaṃ nāvṛṇotīti saṃvegaparicayaḥ kāryaḥ / maraṇasaṃjñāvarṇe 'pi vācyam - evamāśumaraṇasaṃjñā saṃvegāya bhavatīti / tathā maraṇānusmṛtivarṇe 'nityatākathāyāmapyupaneyam - evamanityāḥ sarvasaṃskārā iti / tathā sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñāyām - evamanāśvāsikaṃ saṃskṛtamiti / evamatrāṇo 'yamasahāyaśca loka ityevamapi vācyam / evaṃ vane dharmaḥ sukhaṃ pratipattuṃ na geha ityevamapyunneyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, even the splendor of kingship does not obstruct the path to the highest good for those whose minds are filled with spiritual urgency — therefore one should cultivate familiarity with <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency). In the description of the perception of death, it should also be said: 'Thus the perception of imminent death conduces to spiritual urgency.' Likewise, in the description of the recollection of death, and in the discourse on impermanence, it should be adduced: 'Thus all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) are impermanent.' Similarly, regarding the perception of dissatisfaction with the entire world: 'Thus the conditioned is unreliable.' And it should also be said: 'Thus this world is without protection and without companionship.' And it should also be inferred: 'Thus in the forest <s>Dharma</s> is easy to practice, not in the household.'

body.text: // iti ayogṛhajātakaṃ dvātriṃśattamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-second [story], the <s>Ayogṛha Jātaka</s> (The Iron House). ||

body.text: 33. Mahiṣajātakam
body.translated_text: 33. The <s>Mahiṣa Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Buffalo)

body.text: sati kṣantavye kṣamā syānnāsatītyapakāriṇāmapi sādhavo lābhamiva bahu manyante / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: When there is one who deserves forbearance, patience should be shown, not when there is none — thus the virtuous esteem even those who wrong them, as if they were a gain. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānyatamasminnaraṇyapradeśe paṅkasaṃparkātparuṣavapurṇīlameghaviccheda iva pādacārī vanamahiṣavṛṣo babhūva / sa tasyāṃ durlabhadharmasaṃjñāyāṃ saṃmohabahulāyāmapi tiryaggatau vartamānaḥ paṭuvijñānatvānna dharmacaryānirudyogamatirbabhūva /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, in a certain forest region, his body rough from contact with mud, like a fragment of a dark cloud walking on foot, was a wild buffalo bull. Even while existing in that animal state — so prone to delusion and where the notion of <s>Dharma</s> is rare — owing to the keenness of his understanding, his mind was not inactive in the practice of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: cirānuvṛttyevaḥ nibaddhabhāvā na taṃ kadācitkaruṇā mumoca /
children.translated_text: Compassion, its nature bound by long-continued practice, never abandoned him;

children.text: ko 'pi prabhāva sa tu karmaṇo vā tasyaiva vā yatsa tathā babhūva // Jm_33.1 //
children.translated_text: whether it was some power of <s>karma</s> or his own [innate nature] that he became thus — who can say? || Jm 33.1 ||

children.text: ataśca nūnaṃ bhagavānavocadacintyatāṃ karmavipākayukteḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) surely declared the inconceivability of the connection between <s>karma</s> and its ripening —

children.text: kṛpātmakaḥ sannapi yatsa bheje tiryaggatiṃ tatra ca dharmasaṃjñām // Jm_33.2 //
children.translated_text: for though he was compassionate by nature, he took an animal birth, and even there [retained] the perception of <s>Dharma</s>. || Jm 33.2 ||

children.text: vinā na karmāsti gatiprabandhaḥ śubhaṃ na cāniṣṭavipākamasti /
children.translated_text: Without <s>karma</s> there is no continuity of existences; and what is wholesome does not have an unpleasant ripening;

children.text: sa dharmasaṃjñīpi tu karmaleśāṃstāṃstān samāsādya tathā tathāsīt // Jm_33.3 //
children.translated_text: yet he, though possessing the perception of <s>Dharma</s>, encountering various residues of <s>karma</s>, existed in such and such [states]. || Jm 33.3 ||

body.text: athānyatamo duṣṭavānarastasya kālāntarābhivyaktāṃ prakṛtibhadratāṃ dayānuvṛttyā ca vigatakrodhasaṃrambhatāmavetya nāsmādbhayamastīti taṃ mahāsattvaṃ tena tena vihiṃsākrameṇa bhṛśataramabādhata /
body.translated_text: Then a certain wicked monkey, perceiving the great being's innate goodness, which had manifested over time, and his freedom from the turbulence of anger due to his habitual compassion, thinking 'There is no danger from this one,' tormented that great being exceedingly through various forms of harassment.

children.text: dayāmṛduṣu durjanaḥ paṭutarāvalepodbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Toward those who are tender with compassion, the wicked one, swelling with intensified arrogance,

children.text: parāṃ vrajati vikriyāṃ na hi bhayaṃ tataḥ paśyati /
children.translated_text: proceeds to extreme mischief, for he sees no danger from them;

children.text: yatastu bhayaśaṅkayā sukṛśayāpi saṃspṛśyate
children.translated_text: but from one by whom he is touched even with a slight apprehension of fear,

children.text: vinīta iva nīcakaiścarati tatra śāntoddhavaḥ // Jm_33.4 //
children.translated_text: he moves about as if subdued, his insolence pacified. || Jm 33.4 ||

body.text: sa kadācittasya mahāsattvasya visrabdhaprasuptasya nidrāvaśādvā pracalāyataḥ sahasaivopari nipatati sma / drumamiva kadācidenamadhiruhya bhṛśaṃ saṃcālayāmāsa / kṣudhitasyāpi kadācidasya mārgamāvṛtya vyatiṣṭhata / kāṣtheṇāpyenamekadā śravaṇayorghaṭṭayāmāsa / salilāvagāhanasamutsukasyāpyasya kadācicchiraḥ samabhiruhya pāṇibhyāṃ nayane samāvavre / apyenamadhiruhya samudyatadaṇḍaḥ
body.translated_text: Sometimes he would suddenly leap upon that great being while he was sleeping trustfully or nodding off due to drowsiness. Sometimes, climbing upon him as upon a tree, he shook him violently. Sometimes, when [the buffalo] was hungry, he blocked his path and stood in his way. Once he even struck him on the ears with a stick. Sometimes, when [the buffalo] was eager to bathe in water, he climbed upon his head and covered his eyes with his hands. And mounting upon him with a raised stick,

body.text: prasahyaiva vāhayan yamasya līlāmanucakāra / bodhisattvo 'pi mahasattvaḥ sarvaṃ tadasyāvinayaceṣṭitamupakāramiva manyamāno niḥsaṃkṣobhasaṃrambhamanyurmarṣayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: driving him by force, he imitated the sport of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death). The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that great being, regarding all this insolent behavior as if it were a kindness, endured it without agitation, turbulence, or anger.

children.text: svabhāva eva pāpānāṃ vinayonmārgasaṃśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is the very nature of the wicked to resort to the wrong path of misconduct;

children.text: abhyāsāttatra ca satāmupakāra iva kṣamā // Jm_33.5 //
children.translated_text: and through habitual practice, patience toward them becomes, as it were, a service for the virtuous. || Jm 33.5 ||

body.text: atha kilānyatamo yakṣastamasya paribhavamamṛṣyamāno bhāvaṃ vā jijñāsamānastasya mahāsattvasya tena duṣṭakapinā vāhyamānaṃ taṃ mahiṣavṛṣabhaṃ mārge sthitvedamuvācamā tāvadbhoḥ kiṃ parikrīto 'syanena duṣṭakapinā? atha dyūte parājitaḥ? utāho bhayamasmātkiṃcidāśaṅkase? utāho balamātmagataṃ nāveṣi yadevamanena paribhūya vāhyase? nanu bhoḥ
body.translated_text: Then a certain <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit), unable to bear the humiliation of that [buffalo] — or wishing to test the disposition of that great being — stationed himself on the path where the great buffalo bull was being ridden by that wicked monkey, and said: 'Stop a moment! What is this — have you been purchased by this wicked monkey? Or were you defeated by him in a game of dice? Or do you perhaps fear something from him? Or do you not know the strength that resides in yourself, that you are thus ridden about in humiliation by him? Surely,

children.text: vegāviddhaṃ tvadviṣāṇāgravajraṃ vajraṃ bhindyādvajravadvā nagendrān /
children.translated_text: the diamond-tip of your horns, hurled with force, would shatter a thunderbolt, or like a thunderbolt, [shatter] the lords of mountains;

children.text: pādāśceme roṣasaṃrambhamuktā majjeyuste paṅkavacchailapṛṣṭhe // Jm_33.6 //
children.translated_text: and these hooves of yours, released with the fury of rage, would sink into a mountain peak as into mud! || Jm 33.6 ||

children.text: idaṃ ca śailopamasaṃhatasthiraṃ samagraśobhaṃ balasaṃpadā vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: And this body of yours, compact and firm as a mountain, complete in splendor, endowed with fullness of strength,

children.text: svabhāvasaujaskanirīkṣitorjitaṃ durāsadaṃ kesariṇo 'pi te bhavet // Jm_33.7 //
children.translated_text: formidable by the gaze of its natural vigor — it would be unapproachable even for a lion! || Jm 33.7 ||

children.text: mathāna dhṛtvā tadimaṃ kṣureṇa vā viṣāṇakoṭyā madamasya voddhara /
children.translated_text: Crush him, having seized him, or [flay him] with a blade, or gouge out his pride with the tip of your horns!

children.text: kimasya jālamasya kaperaśaktavatprabādhanāduḥkhamidaṃ titikṣase // Jm_33.8 //
children.translated_text: Why do you endure this suffering from the harassment of this powerless wretch of a monkey? || Jm 33.8 ||

children.text: asajjanaḥ kutra yathā cikitsyate guṇānuvṛttyā sukhaśīlasaumyayā /
children.translated_text: How is an ignoble person to be treated anywhere — by the gentle, pleasant cultivation of virtues?

children.text: kaṭuṣṇarūkṣākṣi hi yatra siddhaye kaphātmako roga iva prasarpati // Jm_33.9 //
children.translated_text: For where there is a disease of a phlegmatic nature, it spreads precisely through what is pungent, hot, rough, and sharp [in treatment] — [similarly, mildness aggravates the wicked]. || Jm 33.9 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvastaṃ yakṣamavekṣamāṇaḥ kṣamāpakṣapatitamarūkṣākṣaramityuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, looking at that <s>yakṣa</s>, spoke these words, gentle and not harsh, leaning toward the side of forbearance:

children.text: avaimyenaṃ calaṃ nūnaṃ sadā cāvinaye ratam /
children.translated_text: I know this one to be fickle indeed, and always delighting in misconduct;

children.text: ata eva mayā tvasya yuktaṃ marṣayituṃ nanu // Jm_33.10 //
children.translated_text: for that very reason, is it not fitting for me to bear with him? || Jm 33.10 ||

children.text: pratikartumaśaktasya kṣamā kā hi balīyasi /
children.translated_text: For one who is unable to retaliate, what patience is truly powerful?

children.text: vinayācāraśīreṣu kṣantavyaṃ kiṃ ca sādhuṣu // Jm_33.11 //
children.translated_text: And among the virtuous, who are disposed to disciplined conduct — what is there to be endured? || Jm 33.11 ||

children.text: śakta eva titikṣate durbalaskhalitaṃ yataḥ /
children.translated_text: It is precisely the powerful one who bears the stumbling of the weak;

children.text: varaṃ paribhavastasmānna guṇānāṃ parābhavaḥ // Jm_33.12 //
children.translated_text: better, therefore, is humiliation than the defeat of one's virtues. || Jm 33.12 ||

children.text: asatkriyā hīnabalāścca nāma nirdeśakālaḥ paramo guṇānām /
children.translated_text: Disrespect from those of inferior strength is, as it were, the supreme occasion for the display of virtues;

children.text: guṇapriyastatra kimityapekṣya svadhairyabhedāya parākrameta // Jm_33.13 //
children.translated_text: why then should one who loves virtue, considering this, strive to break his own steadfastness? || Jm 33.13 ||

children.text: nityaṃ kṣamāyāśca nanu kṣamāyāḥ kālaḥ parāyattayā durāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The occasion for patience — which depends on another — is always difficult to obtain for one who practices patience;

children.text: pareṇa tasminnupapādite ca tatraiva kopapraṇa kopapraṇakramaḥ kaḥ // Jm_33.14 //
children.translated_text: when another has provided that very occasion, what ground is there for anger? || Jm 33.14 ||

children.text: svāṃ dharmapīḍāmavicintya yo 'yaṃ matpāpaśuddhyarthimiva pravṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one, without considering the harm to his own <s>Dharma</s>, has set about as if intent on purifying my sins;

children.text: na cetkṣamāmapyahamatra kuryāmanya kṛtaghno bata kīdṛśaḥ syāt // Jm_33.15 //
children.translated_text: if I were not to practice patience even here, what greater ingrate could there be? || Jm 33.15 ||

body.text: yakṣa uvāca - tena hi na tvamasyāḥ kacācitprabādhanāyā mokṣyase -
body.translated_text: The <s>yakṣa</s> said: 'Then you will never be freed from this harassment of his —

children.text: guṇeṣvabahumānasya durjanasyāvinītatām /
children.translated_text: for one who has no respect for virtues, the ill-conduct of a wicked person —

children.text: kṣamānairbhṛtyamatyaktvā kaḥ saṃkocayituṃ prabhuḥ // Jm_33.16 //
children.translated_text: who is able to restrain it by forbearance alone, without abandoning the disposition of a servant?' || Jm 33.16 ||

body.text: bodhisattva uvāca -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: parasya pīḍāpraṇayena yatsukhaṃ nivāraṇaṃ syādasukhodayasya vā /
children.translated_text: That happiness which comes through the desire to cause pain to another, or the prevention of an arising of unhappiness —

children.text: sukhārthinastanna niṣevituṃ kṣamaṃ na tadvipāko hi sukhaprasiddhaye // Jm_33.17 //
children.translated_text: it is not fit for one who seeks happiness to resort to that, for its ripening does not lead to the attainment of happiness. || Jm 33.17 ||

children.text: kśamāśrayādevamasau mayarthataḥ prabodhyamāno yadi nāvagacchati /
children.translated_text: If this one, being thus admonished by me through the practice of patience with good reason, does not understand,

children.text: nivārayiṣyanti ta enamutpathādamarṣiṇo yānayamabhyupaiṣyati // Jm_33.18 //
children.translated_text: then those wrathful ones whose path he will approach will restrain him from the wrong course. || Jm 33.18 ||

body.text: asatkriyāṃ prāpya ca tadvidhājjanānna mādṛśe 'pyevamasau kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: And having received ill-treatment from such people, he will not behave thus even toward one like me;

body.text: na labdhadoṣo hi punastathācaredataśca muktirmama sā bhaviṣayti // Jm_33.19 //
body.translated_text: for one who has received [the consequences of] his faults does not act in that way again — and from that will come my deliverance. || Jm 33.19 ||

body.text: atha yakṣastaṃ mahāsattvaṃ prasādavismayabahumānāvarjitamatiḥ sādhu sādhviti saśiraḥprakampāṅgalivikṣepamabhisaṃrādhya tattatpriyamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>yakṣa</s>, his mind won over by faith, wonder, and esteem toward that great being, applauding 'Excellent! Excellent!' with nodding head and pointing finger, and greatly pleased, spoke these affectionate words:

children.text: kutastiraścāmiyamīdṛśī sthitirguṇeṣvasau cādaravistaraḥ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whence comes such steadfastness among animals? And whence this extensive regard for virtues?

children.text: kayāpi buddhyā tvidamāsthito vapustapovane ko 'pi bhavāṃstapasyati // Jm_33.20 //
children.translated_text: By some [higher] intelligence you must have assumed this body — surely you are some great one practicing austerities in an ascetic grove! || Jm 33.20 ||

body.text: ityenamabhipraśasya taṃ cāsya duṣṭavānaraṃ pṛṣṭhādavadhūya samādiśya cāsya rakṣāvidhānaṃ tatraivāntardadhe /
body.translated_text: Having thus praised him, and having shaken off that wicked monkey from his back, and having appointed guardians for his protection, [the <s>yakṣa</s>] vanished right there.

body.text: tadevaṃ sati kṣantavye kṣamā syānnāsatītyapakāriṇamapi sādhavo lābhamiva bahu manyante iti kṣāntikathāyāṃ vācyam / evaṃ tiryaggatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pratisaṃkhyānasauṣṭhavaṃ dṛṣṭam / ko nāma manuṣyabhūtaḥ pravrajitapratijño vā tadvikalaḥ śobheta? ityevamapi vācyam / tathagatavarṇe satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇe ceti /
body.translated_text: Thus, when there is one who deserves forbearance, patience should be shown, not when there is none — thus the virtuous esteem even those who wrong them, as if they were a gain. This should be cited in a discourse on patience (<s>kṣānti</s>). Thus, even among <s>Bodhisattvas</s> born in animal states, the excellence of discernment has been seen. Who, being a human, or one who has taken the vow of renunciation, would look well without it? — this too should be said. Likewise in praise of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and in [discourses on] hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with reverence.

body.text: iti mahiṣajātakaṃ trayastriṃśattamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-third [story], the <s>Mahiṣa Jātaka</s> (The Buffalo). ||

body.text: 34. Śatapatrajātakam
body.translated_text: 34. The <s>Śatapatra Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Parrot)

body.text: protsāhyamāno 'pi sādhurnālaṃ pāpe pravartitumanabhyāsāt / tadyathānuśrūyate -
body.translated_text: Even when urged, a virtuous person is unable to engage in evil, due to lack of habituation. As the tradition relates:

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ kilānyatamasmin vanapradeśe nānāvidharāgaruciracitrapatraḥ śatapatro babhūva / karuṇāparicayācca tadavastho 'pi na prāṇihiṃsākaluṣāṃ śatapatravṛttimanuvavarta /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said, in a certain forest region, was a parrot named <s>Śatapatra</s> (Hundred-Feathered), with beautiful multicolored plumage resplendent with various hues. And due to his habitual compassion, even in that state, he did not follow the parrot's way of life, which is tainted by the killing of living beings.

children.text: bālaiḥ pravālaiḥ sa mahīruhāṇāṃ puṣpādhivāsairmadhubhiśca hyadyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With tender young shoots of trees, with flowers fragrant with nectar, and with delightful [nectars],

children.text: phalaiśca nānārasagandhavarṇaiḥ saṃtoṣavṛttiṃ vibharāṃcakāra // Jm_34.1 //
children.translated_text: and with fruits of various flavors, fragrances, and colors, he maintained a life of contentment. || Jm 34.1 ||

children.text: dharmaṃ parebhyaḥ pravadan yathārhamārtān yathāśakti samuddharaṃśca /
children.translated_text: Expounding <s>Dharma</s> to others as was fitting, rescuing the afflicted as far as he was able,

children.text: nivārayaṃścāvinayādanāryānudbhāvayāmāsa parārthacaryām // Jm_34.2 //
children.translated_text: and restraining the ignoble from misconduct, he cultivated the practice of benefiting others. || Jm 34.2 ||

body.text: iti paripālyamānastena mahāsattvena tasmin vanapradeśe sattvakāyaḥ sācāryaka iva bandhumāniva savidya iva rājanvāniva sukhamabhyavardhata /
body.translated_text: Thus, under the protection of that great being, the community of creatures in that forest region flourished in happiness — as if having a teacher, as if having kinsmen, as if having knowledge, as if having a king.

children.text: dayāmahattvātparipālyamāno vṛddhiṃ yathāsau guṇato jagāma /
children.translated_text: Just as that [great being], protected by the greatness of compassion, grew in virtues,

children.text: sa sattvakāyo 'pi tathaiva tena saṃrakṣyamāṇo guṇavṛddhimāpa // Jm_34.3 //
children.translated_text: so too that community of beings, guarded by him, attained growth in virtue. || Jm 34.3 ||

body.text: atha kadācitsa mahāsattvaḥ sattvānukampayā vanāntarāṇi samanuvicaraṃstīvravedanābhibhavādviceṣṭamānaṃ digdhaviddhamivānyatamasmin vanapradeśe reṇusaṃparkavyākulamalinake sarasaṭaṃ sihaṃ dadarśa / samabhigamya cainaṃ karuṇayā paricodyamānaḥ papraccha - kimidaṃ mṛgarāja? bāḍhaṃ khalvakalyaśarīraṃ tvāṃ paśyāmī /
body.translated_text: Then once, that great being, wandering through the depths of the forest out of compassion for creatures, saw in a certain forest region a lion — writhing in agony from the overwhelming force of acute pain, like one struck by a poisoned arrow, his mane matted and dirty from contact with dust. Approaching him, impelled by compassion, he asked: 'What is this, O king of beasts? I see indeed that your body is gravely unwell.

children.text: dvipeṣu darpātirasānuvṛttyā javaprasaṅgādathavā mṛgeṣu /
children.translated_text: Has this indisposition of yours been caused by exertion from pursuing elephants in their rut with excessive zeal, or from a chase after deer,

children.text: kṛtaṃ tavāsvāsthyamidaṃ śrameṇa vyādheṣuṇā vā rujayā kayācit // Jm_34.4 //
children.translated_text: or by a hunter's arrow, or by some ailment?' || Jm 34.4 ||

children.text: tad brūhi vācyaṃ mayi cedidaṃ te yadeva vā kṛtyamihocyatāṃ tat /
children.translated_text: Tell me, if this matter may be spoken of to me, or whatever task there may be, let it be stated;

children.text: mamāsti yā mitragatā ca śaktistatsādhyasaukhyasya bhavān sukhī ca // Jm_34.5 //
children.translated_text: whatever ability I have, born of friendship — through it may your comfort be achieved, and may you be well! || Jm 34.5 ||

body.text: siṃha uvāca - sādho pakṣivara na me śramajātamidamasvāsthyaṃ rujayā vyādheṣuṇā vā / idaṃ tvasthiśakalaṃ galāntare vilagnaṃ śalyamiva māṃ bhṛśaṃ dunoti / na hyenacchaknomya bhyavahartumudgarituṃ vā / tadeṣa kālaḥ suhṛdām / yathedānīṃ jānāsi, tathā māṃ sukhinaṃ kuruṣveti /
body.translated_text: The lion said: 'O noble one, O best of birds, this indisposition of mine is not born of exertion, nor of an ailment, nor of a hunter's arrow. But this splinter of bone, lodged in my throat, torments me terribly like a thorn. For I am unable either to swallow it or to expel it. This, then, is the occasion for friends. As you now understand [the matter], make me well.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ paṭuvijñānatvādvicintya śalyoddharaṇopāyaṃ tadvacanaviṣkambhapramāṇaṃ kāṣṭhamādāya taṃ siṃhamuvāca - yā te śaktistayā samyak tāvatsvamukhaṃ nirvyādehīti / sa tathā cakāra / atha bodhisattvastadasya kāṣṭhaṃ dantapālyorantare samyagniveśya praviśya cāsya galamūlaṃ tattiryagavasthitimasthiśakalaṃ vadanāgreṇābhihṛtyaikasmin pradeśe samutpāditaśaithilyamitarasmin parigṛhya paryante vicakarṣa / nirgacchanneva tattasya vadanaviṣkambhaṇakāṣṭhaṃ nipātayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having devised a method for extracting the splinter (<s>śalya</s>) by virtue of his sharp intelligence, took a piece of wood of the same measure as the width of the lion's mouth and said to that lion: 'Open your mouth fully with all your strength.' He did so. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having properly lodged that piece of wood between the rows of the lion's teeth, and having entered into the root of his throat, grasped that bone-fragment lodged crosswise with the tip of his beak, loosened it on one side, seized it on the other, and at the edge pulled it out. As it came out, he also knocked away the wood propping open the mouth.

children.text: sudṛṣṭakarmā nipuṇo 'pi śalyahṛnna tatprayatnādapi śalyamuddharet /
children.translated_text: Even a skilled splinter-remover (<s>śalyahṛt</s>), well-practiced and observant of his work, could not extract that splinter by such effort alone,

children.text: yadujjahārānabhiyogasiddhayā sa medhayā janmaśatānubaddhayā // Jm_34.6 //
children.translated_text: which he extracted through the intelligence attained not by mere practice but cultivated over hundreds of births. || Jm 34.6 ||

children.text: uddhṛtya śalyena sahaiva tasya duḥkhaṃ ca tatsaṃjanitāṃ śucaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having extracted the splinter, together with the pain it had caused and the grief born of it,

children.text: prītaḥ sa śalyoddharaṇādyathāsīt prītaḥ saśalyoddharaṇāttathāsīt // Jm_34.7 //
children.translated_text: as pleased as he was at the extraction of the splinter (<s>śalya</s>), so too was he pleased at the extraction of the one afflicted by it (<s>saśalya</s>). || Jm 34.7 ||

body.text: dharmatā hyeṣā sajjanasya /
body.translated_text: For this is the very nature of a good person:

children.text: prasādhya saukhyaṃ vyasanaṃ nivartya vā sahāpi duḥkhena parasya sajjanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having secured the happiness of another or averted his misfortune, the good person, even at the cost of suffering to himself,

children.text: upaiti tāṃ prītiviśeṣasaṃpadaṃ na yāṃ svasaukhyeṣu sukhāgateṣvapi // Jm_34.8 //
children.translated_text: attains that extraordinary abundance of joy which he does not experience even in his own pleasures, however easily gained. || Jm 34.8 ||

body.text: iti sa mahāsattvastasya tadduḥkhamupaśamayya prītahṛdayastamāmantrya siṃhaṃ pratinanditastena yatheṣṭaṃ jagāma /
body.translated_text: Thus that great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), having alleviated the lion's suffering, with a joyful heart, having addressed the lion and been thanked by him, went on his way as he pleased.

body.text: atha sa kadācitpravitataruciracitrapatraḥ śatapatraḥ paribhraman kiṃcitkvacit tadvidhamāhārajātamanāsādya kṣudagniparigatatanustameva siṃhamacirahastasya hariṇataruṇasya māṃsamupabhuñjānaṃ tadrudhirānurañjitavadananakharakesarāgraṃ saṃdhyāprabhāsamālabdhaṃ śaranmeghavicchedamiva dadarśa /
body.translated_text: Now once, that <s>Śatapatra</s> (the hundred-petalled one), his beautiful and colorful plumage spread wide, while wandering about and finding no food of that kind anywhere, his body consumed by the fire of hunger, beheld that very lion devouring the flesh of a recently killed young deer — his face, claws, and mane-tips stained with its blood — appearing like an autumn cloud at twilight, tinged with the glow of the setting sun.

children.text: kṛtopakāro 'pi tu na prasehe vaktuṃ sa yācñāvirasākṣaraṃ tam /
children.translated_text: Yet though he had rendered a service, he could not bring himself to utter a single word of supplication to him,

children.text: viśāradasyāpi hi tasya lajjā tatkālamaunavratamādideśa // Jm_34.9 //
children.translated_text: for even though he was confident, shame at that moment imposed upon him a vow of silence. || Jm 34.9 ||

body.text: kāryānurodhāttu tathāpi tasya cakṣuṣpathe hrīvidhuraṃ cacāra /
body.translated_text: Yet, compelled by necessity, he walked to and fro within the lion's sight, overcome with embarrassment;

body.text: sa cānupaśyannapi taṃ durātmā nimantraṇāmapyakaronna tasya // Jm_34.10 //
body.translated_text: but that wicked one, though he saw him, did not even extend an invitation to him. || Jm 34.10 ||

children.text: śilātale bījamiva prakīrṇaṃ hutaṃ ca śāntoṣmaṇi bhasmapuñje /
children.translated_text: Like a seed scattered upon a slab of stone, like an offering cast into an ash-heap whose heat has died,

children.text: samaprakāraṃ phalayogakāle kṛtaṃ kṛtaghne vidule ca puṣpam // Jm_34.11 //
children.translated_text: just so is a kindness done to an ungrateful wretch — and a flower upon a <s>vidulā</s> (reed) at the time when fruit should ripen. || Jm 34.11 ||

body.text: atha bodhisattvo nūnamayaṃ māṃ na pratyabhijānīta iti nirviśaṅkataraḥ samabhigamyainamarthivṛttyā prayuktayuktāśīrvādaḥ saṃvibhāgamayācata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thinking 'Surely he does not recognize me,' approached him with even greater confidence, and employing the manner of a supplicant with appropriate blessings, requested a share of the food:

children.text: pathyamastu mṛgendrāya vikramārjitavṛttaye /
children.translated_text: "May it be well with the lord of beasts, whose livelihood is won by valor!

children.text: arthisaṃmānamicchāmi tvadyaśaḥpuṇyasādhanam // Jm_34.12 //
children.translated_text: I desire the honoring of a supplicant, which is the means to your fame and merit. || Jm 34.12 ||"

body.text: ityāśīrvādamadhuramapyucyamāno 'tha siṃhaḥ krauryamātsaryaparicayādanucitāryavṛttiḥ kopāgnidīptayātipiṅgalayā didhakṣanniva vivartitayā dṛṣṭyā bodhisattvamīkṣamāṇa uvāca - mā tavadbhoḥ /
body.translated_text: Though addressed with words thus sweet with blessings, that lion, accustomed to cruelty and envy, unfit for noble conduct, glaring at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a gaze turned aside — blazing with the fire of anger, exceedingly tawny, as if wishing to burn him — said: 'Enough of you, sir!'

children.text: dayāklaibyaṃ na yo veda khādana visphurato mṛgān /
children.translated_text: "One who knows no weakness of compassion, who devours animals as they tremble —

children.text: praviśya tasya me vaktraṃ yajjīvasi na tadbahu // Jm_34.13 //
children.translated_text: that you entered my mouth and lived — that is no great feat. || Jm 34.13 ||

children.text: māṃ punaḥ paribhūyaivamāsādayasi yācñayā /
children.translated_text: Yet you come and presume upon me with this begging!

children.text: jīvitena nu khinno 'si paraṃ lokaṃ didṛkṣase // Jm_34.14 //
children.translated_text: Are you weary of life? Do you wish to see the next world? || Jm 34.14 ||"

body.text: atha bodhisattvastena tasya rūkṣākṣarakrameṇa pratyākhyānavacasā samupajātavrīḍastatraiva nabhaḥ samutpapāta / pakṣiṇo vayamityarthataḥ pakṣavisphāraṇaśabdenainamuktvā pracakrāma /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, shame having arisen in him at the harshness of those rough words of refusal, flew up into the sky right there. 'We are birds' — conveying this meaning by the sound of spreading his wings, without saying it in words, he departed.

body.text: athānyatamā vanadevatā tasya tamasatkāramasahamānā dhairyaprayāmajijñāsayā vā samutpatya taṃ mahāsattvamuvāca - pakṣivara, kasmādimamasatkāramasya durātmanaḥ kṛtopakāraḥ / san saṃvidyamānāyāṃ śaktāvapi marṣayasi? ko 'rthaḥ kṛtaghnenānenaivamupekṣitena?
body.translated_text: Then a certain forest deity (<s>vanadevatā</s>), unable to endure such disrespect toward him, or perhaps wishing to test his steadfastness, flew up and said to that great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>): 'O best of birds, why do you, who have rendered a service to this wicked one, tolerate this disrespect, even when you possess the power [to retaliate]? What use is this ungrateful wretch who has treated you thus with indifference?'

children.text: śaktastvamasya nayane vadanābhighātād visphūrjitaḥ pramathituṃ balaśālino 'pi /
children.translated_text: "You are capable, by a blow to the face, of destroying his eyes even though he is mighty and roaring;

children.text: daṃṣṭrāntarasthamapi cāmiṣamasya hartuṃ tanmṛṣyate kimayamasya balāvalepaḥ // Jm_34.15 //
children.translated_text: and of snatching the meat from between his fangs — so why is this insolence of his, born of pride in his strength, endured? || Jm 34.15 ||"

body.text: atha bodhisattvastathāpyasatkāraviprakṛtaḥ protsāhyamāno 'pi tayā vanadevatayā svāṃ prakṛtibhadratāṃ pradarśayannuvāca - alamalamanena krameṇa / naiṣa mārgo 'smadvidhānām /

children.text: ārte pravṛttiḥ sādhūnāṃ kṛpayā na tu lipsayā /
children.translated_text: "The engagement of the virtuous toward the afflicted arises from compassion, not from desire for gain;

children.text: tāmavaitu paro mā vā tatra kopasya ko vidhiḥ // Jm_34.16 //
children.translated_text: whether the other acknowledges it or not — what grounds are there for anger? || Jm 34.16 ||

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though thus mistreated with disrespect and though urged on by that forest deity, displaying his own innate goodness of nature, said: 'Enough, enough of that course! That is not the path of those like us.'

children.text: vañcanā sā ca tasyaiva yanna vetti kṛtaṃ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: It is indeed a deception upon himself that the other does not recognize a kindness done;

children.text: ko hi pratyupakārārthī tasya bhūyaḥ kariṣyati // Jm_34.17 //
children.translated_text: for who, seeking a return favor, will act for him again? || Jm 34.17 ||

children.text: upakartā tu dharmeṇa paratastatphalena ca /
children.translated_text: But the benefactor, through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and further through its fruit,

children.text: yogamāyāti niyamādihāpi yaśasaḥ śiryā // Jm_34.18 //
children.translated_text: inevitably attains union — here too, with the splendor of fame. || Jm 34.18 ||

children.text: kṛtaśceddharma ityeva kastatrānuśayaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: If a deed was done simply because it was <s>dharma</s> — what regret can there be about it?

children.text: atha pratyupakārārthamṛṇadānaṃ na tatkṛtam // Jm_34.19 //
children.translated_text: If, however, it was done for the sake of a return favor, then that deed was but a loan, not a true act of kindness. || Jm 34.19 ||

children.text: upakṛtaṃ kila vetti na me parastadapakāramiti prakaroti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, knowing well that a kindness was done to him, yet commits an offence in return —

children.text: nanu viśodhya guṇaiḥ sa yaśastanuṃ dviradavṛttimabhipratipadyate // Jm_34.20 //
children.translated_text: does he not, having purified his own body of fame through [the display of others'] virtues, adopt the behavior of an elephant [who bathes then rolls in dust]? || Jm 34.20 ||

children.text: na vetti cedupakṛtamāturaḥ paro na yokṣyate 'pi sa guṇakāntayā śriyā /
children.translated_text: If the other, being afflicted [by ingratitude], does not recognize the kindness done, he shall not be joined with the glory that is won by virtues;

children.text: sacetasaḥ punaratha ko bhavetkramaḥ samucchritaṃ pramathitumātmano yaśaḥ // Jm_34.21 //
children.translated_text: but if he is conscious of it, then what course could there be for him to destroy the fame that he himself has raised? || Jm 34.21 ||

body.text: idaṃ tvatra me yuktarūpaṃ pratibhāti -
body.translated_text: But here is what seems fitting to me:

children.text: yasmin sādhūpacīrṇe 'pi mitradharmo na lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: When, even though one has been treated well, the duty of friendship is not observed in someone,

children.text: aniṣṭhuramasaṃrabdhamapayāyācchanaistataḥ // Jm_34.22 //
children.translated_text: one should withdraw from him gently, without harshness and without anger. || Jm 34.22 ||"

body.text: atha sā devatā tatsubhāṣitaprasāditamanāḥ sādhu sādhviti punaruktamabhipraśasya tattatpriyamuvāca -
body.translated_text: Then that deity, her mind delighted by those well-spoken words, having praised them repeatedly saying 'Excellent! Excellent!', spoke these dear words:

children.text: ṛte jaṭāvalkaladhāraṇaśramādbhavānṛṣistvaṃ viditāyatiryatiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Without the exertion of wearing matted hair and bark garments, you are a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage); you are a <s>yati</s> (ascetic) who knows the future;

children.text: na veṣamātraṃ hi munitvasiddhaye guṇairupetastviha tattvato muniḥ // Jm_34.23 //
children.translated_text: for mere appearance does not achieve the state of a <s>muni</s> (sage) — one who is endowed with virtues is truly a <s>muni</s>. || Jm 34.23 ||"

body.text: ityabhilakṣya pratipūjyainaṃ tatraivāntardadhe /
body.translated_text: Having thus recognized and honored him, she vanished right there.

body.text: tadevaṃ protsāhyamāno 'pi sādhurnālaṃ pāpe pravartitumanabhyāsāditi sajjanapraśaṃsāyāṃ vācyam / evaṃ kṣāntikathāyāmapyupaneyam - evaṃ kṣamāparicayānna vairabahulo bhavati, nāvadyabahulo bahujanapriyo manoṅaśceti / evaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabahulāḥ svāṃ guṇaśobhāmanurakṣanti paṇḍitā iti pratisaṃkhyānavarṇe vācyam / tathāgatamāhātmye ca bhadraprakṛtyabhyāsavarṇe ca - evaṃ bhadraprakṛtirabhyastā tiryaggatānāmapi na nivartata iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, even when urged, a good person is unable to engage in evil because of lack of practice in it — this should be cited in praise of the virtuous. And this should be adduced in a discourse on patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) as well: thus through habitual practice of forbearance, one does not become given to enmity, nor blameworthy, but dear to many and agreeable of mind. Thus the wise, through abundant reflective discernment (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>), guard the beauty of their own virtues — this should be cited in the description of reflective discernment. And in [illustrating] the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and in the description of the practice of a virtuous nature: thus a virtuous nature, once cultivated, does not cease even among those born in animal states.

body.text: // iti śatapatrajātakaṃ catustriṃśattamam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-fourth [story], the <s>Śatapatra Jātaka</s> (The Story of the Hundred-Petalled Bird).

body.text: // kṛtiriyamāryaśūrapādānām //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the venerable <s>Āryaśūra</s>.
